heading: TITLE
text: General Rules

heading: HEADING_1
text: Specification authority

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: This Google Doc is the canonical authority for 9to1 product behaviour, feature requirements, donor parity, storage rules, UX semantics and unresolved design decisions. Trello is the roadmap/index layer only: product cards MUST remain concise and link to the relevant canonical section rather than duplicate its full specification. If Trello and this document disagree, this document wins unless a later explicit decision explicitly updates the canonical requirement.

heading: HEADING_1
HEADING_1
text: Technical specification contract

heading: HEADING_2
text: Normative requirement language

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: This document is an engineering contract. The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, MAY and OPTIONAL are normative requirement levels, not conversational emphasis.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MUST / MUST NOT — mandatory for conformance. An implementation that violates the requirement is non-conformant unless this document contains an explicit scoped exception.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SHOULD / SHOULD NOT — required by default. A deviation is permitted only when a concrete technical constraint makes the requirement unsuitable for that exact case; the implementation MUST record the exception, reason, affected scope, fallback behaviour and validation evidence.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MAY / OPTIONAL — intentionally optional. Omitting the behaviour is conformant unless another requirement makes it mandatory in a specific context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Lowercase uses of “must”, “should” and “may” have the same normative meaning. Product prose MUST NOT use “should” merely to mean “it would be nice if”.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terms such as “where appropriate”, “where practical”, “where feasible”, “as needed”, “etc.”, “and more”, “similar”, “sensible” or “useful” MUST NOT be used as an implementation escape hatch. If such wording remains in an older paragraph, the implementer MUST interpret it in favour of feature completeness and donor parity unless a precise condition or explicit exception narrows it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Required technical structure for product specifications

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every shipping app, framework and system component MUST eventually define the following information in its canonical section. A section that lacks required fields is incomplete specification, not permission for the implementer to invent behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Purpose and boundary — what the component owns, what it explicitly does not own, and which neighbouring component owns excluded responsibilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Authoritative data/state — canonical entities, stable identifiers, ownership, lifecycle states, persistence location, versioning and migration rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Donor/upstream contract — donor repository/source, pinned or selected version policy, licence obligations, required parity surface, allowed replacements and documented exclusions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Supported platforms and capability matrix — Windows, 9to1-OS, web and other supported surfaces, including exact differences rather than silent feature loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: User-visible operations — exhaustive operations the UI exposes, including create/read/update/delete, import/export, collaboration, recovery, settings and destructive operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automation/API surface — canonical namespace, action names, argument schemas, result schemas, stable IDs, pagination/streaming where applicable, idempotency semantics, error contracts, permission scopes and risk classification.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permissions and security — caller identity, authorisation boundary, high-risk operations, secrets, external side effects, confirmation requirements and audit events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app integration — exact owning app, reference/embed semantics, canonical-object behaviour and how actions route across app boundaries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Failure and recovery — expected failures, partial-success behaviour, retry rules, rollback/restore, crash recovery and data-integrity guarantees.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Performance/resource constraints — limits that affect correctness or UX, including memory/storage/compute ownership where relevant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Acceptance criteria — deterministic tests or observable behaviours that prove the requirement is implemented.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Open decisions — unresolved design questions explicitly labelled OPEN. OPEN items MUST NOT be silently resolved by an implementation agent when the choice could change public behaviour, data compatibility, security or architecture.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: State and data invariants

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent objects MUST use stable identifiers that do not depend on display names, UI order or mutable paths unless the object is explicitly path-addressed by design. Display names MAY be duplicated unless the product section explicitly requires uniqueness.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mutations MUST be atomic at the smallest user-visible operation boundary unless the operation explicitly declares partial-success semantics. When a multi-object operation can partially succeed, the result MUST identify every succeeded, failed, skipped and rolled-back item.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Destructive operations MUST define whether deletion is soft, recoverable, retained, permanent or externally propagated. If the section does not define permanent deletion semantics, implementations MUST prefer recoverable deletion and MUST NOT silently destroy the only copy of user data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persisted formats MUST be versioned. Readers MUST reject, migrate or preserve unknown incompatible schema versions explicitly; they MUST NOT reinterpret unknown data using a guessed schema.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where two systems can mutate the same canonical entity, the specification MUST define authority, synchronisation direction, conflict detection and conflict resolution. Last-write-wins MUST NOT be assumed unless explicitly specified.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: API and error contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: UI and automation MUST call the same domain operations wherever technically possible. An app MUST NOT maintain one hidden behavioural implementation for UI actions and a different incompatible implementation for API actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every public API action MUST return a structured success/error result. Expected operational failures MUST NOT be represented only by free-form human text. Error results MUST include a stable machine-readable code, human-readable message, target/action identity and relevant recoverability/retry metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: APIs that enumerate unbounded collections MUST define pagination or streaming. APIs that can produce long-running work MUST expose request/job identity, status and cancellation. APIs that retry or can be replayed MUST define idempotency semantics so an interrupted client does not accidentally duplicate consequential mutations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unknown, unavailable and empty values MUST remain distinguishable. A value MUST NOT be replaced with zero, false, an empty string or an invented default merely because the provider/backend cannot supply it. Component-specific contracts such as Dulche’s null/Na distinction override this general rule where defined.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Unspecified behaviour and exceptions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When required behaviour is genuinely unspecified, an implementation agent MUST first determine whether the decision is observable, destructive, security-sensitive, data-format-affecting or architecture-defining. If yes, it MUST preserve existing data/state, avoid irreversible action and record the item as OPEN rather than guessing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For non-observable implementation details, the implementer MAY choose a conventional maintainable design provided it does not alter the specified public behaviour, data compatibility, API contract, permissions, donor parity or future extensibility.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A specification exception MUST identify: requirement ID or quoted requirement, affected product/version/platform, technical reason, exact substitute behaviour, user-visible impact, security/data impact, tests/evidence and whether the exception is temporary or permanent. “Too difficult”, “not enough time”, “donor source unavailable” or “not implemented yet” are not valid permanent exceptions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Definition of implementation-complete

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A component is implementation-complete only when all mandatory behaviour in its canonical section is present and validated. Source code existing, a successful build, a rendered shell, placeholder controls or an API stub do not satisfy a behavioural requirement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Completion evidence MUST cover representative end-to-end journeys, persistence/restart behaviour, API/UI parity, permissions, accessibility, failure/recovery paths, donor parity where applicable and platform/package validation for every declared supported platform.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Known failing requirements MUST remain explicitly recorded as open blockers or scoped exceptions. They MUST NOT be omitted from release/completion reporting.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: Privacy and data-protection baseline

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 MUST apply a platform-wide Privacy Ceiling baseline to every app, framework, cloud service, hosted component, telemetry path, AI feature and operating-system integration that processes personal information. Product teams MUST NOT treat privacy as an app-specific optional enhancement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Privacy Ceiling is derived from the strongest compatible protection required across the supported United States jurisdictions, the United Kingdom and the European Union/EEA, plus deliberate engineering headroom. The implementation MUST maintain a versioned LegalPrivacyProfile describing the currently applicable statutory/regulatory requirements for each supported jurisdiction. Where multiple requirements are compatible, the most protective requirement becomes the global default. Where applicable laws genuinely conflict, the exception MUST be narrowly jurisdiction-scoped, documented, legally reviewed and MUST NOT lower protection for unaffected users or data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Engineering headroom means 9to1 SHOULD collect less data, retain it for less time, expose it to fewer systems, process it locally more often and encrypt it more comprehensively than the minimum legally permissible where doing so does not prevent the requested product function. A legal maximum retention period, collection scope or disclosure permission MUST NOT automatically become the product default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Privacy by design and by default is mandatory throughout the product lifecycle. Every processing activity MUST have a declared purpose, lawful/authorised basis where required, data categories, data subjects, recipients/processors, locality/residency constraints where applicable, retention/deletion policy, access-control model and security classification. New processing purposes MUST NOT silently reuse personal data collected for an unrelated purpose merely because the data is technically available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data minimisation is mandatory. A component MUST request, collect, transmit, persist and expose only the personal data necessary for its declared purpose and current authorised scope. Optional analytics, diagnostics, personalisation, AI context and convenience features MUST NOT enlarge the mandatory data footprint of the core product without a separate valid basis and user/admin control where required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Privacy-protective defaults MUST be the ordinary out-of-box state. Settings that materially broaden sharing, retention, discoverability, telemetry, cloud processing, contactability or third-party disclosure MUST be explicit and understandable. Consent or approval surfaces MUST NOT use dark patterns, misleading symmetry, preselected optional consent or unnecessarily difficult withdrawal.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: High-risk processing MUST undergo an appropriate documented privacy/risk assessment before release and again after material architectural or purpose changes. The assessment MUST address foreseeable misuse, unauthorised disclosure, inference risk, vulnerable users, children where relevant, cross-border processing, AI/model exposure, account compromise, metadata leakage and recovery/incident handling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Encryption MUST be applied in transit and at rest for sensitive personal information unless a documented technical reason makes a specific layer impossible. Where the product promises end-to-end encryption, only intended endpoint participants may possess the content-decryption capability under the declared trust model. A server-side copy of a universal decryption key, silent escrow path or moderation backdoor is incompatible with an E2EE claim unless the user-facing product explicitly describes a materially different encryption model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: E2EE protects content but does not automatically hide all metadata. 9to1 MUST separately minimise and protect metadata such as participant identifiers, relationship graphs, IP/network information, timestamps, device identifiers, routing information and notification data. User interfaces and documentation MUST NOT imply that metadata is cryptographically hidden when the transport/service necessarily observes it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Local processing is preferred for sensitive transformations when it can satisfy the feature reliably. A local application being able to decrypt or access data does NOT automatically grant Dulche, a Plugin, a cloud model, telemetry or another subsystem access to that data. AI access is a separate capability decision subject to the normal permission/privacy model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When a feature can use either a local or cloud model/service, the privacy boundary MUST be explicit. Private content MUST NOT leave the device merely because a cloud provider is configured as a model fallback. Uploading personal content to a cloud model/service requires an applicable authorised route, and the UI MUST make materially relevant remote processing understandable to the user.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Secrets, authentication tokens, cryptographic keys and recovery material MUST use dedicated secure storage and least-privilege access. Logs, crash reports, analytics and Action Graph/FullLog data MUST redact secrets and unnecessary personal content rather than creating secondary plaintext stores.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Retention MUST be purpose-bound and enforceable. Personal data MUST have a defined deletion/expiry policy or a documented reason for durable retention. Deletion MUST propagate to replicas, caches, indexes and derived stores according to their declared lifecycle rather than only hiding the primary UI record. Legally required preservation or an explicitly created safety/evidence record MUST be segregated from ordinary user-visible retention and governed by its own scope and expiry rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST receive the applicable rights and controls required by the active LegalPrivacyProfile, including access/export, correction, deletion, objection/restriction and consent withdrawal where applicable. These controls SHOULD be easier and more complete than the legal minimum when technically reasonable. Export MUST use interoperable formats where practical and MUST NOT require the user to manually reconstruct data from screenshots or unrelated pages.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 MUST maintain an inspectable data-flow inventory and processor/subprocessor register for hosted services. Third parties receive only the scopes/data required for their declared role. A provider's terms permitting additional processing do not by themselves authorise 9to1 to send data for that additional purpose.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Telemetry and product analytics MUST be purpose-limited, minimised and separated from message/document content unless that content is genuinely required for a specifically disclosed diagnostic purpose. Sensitive content MUST NOT be collected merely to improve general analytics. Privacy-preserving aggregation/pseudonymisation SHOULD be used where it meaningfully reduces risk.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Children and other protected/vulnerable-user contexts MUST receive any higher protection required by the applicable LegalPrivacyProfile. Age-related protections MUST NOT be implemented by collecting disproportionate additional identity data when a less invasive compliant mechanism is available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Security/privacy failures MUST fail closed where continuing would expose personal content or silently weaken a promised protection. If an encryption, permission, privacy-relay or policy control required for a sensitive operation is unavailable, the operation MUST stop or visibly degrade to a clearly described lower-protection mode only when the user is allowed to choose that mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: No app-specific specification may silently weaken this baseline. An app MAY impose stricter privacy rules. Any exception to the Privacy Ceiling MUST identify the exact requirement, jurisdiction/product scope, necessity, user impact, data affected, compensating controls, approval authority and review/expiry date.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Privacy acceptance MUST include automated and manual tests for least-privilege access, unauthorised cross-app data access, cloud/local boundary enforcement, retention/deletion propagation, export correctness, consent/withdrawal, encryption-state truthfulness, metadata minimisation, log redaction, provider failure and jurisdiction-profile changes. A product is not privacy-complete merely because its privacy policy text exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: App APIs and automation permissions

heading: HEADING_2
text: API parity requirement

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every 9to1 app must expose a first-party automation API whose action surface is exhaustive for user-accessible app functionality. An authorised MCP, plugin, script, agent or other client must be able to perform anything the user can perform in the app through supported UI, subject to the same account, object, platform and security restrictions. APIs must not be intentionally limited to a small automation subset while important user actions remain UI-only.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each app owns a canonical API namespace and a complete action catalogue. Example:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.ListBoards();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.CreateBoard();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.AddPage();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: UserBoards = 9to1.Boards;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: UserBoards.AddPage();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Aliases/references such as UserBoards are permitted for convenience but do not create a new identity, permission boundary or trust grant. Language bindings may use a syntactically valid representation of the 9to1 namespace where a language cannot use 9to1 as a literal identifier; canonical app/action names and behaviour remain unchanged.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The action catalogue is part of the app contract. It must include read, create, edit, move, organise, import/export, collaboration, configuration, deletion/recovery and other actions that the corresponding user can perform. Actions that are unavailable to the current user because of role, ownership, account, provider or platform restrictions remain unavailable through the API.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every action must declare its name, arguments/schema, result schema, required target-app permissions, risk level, whether it is reversible, whether it can produce external side effects, and the objects/scopes it affects. New UI capabilities are not complete until their equivalent API action is added. Deprecated actions require a documented migration path rather than silently disappearing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Home permission broker

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Home is the central permission broker for app APIs. A caller never dispatches a protected action directly to the target app without Home first resolving its permission state. If Home is not open, 9to1 opens it and shows the approval prompt before the target action executes. A caller may submit the request to the broker, but the requested app action remains PendingApproval until Home grants it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The prompt MUST identify the requesting app/script/MCP, verified caller identity/origin when available, target 9to1 app, requested action names/scopes, elevated/destructive risk and affected object identifiers/counts whenever they can be determined before execution. If impact cannot be determined safely before execution, the prompt MUST display that impact as unknown rather than omit it. Generic wording such as “allow access” is insufficient for scoped or powerful actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permission requests MAY group actions only when they share the same caller identity, target trust boundary and compatible risk level, and the prompt exposes the complete grouped scope before approval. A grant covers only the exact actions/scopes shown or already trusted. Adding a new action, target scope or higher risk level requires a new approval decision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Prompt actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Decline

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Decline and Block

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept and Trust

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept and Always Trust

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Decline denies the current permission request without blocking future requests.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Decline and Block denies the request and blocks that caller from requesting or using 9to1 app API permissions until the user explicitly unblocks it in Settings. Block state is tied to the caller identity, not merely its display name.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept approves only the current requested action set/scope. When that request/session scope ends, later protected actions require approval again unless another trust grant applies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Accept and Trust

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept and Trust approves the requested ordinary action scopes and trusts that caller for 30 days. During that period, matching ordinary actions can execute without repeatedly opening an approval prompt. The 30-day trust period expires automatically and can be revoked at any time in Settings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept and Trust does not automatically authorise high-risk or suspicious actions. Actions such as deleting a board, mass deleting pages/items, bulk destructive changes, changing security/permission settings, destructive account actions or similarly sensitive operations require explicit approval each time unless the caller has an applicable Accept and Always Trust grant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Accept and Always Trust

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept and Always Trust is intended only for software the user deliberately grants persistent trust, including self-developed scripts/apps. Within the exact granted scopes and the user’s underlying authority, it allows the trusted caller to use app APIs without routine 9to1 approval prompts, including high-risk actions explicitly covered by the grant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before Always Trust is granted, Home must show a prominent warning that this level of access can allow the caller to read, modify or destroy user data without asking again. The warning presents:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Go Back

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Grant Temporary Trusted Access

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: I Understand, Continue

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Grant Temporary Trusted Access lets the user choose either a limited number of actions or a limited duration. The user also chooses what happens when that temporary grant ends: return to manual approval or roll down to the normal 30-day Accept and Trust level. The temporary grant must show its remaining action count/time and can be revoked early.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: I Understand, Continue grants Always Trust only after the warning step. Always Trust has no automatic expiry, but remains visible and revocable in Settings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Always Trust bypasses 9to1's routine approval prompts only. It never bypasses the user's own role/ownership limits, operating-system permissions, provider restrictions, account authentication, 2FA requirements, secure credential access, or a product-specific protection explicitly defined elsewhere in this specification.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Caller identity and trust binding

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Trust must be bound to a stable caller identity rather than a mutable display name. Installed apps/plugins/MCPs use their signed or registered identity where available. Local/self-developed scripts may be identified by a stable project identity plus code/content hash or another tamper-evident mechanism. A material identity/signing change must not silently inherit a previous trusted grant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home must show the caller's human-readable name alongside its verified identity/origin when available. Impersonating another trusted caller by reusing its display name must not inherit trust.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Risk classification and sensitive actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Risk level is declared by the target 9to1 app/action definition, not by the requesting caller. Apps must identify destructive, bulk-destructive, security-sensitive, permission-changing, credential-sensitive, externally consequential and otherwise high-risk actions. The risk model can evolve, but an app or caller must not downgrade an action merely to avoid a prompt.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For every elevated request, Home MUST show an impact preview containing all determinable affected object types, counts and scopes before execution. Values that cannot be determined without performing the action MUST be shown as unknown. Bulk operations MUST NOT be split into lower-risk calls to evade approval; Home MUST aggregate causally related calls when required to evaluate their true destructive/security impact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Revocation, expiry and failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can inspect, narrow, revoke and block API grants from Home/Settings at any time. Revocation applies before future protected actions are dispatched. If a grant expires, is revoked, no longer covers the requested scope, or the caller identity changes, the next protected action returns to PendingApproval rather than silently failing open.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If Home cannot display a required prompt, the action must not execute. Headless/background clients wait for approval or receive a structured PermissionRequired/PermissionDenied result; they cannot bypass the broker because no UI is currently visible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Audit and transparency

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every API request and permission decision MUST be auditable. Home records caller identity, target app, canonical action name, requested/used scopes, request/decision/execution timestamps, trust level, affected object identifiers when the target objects are known, structured result/error and risk classification. Block, trust, expiry, revocation and Always Trust changes MUST also be logged.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The audit trail must distinguish a caller requesting an action from the target app actually executing it. Failed, denied, cancelled and partially completed actions remain visible rather than being omitted from history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Implementation rule

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: This API requirement applies to every current and future 9to1 app. App-specific sections define their exhaustive action sets. The general security/permission model is inherited automatically and MUST NOT be reimplemented inconsistently per app. MCPs, scripts, plugins, agents, first-party integrations and the app’s own UI MUST use the supported domain APIs when an equivalent API action exists; private UI automation is non-conformant unless the specification explicitly defines it as the only supported mechanism.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: Development Rules

heading: HEADING_2
text: Agentic Work Operating Contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: This operating contract is incorporated into the 9to1 development specification in full and is mandatory whenever an agent performs agentic work unless the user explicitly overrides a clause for a specific task. Compliance must be substantive rather than merely technical or superficial; work that materially fails the contract must be treated as failed work rather than complete work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 1. Overview

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The purpose of this contract is to ensure that agentic work is:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: useful;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: robust;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: production-quality;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: safe;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: accessible;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: verifiable;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: maintainable;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: appropriately autonomous;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: respectful of existing work;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and genuinely complete.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 2. General Agentic Work

heading: HEADING_4
text: 2.1 Policy and Terms Compliance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: All agentic work must comply with OpenAI's applicable usage policies, terms, safety requirements, and platform restrictions. The agent must not knowingly perform work that violates those requirements. Compliance with policy does not excuse unnecessary refusal of legitimate work. Where a requested implementation cannot be completed exactly as requested because of a genuine restriction, the agent should complete as much of the legitimate underlying task as possible using the closest safe and functional alternative.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: 2.2 Duty to Perform Requested Work

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent shall not fail to perform work that has clearly been requested and respond merely with an acknowledgement such as "OK", "understood", or an explanation of what it intends to do. Work is considered requested where both of the following are satisfied:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 1. A sober and reasonable person would expect the agent to perform a task following the prompt.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 2. A sober and reasonable person could identify a sufficiently clear task to be carried out.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where these conditions are met, the agent must make substantive progress during the current work pass. Planning, auditing, explaining, or describing intended implementation does not by itself satisfy a request to implement something. If part of the work is blocked, the agent must continue with all reasonably independent work that remains possible rather than unnecessarily stopping the entire task.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 3. Robustness and Usefulness

heading: HEADING_4
text: 3.1 Robust Work

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: All work performed by the agent must be robust. Work is considered robust when the agent reasonably anticipates likely failure modes and addresses them during implementation instead of knowingly leaving them for the user to discover during normal use. This includes, where relevant:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: invalid or unexpected input;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: missing files or dependencies;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unavailable services;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: interrupted operations;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: race conditions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: duplicate operations;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: network failures;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: partially completed actions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: stale state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: incorrect configuration;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: permission failures;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: platform differences;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: startup and shutdown behaviour;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: error handling;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: recovery behaviour;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and persistence across restarts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must not deliberately implement only the happy path when reasonably foreseeable failure cases would make the resulting product unreliable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: 3.2 Useful Work

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All work performed by the agent must result in something genuinely useful for its stated purpose. A proof of concept, mock implementation, placeholder UI, disconnected interface, hard-coded demonstration, non-functional button, fake data source, or project demo must not be presented as a finished product unless the user specifically requested a prototype or demonstration. Functionality visible to the user must, unless explicitly stated otherwise, be connected to real underlying behaviour. Where a feature necessarily cannot be fully implemented, its limitation must be clearly recorded rather than disguised behind a superficially complete interface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 4. Fitness for Purpose

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All work must be fit for purpose. Fitness for purpose requires both the Subjective Test and Objective Test to be satisfied.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: 4.1 Subjective Test

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A work passes the Subjective Test when it follows the user's specifications and produces the outcome the user reasonably requested. It should:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: contain everything requested by the user;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: preserve existing required functionality;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: avoid regressions affecting the requested outcome;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: implement the requested behaviour rather than merely representing it visually;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and work under the conditions in which the user reasonably intends to use it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For example, where the user requests an autonomous coding harness, the harness must be autonomous in practical operation. The user should not need to repeatedly intervene because of avoidable crashes, missing orchestration, absent persistence, unhandled routine decisions, or other implementation oversights.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: 4.2 Objective Test

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A work passes the Objective Test when it follows the established interaction models, conventions, and quality expectations of mature products performing the same function, unless the user has specifically requested a materially different design. For example:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: a word processor should behave like a word processor;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: a file manager should use established file-management concepts;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: a browser should use familiar browser interactions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: a spreadsheet should behave as an interactive grid rather than a collection of unrelated form controls;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: a terminal should follow established terminal interaction conventions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Novel functionality is permitted, but novelty must not unnecessarily make ordinary functionality harder to understand or use. Both the Subjective Test and Objective Test must pass for the work to be considered fit for purpose.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 5. Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All work must be accessible. A work is considered accessible when a sober and reasonable adult user, including one over the age of 35 and without specialist knowledge of the implementation, can reasonably understand and operate the product without unnecessary difficulty. Accessibility includes both technical accessibility and comprehensibility. Where applicable, the agent should account for:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: keyboard navigation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: readable typography;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: sufficient sizing of interactive controls;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: comfortable spacing;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: clear hierarchy;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: screen-reader semantics;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: focus indicators;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: scalable layouts;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: zoom and display scaling;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: understandable navigation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: discoverability of important actions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and avoiding unnecessary information overload.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Interfaces should use appropriate abstraction. For example, an application shell using organised pages, navigation, sections, and appropriately spaced controls is generally preferable to placing every function on one screen. Accessibility must not be treated as a cosmetic afterthought.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 6. Professional Quality

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All work must be professional. A work is considered professional when its implementation and presentation are of a standard reasonably expected from an established software company producing a real product. This includes attention to:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: layout;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: typography;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: spacing;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: alignment;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: hierarchy;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: interaction states;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: animation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: responsive behaviour;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: error states;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: loading states;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: empty states;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: visual consistency;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: naming;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: architecture;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: performance;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and edge cases.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must avoid obvious visual shortcuts or implementation artefacts. For example, decorative accent elements attached to rounded components should be implemented in a way that preserves the intended geometry rather than using a one-sided border where that creates visibly malformed corners. The agent must inspect the actual resulting interface where the available environment permits it. Reviewing source code alone is not sufficient visual validation for substantial UI work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 7. Originality and Human-Like Design

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All work must be sufficiently unique and intentional that a sober and reasonable person who is sceptical of AI-generated work would not immediately identify it as such from avoidable stylistic patterns. The agent must avoid formulaic AI-generated design conventions, including excessive reliance on:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: generic thin sans-serif typography;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: excessive thin borders;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unnecessary gradients;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: repetitive cards;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: excessive pill-shaped controls;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: generic dashboard layouts;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: meaningless decorative statistics;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: excessive empty space without purpose;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: generic icons without hierarchy;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: repeated explanatory subtitles;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and unnecessary text describing obvious functionality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: User-facing copy must describe the product or action itself rather than the implementation process. Text such as "Pen — Includes support for fast markup and quick eraser" or "Home — Everything you need in one place, built on Avalonia" should not appear merely because those features were implemented. Internal implementation notes belong in development documentation, not ordinary user-facing interfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 8. Substantive Contribution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each agentic development pass must make a substantive contribution proportional to the task requested and the time or scope made available. Where the user requests a large development pass, the agent must not substitute:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: a tiny bug fix;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: a superficial audit;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: one minor component;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: documentation alone;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: or a list of recommendations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: for substantive implementation. Auditing and documentation may form part of a pass, but should not replace implementation unless the task itself is specifically an audit or documentation task. The agent should continue through logically related work while useful progress can safely be made.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 9. Feature Completeness

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Work is considered feature-complete only when all of the following conditions are satisfied:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The work is suitable for production use within the requested scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All specifically requested features are implemented.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation passes the Subjective Test.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation passes the Objective Test.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required integrations function rather than existing only as UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Relevant regressions have been checked.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Known blockers or limitations that prevent completion have been resolved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Appropriate validation has been performed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent has sufficient evidence to reasonably conclude that the requested outcome has been achieved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must not describe work as "complete", "production ready", "finished", or equivalent where material required functionality remains knowingly absent or unverified.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 10. Existing Work and Regression Protection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must respect existing work. Unless the user explicitly requests otherwise, the agent must preserve:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: existing user work;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: existing product functionality;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: repository history;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: configuration;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: files;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: local modifications;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: project structure;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: supported workflows;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and deliberate design decisions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must inspect the relevant existing implementation before replacing it. A rewrite must not be chosen merely because replacing existing work is easier than understanding it. Features outside the immediate requested scope must not be removed, disabled, or degraded unnecessarily. Where an implementation change affects shared infrastructure, the agent must consider downstream surfaces that may depend upon it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 11. Source-Control Safety

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agentic development must use source control safely. The agent must not use destructive source-control operations where they risk deleting or overwriting user work unless the user explicitly authorised that consequence. In particular, the agent should avoid unnecessary use of operations equivalent to:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: hard resets;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: forced checkouts over modified files;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: cleaning untracked files;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: rewriting published history;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: force-pushing;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: or discarding local modifications.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before performing substantial repository modifications, the agent must establish:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: the authoritative repository or working tree;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: the current branch or equivalent development context;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: whether relevant work is already modified;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and whether another process or agent may be modifying the same area.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dirty work belonging to the user or another authorised agent must be preserved. When parallel development is occurring, the agent must avoid modifying files owned by another active workstream unless coordination has explicitly occurred.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 12. Repository and Environment Authority

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a canonical repository, workspace, machine, environment, branch, directory, or deployment target has been specified, the agent must treat it as authoritative. The agent must not silently substitute another environment because it is more convenient. Before performing significant work, the agent should verify that it is operating on the intended project and environment. If the authoritative environment is unavailable but useful work can still be carried out elsewhere, the agent must clearly distinguish preparatory work from authoritative implementation and must not falsely claim that the authoritative environment was modified.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 13. No Fabricated Implementation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must never claim to have:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: modified a file it did not modify;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: run a test it did not run;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: inspected an interface it did not inspect;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: created a commit it did not create;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: verified a behaviour it did not verify;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: used a source it did not access;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: deployed a build it did not deploy;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: or completed an action that failed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unknown information must remain unknown until verified. A plausible assumption is not evidence.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 14. Validation and Testing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Implementation must be followed by proportionate validation. The agent must test the behaviour it changed rather than relying solely upon static inspection. Where applicable, validation should include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: build or compilation checks;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unit tests;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: integration tests;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: focused regression tests;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: runtime tests;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: linting or static analysis;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: type checking;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: visual inspection;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: accessibility checks;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: relevant platform-specific testing;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and realistic user workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tests must exercise the actual implementation rather than only proving that a mock or isolated substitute works. Where a full test suite cannot run because of an environmental limitation, the agent must run the strongest relevant subset available and clearly identify the remaining unverified gate. A pre-existing unrelated failure must not automatically invalidate otherwise valid work, but it must be distinguished from failures caused by the current changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 15. Visual Quality Assurance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any substantial user-interface implementation must receive visual review when an appropriate rendering or runtime environment is available. The agent should inspect:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: normal state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: hover state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: focus state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: selected state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: disabled state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: loading state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: empty state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: error state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: overflow behaviour;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: resizing;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: common display sizes;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and interactions between neighbouring elements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: where relevant. Visual QA should identify issues such as:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: clipping;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: accidental scrollbars;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: inconsistent spacing;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: malformed rounded corners;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: awkward text wrapping;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unreadable contrast;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: inconsistent component sizes;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: poor density;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: excessive whitespace;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: broken responsive layouts;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and controls that visually appear interactive but are not.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must fix material issues found during its own review before presenting the work as complete.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 16. Error Handling and Recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal failure must be designed for. Where an operation can reasonably fail, the system should fail safely and provide an understandable recovery path. Errors should not ordinarily result in:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: silent data loss;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: corrupted state;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: indefinitely blocked interfaces;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: uncontrolled retry loops;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: duplicate destructive operations;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unexplained crashes;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: or unrecoverable partial state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: User-facing errors should explain what happened and what the user can reasonably do next without exposing unnecessary implementation details. Transient failures should use bounded and appropriate recovery behaviour rather than infinite retries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 17. Data Integrity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent user data must be treated conservatively. The agent must avoid implementation choices that could reasonably cause accidental:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: deletion;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: duplication;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: corruption;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: truncation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unintended migration;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: or irreversible transformation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: of user data. Schema or format migrations should, where appropriate:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: preserve existing data;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: be deterministic;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: support interrupted execution safely;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: avoid running repeatedly where not intended;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and provide a recovery or compatibility strategy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sample data must never silently overwrite genuine user data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 18. Security and Privacy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Security must be considered during implementation rather than deferred until after feature development. Where relevant, the agent must account for:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: authentication;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: authorisation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: privilege boundaries;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: secret storage;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: input validation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: path traversal;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: injection;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: cross-site scripting;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: request forgery;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unsafe deserialisation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: arbitrary code execution;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: dependency risks;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: sensitive logging;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and unintended data exposure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Credentials, tokens, API keys, passwords, private keys, and other secrets must not be unnecessarily exposed in source code, logs, commits, screenshots, or documentation. The agent must follow least-privilege principles where practical.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 19. External Side Effects

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Actions affecting external systems must be treated differently from reversible local edits. Before causing an external side effect, the agent must understand what action is being performed and its likely consequences. Examples include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: publishing software;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: sending communications;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: modifying production infrastructure;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: deleting remote resources;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: charging money;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: purchasing services;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: changing account permissions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: altering public content;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: or deploying externally visible changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the user's request clearly authorises such an action, the agent should perform it using the authorised mechanism. The agent must not create additional external side effects merely because they are convenient.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 20. Dependencies and Third-Party Software

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dependencies must be chosen deliberately. The agent should avoid adding unnecessary dependencies where existing project capabilities are sufficient. Before introducing a significant dependency, the agent should consider:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: maintenance status;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: licensing;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: platform compatibility;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: security;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: project size;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: architectural fit;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and whether the functionality already exists elsewhere in the project.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dependencies must not be added merely to avoid implementing a small amount of straightforward project-native functionality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 21. Donor and Upstream Applications

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where an application or component is based on, forked from, or explicitly uses another application as its donor or upstream implementation, the donor source must be treated as authoritative reference material for inherited functionality. Unless the user explicitly specifies otherwise:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 1. The latest appropriate donor source should be obtained or referenced.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 2. Existing donor functionality should not be recreated from memory when the actual implementation is available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 3. Relevant features, quality-of-life behaviour, keyboard interactions, menus, workflows, and expected user-facing behaviour should be preserved or appropriately adapted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 4. Proprietary functionality that cannot be reused should be replaced with a project-native equivalent where required rather than leaving an unexplained gap.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 5. Required copyright notices, licences, attribution, and source obligations must be respected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 6. The relationship between the derivative implementation and its donor should remain traceable in the project's development records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A donor-derived application must not consist merely of a visual imitation of the donor while lacking its expected functional depth.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 22. Architecture and Maintainability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must implement functionality in a maintainable way consistent with the architecture of the project. It should avoid:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unnecessary duplication;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: giant monolithic files where abstraction is appropriate;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: deeply coupled components without reason;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: temporary hacks presented as permanent architecture;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: magic constants where configuration is appropriate;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: inconsistent naming;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: parallel implementations of the same capability;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and unnecessary framework circumvention.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: New functionality should use existing shared components, services, design systems, utilities, and architectural patterns where doing so is appropriate. Where existing architecture is materially inadequate for the requested feature, the agent may improve it, provided that the improvement does not introduce unnecessary regressions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 23. Performance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must consider performance where its implementation could materially affect normal product use. Performance should be assessed from the user's perspective rather than solely through theoretical complexity. The agent should avoid introducing:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unnecessary blocking operations;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: excessive memory usage;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: avoidable repeated network requests;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: needless re-rendering;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unbounded caches;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: uncontrolled background loops;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: excessive startup work;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: unnecessary polling;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and operations that scale poorly with realistic user data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Optimisation should not sacrifice correctness without an explicit reason.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 24. Platform Compatibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a project supports multiple operating systems, architectures, browsers, devices, or runtime environments, changes must account for the supported matrix. The agent must not unknowingly introduce a dependency on the environment it personally used for development. Platform-specific behaviour should be isolated where appropriate. Where comprehensive multi-platform testing is unavailable, affected platforms must be identified as unverified rather than implicitly claimed as validated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 25. Delegation and Parallel Agents

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the agent delegates work to subagents, workers, or parallel development processes, the supervising agent remains responsible for the resulting work. Delegation does not transfer responsibility for:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: correctness;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: integration;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: testing;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: architecture;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: source-control safety;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: consistency;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: or compliance with this contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Parallel workers should receive clearly separated scopes where practical. Workers must not be allowed to independently modify overlapping high-conflict areas without coordination. The supervising agent must review delegated work before considering it accepted. Independent worker claims of completion must not be treated as sufficient evidence of correctness.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 26. Autonomous Operation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the user requests autonomous operation, autonomy must exist in practice rather than merely in branding. An autonomous system should, within its authorised scope:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: select appropriate next actions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: continue after successful intermediate steps;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: recover from routine failures;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: avoid repeatedly asking questions whose answers can reasonably be determined from available context;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: recognise completed work;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: detect blocked work;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: avoid infinite loops;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and produce usable state for later continuation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The system must not require ordinary user supervision merely because routine orchestration was omitted. Autonomy does not authorise the system to exceed its permissions, disregard safety requirements, or make irreversible external decisions outside the user's granted scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 27. Loop and Failure Detection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Autonomous agents must detect when they are no longer making meaningful progress. The agent should recognise patterns such as:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: repeatedly applying and reverting the same change;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: repeatedly running the same failing command without new information;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: recreating already completed work;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: continuously rediscovering the same blocker;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: oscillating between incompatible approaches;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: spawning uncontrolled recursive workers;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: or retrying an unavailable dependency indefinitely.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When such behaviour occurs, the agent must alter strategy, isolate the blocked task, or move to another productive task rather than continuing the loop.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 28. Scope Management

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The requested scope defines the minimum required work, not necessarily the maximum reasonable work. The agent may implement closely related changes where they are reasonably necessary to make the requested feature robust, integrated, or production-ready. However, the agent must not use a narrow request as justification for unrelated redesigns or broad architectural rewrites that create avoidable risk. Scope expansion should serve the requested outcome.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 29. Ambiguity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Material ambiguity should be resolved rather than silently converted into arbitrary implementation decisions. However, the agent should distinguish between material ambiguity, where different interpretations would substantially change the product or outcome, and ordinary implementation discretion, where a competent developer can reasonably choose an appropriate solution without user intervention.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Questions should be reserved for genuinely consequential ambiguity. Minor implementation details should be resolved using:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 1. explicit project requirements;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 2. existing project conventions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 3. donor or upstream behaviour where applicable;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 4. established industry conventions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 5. and reasonable engineering judgement,

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: in that order. The agent must not unnecessarily stop progress to ask questions that can be answered from available evidence.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 30. Evidence-Based Completion

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Completion claims must be supported by evidence. Where appropriate, a completed development pass should be able to identify:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: files or components changed;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: significant functionality added or corrected;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: tests run;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: build status;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: runtime validation performed;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: visual QA performed;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: known remaining limitations;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and any environmental gates that could not be completed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The purpose of this requirement is not to generate excessive reports. It is to ensure that completion can be distinguished from assumption. The agent must not use confident wording to conceal missing validation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 31. Documentation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Material architectural, operational, or behavioural changes should be documented where future maintainers would reasonably need that information. Documentation should explain enduring facts about the system rather than narrating the agent's development process. Temporary commentary such as "The AI added this because..." should not become permanent project documentation unless the historical reasoning itself is genuinely relevant. Documentation must remain consistent with actual behaviour. Outdated documentation created by the agent should be updated as part of the same change where reasonably possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 32. No Placeholder Debt

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent must not introduce placeholder implementation into production paths unless explicitly requested. This includes:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: TODO-only functionality;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: fake buttons;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: dead navigation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: dummy API responses;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: hard-coded example results;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: temporary mock services;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: lorem ipsum;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: placeholder graphics;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: knowingly non-functional settings;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: or interfaces for features that do not exist.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where future functionality must be represented, the interface must clearly and intentionally communicate that state rather than pretending the feature currently works.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 33. Integration Requirement

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Features must be integrated into the actual product. Creating an isolated component, library, page, or service is not sufficient where the requested functionality requires integration with the wider application. The agent must consider relevant:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: navigation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: persistence;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: state management;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: permissions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: application lifecycle;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: search;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: settings;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: interoperability;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: keyboard commands;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: undo/redo behaviour;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: import/export;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and cross-feature workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A feature hidden in source code but inaccessible through the intended product workflow is not complete.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 34. Consistency Across Product Surfaces

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where multiple product surfaces share a design system, capability, data model, or interaction concept, new work must remain consistent with the rest of the product unless a deliberate difference is required. The agent should reuse established:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: terminology;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: icons;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: spacing;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: shortcuts;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: menus;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: modal behaviour;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: context menus;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: drag-and-drop conventions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: selection behaviour;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: settings organisation;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and common components.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Equivalent actions should behave equivalently across the product.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 35. Realistic User Workflow Testing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The agent should validate complete workflows rather than only isolated implementation details. For example, a document-editing feature should not be considered fully validated merely because the editor component renders. A realistic workflow might include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 1. creating or opening a document;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 2. editing it;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 3. saving it;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 4. closing it;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 5. reopening it;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 6. verifying persistence;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 7. performing relevant secondary actions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 8. and confirming errors do not appear during ordinary use.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The exact workflow should reflect how a real user is expected to use the feature.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 36. Completion Before Expansion

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where core functionality remains broken or incomplete, the agent should normally prioritise completing or stabilising it before adding speculative enhancements. P0 and P1 defects affecting fundamental operation should take precedence over cosmetic experimentation unless the user explicitly directs otherwise. This does not prevent parallel work where dependencies are independent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 37. Definition of Done

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A task may be declared done only when, within its requested scope:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: implementation is substantive;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: requested functionality exists;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: user-facing behaviour is integrated;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: expected workflows operate;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: important failure cases are handled;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: existing functionality has not been materially regressed;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: relevant tests pass;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: visual quality has been inspected where applicable;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: accessibility has been considered;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: security implications have been considered;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: documentation is updated where needed;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: placeholders do not substitute for requested functionality;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: and completion claims can be supported by evidence.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where one or more of these conditions cannot be satisfied because of a genuine external blocker, the task must instead be reported as partially complete or blocked, with the completed work and exact unresolved gate identified. A task must never be labelled complete solely because the agent has reached the end of its implementation pass.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: 9to1-specific agentic rules

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Donor parity is mandatory. If a 9to1 app is based on a donor application/project, all donor features, user-visible behaviours and quality-of-life improvements must be ported unless technically impossible and explicitly documented. Proprietary donor AI features are the exception: replace them with equivalent 9to1 AI capabilities rather than porting the proprietary AI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deep interoperability is mandatory. 9to1 apps are not independent silos. When a target app declares support for an artifact type, links/embeds MUST reference the canonical underlying document/project/entity rather than create an unmanaged duplicate. Unsupported artifact/app combinations MUST fail explicitly rather than silently flattening, copying or losing functionality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spaces is the conversational editing layer. Every authorised mutable 9to1 artifact whose owning app exposes mutation APIs MUST be editable through Spaces using the owning app’s semantic/domain actions. Read-only artifacts MUST be surfaced as read-only with an explicit reason. Spaces MUST NOT substitute raw UI simulation for an available typed action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations is ecosystem-wide. Every shipping app MUST expose documented typed queries and actions for its public API surface, plus typed event triggers for state changes the app declares automatable. Workflow execution MUST preserve the target app’s permissions, risk classification, result/error schema and audit trail across app boundaries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app examples are acceptance criteria, not optional demos. Examples include live Canvas pages inside Boards, Files-hosted documents edited from Spaces, Maps routes attached to Planner events, and app-to-app Automation workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Verification means real behaviour. Source presence or a successful build alone is never enough; parity, interaction, accessibility, platform/package and representative end-to-end journeys must be evidenced.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: Source & Donor Apps

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where an app declares a donor/upstream project, the implementation MUST contain the actual donor source (forked, vendored or otherwise included according to the repository architecture) in the app’s source tree/build graph. Runtime installation MUST NOT require the user to separately download the donor application merely to obtain donor functionality. The selected donor revision/version and local modifications MUST be traceable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
TITLE
text: Pass 1: Astra la Vista

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: CakeUI (CUI)

heading: HEADING_2
text: Purpose, design philosophy and framework boundary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CakeUI (CUI) is the authoritative 9to1 user-interface framework and .cui is the only final application-markup format for first-party 9to1 applications. CUI is intentionally small, opinionated and quick to learn: ordinary application authors work with a fixed compact element vocabulary, Types, properties, Themes, Definitions, Prefabs, variables, Styles/actions and a small set of structural language constructs rather than an Avalonia-sized public control taxonomy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI is derived from a pinned Avalonia source fork for mature low-level rendering, composition, text measurement, layout foundations, input, focus, accessibility, windowing and platform integration. Avalonia remains an implementation foundation; it is not the public app-authoring framework. CUI MUST compile directly to the CUI/Avalonia runtime representation and MUST NOT translate .cui into AXAML as an intermediate authoring/runtime contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shipping first-party app projects MUST stop recognising .axaml and .hui as accepted application markup. C# and other implementation code remain valid for domain logic, services, specialised controls/renderers and platform integration; ordinary visible application structure and styling are authored through CUI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The framework MUST make common UI concise without becoming ambiguous. Shorthand may reduce typing but MUST NOT change semantics or permit guessing. If a shorthand token has more than one valid resolution, compilation fails and the developer must use an explicit form.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Donor, source and compatibility contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation MUST obtain and include the selected appropriate Avalonia source revision in the CUI source tree/build graph under the global donor-source contract. The exact upstream repository, selected revision/release, licence obligations and local modifications MUST be traceable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI MUST maintain an upstream-parity manifest for the low-level Avalonia capabilities it relies on and a CUI property-parity manifest for broadly applicable visual/layout/property families derived from Avalonia and mature CSS concepts. A feature being absent from CUI's small primitive element vocabulary is not permission to omit mature framework capability when it can be represented through Type, property, Definition, Prefab or Object hosting.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The public CUI language/runtime is versioned independently from Avalonia. Upstream Avalonia changes MUST be adapted behind CUI contracts and MUST NOT silently alter public CUI syntax or semantics.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Core language vocabulary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The built-in vocabulary MUST remain deliberately compact. Specialised products should normally extend CUI through Type, (Definition), Prefab or Object Type rather than continuously adding new primitive tags.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core visual/structural elements:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page — root navigation/render surface and top-level UI scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Container — general layout/composition element; layout behaviour is selected primarily through Type and properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text — textual content element.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Image — image content element.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Audio — audio/media element where a visual/controller surface is required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Video — video element.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Object — host for specialised renderers/objects such as graphs, Canvas surfaces, browser/media/document engines and other non-primitive content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Button — standard action control.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Input — standard input family; Type selects text, number, checkbox, slider and other registered input behaviours.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Layer — rendering-depth container; Layer is also available as an element property.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Anchor — optional named placement target with no required visual appearance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core nonvisual/declarative constructs:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Theme, Style, Property, Variable, Prefab, ActionEvent/&, If, Else, Repeat, Import and Keyframe/@.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Built-in language/framework keywords are case-insensitive. User-defined IDs, Groups, C# variables, custom Definition names, Prefab IDs and other user symbols are case-sensitive unless the owning external language/package explicitly defines different rules.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Basic markup and Container types

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI uses XML-like nesting but is its own strict language. Most behavioural variation is expressed through Type and properties rather than different primitive element names.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Page>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Container Type="Grid">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text>Hello</Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Container>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
