text: </Page>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Container MUST support at least Grid, Vertical Stack, Horizontal Stack and Absolute as built-in Types. Additional mature layout Types MAY be registered without changing the core element vocabulary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Container Type="Vertical Stack" Horizontal-Scrolling="True" Vertical-Scrolling="True">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Attribute-assignment shorthand uses a colon after an identifier. The following are equivalent when unambiguous:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Container Type="Grid">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Container Type:Grid>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For unquoted shorthand values, underscore MAY represent a space. Therefore Type:Vertical_Stack resolves to Type="Vertical Stack" when that is the only valid symbol. Quoted values are literal and underscore substitution never occurs inside quotes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If both an underscored name and the corresponding spaced name exist in the active resolution scope, shorthand is ambiguous and MUST fail compilation rather than choosing one.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Comments, whitespace and escaping

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Comments use <# and #> and MAY span multiple lines. Comments do not nest and do not create runtime nodes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <# This is a CUI comment #>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Formatting whitespace outside text-bearing content is ignored. Text content uses the Text element's whitespace policy; the default collapses source indentation/newline whitespace that exists only for readable markup, while Whitespace:Preserve retains exact authored whitespace.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quoted values are literal except for explicitly documented escape sequences. The compiler MUST provide an escaping mechanism for CUI-significant punctuation in free text/shorthand. Formatter output MUST be deterministic.

heading: HEADING_2
text: (Definition), custom elements and custom Types

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: (Definition) is a declaration modifier. A Definition creates reusable language/component definitions and is not rendered merely because its declaration is present.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Paragraph (Definition)>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Paragraph>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The declaration above creates a reusable Paragraph element that can later be instantiated as <Paragraph>...</Paragraph>.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text (Definition) Type="ABCDEFG">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Type Definition extends the relevant base element's registered behaviour/style contract. Built-in element and Type names cannot be silently shadowed by user definitions; an intentional framework-supported override must be explicit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Definitions SHOULD be authored using ordinary CUI elements/properties so authors do not have to learn a separate component language.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Themes and inherited theme structure

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Theme is an inherited visual-design scope. Everything within a Theme uses that Theme until a descendant Theme overrides it; after the descendant closes, inheritance returns to the parent Theme.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Built-in Theme names:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Professional.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Glow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Playful.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Bubble.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cinematic.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Themes are complete visual systems, not colour-only palettes. They MAY define typography, colours, surfaces, spacing defaults, control shapes, corner treatment, elevation/shadow, interaction states, animation defaults and other presentation properties, but they MUST NOT silently change the fundamental semantic meaning of controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Theme Name="Glow">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Container Type:Vertical_Stack>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Container>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Theme>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can define custom Theme types in .cui-theme files.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Theme (Definition) Name="Rainbow" Inherits="Professional">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Button (Definition)>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <# Theme-specific Button properties #>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Button>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Theme>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Within a Theme definition, an element Definition without Type defines that Theme's default presentation for that element. A Definition with Type defines the Theme presentation for that element Type. Custom Themes SHOULD inherit another Theme when only deltas are needed.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Default typography

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Montserrat is the default CUI/9to1 interface font wherever technically available and legally redistributable. First-party 9to1 applications and the 9to1-OS shell SHOULD inherit the global CUI typography system rather than independently selecting unrelated UI fonts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI MUST define a robust fallback font stack for environments where Montserrat is unavailable and must support specialised font roles such as monospace/code text. Users may override the system/interface font through the supported customisation/theme framework without requiring application-specific hacks.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Prefabs and reusable shared CUI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Prefab packages reusable shared CUI structure/code in a .cui-prefab file. Prefabs are intended for components that should be implemented once and reused across apps, such as the shared Dulche AI bar.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Prefab (Definition) Type="static" ID="AIBar">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Prefab>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prefab Type MUST be static or dynamic.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Static Prefab — all live instances share one internal mutable Prefab state. If an internal property/state changes, every live instance reflects the same shared state. Host placement, host parent, host size and host Active state remain per instance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dynamic Prefab — each instance receives independent runtime state while sharing the same compiled implementation/defaults.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Static Prefab state is runtime-shared, not automatically persistent across process restart. Persistence occurs only when the owning Prefab/app explicitly stores that state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prefabs may contain normal elements, Definitions, nested Prefabs, variables, Styles, actions, Themes and specialised Objects. Cyclic Prefab/Definition dependencies MUST be rejected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Prefab exposes caller-settable inputs, actions/events and optional CUI-content/Children inputs explicitly. It MUST NOT implicitly capture arbitrary caller state.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Prefab inputs and instantiation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prefab inputs are declared using Variable Definitions or another equivalent typed public-definition form implemented by the compiler.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Variable (Definition) Type="string"::Title>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Variable (Definition) Type="string"::Subtitle>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Prefab instance may provide declared inputs in markup or runtime load arguments. Static Prefabs MUST reject conflicting per-instance mutable input semantics that would violate their shared-state contract; content requiring independent mutable state uses a dynamic Prefab.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Variables and variable-reference syntax

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordinary application variables remain ordinary implementation-language values. CUI reactivity is attached to the CUI reference by default; application authors do not have to wrap every value in a special Live<T> type merely to update UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: string Name = "Jacob";

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text>Hello <:Name:></Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <:Name:> is the compact live variable-reference form. Live is assumed unless static is explicitly requested.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <:Name:live>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <:Name:static>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typed/conversion shorthand prefixes the target type:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <int:Age:>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <int:Age:static>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The long conversion forms are equivalent:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Variable.ToInt>Age</Variable>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Variable Type="int">Age</Variable>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Variable.ToInt and Variable Type="int" MUST resolve to the same typed conversion operation. Equivalent ToString, ToFloat, ToBool and other registered conversion forms MAY exist. Conversion failure MUST return/produce a defined typed validation/conversion error; it MUST NOT silently substitute an unrelated default such as zero.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Live versus static references

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A live CUI reference subscribes to the referenced CUI-visible value and automatically reevaluates the dependent UI when that value changes. A static CUI reference evaluates on load/explicit refresh and does not update merely because the source changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Static subexpressions retain their last evaluated value even when another live reference in the same element causes an unrelated update. Element.Refresh() explicitly reevaluates the element's static references; refreshing a Container/Page recursively refreshes the applicable active subtree.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI build tooling MUST instrument or generate change-notification plumbing for CUI-visible persistent fields/properties/observable collections referenced live. Per-frame polling is prohibited. Short-lived method locals cannot become magically persistent observable state after their scope ends.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Live dependency relationships

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: new Live(...) is reserved for relationships between application values/objects, not for basic CUI binding.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph = new Live(x, y);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The declaration above means Graph depends on x and y. A change to either dependency invalidates/recomputes Graph through Graph's defined derived getter, refresh/update operation or explicitly supplied recomputation function. Live MUST NOT invent a new scalar value when no recomputation semantics exist.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dependency cycles MUST be rejected at compile/build time when statically discoverable and surfaced as typed dependency errors otherwise.

heading: HEADING_2
text: ID/Name and Group addressing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ID and Name are aliases for the same unique identity mechanism. An element may own zero or one ID/Name and any number of Groups. Multiple elements may belong to the same Group.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text ID="txt" Group="Labels,Important">Hello</Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text Name="txt">Hello</Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ID shorthand is :: and Group shorthand is :::.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text::txt:::Labels,Important>Hello</Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Within a scope, IDs are unique. Groups intentionally contain multiple members. An ID and Group MUST NOT use the same identifier in one scope because direct runtime addressing would be ambiguous.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated/runtime handles allow direct element mutation:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: txt.Text = "Hello";

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Labels.Color = "Green";

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A direct Group operation broadcasts to every current compatible member in scope. The runtime MUST validate the entire target set before a persistent group mutation; incompatible required targets cause the operation to fail rather than silently producing partial state.

heading: HEADING_2
text: ID and Group scope

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page creates a top-level CUI addressing scope. Each dynamic Prefab/custom Definition instance creates a child scope for its internal IDs/Groups. A static Prefab has one shared internal state scope. Bare IDs/Groups resolve only in the current scope; cross-scope access must explicitly name the containing Page/Prefab instance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Groups are dynamic: active or inactive members remain members while the corresponding object exists. Persistent active Styles targeting a Group apply to newly loaded compatible members while that Style remains active.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Property declarations and shorthand

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Properties are strongly typed registered CUI properties. The long Property form and compact $ form are semantically equivalent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Property="Color" Color="Green">...</Property>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$Color:Green>...</$Color>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$Color=Green>...</$Color>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The short closing form </$> closes the most recently opened property region when nesting is unambiguous.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$Color:Green>Hello</$>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A property region is a typed property scope, not an ordinary visual element. It can have an ID or Groups using the same shorthand system.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$Color:Green::pinkText>Hello</$>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$Color:Green:::greenText>Hello</$>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiple property declarations may contribute different property types to the same Group. If a target Group exposes exactly one property type, a property mutation may omit the property name. If multiple property types are available, the property name is mandatory.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Property-target mutation directives

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI markup may mutate an existing property target/Group declaratively.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <:::$greenText.Color="Pink">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <:::$greenText="Pink">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The second form is valid only when greenText resolves to exactly one property type. For a multi-property Group such as Color plus Background, the explicit property is required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <:::$fancyText.Color="Blue">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <:::$fancyText.Background="Black">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Outside a Style/event rule, a mutation directive executes when its containing declaration becomes active/loaded and executes again on later reactivation. It is a persistent stored-property mutation, not an automatically reversible Style overlay.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Text and Children runtime content

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text and Children are distinct runtime surfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text is literal textual content. Assigning markup-looking characters to Text displays them as text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Children is structured CUI child content. Assigning to Children parses the value as a CUI child fragment under the host's allowed component/action capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assignment means Replace by default; Replace() is the explicit equivalent and Add() appends.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: txt.Text = "Hello";

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: txt.Text.Add(" world");

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: txt.Children = "<$Color:Green>Hello</$>";

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: txt.Children.Add("<Text>Another item</Text>");

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A failed dynamic Children parse/validation MUST leave the previous valid child tree intact and return a typed error.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Active, Hidden and Interactive

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Active, Hidden and Interactive are separate properties and MUST NOT be collapsed into one Avalonia visibility/enabled flag.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Active=True means the element/declaration participates in its normal active lifecycle/tree. Active=False deactivates/unloads it from normal layout/render/input participation while retaining enough object/state information for later reactivation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hidden=True suppresses visual rendering only. A hidden active object still occupies layout, retains state and can receive interaction/events when Interactive=True.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Interactive=False disables user-originated interaction/focus targeting while leaving the active object visible/layout-participating unless another property changes that.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All objects default to Active=True, Hidden=False and Interactive=True unless a Definition/Type/Theme explicitly defines another default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text::Txt Active="False">Hello</Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Txt.Active(true);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Active(false) is an effective participation gate and MUST NOT overwrite stored Hidden, Interactive or other properties. Reactivating restores those stored properties exactly. Property assignments made while inactive update stored state and become effective when reactivated.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Parent lifecycle and independent activation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal descendants inherit Active state from the nearest active parent. Effective Active is Self.Active AND parent EffectiveActive.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A leading ! or ActiveIndependently=True breaks only the parent-to-child Active dependency.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <!Style::PersistentStyle>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text ActiveIndependently="True">...</Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An independently active child/declaration is not forced inactive when its parent deactivates and must be deactivated separately. ! does not break Theme inheritance, symbol scope, Prefab ownership, variables, Groups, styling inheritance or event targeting.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For independently active visual descendants whose logical parent deactivates, the runtime preserves the required logical/positioning reference state without causing the inactive parent to re-enter ordinary sibling layout.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Lifecycle events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Initial activation generates Loaded. A False-to-True Active transition generates Loaded again. A True-to-False transition generates Deactivated. Event processing is typed and follows the ActionEvent rules below.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stateful/non-once events are temporary overlays for the event lifetime; Once-prefixed variants commit their property/action result as persistent state rather than reverting with event end. Once means committed/persistent, not 'execute only once ever'.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Layout property model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI's property catalogue MUST provide mature visual/layout coverage comparable in scope to broadly applicable CSS and Avalonia properties while retaining CUI's typed semantics. Layout is property-driven.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required layout/property families include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Width, Height, MinWidth, MaxWidth, MinHeight and MaxHeight.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Margin, Padding, CellMargin and CellGap.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: HorizontalAlignment, VerticalAlignment, wrapping/overflow and scrolling properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Grid Rows, Columns, RowSizes, ColumnSizes, Row, Column, RowSpan and ColumnSpan.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Absolute X/Y positioning and associated coordinate modes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typography, colour, background, borders, corner radii, opacity, clipping, transforms, shadows/effects and other applicable mature property families.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Numeric layout units MUST be typed. Bare fixed dimensions use CUI logical/DPI-aware pixels unless the property explicitly defines another unit. Auto, percentages and fractional/fill sizing are supported where meaningful.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ColumnSizes:1fr_2fr_200

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: RowSizes:Auto_1fr

heading: HEADING_2
text: Grid and stack behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Container Type:Grid performs row/column layout. Container Type:Vertical_Stack and Horizontal_Stack perform ordered stack layout. CellGap controls spacing between grid/stack cells/items; CellMargin controls the per-cell/item margin contribution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scrolling is orthogonal to layout Type and can be enabled independently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Container Type:Vertical_Stack Horizontal-Scrolling:True Vertical-Scrolling:True>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Invalid layout-property combinations MUST fail at compile time when statically knowable or return a typed runtime layout error when dynamically introduced.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Absolute positioning and coordinate system

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Container Type:Absolute enables free child positioning. Bare X and Y use CUI's proportional coordinate system by default and MAY be decimal values.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The centre of the positioning surface is (0,0). The normal horizontal range is -1000 at the left edge to +1000 at the right edge. The normal vertical range is -1000 at the bottom edge to +1000 at the top edge. Values outside the normal range are legal and place the reference point beyond the surface, which is useful for transitions/off-screen UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Container Type:Absolute>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text X:-500.5 Y:250.25>Hello</Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Container>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An axis may alternatively use X-px/Y-px for CUI logical pixels or X-%/Y-% for percentage positioning. Percentage 0 is left/bottom, 50 is centre and 100 is right/top. Coordinates in every mode MAY be decimals.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An element may define only one authoritative positioning mode per axis at a time. Supplying X and X-px together, for example, is an error.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Coordinate recalibration and inherited axes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: X-Inherited and Y-Inherited independently recalibrate descendant coordinate resolution to the declaring Container's bounds.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: X-Inherited=True makes that Container's left/right bounds the descendant -1000/+1000 X range and the corresponding percentage/pixel reference surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Y-Inherited=True makes that Container's bottom/top bounds the descendant -1000/+1000 Y range and the corresponding percentage/pixel reference surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The nearest applicable inherited axis scope wins. X and Y may therefore resolve against different ancestor Containers. Outside an Absolute/free-positioning context, free X/Y placement is invalid unless the owning specialised Type explicitly declares support.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Layering and rendering depth

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Layer is both a container element and an inheritable signed-integer property.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Layer Layer="1">...</Layer>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Layer:2>...</Layer>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text Layer="5">Hello</Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Higher Layer values render/hit-test above lower values; negative and positive values are valid. An element-level Layer overrides the parent layer and becomes the inherited layer for its normal descendants unless they override it again. Equal layers use normal tree/source order, with the later item above the earlier item where they overlap.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Layer controls depth only; it does not by itself imply modal behaviour or layout.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Modal behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Modal is a separate property. Modal=True traps applicable focus/input inside the modal subtree and blocks lower-layer interaction in the same render surface until dismissal. Nonmodal high-layer popups may sit above content without blocking unrelated lower-layer interaction outside their bounds.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Anchor and runtime placement

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Anchor is an optional named placement point, not a prerequisite for loading a Prefab or dynamically created UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Anchor::bob>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Runtime placement MUST support at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LoadAt(anchor) — place at an Anchor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LoadAt(x,y) — fixed proportional coordinates in the selected/current Absolute coordinate scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LoadAtPixels(x,y) and LoadAtPercent(x,y).

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LoadUnder(element), LoadAbove(element), LoadLeftOf(element) and LoadRightOf(element).

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LoadIn(grid,row,column, optional spans/alignment).

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LoadInto(container).

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Relative placement operations such as LoadUnder, LoadAbove, LoadAt(anchor) and LoadIn(grid,...) remain live placement relationships and track target movement/resizing. Raw coordinate placement is fixed in the chosen coordinate scope unless the caller changes it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When multiple Prefabs/UI instances are loaded at the same Anchor without another placement rule, they flow downward from that Anchor in load order. Raw repeated coordinate loads overlap unless another rule is supplied.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Style and property precedence

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effective presentation MUST resolve deterministically in the following order from lowest to highest precedence:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI built-in property default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Inherited Theme.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: element Type/(Definition) default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: explicit instance property.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: scoped <$Property> region.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: active Style/event overlay.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A direct runtime property assignment changes the stored explicit property value at its normal level; it is not an invisible new top-level precedence layer. If a temporary event Style currently overrides that property, the new stored value becomes visible when the temporary overlay ends.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Style rules and ActionEvent

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Action events use the long form <ActionEvent Type="..."> or & shorthand.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <&Hover>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <&Clicked>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <&PointerEnter>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <&PointerExit>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Inside a Style, an ActionEvent begins a rule and following property/action declarations belong to that event until the next ActionEvent or the end of the Style. A property declaration before any event is an unconditional Style property while that Style is active.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Style>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <&Hover{::button}>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$Color:Pink{::label}>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$Background:Black{::label}>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Style>

heading: HEADING_2
text: Event target syntax

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Curly braces declare an explicit target. {::foo} targets ID foo; {:::foo} targets Group foo. TargetID and TargetGroup are the verbose equivalent attributes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <&Hover{::greenText}>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <&Hover TargetID="greenText">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$Color:Pink{:::labels}>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$Color:Pink TargetGroup="labels">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When an event/property declaration is owned by an element/Style and no explicit target is provided, it targets the owning element/context according to that construct's standard rule.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Temporary versus Once events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stateful events such as Hover apply their associated Style overlay only while the state is active; ending Hover automatically reveals the previously effective values. OnceHover commits the resulting mutation so it remains after Hover ends.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The same temporary-versus-committed distinction applies to corresponding event families such as Clicked/OnceClick, Loaded/OnceLoaded and Deactivated/OnceDeactivated where meaningful. Once-prefixed events may execute on later qualifying occurrences; 'Once' denotes committed effect semantics, not a one-time lifetime subscription.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Event source, propagation and cancellation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Events target the actual originating element by default and do not automatically bubble through every parent. Bubble=True enables supported upward propagation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Event context MUST expose at least Event.Source, Event.Target, Event.Type and applicable Event.Value. For a Group trigger, Event.Source identifies the particular Group member that generated the event, enabling a single Group rule to affect only that member when desired.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Event.Cancel() cancels further compatible propagation/action when the event family permits cancellation.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Typed actions and asynchronous work

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ActionEvent MAY invoke a named typed application/domain action in addition to Style/property changes. UI actions MUST converge on the same domain operations used by the app's API/Automation surface where an equivalent operation exists; CUI MUST NOT become a parallel private business-logic layer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <&Clicked{::SaveButton} Action:SaveDocument>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Long-running/async actions MUST NOT block the UI thread and must expose typed running/completed/failed/cancelled state/events usable by CUI.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Input and two-way value flow

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Displaying a variable is one-way by default. Writable Input properties bind two-way by default when the source is writable and the conversion is valid.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Input Type:Text Value=<:Name:>>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Input Type:Checkbox Checked=<:Enabled:>>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Input Type:Slider Value=<:Volume:>>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: WriteBack=False disables automatic source update. A :static reference is snapshot-only and has no automatic write-back.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When typed conversion fails during input, the control retains the invalid entered representation and exposes validation error state; the source variable is not overwritten until conversion succeeds.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Conditional UI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI MUST provide structural conditional composition.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <If Condition=<:LoggedIn:>>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </If>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Else>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Else>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Condition is live by default. When the condition changes, the applicable branch is instantiated and the other branch is removed from the structural tree. A static condition reevaluates only on explicit containing-scope refresh.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structural removal is stronger than Active inheritance: an ActiveIndependently child cannot remain alive after the entire conditional branch that owns it ceases to exist.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Repeated UI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Repeat creates one generated UI instance per source item and MUST preserve item identity across live collection additions/removals/reordering.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Repeat Source=<:Users:> As:user Key=<:user.ID:>>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Text><:user.Name:></Text>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: </Repeat>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Key may be omitted only when each item exposes an unambiguous stable ID. A live Repeat without stable identity MUST fail rather than recreate items with ambiguous state transfer. The iteration variable exists only inside its Repeat instance.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Property catalogue and transform support

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The CUI property registry MUST include mature CSS/Avalonia-like visual properties and transforms rather than limiting authors to basic colours and dimensions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: At minimum, applicable registered properties include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rotate, Scale, ScaleX, ScaleY, Skew, SkewX, SkewY, Translate, TranslateX and TranslateY.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opacity, Background, Foreground/Color, Border, BorderColor, BorderWidth, CornerRadius, Shadow, Clip and Effect.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typography, text alignment/wrapping, layout sizing/alignment, scrolling, cursor/input/focus and accessibility properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Animation and animation-control properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Properties remain strongly typed. Unknown/incompatible property names or values are compiler errors when statically knowable.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Effect versus Background backdrop processing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effect and Background modifier chains have different targets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effect processes the element's own rendered appearance. Effect:Blur(1), for example, blurs that element.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background modifier chains process only the live rendered appearance of content behind the element as seen through the element's background region. They MUST NOT mutate, rotate, recolour, blur, move, restyle or otherwise change the actual underlying elements, their layout, hitboxes, state, events, Layer or accessibility tree.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Backdrop processing is live, not a captured fake snapshot. If content behind the background changes because of user interaction, variable updates, animation, video, scrolling, layout or any other render change, the appearance seen through the Background MUST update automatically without calling Refresh(). The compositor MAY cache safely but must invalidate affected backdrop dependencies correctly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A fully transparent background exposes the processed backdrop directly; a semi-transparent colour/material composites over the processed backdrop; a fully opaque result may make the backdrop invisible and may be optimised away when observationally equivalent.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Blur, Refract and chained backdrop modifiers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gaussian blur is built in.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effect:Blur(1)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background:Blur(1).Red

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Blur uses a ratio by default: Blur(1) is equivalent to Blur(100%), Blur(0.5) to Blur(50%). The renderer maps the public ratio to the platform blur implementation deterministically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Refract is a built-in live backdrop modifier that refracts/distorts content behind the Background, enabling liquid-glass-like materials.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background:Refract(1).Blur(1).Color(Green).Red

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Backdrop modifiers are evaluated left-to-right. Visual properties with a defined backdrop-rendering interpretation may participate as modifiers. For example:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background:Refract(1).Blur(1).Color(Green).Rotate(30deg).Red

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: In the example above, only the sampled live backdrop appearance inside the Background is refracted, blurred, colour-treated and rotated; the underlying elements themselves remain unchanged. A property with no meaningful/registered backdrop interpretation MUST produce a typed compiler/runtime error rather than being silently ignored.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Gradients

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gradient is a first-class property value/modifier.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gradient(Linear),Red(10%),Blue(20%),Green(70%)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gradient(Linear),Red,Blue,Green

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gradient(Linear).Red, Blue, Green

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Explicit stop percentages define stop positions. When stops omit positions, they are distributed evenly. Radial and other registered gradient forms are supported through the same Gradient(Type) model. Stop positions MUST be deterministic and validated; duplicate positions MAY be used for hard transitions where supported.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Animation and Keyframes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Animation is the canonical property used to apply a named animation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Button Animation:ShinyButton>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Named animations are declared using @ shorthand or Keyframe long form.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <@ShinyButton>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Keyframe Name="ShinyButton">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyframe positions may be percentages or absolute time in milliseconds.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <$1000> means 1000 milliseconds / one second. Explicit ms/s duration syntax is also supported. Percentage keyframes require a declared/inferable Animation duration; absolute-time keyframes may infer total duration from the greatest absolute keyframe when no longer Duration is declared.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyframe bodies contain ordinary typed property declarations. Animatable/interpolatable property types interpolate between frames; non-interpolatable properties switch at the relevant frame boundary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Animation control properties MUST cover at least Duration, Delay, Easing, Repeat/iteration, direction/playback and reduced-motion behaviour. The exact property registry is versioned with CUI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assigning/changing Animation while an element is active starts/restarts it according to its playback properties. An animation applied by a temporary Style follows that Style's lifetime unless its action explicitly commits/persists animation state.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Theme, Definition and property interaction

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Theme defaults, Type/Definition defaults, explicit properties, property regions, Styles, animations and runtime changes MUST all resolve through the same registered CUI property system. There MUST NOT be separate incompatible colour/layout/transform implementations for each syntax.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Theme changes at runtime MUST invalidate only affected presentation state and preserve canonical app/domain state.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Runtime loading and element methods

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Named/ID-addressable elements expose generated typed runtime handles. Runtime APIs MUST provide property mutation plus lifecycle/content operations including Active(...), Refresh(), Text/Children Replace/Add and placement/load functions where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Runtime calls and markup directives MUST converge on the same underlying CUI property/lifecycle/action operations so behaviour does not depend on how a mutation was initiated.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Imports and project file discovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The CUI toolchain automatically indexes supported local .cui, .cui-theme and .cui-prefab files within the declared project/source roots. External/shared packages use Import.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: <Import Source:"package/path">

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ambiguous symbols from multiple imports MUST fail until disambiguated, including by an explicit alias such as As:SharedUI. Circular Definition/Prefab import dependencies are rejected.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Accessibility, focus and keyboard semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI MUST make accessible behaviour the default. Interactive built-ins provide appropriate semantic roles, focusability and keyboard behaviour unless explicitly overridden for a valid reason.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Framework accessibility/focus properties include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AccessibleName and AccessibleDescription.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Role.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: TabIndex and Focusable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shortcut and focus-state presentation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Focus order follows semantic/tree/layout order unless explicitly overridden. Inactive elements cannot receive user focus. Hidden-but-interactive controls are technically representable under CUI's Hidden semantics, but first-party accessibility lint MUST reject invisible focusable/interactive constructs unless an explicit justified accessibility contract is supplied.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reduced motion, high contrast, scaling/zoom and non-colour-only state communication MUST be framework-level capabilities rather than app-specific reinventions.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Localisation and directionality

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI MUST support resource-backed/localisable user-visible strings, locale-aware number/date formatting and right-to-left directionality. Direction/layout mirroring is framework-managed where applicable. Literal developer/debug strings MAY remain literal; shipping product copy SHOULD use the localisation/resource system.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Security and dynamic CUI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: First-party compiled .cui, Plugin CUI and Generative UI are different trust classes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compiled first-party CUI may reference its declared application contracts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Plugin/external CUI surfaces execute inside their declared/authorised host capability environment and do not gain action permissions merely by rendering controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generative UI is structured data rendered through approved CUI components/actions and MUST NOT become arbitrary trusted .cui/C# execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dynamic Children strings are parsed as CUI only when the caller intentionally uses Children. User/external text should normally use Text or an explicit AddText-equivalent. Dynamic markup MUST be constrained to registered/authorised elements, properties, variables and actions of the current host.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Error boundaries and failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Static syntax/type/property/binding errors are build/compile errors with file, line and column diagnostics and, where safe, suggested corrections.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Runtime failures from dynamic CUI, plugin content, specialised Object hosts, data or async actions MUST be isolated at the nearest declared/default error boundary where feasible so one failed component does not unnecessarily destroy the entire window/application.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An invalid dynamic CUI update must preserve the last valid tree/content. Unknown incompatible compiled CUI/runtime versions fail with a structured compatibility error.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Hot reload and developer tooling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI tooling MUST include compiler/build integration, formatter, linter, hot reload, component/Prefab preview, semantic tree inspector, accessibility inspector, binding/variable dependency inspection, Theme/resource inspection and rendering/performance diagnostics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hot reload preserves the current valid runtime tree when edited CUI is invalid. Once valid again, compatible nodes are patched while preserving state by stable IDs where unambiguous. Definition/Theme/Prefab changes update compatible live instances without arbitrarily resetting unrelated runtime state.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Testing and semantic selectors

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI MUST expose a semantic test/accessibility tree so automated tests can locate elements by ID, role, accessible name and other stable semantic selectors rather than raw screen coordinates when semantic targeting exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The test harness MUST be able to render a CUI Page/Prefab at declared dimensions, Theme, scale, accessibility/reduced-motion settings and platform capability profile; interact through semantic input; inspect resulting state; and capture deterministic visual evidence where applicable.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Performance and rendering

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI MUST use Avalonia's mature low-level rendering/composition foundations while adding CUI-level invalidation, dependency and component semantics without introducing unnecessary full-tree work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live variable changes invalidate only dependent expressions/properties/subtrees.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Virtualisable lists/grids/trees MUST use framework virtualisation rather than constructing every off-screen item by default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Backdrop Blur/Refract/Gradient processing MAY use compositor caching, but cache invalidation MUST remain live and correct when sampled content changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Animation/input loops MUST avoid blocking application/domain work on the UI thread.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Caches must be bounded and revision/dependency invalidated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Performance acceptance requires measured evidence on the declared supported-hardware/platform baseline. 'Looks fast' is not sufficient.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Platform and Home runtime integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native CUI applications depend on the compatible Home-managed CUI/shared runtime under the global Home runtime-dependency contract. The CUI compiler/toolchain belongs to the development/build environment; the runtime version/capability requirement is recorded in app/package metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web CUI MAY use a browser-specific implementation/runtime, but it MUST preserve the same public CUI semantics, component contracts, state identities and supported action/property behaviour except for explicitly declared platform capability differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Platform differences such as unsupported backdrop effects, specialised renderer capabilities or input hardware MUST be capability-negotiated explicitly. The runtime MUST NOT silently reinterpret unsupported CUI into materially different behaviour.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Language/runtime versioning

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compiled CUI output MUST record at least CUI language version, CUI runtime ABI/component-registry version and required capability set. Breaking language/runtime changes require migration tooling or explicit compatibility handling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom distributed Themes/Prefabs/packages SHOULD carry their own version/dependency metadata. Missing/incompatible package versions surface as structured build/runtime dependency errors.

heading: HEADING_2
text: CUI compiler pipeline

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical pipeline is parse -> shorthand normalization -> symbol/import resolution -> Definition/Prefab/Theme expansion metadata -> typed property/variable/action validation -> accessibility/static lint -> dependency graph generation -> compiled CUI representation/source maps -> runtime binding.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The compiler MUST NOT silently accept unknown attributes/tags/types/events/properties. Typographical mistakes such as Type:Vertcal_Stack SHOULD produce an unknown-symbol error with an unambiguous suggestion such as Vertical Stack when available.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Acceptance criteria

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI is implementation-complete only when real compiled/runtime behaviour proves the agreed language and framework semantics. Source presence, parsing a toy file or rendering a static Button is insufficient.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Release validation MUST demonstrate at minimum:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A real app surface authored only in .cui with .axaml/.hui rejected as app markup while using the pinned Avalonia fork underneath.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Fixed core elements, Container Grid/Vertical Stack/Horizontal Stack/Absolute Types, scrolling and mature layout properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Colon attribute shorthand, underscore-to-space shorthand, comments, strict ambiguity detection and explicit quoted disambiguation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: (Definition) custom elements and Types plus built-in/custom inherited Themes including Professional, Glow, Playful, Bubble and Cinematic.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Static and dynamic Prefabs loaded in multiple hosts, proving shared versus per-instance internal state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live/default and static variable references, typed conversion forms and Live(x,y) dependency relationships without per-frame polling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ID/Name aliases, :: ID shorthand, ::: Group shorthand, scoped Prefab IDs/Groups and deterministic cross-scope access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Property long form, $ shorthand, property IDs/Groups, inferred single-property Group mutation and mandatory explicit property selection for multi-property Groups.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text versus Children semantics, Replace/Add and rollback on invalid dynamic child markup.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Active, Hidden, Interactive and !/ActiveIndependently lifecycle semantics including restoration of stored state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Layer tag/property with positive/negative values, element override, same-layer ordering and separate Modal behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Absolute decimal ratio coordinates, x/y pixel and percent modes, X-Inherited/Y-Inherited recalibration and nested independent axis scopes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prefab/UI placement at Anchor, raw coordinates, pixels, percentages, above/below/left/right of elements and Grid positions, including live relative tracking.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Style rules with Hover/OnceHover, Clicked/OnceClick, Loaded/OnceLoaded and Deactivated/OnceDeactivated plus TargetID/TargetGroup and {::}/{:::} shorthand.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Event.Source for Group triggers, opt-in bubbling/cancellation and typed async action invocation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: HEADING_1
text: Apps

heading: HEADING_2
text: Home runtime dependency

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every installable/native 9to1 app has a hard runtime dependency on 9-1 Home. Before initialising the app’s normal UI or opening user artifacts, the app MUST complete a local Home availability/version handshake against the Home-managed shared services it requires.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If Home is not installed, the app MUST refuse normal startup and display only a minimal bootstrap surface explaining that 9-1 Home is required. The bootstrap surface MUST provide an Install Home action that opens/starts the trusted Home installation flow. It MUST NOT create or mutate normal app data while Home is absent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If Home is installed but the required shared service/API version is missing, incompatible or damaged, the app MUST refuse unsafe normal startup and offer the appropriate Home update/repair flow with a structured reason. Apps MUST NOT silently launch private replacement services to bypass the missing Home dependency.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: This local-install dependency applies to native/installable clients. Browser-hosted web surfaces cannot require a local Home installation; they instead use the corresponding authenticated 9to1 shared web services and capability negotiation defined for web clients.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns shared platform services including the permission broker, shared Dulche broker/runtime coordination, package/update metadata and the Shared Productivity Engine defined in the Home section.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Persistent contextual AI bar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every interactive 9to1 app MUST expose the shared persistent floating contextual AI bar at the bottom of its primary content surface. The bar uses Dulche plus the owning app's authorised semantic state. It MUST be able to inspect the current artifact/surface semantically and, when permitted, edit it through the owning app's typed APIs. The bar is not limited to whatever pixels happen to be visible in the viewport.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The shared bar MUST expose an explicit persistent AI access-mode switcher with at least Read-only and Write mode. The current mode MUST remain visible enough that the user can tell whether Dulche may only inspect the surface or may also request mutations. This switcher is a platform-wide interaction contract used consistently by Write, Present, Boards, Files, Canvas, Data, Mail, Planner and every other surface that hosts the shared bar.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: In Read-only mode, Dulche MAY read, search, compare, reason over, summarise, explain and navigate the full authorised semantic surface, including off-screen content that the owning app exposes. It MAY generate proposed changes in conversation, but MUST NOT mutate the owning artifact, structure or app state. Read-only access does not imply permission to inspect data outside the caller's normal authorisation boundary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: In Write mode, Dulche receives the same semantic read context plus the owning app's permitted typed mutation actions. Write mode is capability to request/perform edits, not permission to bypass app state, trust, confirmation, review, external-side-effect or security rules. Mutations MUST use stable semantic identities such as ArtifactID, PageID, SectionID, ObjectID, row/range/entity IDs or equivalent domain identifiers and the owning app's normal revision/conflict semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The AI-bar mode is separate from the host app's own Edit/View/Suggest/Locked/Unlocked or equivalent state. For example, an AI bar in Write mode does not silently bypass a Board that is currently in View mode, and a Write document in Suggest mode represents permitted AI edits as suggestions rather than accepted direct edits. Host-surface rules may narrow the effective mutation set further.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Apps MUST provide a permission-filtered semantic context snapshot including the active artifact/page/entity, current selection, relevant stable object IDs, structure necessary to understand the task, current revision/state and supported typed actions. The bar MUST prefer this semantic context over screenshot/OCR/pixel interpretation and MUST NOT substitute raw mouse/keyboard/desktop automation when typed context/actions exist.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The AI bar MUST remain visually separate from document/page content and MUST NOT change the underlying artifact layout merely by being shown. It MAY collapse to a compact state but MUST remain directly reachable without navigating to a separate AI page. Read/Write mode changes the AI's effective capability only; it does not create a second copy of the current artifact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Surface-specific mutation protections MAY be stricter than the shared Write-mode baseline and cannot be weakened by AI mode or trust state. Data is the mandatory example: every AI-requested Data mutation requires explicit approval for that specific action even while the bar is in Write mode. When the target is a live database, Data MUST additionally show a meaningful preview/diff, validate the operation and create a recoverable backup/snapshot/checkpoint before execution. If the required live-database backup cannot be created, the mutation MUST NOT proceed as though rollback exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For Data live-database changes, the approval surface SHOULD identify the intended operation, affected tables/entities/rows where knowable, schema/dependency impact, external side effects and backup identity. Execution MUST occur only after approval, then verify the actual result and preserve rollback/recovery information. Prior approval, Accept and Trust or Always Trust MUST NOT suppress this Data-specific per-action approval invariant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Equivalent bar actions MUST behave consistently across product surfaces, while menus and available operations remain context-sensitive to the owning app. Unsupported or inapplicable actions MUST not be exposed merely to make the bar look feature-complete.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

These buttons must not appear in compact/mini mode, even when the compact/mini chat bar is focused.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Cross-app invocation and compose contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every interactive 9to1 app that hosts the shared persistent AI bar MUST use Home's canonical compose invocation component and cross-app dispatcher. Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents, Files and the reserved @Computer Use capability MUST therefore resolve consistently across apps rather than each product implementing a private @ syntax or resource picker.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A model may cross an app boundary only when that action is authorised by user intent: explicit @ invocation, an explicit instruction naming the target capability/app, or an unambiguous requested outcome whose canonical owner is another 9to1 app. Implied intent is semantic, not opportunistic; unrelated app access remains out of scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When a target 9to1 app owns the requested artifact/action, the originating model MUST use the target app's typed API/shared semantic action contract and MAY ask Home to launch/reveal the target app so the user can observe progress. For example, a request to create a presentation routes to Present and creates/edits a canonical Present artifact rather than fabricating a slide-like object in the originating app.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Computer Use MUST NOT be selected automatically as a fallback when typed app execution is unavailable, inconvenient or fails. It is usable only after explicit @Computer Use invocation and remains subject to the Computer Use eligibility, permission, game-exclusion and Autoreview rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model-driven typed edits MAY be visualised in the target app with live object motion, selection highlights, text insertion and a synthetic/virtual cursor. This visualisation is not evidence that Dulche is literally controlling the pointer; the typed action/result remains authoritative and the synthetic cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's actual input cursor.

It appears when the app is opened without an existing artifact/session to restore, and whenever the user deliberately returns to the app’s Home/start surface.

HEADING_1
text: Web Apps

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cakemods.com MUST host a web version of every 9-1 Workspace/AI product that is not explicitly listed as web-exempt. Web surfaces MUST share the same CAKE ID identity, canonical artifact formats, domain APIs, permission model and underlying server-side entities as desktop equivalents. Browser-specific UI/layout MAY differ, but it MUST NOT create a separate incompatible product model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The default rule is to provide a web version whenever the product’s core value can sensibly work in a browser. Browser-specific capability limits are acceptable when they are explicit and the useful core product remains intact; a single desktop-only feature is not by itself a reason to omit an otherwise useful web app.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web exemption is permitted only when the product’s core function requires infrastructure, privileged device access or hosted compute that CAKE does not currently provide. Each exemption MUST state the blocking capability/infrastructure. Exemptions MUST be re-evaluated when that blocker is removed; exemption is not a permanent product classification.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
TITLE
text: Accounts & Subscription

heading: HEADING_1
text: CAKE ID and authentication

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CAKE ID is the shared identity used across CAKE and 9to1. A normal CAKE ID is separate from a WordPress user account; WordPress may remain linked for site administration, but ordinary 9to1 users must not need WordPress accounts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 web apps authenticate against CAKEMODS/CAKE ID using a browser-based OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE or an equivalent secure public-client flow. Desktop, web and open-source/custom clients are treated as untrusted public clients: they receive short-lived user access tokens and never contain provider keys, billing secrets or entitlement-signing secrets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The server is authoritative for account state, sessions, entitlements, organisation policy, Dust, storage/site quotas, billing and provider credentials. A modified or self-built client can change its own interface or features but cannot grant itself paid entitlements, bypass quotas or mint trusted usage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Authentication/session operations must support account sign-in/sign-out, current-user/profile lookup, active-session/device inspection and revocation. Sensitive account or billing changes use trusted CAKEMODS web flows rather than accepting raw payment credentials through the open-source client.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: Profiles — customisation and Jacob's reserved account

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Profile customisation MUST include changing the display name and username through the profile/account UI and equivalent authorised APIs. Username availability, uniqueness and reservation checks MUST apply consistently across UI, APIs, registration and rename flows. Changes MUST preserve the canonical CAKE ID/UserID, ownership, history, permissions and entitlements; mutable names MUST NOT become identity or authorisation keys.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The exact handle @CroakyJake MUST be reserved exclusively for Jacob. Registration and rename flows MUST prevent other accounts from claiming it, including case variants that would bypass the reservation. The reservation MUST be bound through trusted provisioning to Jacob's verified canonical account ID, not awarded to whichever account first requests that text. Production identifiers MUST be verified rather than guessed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Jacob's verified account MUST automatically receive all Business features free of charge, including subsequently added Business features, without requiring a paid Business subscription. This is an account-bound entitlement: changing a display name or username MUST NOT grant it to another person or remove it from Jacob. Reservation and entitlement administration MUST be privileged, auditable operations, separate from ordinary profile editing. Free Business access does not bypass security permissions or authorise third-party spending.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Profile customisation — required and optional fields

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The profile editor MUST include the following fields. An asterisk (*) denotes a required field; only Name and Username are required within this field set.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Name* — REQUIRED. The user's profile/display name, extending the existing display-name customisation requirement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Username* — REQUIRED. The user's account handle, subject to the existing availability, uniqueness and reservation rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Icon — OPTIONAL. The user's profile icon, which the user can add, change or remove.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pronouns — OPTIONAL. User-provided pronouns, which the user can add, change or clear.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Job — OPTIONAL. The user's job/job title. This field is especially relevant in a Business context but MUST also be available to ordinary personal users; it MUST NOT be Business-only or mandatory for Business users.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The UI MUST visibly mark Name and Username with an asterisk and explain that * denotes required. Icon, Pronouns and Job MUST be allowed to remain unset and to be cleared without preventing an otherwise valid profile from being saved. Name and Username MUST NOT be saved as empty or whitespace-only values. Optional personal information MUST NOT be inferred or populated without the user's input.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The equivalent authorised profile APIs MUST expose the same five fields and apply the same required/optional validation rules. Partial updates MUST preserve fields omitted from the request rather than clearing them. Existing canonical account identity, ownership, permissions, username reservation and account-bound Business entitlement requirements remain unchanged, including Jacob's reserved @CroakyJake handle and free Business features.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Acceptance MUST verify that a profile can be saved with valid Name and Username while Icon, Pronouns and Job are unset; all three optional fields can subsequently be added, changed and cleared; Job is available to both personal and Business users without becoming required; blank required fields produce validation errors; and equivalent authorised API operations preserve the same behaviour and account identity.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Profile API, provisioning and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extend the existing account/profile APIs for profile reads and partial updates, icon management and username availability. Reservation and account-bound Business-entitlement provisioning MUST remain privileged, auditable operations. APIs MUST expose the same validation as the UI, preserve omitted fields and return structured conflicts or validation failures. Ordinary clients MUST NOT self-grant Business access. Test rename without identity or ownership loss, rejected unauthorised @CroakyJake claims and case variants, and automatic free Business access for Jacob’s verified account only; security permissions and third-party spending approvals still apply.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: Subscription model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 uses a preset-first subscription model with optional customisation. Subscription state has two separate dimensions: price-threshold entitlements and resource configuration. The two MUST be stored and evaluated independently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Price-threshold entitlements determine which feature/model/site capabilities the account unlocks as its canonical configured monthly price crosses defined thresholds. Resource configuration determines the account’s allocated quantities, including AI Dust, storage, hosted-site capacity and other metered resources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Named plans Free, Boost, Plus, Pro, Ultra, Ultra+ and Max serve both as threshold names and as preset configuration names. Their canonical ascending PlanLevel order is Free = 0, Boost = 1, Plus = 2, Pro = 3, Ultra = 4, Ultra+ = 5 and Max = 6. APIs, billing logic and entitlement checks MUST use stable PlanID/PlanLevel rather than inferring ordering from display names. A preset is a convenience starting configuration; the preset label MUST NOT be treated as the sole source of entitlement truth.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Local models and core local tools are not metered through cloud AI Dust. The Free configuration MUST retain useful local/core functionality while cloud AI, hosted storage/sites and other server-funded resources remain subject to server-authoritative entitlements and quotas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Price thresholds

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Let EntitlementPriceMonthly be the canonical monthly price assigned by the subscription backend to the account’s current configuration. The backend MUST compute effective threshold entitlements from this value; clients MUST NOT infer them from the displayed preset name.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Thresholds are cumulative. For every threshold T where EntitlementPriceMonthly >= T.Price, all entitlements defined by T are added to the account’s effective entitlement set. Therefore a Max-priced configuration also receives all lower-threshold grants, including Ultra grants, unless a future threshold explicitly defines a non-cumulative exception.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selecting a preset does not bypass threshold evaluation. If a user customises a preset and the resulting configured price crosses a different threshold, the backend MUST recalculate the effective threshold set from the resulting EntitlementPriceMonthly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The currently defined commercial thresholds are:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Free — £0/month. Unlocks access to select free cloud models and unlimited local/core tools.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boost — £7.99/month. Entry paid cloud-AI tier. It unlocks CAKE-funded cloud models within the Boost model-cost band, benchmarked against Luna-class pricing rather than tied to one specific named model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Plus — £19.99/month. Adds a materially larger cloud-AI/resource allowance than Boost while retaining access to the Boost model-cost band and any other models priced within that effective band. Plus exists as the regular-use tier between Boost and Pro.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pro — £34.99/month. Adds a higher CAKE-funded model-cost band benchmarked against Sol-class pricing, while retaining all lower-band model access. Pro also permits materially higher cloud-AI, storage and hosted-site allocations than Plus.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ultra — £69.99/month. Adds the highest standard CAKE-funded model-cost band, benchmarked against Astra-class pricing, while retaining all lower-band model access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ultra+ — £99.99/month. Retains at least the complete Ultra model-access set and enables materially larger cloud-AI, storage, hosted-site and concurrency allocations than Ultra.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Max — £149.99/month. Retains at least the complete Ultra+ model-access set and enables the highest standard preset cloud-AI, storage, hosted-site and concurrency allocations. Because thresholds are cumulative, Max-priced configurations retain every lower-threshold entitlement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cloud model entitlement MUST be expressed through versioned effective model-cost/capability bands rather than a permanent allow-list of model brand names. References such as Luna-class, Sol-class and Astra-class are pricing/capability benchmarks for the current commercial design, not exclusive model identities. Any CAKE-funded model whose effective provider cost and capability profile fit within the user's unlocked band may be made available, subject to provider availability, safety/privacy policy and backend configuration. Replacing a benchmark model with another comparably priced model MUST NOT require renaming the subscription tier.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: OPEN: the backend still needs one canonical rule defining how temporary discounts, promotional credits, tax and non-monthly billing cadence affect EntitlementPriceMonthly. Until that rule is defined, threshold eligibility MUST be calculated only by the server and MUST NOT be reproduced locally by clients.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Preset configurations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Free, Boost, Plus, Pro, Ultra, Ultra+ and Max also exist as pre-made subscription configurations. A preset MUST define explicit resource values such as allocated AI Dust, storage allocation, hosted-site limits, concurrency/burst limits where applicable and any other metered resources supported by the subscription system.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preset configuration and threshold entitlement state MUST remain separate server-side fields. Changing resource values MAY change the configured monthly price and therefore the unlocked threshold set, but MUST NOT mutate the canonical definition of the source preset.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A customised plan MUST retain the concrete resource values selected by the user even when those values no longer match any named preset. The UI MAY display the source preset for context, but APIs MUST return the actual resource configuration rather than reconstructing it from a tier name.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preset definitions MUST be versioned. Existing accounts MUST retain an auditable reference to the preset version they originally selected plus subsequent customisation state. Updating a preset definition MUST NOT silently rewrite existing subscriber allocations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Known preset requirements are now: Boost is £7.99/month with light cloud-AI usage, small hosted storage, a maximum of 1 full hosted site and 3 single-page sites; Plus is £19.99/month with materially higher cloud-AI usage and storage, a maximum of 3 full hosted sites and 5 single-page sites. Pro (£34.99), Ultra (£69.99), Ultra+ (£99.99) and Max (£149.99) MUST each provide materially more included cloud-AI usage, storage and hosted-site capacity than the preceding paid preset. Exact AI Dust/storage/site quantities above Plus are not yet fully specified and MUST NOT be invented.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Canonical subscription state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The server-authoritative subscription object MUST expose at least the following fields:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PresetID? — stable identifier of the preset used as the starting configuration, or null when no preset applies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PresetVersion? — version of the referenced preset, or null when no preset applies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: IsCustomised — true when the current resource configuration differs from the referenced preset/version.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: EntitlementPriceMonthly — canonical monthly price used for threshold evaluation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: EffectiveThresholds — ordered list/set of all currently unlocked thresholds.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: EffectiveEntitlements — resolved feature/model/site entitlements after threshold, account and organisation-policy evaluation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AIDustAllocated — allocated cloud-AI Dust for the current billing/configuration period.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: StorageAllocatedBytes — storage allocation in bytes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: HostedSiteLimit — concurrent/full hosted-site allowance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SinglePageSiteLimit — additional single-page-site allowance after threshold/resource evaluation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AdditionalResources — versioned typed object/map for future metered resources. Clients MUST ignore unknown keys they do not understand while preserving them when round-tripping configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Free hosted-site inactivity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For a Free hosted site, inactivity takes the site offline rather than deleting it. During the first 120 days the account MUST sign in at least once every 30 days to keep the free site online. After that period, the current rule requires at least one account sign-in per year. Taking a site offline MUST NOT delete its stored site data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Business add-ons — pricing, seats and resource billing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Business costs an additional USD $5 per month per organisation and supports a maximum of 50 seats. Business + costs an additional USD $15 per month per organisation and has no subscription seat cap. Neither add-on has a separate per-seat fee. Purchased AI usage/credits, storage and other funded resources remain separately configured and may be pooled or allocated individually; unlimited seats do not mean unlimited resources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Both add-ons include 9to1 Admin and the functional Business capabilities specified below. Business + includes the Business capability set; further exclusive Business + capabilities are OPEN and MUST NOT be invented from its name. Pricing displays, quotes, invoices and entitlement APIs MUST distinguish the organisation add-on, seat capacity and resource charges. A base-resource quote in another currency MUST NOT be silently relabelled as USD; the trusted billing quote must make currency/conversion explicit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Billing state MUST store AddOnID, add-on definition version, OrgID, seat-limit value or explicit Unlimited, effective dates and applicable account-bound grants separately from user resource configurations. No client-supplied role, username or plan label can self-grant Business. The free Business entitlement for Jacob remains governed by the Profiles subsection and does not authorise paid resource purchases or third-party spending.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing Business + to Business with more than 50 active members MUST require a seat-remediation preview or retain a visibly constrained pending-downgrade state; it must not silently remove users or delete shared content. Add-on cancellation and billing failure MUST have explicit entitlement/recovery states. Account-level billing, export and recovery remain available through appropriate authorised routes even when normal Business editing is unavailable. Exact grace periods, proration and suspended/pending-seat accounting remain OPEN unless defined in the canonical billing policy.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Entitlements and usage API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The subscription/account layer must expose supported first-party APIs for the information and actions available to the user, following the global API-parity rule. The core surface includes:

text: 9to1.Subscription.GetPlan();
