heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Billing-changing calls do not accept raw payment-card details. OpenCheckout/OpenManage hand off to an authenticated trusted CAKEMODS billing flow. Read APIs return the server-authoritative account state rather than trusting client-maintained counters.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Server-authoritative enforcement

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All paid/cloud usage is enforced server-side. The open-source client is never the authority for remaining Dust, model access, storage, site count, billing state or quotas. Custom/forked clients use the same live account entitlements and cannot bypass limits by changing local code.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For cloud AI, the trusted gateway checks identity, organisation policy where applicable, model entitlement, hard limits and Dust before execution. Usage follows a reserve → run → settle model so concurrent requests cannot overspend the same balance. Provider keys and commercial billing logic remain server-side.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Short-lived or one-time signed capability tokens may be used internally for narrowly scoped operations, but they do not become reusable secrets embedded in applications. Server-side storage/site operations perform the same authoritative entitlement checks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Personal API access

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accounts with at least 80,000 allocated AI Dust unlock Personal API access. Personal API usage consumes the same account Dust allowance as normal 9to1 cloud-AI usage; it is not a separate unlimited pool.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Personal API access is for the account holder’s own external integrations and workflows. It is not a public-facing resale allowance and does not grant permission to redistribute CAKE provider credentials or resell the underlying service.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: Web subscription behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web and desktop clients MUST resolve account state from the same CAKE ID and entitlement service. For the same account and organisation context, plan identity, Dust balance, hosted-storage usage, site quota/usage and applicable feature entitlements MUST be consistent across official clients, subject only to explicitly documented platform capability differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a future web feature requires material hosted compute that is not available on the free/local product - for example hosted Mini Computer virtual machines - it may be offered as a subscription-backed server capability with explicit resource limits. The browser UI must never pretend that local-only or unavailable server compute exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: Business features — functional specification

heading: HEADING_2
text: BIZ-01 — Organisation boundary and shared state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Business is an organisation collaboration and management capability set, not merely labels on pricing cards. It comprises Team Space and an organisation drive; organisation Connect; cross-account device Mesh; pooled or individually partitioned usage; team-wide Agents; and device-level policy controls for managed 9to1-OS Business accounts. 9to1 Admin supplies their management interface, while the existing apps retain canonical ownership of their domain data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every organisation-scoped operation MUST carry an explicit OrgID and authenticated membership/delegation context. Personal and organisation work remain separately identifiable in switchers, search, storage, AI context and billing. Joining an organisation MUST NOT merge personal files, chats, memories, devices or credentials into it. Moving/sharing personal material requires a deliberate authorised operation with destination ownership, access and billing impact shown. Leaving one organisation cannot revoke or destroy unrelated personal work or membership elsewhere.

heading: HEADING_2
text: BIZ-02 — Team Space and organisation drive

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each organisation MUST support a canonical shared Team Space backed by organisation-owned shared storage, not an independent copy of every member’s files. Space membership, role/group access, instructions, permitted models/tools and shared Agent bindings are managed through the existing Spaces model. Files, Pages, Boards and other app artifacts retain stable canonical IDs and their owning formats; references/embeds do not create silent forks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The organisation drive MUST support folders, create/upload/open/edit where the owning app supports it, search, move/rename, version history, sharing/access review, archive/delete/recover and authorised export. Access may be assigned to organisation roles/groups or explicitly scoped members. Effective object access is checked by storage, search/indexing, previews, AI retrieval and exports, not just the Files UI. External sharing requires policy permission and explicit recipient/link scope; revocation must remove future server access and invalidate applicable derived access paths.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared-storage accounting MUST identify the owning organisation and charge canonical stored data once according to the storage policy rather than once per viewer. Access removal preserves organisation-owned artifacts and transfers responsibilities where necessary; it does not give administrators ownership of a departed member’s unrelated personal files. Restore/export workflows retain identity and permissions deliberately rather than accidentally republishing private content.

heading: HEADING_2
text: BIZ-03 — Organisation Connect

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST provide an organisation directory and scoped organisational groups/channels and contact endpoints, with role-controlled membership, creation and management. Where shared business identities or communication endpoints are configured, delegates act through named authorised roles with auditable attribution, not password sharing or undetectable impersonation. Inviting an external correspondent to communicate is distinct from making them an organisation seat or allocating paid usage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Organisation communications MUST use Connect’s canonical conversations, contacts, calls and message identities. Agent email/call/text endpoints resolve to the same canonical team Agent and its permissions. External providers and device-backed transports require actual supported connections and credentials; provisioning paid endpoints needs separate approval. Membership or admin status does not create blanket permission to read private/E2EE content, export it to a model or bypass participant consent and retention controls.

heading: HEADING_2
text: BIZ-04 — Cross-account device Mesh

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Business Mesh MUST allow explicitly authorised devices belonging to different organisation members to share supported compute/storage capabilities through Home/Mesh. Enrolment records MUST bind DeviceID, device/account owner, OrgID, verified trust/key material reference, supported capabilities, resource limits and grant expiry/revocation state. Organisation membership alone must not automatically pair a personal device or expose its files, GPU or network.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A resource grant MUST specify permitted consumers/workloads, CPU/GPU/memory/storage/concurrency budgets and permitted data locations. Job admission checks both requester permissions and the contributing device’s current policy. Data/secrets are scoped to the job and authorised endpoint; device contribution does not grant unrelated file, screen, microphone or personal-session access. Sensitive/local-only work cannot silently migrate to a different member’s device or a cloud provider without an authorised processing route.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mesh MUST expose availability, queued/running jobs, utilisation, failure and cancellation/revocation outcomes. Revocation blocks new work and cancels or safely terminates existing work where supported; it must not claim to undo already completed actions or erase copies outside its actual control. A disconnected device remains unavailable/pending, never fictitiously running a workload. Windows and 9to1-OS expose only supported native capabilities; web can manage grants and observe jobs without pretending to supply privileged local resources.

heading: HEADING_2
text: BIZ-05 — Shared and individual usage pools

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An organisation MUST be able to use a shared funded AI/resource pool or individually partition its purchased allocation by member/role. Partitioning is accounting over the same authoritative ledger, not duplicate credits. Store PoolID, source allocation, period, remaining/reserved/settled amounts, allocation owner and applicable policy. Member views show their effective allowance; authorised administrators can inspect aggregate and scoped consumption without exposing private work content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Requests reserve capacity before execution and settle actual usage afterwards, releasing unused reservation according to the backend contract. The organisation total, individual ceiling and role ceiling all apply where configured. Parallel requests, retries and delayed provider reports MUST NOT spend the same balance twice. Changing pool mode preserves in-flight reservations and history and requires a validated allocation plan; insufficient funds or ambiguous settlement blocks unsafe transfer rather than inventing capacity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Role-based rollover permission defined in Admin MUST be applied to eligible credit lots at rollover/expiry transitions and be visible in member balances. Changes preserve original lot provenance and settled charges. The product MUST distinguish rolled-over credits from newly purchased allocation and show the effective expiry. No personal balance is swept into an organisation pool merely because its owner joins; no organisation-funded balance becomes a departed member’s personal credit without an explicit supported transfer policy.

heading: HEADING_2
text: BIZ-06 — Team-wide Agents

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A team Agent is a canonical Dulche Agent with organisation ownership/scope and configurable discovery, invocation, authoring and administration grants. Eligible members MUST be able to discover and invoke it from supported Spaces/app pickers and configured Connect channels without creating separate private copies. Shared configuration and approved knowledge are distinct from per-user conversations and private memories; access to one member’s context cannot leak into another member’s response.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent publishing/versioning, ownership transfer, required Plugins, allowed models, tool scopes, approval boundaries, schedules, budgets and concurrency limits MUST be enforced by Dulche/Home and the owning services. An Agent cannot use its owner’s wider authority to bypass the requesting member’s restrictions unless an explicit, separately authorised delegated service capability covers that operation. Persistent scheduled work records the service principal, scope and funding source and is re-evaluated on role, policy or membership changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pausing, revoking or archiving a team Agent MUST stop new authorised dispatch, preserve auditable run history and report what happened to queued/running work. Sensitive credentials remain secure references; publishing an Agent is not permission to reveal them. AI Studio, Admin and runtime surfaces all edit or reference the same Agent identity and versioned definition.

heading: HEADING_2
text: BIZ-07 — Managed 9to1-OS accounts and device policy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Business MUST provide device-level administrative controls for explicitly enrolled managed 9to1-OS Business accounts. Controls MUST cover supported app/package and Plugin installation/enablement restrictions, allowed features and Automations, required organisation/role Plugins, enforced settings, default-model/routing policy and Mesh-resource participation. Existing compatibility-framework and privileged-operation restrictions continue to apply beneath every launch surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The OS policy agent MUST verify policy origin/version, apply only the enrolled managed scope and report Applied, Pending, Failed, Unsupported or NonCompliant status with reasons. Local UI changes, direct API calls and alternate launch paths cannot bypass enforced settings. Offline endpoints retain their last valid policy and cannot claim a newly published policy was applied without acknowledgement. Revocation and next-contact reconciliation must be explicit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Managed account policy is not automatic whole-device ownership. Personal users, personal artifacts and unenrolled devices remain outside the organisation’s authority. Destructive remote actions, full-device wipe, arbitrary privileged shell access and surveillance are not implicitly authorised by Business. Other operating systems may expose supported Mesh and app policy, but they must not claim complete 9to1-OS endpoint-management parity without an explicit capability implementation.

heading: HEADING_2
text: BIZ-08 — Cross-app enforcement and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permissions, policy, membership and credit changes MUST propagate through supported authoritative services and invalidate affected cached grants before further protected server actions. Published configuration, delivered configuration and acknowledged enforcement remain different states. Long-running rollout, export and reassignment use resumable jobs with per-target results. Downgrade, service outage or partial rollout must preserve data and fail closed for newly unauthorised actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Acceptance MUST demonstrate a shared artifact edited through two apps without forking; denied access absent from search, preview and AI context; organisation Connect without access to personal messages; explicit two-account Mesh enrolment, bounded execution and revocation; shared-pool concurrency and individual ceilings; role-dependent rollover; a team Agent that cannot leak another member’s private context; and OS restrictions enforced below UI across restart/offline/reconnect. Each feature requires equivalent authorised API coverage, persistence, accessibility, failure/recovery and actual end-to-end evidence. Inclusion on a pricing card alone is not conformance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
TITLE
text: Apps

heading: HEADING_1
text: Workspace Apps

heading: HEADING_2
text: Home

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and ownership

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Home is the mandatory native ecosystem hub, platform shell and control plane for installed 9to1 applications. It is not merely a dashboard application. Home owns shared platform services that must have one canonical implementation across the ecosystem: app/package management, the Home Core service registry, shared Dulche lifecycle/broker coordination, permission/trust brokerage, account/subscription state, the Shared Productivity Engine, shared model/provider configuration, Action Graph rendering, Mesh coordination, notifications, shared search/index coordination and ecosystem-wide settings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other apps MUST consume Home-owned shared services through supported authenticated interfaces and MUST NOT silently launch incompatible private replacements when a Home service is unavailable. App-owned documents, projects and domain data remain owned by their respective apps/storage layers; Home MUST NOT become the only canonical copy of another app’s artifacts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home installation includes the Home Core background service/runtime required by native apps plus the Home user-facing CUI shell. Native apps require a compatible Home installation/Home Core service, but the visible Home window does not need to remain open while other apps run. On 9to1-OS, Home Core may be integrated as a system component while preserving the same service contracts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Home shell and navigation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Home shell MUST be dashboard/home-oriented rather than primarily a conventional settings application. Its stable primary navigation MUST provide at least Home/Dashboard, Apps, Library, Events, Discover, Mesh and Settings. Account/profile controls MAY live in persistent shell chrome. Chat remains a Spaces destination and MUST NOT become Home’s primary landing surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Navigation destinations MUST preserve their own scroll/filter/selection state while the Home process remains active where practical. Deep links from notifications, Go, other apps or the OS MUST be able to open the relevant Home destination/object directly without first routing through the Dashboard.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Dashboard

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The 9-1 AI Dashboard is a generative briefing/dashboard surface, not a chat landing page. It MUST assemble permission-authorised cross-app information into a concise live brief and MUST derive every surfaced tile from identifiable source entities/events or an explicitly generated synthesis over identifiable sources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dashboard tiles MAY surface upcoming Planner items, tasks, recent files/artifacts, project progress, reminders, travel/routes, Agent or Automation status, relevant Mail/messages, package/update state, storage/account warnings and other timely ecosystem context. Every actionable tile MUST use typed app actions; the Dashboard MUST NOT use raw UI automation to perform app mutations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Chat remains in Spaces. The Dashboard MAY expose a lightweight ask/action affordance, but its primary purpose is synthesis, prioritisation, status and quick action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dashboard layout and customisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dashboard layout is user-configurable. The user MUST be able to add supported fixed/provider tiles, remove/hide tiles, resize tiles where the tile declares supported sizes, drag/reorder tiles, arrange tiles into the supported responsive layout, pin/lock tiles against automated movement and restore/reset a layout.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical DashboardLayout MUST use stable TileInstanceID values and store at least TileType, source/provider identity, position/order, declared size, user visibility state, pinned/locked state, tile-specific configuration and layout revision. Responsive rendering MAY adapt exact pixel/grid placement to the current window/device, but it MUST preserve the user’s semantic ordering/grouping and pinned constraints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual user layout changes are authoritative. Automated generation/reordering MUST NOT silently overwrite a newer manual layout revision. When a layout conflict occurs across synced devices, Home MUST preserve both revisions or resolve through an explicit revision/merge policy rather than blind last-write-wins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated tiles and AI layout control

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dashboard settings MUST expose two independent user controls: AllowAIGeneratedTiles and AllowAIReorder. These controls are opt-in/opt-out independently; disabling one MUST NOT implicitly disable the other.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When AllowAIGeneratedTiles = false, Dulche/Generative UI MUST NOT create new arbitrary Dashboard tile instances. Existing user-added/system/provider tiles remain usable, and AI MAY still generate content inside a tile whose explicit tile contract permits generated content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When AllowAIGeneratedTiles = true, Dulche MAY create contextually useful temporary or persisted tiles through the safe Generative UI/CUI schema. Generated tiles MUST declare provenance, the source entities/events they summarise, their lifetime/persistence policy and available typed actions. Generated tiles MUST NOT inject arbitrary executable code.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When AllowAIReorder = false, Dulche MUST NOT move, resize, regroup, reorder or hide existing tiles. When AllowAIReorder = true, Dulche MAY optimise unpinned/unlocked tile placement according to user goals/context, but MUST NOT move or resize tiles marked pinned/locked, MUST preserve explicit hidden-tile choices, and MUST retain an undoable prior layout revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI layout changes MUST be attributable in Events/audit history and MUST be reversible. A user action that manually repositions or pins a tile immediately supersedes older AI layout intent for that tile.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dashboard tile provider contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Apps and Home services MAY register Dashboard tile providers through a versioned provider contract. A provider MUST declare TileType, source app/service, supported sizes, required permissions, refresh policy, data dependencies, available actions, whether the tile can be instantiated manually, and whether its content may be generated/modified by Dulche.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tile data MUST remain source-backed. A tile provider that loses access to its source MUST enter an unavailable/stale state with an explanation rather than silently displaying fabricated current data. Permission revocation MUST prevent future refresh/access and purge or redact cached sensitive content according to the owning source’s policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Apps surface and package management

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home Apps is the primary native app catalogue and management surface. It MUST show installed and available 9to1 apps/packages with stable PackageID/AppID, name/icon, installed version, available version, update channel, installation state, dependency/compatibility state, update availability and repair/rollback availability where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home MUST support install, uninstall, update, repair, launch/open, channel/version selection where allowed and rollback to a validated previous package version where retained. Uninstalling an app MUST NOT silently delete user-created artifacts owned by that app. Artifact-retention/deletion MUST be a separate explicit operation governed by the owning app/storage semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Package installation/update MUST use staged validation and atomic activation. Integrity/signature verification, dependency resolution and Home/shared-service compatibility checks MUST complete before activation. A failed activation MUST leave the previous known-good package usable when rollback data is available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home and Launcher MUST consume one canonical package/update database and service. Launcher is the bootstrap/outside-Home client of the same package system; it MUST NOT maintain a second incompatible installer/updater state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Library

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Library is Home’s cross-app artifact index/browser, not a duplicate Files app and not a separate storage authority. It MUST surface canonical references to authorised artifacts across 9to1 apps, including recent, favourite/pinned, shared, generated/created and app/type-filtered content where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Library entry MUST identify the canonical owning app, stable artifact/entity ID, display name, artifact type, relevant location/owner/share metadata and last-modified state. Opening a Library item routes to the owning app/surface and MUST NOT create a duplicate artifact merely because the item is listed in Home.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Library search/filter/sort MUST use the shared search/index service but enforce current permissions at query/open time. Revoked or deleted artifacts MUST not remain usable through stale Library entries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Events is Home’s ecosystem activity/timeline surface. It is not Planner’s calendar. Events MUST aggregate authorised typed activity from apps/services such as Agent/Automation runs, package/update events, permission/trust decisions, important artifact changes, Mesh/device events, notifications and other meaningful system activity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each Event MUST have a stable EventID, timestamp, source app/service, event type, actor/caller identity where relevant, object/entity references, severity/category, human-readable summary and typed deep-link/action references where available. Events MAY reference RequestID/ActionGraphID for AI/agentic activity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Events MUST preserve source provenance and MUST NOT invent event history from generated summaries. Home MAY generate a concise natural-language digest of events, but the underlying event records remain the authority.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Discover

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Discover is the model browser/discovery surface inside Home. It MUST aggregate model/catalogue information from configured providers rather than depend on one catalogue. Search, filter and comparison MUST support model identity, provider/origin, modality, capabilities, architecture/parameter information when known, context limits, quantisation/format where known, local/cloud status, hardware-fit estimate, install/connection state, entitlement/cost class and privacy/residency information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Discover MUST treat Chat, Image and Voice as first-class model categories. Advanced discovery additionally exposes Audio and Video models. Voice MUST NOT be buried under Audio: conversational/live voice is a primary model category because it has distinct runtime, quality and capability requirements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice discovery MUST expose capability metadata such as Conversational compatibility, Monologue compatibility, Live Listener compatibility, Live Translate compatibility, visual understanding, tool/action support, streaming, interruption/turn-taking support, supported languages/accents and translation language pairs when known, one-way/bidirectional/multi-language live interpretation support, local/cloud execution, latency characteristics, privacy/residency and entitlement/cost.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Discover MUST recommend the highest-quality compatible Voice models/configurations for the user's required mode and constraints. Recommendation dimensions MAY include reasoning quality, speech naturalness, speech-recognition accuracy, expressiveness, instruction following, turn-taking quality, interruption handling, long-form coherence, audio-context understanding, visual capability, tool reliability and latency. Unknown measurements remain Unknown rather than being invented.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice recommendations MUST be contextual rather than a single universal ranking. Discover may surface labels such as Highest quality, Best for Conversational, Best for Monologue, Best for Live Listener, Best for Live Translate, Best local and Fastest when supported by actual capability/evaluation data. Each recommendation MUST explain the relevant reasons/constraints rather than presenting an unexplained badge. Live Translate recommendations should consider speech-recognition accuracy, translation quality, output-speech quality, latency, turn detection, code-switching and multi-language support where measured.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Discover MAY recommend either a native realtime Voice Model or, where 9to1 supports it, a compatible composite voice configuration. Composite implementation detail is secondary to the normal user-facing Voice selection and MUST NOT force ordinary users to manually assemble STT/reasoning/TTS pipelines.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When a selected Voice Model exposes multiple named voices, Discover MUST show those voices as selectable variants with the underlying Voice Model as secondary metadata. Voice-quality/model recommendations and named-voice selection are distinct concepts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A model listing MUST preserve stable provider-scoped identity even when multiple providers expose the same human-readable model name. Unknown metadata MUST remain unknown rather than being fabricated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Discover MUST support the relevant install/pull/connect/open-in-picker action for providers that expose those capabilities. Install/connect actions route through Dulche/provider/package APIs and the normal permission/account model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Universal Model Picker

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Universal Model Picker is the single shared model/provider selection and routing interface for the 9to1 ecosystem. On Windows/regular 9to1 it is hosted by Home; on 9to1-OS the same canonical state is surfaced by the OS. Apps, Agents and AI surfaces MUST NOT create incompatible private model pickers, provider registries or fallback logic when this shared capability applies.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Compact picker and full manager

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The compact picker is used inside apps, Agents and AI surfaces when selecting the effective model/route. The full manager lives in Home/Settings → AI/Models and adds provider configuration, installation/acquisition, aliases, defaults, route ordering, background routing, fallbacks, privacy, resource and lifecycle controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Entries expose stable Dulche model identity plus user-facing name/alias, provider/source, local/cloud/remote state, modalities/capabilities, tool/structured-output support, reasoning controls, context/output limits, loading/availability, privacy/residency, entitlement/cost where known and local RAM/VRAM fit where meaningful. Display names are never used as canonical identity.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Simple defaults and capability categories

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The normal picker keeps the primary capability configuration approachable: Chat Model/Route, Image Model/Route and Voice Model/Voice. Advanced exposes Audio Model/Route and Video Model/Route. The user may instead choose one Active Model/Route and allow all compatible capabilities to inherit it, with ordered fallback resolving unsupported capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Chat is the primary general-purpose route for conversation, reasoning, writing, coding, tool use, agentic work and multimodal chat where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Image supports an explicit Inherit from Active/Chat route. Inheritance means use that ordered route and its native image-generation/editing-capable candidates; it MUST NOT silently substitute an unrelated unconfigured image provider. A dedicated Image route is an explicit override.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice is the first-class conversational/live-voice selection used by Vision & Voice for supported Conversational, Monologue, Live Listener and Live Translate modes. When the selected Voice Model exposes named voices, the user-facing field is labelled Voice and selects VoiceID while showing VoiceModelID as secondary metadata. When there are no named variants the field remains Voice Model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Advanced Audio covers dedicated transcription, synthesis, audio understanding/transformation or music/audio generation where applicable. Advanced Video covers video generation, editing/transformation or video-native understanding. These category routes may inherit the Active route or use explicit independent ordered routes.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Active and Background routes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users may configure a single Active Model/Route for all foreground AI work or assign capability-specific/app/Agent overrides. Separately, a Background Model/Route can be configured for non-interactive work such as background summarisation, indexing/classification, Background Learning processing, permitted Automations AI work, proactive suggestions and other low-priority background tasks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If no Background route is configured, background work inherits the Active route subject to normal capability/privacy/policy filtering. A task-specific explicit model outranks Agent/app/category defaults; a configured Background route applies only to eligible background work and MUST NOT override an explicit Agent/task requirement.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Ordered Model Routes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home/Dulche MUST support versioned ordered Model Routes shared by regular 9to1 and 9to1-OS. A Model Route is an ordered list of stable configured model identities plus per-entry enabled/disabled state and routing policy. Users can reorder candidates directly in Home, including by drag/reorder UI, without changing the models' canonical identities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example: an Active route may be ChatGPT 6 Sol → Gemma 4 → Fable 5. The ordering means use the highest-priority candidate that is both eligible and available for the request. The router MUST evaluate compatibility before invocation rather than deliberately sending impossible requests to higher entries first.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Foreground and background workloads may use different ordered routes. A user can therefore choose a powerful cloud model first for interactive work while using a small local model first for background work. Users who want simplicity can select a single model and leave fallback entries empty.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Eligibility-first routing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For every routed request Dulche first derives task requirements such as modality/capability, tool use, structured output, context/output requirements, reasoning support and foreground/background role. It then filters candidates against provider/model capability, privacy/locality policy, administrator policy, connection/authentication permission, user fallback policy, entitlement and other hard constraints before considering route priority.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: After filtering, Dulche selects the highest-priority available candidate. A lower candidate may be used automatically when a higher candidate is unavailable because of a classified routing condition such as usage/quota exhaustion, provider/model outage, unsupported required capability, context incompatibility, authentication/provider unavailability when another authorised option exists, or local resource insufficiency after permitted reclamation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Capability mismatch should normally be detected before invocation. For example, if the first two models in a route cannot generate video and the third can, a video-generation request routes directly to the third eligible model rather than failing through the first two.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Conditions that are not model fallback

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model fallback is not a generic retry mechanism. Errors such as missing user files, invalid tool arguments, target-app permission denial, required human approval, business-logic rejection or an external service action failure do not justify silently switching models unless the failure is independently classified as a model/provider-routing condition.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Fallback privacy and control

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each route and candidate can restrict fallback, including no fallback, local-only fallback, cloud-allowed fallback or provider-specific constraints. A route containing cloud candidates does not itself authorise sensitive context to leave the device. Privacy, administrator and task policies are evaluated before route ordering.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A request explicitly pinned to a model with fallback disabled MUST fail transparently rather than silently substitute another model. Likewise a local-only request cannot fall through to cloud merely because the local model is unavailable.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Routing transparency

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The effective model and routing reason remain inspectable. Home/Dulche records route identity, selected model and skipped/fallback reasons where relevant, for example 'Sol skipped: usage exhausted; Gemma selected' or 'Sol skipped: video-generation unsupported; Fable selected'. This metadata may be surfaced subtly in normal UI and in more detail through diagnostics/Action Graph without cluttering every response.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Selection inheritance and overrides

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The configuration hierarchy MUST be deterministic: request-specific explicit selection → Agent/task override → app/surface override → capability/category route → Background route for eligible background work or Active route for foreground work → configured route fallbacks. A lower-level explicit override wins, while inherited state is visibly distinguishable from an explicit override.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LLM Space and Desktop Space overrides MAY exist but remain scoped. Category overrides are independent; for example an LLM Space may override Chat while inheriting global Image/Voice/Audio/Video routes.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Reasoning and capability validation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The picker renders only reasoning/effort levels actually exposed by the selected model/provider. It MUST NOT invent Low/Medium/High controls for a model that does not support them. Incompatible explicit selections are blocked or clearly explained unless an authorised fallback route can satisfy the requirement.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Aliases and model identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can assign friendly aliases/nicknames to models. Aliases are presentation conveniences and may be duplicated; all routing objects store stable provider-scoped Dulche ModelID values so duplicate names never create ambiguous execution.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Local model lifecycle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where supported, the full manager provides discover/install or pull, import, verify, download progress, load, unload, remove, update/replace, rollback, storage-location and compatible CPU/GPU/offload configuration. These operations use Dulche Runtime/Den and provider/package APIs rather than a second model-host implementation.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Provider support

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Routes may contain compatible local runtimes, configured commercial/cloud providers, self-hosted/OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, another Dulche device, enterprise endpoints and authorised provider/Plugin implementations. Provider authentication and credentials remain owned by the appropriate shared credential/provider system.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Resource awareness

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For local candidates the picker may show estimated RAM/VRAM requirement, current availability, loading state and reclaimable resources when known. On 9to1-OS this integrates with the AI-aware resource manager; on other Home platforms it uses the available Dulche/runtime resource information without pretending OS-level reclamation exists where it does not.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Administrator and managed-profile policy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Managed profiles may limit approved models/providers, acquisition, external cloud use, maximum cost/usage class or fallback destinations. Policy filtering happens before user ordering so reordering a blocked provider cannot bypass a School/organisation restriction.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use one canonical Dulche model catalogue and versioned routing contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can use one Active Model for everything compatible or configure separate capability/app/Agent and Background routes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordered model routing automatically falls through on classified quota, availability, capability, context or resource conditions while respecting privacy, permissions and admin policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Capability mismatch is filtered before invocation where knowable; model fallback is not misused for unrelated tool/app/business-logic failures.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can reorder, enable/disable and inspect route candidates and understand which model ultimately handled a request.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice named variants, Image inheritance, Advanced Audio/Video, reasoning controls, aliases and local-model lifecycle preserve the existing category-specific contracts.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dulche runtime control

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home Core owns the single shared Dulche broker/runtime lifecycle for native 9to1 apps. It MAY host multiple logical endpoints/models concurrently subject to resource policy, but apps MUST attach to the shared broker rather than launching competing private model servers.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home MUST expose shared Dulche service state including Starting, Ready, Degraded, Restarting and Stopped plus endpoint/model load state, resource pressure and health/diagnostic information required for recovery. Logical EndpointID/SessionID identity remains governed by the Dulche Runtime contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If the visible Home shell closes, Home Core MAY continue in the background. If Home Core crashes/restarts, attached apps MUST enter a degraded/reconnecting state for Home-dependent features, preserve their own user data, and reconnect to restored shared services. Apps MUST NOT launch private replacement Dulche servers during recovery.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Permission and trust broker

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns the operational permission/trust broker defined by App APIs and automation permissions. It stores and evaluates caller identity, scoped grants, blocks, temporary trust, 30-day Accept and Trust grants, Accept and Always Trust grants, expiry/revocation state and audit history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Settings MUST expose a Permissions & Trust management surface where the user can inspect caller identity/origin, granted apps/actions/scopes, trust level, creation/expiry, last-use metadata where available, and revoke/block/unblock/narrow grants. Revocation MUST affect future actions immediately subject to in-flight action semantics defined by the target API.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Mesh

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mesh is a Home feature, not a standalone app. It connects authorised user/team devices so selected 9to1 context, projects, Agents and capabilities can operate across devices without requiring every workflow to live entirely in remote cloud infrastructure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Mesh device MUST have a stable DeviceID bound to an authenticated device identity/key rather than a mutable device name. Pairing MUST require explicit user/account authorisation and establish an authenticated encrypted relationship. A device advertises supported 9to1 capabilities/services and versions; peers MUST NOT assume capabilities that were not advertised.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mesh data sharing/sync MUST be namespace/object scoped. Personal Mesh may sync selected personal Den/chat/context/project state; Team/Organisation modes may sync explicitly shared team/org state while preserving personal/private namespaces. Joining Mesh MUST NOT automatically share all local files, secrets, model context or app data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Remote capability invocation MUST use typed APIs and pass both caller-side and target-device permission/policy checks. Mesh MUST NOT become an implicit generic remote-desktop, mouse/keyboard or arbitrary-code-execution channel.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Lost/revoked devices MUST be removable from Home. Revocation invalidates future Mesh authentication/session material for that device and prevents further sync/remote calls. Offline devices queue only operations whose owning service explicitly supports safe offline replay/conflict handling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Action Graph renderer

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns the shared user-facing Action Graph renderer/source. Dulche owns execution graph/log data and persistence semantics; Home provides the reusable CUI/Markdown presentation component used to display authorised graph data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any authorised app MAY host the shared renderer given an authorised RequestID/ActionGraphID. Home MUST NOT create a second execution history or mutate Dulche’s causal graph merely for presentation. Events, Agents, Spaces and other surfaces MAY deep-link into the same renderer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home does not own the primary Voice, Vision or AI Overlay session controls. Those live in Vision & Voice; Home remains responsible only for the shared runtime/model configuration and renderer/platform services they consume.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Persistent contextual AI bar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns the reusable base component/service contract for the global persistent bottom AI bar required by interactive 9to1 apps. The shared component provides CUI rendering, Dulche connection, Universal Model Picker integration, permission/trust plumbing, request state and common Action Graph access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each host app MUST provide the bar with a permission-filtered semantic context snapshot and its typed supported actions. Home MUST NOT obtain app context through raw screen scraping when the host provides structured context. App-specific mutation semantics remain owned by the target app APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Floating compose @ invocation menu

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The shared Home-owned floating AI compose component MUST provide one searchable @ invocation menu for Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents and Files. The menu is a single interaction surface with collapsible type sections rather than separate unrelated pickers. Typing @ opens the resource list; typing text after @ filters across all sections while preserving each result's type and identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selecting an item inserts an inline invocation chip/token inside the compose field at the caret position. The rendered token MUST display the resource's icon where available plus its human-readable label, for example an Agent may render as '@[agent icon] John'. The token MUST use a distinct invoked visual state, including colour/style differentiation, while also using non-colour cues for accessibility. Editing/deleting the token removes or changes the invocation rather than leaving invisible hidden attachment state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Invocation tokens MUST store stable canonical identities, not only display text: Plugin PackageID/version or resolved active version, SkillID/version, AppID, AgentID/DefinitionRevision where required and File/Artifact reference identity/revision or access token as appropriate. Duplicate display names MUST therefore remain unambiguous. The resolved invocation set is included in request metadata, FullLog and Action Graph.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Plugins section lists Dulche Plugins enabled/available in the current scope; Skills lists eligible Dulche Skills including the built-in Persistent Skill; Agents lists Agents available through Dulche scope resolution; Files searches authorised files/artifacts without silently granting new access. Availability in the picker never grants permission to execute protected actions or read inaccessible content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Apps section MUST contain every installed/available first-party 9to1 app plus user-installed applications that 9to1 can classify as safely operable through a typed API/integration or, when separately authorised, Computer Use. App entries MUST expose whether their interaction path is Typed/API, Computer Use Required, or both. Selecting an app whose only route is Computer Use MUST NOT activate Computer Use by itself; the request also requires the explicit @Computer Use invocation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Game executables and anti-cheat-protected game surfaces MUST be excluded from the operable Apps invocation results even when discovered through Steam, Epic Games Launcher or another launcher/library. If 9to1 cannot confidently distinguish an eligible ordinary application from a game/anti-cheat target, it MUST omit or mark the target unavailable for Computer Use rather than risk automation. Play remains the supported Agent-game route defined by its own contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: @Computer Use is a reserved first-party system capability entry in the same searchable invocation surface. Selecting it creates the explicit ComputerUseInvocationID required by the Dulche Computer Use contract and makes its active state visible in the compose field before the request is submitted.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Cross-app execution visualisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Models operating inside any 9to1 app MAY invoke another 9to1 app only when the user's request explicitly names/invokes that app, directly asks for an outcome owned by that app, or unambiguously implies the owning app from the requested artifact/action. For example, 'create a presentation' resolves to Present; 'make a spreadsheet' resolves to Data; an unrelated app MUST NOT be opened merely because the model thinks it might be useful.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app intent resolution MUST bind to the owning app's stable AppID and typed capability contract. If the required app is not running, Home MAY launch/open it automatically when that is part of fulfilling the request. The target artifact remains canonical in its owning app, and the originating app/Space receives references/status rather than an unmanaged duplicate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typed app APIs and shared semantic actions are the normal execution path. Computer Use is not a fallback for missing/failed APIs and remains unavailable unless @Computer Use was explicitly invoked. Permission, review, edit/suggest/view state, conflicts and external-side-effect rules of the target app still apply to cross-app work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where an app has a visible editing surface, the user SHOULD be able to watch model-driven edits occur in real time. Home/shared app infrastructure MUST provide an execution-visualisation stream that maps semantic actions to visible UI changes such as objects moving, text appearing, selections changing, slides being created or a virtual cursor hovering over the affected target.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The execution visualiser is representational, not the control mechanism. A virtual cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's real pointer and MUST NOT generate mouse/keyboard input merely to make the animation believable. The canonical typed API/action result remains authoritative; visual animation follows confirmed/provisional semantic events and MUST reconcile to final app state after errors, retries or rollback.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI conversation presentation settings

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home Settings MUST expose global conversation presentation preferences for Plain text versus Speech bubbles. The preference applies to compatible 9to1 conversational/AI surfaces through the shared renderer rather than each app inventing a different message layout.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: User-message alignment and model-message alignment MUST be independently configurable as Left or Right. All four combinations are valid, including both parties on the same side. Alignment changes presentation only and MUST NOT alter message order, authorship, accessibility reading order or exported conversation data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The selected Dulche thinking-log mode (Precise, Concise, Detailed or Ramble) MUST be configurable in the same AI/conversation settings family. Inline thinking/work regions render beneath or between message text according to chronology; when Speech bubbles are enabled, the thinking/work region visually belongs beneath the relevant model bubble without being styled as ordinary model-authored message text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Thinking/work presentation MUST use lower visual emphasis than normal chat while remaining readable and accessible. Collapsed 'Thought for ...'/'Worked for ...', ETA status, blockers and Problem events MUST use the same shared renderer across apps so equivalent Runtime state is not represented differently by each product.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shared Productivity Engine

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns the Shared Productivity Engine used by Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces for overlapping document/object behaviours. The engine is a shared canonical object/rendering/action layer, not five copied implementations. App shells MAY provide different workflows and layout chrome, but a shared object type MUST use the same schema, formatting semantics, rendering rules and typed object actions wherever that type is supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The initial required shared object families include rich text/paragraphs, headings, lists/checklists, code blocks, equations, tables, images/media, drawings/ink, graph objects and typed embedded 9to1 artifact references. The registry MUST be extensible so a new shared object type can be implemented once and enabled in multiple supporting surfaces without rewriting its core editor/renderer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: App-specific document structures remain allowed. Present still owns slides and presentation-level layout; Canvas still owns its infinite spatial surface; Boards owns Board/Page hierarchy and Board-specific layout. The shared engine standardises reusable embedded/shared objects rather than forcing one top-level document model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canonical object identity, schemas and style registry

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every shared object instance MUST have a stable ObjectID within its owning artifact plus a versioned ObjectType/schema identifier. Object content, formatting, accessibility metadata, asset references and app-neutral layout properties MUST be serialisable independently from transient UI state. Unknown required schema versions MUST fail explicitly rather than being silently flattened or reinterpreted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared object schemas MUST preserve enough information for semantically identical rendering/editing across participating apps. If an app cannot support a property, it MUST retain that property in the object payload when round-tripping and surface the limitation instead of destructively stripping it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The engine MUST provide a shared versioned style registry for reusable text/paragraph/object style definitions. Style definitions use stable StyleID identity independent of display name so renaming a style does not detach existing objects. App-specific style extensions MAY exist but MUST preserve shared base properties when transferred.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app copy, paste and embeds

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The engine MUST provide a versioned ProductivityObjectBundle clipboard/transfer format containing shared object payloads, style definitions, asset references, accessibility metadata and a portable fallback representation. Copying a supported object from one participating app and pasting it into another MUST preserve the same shared-object semantics and appearance rather than converting it to an image or lossy app-specific approximation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When the destination supports the same shared object type, paste creates/imports a native shared object instance using the same schema. When the destination does not support that object type but supports embedded 9to1 artifacts, the UI MUST offer an embed/reference path. Destructive flattening is allowed only as an explicit export/paste-as-static action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spaces MUST use the Shared Productivity Engine for rich pasted/embedded content so tables, code blocks, drawings, graphs and other shared objects preserve their structure instead of degrading to plain text. Spaces may present a conversational shell around the object, but editing MUST route through the same shared object actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rendering, editing, undo and actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The engine MUST provide shared selection, focus, formatting, object insertion/removal, resize/transform where applicable, clipboard, accessibility and undoable action primitives for shared object types. Shared actions MUST have stable typed representations so compatible apps can participate in undo/recovery and AI/Automation execution without reproducing hidden per-app commands.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: App-specific shells MAY add contextual commands, but MUST NOT fork the underlying object semantics into incompatible versions. Object actions MUST be exposed through typed APIs and usable by UI, Spaces, Automations and Dulche-driven AI without raw UI simulation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The shared engine MUST emit semantic selection/context information for the persistent AI bar and app-specific contextual toolbars. This context MUST contain stable object/selection identity rather than requiring consumers to infer meaning from rendered pixels.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drawing engine

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The shared engine MUST expose the Rnote-derived drawing/ink engine as a reusable shared object/layer so Canvas and Boards use the same stroke model, pen/eraser behaviours and serialisation primitives. Other productivity surfaces MAY opt into the same drawing object without implementing a separate ink stack.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deployment boundary and compatibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home Core MUST expose the Shared Productivity Engine as a versioned shared platform capability. Apps may link/embed approved shared engine libraries/components as part of their package for rendering performance, but the canonical schema registry, compatibility negotiation and shared service/version authority remain Home-owned. Apps MUST validate compatible engine/schema versions during startup.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared object schemas and ProductivityObjectBundle MUST be versioned independently of individual app versions. Home MUST expose compatibility negotiation so an older app can detect a newer unsupported shared object type/property before editing. Compatible unknown optional properties MUST be preserved; incompatible required features MUST produce a structured compatibility state rather than silent data loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

NORMAL_TEXT
text: The above are minimum cross-app entry points. Each shared object type MUST also expose its typed creation/update/query actions through the owning app/API surface required by the global API-parity rule.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Settings

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home Settings owns ecosystem-wide settings only. The Settings surface MUST include at least Account & Subscription, Appearance/CUI, AI & Models, Permissions & Trust, Apps & Updates, Storage, Mesh & Devices, Privacy, Accessibility, Notifications and Advanced/Diagnostics. App-specific preferences remain in the owning app unless a setting intentionally governs multiple apps.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Settings changes MUST use typed settings keys/schemas with validation and explicit scope (device, account, workspace/team or organisation where applicable). Unknown or incompatible settings versions MUST NOT be silently discarded during upgrade/downgrade.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Account and subscription surface

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home MUST provide the primary native CAKE ID account/subscription surface. It displays authenticated user identity, organisation/workspace context where applicable, current configured subscription/preset source, EntitlementPriceMonthly, EffectiveThresholds, EffectiveEntitlements, AI Dust balance/allocation/usage, storage allocation/usage, site limits/usage and active sessions/devices using server-authoritative values.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home MUST NOT recalculate paid entitlements locally from a displayed tier label. Checkout, plan changes and sensitive billing management hand off to the trusted authenticated CAKEMODS billing flow defined by the Accounts & Subscription contract. Sign-out/session revocation actions MUST preserve local user data according to each app’s offline/storage policy rather than deleting it by default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Notifications

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns the native 9to1 notification service/centre. Apps publish typed notifications containing NotificationID, source app/service, category/severity, title/body, created time, read/dismissed state, related entity references and typed actions/deep links. Notifications MUST NOT encode consequential behaviour only as arbitrary executable callbacks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home MUST support notification history, read/unread state, dismiss/clear subject to retention policy, per-source/category preferences and deep-link actions. Where Windows/9to1-OS system notifications are available, Home MAY bridge eligible notifications to the OS while retaining the canonical 9to1 notification record/state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Shared search and Go indexing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns/co-ordinates the shared searchable-entity index consumed by Go and Home Library/Search. Apps MUST publish supported searchable entity metadata through a typed indexing contract rather than Home scraping arbitrary app databases.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search records MUST include stable source app, EntityID/type, title/display metadata, search/index text or vector references as permitted, modification state and current access-scope metadata. Search results MUST re-check current authorisation before exposing sensitive content or opening an entity; stale index access MUST NOT bypass revoked permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: On deletion/revocation, apps MUST be able to invalidate/remove affected index records. Home may maintain rebuildable indexes/caches, but the index MUST NOT become the only canonical copy of source content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Service registry and compatibility handshake

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home Core MUST expose a machine-readable service registry describing Home-owned platform capabilities and versions. At minimum it includes Dulche broker/runtime coordination, permission/trust broker, Shared Productivity Engine, package/update service, notifications, search/index, Mesh and account/session capability availability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before normal startup, every native 9to1 app MUST complete a compatibility handshake against Home Core and declare the required service/capability versions it needs. Missing/incompatible required services result in the global Home repair/update/bootstrap flow rather than undefined partial operation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Service identity/version MUST be explicit; apps MUST NOT infer compatibility solely from the Home marketing version string.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Startup, background lifecycle and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home Core MUST auto-start on demand or at session startup when required by installed 9to1 apps. Closing the visible Home window MUST NOT necessarily stop Home Core. Home Core shutdown is allowed only when no required dependent operation is active or when the user/system explicitly requests full 9to1 service shutdown.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home Core persistent state MUST use crash-safe versioned storage. Corrupt or incompatible Home state MUST enter a diagnosable recovery/repair mode; Home MUST NOT silently discard permission grants, package state, device identities or other durable control-plane state to regain startup.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a Home service fails while apps are open, dependent apps MUST receive a structured service-unavailable/degraded signal. They MUST preserve their own artifact state and block only operations that require the failed service. When the service recovers, clients reconnect/resynchronise through stable IDs/revisions rather than restarting with assumed fresh state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Home data/state model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home MUST maintain stable IDs/versioned records for installed packages/apps, Home services, Dashboard layouts/tiles, Mesh devices/pairings, notification records, search index records, permission/trust grants, account/session cache metadata and other Home-owned settings/control-plane entities. Display names, paths and UI ordering are not identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Caches/indexes that are rebuildable MUST be marked as non-authoritative. Durable grants, package activation state, device trust and user layout/settings state MUST be recoverable and versioned. Home MUST distinguish device-local state from account/workspace-synchronised state explicitly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Security boundary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home Core is a high-privilege local control plane. All local IPC/service calls MUST authenticate/identify the caller and evaluate the caller’s effective scopes before exposing privileged operations. Executable filename, window title or self-asserted display name MUST NOT be accepted as caller identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Installed signed/registered apps MAY use package identity plus Home-issued process/session credentials. Development/self-built callers MAY use an explicit registered developer/project identity with tamper-evident binding as defined by the global permission model. Trust MUST NOT silently transfer after a material caller identity/signing/content change.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Secrets/credentials MUST be stored through secure credential references and MUST NOT be persisted in plaintext Home configuration, logs, Events, Dashboard tiles or package manifests. Home logs/audits MUST redact secret payloads while retaining accurate action/provenance records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Platform behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows: Home provides the full native hub/shell, Home Core background services and the Home-hosted Universal Model Picker. Native apps depend on the compatible Home installation/Home Core handshake.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-OS: Home Core/shared service contracts remain authoritative platform services, but selected controls may be integrated into OS-native system surfaces. The Universal Model Picker is OS-hosted while using the same canonical Dulche/model/provider state. 9to1-OS MUST NOT create divergent duplicate settings/package/model databases.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web: the Home web surface uses CAKE ID and server-hosted equivalents for account, Library, Dashboard, notifications, search and other supported cloud capabilities. It MUST capability-negotiate and clearly mark local-only/native-only functions such as local package management, local models/devices or unavailable Home Core services rather than pretending they exist in-browser.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home APIs/services MUST return structured failures including HomeServiceUnavailable, HomeServiceIncompatible, PackageIntegrityFailed, PackageDependencyConflict, PackageActivationFailed, DashboardRevisionConflict, TileProviderUnavailable, PermissionDenied, DeviceRevoked, MeshUnavailable, IndexUnavailable and AccountServiceUnavailable in addition to the global error contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Failures in one Home service MUST NOT automatically corrupt or erase unrelated Home state. For example, Discover/provider failure must not invalidate package state; search-index corruption must be recoverable by rebuilding the index; Dashboard tile-provider failure must degrade only affected tiles.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A native app refuses normal startup when Home is not installed and successfully resumes through the trusted Install Home/bootstrap flow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Closing the visible Home window does not break dependent apps while Home Core remains healthy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Home Core/service crash produces structured degraded state in attached apps, preserves user artifacts and reconnects after service recovery without spawning duplicate private services.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dashboard manual tile add/remove/resize/reorder/pin state persists across restart and responsive window sizes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AllowAIGeneratedTiles=false prevents arbitrary generated tile creation while existing tiles continue to function.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AllowAIReorder=false prevents AI movement/layout changes; when enabled, AI cannot move pinned/locked tiles and every AI layout change is reversible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated Dashboard tiles expose source provenance and fail stale/unavailable rather than fabricating live data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Apps install/update/repair/rollback uses the shared package database and survives a failed staged activation without deleting user artifacts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Library opens the same canonical artifact in its owning app rather than creating a duplicate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Events preserve typed source records and link to the corresponding Action Graph/entity where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Discover aggregates at least two configured model/provider sources without identity collisions and performs a valid install/connect action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Universal Model Picker override precedence and fallback policy resolve deterministically and do not cross local-to-cloud boundaries when policy forbids it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permission/trust grants can be inspected, narrowed/revoked/blocked and future calls immediately respect the updated state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mesh pairing establishes stable device identity; capability calls obey both ends’ permissions; device revocation prevents subsequent sync/invocation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home notifications preserve read/dismiss state and typed deep links across restart and OS notification bridging.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search/Library results stop exposing content after permission revocation/deletion and indexes can be rebuilt without source-data loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A representative shared productivity object can round-trip across Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces through the Shared Productivity Engine without schema/format loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Account/subscription values shown in Home match the server-authoritative CAKE ID entitlement state and are not inferred from preset labels.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An app with an incompatible required Home service version is blocked into update/repair instead of running against an undefined interface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home persistent control-plane state can recover from process interruption without silently dropping package activation state, device trust or permission grants.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Node Graph Framework

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns the shared Node Graph Framework used by Automations and Space graph editors. It is an editing/schema/validation/execution-visualisation framework, not a second automation or AI runtime. Product surfaces register domain-specific events, actions and node types; Dulche and owning apps execute the resulting authorised runtime actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The framework MUST provide a versioned graph data model, stable GraphID/NodeID/PortID identity, node registry, typed input/output ports, typed connections, node configuration schemas, pan/zoom/selection, grouping/comments, copy/paste/duplicate, undo/redo, validation, Draft/Active graph revision support, execution-state overlays and contextual AI-bar integration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connections MUST be type-checked. Incompatible ports cannot connect unless an explicit registered conversion node exists. Nodes and graph actions MUST reference canonical stable app/capability/entity IDs rather than screen coordinates or UI implementation details.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The framework MUST support product-defined capability profiles. For example, built-in Spaces receive a constrained Events & Extensions node registry while user-created Spaces and Automations may receive broader registries. A capability profile cannot expose an action prohibited by the product/security contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph mutation from the contextual AI bar MUST use typed graph APIs. AI may add/remove/configure nodes and connections only within the current capability profile and permissions, and MUST NOT simulate mouse/keyboard graph editing.
