heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: 9to1 Admin

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-01 — Product role, access and platforms

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Admin is a standalone Business-exclusive 9to1 application, not a renamed account-settings page or WordPress administration screen. It is the organisation-management interface for the Business features specified separately under Business features — functional specification. Business and Business + include it; the account-bound free Business grant defined for Jacob also applies. App access does not grant administrative permissions: every operation additionally requires the appropriate role and target scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Admin MUST have Windows, 9to1-OS and browser/web surfaces sharing the same CAKE ID, organisation entities, domain APIs and permission evaluation. Native clients use Home’s shared services. The web app uses authenticated shared web services without requiring a local Home installation for ordinary organisation administration. Device operations require an enrolled compatible endpoint; a browser cannot directly enforce unsupported local OS controls. Unsupported capabilities MUST remain distinguishable from denied permission or an offline device.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Admin owns management workflows and policy editing. The account/billing service owns subscriptions and ledgers; Spaces owns Team Spaces; Files owns shared-drive content; Connect owns communications; Home/Mesh owns pairing and device-resource execution; Dulche/Den owns Agents; the 9to1-OS policy service owns endpoint enforcement. Admin MUST invoke these canonical services rather than create duplicate content, Agent registries, payment records or a competing permission broker. This is a native CUI product built on those existing services; no new paid administration donor or hosting service is selected by this specification.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-02 — Navigation and organisation lifecycle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The start screen MUST list organisations the user can manage, with an explicit organisation switcher and current organisation identity on every administrative screen. Navigation MUST include Overview; People; Roles & Permissions; Policies; Models, Apps & Features; Plugins & Settings; Usage & Credits; Billing; Team Space & Drive; Connect; Devices & Mesh; Team Agents; and Audit & Activity. Visibility is permission-filtered, while denial states explain the required capability without leaking inaccessible organisations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overview MUST show member/seat counts, resource allocation and consumption, pending invitations/approvals, policy-deployment status, blocked actions, device health and billing state, each with source freshness. Unknown or stale values MUST NOT appear as zero or healthy. Search, filtering, accessible keyboard operation, bulk-selection previews and per-item bulk results are required. Admin is not an artifact editor: blank-document/template import surfaces are not applicable; organisation creation, invitation and configuration import/export replace them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Authorised owners MUST be able to create and edit organisation identity, manage ownership, inspect linked Business entitlement, archive/reactivate the organisation and request export or deletion. Ownership transfer requires authenticated acceptance by the recipient; removing or suspending the last active owner MUST be rejected. Archive is recoverable and distinct from permanent deletion. Deletion requires an impact preview, explicit confirmation and the applicable retention/export workflow, and MUST NOT delete a member’s personal account or personal artifacts.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-03 — People, roles and permissions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: People management MUST support invite, resend/revoke invitation, accept, list/search, assign/change roles, suspend, reinstate and remove membership. Membership states MUST distinguish Invited, Active, Suspended and Removed, with stable MembershipID and UserID. Invitations are time-bounded and single-use for the intended identity. Acceptance and capacity reservation MUST be transactional so concurrent requests cannot bypass the seat cap. The UI MUST distinguish members, pending/reserved invitations and external Connect correspondents; corresponding counting rules must be explicit, not hidden billing assumptions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Roles MUST be editable capability sets, not just labels. Provide owner, administrator and member roles, plus separately assignable billing, usage-reporting, device-management, Agent-management and audit-reading capabilities. Custom roles MUST support scoped read, add/edit, delete/recovery and specialised administrative actions. A role editor MUST show effective permissions and inherited restrictions. A delegated administrator MUST NOT grant capabilities outside their own delegation boundary, elevate themselves to owner or modify protected grants. Membership alone does not grant access to every shared document, private conversation or Agent memory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Suspension/removal MUST revoke organisation sessions/capabilities, block new organisation-funded jobs, remove applicable shared access and reconcile owned organisation resources and outstanding reservations. Show a transfer/reassignment preview for shared assets, scheduled Automations and Agent responsibilities. Already completed external actions remain historical facts. Revocation MUST leave personal accounts and unrelated organisations intact; offline devices must report pending revocation until enforcement is acknowledged.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-04 — Enforced policy editor

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Administrators MUST be able to enforce organisation-wide and role-specific policies, inspect their effective result for a selected member/device/Agent, and preview affected objects before publication. PolicySet and PolicyAssignment records MUST carry stable IDs, schema version, revision, scope, author, effective time and change reason. A change follows Draft → Validated → Published, with per-target delivery/enforcement status; publication is not proof that an offline endpoint applied it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Restrictions MUST cover model/provider access; apps; individual app features/actions; Plugins and their capabilities; Agents and Automations, including creation, editing, invocation, schedules and external side effects. Restricted capabilities must be enforced by the owning service at dispatch, not merely hidden in the UI. APIs, command-line tools, modified clients and nested Agent/Plugin calls receive the same policy decisions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effective capability grants are the intersection of server entitlement, delegated role, organisation/role policy, object access, caller trust and applicable device/privacy restrictions. A denial at a required boundary cannot be overridden by a broader grant elsewhere. Conflicting mandatory settings or required-versus-blocked Plugin rules MUST produce a validation conflict instead of an arbitrary last-write-wins outcome. New sensitive requests remain subject to Home’s normal approval rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-05 — Required Plugins, forced settings and default models

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Admin MUST support required organisation-wide Plugins and additional requirements by role, with package identity, approved version/update policy, required configuration and deployment status. Required does not mean silently trusted: package integrity, compatibility, requested scopes and secret connections must validate before enablement. A blocked or failed required Plugin produces an actionable non-compliance state. Disabling an unsafe Plugin remains possible for authorised security response; updates cannot widen permissions without the required approval.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Administrators MUST be able to force supported organisation/role settings and separately supply editable defaults. Members see the effective value, whether it is locked and which policy supplies it. Settings must be addressed by versioned typed keys supported by the target app/device; unsupported settings cannot be reported as applied. Forced settings affect only the managed scope and cannot silently rewrite personal settings outside it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Default-model configuration MUST support organisation defaults and role-specific defaults, plus permitted user overrides. The effective model must also satisfy model restrictions, entitlement, capability, privacy and local/cloud routing rules. An unavailable or prohibited default blocks with a clear reason or uses an explicitly authorised fallback; it MUST NOT silently send private local-only content to a cloud provider. Conflicting forced role defaults must be resolved explicitly in policy configuration before publication.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-06 — Subscription assignment, usage controls and rollover

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Usage & Credits MUST let authorised administrators assign a funded subscription/resource configuration to a member or role, choose a shared organisation pool or individually partitioned allocations, set limits, inspect consumption/reservations and move eligible unspent organisation-owned allocation between partitions. Changing a display tier or role MUST NOT mint credits, unlock an unfunded model band or duplicate an allocation. A cost-changing assignment requires the Billing approval flow rather than silently purchasing resources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Controls MUST include organisation, role and member ceilings for AI usage and applicable storage/site resources; warnings and hard-stop behaviour; configured time windows; and model/Agent/Automation attribution. A hard ceiling is enforced before work is admitted. No paid overage or automatic top-up is enabled merely because a warning threshold is crossed. Reports MUST separate allocated, available, reserved, consumed, rolled-over and expired credits and display the reset/expiry policy and freshness.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Admins MUST be able to configure, by role, whether eligible expired/expiring credits may roll over, with explicit inheritance, allow or disallow settings and the supported carryover period/cap. This is a real server-enforced credit-lifecycle rule, not an interface label. Credit lots retain source allocation, original expiry, rollover policy/version and resulting expiry, with an auditable rollover event. Changes cannot spend the same credit twice or alter settled usage. Eligibility, funding and allowed carryover bounds come from the versioned billing policy; unresolved commercial durations are OPEN rather than guessed. Members MUST see their effective rollover rule.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-07 — Billing, invoices and reporting

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Billing MUST expose the current Business add-on, seat capacity, funded resource configurations, invoice/payment status and authorised invoice download, plus a preview of changes and their effective date. Separate the fixed organisation add-on from AI/storage/other resource costs. There is no per-seat fee. Usage allocation may change resource cost, but an invitation or role assignment must not conceal a seat charge.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Purchases, upgrades or other spending require an authorised human’s explicit approval of a current quote identifying organisation, currency, itemised amount, recurring terms and effective date. Paid carrier numbers, third-party services and hosting are separate spending decisions. Approval must be bound to the quote/version and protected against replay; a changed or expired quote requires a new decision. Raw payment details remain in the trusted billing flow, never in Admin client code, Plugins, prompts or logs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Analytics MUST offer permission-filtered totals and breakdowns by period, member, role, model, app, Agent and pool, with exportable reports and reconciliation to ledger events. Estimates/forecasts are labelled separately from settled charges. Reporting is operational accounting, not covert inspection of message contents, documents or personal activity. Personal-account usage is excluded unless explicitly and validly brought into the organisation billing scope.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-08 — Shared resources, devices and team Agents

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Team Space & Drive MUST manage organisation ownership, role/group access, sharing restrictions, storage limits, access reviews, archival/recovery and export through Spaces/Files. Connect management MUST cover the organisation directory, channels/groups, delegated organisational identities, allowed external contact and Agent channel bindings through Connect. Administrative metadata access does not create a plaintext backdoor to encrypted or private conversations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Devices & Mesh MUST expose enrolled devices, owner/account, platform, supported capabilities, trust/enrolment state, last contact, effective policy and resource contributions. Authorised actions MUST include enrolment approval, group/role assignment, policy deployment, access/resource revocation and inspection of acknowledged enforcement. Cross-account Mesh grants require explicit enrolled-device trust and configured compute/storage limits. A stale/offline device remains Pending or Unknown; a submitted command is not reported as executed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Team Agents MUST list canonical organisation Agents and support create/import, assign owner/scope, edit/publish versions, configure model/tools/required Plugins and budgets, share invocation access, schedule approved work, pause/resume/stop, archive/recover and inspect authorised run history. AI Studio opens the same Agent for detailed authoring. Administrative control cannot silently copy private user memories, credentials or grants into a shared Agent. Revoked members cannot keep invoking an organisation Agent through an old endpoint.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-09 — Audit, failure and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consequential management actions MUST record AuditEventID, OrgID, verified actor/delegation, action and target IDs, timestamp, policy/revision, approval reference where required, redacted before/after state and observed outcome. Policy evaluation denials, privilege changes, billing approvals, credit adjustments, device grants and Agent publication/revocation are auditable. Audit permission is separate from content access; secrets and unnecessary personal content are excluded. Administrators cannot silently edit historical audit entries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mutations use optimistic revision checks and idempotency keys. Multi-target jobs expose JobID, target-level Succeeded/Failed/Pending/Skipped/RolledBack states, retry eligibility and cancellation limits. Failed policy rollout retains the last acknowledged safe policy and offers scoped rollback, not an invented all-success state. Unknown billing/external-action outcomes must be reconciled before retry. Offline administrative clients may inspect permitted cached metadata with a stale marker but cannot assert that a new server policy or purchase has taken effect.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-10 — Canonical data and API contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canonical records MUST include Organisation, Membership, Role, CapabilityGrant, PolicySet, PolicyAssignment, ResourcePool, MemberAllocation, CreditLot, DeviceEnrolment, MeshGrant, TeamAgentBinding, Approval, AdminJob and AuditEvent. Each carries stable IDs, OrgID where applicable, lifecycle and revision/schema metadata. Identity and subscription authority remain server-side; caches are derived and permission-filtered. Exports omit secrets and preserve portable configuration plus dependency references; imports validate compatibility and require a dry-run/impact preview before mutation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical management namespace is 9to1.Admin. Required action families are Organisations (List, Get, Create, Update, TransferOwnership, Archive, Restore, Export, RequestDeletion); Members (List, Invite, RevokeInvitation, AcceptInvitation, SetRoles, Suspend, Reinstate, Remove); Roles (List, Create, Update, Delete, GetEffectivePermissions); Policies (Get, Preview, Validate, Publish, GetDeployment, Rollback); Resources (GetUsage, SetAllocation, SetLimits, TransferAllocation, SetRolloverPolicy); Billing (GetConfiguration, PreviewChange, OpenCheckout, ListInvoices, DownloadInvoice); SharedResources (Get, PreviewAccessChange, ApplyAccessChange); Devices (List, Enrol, AssignPolicy, Revoke, GetEnforcement); Mesh (ListGrants, Grant, Revoke, SetLimits); Agents (List, Bind, Configure, Publish, SetAccess, SetBudget, ControlRun, Archive, Restore); and Audit/Jobs (List, Get, Export, Cancel where cancellable). Domain operations dispatch to their existing owning service; these are management entry points, not duplicate runtime implementations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every action contract MUST declare typed arguments/results, permission scope, risk, reversibility and external effects. Scoped requests include OrgID and stable target IDs; mutations include ExpectedRevision and IdempotencyKey. Collection APIs provide cursor pagination and bounded page sizes; jobs provide JobID, status and target results. Success returns canonical IDs, new revision and applied/pending status. Failures return structured codes including PermissionDenied, EntitlementRequired, SeatLimitReached, PolicyDenied, PolicyConflict, RevisionConflict, InsufficientCredits, QuotaExceeded, ApprovalRequired, QuoteExpired, DeviceOffline, UnsupportedCapability and ProviderUnavailable, with recoverability/retry metadata. UI-only management actions are non-conformant.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-11 — Acceptance and release gates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Acceptance MUST prove: a non-Business account cannot gain Admin capabilities; Business access without an admin role does not grant privileged operations; Jacob’s verified free grant works without enabling another account; a Business organisation with 50 active seats cannot admit a 51st concurrently; and Business + has no subscription seat cap while ordinary resource/security limits still apply. Verify that adding an unfunded seat never creates a seat invoice.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: End-to-end tests MUST cover organisation ownership transfer and last-owner protection; invite/suspend/remove with immediate server access revocation; custom-role restrictions through UI and direct API; blocked models/apps/features/Plugins/Automations; required Plugins by organisation and role; forced settings and default-model conflicts; shared versus individual budgets; role-based rollover; concurrency-safe credit reservation/settlement; itemised quote approval and retry protection; shared-resource ACLs; cross-account Mesh opt-in/revocation; and team-Agent isolation and lifecycle.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Platform tests MUST cover Windows, 9to1-OS and web, including browser administration without local Home, unsupported endpoint controls and offline rollout remaining pending. Test restart/persistence, stale revisions, partial bulk failure, rollback, secret redaction, report reconciliation, keyboard/focus/screen-reader operation and equivalent API behaviour. Lists MUST remain paginated, exports/rollouts asynchronous where long-running, and expensive reports must not block policy checks. A rendered dashboard or stub action is not implementation completion.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ADM-12 — Explicit open decisions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: OPEN: exact billing-period and carryover durations/caps not already fixed by the authoritative subscription policy; how pending and suspended memberships count toward reserved seat capacity; any Business +-only feature beyond the absence of a seat cap; contractual retention/support commitments; and supported version boundaries for endpoint management. These require explicit canonical decisions before the relevant behaviour ships. Do not invent paid SSO/SCIM, unlimited compute/storage, support SLAs, remote full-device wipe or access to personal content as implicit Business features.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Files

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and donor-first implementation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Files is both the native CUI file-manager app and the 9to1 hosted storage service. The desktop/native product is donor-backed by Files/WinUI and MUST first reach behavioural/layout parity with the selected appropriate donor source before 9to1-specific extensions are treated as complete. CUI replaces the rendering/framework layer; the donor’s mature information architecture, workflows, interaction semantics and quality-of-life behaviour remain the baseline unless a scoped donor-parity exception is recorded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The parity baseline includes applicable donor navigation/sidebar structure, toolbar/commands, tabs, back/forward history, breadcrumbs/address bar, file/folder views, details/grid layouts, sorting/grouping, context menus, properties, previews, search, tags/favourites, drag/drop, clipboard, archives, network/location handling, keyboard shortcuts, selection behaviour, file-operation UX, progress/conflict dialogs, session restoration and other user-visible donor behaviours available in the selected legally usable source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A donor-parity manifest MUST identify the selected donor revision and classify each applicable donor feature as Preserve, Replace with 9to1-native equivalent or Not applicable. Proprietary donor AI is not copied; equivalent AI functionality uses Dulche/9to1 APIs. Subscription/account infrastructure specific to the donor is not inherited unless independently required by this specification.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Authority and ownership boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files owns file/folder identity, hosted storage, locations/providers, structural hierarchy, transfers, sync, versions, sharing/ACLs, Trash/recovery, file-operation history and filesystem-level collaboration. Files does NOT own semantic editing/collaboration inside another app’s document/project format.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The owning app remains authoritative for semantic file content and live in-document collaboration: Write owns Write-document collaboration, Present owns presentations, Boards owns Boards content, Canvas owns Canvas content, Data owns workbook/database semantics and Stack owns Git/Stack source-control semantics. Files stores and synchronises durable revisions produced by those apps but MUST NOT attempt to merge paragraphs, spreadsheet cells, Board blocks, Canvas strokes or Git histories generically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Raw/unowned binary/text files use Files’ revisioned-content storage model. When two clients concurrently modify bytes and no owning semantic merge engine exists, Files MUST preserve both conflicting revisions or expose a structured conflict; it MUST NOT silently choose the newest wall-clock timestamp.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Canonical identity and item model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every 9to1-hosted file and folder MUST have a stable FileID or FolderID independent of name, path, sort position or parent. Rename and move MUST preserve identity. Paths are human-facing projections of hierarchy and MUST NOT be used as canonical identity by other 9to1 apps.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hosted file metadata MUST include at least FileID, ParentFolderID, Name, ItemType, content/media type, owner/scope, size, created/modified timestamps, current content revision, sync/availability state, sharing state and version metadata. Folders MUST expose equivalent stable identity and ordered/queriable child relationships.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Synced local materialisations of 9to1 Drive items MUST retain metadata linking the local file to the canonical hosted FileID and base/current remote revision. Identity MUST NOT be reconstructed from pathname alone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Locations and provider abstraction

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST expose all storage roots through one typed Location/Provider abstraction. Required native location classes include 9to1 Drive, local disks, removable storage and supported network locations. Connected cloud providers MAY be added through adapters.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every provider MUST declare capabilities explicitly, including read, write, rename, move, copy, trash, permanent delete, versions, sharing, offline availability, search, streaming, server-side copy/move, change feeds and any provider-specific constraints. The UI and APIs MUST disable/report unsupported operations rather than pretending parity exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider authentication and secrets MUST be stored through secure credential references. Provider-specific OAuth/tokens MUST NOT be persisted in plaintext Files configuration or logs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Desktop shell, tabs and views

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The CUI desktop shell MUST preserve the donor’s applicable tabbed browsing, navigation history, breadcrumbs/address bar, command toolbar, sidebar/location hierarchy, selection behaviour and view-management semantics. Session restore MUST reopen the prior tab/location set where available; unavailable removable/network locations restore into an explicit unavailable state rather than being silently discarded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Grid/list/details and other applicable donor view modes MUST be supported. Sort, group, visible columns, thumbnail size and compatible folder/view preferences MAY persist per-folder or per-location according to provider capability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Folder colour customisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST support native folder-colour customisation independently of any OneDrive-specific donor capability. Users can choose from presets or an arbitrary colour using a full colour wheel/picker, apply the chosen presentation to a folder and reset it to the default appearance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Folder colour is Files presentation metadata associated with the stable folder identity, not a pathname-only hack. It must work for local folders and 9to1-hosted folders and should work for connected-provider folders where provider capability or Files-owned metadata permits. A provider that lacks native folder-colour metadata MUST NOT force Files to disable the feature if the presentation override can safely be stored by Files.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where compatible with sync/account policy, folder-colour metadata may follow the canonical folder across devices. Files MUST expose the same typed operation to Dulche and Automations, enabling actions such as changing selected/project folder colours without GUI automation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Native 9to1 creation and project integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST replace Office-centric creation defaults with first-class 9to1 creation entries. The toolbar/context New menu MUST include at least Folder, Write document, Presentation, Spreadsheet/Data artifact, Board, Canvas and Stack project when the current location/provider can store the requested artifact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Creation MUST invoke the owning app’s canonical API rather than having Files manufacture private document internals. For example, creating a Write document from Files calls the Write creation API and receives the resulting canonical ArtifactID/FileID. Files owns placement/storage; the owning app owns document structure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST support Create Stack here and Create Stack from this folder for appropriate folders. The latter registers/imports the existing source location as a Stack project rather than creating a nested duplicate source tree. Stack identity/backing remains owned by Stack; Files supplies the selected backing location/reference.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: App/project folders MAY expose a project-aware representation so users see a meaningful project entity instead of internal managed metadata by default. Advanced inspection MAY reveal underlying files when the owning app permits it. Files MUST respect app-managed/protected metadata markers and warn/block casual destructive edits that would corrupt managed project state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: 9to1 Drive integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Drive MUST appear directly in the normal Files sidebar/location tree alongside local drives and other providers. Hosted storage MUST NOT open into a separate incompatible cloud-files UI. Desktop, web and owning apps address the same canonical hosted objects by stable IDs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A file uploaded through cakemods.com and later opened in desktop Files MUST refer to the same FileID/content revision, not a separately imported desktop copy. Local materialisation is a cache/replica of the hosted object associated with FileID/revision metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hosted storage MUST expose quota/allocation, used space and pending/reserved upload space where applicable. Quota exhaustion MUST fail structurally and MUST NOT leave invisible orphan uploads.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Rapid push-based sync architecture

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sync is a core correctness requirement. 9to1 Drive MUST use event/push-driven incremental synchronisation as the normal connected path. Polling/full rescans are recovery/fallback mechanisms and MUST NOT be the primary source of ordinary change propagation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The server MUST produce ordered change events for filesystem-level changes including create, rename, move, metadata change, content-revision commit, delete, restore, share/ACL changes and relevant availability/sync metadata changes. Connected clients maintain a durable SyncCursor/last acknowledged server revision and apply deltas incrementally.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: On reconnect, a client submits its last durable cursor plus pending local operation journal state; the server returns deltas since that cursor, the client reconciles queued local operations, then resumes the live stream. Duplicate/replayed operation IDs MUST be idempotent and MUST NOT perform consequential mutations twice.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordinary metadata operations such as rename/move/create MUST be pushed immediately after commit and processed continuously by connected clients. Intentional multi-minute delays for normal metadata propagation are non-conformant. Foreground/open artifacts and explicit manual sync receive scheduling priority over background hydration/prefetch.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Optimistic local operations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: User-initiated structural operations SHOULD feel immediate. Files MAY optimistically apply a local rename/move/create to the UI before the remote round trip, but MUST record the operation durably as Pending with OperationID, expected/base revision and inverse/recovery metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If the server accepts the mutation, the operation becomes committed/synced and remote clients receive the corresponding event. If validation fails, Files MUST reconcile/reverse the optimistic state and display the structured reason; it MUST NOT leave the UI pretending the server accepted a rejected mutation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Sync and availability state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hosted items MUST expose explicit sync/availability state rather than a generic spinner. Required states include CloudOnly, Hydrating, AvailableOffline, AlwaysAvailable, LocalChanges, Uploading, Synced, Conflict, Paused and Error. Internal implementations MAY maintain separate content and metadata states so lightweight metadata can become synced while content transfer continues.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: CloudOnly means metadata is locally visible but content bytes are not guaranteed local. AvailableOffline means content is currently materialised and may be evicted by managed cache policy only when safe. AlwaysAvailable means the user has pinned the content and Files MUST retain a local copy until the user changes that policy or storage becomes critically unavailable and the user explicitly resolves the situation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening, previewing or an owning app requesting bytes for CloudOnly content triggers hydration on demand. Hydration MUST expose progress/failure and MUST NOT claim the item is locally available before durable content validation completes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Manual sync and sync-on-demand

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST provide visible manual sync controls, including Sync now, Sync this item, Sync this folder/selection, Pause sync, Resume sync, retry eligible failures and refresh/reconcile from cloud. Manual sync is an acceleration/reconciliation control, not a substitute for reliable automatic sync.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sync now MUST flush eligible pending local mutations, request current server deltas since the durable cursor, retry eligible transfers, reconcile conflicts that have deterministic policy and report the resulting pending/error/conflict state. It MUST NOT discard unsynced changes merely to match cloud state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Offline-first behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Locally materialised files/folders MUST remain usable offline according to their owning app/file-format capabilities. While offline, Files MUST allow safe queued structural operations including create folder, rename, move, delete/restore and reorganisation, and it MUST allow edits to locally available content through the owning app.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Offline mutations enter a durable ordered operation journal that survives Files/Home/process/device restart. On reconnect, operations are reconciled against remote revisions/permissions before commit. Blind last-write-wins based solely on timestamps is prohibited for conflicts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Free up space MUST verify that the canonical hosted revision is durable and equivalent/newer before evicting local bytes. Items with unsynced local content MUST NOT be evicted. AlwaysAvailable items MUST NOT be evicted by normal cache cleanup.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Real-time filesystem collaboration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST provide real-time collaboration for filesystem structure and Files-owned metadata. Connected authorised clients viewing the same hierarchy should receive live create, rename, move, delete/restore, share/ACL and metadata updates without requiring manual refresh.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structural mutations MUST carry stable OperationID, actor/caller identity, target object ID, base/expected revision, operation type and result revision. Simultaneous incompatible structural edits MUST produce a deterministic RevisionConflict/Conflict object rather than silently letting whichever request arrived last overwrite the other.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If an owning app has a file open by FileID and another collaborator moves/renames that file, Files MUST publish LocationChanged/metadata events while preserving FileID. The owning app continues editing the same canonical file without losing attachment simply because the path changed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Semantic collaboration inside a file is exclusively owned by the file’s owning app. Files receives/commits durable revisions from that collaboration layer and exposes version/storage metadata, but it MUST NOT run a second generic content-collaboration engine over the same file.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Transfers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Copy, move, upload, download and provider-transfer operations MUST be represented as durable Transfer jobs with TransferID, item set, source/destination, bytes/items totals where known, progress, state, retryability, error list and pause/resume/cancel support where technically possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hosted uploads/downloads MUST use resumable/chunked transfer when the service/provider supports it. Files/Home restart MUST resume from validated committed chunks where possible rather than restarting large transfers from zero.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transfer completion MUST include integrity validation where hashes/checksums are supported. Integrity failure is a failed transfer and MUST NOT be represented as successful-with-warning.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Destination conflicts MUST use explicit policy: Ask, Replace, KeepBoth or Skip, with ApplyToRemaining where appropriate. Automated callers MUST specify a policy or receive ConflictRequiresDecision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Version history and durable revisions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Drive files MUST have durable version history. Each durable revision MUST include VersionID/RevisionID, timestamp, actor/source, parent/base revision where relevant and content identity/hash where available. Restoring an older revision MUST create a new current revision or otherwise preserve the later history rather than deleting it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Owning apps MAY commit incremental/semantic collaboration checkpoints, but Files stores the durable file/artifact revision boundary supplied by the app. Files MUST not reinterpret app-specific internal history as generic filesystem versions unless the owning app explicitly publishes those revisions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Trash, delete and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal hosted deletion MUST be soft/recoverable. Trash records MUST preserve stable item ID, original parent/location, deletion timestamp and restoration metadata. Permanent purge is a distinct high-risk operation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deleting a Files container or reference MUST NOT silently cascade-permanently-delete separately owned embedded/project artifacts unless the owning app explicitly defines cascade semantics and Files presents the impact before execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Sharing and ACLs

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hosted files/folders MUST support first-class sharing using stable account/team/organisation principal IDs. Required ACL concepts include owner, direct grants, inherited grants and viewer/editor-style capability roles or their equivalent typed scopes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Folder permission inheritance MUST distinguish inherited from direct grants. Moving an item between differently permissioned folders MUST calculate/result in an explicit effective permission change and MUST NOT silently retain/remove direct grants contrary to the configured inheritance policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared with Me MUST reference canonical objects owned elsewhere rather than cloning them into the recipient’s Drive. Revocation affects future access immediately subject to already-downloaded/offline-data retention policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If public/link sharing is supported, link shares MUST use revocable ShareID/token state with explicit permission level and optional expiry/password where implemented. Raw file URLs MUST NOT themselves imply authority.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Search, metadata and previews

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST support filename/folder search plus indexed metadata/content search where provider/file-type policy permits. Files publishes supported searchable entities to Home’s shared index; current permissions are rechecked when rendering/opening results.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Common item metadata MUST include provider/location, type, size, relevant timestamps, owner/sharing, sync/offline state, current revision and hashes/integrity data where available. App-specific metadata MUST be namespaced/versioned.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST provide preview/thumbnail contracts. Owning apps/providers MAY register read-only preview renderers for native artifacts. Preview MUST NOT mutate the source artifact or require launching a full app window unless no lightweight preview capability exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Open routing, context actions and drag/drop

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home’s app/file-handler registry determines default/open-with routing. Native 9to1 artifacts MUST expose enough type/version metadata that routing is not dependent solely on filename extension. Users MAY choose alternate compatible handlers where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Installed apps MAY contribute typed registered context actions based on item type/capability, such as Open in Write, Add to Board, Open in Pictures, Create Stack from folder or other ecosystem actions. Context actions MUST be declared through Home’s registry and MUST NOT inject arbitrary untrusted shell code into Files.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drag/drop and clipboard operations MUST preserve operation intent, source identity and provider capability. Cross-provider drag MUST make copy-vs-move semantics explicit. A cut/paste MUST NOT delete the source until destination commit succeeds.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: AI bar and privacy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST host the global persistent contextual AI bar. The Files context snapshot includes current location/provider, selected FileIDs/FolderIDs, artifact types, sync state and permissions. AI requests use typed Files/owning-app/Stack actions for operations such as organise, rename, move, convert, summarise or create a Stack.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selecting a private local file MUST NOT silently upload file content to a cloud model. Dulche’s local/cloud privacy and permission rules apply. Context handoff MUST identify the exact file/revision being provided and whether bytes/content leave the device.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST remain fully functional with AI disabled/unavailable. AI is additive and MUST NOT replace essential manual file-management UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Operation journal, undo and change feed

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consequential filesystem operations MUST be recorded in a durable operation journal with OperationID, actor/caller, target object IDs, source/destination where applicable, base/result revisions, state and structured error/result. The journal supports crash recovery, sync reconciliation and auditability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Safely reversible operations such as rename, move and soft-delete SHOULD expose undo by performing a real inverse storage mutation against current revision checks. Undo MUST NOT be UI-only fiction and MUST fail explicitly if intervening changes make the inverse unsafe.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST expose a resumable typed change feed with stable event IDs/cursors for create/change/move/share/delete/restore/sync-state and other supported filesystem events. Automations/watchers can resume from a cursor without arbitrary full rescans.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Properties and sync diagnostics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Properties/details surface MUST expose stable identity, path/location, provider, type, size, timestamps, owner/sharing, sync/offline state, current version/history access, app association and provider-specific metadata where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST provide clear sync diagnostics for 9to1 Drive, including current connectivity/server contact, pending uploads/downloads, pending structural operations, conflicts, paused/error state, offline-pinned usage and local cache usage. Item-level errors MUST expose local/base/cloud revision information where relevant and provide Resolve/Retry/View details actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Safety and filesystem edge cases

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider adapters and local materialisation MUST define handling for illegal/reserved filenames, case sensitivity, path length, path traversal, symlinks/reparse points and unsupported metadata. Remote names MUST NOT escape the intended local sync root or overwrite unrelated local paths.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Filesystem shortcuts/symlinks MUST remain distinct from 9to1 artifact references/shortcuts. Copying a reference MUST NOT accidentally clone the referenced canonical artifact unless the user explicitly chooses duplication.
