heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files MUST return structured failures including ItemNotFound, RevisionConflict, NameConflict, ConflictRequiresDecision, PermissionDenied, ProviderUnavailable, ProviderCapabilityUnsupported, QuotaExceeded, Offline, TransferInterrupted, IntegrityFailed, SyncConflict, FileInUse, StorageUnavailable, InvalidName, DestinationUnavailable, HomeServiceUnavailable and structured partial bulk results in addition to the global error contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Platform behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows and 9to1-OS native Files expose local, removable, network, hosted and connected-provider locations according to platform/provider capability. Web Files exposes hosted/provider-accessible content but MUST NOT pretend to have arbitrary access to the browser user’s local filesystem. Browser local upload/download uses explicit browser-authorised file/folder selection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The CUI port accounts for applicable Files/WinUI donor functionality and preserves its core layout/workflows/QoL through a donor-parity manifest.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Drive appears as a normal first-class location and the same FileID opened via web and desktop represents the same canonical hosted object.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rename/create/move on one connected client appears live on another client without manual refresh and preserves stable item identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Moving/renaming a file while it is open in its owning app does not break the open document because the app remains attached by FileID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual Sync now flushes eligible pending operations, retrieves server deltas and reports unresolved errors/conflicts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A CloudOnly file hydrates on demand; AvailableOffline works without network; AlwaysAvailable survives restart/cache cleanup.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Free up space refuses to evict unsynced content and verifies durable cloud revision before eviction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Offline structural operations survive device restart and reconcile correctly after reconnect.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Two conflicting concurrent binary/raw-file edits preserve both revisions or create an explicit conflict; no version is silently lost.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Two collaborators concurrently reorganising the same hierarchy receive deterministic structural conflict behaviour rather than blind last-write-wins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A large resumable upload survives Files/Home restart and continues from validated committed progress.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A failed transfer integrity check is reported as failure and never as completed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Version history and restore preserve later history and identify actor/source/revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Trash/restore/purge behave distinctly and purge uses the elevated destructive flow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sharing/ACL changes propagate to connected clients and revocation prevents future authorised access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Creating Write/Present/Data/Board/Canvas artifacts from Files invokes the owning app and creates canonical artifacts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Create Stack here/from this folder produces the expected Stack project without duplicating existing source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Owning-app real-time collaboration commits durable Files revisions without Files attempting semantic content merges.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider capability differences disable/report unsupported operations rather than pretending support.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Bulk operations return exact succeeded/failed/skipped outcomes and never silently lose items.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Private local content is not sent to a cloud AI merely because it is selected in Files.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Change-feed cursor resume does not require a full filesystem rescan and does not duplicate consequential events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home crash/recovery preserves pending sync journal state and does not create duplicate operations or storage corruption.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A very large hierarchy can process ordinary incremental changes without complete rescans for each event.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Connect

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and donor strategy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Connect is the native CUI communications and collaboration application for people, teams and organisations. It combines real-time messaging, voice/video calling, SMS/RCS integration, organisational collaboration and the full Mail experience inside one coherent product. Connect is the parent communications product; Mail remains a first-class child mode/subsystem rather than being removed or flattened into chat.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The whole Connect application MUST use an open-source donor/reference for mature real-time communications behaviour. Element, together with Matrix as its underlying open communications protocol/reference architecture, is the preferred donor/reference for real-time messaging, rooms/conversations, threading, reactions, multi-device state, end-to-end encryption, presence-compatible collaboration and calling. The selected donor revision and applicable licensing obligations MUST be recorded in the donor-parity manifest before implementation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The existing Mail subsystem retains Thunderbird as its preferred mature donor/reference for email protocol, MIME, IMAP/SMTP, authentication, offline mail, attachments, drafts, folders/labels, threading, certificates and mature email edge cases. Connect MUST NOT replace Thunderbird mail behaviour with a reduced chat-derived email implementation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Donor parity applies to mature behavioural capability, interoperability and edge-case handling, not donor-native visual chrome. Connect MUST use a modern native CUI design consistent with 9to1. Proprietary donor services or branding MUST be replaced with 9to1-native equivalents where required.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Architecture and canonical entities

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST maintain stable canonical identities for at least UserID, ProfileID, OrganisationID, MembershipID, RoleID, ConversationID, RoomID/ChannelID where applicable, MessageID, ThreadID, CallID, ParticipantID, ContactRelationshipID, ReportID, IncidentID, EnforcementActionID and BanEvasionCaseID. Display names, usernames, email addresses, phone numbers, room names and mutable paths MUST NOT be used as canonical identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Email messages remain Mail entities governed by the Mail subsystem and its provider semantics. Native Connect chat/room messages remain Connect/Matrix-style communication entities. The product MAY provide unified navigation/search/notifications over both, but MUST NOT merge email and real-time messaging into one incompatible storage/protocol model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect SHOULD use canonical 9to1 services rather than duplicating them. Shared files SHOULD reference canonical Files objects when applicable; assignments/tasks SHOULD reference canonical Planner objects where appropriate; Home owns notifications/permissions; Dulche provides AI; Contacts/people services own canonical contact data where defined.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Conversations, organisations and hierarchy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST support one-to-one conversations, group conversations, organisation/team rooms or channels, threaded replies, reactions, message edits, message deletion according to policy, typing indicators, read state/receipts where enabled, presence/availability controls, mentions, attachments/media and conversation search subject to encryption/indexing constraints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MAY belong to multiple organisations simultaneously. Organisations MUST support nested teams/departments/groups and explicit role/membership relationships, including organisational hierarchies such as management/employee or school leadership/department/teacher/student structures. Hierarchy MUST be represented through stable role/membership data rather than inferred only from room placement or display names.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Role and organisation policy MAY govern room creation, membership management, announcement rights, moderation powers, task assignment and administrative settings, but organisation policy MUST NOT silently override personal privacy protections that are not genuinely necessary for the organisation to operate.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Mail mode

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail is a first-class Connect mode and retains the complete canonical Mail specification, Mail APIs and Thunderbird donor contract. Users MUST be able to use Mail as a complete manual email client with AI unavailable. Connect MUST provide coherent navigation between Mail and real-time communications while preserving the different underlying protocols, privacy properties and provider semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MAY remain independently deep-linkable and launchable where the package/shell architecture supports app shortcuts, but such launch targets resolve to the Mail mode of the canonical Connect application rather than creating a second incompatible Mail implementation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Native messaging encryption and privacy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native Connect conversations MUST use end-to-end encryption by default. Ordinary native Connect users MUST NOT be offered a misleading normal-chat mode that silently downgrades private communication to server-readable plaintext merely for implementation convenience.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation MUST follow the platform-wide Privacy Ceiling and apply stricter communications protections where required. Content decryption keys MUST be available only to authorised endpoint devices/participants under the declared trust model. Servers MUST NOT possess a universal content-decryption key or silent moderation/decryption backdoor while the product claims E2EE.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multi-device encryption MUST define device identity, device trust, key distribution, verification, rotation, lost-device handling, session recovery and cryptographic backup/recovery. Recovery MUST NOT introduce a server-held master key that silently allows universal message decryption.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST minimise communication metadata separately from content encryption. Participant graphs, timestamps, delivery state, IP/network information, device identifiers, routing metadata and notification data MUST be collected/retained only as required for operation, safety or declared policy and MUST NOT be presented to users as E2EE-protected when they are observable to infrastructure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Notification delivery MUST minimise plaintext leakage. Notification previews of encrypted conversations MUST use the most private technically reliable path and MUST respect user settings; push providers MUST NOT receive unnecessary message content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search/indexing over encrypted content SHOULD occur locally or through another architecture that preserves the declared E2EE model. Server-side plaintext indexing of native E2EE conversations is prohibited unless the user has explicitly exported/disclosed specific content into a separately governed service.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Disappearing messages

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST support disappearing-message policies at conversation and/or message scope. Policies MAY include predefined and custom expiry periods and MUST expose the active expiry state visibly enough for participants to understand it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Expiry MUST be represented canonically and reconcile across authorised devices, including devices that were offline at the expiry time. Expired content MUST be removed from ordinary conversation history and applicable local indexes/caches according to the declared lifecycle.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST NOT claim that disappearing messages prevent screenshots, manual copying, external capture or information already legitimately disclosed outside the conversation. Quoted/replied-to message representations MUST NOT preserve the full expired content indefinitely unless an explicit retention/evidence rule requires it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Safety reports/evidence records that lawfully and transparently retain reported content are separate from ordinary disappearing-message history and MUST have their own access, purpose and retention policy.

heading: HEADING_3
text: SMS and RCS

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST support SMS and RCS where the current platform, telephony stack, carrier/provider and user permissions allow it. SMS/RCS identities and transport state MUST remain distinct from native Connect messaging.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The UI MUST truthfully represent the protection of the actual transport used. Ordinary SMS MUST NOT be labelled end-to-end encrypted. RCS MUST show E2EE only when encryption has actually been negotiated/supported for that conversation and participant set.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If an intended RCS message would fall back to SMS, any material change in privacy/security capability MUST be represented clearly enough that the user is not led to believe the stronger state still applies. Transport fallback MUST NOT reuse an E2EE badge/state from the prior route.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Voice and video calling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST provide mature one-to-one and group voice/video calling with expected modern functionality including incoming/outgoing calls, ringing, missed calls, call history, join/leave/reconnect, participant roster, grid/speaker layouts, pin/spotlight where applicable, microphone mute/unmute, camera enable/disable, camera switching, input/output device selection, screen/window/application sharing, optional system-audio sharing where supported, reactions, raise hand, in-call text chat, picture-in-picture/full-screen and accessible keyboard/screen-reader controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Calls MUST use end-to-end encrypted media wherever the selected call architecture supports the native Connect trust model. Signalling and sensitive call state SHOULD receive equivalent or stronger protection where technically feasible. Infrastructure MUST NOT claim stronger privacy than the actual transport provides.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Microphone, camera and screen-capture permissions MUST be explicit, visible and revocable. Joining a call MUST NOT silently enable the camera or microphone contrary to the user's saved/default state. The UI MUST continuously and unmistakably show local mic/camera/screen-share state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Call infrastructure MUST minimise retained metadata, and self-hosted/private infrastructure SHOULD be supported where compatible with the donor/protocol architecture. TURN/relay/direct-connect behaviour and the associated exposure of participant network addresses MUST be documented and privacy-aware.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background blur, noise suppression, gain control, camera filters/effects, virtual backgrounds and similar media processing SHOULD run locally where technically practical. A cosmetic filter MUST NOT silently upload raw camera/microphone content to an external processor.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recording, transcription and AI participation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recording is disabled by default. Starting recording MUST use a Request Recording workflow rather than an immediate unilateral record action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before recording begins, every current participant MUST explicitly approve the recording request. Any participant declining or failing to approve within the defined request state prevents recording from starting. Approval is scoped to that recording session and MUST NOT become a permanent blanket permission.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When recording is active, all participants MUST receive a persistent, unmistakable recording indicator. A participant joining after recording has started MUST be informed before/while joining that recording is active and MUST explicitly acknowledge/approve participation under the recording state before their media is included. A new participant's refusal MUST prevent their media from being recorded and, where the architecture cannot isolate them, MUST pause/stop recording until consent is resolved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recording state, requester, participant approvals, start/stop times and resulting artifact identity MUST be auditable. Recordings MUST be stored as permissioned canonical artifacts with explicit owner/access/retention policy rather than hidden provider blobs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recording permission MUST NOT imply permission for transcription, AI summarisation or remote model processing. Recording, transcription and AI participation are separate capabilities with separate disclosure/permission requirements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Adding Dulche, an Agent, transcription service or other non-human processor to a human conversation/call MUST be visible to affected participants where it can receive their communication. Ordinary access by the local Connect client to decrypted E2EE content does NOT automatically grant Dulche/cloud models access.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Contact and communication privacy controls

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST provide first-class Block, Mute and Contact Settings controls. Blocking and muting MUST be semantically distinct: mute suppresses attention/notifications according to user policy; block prevents the blocked identity from contacting/interacting with the blocker through applicable Connect channels and MUST be enforced beyond merely hiding content locally.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Contact Settings MUST allow the user to control, where applicable, who can directly message them, call them, video call them, add/invite them to groups, see presence/last-active, see read receipts and access profile/contact fields. Unknown contacts MAY be routed to message/contact requests rather than the primary inbox.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Per-conversation notification/mute controls, read-receipt controls, presence controls, privacy/discoverability controls and block lists MUST be available without requiring AI.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Reporting and Trust & Safety

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST provide a first-class Report workflow for inappropriate, abusive, fraudulent or illegal content/behaviour. Reporting MUST be possible from messages, conversations, calls, contacts/accounts and relevant media where evidence is available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Because native Connect messaging is E2EE, routine server-side moderation MUST NOT silently scan all decrypted private conversations. A participant-initiated report MAY deliberately disclose selected reported messages/media and the minimum necessary surrounding context/provenance to the Trust & Safety system. The reporting UI MUST make the disclosure scope understandable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reports are allegations, not strikes. A Report MUST NOT automatically become a verified violation or count as an offence merely because it exists. Trust & Safety must distinguish Report, Incident and EnforcementAction as separate canonical objects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reported user-supplied text, quoted messages, media metadata and report descriptions are evidence/input, not privileged instructions to the moderation system. Prompt-like content inside evidence MUST NOT be able to override moderation policy or system instructions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Moderation AI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MAY use an intelligent AI-assisted Trust & Safety evaluator to triage reports, correlate evidence, identify repeat patterns, create/maintain structured Incident records and recommend or apply policy-defined protective restrictions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The moderation AI MUST NOT expose a direct free-form conversational prompt surface to ordinary users. Users interact through structured report/appeal flows; they MUST NOT be able to directly prompt the moderation model to punish another user.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The evaluator SHOULD produce structured results including alleged policy category, evidence reviewed, provenance, confidence/uncertainty, severity, verified prior Incidents where policy permits, pattern/repetition state, recommended action, automatic-action eligibility and human-review requirement. User accusation volume alone MUST NOT be treated as proof.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automatic detection/evaluation MUST resist coordinated false-report campaigns, duplicate-report amplification, fabricated evidence where provenance can be checked, prompt injection within evidence and circular reliance on previous unverified allegations. Dismissed/overturned reports/incidents MUST NOT continue increasing enforcement severity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Protective restrictions MAY be applied quickly when needed to stop ongoing harm, including reporter-specific contact blocking, temporary DM/call restrictions, new-contact limits, invitation restrictions, media restrictions or rate limits. These temporary protections are distinct from a Connect-wide ban.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Severe-offence ban threshold

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Connect-wide account ban is a last-resort enforcement action reserved for severe offences or a substantial verified history of serious misconduct. Ordinary disagreements, unpopular opinions, isolated low-level rudeness or weak/ambiguous reports MUST NOT result in a Connect-wide ban.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ban-eligible examples include accounts demonstrably operated primarily for scams/phishing or large-scale malicious spam; repeated targeted harassment/stalking/doxxing; repeated serious threats or malicious impersonation/scams; distribution of illegal images/content; or comparably severe abuse supported by evidence and applicable policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A substantial history means verified Incident records, not raw Report count. Multiple unverified or dismissed reports MUST NOT accumulate as though they were convictions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Enforcement SHOULD be proportionate below the severe-ban threshold and MAY include warnings, temporary communication restrictions, feature-specific suspension, contact/request limits, group-invite restrictions, rate limiting or temporary account suspension according to policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every ban MUST reference the applicable policy category, supporting IncidentIDs/evidence basis, decision source, effective time, duration/permanence, review status and appeal state. The system MUST preserve the distinction between evidence, analysis and final enforcement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permanent or long-duration account-wide sanctions SHOULD require stronger evidentiary confidence and/or human review according to severity and policy. Clearly malicious automated/scam accounts with strong evidence MAY be restricted rapidly without artificial delay merely because the final action is severe.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Appeals

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Affected users MUST have a clear appeal mechanism for significant restrictions and bans. Appeal review MUST inspect the evidence and enforcement decision rather than merely rerun the identical model prompt and automatically return the same result.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overturned enforcement MUST remove or appropriately quarantine the sanction's contribution to future escalation/ban-evasion logic. Audit history MAY retain the historical decision for accountability, but it MUST NOT continue operating as an active verified offence.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Ban-evasion and alternate-account detection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An active Connect ban MUST NOT be trivially circumventable by creating or switching to another account. Connect MUST provide a privacy-preserving Ban Evasion Risk Engine capable of identifying likely alternate accounts used to evade an active severe sanction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Detection MUST be purpose-limited to security/abuse enforcement and MUST comply with the Privacy Ceiling. It SHOULD combine multiple relevant signals rather than relying on one simplistic identifier. Signals MAY include verified account relationships, device/account linkage legitimately available to 9to1, authentication attributes, repeated malicious behavioural patterns, overlap of abuse targets, timing patterns, organisation relationships and payment/entitlement linkage where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared IP address, household, school/workplace network, carrier NAT, VPN use or a shared device MUST NOT by itself establish that two accounts belong to the same banned person. Legitimate possession of multiple accounts is not ban evasion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The engine MUST distinguish low-, medium- and high-confidence linkage. Low-confidence matches SHOULD trigger additional verification, monitoring within permitted bounds or temporary protective limits rather than automatic permanent inheritance of the original ban. High-confidence evidence tied to a severe active ban MAY cause the alternate account to inherit/continue the restriction according to policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every suspected linkage MUST create a BanEvasionCase with evidence/signal references, original EnforcementActionID, confidence, decision and review/appeal state. Banned-account linkage MUST NOT depend on weakening E2EE or reading unrelated private messages.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Signals from an overturned/dismissed ban MUST be removed from active enforcement decisions. Anti-alt detection MUST NOT evolve into a general-purpose cross-service fingerprinting system unrelated to preventing sanction evasion.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI and encrypted communication boundary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MAY assist with permitted Connect tasks such as drafting, summarisation, search, action extraction and organisation, but encrypted communication content is not automatically AI context. The user/organisation policy and the local/cloud Privacy Ceiling determine what content may be exposed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A local AI route MAY process authorised content locally according to permissions. Sending decrypted chat/call/email content to a cloud model requires an authorised cloud-processing route and MUST NOT occur merely because the cloud model is the global fallback.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated actions that send messages, email, make calls, change membership, report users or perform enforcement are consequential typed actions subject to the normal Home permission/risk model plus any stricter Connect rule.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Agent updates — contact through Connect

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agents MUST be emailable, callable and textable through Connect. This includes email through Connect's Mail subsystem, supported voice-call routes, and text messaging through Connect, including SMS/RCS when an authorised configured provider/device supports that transport. Agents MUST appear as addressable Agent contacts rather than requiring users to open a separate Agent chat before contacting them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Channel addresses/endpoints MUST resolve to the same canonical Agent identity. Incoming contact MUST route to that Agent and its authorised runtime; responses MUST return through the relevant Connect channel with conversation/call/run correlation. Agent permissions, memory boundaries, caller access, availability, privacy, retention and external-action approvals remain governed by the existing contracts. A message or call from a third party MUST NOT automatically acquire the account owner's permissions. Unsupported or disconnected transports MUST be reported accurately. Provisioning paid numbers, carrier services or other paid infrastructure requires separate spending authorisation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Connect Agent-channel API and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extend Connect’s existing contact and communication APIs for Agent contact/channel configuration, endpoint resolution and the supported email, voice-call and text operations. Preserve canonical Agent, Conversation, Call and Run IDs, permission scopes, correlation and idempotency on retries. Tests MUST deliver an email, call and text to the intended canonical Agent through each supported configured route and verify its response on that route; cover revoked caller access, disconnected or unsupported transport, failed delivery and prevention of duplicate external sends. A required route lacking a working supported implementation remains an explicit gap, not a completed parity claim.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Connect API and events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST expose typed APIs for conversations/messages, organisations/memberships/roles, contacts/privacy controls, calls, SMS/RCS routing where supported, reporting, safety state and user-authorised actions. Email-specific operations remain under the canonical 9to1.Mail API and are reachable through Connect without duplicating them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Minimum Connect API families MUST include conversation list/get/create/update/membership, message send/edit/delete/react/thread, contact/block/mute/settings, organisation/membership/role, call start/join/leave/media-state/screen-share/record-request/record-state, report/create/status/appeal, and change/event subscriptions. Every consequential action MUST use stable IDs, structured results, revision/conflict semantics and the global permission/audit contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Trust & Safety internal APIs MUST be separately permissioned from ordinary client APIs. Direct user clients MUST NOT receive privileged moderation-model prompt access or arbitrary enforcement mutation authority.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Failure and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect MUST provide structured failures including ConversationNotFound, MembershipDenied, EncryptionStateUnavailable, DeviceNotTrusted, KeyRecoveryRequired, TransportUnavailable, SMSFallbackRequired, CallUnavailable, MediaPermissionDenied, RecordingConsentRequired, RecordingConsentDeclined, ParticipantConsentPending, ReportNotFound, EvidenceUnavailable, EnforcementDenied, AppealUnavailable, BanEvasionReviewRequired and ProviderCapabilityUnsupported in addition to global errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Network interruption MUST preserve unsent messages/call state truthfully, reconcile delivered/read state after reconnect and avoid duplicate sends. Encryption/session recovery MUST NOT silently reset conversation security or create a new unverified device identity without disclosure.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connect is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least: native one-to-one and group chat with E2EE; multi-device key/device trust and recovery; threads/reactions/typing/read-state/presence controls; organisation/team hierarchy; complete Thunderbird-derived Mail mode; SMS/RCS transport-state truthfulness; mature one-to-one/group voice/video calls; screen sharing and standard call controls; local media effects where applicable; unanimous recording consent including future joiners; distinct recording/transcription/AI permissions; block/mute/contact privacy controls; disappearing messages; participant-initiated encrypted-chat reporting without universal server decryption; structured AI-assisted report triage without user prompt access to the moderation model; proportionate restrictions; severe-only Connect-wide bans; appeals; privacy-preserving ban-evasion detection; and enforcement of the platform-wide Privacy Ceiling.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Mail

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and donor strategy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Mail is the native CUI email client for connected accounts. It MUST be a fully capable manual email client with AI disabled or unavailable. AI is additive: it may summarise, search, draft, rewrite and triage, but core reading, composition, sending, organisation, search, offline use and account management MUST remain directly usable without AI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Thunderbird is the preferred mature technical donor/reference for email protocol and compatibility behaviour, including IMAP, SMTP, OAuth, MIME parsing, attachments, offline mail, drafts, folders, threading, search foundations, junk/spam handling, certificates and mature email edge cases. Donor reuse MUST comply with the selected source version and licensing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Donor parity applies to mature email capabilities and behaviours, NOT to Thunderbird’s visual shell. Legacy donor chrome, menus, dialogs, pane styling or dated interaction patterns MUST NOT be reproduced merely for parity. The final product MUST be a modern, clean, native CUI Mail interface designed for 9to1.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Mail donor-parity manifest MUST identify the selected donor revision and classify applicable capabilities as Preserve, Replace with 9to1-native equivalent or Not applicable. Proprietary AI/subscription services from any donor/provider are not copied.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Modern CUI shell and responsive layout

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The default desktop layout MUST use a clean three-pane structure: navigation/account sidebar, message/conversation list and reading pane. Visual separation MUST be subtle and CUI-native rather than relying on heavy boxes, legacy toolbars or nested window chrome. Message content should receive the majority of visual emphasis.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to select reading-pane right, reading-pane bottom or reading-pane off, plus supported density options. Smaller windows MUST responsively collapse the layout into two-pane or single-pane navigation without squeezing unreadable columns.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The message list MUST prioritise sender/avatar or initials, subject, concise preview, timestamp, unread/important state and attachment/category indicators. Low-frequency controls MAY appear on hover/selection while common quick actions such as archive, delete, star and snooze remain directly discoverable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The reading pane MUST present a compact sender/recipient/date header, clear reply/reply-all/forward/other actions and an uncluttered message body. Long conversations MUST support collapsing older messages/quoted sections without losing access to full content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The final client MUST not expose donor-native UI surfaces. Settings, account management, compose, security prompts and advanced inspection must all use 9to1 CUI unless an OS-level credential/security dialog is explicitly required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Sidebar and navigation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST provide a unified top-level navigation including Unified Inbox, Starred/Favourites, Snoozed, Drafts, Sent, Scheduled, Outbox, Archive, Junk and Trash where the effective connected-account capabilities permit them. Individual accounts appear below with collapsible provider-native folders/labels.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unified views are query/projection surfaces over canonical provider/account messages and MUST NOT duplicate messages into a separate mailbox. Actions taken from a unified view route to the owning AccountID/provider semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider-native structures MUST be preserved. Gmail-style labels, Outlook categories/folders and generic IMAP folders MUST NOT be flattened into one simplistic hierarchy when that would break provider behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Account and provider model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every connected mailbox MUST have stable AccountID identity independent of mutable email address/display name. MailAccount MUST store at least provider type, provider account identity, primary address/display name, supported capability set, authentication reference, sync configuration, signature configuration and sending configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST support generic IMAP + SMTP as a baseline and provider-native adapters where beneficial, including Gmail/Google and Outlook/Microsoft. Provider adapters MAY expose richer push, label, thread, archive, snooze, scheduled-send or search behaviours while remaining behind the common Mail contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider capabilities MUST be discovered/declared explicitly, including labels vs folders, archive, snooze, scheduled send, native search, push/change feed, undo send, aliases/from identities, read receipts, encryption/security features and provider-specific actions. Unsupported actions MUST be hidden/disabled or return ProviderCapabilityUnsupported rather than appearing functional.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: OAuth 2.0 is preferred when supported. Credentials/tokens MUST be stored through secure credential references. Token refresh, revoked access, reauthentication, app-password/provider-password flows and certificate errors MUST be handled without deleting valid local cached mail.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Message, thread and folder identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST maintain stable local canonical identities for AccountID-scoped messages and threads. Message records MUST include MessageID, AccountID, provider-native message ID, Internet Message-ID where present, ThreadID/provider conversation identity where applicable, folder/label state, timestamps, sender/recipients, flags and provider change/revision token where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Internet Message-ID MUST NOT be assumed globally unique enough to serve as the sole database identity. Provider-native IDs are authoritative only within their AccountID/provider scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Threads/conversations preserve ordered references to individual messages, participants, subject/summary metadata, unread count and latest-message state. Provider-native thread identity MUST be preserved when available. Generic IMAP MAY use a deterministic local threading model, but Mail MUST distinguish local grouping from provider-native conversation identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST NOT automatically merge threads across separate accounts solely because subjects or Message-ID relationships appear similar.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Message rendering and privacy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST safely render plain-text and HTML email, inline images, quoted replies, signatures and attachments. HTML MUST be sanitised; arbitrary message script/executable application code MUST NOT execute in the trusted Mail surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Remote images/external tracking resources MUST be blocked, privacy-proxied or otherwise privacy-controlled by default according to Mail privacy settings. The UI MUST provide a clear per-message/per-sender Load remote content/trust action rather than silently leaking message opens.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MAY offer tracking-protection features such as known tracking-pixel blocking or privacy-preserving remote-image proxying, but protection state MUST be visible and breakage must be recoverable by the user.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Compose and drafts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compose MUST use a clean CUI editor that can operate as a focused pane/window and provides From identity/account, To, Cc, Bcc, subject, rich-text body, plain-text mode, attachments, inline images, signatures, reply/reply-all/forward and provider-supported message options. Recipient fields SHOULD progressively disclose Cc/Bcc rather than permanently consuming space.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The composer SHOULD use Home’s Shared Productivity Engine for supported rich-text primitives, while exporting through an email-compatible formatting pipeline that produces valid email-safe HTML plus a plain-text alternative. Unsupported rich shared objects MUST be explicitly converted/attached rather than silently mangled.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drafts MUST autosave and survive app/process restart. Local/provider draft conflicts MUST preserve both revisions or surface a conflict rather than silently overwriting newer user text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: FromIdentity MUST be separate from AccountID so provider-supported aliases can define address, display name, Reply-To and signature independently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Attachments and Files integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Attachments MUST expose stable AttachmentID scoped to MessageID plus filename, MIME type, size, Content-ID where relevant, download/cache state and security state. Attachment bytes MAY hydrate on demand according to offline/cache policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Attachment actions MUST integrate with Files/Home handlers, including Open, Save, Save to 9to1 Drive, Save all, Add to Board and Open in compatible owning 9to1 app where applicable. Attachment saving creates a normal Files item and MUST not alter the original message.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compose MUST support Attach from Files across local files, 9to1 Drive and authorised connected providers. A future/share-link mode MAY send a hosted Files link instead of attaching bytes, but it MUST be an explicit access-semantic change rather than an invisible optimisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Sync, push and offline behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail sync MUST use the fastest reliable provider mechanism available: provider push/change streams, webhooks or IMAP IDLE/incremental change tokens first; periodic polling/full mailbox scans only as fallback/recovery. Every account maintains durable sync/change cursor state and pending local operation state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST provide Sync all, Sync this account, Sync this folder, Retry failed sync, Pause sync and Resume sync controls plus clear sync diagnostics including last successful contact, pending operations and errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Offline use MUST support configurable caching of headers, recent/full message bodies and attachments on demand, plus selected folders/messages available offline. Cached mail remains readable without network.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Offline-safe mutations including read/unread, star, label/category, move, archive, delete/restore, draft updates and queued sends MUST enter a durable operation journal and reconcile on reconnect using provider change tokens/revisions. Blind timestamp-based last-write-wins is prohibited for conflicts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Send pipeline, Outbox and Undo Send

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Outgoing messages MUST have explicit lifecycle states including Draft, Queued, Sending, Sent, Failed and Cancelled. An offline Send enters Outbox/Queued and MUST NOT be represented as Sent until the provider accepts the message.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST support client-side Undo Send through a configurable local hold delay before provider submission, even when a provider has no native undo. During the hold window the user can cancel. After irreversible provider submission, Mail MUST NOT claim that the send remains undoable unless the provider genuinely supports cancellation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Send failures MUST remain visible/retryable in Outbox with the actual provider/transport error and must not silently discard the draft/message.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Scheduled send

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scheduled send MUST use provider-native scheduling when available. Otherwise Mail may use a reliable 9to1 server/cloud scheduler or device-local scheduler only when its execution guarantees are accurately represented.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The UI MUST identify execution location/guarantee as Provider scheduled, 9to1 cloud scheduled or This device scheduled. Device-local schedules MUST clearly state that execution depends on the device/runtime being available; they MUST NOT masquerade as guaranteed server scheduling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Search and smart views

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail search MUST support sender, recipient, subject, message body where indexed/available, attachment name, date range, account, folder/label, read/unread, attachment presence, categories/labels and starred state. Provider-native search MAY be used but cached/offline content MUST also support local indexed search where policy permits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to save supported queries as smart views/folders. Smart views are dynamic queries over canonical messages and MUST NOT duplicate messages.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Rules and automation integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST support convenient message rules/filters for provider/local-supported triggers such as sender, recipient, subject and message metadata with actions such as move, label/category, mark read, star, notify or hand off to Automations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app consequential workflows MUST be represented through Automations/typed app APIs rather than hidden arbitrary scripts inside Mail rules. Rule execution MUST be auditable and idempotent where replay is possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Snooze, archive and delete semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Snooze MUST hide/deprioritise a message/thread until a specified time and restore it to the appropriate attention view. Provider-native snooze is preferred where available; a 9to1 metadata-layer implementation MAY be used only if it preserves provider consistency.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Archive and Delete MUST be provider-aware. Archive may mean removing an Inbox label or moving to a configured Archive folder depending on provider. Delete MUST distinguish remove-current-label/folder, move to Trash and permanent delete where the provider exposes those concepts. Permanent deletion is a high-risk explicit action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Signatures, aliases and contacts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST support per-account and per-FromIdentity signatures with rich-text plus plain-text fallback. Signature selection may be automatic per identity but remains user-editable in the composer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recipient autocomplete SHOULD use authorised shared Contacts/people services and provider contacts where configured, with local recipient history as fallback. Mail MUST NOT make its message database the canonical contacts store.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Notifications

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST publish typed notifications through Home Notifications for events such as new important mail, send failure, authentication required and significant sync error. Notifications MUST deep-link to the exact AccountID/ThreadID/MessageID or relevant settings surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST NOT implement a second incompatible notification centre; Home owns notification history/preferences/OS bridging.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI bar and AI action boundary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST host the global persistent bottom AI bar. Its context snapshot may include AccountID, current folder/view, selected MessageIDs/ThreadIDs, DraftID and selected recipients/content according to current permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Supported AI experiences MAY include summarise thread, identify action items, draft/rewrite a reply, conversational mailbox search, triage suggestions and creation of typed cross-app actions such as Planner items or saving attachments.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordinary conversational AI MUST NOT silently send email merely because it generated a draft. Sending remains a consequential typed Mail action subject to the Home permission/risk model. An explicitly authorised Agent/Automation MAY send autonomously only when its effective permission/trust scope permits Mail.Send.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail content provided to Dulche MUST obey local/cloud privacy policy. Selecting a mailbox/thread MUST NOT implicitly upload the whole mailbox to a cloud model. Context scope such as selected messages, current thread or explicit mailbox search MUST be represented and permission-filtered.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Security, phishing and remote-content safety

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail MUST provide conventional safety signals without claiming infallible detection, including clear actual sender address vs display name, suspicious-link/attachment warnings, executable attachment restrictions and provider/header authentication information such as SPF/DKIM/DMARC results where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Read receipts MUST require user/provider policy approval and MUST NOT be automatically sent solely because a sender requested one.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider spam/junk systems SHOULD be used when available; generic accounts may use local classification/rules. Mark Junk/Not Junk MUST update provider state when supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: OpenPGP, S/MIME and advanced mail features

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where supported by the selected mature donor source and target platform, Mail MUST preserve applicable OpenPGP and S/MIME signing/encryption workflows, certificate/key management and message verification/decryption behaviour unless a documented parity exception exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Advanced message inspection MUST expose message source/raw MIME, headers, Internet Message-ID and provider/debug details without making these advanced controls dominate the default reading experience.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Print and export

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Messages/threads MUST support print and supported export such as PDF, .eml and applicable text/HTML forms. Export MUST preserve attachments only when the selected format/workflow explicitly supports them.
