heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spaces MUST return structured failures including SpaceNotFound, ConversationNotFound, MessageNotFound, ContextUnavailable, ContextRevisionConflict, SourceIngestionFailed, PermissionDenied, ModelUnavailable, ModelCapabilityMismatch, ToolUnavailable, ToolFailed, ArtifactUnavailable, ArtifactRevisionConflict, RunBlocked, RunCancelled, RunFailed, WebAccessDisabled, MemoryScopeDenied, SharedContextUnavailable, ProtectedSpaceMutationDenied, InvalidGraphConnection, GraphValidationFailed and ExtensionHookIncompatible in addition to the global error contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spaces is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Chat, Study, Tasks, Agent, Shopping, Research, Translate and Experiences remain distinct protected first-party Space types.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Translate Space shows selected language chips immediately above the normal chatbar, uses normal Space context, and renders each target-language result as its own labelled assistant speech bubble.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Experiences maintains canonical structured Experience state separately from generated narrative text, including hidden/private state where configured.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Experience branching/rewind preserves the matching conversation and Experience-state revision without pretending to undo real external side effects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Agent characters receive only their authorised Experience view, while lightweight characters do not require permanent Den Agent creation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Experiences can launch a formal Play Match and receive an explicit Play-to-Experiences handoff without implicitly merging MatchState and ExperienceState.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: + New Space creates a user-defined Space and Edit Spaces can reorder/nest/manage Spaces without exposing protected first-party internals.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The sidebar uses the selected-Space control, built-in destinations, New Chat, Space-relevant options, + New Space and Edit Spaces in the defined hierarchy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stopping a resumable response replaces Stop with Play/Resume and Resume continues the same run without redoing completed consequential actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editing/regenerating earlier messages creates branches without destroying prior history/action records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Space inherits globally installed/enabled Dulche Skills/Plugins and available Agents by default, while per-Space exclusions work and do not grant permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Built-in Spaces expose only the protected Events & Extensions graph and cannot remove/replace required first-party behaviour/UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A built-in Study extension can turn on Do Not Disturb on activation and restore/perform a configured safe action on deactivation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A built-in Space can add a custom sidebar item without shadowing/removing protected items.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom sidebar items can host an authorised app surface such as Planner, an authored CUI interface and a safe Generative UI interface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: User-created Spaces expose the full graph editor with Draft/Validate/Activate behaviour and rollback-capable prior active revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The graph-editor AI bar can create a valid extension graph through typed Node Graph actions and explain the resulting behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Invalid type connections, unavailable packages/Agents, missing permissions and unbounded cycles are detected before activation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Write artifact and Board/shared object can be opened/edited canonically from Spaces without duplicate copies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared Productivity Engine objects round-trip between Spaces and supporting productivity apps without schema/format loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Explicit sources preserve identity/revision/provenance and large source sets use inspectable retrieval/context budgeting.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A web-disabled/source-only workflow cannot silently browse outside its allowed corpus.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Agent permissions are not expanded merely because the Agent is invoked from a Space.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Private personal Den context does not leak into a shared Space.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Long-running background-capable work survives navigation/closing the UI and reconnects to Home/Dulche state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Action Graph opens the real Dulche execution graph and Subagents remain distinct from persistent Agents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Study progress is based on recorded study interactions/answers rather than unsupported confidence inference.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tasks remain distinct entities from Agents and Automations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home/Dulche restart preserves durable conversation/run state and does not corrupt Space history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spaces remains usable for ordinary conversation when advanced agentic/tool capabilities are unavailable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Vision & Voice

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice is the dedicated user-facing multimodal AI surface for live voice, text-with-voice, images, screenshots, camera input, screen-aware interaction and contextual ambient listening. The underlying realtime/audio model runtime lives in Dulche; Vision & Voice owns user-facing session controls, capture sources, privacy state, presentation and Overlay integration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice MUST use the same canonical conversations, Spaces, model/provider state, Plugins, Skills, Agents, permissions, Action Graph and Dulche Den context as the rest of 9to1. Starting Voice MUST NOT create an isolated voice-only conversation database.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Session-first modern interface

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The full Vision & Voice app MUST use a modern session-first CUI interface focused on the active interaction rather than a conventional text-chat layout. The centre of the UI shows session state and current multimodal activity, with compact Mic, Camera, Screen and more controls plus an explicit End session action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transcript, current visual sources, model/voice, Space/conversation, tools/actions, Action Graph and device/session details SHOULD be available through collapsible secondary surfaces so the primary experience remains uncluttered.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Starting and continuing sessions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A multimodal session may start from Vision & Voice, the global AI bar, Spaces, AI Overlay or another app's contextual AI controls. Callers MAY supply SpaceID, ConversationID, current artifact/entity references, selected objects and suggested mode. Supplied semantic context MUST be preferred over redundant visual capture.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If no conversation is supplied, Vision & Voice creates or selects an appropriate conversation under the applicable Space policy. Moving between full Vision & Voice, floating voice pill, Overlay and Spaces MUST preserve the same canonical session/conversation where the user is continuing the same interaction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Multimodal session model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: MultimodalSession MUST contain at least SessionID, ConversationID, SpaceID, VoiceMode, Voice runtime/session reference, effective model policy, selected VoiceModelID/VoiceID where applicable, microphone/camera/screen states, active visual sources, input/output devices, status, created timestamp and revision/state metadata. Live Translate sessions additionally bind a LiveTranslateLanguageSet containing one or more selected languages/locales, direction mode (one-way, bidirectional or multilingual), per-output caption/speech preferences and selected glossary/terminology references where present.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required session states include Starting, Listening, UserSpeaking, Processing, AssistantSpeaking, Paused, Reconnecting, Stopped, Ended and Failed or equivalent explicit states. The UI MUST make microphone/capture/listening state unambiguous and MUST NOT rely on a purely decorative animation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Voice modes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice MUST support four first-class modes: Conversational, Monologue, Live Listener and Live Translate. They share Dulche/session infrastructure but have distinct turn-taking, execution and retention behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Conversational mode

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conversational mode is optimised for low-latency back-and-forth dialogue, natural interruption, normal questions/follow-ups, mixed speech/text input, tools/actions and moderate assistant turns. The assistant expects turn exchange rather than uninterrupted long-form narration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Monologue mode

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Monologue mode is optimised for sustained AI speech such as podcasts, lectures, project briefings or long-form explanations. It MUST support substantially longer uninterrupted output, section/chapter planning, pause/resume, user interruption and continuation from the prior position without losing the planned structure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Monologue MAY expose optional target duration and style controls such as briefing, podcast, lecture or explanation while still inferring these settings from the user's request when clear. A MonologueRun SHOULD retain Objective, optional TargetDuration, ordered Sections, CurrentSection, playback/progress state and SourceRefs so Resume has deterministic semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Live Listener mode

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Listener is a contextual ambient-listening mode for lessons, lectures, meetings, presentations, workshops and similar environments. It MUST continuously derive relevant semantic information and permitted actions without behaving as a default permanent recorder/transcriber.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Listener MUST be capable of extracting useful structured information such as current topic, important points, key dates, homework/tasks, decisions, questions, referenced resources and potential actions. It MAY react to contextual cues through typed actions, for example opening Canvas when a lesson moves to whiteboard work or creating a Planner item when homework/deadline information is clearly detected and authorised.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Listener MUST contextually distinguish likely primary relevant speech from background conversation, incidental noise, repeated information, action cues and uncertain material using available audio characteristics, continuity, current Space/topic and semantic relevance. It MUST represent uncertainty rather than treating every audible statement as authoritative/relevant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Live Listener ephemeral audio and privacy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Listener MUST NOT persist a room conversation as a transcript or permanent audio recording by default. Ambient audio is processed through a short-lived ephemeral rolling buffer required for understanding; once no longer needed for semantic extraction/runtime continuity, raw audio is discarded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Durable Live Listener output should be the useful derived result such as notes, tasks, dates, decisions, references or explicit user-approved retained snippets, not a verbatim transcript of everyone in the room.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Explicit recording/transcription is a separate opt-in retention mode with clear persistent UI indication and applicable legal/privacy warnings. Live Listener MUST NOT silently enable recording merely because retaining audio would improve later processing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Live Listener surface MUST clearly show Listening state, current Space/context, extraction categories/actions enabled, Recording audio state and Transcript retention state, with Pause and Stop controls. A compact activity feed MAY show semantic events/actions without reproducing ambient speech verbatim.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Live Listener notes and actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to choose where Live Listener writes durable notes/results, including temporary session notes or supported canonical destinations such as a Write document, Board page or Study Space notes. Updates MUST use the destination app's typed API and revision semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automatic Live Listener action policy MUST be configurable through normal Home permissions/trust. Low-risk actions such as adding notes, recording homework, opening relevant 9to1 apps or adding authorised Planner dates MAY run automatically where trusted; consequential external communication, submission, deletion, purchase or similarly high-risk actions retain their normal confirmation/trust requirements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Listener integrates with Spaces. Starting it from a Study/Research/Agent/user-created Space supplies that Space's authorised sources, tools, Skills, Plugins, Agents, memory and model policy. Space graphs may subscribe to safe Live Listener events and invoke typed actions within their capability profile.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Live Translate mode

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate is a first-class realtime interpretation mode backed jointly by Dulche Voice and Dulche Translate. Vision & Voice owns the live session UI/capture/output presentation; Dulche Voice owns realtime audio/session streaming; Dulche Translate owns language detection, translation, terminology/glossaries, translation context and multi-language variant generation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate MUST support one-way, bidirectional and multilingual interpretation. A one-way session may translate one source language into one or more output languages. Bidirectional mode interprets between selected languages based on turn/language context. Multilingual mode may contain more than two active languages and MUST support multiple simultaneous target outputs when the active model/runtime can do so.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Live Translate session MUST expose the selected language/locale set clearly and allow languages to be added or removed without ending the session where supported. Source language MAY be Auto Detect, but an explicit expected language set SHOULD be used to improve reliability in noisy multilingual environments.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Translated speech, translated captions and original-language captions MUST be independently controllable where supported. One source utterance MAY produce simultaneous caption/output streams in multiple target languages. Each connected/authorised output client MAY choose its preferred target language when platform/session architecture supports per-client outputs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate SHOULD preserve short-lived conversational translation context so pronouns, corrections, terminology and follow-up statements remain coherent. It MUST represent uncertainty rather than inventing a confident translation when language/speaker/meaning is materially ambiguous.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate MUST handle natural corrections and partial speech without prematurely treating unstable hypotheses as final durable content. For example, a speaker correcting a date within the same turn should yield a coherent corrected translation rather than two contradictory final statements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate MAY use Vision sources to translate signs, menus, presentation slides, shared screens and other visible text during the same session. When structured semantic text is available from a 9to1 app, that semantic text is preferred over OCR/pixels.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate supports normal Voice tools, Dulche Agents and authorised typed actions. A user may ask for an action based on translated context, such as saving translated notes, sending an approved translated message or applying translated content to an owning artifact. Agentic actions MUST use the normal owning-app APIs, permissions, approvals, idempotency and Action Graph; translation does not grant broader authority.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate MAY use selected Dulche Translate glossaries/protected-term rules so product names, legal terms, code identifiers or domain terminology remain consistent across speech and captions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate raw audio and ordinary conversation transcript MUST be ephemeral by default. The runtime may retain a short-lived rolling audio/translation-context buffer required for realtime interpretation and then discard it. Saving a transcript or audio recording is a separate explicit opt-in with visible state and applicable privacy/legal warnings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate is distinct from Live Listener: Live Translate's primary purpose is realtime cross-language interpretation, whereas Live Listener's primary purpose is ambient understanding, derived notes and contextual actions. Either may use normal Agents/tools, but one mode MUST NOT silently change into the other.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Text input during Voice

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every active Voice session MUST support typed text input without ending the session. Spoken and typed user messages share the same ConversationID and session context. Text input is required for precise names, URLs/code, private instructions, corrections, attachments and situations where the user wants speech output without speaking aloud.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice MUST support modality combinations including Voice in + Voice out, Voice in + Text out, Text in + Voice out and Voice with captions where the active model/configuration supports them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Interruption, stop and resume

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to interrupt assistant speech naturally. Dulche should stop/duck current speech output and process the new input without requiring a manual Stop first, subject to runtime capability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Explicit Pause, Resume, Mute and End controls remain available. If a generated response/run is manually stopped but resumable, Vision & Voice uses the same Stop → Play/Resume semantics as Spaces and MUST NOT repeat already-completed consequential actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Floating voice pill

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When the full Vision & Voice app is not foregrounded, an active session MAY collapse to a lightweight floating voice pill. The pill MUST expose true listening/speaking/status indication, mute/unmute, pause/resume where applicable, return to full Vision & Voice and End session.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening the pill/full app returns to the same SessionID and MUST NOT silently start a second Voice session.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Transcript and captions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conversational/Monologue sessions MAY expose a live transcript as an optional/collapsible conversation view distinguishing user, assistant and tool/action events. Partial speech-recognition hypotheses may update live, but only stable/final user content should enter durable conversation history unless a revision model explicitly supports corrections.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Listener and Live Translate do not use ordinary transcript retention by default as defined above. Live captions may be enabled independently of durable transcript retention. In Live Translate, original-language and translated captions are independently controllable where supported; caption display alone MUST NOT imply that a permanent transcript is being saved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Audio devices and processing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice MUST support input microphone selection, output device selection, default/automatic device, hot-switching during a session, permission/unavailable/disconnected states and appropriate input/output level feedback. Device loss MUST degrade/recover gracefully rather than corrupt the conversation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Noise suppression, echo cancellation, automatic gain and voice-activity detection MAY be provided when supported by the platform/runtime, with sensible defaults and inspectable advanced settings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Universal Model Picker integration and named voices

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice uses Home's Universal Model Picker. The selected Voice Model/configuration MUST be capability-checked for the requested mode and modalities, including realtime audio, Monologue, Live Listener, Live Translate, vision, tools/actions, required language/translation support and interruption where relevant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If the selected Voice Model exposes multiple named voices, the user-facing picker field is Voice and shows the available voices, with the underlying Voice Model shown as secondary metadata. Internally VoiceModelID and VoiceID remain separate. If no separate voices are exposed, the field is Voice Model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Discover/Home SHOULD recommend the highest-quality compatible Voice Model/configuration for the requested mode/constraints when the user has not explicitly overridden it. Switching named Voice MUST NOT be misrepresented as changing the underlying model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Vision sources

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Supported explicit visual-source families include UploadedImage, Screenshot, ScreenRegion, WindowShare, DisplayShare, Camera and AppProvidedVisualContext. Every active source MUST have session-local stable identity, provenance/source type and visible active/paused state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The UI MUST make clear what AI can currently see. Continuous sharing is distinct from a single screenshot and must expose source, pause, change source and stop-sharing controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Screenshots, screen sharing and camera

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Screenshot capture SHOULD support full display, selected window and selected region, with easy region capture from Overlay. Captures MAY be cropped/annotated before submission where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Continuous screen sharing MUST show an unmistakable persistent capture indicator and source identity. Pausing/stopping sharing MUST stop new visual frames from reaching the runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Camera mode MUST support available camera selection, snapshot, supported continuous camera context, pause and camera switching. Microphone/camera/screen capture MUST never activate solely because the model decides additional context would help.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Adaptive visual sampling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For continuous camera/screen input, Dulche MAY use adaptive frame sampling/change detection and model/provider limits to reduce redundant processing. Sampling is an optimisation only; stale visual state MUST NOT be represented as current.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Semantic context before pixels

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When a 9to1 app exposes semantic context such as ArtifactID, selection/object IDs, structured document context and available typed actions, Vision & Voice MUST prefer that structured context over screenshot/OCR/screen scraping. Vision supplements semantic APIs rather than replacing them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deliberately attached images/screenshots may persist as conversation sources. Continuous camera/screen frames MUST remain ephemeral by default and MUST NOT all become permanent attachments.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Privacy and local/cloud boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice MUST visibly indicate active microphone, camera and screen/window sharing plus relevant cloud-model use when required by privacy policy. Pausing/stopping a source must actually stop new data delivery.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Local-only/private model policy MUST NOT silently fall back to a cloud model for audio, camera or screen processing. Any local-to-cloud fallback follows the Universal Model Picker's explicit fallback/privacy rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: AI Overlay

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Overlay is a global lightweight contextual entry point owned by Vision & Voice and invoked through a configured keyboard shortcut, floating button and/or supported contextual selection action. It is not a normal page opened inside the Vision & Voice app.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overlay combines authorised semantic context from the foreground 9to1 app, selected text/objects, explicit screenshot/window/region capture and manually attached files/images. For non-9to1 apps or unavailable semantic APIs, explicit Vision capture may provide visual context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overlay MUST be fast, compact and capable of rendering CUI/Generative UI result/action cards. Overlay actions MUST invoke typed 9to1 APIs/Automations rather than arbitrary mouse/keyboard automation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Overlay automation execution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overlay MUST be able to discover and execute existing Automations relevant to the current typed selection/context. For example, selecting text and invoking an Automation named Send to my Boss supplies the selected text plus source metadata through the Automation's declared input schema.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overlay passes typed inputs such as selected Text/File/Artifact references, AppID, ArtifactID/ObjectID and additional authorised context. Missing required Automation inputs MUST be requested from the user rather than guessed when unsafe.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automation execution from Overlay uses the canonical Automation definition, permissions, approvals, Action Graph, logging, idempotency and error handling. Overlay MUST NOT independently emulate the Automation's actions or use it to bypass consequential-action confirmation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Overlay continuity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overlay MUST support Continue in Spaces, preserving the same conversation/request context and retained explicit sources. Closing the transient Overlay closes only the overlay UI; ephemeral captures are discarded according to retention policy unless deliberately retained.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a Voice session is already active, invoking Overlay MAY augment the same session, for example allowing the user to select a screen region while saying 'look at this bit' without spawning a second assistant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Voice tools and consequential actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spoken or typed Voice requests may execute normal authorised 9to1 app/tool actions. Voice does not reduce permission requirements. High-risk confirmation prompts MUST identify the concrete target/action rather than relying on ambiguous verbal confirmation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: AI-assisted dictation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dictation is a separate reusable speech-to-text editing capability, not a full Voice conversation mode. It MUST be available to supported editable text surfaces such as Write, Spaces, Mail, Boards, Present speaker notes, Planner descriptions, Sites, AI Studio and other CUI text editors through the shared platform capability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: During Dictation the AI does not respond conversationally or speak back. It converts speech into editable text/actions in the host app. Dictation SHOULD support Raw, Clean and Polished modes or equivalent: Raw remains close to literal transcription; Clean removes filler/repetition/false starts and adds punctuation; Polished may lightly restructure rambling speech into well-written prose while preserving intended meaning.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dictation MUST support contextual correction/commands such as new paragraph, bullet list, heading changes, delete/replace recent text and spoken self-corrections, applied through the host app/shared productivity engine rather than being inserted literally when recognised as commands.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dictation MAY use limited authorised current-editor context to improve terminology, names and punctuation. It MUST NOT use unrelated private context merely to improve transcription.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Background/session continuity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: An explicitly active Voice session may continue when the Vision & Voice window loses focus according to platform permission/background rules. Camera/screen sharing continues only while its visible capture state remains active; OS/session lock must suspend/stop sensitive capture according to platform policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If Home/Dulche temporarily restarts, Vision & Voice MUST preserve durable conversation/session metadata, show truthful Reconnecting/failed state and reconnect where supported. It MUST NOT indicate that microphone/model processing is active while disconnected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice MUST support captions, keyboard-only controls, screen-reader-labelled session/capture states, visual equivalents for audio state, adjustable caption/text sizing where applicable, reduced motion and non-colour-only state indication. No required action may be voice-only.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native Windows/9to1-OS may provide the full OS-global Overlay, native window/display capture and background voice capabilities. Web may provide microphone, camera and browser-authorised screen sharing but MUST NOT claim an OS-global Overlay outside the browser. Mobile uses supported camera/microphone/share-sheet/screen-capture capabilities. All surfaces capability-negotiate rather than assuming parity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.VisionVoice.SetCamera(sessionID, source?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche remains execution authority for realtime audio/model streaming and exposes the corresponding Voice runtime APIs. Vision & Voice APIs own user-facing session/capture/presentation state and MUST NOT duplicate the Dulche runtime as a second incompatible engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice MUST return structured failures including MicrophonePermissionDenied, CameraPermissionDenied, ScreenCapturePermissionDenied, InputDeviceUnavailable, OutputDeviceUnavailable, CameraUnavailable, CaptureSourceUnavailable, VoiceModelUnavailable, VisionCapabilityUnavailable, ModelCapabilityMismatch, SessionDisconnected, SessionNotFound, VisualSourceUnavailable, CaptureStopped, ProviderUnavailable, PrivacyPolicyDenied, AutomationInputMissing, DictationUnavailable, LiveTranslateLanguageUnsupported, LiveTranslateLanguageAmbiguous, LiveTranslateCapabilityUnavailable and LiveTranslateOutputUnavailable in addition to normal Dulche/Translate/tool/action errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conversational, Monologue, Live Listener and Live Translate operate as distinct modes on shared canonical session/conversation infrastructure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typed text can be submitted during an active Voice session without ending it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conversational Voice supports natural interruption plus explicit pause/mute/end state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Monologue preserves outline/progress and can resume after interruption/stopping without restarting completed content/actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Listener extracts structured lesson/meeting information while raw ambient audio/transcript is not persisted by default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Explicit recording/transcription opt-in is visibly distinct from default Live Listener.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Listener can create authorised notes/homework/date actions and trigger a low-risk contextual app action such as opening Canvas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate supports one-way, bidirectional and more-than-two-language sessions, including simultaneous target captions/output where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate uses Dulche Translate for language/glossary/context handling and does not create a second translation engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate raw audio and ordinary transcript are ephemeral by default unless the user explicitly enables retention.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Translate can use normal Agents/tools and perform authorised translated-context actions only through owning typed APIs and normal approval rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background/irrelevant speech is not indiscriminately written into notes and uncertain action cues do not silently cause consequential actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Floating voice pill controls the same SessionID as the full app.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Microphone/output device can hot-switch and device loss produces a recoverable truthful state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice named-voice selection stores VoiceID separately from VoiceModelID and the UI label becomes Voice when multiple voices exist.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Discover/Universal Model Picker can recommend/select a compatible high-quality Voice Model without burying Voice under Audio.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice + screenshot, Voice + continuous screen share and camera input work with visible capture state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stopping camera/screen sharing immediately stops delivery of new frames.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Semantic app context is preferred over screen scraping when available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Local-only/privacy policy cannot silently route audio/visual input to cloud.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overlay can capture selected context and use typed APIs rather than arbitrary input simulation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overlay can execute an existing Automation using typed selected-text/context input and preserves the Automation's permission/Action Graph contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Continue in Spaces preserves the active conversation/context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A high-risk spoken action still requires the correct explicit target-aware confirmation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dictation works in at least Write, Spaces and Mail as non-conversational speech-to-text with Raw/Clean/Polished behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dictation removes filler/false starts in Clean/Polished modes without changing intended meaning and applies supported editing commands through host APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home/Dulche restart produces a truthful reconnect/failed state without losing durable conversation state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Continuous capture frames remain ephemeral rather than being permanently attached by default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web/native capability differences are reported accurately, including no false claim of OS-global Overlay on web.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mic/camera/screen/listening states and all required controls are accessible and not communicated by colour alone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: AI Studio

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 AI Studio is the advanced authoring, testing, debugging and packaging environment for reusable Dulche systems. It is not a second AI runtime. Dulche owns model/Agent/tool execution; Home owns permissions and the shared Node Graph Framework; Den owns persistent Agent state; AI Studio owns the structured authoring and developer experience over those canonical systems.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Studio MUST support both project-backed artifacts and direct editing of canonical Dulche entities. Harnesses and Tool packages are AI Studio projects; Agents are canonical Den-backed Dulche Agents edited directly through Agent Builder rather than duplicated as an AI Studio-only project type.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Navigation and landing page

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Studio MUST use a clean persistent sidebar organised into Home, Projects, Build, Test & Debug, Resources and Templates. Build MUST expose Harnesses, Agents and Tools. Test & Debug MUST expose Playground, Evaluations, Test Suites and Replay. Resources MUST expose Schemas, Model Routers, Generative UI and Run Profiles.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The landing page MUST provide prominent New Harness, New Agent and New Tool actions plus Recent, Favourites/Pinned, Templates, search and Open/Import where applicable. New Agent opens Agent Builder and creates a canonical Dulche Agent directly in Den. New Harness and New Tool create AI Studio projects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Projects lists AI Studio project-backed entities such as Harnesses and Tools. Agents appears as a first-class Build destination but resolves to the canonical Dulche Agent registry rather than a duplicate AI Studio project store.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search, Recent, Favourites and Templates MUST use real persisted metadata/entities and MUST NOT be static mock content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Project model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every AI Studio project MUST have stable ProjectID, ProjectType, Name, Version, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, owner/scope, project files/resources, dependency references, permission metadata and revision history. In the current release scope ProjectType MUST distinguish at least Harness and Tool. Display names are not identities and MAY be duplicated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Studio projects persist independently from the currently running Dulche endpoint. Definitions reference models, Agents, Plugins, Skills, MCP capabilities, schemas, files/context and other dependencies by stable identity/version policy where available. Opening a project MUST NOT automatically execute model/tool work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project-backed artifacts MUST support create, open, save, duplicate, rename, history/versioning, validate, test, export/import where applicable, delete/recover and dependency inspection through typed APIs. Build/install/deploy/activate actions remain explicit operations distinct from editing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Build — Harness Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Harness Builder creates runnable, inspectable Dulche-powered AI systems. A new Harness MUST start from a functional selected template or validated baseline rather than an empty non-working shell.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Harness definition MUST be able to configure model/provider policies, prompts/instructions, context/session handling, tools, persistent Dulche Agents, Dulche Subagents/parallelisation, Skills, Plugins, MCP capabilities, permissions, budgets/limits, checkpoints/recovery, logging/Action Graph, structured outputs, Generative UI and supported APIs/entry points.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Harness Builder MUST distinguish persistent Den-backed Dulche Agents from transient Dulche Subagents. Harnesses MAY invoke both where allowed, but they are separate identity, memory and lifecycle concepts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated/configured Harness source and configuration MUST remain inspectable/editable. Harness Builder MUST NOT lock the user into an opaque private runtime that cannot be reproduced, validated or debugged.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Harness projects MUST support Preview/Test using the same Dulche runtime contracts used by normal execution. Test UI MUST expose the effective model/provider, tools, Agents/Subagents, permissions, selected context, usage/timing, Action Graph, structured errors and outputs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: Harness advanced graph

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Harness Builder MAY use the Home-owned Node Graph Framework for advanced orchestration. Supported graph logic may include request/event entry points, routing/classification, conditionals, model selection, Agent invocation, Subagent fan-out/merge, tools, retries, approvals, state and typed outputs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Basic Harness creation MUST remain possible without graph editing. The graph is an advanced representation over canonical typed Harness behaviour rather than a requirement for every user.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Build — Agent Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent Builder is AI Studio’s direct structured editor for persistent Dulche Agents. It creates and edits the canonical Dulche Agent entity stored in Den; it MUST NOT create a separate incompatible AI Studio-only Agent project or use AI Studio as the Agent runtime host. Closing AI Studio does not stop or delete the Agent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent Builder MUST follow a Workspace-Agents-style structured editing workflow rather than a GPT-style conversational creation wizard. The actual Agent configuration is visible and editable directly from the beginning; AI assistance may modify that configuration through typed Agent/graph APIs but MUST NOT hide the resulting state behind an opaque builder conversation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The primary editor header MUST provide updated/save state plus Automations, Preview, Share and overflow actions. The Agent’s icon/avatar and name are presented prominently beneath the header.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The default-visible configuration sections MUST be Plugins / Connectors, Skills and Knowledge / Files, followed by a collapsed More Options disclosure and then the directly editable Instructions document.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: Plugins / Connectors

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Plugins / Connectors lists canonical Dulche Plugins, MCP/external connectors and applicable 9to1 app capability bindings available to the Agent. + Add opens the relevant Dulche capability browser. Entries are stable references; Agent Builder MUST NOT clone Plugin/connector definitions into the Agent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: Skills

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Skills lists canonical installed Dulche Skills available to the Agent. + Add selects Skills by stable PackageID/version policy. Missing, incompatible, disabled or unauthorised Skills MUST be visibly diagnosed before activation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: Knowledge / Files

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Knowledge / Files contains the Agent’s Den-backed Memory entry plus linked knowledge sources such as Files, folders, Drive documents, 9to1 artifacts and other authorised sources. Sources remain canonical references where possible rather than arbitrary duplicated attachments. Knowledge scope, provenance and permissions must remain inspectable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: More Options

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: More Options MUST be collapsed by default and contain Availability, Default Model and Quick Actions. The UI MAY remember the user’s local expanded/collapsed preference without changing Agent semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Availability shows a simple primary state such as Global plus a Restrict Access action. Global means Dulche exposes the Agent on every compatible 9to1 surface. Restrict Access opens detailed scope controls for surfaces, Spaces, projects/entities, users/teams or other supported scopes. Availability is separate from permission.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Default Model uses the Universal Model Picker and supports Inherit or an explicit model/model-policy override plus supported reasoning/effort controls. Agent Builder MUST validate capability mismatches before activation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quick Actions are named manual Agent entry points with stable QuickActionID, label, optional icon/description, predefined instruction or named graph entry, optional typed InputSchema, context requirements, confirmation policy and order. They cascade wherever the Agent is available, subject to context visibility, and are distinct from Automations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: Instructions and assistant

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Instructions are directly editable on the main Agent Builder page as a substantial document. Users can write Role, Responsibilities, boundaries and procedures directly rather than editing an opaque generated prompt.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent Builder SHOULD expose a contextual assistant rail with actions such as Test this agent, Add advanced logic and Improve this agent plus an Ask anything input. AI modifications use typed definition/graph APIs and the resulting concrete configuration MUST remain visible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: Agent advanced logic, preview and revisions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Add advanced logic opens the Home Node Graph Framework with the Agent capability profile. Advanced logic MAY define lifecycle hooks, routing, conditional behaviour, Agent-to-Agent delegation, Skill/Plugin/tool invocation, state, retries, approval gates and other authorised behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preview runs the current draft definition as an explicitly test-scoped Dulche AgentRun using normal runtime semantics. It MUST NOT silently permit production side effects simply because the Agent is being previewed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations opens/creates canonical Automations associated with the Agent. Scheduling or event-triggering an Agent MUST create a real Automation rather than an Agent-private timer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent definitions MUST have stable AgentID and DefinitionRevision. Draft revisions are validated before activation. Existing AgentRuns retain the definition/model/capability provenance with which they began. Prior valid revisions SHOULD be rollback-capable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: Visual animated-avatar builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Studio MUST provide a visual animated-avatar builder within the existing Agent Builder workflow. It MUST support visually editing the avatar, its animation states, transitions and event-to-animation mappings; previewing activity and conversational reactions; saving and reopening the configuration; and assigning the result to an Agent. Authoring MUST update the canonical Den-backed Dulche Agent and referenced assets rather than creating an incompatible AI Studio-only Agent or runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The builder MUST expose the canonical Dulche Agent presentation fields and referenced assets, including static fallback, activity states, transitions and conversational reaction mappings. Preview MUST simulate presentation events without executing the corresponding real-world task or widening permissions. Equivalent authorised AI Studio/Agent APIs MUST support the visible editing, preview, save, reopen and assign operations with revision-conflict and asset-validation errors. Acceptance MUST cover a saved/reopened coding animation, a joke/laugh reaction and reduced-motion/static fallback on the same Den-backed Agent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Build — Tool Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tool Builder is the AI Studio builder for reusable Dulche capabilities. Supported first-class output types MUST include Skill, Plugin and MCP. Additional package kinds MAY be added without weakening stable identity, manifest, schema, dependency, permission, validation and version requirements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Creating a Tool MUST begin with an explicit type-specific template rather than forcing Skill, Plugin and MCP concepts into one generic editor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: Skill Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Skill projects MUST support name/icon/description, directly editable instructions/workflows, examples, resources/files, required Plugins/MCP dependencies, supported contexts, declared permissions, version and a real Test Skill action against Dulche.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Skills are primarily declarative and MUST NOT gain arbitrary executable code solely because they are Skills. Executable behaviour must use declared authorised tool/Plugin/MCP dependencies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: Plugin Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Plugin projects MUST support versioned manifest editing, actions/tools, typed input/output schemas, permission/risk declarations, external account connections, optional CUI surfaces, dependencies, secure secret references, tests and package/install workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Plugin UI surfaces MUST use approved CUI contracts. Plugin Builder SHOULD provide preview/testing of those surfaces without granting their actions permissions automatically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_4
text: MCP Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: MCP projects MUST support client/server role, transport/process/endpoint definition, capability schemas, tools/resources/prompts where supported, authentication references, permissions, compatibility/versioning, test client/server operation and logs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: MCP Builder MUST support both consuming an MCP server and intentionally exposing approved 9to1 capabilities through server mode without bypassing their original permission model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Shared builder assistant

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Harness Builder, Agent Builder and Tool Builder SHOULD use a consistent contextual builder-assistant pattern. The assistant can test, improve, add advanced logic and perform typed edits against the currently open canonical definition/project.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Natural-language requests such as 'add a GitHub tool and require approval for merge actions' MUST resolve to actual manifest/graph/permission changes that remain directly inspectable rather than only producing explanatory prose.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Test & Debug — Playground

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Playground is a developer scratch environment for experimenting with Dulche models, Agents, Skills, Plugins, tools/MCPs, instructions, context and Run Profiles without first creating a project or production Agent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Playground run MUST show result content, Generated UI where present, effective model/provider, effective instructions/context, tool/Agent activity, permissions, usage/timing, errors and Action Graph. It SHOULD support Save as Evaluation Case, Save as Test, Open in Agent Builder and Create Harness from this where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Playground is not a replacement for Spaces: it deliberately exposes technical execution/configuration detail rather than presenting the consumer conversational experience.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Test & Debug — Evaluations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Evaluations measure AI-system quality and behaviour across repeatable cases. Evaluation targets MAY include Dulche Agents/revisions, Harnesses, Skills, Plugins/tools, model/model-router policies and other supported reusable definitions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every EvaluationSuite MUST have stable EvalSuiteID, name, target/configuration, Cases, Graders, selected RunProfile/environment, optional baseline and revision metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: An EvaluationCase MAY define input, context, expected properties, expected output schema, required actions, forbidden actions, cost/latency limits and scoring/rubric criteria. Cases MUST preserve input/source provenance and target revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Supported grader families SHOULD include deterministic exact/schema checks, tool/action assertions, state assertions, rubric/LLM grading, human review and authorised custom Tool/Plugin graders. Results MUST distinguish deterministic facts from model-graded judgements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Evaluation runs SHOULD support multiple repetitions/seeds where stochastic variation matters and MUST allow comparison against a baseline without pretending one run proves overall quality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Test & Debug — Test Suites

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Test Suites verify deterministic contracts rather than subjective quality. Tests MAY assert expected node/path, expected or forbidden tool/action calls, permission requests, schemas, output types, state transitions, retry behaviour and structured errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tests MUST be runnable manually and through typed/CI-capable APIs. Agent activation, Tool install or Harness deployment MAY require configured mandatory suites to pass.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A failed test MUST preserve the exact target revision, Run Profile, effective dependencies and Action Graph needed to reproduce the failure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Test & Debug — Replay & Debugger

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replay opens a real previous Dulche request or Agent/Harness/Playground/Automation-triggered AI run and presents its canonical Action Graph/timeline for debugging.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to branch/replay from a valid node with controlled changes such as different model, Agent revision, instructions, context, tool result, capability availability, permission simulation or Run Profile. The original run/history remains immutable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replay MUST use Dulche restart/fork semantics and preserve side-effect safety. Replaying from before a consequential action MUST NOT blindly repeat an externally completed action without idempotency/explicit user-authorised behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Resources — Schema Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schema Builder creates reusable versioned typed contracts used across AI Studio and Dulche, including Agent/Quick Action inputs, Agent outputs, Plugin actions, MCP capabilities, Automation data, structured model output, Generative UI actions and Harness entry points.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every reusable schema MUST have stable SchemaID, version/compatibility metadata, field/type/constraint definitions and reverse dependency visibility. The editor SHOULD support both structured visual editing and raw schema/source editing for technical users.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing a shared schema MUST show affected dependants and compatibility impact before activation rather than silently breaking consuming Agents/Tools/Harnesses.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Resources — Model Router Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model Router Builder creates reusable Universal Model Picker-compatible routing policies rather than a competing model system. Rules MAY route by modality, task classification, context size, required tools/capabilities, latency, cost budget, privacy/local-only constraints, Agent, surface or other typed request metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Router policies MUST have deterministic precedence and explicit fallback rules. Local/private-to-cloud transitions require the same explicit privacy policy as the Universal Model Picker. The builder SHOULD visualise routes using the shared Node Graph Framework where useful while retaining a simpler rules view.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Resources — Generative UI Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generative UI Builder authors and tests reusable CUI schemas/components/generation envelopes used by Dulche Generative UI, Plugins, Agents, Harnesses and Space sidebar interfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: It MUST support component hierarchy, typed state/bindings, approved typed actions, responsive behaviour, accessibility metadata, theming, fallback representation and preview. AI-generative definitions MUST explicitly constrain which components/actions can be generated and MUST NOT permit arbitrary trusted executable code.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preview SHOULD cover supported desktop/narrow/mobile widths, light/dark themes, reduced motion, keyboard operation and accessibility semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Resources — Run Profiles

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run Profiles are reusable execution-environment overlays such as Development, Test, Local Only, Production, Cheap or Maximum Quality. They let users change execution policy without mutating the underlying Agent/Harness/Tool definition.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A RunProfile MAY define model/fallback policy, budgets, timeouts, logging level, mock/sandbox connectors, permission simulation, concurrency/Subagent limits and network/privacy policy. Profile identity and revision MUST be recorded in runs/evaluations/tests for reproducibility.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Context Inspector

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context Inspector is a contextual AI Studio debugging tool showing what the model actually received or would receive for a request/run. It MUST distinguish Agent/Harness instructions, active Skills, Space/context instructions, selected artifacts, retrieved chunks, memory items, tool schemas, summarised context and omitted material.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For each context item, Context Inspector SHOULD show source identity/revision, provenance, full/summarised/retrieved status, token/size estimate where available, retrieval metadata and why it was selected or omitted. It MUST NOT imply that omitted sources were considered by the model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Permission Simulator

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permission Simulator evaluates effective capabilities for a selected Agent/Harness/request context without executing the consequential action. It MUST show Allowed, Ask or Denied outcomes plus the contributing Agent, surface, Space, project/entity, caller/organisation and Home trust/policy decisions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The simulator MUST explain the controlling reason for a denial/approval requirement and MUST use the same permission-resolution contracts as real execution. It is a diagnostic surface, not a way to grant permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Dependency Inspector

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dependency Inspector visualises the canonical dependency graph of Agents, Harnesses, Tools, models, Skills, Plugins, MCP capabilities, schemas, knowledge sources, Automations, other Agents and related resources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: It MUST highlight missing dependencies, updates, disabled packages, revoked permission/access, version/schema incompatibility, inaccessible source and dependency cycles. Clicking a dependency SHOULD open/inspect the canonical entity where permitted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Comparison view

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compare is a reusable contextual view for compatible entities/runs, including Agent revision vs revision, model vs model, Harness run vs run, Eval run vs baseline, Run Profile vs Run Profile and instruction/configuration revisions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Comparison MAY show side-by-side outputs plus evaluation scores, deterministic test results, tool/action differences, Action Graph differences, latency, tokens/cost, errors, retries, selected context and effective model/provider. Model-quality comparisons SHOULD support multiple repetitions where needed rather than overgeneralising from one stochastic run.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Documentation Generator

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Documentation Generator creates human-readable documentation from canonical definitions rather than requiring a separately maintained copy. It MUST be able to derive relevant identity/version, purpose, availability, dependencies, permissions, actions/APIs, schemas, examples, errors and compatibility information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Supported outputs MAY include Markdown, HTML, Write documents, developer-site documentation or other typed export targets. Regeneration/update MUST reflect the canonical definition and MUST NOT silently overwrite hand-authored material without an explicit merge/replacement workflow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Templates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Templates MUST be real inspectable versioned starter definitions/projects. Supported template families SHOULD include Harness, Agent, Skill, Plugin, MCP, Evaluation, Test Suite, Schema, Model Router, Generative UI and Run Profile where appropriate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Instantiating an Agent template creates a new canonical Den-backed Dulche Agent. Instantiating project/resource templates creates new entities with their own stable IDs; template identity/version remains provenance rather than shared mutable state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Validation, install and deployment boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Studio MUST clearly distinguish authoring, validation, test/preview, build/package, install, activate and deploy/run concepts. Building a valid Plugin/Skill/MCP package does not automatically enable it, grant permissions, connect accounts or establish trust. Activating an Agent does not bypass runtime permissions. Deploying/running a Harness does not make its draft edits production state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: All validation MUST use the same canonical Dulche/Home schema, dependency, model-capability, permission and runtime contracts used after activation/install. A preview that succeeds only because it bypassed real contracts is non-conformant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permission Simulator explains the actual effective permission outcome without executing the action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context Inspector shows included/retrieved/summarised/omitted context truthfully with provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model Router policies integrate with Universal Model Picker/fallback privacy rules rather than creating a competing model system.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generative UI Builder restricts generated UI to approved CUI components/actions and validates accessibility/responsive behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dependency Inspector detects missing/disabled/incompatible/cyclic dependencies and opens canonical entities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run Profiles alter execution environment/policy without mutating the underlying Agent/Harness/Tool definition.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compare can compare compatible revisions/runs/models with outputs plus relevant eval/test/runtime differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Documentation Generator derives documentation from canonical definitions and preserves explicit merge/overwrite semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Templates create independent entities with template provenance rather than shared mutable copies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Authoring, validation, preview/test, install, activation and runtime execution remain separate permissioned lifecycle stages.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
