heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core operations across builders and test/debug/resources have equivalent typed API coverage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Play

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Play is the structured Agent-game framework and user-facing game surface where humans and Dulche Agents participate as contestants under explicit game rules. Play supports human-vs-Agent, Agent-vs-Agent, mixed teams and spectator-only matches. It is distinct from the built-in Experiences Space: Play owns formal games with contestant slots, rules, typed actions, visibility, turns/rounds, judging/scoring and winner conditions; Experiences owns open-ended conversational roleplay/simulation/story state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical reference experience is a generated maths quiz in which the user competes against ten AI Agent contestants. Each contestant receives the same authorised question state, submits independently, cannot see competitors' answers before reveal, and is scored by the game engine using deterministic maths validation where possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Game definitions and matches

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A GameDefinition describes reusable game rules/configuration and MUST have stable GameDefinitionID plus version/revision. It MAY define title/description/category, contestant limits/roles, teams, rounds/turn structure, state schema, visibility rules, available typed actions, timing policy, scoring/judging policy, win/elimination conditions, capability profile, UI/Generative UI definition, model requirements and template provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Match is one concrete execution of a GameDefinition and MUST have stable MatchID, GameDefinitionID/GameRevision, Contestants, MatchState, current round/turn, scores, timing state, judge policy, visibility policy, status, ActionGraphID, created/updated timestamps and recovery/checkpoint metadata where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Starting a Match snapshots or pins the GameDefinition revision used for that Match. Later edits to the game definition MUST NOT silently alter an in-progress Match.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Contestants

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every contestant MUST have stable ContestantID within the Match and a contestant type such as Human, DulcheAgent or SessionAgent. Agent contestants MAY additionally reference canonical AgentID/DefinitionRevision or a session-scoped temporary Agent configuration, model policy, team, display identity, score/status and applicable game capability profile.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Dulche Agents remain canonical Den-backed Agents with their normal identity/memory policy. Play MUST NOT clone them into private Play Agents. A persistent Agent participating in a Match receives only the game-authorised contestant view/capabilities for that Match.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: SessionAgent contestants are lightweight temporary game participants used when the user asks for generated/random opponents. They MAY have name/personality/strategy/model configuration for the Match but MUST NOT become permanent Den Agents unless the user explicitly saves/promotes them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MAY provide built-in contestant archetypes such as careful/accurate, fast/risky or balanced where appropriate. Such behavioural profiles may influence strategy/timing but MUST NOT alter objective truth, answer keys or hidden game rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Contestant selection and automatic filling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Game setup MUST support manual contestant selection from available Dulche Agents plus automatic creation/filling of remaining SessionAgent slots. The user may specify opponent count, model/Agent mix, team structure and broad difficulty/strategy policy where the GameDefinition supports it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MAY support model-vs-model style matches by assigning different explicit model policies to SessionAgent contestants, provided each still participates through the same contestant/action contract. The UI MUST disclose the effective model/Agent configuration when that distinction is relevant to the game.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Isolation, visibility and fairness

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MUST enforce contestant-specific context isolation at the runtime/data layer rather than relying only on instructions such as 'do not cheat'. Before every Agent turn, the canonical MatchState is filtered through the GameDefinition visibility policy to produce that contestant's authorised view.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A contestant MUST NOT receive another contestant's hidden answer/action, reference solution, hidden role, private inventory/state, unrevealed future round content, judge internals or other protected information unless the rules explicitly reveal it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hidden-role, deduction and asymmetric-information games MAY assign different private state to each contestant. Private state MUST remain inaccessible to unauthorised contestants, spectator views and model context even if all participants are represented within the same Match.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where fairness requires simultaneous decisions, submissions MUST remain sealed until all eligible contestants have submitted or the configured deadline expires. Reveal is a separate state transition.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Canonical game state and rules

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Match truth MUST live in canonical structured MatchState rather than in generated commentary. Narrative/UI text may describe a state transition only after the corresponding typed transition is accepted by the game engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: GameDefinition rules MUST be enforceable independently from contestant prompts where practical. Typed constraints may cover legal moves, resource limits, turn ownership, score bounds, prerequisites, timers, elimination, visibility and other deterministic rules. An Agent proposing an illegal action receives a structured rejection and may retry according to game policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rule-critical data such as quiz answer keys, legal move generation or score calculations SHOULD use deterministic evaluators where technically appropriate rather than an LLM judge.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Typed game actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agents and humans interact with a Match through GameDefinition-declared typed actions. Play MUST NOT depend on parsing arbitrary prose to infer critical actions when a structured action contract is available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples include SubmitAnswer, SelectOption, MakeMove, PlaceBid, ChooseTarget, Pass, Vote, SubmitCreativeEntry or EndTurn. Every available action MUST define input schema, visibility/availability conditions, validation rules and whether the action is reversible before resolution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent contestants receive only the actions currently available to them. Calling an unavailable/illegal action returns a structured error without mutating MatchState.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Rounds, turns and timing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MUST support at least Sequential, Simultaneous and RealTimeLike timing models where required by a GameDefinition. Quiz/race games SHOULD support simultaneous submission; board/strategy games may use sequential turns; other games may use event/timer-driven phases.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When speed affects scoring, Play MUST record authoritative presentation/start and submission timestamps from the Match runtime rather than trusting contestant-supplied timing. Pauses/reconnects MUST follow the GameDefinition timing policy and be represented explicitly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Round state SHOULD expose at least Pending, Active, AwaitingSubmissions, Resolving, Revealed and Completed or equivalent typed phases where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Judging and scoring

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every GameDefinition that scores or selects winners MUST declare a JudgePolicy/ScoringPolicy. The policy MAY use deterministic rules, human voting, one or more Dulche judge Agents, rubric-based model grading or a combination.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Objective domains MUST prefer deterministic evaluation when available. For example, maths answers should use symbolic/numeric validation rather than asking an LLM which contestant 'looks correct'. Subjective games such as slogan or creative-writing competitions MAY use transparent Agent/human rubric judging.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If model/Agent judging is used, Play MUST record judge identity/model/revision, rubric, inputs available to the judge and resulting score/reasoning artifact where policy allows. A judge MUST NOT receive contestant identity when blind judging is part of the game rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scores, penalties, tie-breaks, eliminations and winner resolution MUST be derived from the GameDefinition rules and stored as canonical Match events/state rather than only rendered text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Tools and capability profiles

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A GameDefinition MUST declare the game-specific capability profile available to Agent contestants. Tools such as web search, calculators, code execution, Files, Plugins or external connectors may be Allowed, Denied or constrained per game/role.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Disallowed capabilities MUST be removed/blocked at runtime rather than merely discouraged in instructions. A no-calculator maths quiz cannot expose calculator/code/web tools to Agent contestants. A research contest may explicitly permit them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: External consequential 9to1 actions are denied by default for Play contestants unless the GameDefinition explicitly integrates an approved capability and normal Home permission/approval policy permits it. Simulated game actions MUST remain clearly distinct from real-world side effects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Teams and collaboration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MUST support optional team membership where the GameDefinition permits it. Teams MAY mix human and Agent contestants. Visibility policy may expose team-private state/chat while hiding it from opposing teams.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A team game may therefore support Human + Agents versus Agents, multiple human/Agent teams or other configured compositions without changing the underlying contestant identity/action model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Spectator mode

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MUST support spectator-only Matches in which Agents compete while the user watches. Spectator UI MAY expose live round/turn state, locked/submitted indicators, permitted public reasoning/status, reveal events, scores/leaderboard and replay controls according to the GameDefinition visibility policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spectators MUST NOT automatically gain access to hidden contestant/judge state merely because they are not playing. Debug/developer visibility is a separate explicit permissioned mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Game creation and quick starts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MUST support conversational game creation from a natural-language request, for example 'Make a 15-question A-Level Maths quiz with increasing difficulty where I compete against 10 AI contestants'. The creation flow resolves that request into an inspectable structured GameDefinition before or as the Match starts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Play landing page SHOULD provide Create with AI, quick-start categories/templates, Continue/Recent Matches, saved/favourite GameDefinitions and available shared templates. Candidate categories MAY include Quiz/Knowledge, Strategy, Creative, Deduction/Social and Collaborative/Team games.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated games MUST be real GameDefinitions with typed rules/state/actions rather than a one-off prompt pretending to be a game.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: UI and Generative UI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MAY use CUI/Generative UI for question cards, timers, answer controls, boards, maps, cards, inventories, contestant panels, scoreboards, leaderboards, reveal animations and other game-specific interfaces. Generated UI MUST bind to typed Play actions/state and MUST NOT become an alternate unsynchronised game engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For a quiz, the primary screen SHOULD make the current question, user's answer control, contestant submission status, round state and leaderboard understandable without exposing hidden answers before reveal.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Voice, images and multimodality

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MAY use Vision & Voice while preserving the same MatchID/ContestantID/state. Voice is another input/output modality for the Match rather than a separate game session.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: GameDefinitions MAY use images, generated visuals or other media as questions, assets or submissions where supported. Persistent continuity-critical assets MUST receive canonical asset identity/references rather than being regenerated unpredictably each turn.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Checkpoints, reconnect and replay

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play SHOULD checkpoint canonical MatchState at safe phase/round boundaries and support reconnect/recovery where the game permits. Recovery MUST preserve sealed submissions, scores and resolved side effects rather than restarting a round invisibly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replay/history SHOULD be derived from canonical Match events and Action Graph. A debug/replay branch MUST NOT alter the original completed Match history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Play and Experiences interoperability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play and the Experiences Space are separate products over shared Dulche/Home primitives. Experiences MAY launch a Play Match for a formal competition inside a broader scenario; Play MAY offer Continue in Experiences for open-ended continuation after a Match. Any handoff MUST explicitly map permitted state/artifacts rather than treating MatchState and ExperienceState as the same object.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play MUST return structured failures including GameNotFound, GameRevisionUnavailable, InvalidGameDefinition, MatchNotFound, MatchAlreadyStarted, MatchNotJoinable, ContestantNotFound, ContestantNotEligible, ContestantViewDenied, NotContestantTurn, RoundNotActive, SubmissionAlreadyLocked, SubmissionDeadlinePassed, ActionUnavailable, IllegalAction, CapabilityDeniedByGame, JudgeUnavailable, ResolutionFailed, RecoveryUnavailable and RevisionConflict in addition to normal Dulche/Home/tool failures.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A user can generate and start a maths quiz against ten AI Agent contestants from a natural-language request.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Dulche Agents can enter a Match without being cloned into a Play-private Agent registry.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automatically filled SessionAgent opponents remain session-scoped unless explicitly saved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every contestant receives an isolated authorised view and cannot access sealed competitors' answers, hidden roles or judge/reference state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A simultaneous quiz keeps submissions sealed until reveal/deadline and records authoritative timing when speed affects scoring.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maths correctness/scoring uses deterministic validation where available rather than an unnecessary LLM judge.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent contestants act through typed game actions and illegal/unavailable actions fail without mutating MatchState.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Game-specific tool restrictions are enforced at runtime, including a no-web/no-code/no-calculator quiz profile.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Teams can mix humans and Agents while team-private state remains isolated from opponents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An Agent-vs-Agent spectator Match can run without the user occupying a contestant slot.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canonical MatchState remains authoritative over generated narrative/UI text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reconnect/recovery preserves locked submissions, scores and already-resolved state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play can hand off explicitly to an Experiences Space without merging MatchState and ExperienceState implicitly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core game creation, Match, contestant, action, scoring and replay operations have equivalent typed API coverage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: Productivity Apps

heading: HEADING_2
text: Write

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Write is the production document/word-processing surface. It MUST behave like a mature word processor rather than a web editor, site builder, Markdown editor, collection of HTML blocks or browser contenteditable surface. LibreOffice Writer/LibreOfficeKit is the mature donor/layout/format engine for text-oriented documents; 9to1 owns the CUI shell, shared Productivity Engine integration, collaboration, AI, Sections model and native extensions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The document surface MUST use an actual structured document model with paragraph/run/style/section/table/object/reference/review semantics and real layout/text measurement. Caret movement, selection, rich clipboard, IME input, undo/redo transactions, object anchoring, line wrapping, pagination, spelling/grammar ranges, accessibility semantics and large-document behaviour MUST be implemented as document-editor behaviour, not emulated with disconnected DOM widgets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Continuous view is a presentation of the same structured word-processing document, not conversion into HTML. A document MUST switch between supported views without changing its canonical content or losing document semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Donor parity and objective word-processor behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: All applicable LibreOffice Writer functionality, quality-of-life behaviour, keyboard interactions, menus/workflows and file-format depth MUST be preserved or appropriately adapted unless technically impossible and explicitly documented. The donor source is authoritative for inherited functionality; Write MUST NOT ship as a simplified rich-text clone simply because a smaller editor is easier to implement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Inherited/core capability includes, where applicable, character and paragraph formatting; custom styles; page styles; headers/footers; sections; columns; page/section breaks; lists/outlines; tables; images/drawings/shapes; equations; fields; bookmarks; cross-references; captions; footnotes/endnotes; tables of contents; indexes; citations/bibliographies; comments; tracked changes; document comparison; spelling/grammar/language features; find/replace; hyphenation; print/page layout; mail merge; document properties; object anchoring/wrapping; export/print and other mature Writer functionality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Launch and file entry

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write opens to the shared modern Launch Screen contract with Blank document, Templates, Recent, Favourites, Shared with me, search, Open and Import. Entries MUST be backed by real Files/Drive data rather than mock cards. Creating/opening/importing a document establishes the canonical Write artifact before entering the editor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Editor shell

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST NOT use a permanent Office-style ribbon. The editing shell consists of a document-title row, a floating contextual toolbar immediately below the title at the top of the document area, an optional collapsible Sections sidebar, the document canvas and the persistent shared AI bar at the bottom.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Home button sits immediately to the left of the document title and opens an Office-style backstage/file menu for document-level operations such as Info, New, Open, Recent, Save/Save a copy, Share, Export, Print, Version history, Document properties and Settings. Closing the menu returns to the same document/selection position.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Floating contextual toolbar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The floating toolbar stays in a stable position immediately below the title while its contextual controls change according to the current semantic selection. Text, heading, image, table, reference/review and other contexts expose their own relevant operations. An operation that cannot apply to the current selection MUST NOT appear merely because it exists elsewhere in Write; for example Crop image cannot appear when no image is selected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Three controls are persistent regardless of selection: +, Eye and overflow […]. They remain present even as all other controls change. When horizontal space is constrained, lower-priority contextual actions move into overflow before these persistent controls disappear.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The overflow […] menu contains additional actions relevant to the current context that did not fit or were deprioritised on the main bar. It is not a generic dump of all Write commands. The menu for a table selection differs from the menu for text or an image and MUST exclude inapplicable actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Right-click/context menus expose the same semantic action model in menu form. Context menus and the floating bar call the same typed Write/Productivity APIs rather than maintaining parallel behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Pinned toolbar actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to pin supported contextual actions to the top bar and reorder/reset their pinned preferences. Pinning means prioritise this action whenever it is applicable; it MUST NOT force an irrelevant disabled action to occupy the toolbar in unrelated contexts. Pinning is per-user UI preference rather than collaborative document state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Toolbar priority SHOULD resolve from the most important current-context control, then applicable user-pinned controls, then common contextual actions, followed by the persistent +, Eye and […] controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Universal Insert (+)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent + control is the universal Insert entry point. It opens a searchable, context-aware insertion palette rather than requiring an Insert ribbon. The complete palette MUST expose applicable content/structure/reference/9to1 artifact options while prioritising items relevant to the current caret/object context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Insertion types SHOULD include tables, images, drawings, equations, code blocks, text boxes, shapes/callouts, horizontal lines, page/section breaks, columns, headers/footers, footnotes, citations, cross-references, bookmarks, captions, table of contents, special characters, fields, links/files and supported embedded 9to1 artifacts such as Canvas, Board, Data ranges/charts, Picture, Planner items, Maps and Graphs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Eye / visibility controls

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent Eye control owns view/visibility options rather than document-format mutations. Its menu MUST include the current Write View mode and may include Sections visibility, Comments, spelling/grammar marks, formatting marks, ruler, page boundaries, object anchors, alignment/snap guides and the floating word/character count where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Most Eye settings are per-user view preferences and MUST NOT change what collaborators see. Contextually useful visibility aids MAY appear only when relevant, for example object bounds/anchors/guides when an object is selected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Floating document statistics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When enabled from Eye, an unobtrusive document-statistics indicator floats in the bottom-right of the document area without becoming document content or consuming page layout. It SHOULD show document word and character counts, and when text is selected it SHOULD prioritise selection word/character counts. Clicking it MAY reveal expanded statistics such as characters without spaces and page count where meaningful.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The statistics indicator and bottom AI bar MUST coexist without overlap at supported sizes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Sections sidebar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write has a Google-Docs-inspired collapsible Sections sidebar on the left. The product terminology is Sections, not Tabs. A Section is a stable user-created structural division of the same Write document and MAY contain nested Sections. Headings inside each Section are derived automatically from document heading/outline styles.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Section MUST have stable SectionID, DocumentID, optional ParentSectionID, Name, optional icon/metadata, ordering and revision/state information. Renaming/reordering/nesting MUST preserve SectionID so links, AI context and cross-references are not tied to visible names.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The expanded sidebar presents Sections as stronger/root nodes with the heading hierarchy beneath each Section. Clicking a heading navigates to it; changing heading style updates the outline live. Moving a heading moves its heading plus subordinate content using structured document operations. Moving a Section moves the Section's canonical content safely.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The sidebar has a + control for New section, New subsection, From selection and supported Import-as-section workflows. Section/headings support context actions such as rename, duplicate, move before/after/into, copy link, export section, delete and relevant AI/translation operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Sections sidebar MUST be collapsible to a narrow edge/rail and resizable when expanded. Collapsed/expanded state and width are per-user/device preferences. Collapsing immediately returns horizontal space to the document canvas; navigation/AI actions MUST NOT forcibly reopen it. On narrow layouts the sidebar becomes a temporary drawer. Keyboard and non-drag movement/navigation alternatives are mandatory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Sections sidebar and an inserted Table of Contents are distinct. The sidebar is editing/navigation structure; + → Table of contents inserts a real document object generated from configured heading levels/styles.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: View modes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Eye exposes three first-class Write View modes: Continuous, Pages and Book. Switching view is immediate presentation state over the same DocumentID, SectionIDs, ObjectIDs, selection, comments and revision. The user's view mode does not force collaborators into the same view.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Continuous is the default for new .9to1w documents unless the chosen template requires another view. It presents one seamless pageless writing surface with a sensible readable content width and no artificial sheet gaps. Real page breaks remain canonical and are shown as unobtrusive markers rather than forcing paper sheets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Continuous view MUST retain page-aware document features such as headers/footers, footnotes, page numbers, margins, section/page breaks and columns in the underlying document model. The view may present them contextually rather than permanently rendering every page boundary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pages renders exact page layout using modern rounded pages, restrained elevation, clean spacing and a neutral workspace while preserving true margins, headers/footers, footnotes, page numbers and print pagination. It MUST not use dated harsh page chrome merely because the donor does.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Book renders publication-aware facing-page spreads and supports odd/even pages, right/left page semantics, mirrored inside/outside margins, binding gutter, different left/right headers/footers, section starts/front matter and deliberate blank-page behaviour. Narrow displays MAY show one page at a time while preserving spread semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: View mode is independent from Locked/Unlocked layout mode. Supported combinations include Continuous + Locked, Continuous + Unlocked, Pages + Locked, Pages + Unlocked, Book + Locked and Book + Unlocked.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Locked and Unlocked layout

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST implement the same first-class Locked/Unlocked layout concept as Boards. LayoutMode is independent from the user's current View mode and from AI Read/Write mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Locked is the conventional word-processing flow and the default for ordinary documents. Paragraphs/inline content follow document structure and supported objects use anchors/wrapping rules so accidental free positioning is constrained.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unlocked adds a professional free-positioned visual object layer for supported images, text boxes, shapes, drawings, charts, embedded artifacts, callouts, equations and tables where applicable. Users may drag, resize, rotate, overlap, layer, align, distribute and snap these objects without converting the whole document into arbitrary floating text boxes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unlocked object controls MUST support position/size/rotation; page/Section/paragraph/character anchoring where meaningful; inline/square/tight/behind/in-front/custom wrapping; aspect and position locks; z-order; align/distribute; grouping; snapping to margins, columns, guides, text bounds and other objects; and accessible non-drag alternatives.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Switching layout modes MUST preserve data and positions as far as the target representation supports. If an object cannot be represented safely under the requested mode/foreign format, Write MUST warn rather than silently discard/flatten it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Styles and custom styles

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom styles MUST be first-class and front-and-centre whenever the selected content supports styles. For text, the active semantic style control SHOULD normally be the first contextual toolbar control rather than leading with raw font/size controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST support built-in and arbitrary custom character/paragraph/document styles with stable StyleID, inheritance/overrides where supported, modify/create/update-from-selection, usage inspection and import/copy of style sets. Styles MAY control typography, paragraph/line spacing, indentation, alignment, borders/background, list behaviour, pagination/keep-with-next, language, outline level and semantic/accessibility role.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing a shared/custom style MUST update linked uses while preserving explicit local overrides according to the style model. Write SHOULD preview the scope/impact of broad style changes where useful.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Equivalent reusable style concepts SHOULD exist for tables and other supported object classes where they provide real value; these remain canonical style definitions rather than visual presets copied independently into each object.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Tables

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tables MUST support mature Writer/Office-level editing plus a stronger native .9to1w styling model. The contextual toolbar for a table SHOULD prioritise active Table Style plus common Borders, Fill, Padding, Alignment and structural actions, with less-common relevant actions in […].

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Whole-table controls MUST include width/height and fixed/content/flexible sizing as supported; alignment; wrapping; position/anchor; table padding/margins; background/opacity; border; shadow; caption; repeating header rows; pagination/split behaviour; and native rounded-corner support.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native .9to1w tables MUST support table corner radius, including linked or independent top-left/top-right/bottom-right/bottom-left radii. Foreign export MUST preserve this where the target format can represent it or explicitly warn/use a documented compatibility representation when it cannot.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Row/column controls SHOULD include explicit/flexible/min/max sizing, equal distribution, visibility/header designation, keep-together and appropriate responsive/fixed behaviour. Cell controls MUST include independent top/right/bottom/left padding, horizontal/vertical alignment, text direction, background/fill, border per side, border width/style/colour/opacity, merge/split, minimum dimensions and defined overflow behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Border editing MUST distinguish outer border, inner horizontal, inner vertical and individual cell edges. Cell padding MUST be directly discoverable and support linked/unlinked values rather than being buried in an obscure properties dialog.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom Table Styles MUST be reusable first-class definitions capable of controlling whole-table appearance, header rows, first/last columns, odd/even rows, typography, borders, corner radius, cell padding, alignment and backgrounds. Linked tables update when the style changes except for explicit local overrides.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Images, drawings and positioned objects

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Images and visual objects MUST support professional crop, resize, aspect ratio, wrap, anchor, positioning, z-order, caption, alt text, replacement and supported compression/export controls. The shared Rnote-derived drawing object is used for handwriting/sketch/annotation/diagram content so supported drawings remain editable across Write, Boards and Canvas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiple selected free objects expose align/distribute/group operations. Object controls and […] overflow remain contextual; irrelevant image controls MUST not appear for text/table selections.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: References and document structure

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: References is a first-class semantic capability even though Write does not expose a permanent References ribbon. +, contextual controls, right-click and […] provide footnotes/endnotes, citations/bibliography, table of contents, captions, cross-references, bookmarks, indexes and fields where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Citation/reference data MUST be structured rather than only formatted prose so Agents and APIs can insert, validate, update and export references safely. Section/heading links and cross-references SHOULD use stable IDs rather than visible text/page numbers as identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Review, comments and collaboration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST support comments, tracked/suggested changes, accept/reject, previous/next change, document comparison and version history using real document/review semantics. AI edits in Suggest mode create suggestions rather than silently accepted direct changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Realtime collaboration MUST use the normal 9to1 shared-artifact model for presence, cursors/selections, concurrent editing, comments, permissions/sharing and revision/conflict semantics. Naive timestamp last-writer-wins overwrite is non-conformant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Native format and foreign document formats

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: .9to1w is the versioned native Write format and MUST preserve the full native document model, stable Productivity object identity, Sections, custom styles/table styles, embedded 9to1 artifact references, review/collaboration metadata, drawings/graphs, supported AI provenance and native features that foreign formats cannot represent. Migrations MUST be deterministic and preserve compatible unknown optional data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST support reliable DOCX and ODT import/export plus supported Markdown/TXT interchange and PDF export. Import/export fidelity is a release criterion, not a demo feature. Unsupported or lossy foreign-format behaviour MUST be surfaced rather than silently deleting content to force compatibility.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: PDF opening and editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST open and edit PDFs as first-class fixed-layout documents; PDF support is not export-only and MUST NOT simply convert every PDF into HTML or an approximate web editor. The Write shell remains consistent while an appropriate PDF/page-object engine (including applicable LibreOffice Draw/PDF capabilities or equivalent mature implementation) owns fixed-layout PDF object semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A digitally structured PDF SHOULD preserve selectable/editable native text, fonts, images, vector/page objects, links, annotations, forms/layers where supported and page geometry. Such PDFs default to Pages view and Unlocked layout because fixed page geometry is intrinsic.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scanned PDFs MUST be recognised as image/scanned content rather than falsely presented as native text. Write SHOULD offer explicit Recognise text/OCR-style transformation, preserve correspondence to the original page image and expose uncertain/low-confidence recognition rather than claiming perfect extraction. Mixed PDFs are handled page/object-by-page/object rather than forcing one simplistic document-wide mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: PDF editing MUST support useful fixed-layout workflows where technically supported: editing/moving existing text blocks, inserting/deleting text, images and objects, resize/crop, drawings/shapes, page rearrange/insert/delete/rotate, combine/extract pages, links, annotations/comments/highlights, proper redaction, supported form fields/signatures and headers/footers/page numbers.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before the first destructive PDF save, Write MUST preserve an original recoverable revision/backup and maintain normal version history. PDF AI operations use semantic PDF text/object structure when available and MUST NOT OCR screenshots of text that the PDF already exposes semantically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Continuous MUST NOT be forced onto a fixed-layout PDF. PDF defaults to Pages; only views/reflow operations that are meaningful for the active PDF are exposed, with fidelity implications made explicit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI bar in Write

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write implements the platform-wide shared AI-bar Read-only / Write-mode contract. In Read-only, Dulche can semantically inspect/search/compare the full authorised document, including off-screen Sections, headings, objects, styles, comments, references, tables and embedded artifact metadata, but cannot mutate the document. In Write mode it can use typed Write/Productivity actions subject to host editing/review/permission state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The AI context MUST expose stable DocumentID, document revision, current SectionID/heading/object, selection ranges/ObjectIDs, document structure, styles, comments, references, tables/images/embedded artifacts and available typed actions as authorised. Viewport visibility is not the AI's document boundary. Visual rendering may supplement this when layout must be inspected, but semantic access is primary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Read/Write mode is separate from document Edit/Suggest/View and Locked/Unlocked. For example AI Write mode + Suggest creates tracked suggestions; AI Write mode + Edit may perform direct typed edits; AI Read-only always prohibits mutations. The bar MUST NOT use mouse/keyboard simulation instead of Write APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The AI bar supports actions such as rewrite/shorten/expand, restructure, create/move Sections, apply/change styles, manipulate tables, insert objects/references, inspect missing citations, translate, compare Sections and perform other authorised semantic edits. Broad edits remain revision-safe, undoable/versioned and subject to normal conflict handling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Agents, sources and Translate integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MAY expose applicable Global, Write-scoped, Space and contextual Dulche Agents through the shared Agent picker. Specialist writing Agents such as Editor, Proofreader, Citation Assistant or Long-form Writer are canonical Dulche Agents, not private hard-coded AI runtimes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Documents MAY reference authorised source sets/files without unnecessarily duplicating them into the document. Source-backed AI work SHOULD preserve provenance where appropriate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selection-level Translate invokes Dulche Translate directly for simple translation. Continue in Translate opens/preserves context in the built-in Translate Space for larger localisation workflows. Whole-document translation can produce separate Write derivatives/locale variants while preserving structure and source provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Embedded 9to1 artifacts and interoperability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MAY embed/reference supported Boards, Canvas, Data ranges/charts, Picture assets, Planner items, Maps, Graphs and other canonical 9to1 artifacts as live embeds, linked previews or explicit snapshots according to the target type and permissions. Embedding MUST reference canonical entities rather than creating unmanaged duplicate state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared Productivity Engine bundles and object identities MUST support rich cross-app copy/paste/conversion where semantics are compatible; unsupported conversion MUST fail explicitly rather than silently flattening required behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Navigation, search and long-document performance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST provide document search/find-replace and efficient navigation for large documents. Sections/headings are semantic navigation, not a DOM outline derived from whatever is currently rendered. Long documents MUST not require eagerly rendering every page/object to remain editable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Switching Continuous/Pages/Book, opening/collapsing Sections, enabling counts/marks and changing selections MUST avoid unnecessary full-document re-rendering where the document engine can update incrementally.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Recovery, persistence and accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST support autosave, unsaved-draft protection, crash recovery, revision/version history, conflict recovery and safe interrupted-save behaviour. A crash or partial write MUST not casually lose a user's document. Save/reopen workflows are part of acceptance testing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard-only operation, screen-reader semantics, focus indicators, scalable typography/zoom, accessible toolbar/context menus, non-drag alternatives for movement/layout, readable selection/review state and narrow-screen adaptation are mandatory. The Sections drawer, toolbar, floating statistics and AI bar must remain usable without overlap at supported scale factors.

HEADING_3

NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write uses a real structured word-processing/document engine and is not implemented as a generic HTML/contenteditable/web editor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A new .9to1w opens in Continuous view by default and can switch to Pages and Book without changing canonical content or losing selection/state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pages renders modern rounded pages with exact pagination; Book renders correct facing-page/book layout semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The floating contextual toolbar sits directly beneath the title, stays positionally stable and changes only to relevant controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: +, Eye and […] remain persistent across text, image, table and other selection contexts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: […] contains only additional actions relevant to the current context; inapplicable actions such as Crop with no image are absent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can pin/reorder contextual actions and pinned actions appear only when applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: + opens a real searchable insertion palette that inserts supported document/reference/9to1 objects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Eye toggles view/visibility features including Continuous/Pages/Book, Sections and word/character count where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Floating word/character count appears at bottom-right without becoming document content or overlapping the AI bar.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Sections sidebar is collapsible/resizable, uses stable SectionIDs, includes live heading outline and supports nested Sections and accessible movement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Locked mode preserves conventional document flow; Unlocked mode provides real free placement, z-order, snapping, alignment/distribution and wrapping without converting normal body text into arbitrary boxes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom text styles are front-and-centre in applicable contexts and create/update/apply through stable StyleIDs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native tables support reusable custom Table Styles, independent cell padding, advanced borders and rounded corners including independent corner radii.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write preserves applicable LibreOffice Writer donor functionality/QoL rather than shipping a simplified editor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DOCX and ODT import/export plus native .9to1w and supported Markdown/TXT/PDF export complete real save-close-reopen workflows with fidelity checks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write opens digital, scanned and mixed PDFs through an appropriate fixed-layout editor, defaults PDFs to Pages/Unlocked and never pretends scanned text is native.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PDF text/object/page editing and destructive-save backup/version recovery work for supported PDF cases; backup failure is surfaced rather than ignored.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The shared AI bar can semantically read the entire authorised document in Read-only mode and cannot mutate it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Write mode edits through typed APIs and obeys Edit/Suggest/View, permission, undo/version and conflict semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI context is not limited to the viewport and does not substitute screenshot/OCR for available semantic document/PDF text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Realtime collaboration preserves concurrent edits/comments/review without naive timestamp last-writer-wins data loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crash/interrupted-save recovery and realistic create/open-edit-save-close-reopen validation preserve document content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Toolbar, Sections, page/book views, review state, free-layout controls and AI bar remain keyboard/screen-reader/zoom accessible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core Write operations have equivalent typed API coverage and no visible toolbar/menu action is a placeholder or disconnected fake.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST use Home’s Shared Productivity Engine for every shared object type it supports. Shared objects copied between Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces MUST preserve the common object schema, formatting and behaviour rather than being converted into Write-only representations.

heading: HEADING_2
HEADING_2
text: Present

heading: HEADING_3
text: Purpose, ownership and conformance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Present is the CUI presentation authoring, presenting and interactive-runtime application. LibreOffice Impress/Draw is the donor foundation for applicable mature presentation editing, interoperability and quality-of-life behaviour. 9-1 owns the CUI shell, the native .9to1p model, the Actions runtime, typed APIs, AI integration, component model and cross-app semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Applicable donor functionality MUST be preserved unless a scoped donor-parity exception is recorded in the canonical donor-parity manifest. Present MUST NOT ship as a reduced slide editor whose only conformance evidence is file opening or basic text/shape editing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST use Home's Shared Productivity Engine for every registered shared object type that it supports. Shared text, tables, charts/graphs, images/media, drawings/ink and other shared objects copied between Present, Write, Canvas, Boards and Spaces MUST preserve the shared object schema, semantic identifiers, formatting, accessibility metadata and clipboard representation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Release boundary:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present owns PresentationID, SlideID, slide order, slide composition, presentation-level state, slide-local state, speaker notes references, presentation sessions and the Actions graph.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns shared productivity object schemas, permission brokerage, shared AI/runtime services, common clipboard bundles and other platform services defined in Home.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST NOT introduce a second private implementation of a Home-owned shared object or platform service.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The native .9to1p representation is authoritative for full-fidelity 9-1 behaviour.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Normative applicability and capability negotiation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terms such as applicable, supported and available are not discretionary escape hatches in this section. They are resolved from explicit manifests or runtime capability declarations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A donor feature is applicable unless it is classified in the Present donor-parity manifest as Replace with 9-1-native equivalent or Not applicable with a recorded technical/legal reason.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A platform capability is supported only when the platform capability registry declares the required capability and version for the active device/runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A file-format construct is representable only when the import/export capability matrix declares a mapping for the source construct and target format/version.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Failure of a required capability check MUST produce a typed unavailable/unsupported result and the specified fallback or CompatibilityIssue; silent omission is prohibited.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An implementation MUST NOT reinterpret a MUST requirement as optional merely because its current code path does not implement the required capability.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST implement the global launch-screen contract. The launch surface MUST expose Create New, Open/Import, recent presentations and real template/theme discovery. Recent items MUST be derived from persisted history; fabricated recent files are prohibited except for explicitly labelled onboarding or template content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The release file contract MUST support native .9to1p plus PPTX and ODP import/export. Static output MUST support PDF and image export. Present MUST provide complete create -> edit -> save -> close -> reopen workflows with autosave, crash/interrupted-save recovery, revision tracking and conflict-safe persistence.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A failed save, partial media write, unresolved revision conflict or recovery failure MUST be surfaced as an explicit error state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST NOT report success until the target revision and all referenced persisted objects required for the save have been committed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recovery MUST preserve the last known-good durable revision and MUST NOT overwrite it with a partially reconstructed presentation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical data model and identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All persistent entities MUST use stable opaque IDs. Slide number, slide title, list position, object name and file path are mutable presentation attributes and MUST NOT be used as persistent identity.

text: Presentation {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ActionsGraphRef: GraphID + GraphRevision

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Settings: PresentationSettings

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permissions: PermissionDescriptor

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Slide {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SlideID: StableID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MasterID?: StableID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LayoutID?: StableID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ObjectOrder: ObjectID[]

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reordering, renaming, hiding, duplicating or moving a slide MUST NOT mutate the identity of an existing SlideID. Duplicating a slide MUST allocate a new SlideID and new IDs for duplicated slide-owned objects while preserving references that are explicitly shared by definition.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A reference to a slide or object MUST resolve by stable ID. Position-based references such as 'slide 4' MAY be accepted as user input, but MUST be resolved to a stable ID before persistence or execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing a release default MUST create an explicit persisted setting override. Absence of an override means the release default above; implementations MUST NOT infer a different default from platform, file origin or prior session state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Authoring shell and slide navigation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The editing shell MUST expose a persistent slide navigator, thumbnail view, slide sorter/grid view and searchable presentation outline. The same SlideID MUST back every representation of a slide.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required slide operations:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Create, duplicate, delete/recover, reorder, hide/unhide and move slides between presentation sections.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Jump to slide by outline/search result, stable reference or user-visible position.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multi-select slides for reorder, duplicate, delete, export and section assignment where the operation is semantically valid.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preserve selection and focus predictably after slide mutations; deleting the active slide MUST move focus to a deterministic adjacent surviving slide.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The authoring shell MUST provide undo/redo, zoom, fit slide, fit selection, rulers, guides, grid, snapping controls and a status surface showing at least current slide/total slide count, zoom and relevant selection/document state. Keyboard-only navigation MUST cover the navigator, canvas, notes pane and inspectors.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Conventional object editing and layout

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST provide mature slide-object editing for text, shapes, lines/connectors, images, shared tables/charts/graphs, drawings, media, code objects, 3D objects, Generative UI objects and supported embedded/shared objects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every spatial object type that declares geometric editing MUST support the applicable subset of:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Create, duplicate, delete, multi-select, group/ungroup and lock/unlock.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Move, resize, rotate, flip, z-order change, align and distribute.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Snap to grid/guides/objects and enter exact position, size and rotation values.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crop or mask only for object types whose renderer declares crop/mask support.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Style copy/paste without silently copying object identity, runtime state or permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shape and text styling MUST persist actual stored values. Inspectors, toolbars and keyboard commands MUST read from and write to the same canonical object properties; a visible control that does not mutate the corresponding stored property is non-conformant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST support object naming and a selection/object tree. The tree MUST expose stacking order, locked/hidden state and semantic object identity. Reordering the tree MUST change z-order only when the selected object type participates in z-order.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Themes, masters, layouts and templates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST support theme colours, theme fonts, backgrounds, reusable style tokens, slide masters, slide layouts, placeholders and reusable templates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A slide linked to a layout MUST inherit layout/master properties unless that property has an explicit slide-level override.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing a master or layout MUST update linked slides without deleting valid slide-level overrides.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reset Layout MUST remove only slide-level overrides governed by the selected layout; it MUST NOT delete unrelated slide-owned objects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PPTX/ODP import MUST preserve representable master/layout relationships instead of flattening every slide to unrelated absolute objects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Notes-page and handout layout data present in an imported format MUST be retained when the source construct maps to a declared Present capability. If no declared mapping exists, import MUST emit a CompatibilityIssue rather than silently dropping the construct.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Speaker notes and notes workflow

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every slide MUST have first-class speaker notes identified by a stable NotesID. Notes are authoring content associated with a SlideID and are not audience-slide content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SpeakerNotes {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: NotesID: StableID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SlideID: StableID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Content: SharedRichTextDocument

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Locale?: LocaleID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: RevisionID: RevisionID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Notes MUST be editable in a dedicated notes pane and a full Notes view.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Notes MUST support shared rich-text editing, lists, links, proofing and supported shared embedded objects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Notes MUST be searchable and addressable by typed APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The shared Dictation capability MUST operate in speaker notes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Notes MUST appear in Presenter View and notes-page print/export when explicitly selected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal slideshow output, ordinary audience capture, PDF/image export and generated video MUST exclude speaker notes by default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A notes-inclusive export MUST require an explicit notes output mode; it MUST NOT be inferred from the presence of notes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PPTX/ODP import/export MUST preserve speaker notes when the destination format supports them. Loss or degradation MUST be listed in the compatibility report.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Word, character and speaking statistics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST provide live text statistics for presentation content. The statistics engine MUST expose the following explicit scopes: SELECTION, CURRENT_SLIDE, CURRENT_NOTES, ALL_SLIDES, ALL_NOTES and PRESENTATION_COMBINED.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PresentationTextStatistics {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scope: StatisticsScope

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: WordCount: integer >= 0

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CharacterCountWithSpaces: integer >= 0

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CharacterCountWithoutSpaces: integer >= 0

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SlideTextWordCount?: integer >= 0

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: NotesWordCount?: integer >= 0

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: EstimatedSpeakingSeconds?: integer >= 0

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Word boundaries MUST follow the platform Unicode word-segmentation implementation based on Unicode word-boundary rules. Character counts MUST count user-perceived Unicode grapheme clusters rather than UTF-16 code units. CharacterCountWithoutSpaces MUST exclude grapheme clusters classified by the platform Unicode implementation as whitespace.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Slide-text statistics include authored text visible in text-bearing slide objects and component labels in the selected scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Speaker-note statistics include only speaker-note rich-text content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Comments, alt text, object names, Actions node labels, code source, hidden implementation metadata and compatibility metadata MUST NOT be included in ordinary word/character counts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ALL_SLIDES MUST include hidden slides by default because they are part of the authored document; the statistics UI MUST provide an explicit Exclude hidden slides filter.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PRESENTATION_COMBINED MUST expose slide-text and notes counts separately in addition to the combined totals.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Estimated speaking time MUST be calculated from notes WordCount using SpeakerWordsPerMinute. The release default is 130 words/minute. The user MUST be able to change this value without altering the note text. EstimatedSpeakingSeconds = round(WordCount / SpeakerWordsPerMinute * 60).

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Counts MUST update after a committed text edit without requiring a save/reopen cycle and MUST be accessible from normal authoring UI without inserting count text into the presentation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Search, proofing, comments and collaboration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST provide presentation-wide search and replace across slide text and speaker notes. Every result MUST identify the SlideID, object/notes target and exact text range required to navigate to the match semantically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spell-check/proofing MUST operate on slide text and speaker notes and MUST preserve per-range language metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Comments and replies MUST be anchorable to a SlideID, ObjectID and, where supported, a text range.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Realtime collaboration MUST preserve concurrent object, text, notes and comment edits using revision/conflict semantics; naive timestamp last-writer-wins data loss is prohibited.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Presence indicators and remote selections are session UI state and MUST NOT mutate presentation content.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Actions runtime and state model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST NOT implement an independent legacy animation engine or an independent transition runtime. All dynamic, timed, interactive and transition behaviour MUST be represented by a canonical typed Actions graph executed by the shared graph runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ActionGraph {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GraphID: StableID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GraphRevision: RevisionID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Nodes: ActionNode[]

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Edges: ActionEdge[]

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Entrypoints: ActionBinding[]

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PresentationRuntimeState {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GlobalVariables: VariableMap

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SlideVariables: Map<SlideID, VariableMap>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ComponentState: Map<ComponentInstanceID, VariableMap>

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SessionState: VariableMap

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Slides, objects, interactive components, media, code objects, 3D objects and live-drawing surfaces MUST expose versioned typed events. Event payloads MUST be schema-validated before graph execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The release event vocabulary MUST include at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PresentationStarted, PresentationEnded, SlideEntered, SlideLeft, NextSlideRequested and PreviousSlideRequested.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clicked, DoubleClicked, PointerEntered, PointerLeft, Focused, Blurred and supported key/gesture events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: TimerElapsed and VariableChanged.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MediaStarted, MediaPaused, MediaPositionChanged, MediaEnded and MediaError.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ComponentValueChanged and ComponentSubmitted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DrawingChanged and code-result/code-event output.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Actions MUST support conditions, branching, sequencing, parallel branches, delays/timers, reusable subgraphs and typed error paths. Actions MUST address targets by stable semantic IDs and MUST NOT simulate mouse/keyboard input when a typed capability exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph execution MUST be deterministic for the same graph revision, initial local state and deterministic inputs. When multiple nodes become runnable simultaneously, ordering MUST be defined by explicit dependencies/priority and a stable NodeID tie-breaker. External service results are recorded inputs and do not make the local scheduling order unspecified.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cycles are permitted only when the runtime execution guard can bound them. Every event cascade MUST have a finite execution budget and loop detection. Exceeding the budget MUST terminate the affected cascade with a typed runtime error rather than freezing the presentation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Starting a presentation creates a new PresentationSession with a defined initial state. SessionState and component runtime state reset on restart by default. Persistence requires an explicit author-configured persistence binding and the normal permission/write rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Transitions builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Transitions sidebar MUST remain available as a simple authoring surface, but it is a specialised Actions-graph editor. It MUST NOT invoke a second transition engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Choosing or editing a transition MUST create/update a marked Actions subgraph owned by that transition definition.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The sidebar MUST expose Open in Actions to reveal the exact generated subgraph.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Simple-editor changes MUST modify only nodes owned by the transition definition and MUST preserve user-authored extension nodes connected outside that owned region.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If an advanced graph edit makes the transition no longer representable by the simple sidebar, the sidebar MUST show a Custom/Advanced state rather than deleting or approximating the graph.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A transition completes only when its graph reaches the transition completion node. Slide navigation MUST commit exactly once per NavigationRequestID.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Interactive and reusable components

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST ship first-class accessible Button, Switch, Text Input, Dropdown, Slider and Flashcard component types.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Components MUST expose typed properties, state, focus/keyboard semantics, accessibility role/name/value and versioned events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Built-in hover, focus, pressed and value behaviour MUST work without requiring an author to construct a graph.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: HEADING_3

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Runnable code:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A runnable-code object MUST store source, registered language/runtime ID, declared inputs, typed outputs, permissions and execution limits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Execution MUST occur in a sandbox. Filesystem, network, account and device access are denied by default and may be granted only through declared platform capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CPU/time, memory and output limits MUST be enforced by the selected runtime provider. Limit violations MUST return typed errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Code results/events MUST be consumable by Actions and MAY update authorised presentation objects through typed APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Audio and video:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Media objects MUST expose Play, Pause, Stop, Seek, SetVolume and SetPlaybackRate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Media events MUST include Started, Paused, PositionChanged, Ended and Error.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Missing, offline or unsupported media MUST produce an explicit media error state; silent broken placeholders are prohibited.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native 3D:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The initial supported interchange formats MUST include glTF and GLB.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 3D objects MUST support transform, camera/orbit controls, camera presets, lighting/environment, material rendering, hotspots and Actions integration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model-intrinsic animation/timeline playback MUST be controlled through typed 3D Actions; it MUST NOT create a legacy presentation-animation subsystem.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drawing/live ink:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST use the shared Rnote-derived structured drawing/ink model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live drawing modes are OFF, PRESENTER_ONLY and PARTICIPANTS where the collaboration surface supports participant input.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live ink persistence modes are SESSION_ONLY, AUTO_SAVE and EXPLICIT_COMMIT.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DrawingChanged MUST be available to Actions and, when authorised, Dulche.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST support full-screen and windowed slideshow playback and presenter/audience display selection when multiple display targets are available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Presenter View MUST display current slide, next slide, speaker notes, slide navigator, elapsed timer, clock and presentation controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AudienceOutput and PresenterUI are separate render targets. Speaker notes, timers, controls, diagnostics and presenter-only overlays MUST NOT enter AudienceOutput unless the user explicitly selects a presenter-view recording/export mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The runtime MUST support keyboard navigation, slide jumping, hidden-slide rules, black/white blank screen, presenter pointer/laser, permitted live ink, live captions/subtitles where configured and interactive components/Actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reduced-motion preference MUST be exposed to the Actions runtime. Motion-heavy Actions MUST provide a defined reduced-motion result rather than ignoring the preference.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: HEADING_3
text: Rehearsal, timings and recording

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST support rehearsal of timings and structured session recording.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rehearsal MUST record navigation and Action-path timing without converting the authored presentation into a fixed linear deck.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recording MAY capture narration, camera, pointer/ink and the actual executed Action path subject to device permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A recorded session MUST retain RouteHistory and timing data sufficient to replay or export the recorded route.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replacing an existing recording MUST be reviewable and undoable; destructive replacement without a recoverable prior revision is prohibited.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI-aware authoring and live presentation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent AI bar MUST receive permission-filtered semantic context for all authorised slides, off-screen objects, speaker notes, Actions graphs, component definitions/state, media metadata, runnable code metadata, 3D objects, drawings and current presentation-session state. Semantic context MUST be preferred over screenshot/OCR interpretation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Read-only AI mode MAY inspect, explain, summarise, rehearse and propose changes, but MUST NOT mutate the presentation or live runtime state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write AI mode MAY create/edit slides, notes, objects, components and Actions only through typed Present APIs and the normal permission, revision, undo and conflict semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Requests such as branching on an audience answer, converting objects into a flashcard component or highlighting diagram regions on click MUST produce canonical typed graph/component mutations rather than UI automation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated edits MUST be attributable to a revision/audit event and MUST be reversible through the normal revision/undo model.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Video, audio, podcast, print and static export

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST generate Video, Audio and Podcast outputs from the canonical presentation model rather than from a detached textual summary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Video rendering MUST execute the actual presentation runtime and timed Actions for a selected route.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Audio output MUST use presentation content and speaker/narration configuration without rendering slide visuals.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Podcast output MUST transform presentation content into a conversational treatment using selected Dulche Voice models/voices.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated narration/script and timeline MUST be previewable and editable before final rendering.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An interactive presentation may have multiple valid routes. Export MUST require one of RECORDED_SESSION, DEFAULT_ACTION_PATH or EXPLICIT_BRANCH_PATH. Present MUST NOT guess arbitrary button/quiz choices.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Static output MUST support full slides, selected slides, notes pages, outline text and configurable handout layouts with multiple slides per page where the target supports them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PDF/image export MUST expose slide range, hidden-slide inclusion, background/transparency handling and notes inclusion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Speaker notes are excluded from audience-facing static output by default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page size, orientation, margins and scaling MUST be explicit and previewable for print/handout output.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Import/export compatibility contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Import/export MUST produce an explicit CompatibilityReport whenever a source or destination format cannot represent the complete native model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CompatibilityIssue {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
