heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compatibility severity semantics:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: INFO means the construct is translated without user-visible semantic loss; export/import may continue without acknowledgement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: WARNING means the construct is degraded or omitted but the operation can still produce a usable artifact; the issue MUST identify the exact affected source/target and resulting behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ERROR means continuing would violate the selected export/import policy, produce an invalid artifact or cause unaccepted destructive loss; the operation MUST block until the user changes the policy, removes the blocking feature or chooses a supported target.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: TRANSLATED means the destination preserves the source semantics; DEGRADED means semantics remain usable but differ; OMITTED means the construct is absent from the result; BLOCKED means no result is committed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PPTX/ODP legacy transitions and animations MUST be translated into Actions graphs when representable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST NOT retain a hidden executable legacy animation engine solely for compatibility.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unsupported or partially translated import behaviour MUST be listed in the CompatibilityReport.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PPTX/ODP export MUST compile the representable Actions subset into destination-native constructs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom components, arbitrary stateful branching, runnable code, Generative UI, AI behaviours and richer interactive 3D logic that cannot be represented MUST be reported explicitly; silent disappearance is prohibited.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Import/export validation MUST cover slides, masters/layouts, text, speaker notes, media, supported charts/tables, links, accessibility metadata and representable Actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: .9to1p is the authoritative full-fidelity format. A successful destination file creation is not sufficient evidence of compatibility.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present MUST expose accessible semantics in both authoring and presentation runtimes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Relevant visual objects MUST support alt text/description.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Slides MUST have an explicit reading order; interactive content MUST have an explicit focus order when reading order is insufficient.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Interactive components MUST expose accessible role, name, state/value and keyboard interaction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Authoring and presenting MUST be operable without a pointer for required workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Focus MUST be visible; required state MUST NOT be communicated only by colour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Zoom/text scaling and reduced-motion behaviour MUST be supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An accessibility checker MUST identify at least missing required alt text, problematic reading/focus order and inaccessible interactive controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accessibility metadata MUST round-trip through .9to1p and MUST be preserved in PPTX/ODP when the destination construct can represent it.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Security, permissions and external side effects

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present Actions, generated UI, runnable code, media, participant input and AI integrations MUST obey the platform permission broker and risk classification. A presentation MUST NOT gain arbitrary filesystem, network, account or device control merely because it is opened or presented.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Viewer interaction MUST NOT grant permissions that the presenting user/session does not already possess.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: External side effects invoked from a slideshow MUST use the same confirmation, idempotency, audit and typed-error rules as the equivalent app/Automation action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A denied permission MUST produce an explicit denied/error result that Actions can handle; the runtime MUST NOT silently substitute a weaker or different side effect.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Presentation content from untrusted sources MUST NOT be able to modify Home permissions or disable sandbox restrictions.

heading: HEADING_3

heading: HEADING_3
text: Release acceptance criteria

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Release conformance requires behaviour evidence. Source presence, UI screenshots or a successful build are insufficient on their own.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The release validation suite MUST demonstrate, at minimum:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Create -> edit -> save -> close -> reopen with slide/object identity, masters/layouts/themes and speaker notes preserved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live word/character statistics for selection, slide, notes and full-presentation scopes, including separate slide/notes totals and speaking-time calculation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mature conventional slide editing: multi-select, group, align/distribute, exact geometry, z-order, lock, crop/mask where applicable, guides/grid/snapping and object-tree operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A non-trivial Actions graph containing an event, condition, parallel/sequential work, state mutation and navigation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Transitions-sidebar edit that produces an Actions subgraph and survives Open in Actions plus a compatible round-trip back to the simple editor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All required built-in interactive components and one reusable custom Component Type with revisioned linked instances.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Generative UI object connected to Actions without raw HTML/JavaScript injection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: One sandboxed runnable-code example that emits a typed result and one denied-capability test.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Audio/video playback through typed controls and media events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A supported glTF/GLB model with camera/hotspot Actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured live ink in at least SESSION_ONLY and EXPLICIT_COMMIT modes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Presenter View with current/next slide, notes and timer while AudienceOutput remains free of presenter-only state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rehearsal/recording with recoverable RouteHistory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PPTX/ODP import containing legacy transitions/animations with translated or explicitly reported results.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PPTX/ODP export with a CompatibilityReport for any non-representable native feature.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PDF/handout/notes-page export with explicit slide range and notes policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard-only authoring/presenting and accessibility-checker coverage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Read-only versus Write enforcement and typed mutation auditability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crash/interrupted-save recovery and concurrent-edit/revision-conflict behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app shared-object clipboard fidelity for Present <-> Write, Present <-> Canvas and Present <-> Boards, using at least one shared text object and one non-text shared object supported by each tested endpoint.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any acceptance case that fails by silently omitting data, silently degrading behaviour, bypassing typed APIs or exposing presenter-only/private state to the audience MUST block release conformance.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Canvas

heading: HEADING_3
text: Purpose, ownership and boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Canvas is the handwriting, sketching, drawing and freeform spatial-authoring application in 9to1. Canvas owns Canvas artifacts, spatial composition, page/infinite-canvas geometry, drawing/ink editing, Canvas tool state, Canvas-specific view state and the Canvas domain API.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas is not a Boards replacement and MUST NOT become a generic workspace/page system. Boards owns structured mixed-content workspaces and pages; Canvas owns freeform spatial drawing documents. Boards MAY host a live Canvas artifact, but the embedded Canvas remains owned by Canvas and retains its Canvas ArtifactID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST use CUI for the visible application shell, menus, toolbars, inspectors, dialogs, launch screen and ordinary controls. A specialised accelerated drawing/rendering surface MAY exist as a CUI control for performance; .cui markup MUST NOT require each stroke sample to become an independent generic UI widget.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Donor and upstream contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rnote is the authoritative donor for mature handwriting, drawing, stroke, selection, rendering and applicable import/export behaviour. The implementation agent MUST obtain the latest appropriate stable Rnote source when the Canvas implementation pass begins, record the exact upstream repository, commit/release identifier and licence, and include the selected donor source in the Canvas source tree/build graph in accordance with the global Source & Donor Apps contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST maintain a donor-parity manifest generated from inspection of the selected Rnote revision. Every user-visible donor capability MUST be classified as PRESERVE, REPLACE_WITH_9TO1_NATIVE_EQUIVALENT or NOT_APPLICABLE. An unclassified donor feature is a release blocker, not permission to omit it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PRESERVE means the donor behaviour, shortcuts, input semantics, quality-of-life behaviour and applicable data behaviour remain available through the 9to1 implementation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: REPLACE_WITH_9TO1_NATIVE_EQUIVALENT is used when 9to1 already owns the equivalent platform capability, including CUI shell/UI, Dulche AI, Home permission handling, Files storage integration or other shared 9to1 services.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: NOT_APPLICABLE requires a concrete technical, legal or product-boundary reason and validation that its omission does not remove expected Canvas functionality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Proprietary donor AI MUST NOT be copied. Any applicable AI-assisted behaviour is implemented through Dulche and the Canvas typed API.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Supported platforms and capability negotiation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST ship on every 9to1 platform for which the app is not explicitly exempt under the global platform/web rules. Desktop/native and web implementations MUST share the same Canvas artifact schema, stable identities, domain API semantics and server-side canonical entities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Platform-specific input or rendering capability differences MUST be negotiated explicitly. Hardware capability absence MUST NOT be misrepresented as format incapability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If pressure is unavailable, Canvas records and renders strokes using the declared non-pressure fallback without deleting pressure data already stored in the artifact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If tilt, barrel buttons, palm rejection assistance or another device capability is unavailable, the UI MUST disable or omit only the dependent control and expose a capability-unavailable reason where the absence is user-relevant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening an artifact on a lower-capability platform MUST preserve unsupported stored data for later use on a capable platform.

heading: HEADING_3

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The native full-fidelity Canvas format is .9to1c. Persisted Canvas data MUST be schema-versioned. Readers MUST migrate, preserve or reject incompatible schema versions explicitly and MUST NOT guess the meaning of unknown fields.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Document mode and page-type model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST support both INFINITE and PAGED document modes as first-class modes selectable through the top-right quick-settings surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: INFINITE mode provides a spatially unbounded working area for normal user workflows and MUST NOT expose an artificial page edge as document structure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PAGED mode contains ordered PageID entities with explicit page size, orientation where applicable and page/background settings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page size, orientation, background and page ordering are document state and therefore collaborate, persist and travel with the artifact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing between INFINITE and PAGED is a structural conversion, not a cosmetic toggle. The conversion workflow MUST preview the mapping of existing content, identify content that would cross/clash with generated page boundaries, and require explicit confirmation before committing a conversion that changes layout.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conversion MUST be undoable/recoverable through document history and MUST NOT clip, discard or rasterise existing objects silently.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistence, autosave and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas persistence MUST be atomic at the smallest user-visible document mutation/revision boundary supported by the storage architecture. A partially written resource MUST NOT make the last known-good artifact revision unreadable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Autosave MUST persist committed document mutations without requiring a manual Save command.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A save failure MUST surface an explicit unsaved/error state and retain recoverable local work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crash recovery MUST restore the last durable revision and recover newer journaled/temporary operations where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Imported source files MUST NOT be destructively overwritten merely because they were opened. Overwrite/export requires an explicit user operation appropriate to the source format.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Closing an artifact while durable persistence is unresolved MUST provide an explicit recovery choice rather than silently discarding changes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Launch screen and document lifecycle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST implement the global launch-screen contract using real Files/storage state. Required launch capabilities are Create Blank, templates/starter canvases where supported, Recent, Favourites/Pinned, Shared with Me, search, Open and Import.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Create Blank MUST create a real Canvas artifact with a new ArtifactID and selected/default CanvasMode. Launch entries MUST NOT be mock cards.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening, renaming, moving, favouriting, sharing and deleting an entire Canvas artifact MUST integrate with Files' canonical artifact/storage semantics. Moving or renaming a file MUST NOT change ArtifactID.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Primary Canvas shell

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The normal editing surface MUST prioritise the canvas and MUST NOT permanently reserve a ribbon, large left tool rail or large inspector panel for routine drawing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Top-left document controls:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A compact ≡ pill opens the Canvas/application command surface for document/application commands assigned to it by the final CUI command model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A neighbouring document-name pill displays the current DisplayName, for example Notebook 3, and provides document-level operations including rename, location/document information and applicable document collaboration/navigation commands.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing DisplayName MUST NOT change ArtifactID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Bottom primary toolbar:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical default order is Select, Pan, Pen, Eraser, Insert, Tools, AI. The toolbar is a floating horizontal CUI surface centred near the bottom of the primary canvas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: | Select | Pan | Pen | Eraser | Insert | Tools | AI |

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The currently selected tool MUST display both its icon and human-readable name.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Non-selected tools MAY display icon-only in the compact state, but their names and primary shortcut MUST be exposed by hover and keyboard-focus tooltips.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The toolbar MUST remain usable with mouse, touch, stylus and keyboard navigation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Responsive compaction MAY use controlled overflow or horizontal scrolling; tools MUST NOT silently disappear.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The active editing tool is document-session/editor state, not persisted canonical document content unless a specific tool setting is declared as a user preference.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Contextual tool-options host

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When the active tool exposes contextual options, Canvas MUST render one secondary floating options surface immediately above the primary bottom toolbar. Tool implementations MUST declare their options through a common option schema rather than constructing unrelated private popup systems.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: HEADING_3
text: Select and Pan

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Select is the canonical object/stroke manipulation tool. It MUST support the applicable Rnote-derived selection modes plus shared-object selection semantics, including single selection, multi-selection and lasso/area selection where supported by the donor/object type.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Applicable selected content MUST support move, resize, rotate, duplicate, delete/recover, cut/copy/paste, group/ungroup, z-order/layer movement, alignment/distribution where meaningful and lock/unlock.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An operation unsupported by a selected object type MUST be disabled with a defined capability reason rather than appearing to succeed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pan is an explicit navigation tool. Pointer/stylus movement while Pan is active MUST navigate the viewport and MUST NOT create or modify drawing content.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Pen system and preset pens

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pen is the primary structured ink-authoring tool and MUST preserve applicable Rnote pen/brush behaviour. Pen options appear in the contextual tool-options surface above the bottom toolbar.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST ship with useful preset pens derived from the available drawing engines in the selected donor revision. Presets MUST cover the major donor-supported writing/drawing instrument classes that remain applicable, such as ordinary ink/ballpoint-style writing, fountain/variable-width ink, pencil and highlighter/marker behaviour where the donor supports them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Pen menu MUST provide a Custom Pen workflow. Users MUST be able to create, preview, save, duplicate, rename, reorder, favourite, edit and delete/recover custom pen presets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The custom-pen editor MUST expose only properties supported by the selected ToolEngineID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Saving a pen preset MUST NOT retroactively alter existing strokes unexpectedly. Existing strokes retain resolved brush properties or an explicit versioned preset reference sufficient to reproduce their authored appearance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preset and custom pen selection MUST be keyboard and touch accessible.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Eraser

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Eraser tool MUST expose at least two user-facing modes in its contextual options:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Natural Eraser — drag over drawing content to erase according to the configured donor-supported erasure semantics, including partial/stroke behaviour where provided.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quick Eraser — click/tap a target stroke or object to remove the complete resolved target immediately.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quick Eraser deletion MUST use the same document history/domain delete operation as other Canvas deletion and therefore MUST remain undoable/recoverable. The target-resolution rule MUST be deterministic when objects overlap.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Insert catalogue and parity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Insert is the structured object insertion catalogue. Its first-level menu MUST use the following category order and each category opens a submenu to the right on desktop:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text   >

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shapes >

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Media  >

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Table  >

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other  >

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The first-level menu is category-only. Selecting/hovering a category MUST NOT insert a default object silently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text submenu:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text Box — freely positioned shared rich-text object.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Heading — text object with a semantic heading role and heading defaults; it MUST NOT be implemented only as visually larger text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Paragraph — text object with a semantic paragraph/body role and paragraph defaults.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shapes submenu:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opens the registered shared shape/line catalogue supported by Canvas, including applicable lines/connectors and shape families exposed by the Shared Productivity Engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shapes MUST use the same canonical shared shape definitions and editing behaviour used by other 9to1 productivity surfaces rather than a reduced Canvas-only shape model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Media submenu:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Image.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Audio.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Video.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Media objects MUST use the corresponding shared media representation and preserve editable metadata/behaviour rather than flattening to a thumbnail.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Table submenu:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST expose the shared table creation experience and the full Canvas-applicable shared table feature set.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST NOT implement a reduced Canvas-only table type. Table editing capabilities, structure and formatting come from the shared table engine; Canvas owns freeform placement/transform around the table.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other submenu:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other contains registered Canvas-compatible shared object types that do not warrant their own first-level category.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph MUST be available through Other using the canonical shared graph representation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other MAY include Link, File/Artifact, Embed, Equation, Code, Generative UI and additional registered shared types when the shared capability registry declares them Canvas-compatible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drawing MUST NOT appear as a separate Insert item because freeform pen/drawing is already a primary Canvas capability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Insert catalogue parity has two mandatory dimensions:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Catalogue parity — every shared productivity object type declared Canvas-compatible by the shared capability registry MUST be reachable through Insert.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Behaviour parity — after insertion, the object MUST retain the shared object's complete applicable behaviour. Canvas MUST NOT replace a shared object with a feature-reduced Canvas-specific approximation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Insert UI MUST be generated from registered insertion capabilities plus the fixed category taxonomy above. Adding a registered shared object MUST NOT require a separate incompatible Canvas object implementation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Desktop cascading menus MUST use conventional keyboard behaviour: Up/Down move, Right opens a submenu, Left returns, Enter/Space invokes and Escape closes the current menu level. Touch interaction MUST provide an explicit navigable submenu/back model and MUST NOT depend on hover.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Tools family

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tools is the home for specialised Canvas instruments that do not warrant permanent top-level toolbar slots. The exact list MUST be derived from the selected Rnote donor parity manifest and shared Canvas capabilities rather than an arbitrary hand-written subset.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Applicable geometry, line/arrow, ruler/measurement, fill/colour-picker, specialised selection and other donor tools MAY be organised here while retaining their donor behaviour. A tool moved into Tools is not optional merely because it is not a top-level button.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A future pin/favourite mechanism MAY allow users to promote specialised tools to the primary toolbar, but the default canonical toolbar remains Select, Pan, Pen, Eraser, Insert, Tools, AI.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Top-right quick-settings pill

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A compact switch/settings pill MUST appear at the top-right of the Canvas editing surface. Activating it opens a dropdown for high-frequency document-level and editor-level settings. It is not a replacement for the complete Settings application.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Document-scoped quick settings MUST include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas/page type: INFINITE or PAGED.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page size and orientation when PAGED.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background colour/design, including registered ruled/grid/dot or other supported background patterns and their applicable spacing/design parameters.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other document settings explicitly registered as quick-adjustable by Canvas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editor/user-scoped quick settings MUST include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Smart Pen.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Snapping and guide/grid visibility where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stylus/touch interaction preferences and exposed palm-rejection/gesture settings supported by the active platform.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other registered non-document editor preferences appropriate to quick adjustment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Document-scoped settings MUST persist with/collaborate through the artifact. Editor/user-scoped settings MUST persist as user/device preferences unless an individual setting explicitly declares document scope.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Smart Pen

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Smart Pen is an editor setting that modifies new handwriting behaviour while enabled. Its purpose is to make freehand handwriting feel more controlled/snappy and visually neater without converting it into typed text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Smart Pen MUST preserve handwriting as structured editable ink.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Smart Pen MUST NOT silently replace ink with text or discard original authored stroke semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The adjustment algorithm MAY smooth geometry, regularise locally unstable stroke motion and make other constrained handwriting clean-up changes that preserve the user's intended writing rather than redrawing arbitrary content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The resulting adjustment MUST be immediately undoable. The active undo/history window MUST retain enough pre-adjustment data to restore the user's original committed stroke.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Smart Pen state is an editor/user preference unless an explicit future document-scoped mode is specified.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Input, stylus and gesture contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Input quality is a core Canvas requirement. Canvas MUST preserve applicable high-fidelity stylus information provided by the runtime, including pressure and tilt when available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pen/stylus drawing, touch navigation and mouse/trackpad interaction MUST be distinguishable so ordinary navigation does not create unintended ink.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Applicable eraser/barrel-button semantics from the selected donor must remain available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Palm rejection MUST use platform/donor capabilities where available and MUST fail predictably when hardware/runtime support is absent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pan, zoom and rotate gestures MUST NOT mutate document content unless the active tool/action explicitly maps the gesture to a content mutation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stored pressure/tilt data MUST survive save/reopen and lower-capability viewing even if the current device cannot generate equivalent samples.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Layers, ordering and object manipulation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST preserve applicable Rnote layer functionality. Layers use stable LayerID identities and are document state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to create, rename, reorder, hide/show, lock/unlock and delete/recover layers where supported by the donor model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Moving an object between layers changes LayerID membership without changing ObjectID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hidden/locked layers MUST obey the same selection/edit restrictions through UI and API.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Z-order within a layer and layer order are distinct concepts and MUST NOT be conflated by APIs or UI.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shared Productivity Engine and cross-app object semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST use Home's Shared Productivity Engine for every shared object type it supports. Canvas owns spatial placement; the shared engine owns the shared object's semantic content/model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared rich text, shapes, tables, media, graphs, equations, code, Generative UI and other registered shared objects MUST retain their shared schema when copied, embedded or referenced across supporting 9to1 apps.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The shared Rnote-derived ink model MUST allow structured ink to remain editable ink in Boards, Present, Write or Spaces where the destination declares ink support.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unsupported destination/object combinations MUST fail explicitly or require an explicit user-selected flatten/export operation; silent rasterisation or semantic loss is prohibited.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clipboard and drag/drop MUST carry a typed multi-representation payload containing stable/source references plus portable shared-object representations as applicable. The destination chooses the highest-fidelity compatible representation; it MUST NOT silently choose a lower-fidelity bitmap when a supported structured representation exists.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files and Boards integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files is authoritative for storage/navigation semantics of Canvas artifacts. Canvas is authoritative for Canvas document semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST be able to host a live Canvas artifact/reference. A live Board embed references the same ArtifactID and canonical revision stream rather than creating an unmanaged duplicate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editing an authorised live Canvas embed in Boards edits the canonical Canvas artifact through Canvas domain operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening the same ArtifactID in Canvas and Boards MUST resolve to the same underlying artifact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A snapshot/static copy is permitted only through an explicit user operation that clearly identifies the result as a copy/export rather than a live embed.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dulche contextual AI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The bottom-toolbar AI item is the sole normal Canvas entry point for expanding the shared Dulche contextual AI bar. Canvas MUST NOT show a second permanently expanded AI bar while the bottom toolbar is present.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When AI is selected, the shared AI bar floats immediately above the bottom toolbar and the AI toolbar item becomes the selected tool. The bar contains the platform-standard AI access-mode controls, including Read-only and Write modes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selecting a different Canvas tool hides the expanded AI bar but MUST NOT automatically cancel an authorised active AI session. AI surface visibility and AI session lifecycle are distinct state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CanvasAIState {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SessionID?: StableID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Lifecycle: NONE | IDLE | ACTIVE | WAITING_FOR_USER | COMPLETED | FAILED

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SurfaceVisibility: HIDDEN | EXPANDED

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: IsAIToolSelected: boolean

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: IsAIToolSelected = true requires SurfaceVisibility = EXPANDED.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If SurfaceVisibility = HIDDEN and Lifecycle is ACTIVE or WAITING_FOR_USER, Canvas MUST show a compact sparkle session indicator immediately beside the top-right quick-settings pill.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clicking the top-right sparkle indicator selects AI, restores the existing SessionID and expands the AI bar above the bottom toolbar. It MUST NOT create a duplicate session.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a hidden session completes or fails, the indicator MUST enter a non-intrusive completed/error attention state until inspected/dismissed; it MUST NOT force the AI bar open or steal editing focus.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MUST receive permission-filtered semantic Canvas context including the active ArtifactID/PageID, stable object/stroke IDs, spatial relationships, text/shared-object semantics, current selection, document revision, current Canvas tool state where relevant and the Canvas actions allowed by the current AI access mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Read-only mode MAY inspect, search, reason, explain, navigate and propose changes but MUST NOT mutate the artifact or editor state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write mode MAY mutate Canvas only through typed Canvas/shared-object actions and the normal revision, permission, undo and conflict model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A user reference such as 'these four boxes' MUST resolve to stable target IDs at request/execution binding time. Later selection changes MUST NOT silently retarget the running operation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If targeted objects change incompatibly before an AI commit, the operation MUST return a revision/conflict result rather than blindly overwriting newer edits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Handwriting recognition, OCR or AI-generated descriptions are derived metadata unless the user explicitly invokes a conversion that creates a new typed/text representation. Derived recognition MUST NOT silently replace canonical ink.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Spaces and Automations integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spaces MUST be able to open/reference an authorised Canvas artifact and edit it conversationally using 9to1.Canvas typed actions. Spaces MUST NOT use mouse/keyboard simulation when the equivalent Canvas action exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations MUST receive exhaustive Canvas UI/API parity subject to the same permissions and platform capabilities. Canvas MUST publish typed events for meaningful document changes and MUST NOT flood workflows with raw pointer-move events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Minimum automatable event families:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Artifact opened/closed/saved/recovered.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page created/deleted/reordered and document mode changed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Object/stroke created/changed/deleted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Layer created/changed/deleted/reordered.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared object inserted/changed/removed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Collaboration/revision conflict and recovery state changes that are meaningful for automation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Collaboration and conflict semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas collaboration MUST operate on canonical structured document entities rather than exchanging flattened screenshots or whole-document last-write-wins blobs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Concurrent edits to independent strokes/objects/pages SHOULD merge without destroying unrelated work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conflicting edits to the same canonical entity MUST be detected using revision/operation semantics and resolved deterministically or surfaced as a conflict.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Naive timestamp last-write-wins MUST NOT be the default conflict strategy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Remote cursors, selections and transient viewport positions are collaboration presence/session state and MUST NOT alter canonical document content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation MAY use CRDTs, operation logs or another maintainable internal algorithm provided the observable collaboration, revision and recovery contract is satisfied.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Undo, redo and history

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All ordinary Canvas document mutations initiated by UI, AI, Spaces or Automation MUST enter the same canonical history/revision system unless an operation explicitly declares non-document session state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Undo/redo MUST operate on semantic user-visible operations, not arbitrary internal rendering steps.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI/API mutations MUST be attributable in history/audit metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Undoing deletion restores the same stable object/stroke identity where restoration semantics permit it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structural mode conversion, bulk manipulation and imported-content insertion MUST be represented as coherent reversible operations or explicit multi-operation transactions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Import and export

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The native .9to1c format is authoritative for full-fidelity Canvas behaviour. Canvas MUST retain all applicable Rnote import/export capabilities from the selected donor revision in addition to 9to1-native integrations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Import/export MUST preserve supported structured content and MUST produce an explicit compatibility report when the source or destination cannot represent part of the native Canvas model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unsupported features MUST be classified as translated, degraded, omitted or blocked with the affected entity identified.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Silent loss of layers, stroke properties, page structure, shared objects, accessibility metadata or other canonical content is prohibited.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A successful file creation/open is not sufficient validation; representative round trips MUST compare semantic content.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST make ordinary authoring and document-management workflows operable by keyboard and assistive technology even though the primary document is spatial/visual.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All toolbar, menu, submenu, quick-settings, document-pill and AI controls require accessible names, roles, focus states and keyboard operation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Meaningful Canvas objects MUST be inspectable through an accessible structured object/list view exposing object name/type, authored text, alt description and relevant ordering/spatial relationship information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual objects MUST support alt text/description where appropriate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pure freehand ink is not required to become authoritative text automatically. AI/OCR descriptions MUST remain clearly derived metadata unless the user explicitly adopts/converts them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required state MUST NOT be communicated only by colour; focus must be visible; zoom/display scaling and reduced-motion preferences must be respected.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Security and permissions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas inherits Home's permission broker and global API permission model. Canvas MUST declare action risk classifications and MUST NOT bypass Home for protected external or destructive operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening a Canvas file MUST NOT grant embedded code, Generative UI, media or linked artifacts arbitrary filesystem/network/account access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Embedded/shared objects execute only within the permissions of their owning capability/runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Untrusted imported Canvas content MUST NOT change Home trust grants, security policy or sandbox restrictions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Whole-artifact permanent deletion is routed through Files' canonical deletion semantics; ordinary object/stroke deletion remains Canvas document history unless explicitly made permanent through an authorised action.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Typed Canvas API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST expose a versioned first-party API namespace with UI parity. The canonical namespace is 9to1.Canvas; language bindings that cannot use 9to1 literally use the global aliasing rule without changing canonical action names.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CanvasMutationRequest {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: BaseRevisionID: RevisionID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: OperationID: StableID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ActorContext: PermissionFilteredActorContext

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CanvasMutationResult {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: RevisionID: RevisionID

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ChangedIDs: StableID[]

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Warnings: Warning[]

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required action families include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Artifact: Create, Open, Get, Rename, Save/Flush, Close, Recover, GetRevisionHistory, RestoreRevision and document-settings operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pages: List, Get, Create, Duplicate, Move/Reorder, Delete/Restore, SetBounds/Size/Orientation and set page/background properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Layers: List, Create, Rename, Reorder, SetVisibility, SetLocked, MoveObjects, Delete/Restore.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Objects/Strokes: query/get, insert/create, update style, transform, duplicate, group/ungroup, reorder, move layer, delete/restore and semantic search.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ink: begin/append/end stroke for authorised input/runtime integrations, create from structured samples, update allowed stroke properties and query stroke geometry/metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pens: ListPresets, CreatePreset, DuplicatePreset, UpdatePreset, Delete/RestorePreset and favourite/reorder operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Insert/shared objects: enumerate registered Canvas-compatible types and create each through its canonical shared-object action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Import/export: enumerate formats/capabilities, start long-running import/export jobs, query status, cancel and retrieve CompatibilityReport.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI/session integration: semantic-context queries and session binding/status operations; AI model execution remains owned by the shared Dulche platform.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Collaboration: presence/query, comments if Canvas exposes them, share/reference state and conflict/revision operations consistent with the owning collaboration service.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Actions that enumerate unbounded collections MUST paginate/stream. Long-running import/export/render work MUST return JobID, status and cancellation. Retry-safe mutations MUST use OperationID idempotency.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typed errors MUST distinguish at least NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARGUMENT, PERMISSION_DENIED, REVISION_CONFLICT, CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, FORMAT_INCOMPATIBLE, IO_ERROR, RUNTIME_ERROR and CANCELLED.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and resource constraints

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST remain responsive for realistically large documents and MUST NOT render/process the entire spatial document every frame solely because it exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Viewport rendering MUST use spatial culling/virtualisation and appropriate caching so distant off-screen objects do not impose per-frame work proportional to total document size.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Incremental edits such as adding one stroke SHOULD avoid rewriting/re-rendering unrelated content where the persistence/rendering architecture can preserve correctness without doing so.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Caches MUST be bounded and invalidated by semantic revisions rather than growing without limit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large images/media MUST use progressive/appropriate decoding and MUST NOT block the interactive input loop unnecessarily.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation test suite MUST include large-canvas fixtures with high stroke/object counts, embedded images/shared objects and widely separated spatial extents. Performance claims require measured runtime evidence on the declared supported-hardware baseline; 'feels fast' is not acceptance evidence.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Failure and recovery behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a shared object renderer fails, Canvas MUST preserve the object data and show a typed recoverable error representation rather than deleting or flattening it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a donor tool/backend capability fails to initialise, Canvas MUST report the unavailable capability and keep unaffected tools usable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transient save/sync failures MUST use bounded retry/backoff and expose unresolved state; infinite retries are prohibited.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If collaboration connectivity is lost, local permitted editing MAY continue when the storage/conflict model supports it, but unsynchronised state MUST be visible and reconciliation MUST use revision/conflict rules on reconnect.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If an import is partially parseable, Canvas MUST follow the declared import policy: either commit an explicitly reported partial result as a new artifact or fail atomically. It MUST NOT silently present a partial result as full-fidelity success.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Release acceptance criteria

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas is release-conformant only when behavioural evidence proves the complete agreed interaction model, donor parity and cross-app integration. Source presence, screenshots, disconnected controls or a successful build alone are insufficient.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The release validation suite MUST demonstrate at minimum:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Create an INFINITE artifact, draw/write with pressure-capable test input, pan/zoom, select/manipulate objects, save, close and reopen with stable IDs and stroke properties preserved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Create a PAGED artifact, configure size/orientation/background, add/reorder pages and save/reopen.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Convert between document modes through the preview/confirmation workflow without silent clipping/loss and verify undo/recovery.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Bottom toolbar layout/order, selected-tool name, hover/focus tooltips and contextual options above the toolbar.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preset Pen use plus create/edit/save/duplicate/reorder/delete/recover Custom Pen workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Natural Eraser and Quick Eraser, including deterministic overlap targeting and undo.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Insert cascading menu with Text, Shapes, Media, Table and Other; verify Text Box/Heading/Paragraph, shape/line catalogue, Image/Audio/Video, shared Table and Graph under Other.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Verify Drawing is not exposed as a redundant Insert item.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared-object parity tests proving Canvas does not substitute reduced private Text/Shape/Media/Table/Graph implementations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Top-right quick-settings pill with page type, background and Smart Pen plus correct document-vs-user persistence scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Smart Pen creates neater structured ink, does not convert to typed text and restores exact pre-adjustment content through undo.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI selected -> shared floating Dulche bar appears above toolbar; changing tool hides the bar without cancelling an active session; active hidden session shows the top-right sparkle indicator; clicking that indicator restores the same SessionID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Read-only AI is unable to mutate; Write AI performs a real typed edit and respects revision conflict if targets change.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live Canvas embed in Boards edits the same ArtifactID, and an explicitly created snapshot produces a distinct copy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files rename/move does not change ArtifactID; Files delete/recovery semantics work for the whole artifact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spaces performs a semantic Canvas edit through the Canvas API without UI simulation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automation/API parity for representative page, layer, stroke, shared-object, pen, settings, import/export and recovery operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app clipboard fidelity for structured ink and at least two supported shared-object types with Boards plus at least one of Write/Present.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Concurrent editing on independent objects preserves both edits; conflicting same-entity edits produce deterministic merge/conflict behaviour rather than silent last-write-wins loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard-only operation of required shell/menu/tool workflows and assistive-technology inspection of meaningful Canvas objects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative Rnote donor-parity suite against the pinned donor manifest, with every manifest entry evidenced or explicitly accepted as a scoped exception.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native and web/open-on-lower-capability round trips preserve unsupported pressure/tilt and other stored data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crash/interrupted-save recovery from a last-known-good revision plus recoverable newer work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large-canvas stress fixtures demonstrate bounded memory/cache behaviour, viewport culling and acceptable measured pointer/pan/zoom responsiveness on the declared baseline.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any acceptance path that silently drops user data, silently flattens a supported structured object, reports a disconnected UI control as working, creates duplicate canonical artifacts during live embedding, loses a running AI session solely because its UI is hidden, or omits an unreviewed donor feature MUST block release conformance.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Boards

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and donor contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Boards is the flexible visual workspace, note-taking and project-composition app. AppFlowy is the primary donor for applicable workspace/page/database/block behaviours. Boards MUST preserve applicable AppFlowy features, quality-of-life behaviours and non-proprietary block types from the selected donor revision unless a scoped donor-parity exception is recorded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AppFlowy proprietary AI, AppFlowy account/billing/subscription infrastructure and proprietary paid services are not copied. Only donor functionality available under legally usable source/licensing is eligible for direct source parity. Proprietary AI capabilities are replaced by 9-1/Dulche behaviour; unavailable proprietary services require a documented 9to1-native replacement or explicit non-applicability decision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation MUST maintain a donor-parity manifest for Boards identifying the selected AppFlowy revision and classifying each applicable user-visible feature/block as Preserve, Replace with 9to1-native equivalent or Not applicable. “Most AppFlowy features” MUST NOT be interpreted as permission to omit unreviewed donor functionality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Visual shell

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST use native CUI and a clean, seamless workspace surface. Native Board pages MUST NOT render as a paper/card floating inside another background, and MUST NOT add a persistent page border, shadow or sheet frame around the editable content area. The page/workspace background fills the available content surface continuously.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The interface MAY take interaction/layout inspiration from mature workspace/note apps such as AppFlowy and Notion, but it MUST use 9to1/CUI design language rather than reproducing another product’s visual styling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Landing page

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST implement the global launch-screen contract. Its landing page uses a board-centric card/grid composition: Create New is immediately available, recent boards are presented as visual cards with title/icon/preview metadata and last-modified state, and the left navigation/sidebar remains available so the user can move directly into an existing board.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The default landing view MUST expose Boards plus a Recent pages/components view. Templates and other discovery/idea surfaces MAY be added only when backed by real persisted/template data. The landing page MUST NOT fabricate recent/sample boards except explicitly labelled onboarding/template content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Sidebar and board switching

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Boards sidebar MUST show the currently selected Board as a dedicated board switcher control above that Board’s page tree. The control contains at least the Board icon and name. Activating it opens the board picker, allowing the user to search/select another Board without leaving the Boards app or opening a separate management screen.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The sidebar page tree is scoped to ActiveBoardID and MUST support nested pages/subpages, selection, add page, rename, reorder/move and delete/recover according to the user’s permissions. Switching Board changes the page tree atomically to the selected Board and MUST NOT mix pages from multiple Boards in the active hierarchy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: ActiveBoardID and ActivePageID are client/window navigation state and are not Board identity. Board/Page identity MUST remain stable across rename, reorder and sidebar position changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Canonical Board and Page model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Board MUST contain at least BoardID, Name, Icon?, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, owner/scope, ordered RootPageIDs, settings and revision metadata. BoardID is stable and MUST NOT derive from the Board name or Files path.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: BoardPage MUST contain at least PageID, BoardID, ParentPageID?, PageType, Title, Icon?, SortKey, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, permission metadata, revision and the type-specific content/reference payload. PageID is stable across move, nesting and rename.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: In the release-candidate scope, PageType MUST support Native, Write, Canvas, Chat and ScopedChat. Source subpages belonging to Chat/ScopedChat are represented as explicit source entities/subpages under that chat page and are not silently interpreted as ordinary Native pages.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native Board pages MUST store a versioned BlockTree, page-level DrawingLayer, layout settings and view settings. Write and Canvas pages reference/use their canonical shared-engine artifact model rather than flattening those app behaviours into Boards-specific copies. Chat/ScopedChat pages reference a persistent Agent/chat configuration plus their source collection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Shared Productivity Engine

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST use Home’s Shared Productivity Engine. Shared blocks/objects use the same schemas, formatting semantics, renderer/editor and typed actions as their equivalents in Write, Present, Canvas and Spaces. A table, code block, graph, image, drawing or other shared object copied between supported surfaces MUST retain its shared representation rather than being rebuilt as a Boards-only object.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MAY add Boards-specific container/layout metadata around a shared object, but MUST NOT fork the shared object payload itself. Cross-app copy/paste uses the versioned ProductivityObjectBundle contract owned by Home.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Edit and View modes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Board page surface MUST expose a persistent Edit/View switch in the top-right app/page chrome. Edit and View are authoring modes and are independent from the Locked/Unlocked layout mode defined below.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Edit mode permits mutations allowed by the user’s permissions and exposes authoring controls. View mode blocks document/page mutations while retaining navigation, selection/copy where permitted and explicitly view-safe interactive behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: View mode MAY unlock runtime interactions that are intentionally non-authoring. For example, a Graph block can expose sliders so a viewer can vary values and inspect the resulting graph. Such interaction state is session-local by default and MUST NOT modify the stored document or default graph configuration unless an explicit authorised save action is invoked in Edit mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent AI bar remains available in both modes. In View mode it is read-only with respect to Board/page content; an AI-requested mutation MUST require an authorised transition/action under Edit semantics rather than silently bypassing View mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Locked and Unlocked layout modes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native Board pages MUST support a separate LayoutMode with values Locked and Unlocked. LayoutMode controls spatial placement behaviour only; it does not replace Edit/View permissions and it does not disable free drawing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Locked mode preserves AppFlowy-style block-flow behaviour for flow blocks: blocks participate in the normal ordered document/block tree and are inserted/reordered using the donor-compatible flow layout. Existing absolute-position blocks remain visible at their saved coordinates but their free-position move/resize handles are disabled while Locked.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unlocked mode retains normal flow editing and additionally permits blocks to be placed/repositioned freely anywhere on the page canvas. A freely positioned block receives Layout = Absolute with X, Y, Width, Height and ZOrder. A normal donor-flow block uses Layout = Flow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Switching from Unlocked back to Locked MUST NOT snap, reflow, discard or convert Absolute blocks. Their exact stored coordinates and dimensions remain unchanged. Locked mode simply prevents casual spatial repositioning while continuing to allow the block’s content to be edited in Edit mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unlocked drag/drop MAY convert a Flow block to Absolute only through an explicit spatial placement gesture. Converting an Absolute block back to Flow MUST be an explicit action because it changes document layout semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Free drawing and ink

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native Board pages MUST support free drawing directly over the page canvas using the Home Shared Productivity Engine’s Rnote-derived drawing/ink implementation. Ink is stored in the page DrawingLayer using stable stroke/object IDs and MUST remain editable after save/restart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drawing MUST work in both Locked and Unlocked layout modes. Layout locking MUST NOT disable pen/eraser/ink editing. View mode remains non-authoring and therefore MUST NOT create/erase strokes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drawing coordinates MUST remain anchored to the page/canvas coordinate system so strokes do not drift when surrounding Flow blocks are edited. Where ink is attached/anchored to a specific object, that relationship MUST be explicit in the drawing object rather than inferred from screen pixels.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Floating contextual formatting island

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST expose a persistent floating contextual tool island near the top of the content surface while in Edit mode. It is app chrome, not document content. Common authoring/formatting controls MUST be directly reachable from this island rather than requiring the block insertion (+) menu.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The island adapts to the active block/object/selection. For text it exposes the applicable style/heading, emphasis, text/paragraph formatting and related controls; for tables, images, drawings and graphs it exposes the relevant object-specific controls. Multi-selection exposes only actions valid for the current common selection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When no editable object is selected, the island MAY show page-level/default insertion/layout controls. The + menu remains an insertion/discovery surface; it MUST NOT be the sole location for routine formatting of the currently selected content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: In drawing mode the island MUST expose the active Rnote-derived pen/eraser/ink controls. In View mode authoring controls are removed or replaced by view-safe controls while the Edit/View switch remains reachable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI bar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST implement the global persistent bottom AI bar. Its semantic context MUST include the active Board, active Page, selected block/object IDs, Edit/View state, LayoutMode and the user-authorised Board/Den context relevant to the request.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI mutations MUST use 9to1.Boards.* or the owning embedded artifact APIs. Proprietary AppFlowy AI actions MUST NOT be invoked or emulated through hidden donor services. Dulche is the AI runtime and Home remains the shared permission/context broker.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Block system and AppFlowy block parity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST include every non-proprietary-AI AppFlowy block type available in the selected legally usable donor revision, with its applicable editing behaviour and quality-of-life interactions, unless the donor-parity manifest records a concrete exception. The implementation MUST NOT maintain a manually shortened hard-coded parity list that silently falls behind the selected donor source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards additionally MUST support built-in Heading 4, Heading 5 and Heading 6 block/text styles, in addition to the donor-compatible heading levels, and MUST support user-defined named header and paragraph styles. Custom styles MUST be stored as versioned style definitions referenced by stable StyleID so renaming a style does not detach existing blocks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A custom text style definition MUST be capable of specifying the applicable shared text properties including font family/reference, size, weight, emphasis, foreground/background/highlight, paragraph spacing, line spacing, alignment and other supported shared-engine text attributes. Unsupported properties MUST be preserved during cross-app round-tripping.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: New shared object/block types registered in Home’s Shared Productivity Engine MUST become available to Boards through the common registry whenever Boards declares support for that type. Boards-specific wrappers MAY supply page/layout controls, but duplicate object engines are non-conformant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Graph block

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST provide a shared-engine Graph block for mathematical/analytical graphing. A Graph block MUST support multiple simultaneous expressions/series, independently styled plots, points/markers, labelled axes, configurable viewport/domain/range and shaded regions/inequalities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: GraphBlock data MUST include stable GraphID, ordered plot/expression definitions, variables, optional slider definitions, viewport/axes settings and style metadata. Multiple expressions MUST coexist in one graph without being flattened into a rendered image.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A slider definition MUST include VariableID/name, minimum, maximum, step and default value. In Edit mode the author configures slider bounds/defaults. In View mode viewers MAY manipulate enabled sliders; temporary slider values are per-view session unless explicitly saved as new defaults by an authorised Edit action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph blocks MUST support shared-engine copy/paste and remain editable after transfer to another participating surface that declares Graph support. Exporting to static image is a separate explicit operation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Enhanced image formatting

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Image objects in Boards MUST support, at minimum, resize with aspect-ratio control, crop, rotate, fit/fill behaviour, alignment/positioning, caption, alt text/accessibility description and link/reference metadata. Non-destructive image transforms MUST preserve the source asset until the user explicitly exports/rasterises a transformed copy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Enhanced table formatting

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Table objects MUST support add/remove/reorder rows and columns, row/column resize, merge/split where structurally valid, horizontal/vertical cell alignment, text formatting, cell background/fill, borders, header row/column styling and table width/alignment controls. Formatting MUST remain separate from the cell data/value payload so copy/paste and automation can manipulate either deterministically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Cross-app parity blocks

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST expose shared-engine blocks/objects that have equivalents in the other productivity surfaces instead of creating incompatible lookalikes. Required cross-app object families include rich text, tables, code, equations, images/media, ink/drawings and Graph. Additional shared-engine object types become eligible through the common registry.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: App-specific artifacts MAY be embedded as canonical artifact references. An embedded mutable artifact MUST retain its owning app identity/capabilities and MUST NOT be flattened to a screenshot/static copy except through an explicit static export action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Write and Canvas page types

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Add Page MUST offer Write and Canvas as first-class PageType options alongside Native. Creating a Write page creates/attaches the canonical Write document model inside that Board page and presents Write editing behaviour within the Boards shell. Creating a Canvas page does the equivalent for Canvas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write/Canvas Board pages MUST use the same Home Shared Productivity Engine and underlying artifact behaviour as the standalone apps, not a visually similar Boards reimplementation. The Board page is a container/reference to the canonical artifact; edits made inside Boards and edits made through the standalone owning app or Spaces MUST resolve to the same artifact/revision history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening a Write/Canvas page inside Boards MUST NOT launch a second external app window merely to obtain basic editing behaviour. Shared engine capabilities are hosted through Home and rendered in the Boards page surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Chat page type

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Chat is a first-class Board PageType backed by a persistent 9-1 Agent executed through Dulche. The Agent automatically receives permission-filtered semantic knowledge of the containing Board and its authorised pages/items. It MAY also use the user’s connected apps/integrations and relevant persistent context registered in Dulche Den when the Agent/tool permissions permit those actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Chat MUST use typed 9to1 app/integration actions for consequential work. Board membership or Chat context MUST NOT grant implicit access to an external app, tool or Den namespace that the caller/Agent is not otherwise authorised to use.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Chat page stores a stable AgentID/definition revision plus ChatSession/Conversation references independently from the visual page title. Renaming/moving the page MUST NOT create a new Agent or lose history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Scoped Chat page type

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scoped Chat is a closed-corpus notebook-style Chat PageType. Its answers MUST be grounded only in the authorised contents of the containing Board plus the explicit source collection attached to that Scoped Chat. It MUST NOT search the public web, invoke external-information retrieval tools or consult unrelated connected-app content to fill evidence gaps.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When the permitted corpus does not contain enough information to support an answer, Scoped Chat MUST report that the available sources do not support the requested point rather than silently answering from general model knowledge. Transformation/reasoning over supplied material remains allowed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scoped Chat responses MUST expose source provenance at the Board page/source-object level so the user can navigate back to the material supporting the response.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Chat source subpages

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Chat and Scoped Chat MUST support additional source subpages beneath the Chat page. Uploaded source files become stable Source entities with SourceID, display name, source type, content/artifact reference, ingestion/index status, hash/revision metadata and permission state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Source ingestion MUST be asynchronous/observable for large files and MUST distinguish Pending, Ready, Failed and Removed states. Failed ingestion MUST NOT make the source appear successfully available to the Agent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For ordinary Chat, uploaded sources supplement Board/authorised connected context. For Scoped Chat, the Board plus explicit source collection defines the maximum information corpus. Removing/revoking a source prevents future reads while preserving audit/history semantics required by Dulche Den.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Data-backed structured items

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards does not create a second private database engine. Where the AppFlowy donor exposes database-like blocks, records or views, Boards MUST implement the applicable user-facing behaviour by hosting or referencing canonical 9to1 Data artifacts/views through the Shared Productivity Engine and typed Data APIs. A Board item may therefore display and interact with a Data table/range/view while the underlying rows, fields, formulas, permissions and revisions remain owned by Data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Donor parity still applies to the Boards-facing workflow: applicable filtering, sorting, grouping, view selection, record presentation and related quality-of-life behaviour MUST either map to supported Data capabilities or be recorded as a concrete donor-parity exception. Boards MUST NOT silently fork Data state into an incompatible local database merely to imitate donor UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Board document-space coordinates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persisted Native-page spatial placement MUST use Board document-space coordinates, not CUI's -1000…1000 proportional screen coordinate system. The page content origin is (0,0); X increases to the right and Y increases downward. X, Y, Width and Height MAY be decimal document-space values and MAY extend outside the initial viewport where the page supports panning/free placement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Zoom, DPI scaling, window resizing and panning are view transforms only and MUST NOT rewrite persisted Board coordinates. Absolute blocks and free ink use the same stable document-space basis where applicable so objects/strokes do not drift relative to each other. Conversion into CUI/layout coordinates occurs only at render/input boundaries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Embedded artifact ownership and lifecycle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every mutable embedded/hosted app artifact MUST carry explicit ownership semantics independent from its BoardPage reference. At minimum, Boards distinguishes BoardOwned artifacts created as part of that Board page from Referenced artifacts that are independently owned elsewhere. Attaching an existing Write/Canvas/Data/etc. artifact creates a reference and MUST NOT transfer ownership merely because it appears inside Boards.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deleting or recovering a page follows the referenced artifact's ownership contract. Recoverable deletion of a BoardOwned artifact remains recoverable with its owning page/Board. Permanent purge MAY cascade to BoardOwned artifacts only through an explicit destructive operation whose impact preview names the affected artifacts. Referenced artifacts MUST NOT be deleted by deleting the Board/page. Move, rename, nesting and Board switching never change artifact identity or ownership.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Collaboration and concurrency

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards collaboration MUST resolve concurrent work at the narrowest stable entity possible. Independent block/object edits and independent ink strokes SHOULD merge without forcing a whole-page conflict. Page-tree operations MUST use deterministic stable ordering/parent semantics so simultaneous moves/inserts do not silently reorder unrelated pages.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Concurrent incompatible edits to the same canonical block/object/artifact MUST surface the owning object's merge/conflict behaviour rather than blind last-write-wins. Presence, remote cursors, selections and transient viewport state are ephemeral collaboration state and MUST NOT be written into canonical Board content. Reconnect/offline replay MUST preserve operation identity so retries cannot duplicate mutations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST ship useful supported native behaviour on Windows and 9to1-OS and a useful web version under the global web-product contract. All clients operate on the same Board/Page/artifact identities and canonical revisions. Platform capability differences MUST be explicit and queryable rather than silently dropping features.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browser/native differences may include pen pressure/tilt, OS file drag-and-drop, clipboard richness, filesystem access, windowing and availability of specialised embedded surfaces. When a capability is unavailable, Boards MUST provide the closest useful supported interaction or a clear unsupported-capability state without corrupting or flattening the underlying artifact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Performance and resource behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large Boards MUST use incremental/lazy loading and virtualisation. Opening a Board MUST NOT eagerly instantiate every nested page, every off-screen block, every source document or every embedded app surface. Large block lists, Data-backed views and page trees SHOULD virtualise off-screen content while preserving correct selection, search, keyboard navigation and accessibility semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drawing rendering MUST cull/incrementally render off-screen strokes; previews and embedded-surface caches MUST be bounded and revision-invalidated; Board/search/source indexing MUST update incrementally; and expensive embedded artifacts SHOULD hydrate on demand. Performance acceptance MUST include representative large-Board, large-page, drawing-heavy and collaboration scenarios on the declared supported-platform baseline.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Persistence, history and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Board/page/block edits MUST use revisioned, crash-safe persistence through the owning storage layer. A process/app crash MUST NOT corrupt the entire Board because one page/block write was interrupted. Recovery MUST identify the affected Board/Page and restore the latest consistent revision or surface a structured conflict/recovery state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Delete semantics for Boards and Pages MUST be recoverable by default unless an explicit permanent-delete/purge action is invoked under the applicable high-risk permission flow. Deleting a Board container MUST NOT silently permanently delete separately owned embedded artifacts without explicit cascade semantics and user-visible impact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Concurrent edits MUST use revision/conflict semantics rather than blind last-write-wins when the same canonical object is changed by multiple clients/Spaces/Automations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Boards API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.ListBoards();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.GetBoard(boardID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.CreateBoard(config);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.UpdateBoard(boardID, patch);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.DeleteBoard(boardID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.RestoreBoard(boardID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.SetActiveBoard(boardID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.ListPages(boardID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.GetPage(pageID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Boards.CreatePage(boardID, pageType, parentPageID?, position?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
