NORMAL_TEXT
text: These are minimum canonical entry points, not the exhaustive catalogue. Every additional user-visible Boards operation — including donor-parity actions and contextual-island controls — MUST have an equivalent supported API/domain action under the global API-parity rule. APIs MUST use stable IDs, revision checks where required and structured partial/error results.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Permissions and risk

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Read, edit, share/admin, external-action and destructive permissions MUST remain distinct. View mode does not grant edit permission, and Edit mode cannot override an account/object ACL. Chat/AI/tool actions inherit the effective caller/Agent permissions and the global Home permission broker.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permanent Board/Page purge, destructive bulk actions, permission/share changes and consequential external actions initiated from Chat/AI MUST use the elevated-risk approval rules defined globally. Ordinary text/block edits use normal edit scope but remain audited where performed by automation/AI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST return structured failures for BoardNotFound, PageNotFound, BlockNotFound, UnsupportedPageType, UnsupportedBlockType, InvalidLayoutTransition, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied, SourceIngestionFailed, ScopedChatExternalAccessDenied, DependencyUnavailable and SharedEngineIncompatible, plus the global error contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If Home or the Shared Productivity Engine becomes unavailable after Boards has opened, Boards MUST stop new unsafe mutations, preserve already loaded unsaved state for recovery where possible and surface a repair/reconnect state. It MUST NOT silently switch to an incompatible private document engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The landing page, Board switcher and nested page sidebar operate on persisted Boards/Pages and survive restart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Applicable AppFlowy donor features/block types are accounted for by the donor-parity manifest and tested against the selected donor revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native pages render on a seamless background with no page-card/sheet frame.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Locked mode preserves AppFlowy-style flow behaviour; Unlocked mode supports arbitrary block placement; relocking preserves absolute coordinates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rnote-derived drawing works in both Locked and Unlocked layout modes and survives save/restart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The floating top contextual island adapts across text, image, table, drawing and graph selections.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Edit/View switching blocks authoring in View while graph sliders remain usable as non-persistent interactions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: H1-H6 and named custom header/paragraph styles persist and round-trip.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph blocks render multiple simultaneous plots, shaded regions and interactive slider variables without flattening.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Enhanced image/table formatting persists and remains script/API-addressable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A shared object copied Boards → Write/Present/Canvas/Spaces and back retains equivalent shared schema/formatting.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write and Canvas PageTypes edit the same canonical artifact behaviour as their standalone surfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Chat can reason over Board context and use only authorised Den/app capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scoped Chat cannot search/use external information and reports insufficient source evidence when its Board/source corpus does not support an answer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Uploaded Chat source subpages expose correct ingestion state and become/revoke usable context deterministically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI bar mutations use typed actions and cannot mutate Board content in View mode without authorised Edit semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crash/restart and revision-conflict tests preserve Board/Page integrity without silent last-write-wins data loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AppFlowy database-like Board items use canonical Data-backed state rather than a second Boards-only database engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Absolute blocks and ink retain stable Board document-space coordinates across zoom, pan, DPI/window changes and restart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: BoardOwned versus Referenced embedded-artifact deletion/recovery semantics are enforced without accidental cascade deletion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Concurrent independent block/ink/page operations merge deterministically while same-object conflicts never fall back to silent last-write-wins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web clients capability-negotiate declared differences while preserving the same canonical Board/Page/artifact identities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative large Boards/pages/Data views/drawing workloads remain responsive through lazy loading, virtualisation, incremental rendering/indexing and bounded caches.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Boards refuses normal launch and enters the required Install Home bootstrap flow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Planner

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and boundary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Planner is the CUI calendar, schedule, countdown and assignment-planning app. It answers when something happens, when something is due, what the user needs to do, and which canonical 9to1 entities are connected to that plan. Planner is not Home Events, which is an ecosystem activity/history timeline; it is not Spaces Tasks, which represent goal-oriented agentic work/runs; and it is not Automations, which own recurring/event/condition-triggered execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner MUST expose local/native planning and provider-backed calendar/task data through one coherent typed model without duplicating canonical external or 9to1 entities. References to routes, Mail, Files, Write, Present, Boards, Canvas, Data, Spaces, Automations and other supported entities retain the owning entity's stable identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Donor and upstream contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner is a first-party CUI surface. No external application donor is currently normative for Planner. Implementers MUST NOT silently choose a donor and allow donor-specific storage or behaviour to become public Planner authority. Mature calendar standards, provider APIs and the shared 9to1 frameworks MAY be used as implementation references where they do not contradict this specification.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Primary views and navigation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner MUST provide Today, Day, Week, Month, Agenda and Tasks views. The main calendar views use conventional direct manipulation: selecting a time range can create an item, timed items can be moved/resized where permitted, all-day items have a dedicated region, overlapping items remain legible, the current-time indicator is visible where relevant, and keyboard navigation can move through dates/items without requiring pointer input.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The sidebar MUST expose the user's calendars/task lists plus three optional modules — Schedule, Countdown and Assignments. Each optional module can be enabled, hidden and reordered by the user. Hiding a module removes its navigation surface only; it MUST NOT delete its data.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Agenda

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agenda is Planner's chronological list of upcoming planning items rather than a time-grid view. It MUST group and order upcoming events and other relevant due/scheduled Planner entities by date/time while preserving each item's canonical identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agenda SHOULD surface at least events, scheduled PlannerTasks and Assignment deadlines. It MAY surface other Planner milestones such as selected Countdowns when the user has enabled that integration. Filters can narrow the list by calendar/list, completion/status, category and other applicable typed fields.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical entity model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner's canonical entity families are:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Calendar — organisation/source container for events, with stable CalendarID, display metadata, ownership/provider binding, capability state and revision metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PlannerEvent — a time-bounded or all-day event with stable EventID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PlannerTask — a personal planning/to-do item with stable PlannerTaskID; this is distinct from Spaces/Dulche TaskID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reminder — a notification rule/state attached to an Event, PlannerTask, Assignment, Countdown or other supported Planner entity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: RecurrenceDefinition and recurrence exceptions — a versioned repeating-series contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schedule and ScheduleItem — optional structured day-plan entities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Countdown — optional user-defined target-date/time entity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assignment and AssignmentItem — optional structured deadline/work-completion entities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Display names, sidebar order and current view state are not identities. Stable IDs survive rename, move, reorder, view changes and provider resynchronisation where the provider preserves identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: PlannerEvent

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PlannerEvent MUST contain at least EventID, CalendarID, Title, Description?, Start/End or all-day date span, TimeZone semantics, Location?, Recurrence?, References[], Reminders[], Status, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, owner/scope, source/provider metadata and revision. Provider-backed events additionally retain the provider's stable event identity/version token where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An Event may reference a meeting, Maps route, Files/Write/Present/Board/Canvas/Data artifact, Mail thread/message, Space, Automation output or other registered 9to1 entity. Referencing an entity MUST NOT duplicate its canonical payload.

heading: HEADING_3
text: PlannerTask

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PlannerTask MUST contain at least PlannerTaskID, Title, Description?, Status, TaskListID?, DueAt/date?, ScheduledStart?, ScheduledEnd?, Recurrence?, Priority?, References[], Reminders[], CreatedAt, ModifiedAt, owner/scope and revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A PlannerTask can be due without being scheduled. Scheduling a PlannerTask onto the calendar assigns ScheduledStart/ScheduledEnd to the same PlannerTaskID; Planner MUST NOT manufacture a duplicate Event merely to render the task in a time-grid.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dragging an unscheduled task onto a calendar schedules it. Removing it from the time-grid may clear the scheduled window without deleting the task or its due date. Completing/reopening the task preserves its identity/history.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Time zones, all-day values and daylight saving

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Timed Event/Task values MUST use real timezone-aware semantics. Planner distinguishes the authoritative event timezone, absolute instant(s), viewer timezone and an explicitly supported floating/local-time representation. A user travelling or changing device timezone MUST NOT silently change the intended meaning of the event.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All-day items are date-based and MUST NOT drift onto an adjacent date through UTC conversion. Recurrence across daylight-saving transitions uses timezone database rules rather than fixed UTC offsets.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recurrence and occurrence identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recurring Events, PlannerTasks, Assignments and Countdowns MUST use a recurrence definition rather than pre-creating an unbounded list of copies. Supported recurrence semantics include the normal daily/weekly/monthly/yearly interval patterns, selected weekdays, end date and occurrence count where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each expanded occurrence has stable occurrence identity derived from its series plus occurrence key/date-time. Editing a repeating item MUST support the applicable scopes This occurrence, This and following, and Entire series. A modified/skipped occurrence is stored as an exception; modifying one occurrence MUST NOT flatten the entire series into unrelated records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The runtime expands only the requested/visible/query interval plus bounded prefetch. Infinite recurrence MUST never be materialised eagerly.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Reminders and Home notifications

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner reminder delivery uses Home's shared notification service rather than a private Planner notification runtime. An entity MAY own multiple reminder rules such as at start, relative minutes/hours/days before, or a custom trigger supported by the reminder contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reminder runtime state distinguishes at least Scheduled, Fired, Snoozed and Dismissed. Snoozing a reminder changes reminder state/next notification time and MUST NOT rewrite the Event/Task/Assignment's actual start or due time. Recurring-series reminders are evaluated per occurrence.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Optional sidebar module: Schedule

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schedule lets the user break a day or other bounded period into ordered timed ScheduleItems and inspect live progress through the current item/day. Example uses include a college day split into individual lessons, breaks and study periods.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schedule MUST show, at minimum, current item start/end, elapsed time, remaining time, percentage elapsed and percentage remaining. These values update live from the clock without manual Refresh(). It MAY additionally show an item's share of the containing schedule, but that percentage must be labelled distinctly from time-progress percentage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schedule contains stable ScheduleID, Name, timezone/applicability/recurrence settings and ordered ScheduleItemIDs. ScheduleItem contains stable ScheduleItemID, title, start/end, optional colour/icon/location, References[] and optional links to EventID, PlannerTaskID or AssignmentID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schedules MAY be reusable/recurring and support date-specific exceptions without destroying the base pattern. Clicking a ScheduleItem opens details such as elapsed/remaining progress, previous/next item and its linked Planner entities/artifacts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a ScheduleItem references an Event, PlannerTask or Assignment, the reference remains canonical; changing the referenced entity does not create a divergent duplicate Schedule item payload except for Schedule-owned presentation fields.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Optional sidebar module: Countdown

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Countdown is a dashboard of user-defined future targets such as birthdays, holidays, prom, deadlines or other milestones. Countdown entries have stable CountdownID, Name, TargetDate/TargetDateTime, timezone/all-day semantics, icon/image/category metadata where used, recurrence?, References[] and optional linked EventID/AssignmentID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Countdown can be standalone or linked to another canonical Planner entity. When linked, the linked entity's date/time is authoritative so moving that Event/Assignment automatically updates the Countdown rather than leaving two conflicting dates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The dashboard MAY vary displayed precision by proximity, for example days when far away and hours/minutes/seconds when close, while preserving the same target. All-day Countdowns are date-based. Recurring Countdowns such as annual birthdays/holidays resolve the next occurrence deterministically.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Optional sidebar module: Assignments

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assignment represents structured homework, coursework, project/team work, revision deliverables or similar deadline-based work that needs richer completion tracking than a simple PlannerTask. Assignment has stable AssignmentID, Title, Description?, Status, StartDate?, DueAt/date?, CompletedAt?, Priority?, Category/Course/Project metadata?, owner/scope, Assignees/RelevantPeople, RequiredItems[], OptionalItems[], References[], Reminders[], AutomationRefs[] and revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AssignmentItem has stable AssignmentItemID, AssignmentID, parent/nesting relationship?, title/description, Required/Optional classification, completion/progress state, optional weight, optional assignee and revision. Required and optional items remain distinguishable in UI, API, Automations and completion rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Assignment progress and completion

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assignments MUST support partial completion rather than only Done/Not Done. Required statuses include at least Not Started, In Progress, Completed and Cancelled; overdue is derived from the due date versus completion state and MUST be queryable even if represented visually as a status badge.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Progress MAY be automatically calculated from required items, manually set for work that cannot be represented as a checklist, or calculated using explicit item weights. Equal weighting is the default only when no weights are supplied. Optional items do not prevent formal completion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: By default, an Assignment cannot be marked Completed while required items remain incomplete. A user may explicitly override that rule where permitted, with a visible warning/impact confirmation. Automation/API calls must make an equivalent override explicit rather than silently bypassing required items.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assignment views MUST include useful states such as Due soon, Overdue, In progress, Completed and All, with filters/grouping such as due date, course/project/team, priority and assignee where data exists.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Team assignments

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assignments MAY have an owner, assignees/contributors and item-level assignees. Being named as an assignee or relevant person does not itself grant edit permission; normal sharing/ACL state remains authoritative.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assignment-level completion can aggregate item work across people while preserving who completed/changed each item where audit/history is available.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Assignment Automations and extension workflows

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner exposes Assignment events/state to Automations, but Planner itself MUST NOT secretly send external communications as a built-in overdue side effect. A user may create an Automation such as: when an Assignment becomes overdue and is incomplete, draft or send a Mail extension request to the relevant person.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The workflow boundary is strict: Planner owns Assignment state; Automations owns trigger/condition execution; Mail owns sending. Automatic external sending requires the applicable authorised Mail permission/trust grant and remains subject to the global external-side-effect/risk model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Useful Assignment event families include AssignmentCreated, AssignmentUpdated, AssignmentProgressChanged, AssignmentDueSoon, AssignmentOverdue, AssignmentCompleted, AssignmentReopened and item-completion events. Automations can query DueAt, Status, Progress, RequiredItems, OptionalItems, assignees and references through typed Planner APIs.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Cross-app typed references

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner references MUST use the owning app's canonical stable IDs and permissions. A referenced artifact may render a preview/embedded surface only through the owning app's declared reference/embed contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a referenced entity is unavailable, revoked or deleted, the Planner item remains valid and surfaces the reference as unavailable/broken; Planner MUST NOT delete the Event/Task/Assignment simply because one attachment/reference disappeared.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Maps and travel integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner Events MAY carry both Location and a canonical Maps RouteID. Route ownership remains with Maps. Planner may display current route summary/duration and can offer a departure reminder derived from Event start minus current route duration minus an explicit user buffer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Derived travel reminders MUST NOT rewrite the Event's actual start time. A changed Maps route/duration is reflected from the canonical route rather than a stale Planner copy.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Mail integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mail may create or update Planner items through typed Planner actions while retaining a reference to the source MessageID/ThreadID. AI-extracted date/time/title values that are materially uncertain must be reviewable rather than silently committed as certain facts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner mutations do not mutate the source Mail thread except through a separate authorised Mail action.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Meetings, attendees and external side effects

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Events MAY support attendees, invitations, meeting references/links and RSVP state where the local/provider capability supports them. Provider-backed attendee/invitation operations remain provider-aware.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When saving a change can send invitations, updates or cancellations externally, Planner MUST distinguish local/save-only behaviour from save-and-notify/send behaviour where the provider supports that distinction. Consequential attendee communication uses the normal permission/impact rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: External calendars and provider capability model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner supports 9to1-native calendars and connected provider calendars through External App Integrations. Provider-backed entities remain provider-aware rather than being silently copied into an unrelated local calendar.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider capabilities MUST be explicit and queryable, including relevant support for read/write, recurrence, attendees, free/busy, reminders, meeting links, colours/categories, calendar sharing, task support and push/change feeds. Unsupported operations must be hidden/disabled or return a structured ProviderCapabilityUnsupported error.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connected-provider changes should use incremental change feeds/push where supported. Provider sync state distinguishes pending/synced/conflict/failed where relevant; conflicts MUST NOT be resolved by blind last-write-wins.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Search, filtering and global discovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner search MUST cover Events, PlannerTasks, Assignments, Countdowns and Schedule entities where enabled. Filters MAY include date range, calendar/list, status/completion, category/project/course, assignee/attendee, location and referenced entity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search results preserve stable Planner IDs and open the canonical item. Planner entities that are eligible for Home/global search expose permission-filtered searchable metadata through the shared search/index contract.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Import and export

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner MUST support iCalendar/.ics import and export for representable calendar data. Import preserves timezone/recurrence/attendee semantics when the format/provider can represent them and reports unsupported constructs rather than silently flattening them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Importing data creates/links canonical Planner/provider entities according to the selected destination semantics; it MUST NOT create duplicate copies when a stable imported/provider identity already maps to an existing entity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI bar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner MUST host the global persistent Dulche AI bar. Its semantic context includes selected Event/PlannerTask/Assignment/Countdown/Schedule IDs, selected date/time range, visible calendar interval, active calendars/lists/modules, current timezone, relevant references, revision/sync state and the available typed Planner actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Read-only mode cannot mutate planning state. Write mode uses typed 9to1.Planner actions and the normal Home permission broker. Natural-language changes such as moving a set of tomorrow's events MUST resolve against stable entity/occurrence IDs rather than inferred screen coordinates.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automations integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner recurrence remains Planner state; repeating Events/Tasks MUST NOT be implemented as hidden Automations. Automations consumes Planner's typed events/actions for workflows around those entities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Minimum automatable event families include EventCreated, EventUpdated, EventStarting, EventEnded, PlannerTaskCreated, PlannerTaskDue, PlannerTaskCompleted, ReminderFired and the Assignment event families defined above. For recurring items, event payloads include the concrete occurrence identity as well as the series identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Planner API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner's first-party API catalogue is exhaustive under the global API-parity rule. Minimum canonical entry points include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
