heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every additional user-visible Planner operation — including provider actions, sidebar-module operations, recurrence edits, assignment item manipulation, reminder management and import/export — MUST expose an equivalent supported typed action/query.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistence, sync, history and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner native state is versioned and crash-safe. Calendar/Event/PlannerTask/Assignment/Schedule/Countdown changes use revision-aware mutations; partial failure must not leave a recurrence series or Assignment hierarchy half-updated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal deletion is recoverable where the entity/storage provider supports recovery. Permanent purge is explicit/high-risk. Provider-backed deletion/recovery follows provider capability while preserving local audit/sync state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Offline/reconnect queues MUST preserve operation identity/idempotency. Provider conflicts and concurrent same-entity edits surface deterministic merge/conflict state rather than silently overwriting one revision.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Permissions and risk

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Read, edit, share/admin, provider/external-side-effect and destructive scopes remain distinct. Having a Planner item in view does not grant permission to mutate its referenced artifact, invite attendees, send Mail or operate a connected provider beyond the caller's authorised capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Invitation/cancellation sending, external Mail extension requests, provider sharing changes, permanent purge and destructive bulk changes retain their target action's elevated risk/approval requirements.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner MUST be keyboard-operable across calendar grids, Agenda, task/assignment lists, Schedule and Countdown. Time-grid cells/items expose meaningful accessible date/time labels; current item/progress and overdue state cannot be conveyed by colour alone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Screen readers MUST be able to identify item type, title, date/time/due state, recurrence and applicable progress. Schedule percentages and countdown values require textual equivalents. Reduced motion and scalable text/layout follow the global CUI accessibility contract.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner MUST provide useful supported native behaviour on Windows and 9to1-OS plus a useful web version under the global web contract. All clients operate on the same canonical Planner/provider entities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native clients MAY have richer OS notification/calendar integration; web may depend on browser notification/background constraints. Capability differences are explicit and MUST NOT silently downgrade the canonical planning state or turn the web app into a read-only viewer.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and resource behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Calendar range queries load only the visible/requested interval plus bounded prefetch; recurring-series expansion is interval-bounded. Large Agenda/task/Assignment lists MUST virtualise. Provider change feeds and shared indexes update incrementally rather than repeatedly refetching all calendars/items.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schedule live-progress and Countdown ticking MUST update efficiently without causing full Planner-tree rerenders each second. Background timers should coalesce/update at the precision actually visible to the user.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner MUST return structured failures for EventNotFound, PlannerTaskNotFound, AssignmentNotFound, ScheduleNotFound, CountdownNotFound, InvalidRecurrence, InvalidTimeZone, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied, ProviderCapabilityUnsupported, ProviderSyncConflict, ReferenceUnavailable, ReminderUnavailable and ImportUnsupportedConstruct, plus the global error contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If Home notification/shared services are unavailable, Planner preserves canonical planning state and surfaces notification/reconnect limitations rather than losing Events/Tasks/Assignments. Provider outages preserve queued/retryable state with explicit sync status.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Today, Day, Week, Month, Agenda and Tasks views operate on persisted canonical Planner entities and survive restart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agenda lists upcoming Events/scheduled tasks/Assignment deadlines chronologically without duplicating their underlying identities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scheduling/unscheduling a PlannerTask changes its scheduled window without creating/deleting a duplicate Event.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Timezone, all-day and daylight-saving tests preserve intended event meaning across viewer/device timezone changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recurring series support occurrence/this-and-following/whole-series edits, exceptions and bounded expansion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reminders route through Home notifications and snoozing does not rewrite the item's canonical time.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schedule can be enabled as an optional sidebar module and shows live elapsed/remaining time plus percentage elapsed/remaining for the current item.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Countdown can be enabled as an optional sidebar module, supports standalone and linked targets, and linked targets update without duplicated dates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assignments can be enabled as an optional sidebar module and persist partial progress, required/optional items, nested/weighted items where configured, due state, team assignments and completion rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An overdue Assignment can trigger an authorised Automation that drafts/sends a Mail extension request without Planner bypassing Mail/Automation permission rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps routes, Mail threads and Files/Write/Present/Boards/Canvas/Data/Space/Automation outputs remain canonical typed references when attached to Planner items.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider calendars capability-negotiate recurrence/attendees/reminders/etc. and synchronise without silent last-write-wins conflict loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: iCalendar import/export round-trips representable recurrence/timezone data and reports unsupported constructs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent AI bar reads/writes Planner only through permission-filtered semantic context and typed Planner actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical entity model while surfacing declared capability differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large calendar ranges/lists/recurrences remain responsive through bounded expansion, incremental sync/indexing and virtualisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Planner follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract rather than launching an incompatible private runtime.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Automations

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and execution boundary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Automations is the ecosystem-wide workflow-definition and orchestration app. It owns Automation definitions, triggers, control flow, durable execution state and Run history. It does not reimplement the business logic of target apps: every app/device/provider/third-party action executes through the canonical typed action exposed by its owning capability and retains that capability's permissions, risk classification, result/error schema, idempotency semantics and audit trail.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns the shared Node Graph Framework and permission/trust broker. Automations owns Automation entities and orchestration semantics. Dulche executes AI/model/Agent work. Target 9to1 apps, connected services, third-party apps and devices execute their registered typed actions. Raw mouse/keyboard UI automation is non-conformant where a typed action exists.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Landing page: Home and Library

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Automations landing surface has two primary sections: Home and Library.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home is an operational dashboard. It surfaces recent runs, currently running/waiting workflows, failures/Needs Attention, upcoming scheduled triggers, permission/connection problems, commonly used Automations and concise execution-health information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Library is the canonical list of the user's Automations. It supports search, sort/filter, enabled/disabled state, owner/scope, last run, next trigger when determinable, current active revision, connection/permission health and create/duplicate/share/delete/recover operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home dashboard cards MUST open the canonical Automation or AutomationRun rather than creating separate dashboard state. The landing page SHOULD make Create Automation prominent without forcing a user into an empty graph before they understand what they are creating.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical entities

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automation MUST have stable AutomationID, Name, Description?, Icon?, Owner/Scope, Enabled/OperationalState, GraphID, DraftRevisionID, ActiveRevisionID?, InputSchema?, OutputSchema?, TriggerSummary, RequiredCapabilities, ExecutionPolicy, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AutomationRun MUST have stable RunID, AutomationID, pinned AutomationRevisionID, TriggerID/TriggerEventID, Status, StartedAt, FinishedAt?, typed Inputs, typed Outputs?, NodeExecutionStates, Error?, approval/wait state, causal ancestry and audit/ActionGraph references.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editing, renaming, moving, sharing or changing the landing-page position of an Automation MUST NOT change AutomationID. A Run is historical execution state and MUST remain bound to the exact Automation revision it executed.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Draft and Active revisions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations use the Node Graph Framework's Draft/Active revision model. Editing an active Automation changes a Draft revision. New trigger executions continue using the current Active revision until the user validates and activates/publishes a newer Draft.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An already-running Run remains pinned to its starting revision even if another revision is activated. Activation is atomic. Previous valid Active revisions remain available for inspection and rollback subject to retention policy.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Graph editor and simple creation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The graph is the canonical executable definition. Automations MAY offer simple When / If / Then creation, templates or natural-language creation, but these are graph-authoring views over the same GraphID rather than separate simplified formats. Opening an Automation MUST always allow inspection of the real graph.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The primary advanced editor uses the Home-owned Node Graph Framework with Automations' capability profile, typed ports, pan/zoom, selection, grouping/comments, copy/paste, undo/redo, validation, Draft/Active state and execution overlays.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Node search and connector interaction

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Node creation/search MUST follow an Unreal-style graph interaction pattern. Right-clicking empty graph space opens the node list at that location; the user can immediately type to filter/search registered node types and select a result to create the node at/near the invocation point. Results SHOULD be grouped by meaningful categories while search ranks direct action/event/type matches first.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connector deletion MUST support Ctrl-click directly on a connection/connector to remove it. Right-clicking a connection opens its context menu with Delete Connector as an explicit action. Keyboard-accessible selection plus Delete/Backspace MUST provide an equivalent non-pointer path. Deleting a connector removes only that connection, never either connected node.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search results come from the live registered node catalogue for the current capability profile, target platform/device availability and installed/connected integrations. Automations MUST NOT maintain a stale hard-coded copy of the ecosystem's available actions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Trigger model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Minimum trigger families:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual — explicit user/API invocation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schedule — timezone-aware one-time or repeating schedules such as a specific time, daily/weekly rules or interval schedules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: App Event — typed events published by 9to1 apps.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Condition/Watch — reevaluate a typed predicate when relevant state changes or on an explicitly declared evaluation cadence where event-driven evaluation is unavailable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: External/Connector Event — supported webhooks/provider events/plugin/MCP/connector events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automation invocation — typed call from another Automation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Triggers use typed payloads. Schedule triggers preserve timezone/DST semantics. Event-driven state change MUST be preferred to wasteful polling when an owning capability provides an event/change feed. Trigger delivery MUST have stable identity/deduplication semantics.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Node families

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Automations capability profile MUST include registered node families needed for mature workflow composition, including:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Triggers.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 app Actions and Queries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Device Actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Third-party app/service Actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conditions, Switch/branch and comparisons.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Variables, constants, data access and transforms/conversions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wait/Delay.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For Each/iteration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Parallel/Fan-out and Join.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Approval/Human review.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Retry, On Failure, fallback and error handling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Call Automation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche/Agent/Skill/Plugin/MCP/Connector capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typed Output/Return.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connections are type-checked through the Node Graph Framework. Incompatible ports cannot connect unless a registered explicit conversion/transform exists.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Device-level actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations MUST expose an extensive device-level action catalogue sourced directly from the capabilities actually advertised by the current/selected Home or Mesh device. Device actions are not a small hand-maintained Automations list. When a device/runtime exposes a supported typed action, Automations can surface it subject to OS/device permissions and the Home trust broker.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative device actions include, where the device advertises them:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wi-Fi on/off and supported network-selection/state operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Bluetooth on/off and supported connection/device operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Always On Display on/off plus supported AOD profiles/settings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Lock Screen Clock position, design/style and other supported lock-screen clock properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Display/brightness, sound/volume, notification/DND, power/battery, input, connectivity and other device settings/actions exposed safely by the device capability registry.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every device action node records the required DeviceID/capability/action version or an explicit compatible-device targeting policy. The editor MUST warn when an action is device-specific or not portable and explain that it may not work on another device. Validation on another device MUST report capability mismatch rather than silently substituting a different action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-device execution uses Mesh typed remote capability invocation and therefore passes both caller-side and target-device permission/policy checks. Automations MUST NOT turn device actions into a generic remote-desktop or arbitrary-code-execution channel.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Third-party app and service actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations MUST surface typed third-party app/service actions wherever an installed app, plugin, connector, MCP capability, operating-system integration or registered provider exposes them. Discovery is dynamic and versioned, not a fixed list baked into Automations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Third-party actions carry the originating capability/provider identity, connection/account requirements, input/output schemas, platform/device availability and risk/side-effect classification. Missing/uninstalled apps or expired connections place affected nodes into a clear Needs Attention/capability-unavailable state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example: a Schedule trigger at 16:00 may connect to a registered YouTube/compatible media action that plays a specified video on a selected compatible device. The workflow remains a typed trigger-to-action graph; Automations does not emulate YouTube by screen clicking.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Natural-language graph creation and editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche can create and modify Automations from natural-language requests, but the result MUST be a real editable Node Graph mutation using typed Node Graph APIs. Generated natural-language descriptions are explanatory only and are never the canonical workflow definition.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated graphs MUST validate node/action schemas, connection types, permissions/capabilities and target availability before activation. The editor SHOULD visually highlight nodes/connections added or changed by the most recent AI operation and allow ordinary undo.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Data, variables and nullability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each Run has a typed data environment. Trigger payload fields, node outputs, variables and action inputs can be connected directly where types are compatible. Data transforms use explicit registered nodes/functions rather than implicit lossy conversion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: False, null, unavailable/redacted and error are distinct. Missing data MUST NOT silently become zero, False or an empty string and accidentally take the wrong branch.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Durable Wait and resume

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wait/Delay MUST be durable. A Run that waits for seconds, days, a time/date, device availability, approval or another supported condition persists a continuation record and releases active execution resources. It MUST NOT depend on an application thread/process literally sleeping.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Restart/redeployment must resume a valid waiting Run from persisted state without repeating already-committed side effects. ResumeAt/condition metadata and revision identity are inspectable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Approval nodes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Approval/Human Review is a first-class node. It pauses a Run with WaitingForApproval and presents the intended decision/action to the appropriate authorised user. Approval, rejection, timeout and cancellation are explicit outcomes usable by subsequent graph branches.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An Approval node is distinct from Home's permission broker. Approval expresses workflow-required human review; the broker determines whether the caller is authorised to execute the protected action. Either mechanism may independently block execution.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Permissions, connections and secret handling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each Automation has a stable caller identity bound to AutomationID/workspace identity. Activating a revision MUST show/derive the capabilities and action scopes the active graph requires. Expanding an Automation from a lower-risk action such as Mail.CreateDraft to Mail.Send or adding a new device/provider scope requires normal permission/trust reevaluation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Secrets, tokens and provider credentials MUST NOT be stored as plaintext node properties. Nodes reference Home/connector-managed ConnectionID/secret handles. Sharing a graph does not automatically share the owner's credentials, external account access or trust grants.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Execution location and device targeting

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Execution policy MUST make where the workflow can run explicit. Supported executors may include 9to1 cloud, the current Home/device runtime, a selected compatible Mesh device or a provider-native executor where that provider/action supports it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The UI MUST NOT claim that a device-bound Automation will execute while all required devices are offline. Conversely, a cloud-capable workflow MUST NOT unnecessarily depend on an open desktop UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A device-targetable node may require a specific DeviceID, any compatible paired device or the triggering device according to its declared targeting policy. If no compatible device is available, the Run follows its configured wait/retry/failure policy with an explicit DeviceCapabilityUnavailable/DeviceOffline state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Run lifecycle and operational state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automation definition operational states include at least Draft, Enabled, Disabled and NeedsAttention. AutomationRun states include at least Queued, Running, Waiting, WaitingForApproval, Paused, Completed, Failed and Cancelled.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Disabling an Automation prevents new trigger starts but does not silently delete history. If Runs are already active, the UI must explicitly offer a policy such as allow existing Runs to finish, pause them where safe, or cancel them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home dashboard/Library status MUST be derived from canonical definition/run/connection state, not a separately editable status field.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Run history and execution inspection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Run has a structured execution timeline showing trigger, node start/end, typed input/output summaries, target action, attempt number, duration, waiting/approval state, result/error and causal child-run references. Sensitive values are redacted according to permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The structured Run record is authoritative. Dulche may summarise it in natural language but MUST NOT invent events or hide failed/denied/cancelled nodes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can open a historical Run against the exact pinned graph revision even after the current Automation has changed.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Error handling, retry and idempotency

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An unhandled node failure stops the affected path by default. Authors may explicitly add retry, On Failure, fallback or continue semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Retries of external or destructive actions MUST use the target action's idempotency/OperationID contract where available. If the runtime cannot determine whether a timed-out consequential action committed, it MUST enter a typed uncertain/Needs Attention state rather than blindly repeat an operation that could duplicate its external side effect.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Retry policies are bounded and inspectable; infinite automatic retry loops are prohibited.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Loop and cascade protection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Runs carry TriggerEventID, RunID, ParentRunID? and causal ancestry. The runtime MUST detect repeated event/run cycles, bound recursion/cascade depth and total execution budget, and deduplicate replayed trigger deliveries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If an Automation repeatedly triggers itself or another Automation in a causal loop, the affected cascade is stopped with a diagnostic that identifies the loop rather than continuing to mutate user data indefinitely.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Calling other Automations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Call Automation invokes another Automation by stable AutomationID and declared InputSchema/OutputSchema; it does not copy the target graph into the caller. The callee keeps its own version, permissions and Run history while parent/child Run causality is linked.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Test, validate and run

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The editor MUST distinguish Validate, Test and Run for real.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Validate performs graph/schema/type/capability/permission/connection checks without executing actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Test executes with selected sample/current data and MUST use action preview/dry-run facilities where the target capability provides them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run for real executes the active or explicitly selected validated revision with normal side effects and permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a Test reaches an action that cannot be safely simulated, Automations must identify that limitation and require explicit real-execution confirmation before performing the side effect.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Sharing, teams and run-as identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations MAY be shared within supported personal/team/workspace scopes. Sharing the definition does not transfer credentials, provider connections, device permissions or Always Trust grants.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where shared execution supports multiple identities, run-as semantics MUST be explicit, such as triggering user versus Automation owner/service identity. The runtime MUST NOT silently choose whichever identity has greater authority.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Compatibility and migration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every registered node type/action/event records schema/version identity. If an app/device/provider update retires or incompatibly changes a node schema, the graph enters NeedsAttention/migration state rather than silently dropping the node, retyping a port or changing behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Migration may be automatic only when semantics are provably equivalent; otherwise the editor must show the affected nodes and require review before reactivation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent contextual AI bar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations MUST host the global persistent Dulche AI bar. Its semantic context includes AutomationID, GraphID, Draft/Active revisions, selected NodeIDs/ConnectionIDs, validation state, Run/connection/permission state, registered node catalogue and typed graph mutation actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Read-only mode can explain/debug/inspect. Write mode may modify the graph only through typed Node Graph/Automation APIs. AI MUST NOT simulate graph mouse gestures.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automations API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations' first-party API catalogue is exhaustive under the global API-parity rule. Minimum canonical entry points include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.List(filters?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.Get(automationID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.Create(config);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.Update(automationID, patch);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.Delete(automationID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.Restore(automationID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.Validate(automationID, revision?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.Activate(automationID, revision);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.Disable(automationID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.Run(automationID, inputs?, revision?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.CancelRun(runID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.PauseRun(runID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.ResumeRun(runID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.GetRun(runID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.ListRuns(automationID, filters?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.RetryRun(runID, fromNodeID?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.ListAvailableActions(context?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Automations.ListDeviceActions(deviceID?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph editing remains on 9to1.NodeGraph.* rather than duplicating graph-mutation methods inside Automations. Every additional user-visible Automations operation — Library organisation, connection repair, permission review, execution-policy change, sharing, migration and run controls — requires equivalent typed API coverage.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistence and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automation definitions, Draft/Active revisions, Runs, wait/approval continuations, trigger cursors/deduplication state and connection references are durably versioned. A crash/restart MUST NOT restart the graph from the beginning and duplicate already-committed actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal Automation deletion is recoverable; permanent purge is explicit/high-risk. Run-history retention/purge follows declared policy and audit requirements.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The landing Home/Library, node graph and Run inspector MUST be keyboard-operable and accessible. Node search can be opened without a pointer; nodes, ports and connectors expose semantic labels/types; connection creation/deletion has keyboard equivalents; execution/error states cannot be conveyed by colour alone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph zoom/pan must not be required to discover the textual meaning of a node. A structured accessible node/connection list or equivalent semantic representation MUST be available to assistive technology.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and resource behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large graphs, Libraries and Run histories MUST virtualise where appropriate. Node catalogue search must remain responsive across extensive app/device/third-party action registries and should query/index incrementally rather than blocking on full capability rescans.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Execution is event-driven/durable; idle/waiting Runs must not retain unnecessary UI/execution threads. Run logs/timelines paginate/stream incrementally and caches are bounded.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations MUST return structured failures including AutomationNotFound, RunNotFound, InvalidGraph, ValidationFailed, NodeTypeUnavailable, ConnectionTypeMismatch, CapabilityUnavailable, DeviceCapabilityUnavailable, DeviceOffline, ProviderConnectionUnavailable, PermissionRequired, ApprovalRejected, ApprovalTimedOut, WaitResumeFailed, RevisionConflict, TriggerDuplicate, LoopDetected, ExecutionBudgetExceeded, UnsafeRetryState and MigrationRequired in addition to target-action errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A missing third-party app, disconnected provider or unavailable device never causes the runtime to pretend an action completed; affected definitions/runs surface Needs Attention or the configured wait/failure path.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Landing Home shows canonical operational dashboard state and Library lists persisted user Automations with search/filter/status/last-next-run information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening an Automation exposes its real Node Graph; simple/natural-language creation produces the same canonical graph rather than a hidden alternate workflow format.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Right-click empty graph space opens an Unreal-style searchable node list; typing filters the live registered catalogue; Ctrl-click on a connector deletes it and right-click offers Delete Connector.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Draft and Active revisions remain distinct; activating a new revision does not mutate an already-running Run pinned to an older revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual, Schedule, App Event, Condition/Watch, external/provider and Automation-call triggers deliver typed payloads with deduplication identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A representative extensive device action registry is discovered from real device capabilities, including available Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/AOD/lock-screen-clock actions, and device-specific portability warnings/capability validation are shown.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Third-party app/service actions appear from installed/connected capability registries and missing/unavailable integrations enter a diagnosable Needs Attention state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A schedule at 16:00 can invoke a registered YouTube/compatible media Play action on a compatible target device without UI simulation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Natural-language graph creation/editing produces valid typed Node Graph mutations and remains fully inspectable/undoable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Durable Wait and Approval nodes survive process/device/runtime restart without replaying committed prior actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Retries use idempotency semantics and uncertain external side effects do not blindly repeat.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Self-triggering/cross-Automation loops are detected and stopped with causal diagnostics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Validate, Test and Run-for-real remain distinct and Test does not silently perform unsimulatable external actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared Automations do not inherit another user's credentials/device permissions/trust grants and run-as identity remains explicit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schema/version changes place incompatible graphs into migration/Needs Attention rather than silently altering behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent AI bar inspects/edits graphs only through semantic context and typed APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large node catalogues/graphs/run histories remain responsive through indexing, virtualisation and incremental loading.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Automations follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract rather than launching an incompatible private permission/runtime stack.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Creativity Apps

heading: HEADING_2
text: Picture

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and editing-first boundary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Picture is the native CUI image creation, editing and composition app for raster, vector and hybrid visual work. Its primary purpose is powerful creation/editing, not passive image viewing. Picture MUST support professional-grade manual editing, simple object-first workflows, non-destructive composition, AI-assisted editing, generative image creation, sketch-to-image conversion and advanced vector tooling while remaining approachable to users who do not want to manage low-level layer structure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browsing/viewing/library workflows remain supported but are secondary to Create, Edit and Generate. Core crop/transform/colour/vector/text/drawing/export workflows MUST remain fully usable when AI is disabled, unavailable or disallowed.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shared-engine reuse and fast feature parity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST reuse the mature shared engines already used by Write, Present, Canvas and Boards whenever capability overlaps. It MUST NOT create Picture-private duplicates of shared drawing, text, shape, selection, transform, clipboard, accessibility, undo/history or embedded-object semantics merely for implementation convenience.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required reuse includes at minimum:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Home-owned Shared Productivity Engine for shared text, shapes, media/object identity, selection, transform, clipboard/transfer, accessibility and typed object actions where those semantics apply.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Rnote-derived shared drawing/ink engine already used by Canvas and Boards for pens, strokes, pressure/tilt, eraser behaviour, stroke serialisation and drawing selection/manipulation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared shape/vector primitives, transform handles, snapping/alignment and object manipulation behaviours already exercised by Present/Canvas/Boards where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared rich-text/typography primitives from Write/Present for editable text objects rather than a second incompatible text engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared Files identity/storage, CUI runtime, Home permission/trust, persistent AI bar, revision/action conventions and cross-app artifact references.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where Picture needs a capability that logically belongs in one of these shared engines, the implementation SHOULD extend that shared engine centrally and enable the new capability for other eligible apps rather than fork it inside Picture. This reuse is a release requirement intended to accelerate feature parity and keep behaviour identical across the ecosystem.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical Picture document model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST use a versioned editable PictureDocument rather than treating the current rendered bitmap as the sole source of truth. A document has stable DocumentID, optional backing FileID/source revision, canvas/artboard geometry, colour profile, background, canonical ElementGraph/LayerGraph, linked assets, edit history/revisions, metadata and document revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DocumentType supports Raster, Vector and Hybrid. Hybrid documents can contain raster content, editable vector paths/shapes, text, generated objects, masks, drawing/ink, adjustments and linked assets in one document without destructive flattening.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every independently editable object has stable ElementID plus ElementType, parent/group identity, bounds/transform, visibility, lock state, blend/compositing properties where applicable, mask/effect references, metadata and revision. Renaming/reordering does not change identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automatic composition mode and manual layers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture uses automatic composition/layer management by default. Typical users can select, move, erase, resize, generate, recolour or annotate objects without manually constructing a Photoshop-style layer stack. Picture automatically creates/updates the internal objects, masks, adjustment state and generated fills required to keep the edit non-destructive.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual Layer mode is an optional advanced view over the SAME canonical document model. It exposes explicit layers/groups, masks/clipping, order, visibility, locks, opacity, blend modes, adjustment/effect layers and names. Switching between automatic and manual views MUST NOT flatten or convert the document.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automatic mode may group implementation details into understandable objects such as Subject, Background, Text or Generated Object while preserving the full internal structure for advanced inspection/editing.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Layer and composition semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical layer/composition graph MUST support at minimum RasterImage, VectorShape, VectorPath, Text, Drawing/Ink, GeneratedObject, Adjustment, Fill, Mask, Group, Artboard/Canvas, Background and Linked/Smart Asset element families.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Layer/object order determines compositing order. Groups preserve child identity. Masks remain independently editable. Adjustment/effect nodes SHOULD remain non-destructive and apply to explicit target scope rather than permanently rewriting source pixels.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A user can rasterise/flatten selected content explicitly, but Picture MUST NOT silently flatten editable content merely because a tool is easier to implement that way.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Selection and semantic object extraction

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST provide a mature selection system including rectangle, ellipse, lasso, polygonal/freehand lasso, brush/refine, colour/range selection and smart/semantic selection where AI/vision capability exists. Selection operations include add, subtract, intersect, invert, feather, expand/contract and edge refinement where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Semantic/object selection can identify a subject/object/background and convert the result into an independently editable Picture element/mask. The user can also circle or roughly mark a subject and ask Picture to infer the intended object boundary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selection state is not itself document identity unless explicitly saved as a mask/object, but saved masks/selections receive stable IDs and participate in history/revisions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Object-first editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A selected object/subject MUST support direct Move, Resize, Rotate, Duplicate, Delete/Erase, Replace, Isolate, Recolour/Restyle and front/back ordering actions where compatible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When an object is moved, resized away from its previous occupied area or erased, Picture can use generative/background reconstruction to fill exposed gaps. The original underlying elements MUST remain revision-addressable so the edit can be undone/reverted or regenerated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example: circling a person and dragging them left creates/updates an editable subject object, relocates that subject, reconstructs the exposed background, and preserves both the subject and generated repair as editable/revisioned state rather than destructively baking the result.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Raster editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core raster editing MUST include at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crop, rotate, flip, straighten, resize/resample, canvas resize and perspective correction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Free transform, warp/distort and perspective transform where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Exposure, brightness, contrast, highlights, shadows, whites/blacks, gamma/levels and curves.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Temperature, tint, saturation, vibrance, hue and channel/colour adjustments.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sharpen, clarity/detail, denoise, blur and other declared filters/effects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clone/heal/repair, redaction/blur/pixelate and local adjustment tools.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background removal/extraction and alpha/transparency-aware editing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Raster operations SHOULD be represented as non-destructive adjustments/masks/transform state where technically practical. An operation that must bake pixels MUST create a revision boundary with reversible history.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Vector creation and editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST provide powerful vector creation/editing suitable for serious illustration, asset and graphic-design work, with depth comparable to mature Photoshop-class vector/path tooling while keeping common actions simple.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required vector capabilities include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rectangle/ellipse/polygon/star/line/arrow and shared shape primitives.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pen/path tool, anchor-point editing, Bézier handles, open/closed paths and path segment manipulation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Fill, stroke, stroke width/alignment, opacity and gradient/pattern support where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boolean path operations: union/add, subtract, intersect and exclude/XOR.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Group/ungroup, align, distribute, snap, transform, duplicate and precise positioning.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Masks/clipping paths and vector effects where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text-on-path and convert-text-to-path where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rasterise vector selection and supported raster/vector tracing or conversion workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vector objects remain vector-editable until explicitly rasterised/flattened. Raster and vector elements can coexist in the same Hybrid PictureDocument.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Text objects

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text is a first-class editable object using shared Write/Present typography primitives where applicable. Picture text tools MUST support font family/style/size, colour/fill/stroke, line height, alignment, tracking/kerning where supported, transform/rotation, text box/area text, point text and appropriate effects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Advanced vector-text behaviours such as text on path and convert to path SHOULD reuse the vector engine. Text must remain editable as text until the user explicitly converts/rasterises it.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Drawing and painting

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST reuse the shared Rnote-derived drawing engine for sketching, painting/markup and mask/selection brush workflows rather than implementing a separate stroke format. Supported drawing behaviours inherit Canvas/Boards pen, pressure/tilt, eraser, stroke selection/manipulation and custom pen/preset capability where relevant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture may expose a simplified context-specific toolbar, but underlying stroke behaviour/serialisation remains shared. Sketch strokes can be retained as editable Drawing elements, used as masks/annotations, or supplied to AI generation as structural guidance.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI editing and generative operations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI editing is a first-class core Picture capability rather than an optional afterthought. Picture MUST support typed, revisioned AI operations including object removal, object replacement, generative fill, generative erase, generative expand/outpainting, background remove/replace, object move/resize with scene reconstruction, style/appearance change, image restoration/enhancement, upscaling, relighting/recolour assistance and prompt-based region/full-image editing where the configured model/tool supports them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI operations MUST target explicit DocumentID/ElementID/SelectionID/MaskID/revision context rather than inferred screen coordinates. Results become canonical editable Picture state or explicit generated variants; they MUST NOT silently overwrite the only source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a selected region is moved or deleted, generated background repair is scoped to the exposed/selected region and recorded separately enough to permit undo, regenerate or variant comparison.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Generative image creation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST create new images from text prompts, sketches, reference images, mixed prompt+reference+sketch inputs and supported style/composition guidance. Generation controls include at least output size/aspect ratio, background/transparency intent where supported, reference inputs, style guidance and variant count/options exposed by the selected model/tool.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated results become normal Picture documents/assets that can immediately be edited with raster/vector/text/drawing tools. Generation history and input provenance remain associated with the created revision/variant.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Sketch-to-image

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sketch-to-image is a dedicated workflow. Users can draw a rough composition/shape layout with the shared drawing engine, optionally annotate regions with text or references, and generate a detailed image while retaining the original sketch and generation relationship.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sketch-to-image MUST support iterative workflows such as sketch -> generate -> edit -> select region -> regenerate/refine. The user may preserve the sketch as an editable overlay/reference rather than losing it after generation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Generative region editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The user can define a region by smart selection, lasso, brush/mask, shape or current object and invoke typed actions such as Remove, Replace, Move, Resize, Recolour, Restyle, Extend or Generate In Region.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Remove reconstructs the missing area; Replace creates replacement content constrained to the selected region/context; Move/Resize preserve the selected subject while repairing exposed background; Extend generates outside current content/canvas bounds. Generated output is revisioned and attributable to the operation/input scope.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI-assisted composition

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MAY support high-level composition instructions such as rebalance composition, reposition subject, change background, restyle a poster, convert a rough concept to a polished visual or convert a sketch to a clean vector-like design. These MUST resolve to inspectable canonical Picture mutations/variants rather than an opaque final bitmap when the requested operation can remain editable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Non-destructive adjustments and edit stack

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST preserve non-destructive editability for transforms, crop, colour/light adjustments, effects, masks, vector/text objects and generative operations where technically possible. The app maintains an ordered edit/composition graph rather than repeatedly recompressing the source image after each slider or AI action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can enable/disable or modify prior compatible adjustments, reorder compatible operations, compare before/after, and revert to original/source revision. Invalid reordering that would change unsupported dependency semantics must be rejected or require an explicit bake/convert step.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Variants and revision history

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture provides session undo/redo plus persistent revision history. Users can preserve multiple generated/manual variants, compare them and branch/save a new variant without destroying the original.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI operations record operation type, source revision, selected region/object references, prompt/reference inputs and result revision/tool provenance where available. Generated narrative summaries are not the authority; the structured operation/revision record is.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Smart/linked assets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture supports linked/smart assets where appropriate, including linked raster/vector/Picture assets that retain source identity and can be transformed/effected without immediate destructive embedding. Updating the source can update the linked representation subject to revision/conflict rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The user can explicitly embed/freeze/snapshot a linked asset when a self-contained result is required.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Crop, canvas and artboards

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crop MUST support Free, Original, common ratios such as 1:1, 4:3, 3:2, 16:9 and 9:16, plus custom ratio and straighten/rotation. Crop remains editable until explicit flatten/export semantics require baking.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PictureDocument MAY support one or more artboards/canvases for vector/graphic workflows. Artboard identity/bounds/background are explicit and export can target one artboard, selected artboards or the composed document.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Effects, blend and masks

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST support mature effect/blend workflows including opacity, blend modes, blur/sharpen, shadow/glow and other registered effects where the rendering backend supports them. Effects should be non-destructive and target explicit elements/groups/masks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mask editing uses the shared drawing/selection engine where appropriate. Clipping/masking behaviour must be deterministic and preserved through save/reopen.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Presets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can save, rename, duplicate, reorder, apply and delete/recover reusable edit/effect presets. Presets are typed operation/property sets, not opaque flattened filters, so applied settings remain editable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-assisted presets MAY exist but MUST record which operations are deterministic versus model-generated.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Comparison and preview

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The editor MUST provide Original/current comparison and SHOULD provide split/side-by-side before/after. Preview rendering may use reduced resolution for interactivity but final export/save renders from the canonical source/revision at declared quality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Expensive effects/generation/export expose progress and cancellation without corrupting the last valid document state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: File formats and import

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST support mature viewing/import/edit/export workflows for common raster formats including JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP and TIFF, plus HEIF/HEIC, AVIF and other formats where maintained codec support exists. Animated/multi-frame formats MUST preserve animation unless the user explicitly chooses a flattening conversion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SVG/vector import/export SHOULD preserve editable vector structure where compatible. RAW support MAY be capability-dependent but, where enabled, must preserve the RAW source and use a non-destructive development/render path.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unknown/unsupported format features must be surfaced rather than silently stripped.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Animated and multi-frame images

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Viewer/editor support for animated formats includes playback/pause, frame stepping and timeline/info. Editing operations define whether they apply to current frame, selected frames or all frames. A tool that would flatten animation MUST warn and require an explicit convert/flatten path.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Colour management and HDR

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST honour embedded colour profiles and alpha/transparency. sRGB is the safe baseline; wide-gamut/HDR display/edit behaviour is capability-negotiated where supported. Unsupported profiles/HDR paths must use a declared fallback/transform rather than silently displaying materially wrong colour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Final export MUST allow appropriate colour-profile handling and warn when a target format cannot represent the working colour space/dynamic range.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Metadata and privacy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture's Info/Metadata view exposes available dimensions, format, file size, colour profile, capture date, camera/lens/exposure details, orientation, location and other supported EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata. Unknown metadata should be preserved through non-destructive round trips where possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Export/privacy controls MUST support preserving metadata, removing location metadata and removing all removable metadata where the target format supports it.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Save, export and flattening

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Save persists the editable Picture document/revision for the canonical asset. Save a Copy creates a new Files asset. Export renders to a selected interoperable target format/settings. Revert to Original restores/bypasses editable operations without deleting the source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Formats that cannot store Picture's editable composition are exported as rendered/flattened outputs while the canonical Picture edit state remains separately persisted against the Picture document/asset. Flattening the editable source itself requires an explicit action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Export options include size/resolution, format/compression/quality, transparency/background, colour profile, metadata/privacy and applicable animation/vector options.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files and canonical asset identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files remains authoritative for filesystem/storage identity and operations such as open, create, rename, move, copy, delete/recover, share, provider/cloud hydration and bytes. Picture MUST NOT create a hidden duplicate file store.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Picture asset/document can reference a canonical FileID plus source revision. Renaming/moving the file does not detach Picture state. CloudOnly content hydrates through Files and exposes progress/failure.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Cross-app interoperability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture assets can be embedded/referenced in Write, Present, Boards, Canvas and Spaces through canonical identity. A live reference follows the selected canonical asset/revision policy; an explicit Snapshot/Copy freezes or duplicates content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app paste/drag/drop uses the Shared Productivity Engine/Files transfer contracts so supported raster/vector/text/drawing structure is preserved instead of automatically flattening to pixels.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI bar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST host the global persistent Dulche AI bar. Semantic context includes DocumentID/FileID, revision, selected ElementIDs/SelectionID/MaskID, current tool/mode, relevant composition/layer structure, canvas/artboard geometry, available metadata, linked assets and typed Picture actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Read-only mode can analyse/explain/describe without changing the document. Write mode performs edits only through typed Picture/shared-engine actions. AI MUST NOT simulate raw pointer gestures when semantic object/selection APIs exist.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Picture API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture's first-party API catalogue is exhaustive under the global API-parity rule. Minimum canonical entry points include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
