heading: HEADING_3
text: Automation and Spaces integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations, Spaces and Dulche can invoke the exhaustive Picture action catalogue subject to permissions/capabilities. Long-running generation/render/export operations return job/run state with progress, cancellation and typed errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture publishes typed events for meaningful document/revision/generation/export changes without flooding Automations with raw pointer/stroke-move events.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Collaboration and conflict handling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture mutations are revision-aware. Independent edits may merge where the canonical object graph proves them non-conflicting; concurrent incompatible edits to the same element/mask/layer/revision MUST surface a conflict rather than blind last-write-wins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated edits are attributable to a revision/action actor and are undoable/reviewable through the same history system as manual changes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Security and generated content

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI/image generation/editing follows configured model/tool permissions, content controls, privacy/local-cloud routing policy and source-asset access permissions. Picture MUST NOT upload local/private images to a remote model/provider when the effective privacy policy forbids it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated/imported external content is treated as content, not executable code. Embedded metadata/scripts MUST NOT acquire application execution privileges.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture's Create/Edit/Generate/Browse surfaces MUST be keyboard-operable for required workflows. Sliders/controls expose names, values and keyboard adjustment. Layer/object lists, tools, masks and selection state expose meaningful semantic accessibility information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Image descriptions/alt text MAY be stored/edited where applicable. Colour-only indicators require textual/semantic equivalents. Zoom/crop/transform handles have keyboard-accessible alternatives.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST provide useful Windows, 9to1-OS and web editing/creation experiences over the same PictureDocument model. Codec, RAW, HDR, GPU effect, pen/tilt and local/remote AI capability differences are explicit and queryable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The web app MUST NOT degrade into a read-only image viewer. Unsupported platform features are disabled with a capability reason while preserving the canonical document so another capable client can continue editing.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and resource behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST use resolution-appropriate decode, GPU acceleration where suitable, incremental/tiled rendering for very large images, bounded preview/thumbnail caches, background full-quality rendering and cancellable long-running jobs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Interactive edit previews may use reduced-resolution proxies, but final save/export renders from canonical source content at requested quality. Large layer/vector graphs should avoid full-document rerenders when only a bounded element/region changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated previews/variants and caches are bounded and revision-addressed. Closing or cancelling generation does not corrupt the last valid document.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture MUST return structured failures including DocumentNotFound, ElementNotFound, InvalidSelection, InvalidMask, UnsupportedFormat, UnsupportedCodecFeature, ColourProfileUnsupported, HDRUnsupported, RevisionConflict, LinkedAssetUnavailable, GenerationUnavailable, GenerationFailed, InvalidGenerationRegion, ExportUnsupportedFeature, RenderFailed, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable in addition to shared engine/model errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A failed edit/generation/export leaves the prior valid document revision intact. Unsupported export features are reported before destructive flattening/conversion.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Picture is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A real Raster, Vector and Hybrid PictureDocument can be created, saved, closed and reopened with editable structure intact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automatic composition mode allows ordinary users to create/edit complex images without manual layer management, while Manual Layer mode exposes the same underlying canonical structure without conversion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared Write/Present/Canvas/Boards productivity, text, shape, selection/transform and Rnote-derived drawing engines are actually reused rather than reimplemented as Picture-private equivalents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Raster editing covers crop/transform, light/colour, blur/sharpen/repair and masks with non-destructive/revision-aware behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vector editing covers path/anchor/Bézier editing, fills/strokes, boolean operations, snapping/alignment, text/path integration and raster/vector conversion workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A user can circle/smart-select a subject, freely move/resize/delete/replace it, and Picture reconstructs exposed background while preserving revisioned editable state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generative fill/erase/replace/extend and background replacement operate on explicit selections/objects and preserve source/revision provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text-to-image, reference-guided creation and sketch-to-image create normal editable Picture assets/documents rather than opaque temporary results.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sketch-to-image can use shared drawing-engine strokes and supports iterative region refinement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual drawing/painting/markup uses the shared Rnote-derived drawing engine and retains editable stroke semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before/after comparison, variants, undo/redo and persistent revision history survive restart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Raster, vector, text, generated objects, masks and linked assets coexist correctly in a Hybrid document.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Save, Save Copy and export preserve the editable source while producing interoperable rendered/vector outputs with explicit flattening where required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files identity survives rename/move/hydration and live cross-app references remain canonical.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent AI bar performs semantic typed edits against selected objects/regions and never requires raw UI simulation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical document model while capability-negotiating codecs/GPU/AI/pen differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large source images/layer graphs remain interactive through tiling/proxy rendering/bounded caches and final export renders at requested source quality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Picture follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract rather than launching an incompatible private runtime.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Wave

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and native-generation principle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Wave is the native CUI audio recording, editing, mixing, sequencing and sound-creation app. It combines an approachable multitrack editor with professional waveform/spectral editing, mixing, effects, music sequencing, sound-effect construction, text-to-speech and AI-assisted production.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All generated audio components MUST be native, structured Wave components whenever the requested result can be represented by Wave's own sequencer, synthesis, effect, speech or clip systems. AI MUST NOT normally return an opaque arbitrary waveform as the canonical result for music, sound effects, speech or other structured generative workflows. Rendering to audio is a derived/export/playback result; the editable native component remains canonical.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example: asking AI to create a song produces editable sequencer/instrument/pattern/arrangement data; asking for a laser sound creates an editable Sound Effect Builder patch; asking for narration creates a native Text-to-Speech object retaining its text/voice/prosody settings.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shared media/audio engine

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST share its core audio/media primitives with Motion, Present and other eligible 9to1 surfaces rather than creating incompatible per-app audio engines. The shared media/audio layer owns canonical audio assets, clips, time ranges, transport/playback, waveform/spectrogram analysis, effect descriptors, rendering/export primitives and realtime-safe audio processing where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion uses the same compatible audio clip/effect/timeline primitives for video projects. Present recording/narration uses compatible Wave/shared-media assets. Vision & Voice contributes shared microphone/device discovery, OS audio permissions and applicable capture primitives, while Wave remains the persistent production editor. Dulche Audio/Voice supplies model-backed transcription, analysis and speech capability without becoming a second project model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GStreamer is an approved maintained media backend and GStreamer Editing Services or an explicitly documented equivalent may be used where appropriate. Backend choice MUST preserve the public Wave project/action contracts.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical project model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: WaveProject has stable ProjectID, sample-rate/channel configuration, timeline/timebase, tempo map where used, Tracks[], Markers/Regions[], native generated components, project settings, CreatedAt/ModifiedAt and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AudioTrack has stable TrackID, name, ordered Clips[], Gain, Pan, Mute, Solo, RecordArm, Effects[], AutomationLanes[], routing/bus state where supported and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AudioClip has stable ClipID, SourceAssetID or native GeneratedComponentID, source range, TimelineStart, Duration, Gain, fades, stretch/pitch settings, effects/automation references and Revision. Timeline editing MUST be non-destructive by default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated native components receive stable IDs and can be inserted on tracks like other sources while retaining their editable structured source. Rendering a component for playback/export does not replace that structured source.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Main workspace and transport

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave's primary workspace is a multitrack timeline with transport, track controls, selected clip/component inspector and optional mixer/effects/sequencer/spectral panels. Record, Edit, Mix and Generate are workflow emphases over one project rather than incompatible document modes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transport MUST include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Play, Pause, Stop and Record.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Seek to start/end and previous/next marker or region.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Loop playback/recording.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Timeline position display with time/timecode and musical bars/beats where enabled.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Playback speed and metronome/count-in where relevant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard-first editing shortcuts are required for repetitive timeline operations.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recording

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST support robust microphone/device recording including input-device selection, mono/stereo/multichannel where available, input monitoring, level meters/clipping indication, record-arm per track, count-in/pre-roll/post-roll, punch-in/punch-out, overdub, loop/take recording and pause/resume.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recording is written incrementally/crash-safely so a process or device failure does not discard an entire long recording. Incomplete recoverable takes remain clearly marked until finalised.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Waveform and clip editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required clip/waveform operations include:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Select time range, move, duplicate, copy/paste, split and join/compose where semantically valid.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Trim, slip/source-range edit, delete, ripple delete and insert/ripple move.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Fade in/out and crossfade.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gain/normalise, silence, reverse, resample, time-stretch and pitch-shift.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Snap to grid, markers, transients, clips or musical timing where enabled.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordinary clip edits change clip/source-range/timeline metadata rather than destructively rewriting source bytes. A destructive source edit, where explicitly requested, creates a recoverable revision/new source asset.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Multitrack, mixer, routing and buses

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST support multiple simultaneous audio tracks for voice, music, sound effects, ambience, generated content, imported media and multiple takes. Track grouping and multi-selection allow coherent edits across related clips.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The mixer provides per-track and master gain, pan, mute/solo, meters, insert effects and supported sends/buses/routing. Advanced routing may be hidden by default but the canonical project supports it where exposed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Master processing is explicit and non-destructive. Export rendering follows the current routing/effect graph.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Effects and parameter automation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core non-AI effect families include at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: EQ/filtering including high/low-pass and parametric EQ.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compressor, limiter, gate/expander and de-esser.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reverb and delay.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Chorus/flanger/phaser and modulation effects where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Distortion/saturation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pitch shift/time stretch.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stereo width, gain/normalisation and utility processing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effects are non-destructive insert/processing nodes by default and can be reordered, bypassed, edited and removed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effect/track/instrument parameters may be automated over time using native automation lanes/curves. Automation data is structured and editable rather than baked into a rendered waveform.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Spectral editing and repair

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST provide Waveform, Spectrogram and combined Waveform+Spectrogram views. Time/frequency selections can drive attenuation, filtering, silence, repair and model-assisted cleanup operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native/manual repair includes where supported:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Click/pop removal.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DC offset correction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hum/notch filtering.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Noise reduction and gating.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clipping repair where technically possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Silence trimming and loudness normalisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-assisted cleanup MAY isolate speech, remove/reduce noise, reverb, clicks, breaths/coughs, restore damaged recordings and perform other model-backed repair, but outputs remain represented as native derived clips/effect operations/revisions rather than silently overwriting the source.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Audio enhancement and denoising tools

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST expose first-class Enhance Audio and Denoise tools for selected clips, tracks, time ranges and imported or recorded audio. Enhance Audio is a configurable restoration/mastering pipeline, not a single opaque AI button. At minimum it MUST be able to combine appropriate noise/hum reduction, de-click/de-pop, de-reverb where available, clarity/EQ correction, dynamics/level correction and loudness normalisation; speech-focused enhancement MAY use model-backed processing. Denoise MUST provide an automatic one-click path plus an advanced path with strength/amount and preview/bypass. Where the selected backend supports noise-profile learning, Wave MUST allow a selected region to be used as the noise profile.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Enhancement and denoising MUST be previewable, undoable and non-destructive. Long-running model-backed processing MUST expose progress and cancellation. The source asset remains intact; Wave stores the configured processing and/or derived result with provenance. Applying enhancement MUST NOT silently modify unrelated clips, tracks, effects or master routing.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Music Sequencer

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST include a first-class native music sequencer. Music generation, whether user-authored or AI-assisted, produces editable sequencer content rather than an arbitrary final audio file.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The sequencer supports stable SequenceID/PatternID/NoteEventID/InstrumentID identities, tempo/time-signature maps, piano-roll and step-sequencer editing, note pitch/start/duration/velocity, quantisation, swing/groove, looping patterns, arrangement sections, track/instrument assignment and parameter automation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drum sequencing supports drum-grid/pad-oriented patterns, per-step velocity/probability/variation where supported and reusable kits. Melodic sequencing supports chords, scales/key assistance where enabled, note expression and automation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The arrangement view assembles patterns/regions into song structure such as Intro, Verse, Chorus, Bridge and Outro without flattening them. Users can duplicate/modify a pattern instance or create a linked instance according to explicit identity semantics.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Native instruments and sampling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The sequencer MUST provide a versioned instrument registry. Native instrument families MAY include synthesizers, drums/percussion, sampler instruments and other maintained engines. Each Instrument has structured editable parameters, preset identity/version and automation-capable controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sampler instruments reference canonical audio assets and expose mapped key/range, start/end, loop, pitch/tuning, envelope/filter and other supported parameters without duplicating source bytes unnecessarily.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI may choose/configure instruments, write notes/patterns, create arrangement structure, automate parameters and mix tracks, but MUST produce the same native Sequencer/Instrument/Effect objects a user can inspect and edit manually.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI music generation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A request such as 'make a two-minute upbeat electronic track' MUST generate a native music project/section: tempo and meter, sequencer tracks, instrument choices/settings, editable note/pattern data, arrangement, automation and effects/mix state. The canonical AI result is NOT an opaque two-minute waveform.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI may iterate by editing native structures: 'make the chorus heavier' changes relevant patterns/instruments/automation/effects; 'change the chord progression' rewrites note/chord events while preserving unrelated project structure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated music can subsequently be manually edited in piano roll/step sequencer/mixer. Export renders the structured project into WAV/FLAC/MP3/etc. only when requested.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Sound Effects Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST include a native Sound Effects Builder for procedural/constructed sound effects. A SoundEffectPatch has stable PatchID and a structured processing/generation graph rather than being merely a rendered audio clip.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The builder SHOULD use the Home Node Graph Framework for editing/visualisation where appropriate, with Wave-specific realtime audio nodes and execution handled by the Wave audio engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core SFX node families include where supported:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Oscillator/wavetable/source generators.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Noise generators.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sampler/audio-asset sources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Envelope/ADSR and amplitude shaping.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pitch/frequency modulation and LFO.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Filters/EQ.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Distortion/waveshaping.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Delay/reverb/modulation effects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Layer/mix/split/combine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Randomisation/probability and parameter modulation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Output/render.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A request such as 'create a futuristic laser blast' causes AI to build/configure an editable native patch graph, envelopes, oscillators/noise, pitch movement and effects. The generated patch can be auditioned and inserted onto the timeline, but the patch remains the canonical editable source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The UI SHOULD offer simple high-level macro controls for common users while allowing advanced users to open the complete patch graph.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Text to Speech

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST include native Text-to-Speech components. A SpeechSynthesis object stores stable SpeechID, text/script, selected VoiceID/model/runtime, language/locale, pronunciation/phoneme overrides where supported, speed, pitch, style/emotion/prosody controls, timing/alignment metadata and revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editing the text or voice/prosody regenerates the derived speech render while retaining the same structured SpeechSynthesis source. Speech may be split into utterances/paragraphs/regions and aligned on the timeline without flattening into an anonymous generated waveform.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a TTS backend exposes word/phoneme timings, Wave stores them for transcript/alignment editing. Export may render speech to ordinary audio, but the editable Wave project retains the speech component.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice cloning/conversion or user-supplied voice references, if supported, require the applicable consent/permission and provenance rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Other generated native components

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The same native-generation rule applies to generated ambience, transitions and other constructible audio. AI should build Wave-native source/processing structures — for example layered samplers plus filters/envelopes/automation for ambience — instead of defaulting to opaque audio generation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When a capability fundamentally requires an externally generated waveform that cannot be represented by existing native generators, that waveform MAY enter Wave only as an explicit GeneratedSample source asset with model/provenance metadata. It MUST then be treated like a normal editable sample/clip, and the UI must not pretend it has native sequencer/patch editability. Native structured generation remains the default and required path whenever representable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Transcription and transcript-based editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave transcription is time-aligned to project/source audio and can include speaker diarisation, word timing, language detection, punctuation and corrections where supported. Clicking/selecting transcript text maps to the corresponding audio range.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transcript-based edits such as deleting a phrase or removing long pauses translate into ordinary native timeline/clip edits after preview/validation. The transcript is a semantic editing view over canonical audio/timeline state, not a replacement authority for the audio project.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Custom censorship

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST include Custom Censorship for a selected clip, track, time range or whole-project audio scope. A CensorshipRuleSet can contain exact words, phrases, user-defined terms and one or more semantic themes/categories. Word and phrase rules use time-aligned transcription where available; theme rules MAY use supported model-backed semantic classification. Detection MUST produce reviewable candidate time ranges before application, and the user MUST be able to add, remove or adjust matches to correct false positives and false negatives.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each rule or rule set can choose a treatment including bleep/tone, mute/silence, attenuation, replacement with a user-selected sound, or timeline removal when explicitly chosen. Controls MUST include pre/post padding and fades, and MAY optionally redact matched text from captions/transcripts. Censorship remains a structured editable operation with stable identity; it can be disabled, reconfigured or undone without altering the original source. Export/render follows the active censorship state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Audio separation and derived stems

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where configured model/backends support it, Wave can separate mixed audio into structured derived assets/tracks such as vocals, drums, bass, other/music, speakers or foreground/background. Source audio remains preserved and the separated outputs receive stable asset/track identities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI separation is a transformation workflow, not an excuse to destroy or replace the source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stem splitting MUST be exposed as a first-class Split Stems tool rather than only as an AI command. The UI MUST offer every separation mode supported by the configured backend, including common modes such as Vocals/Instrumental, Vocals/Drums/Bass/Other, speaker separation and Foreground/Background where available. The user can choose which derived stems become tracks, preview/audition the result and re-run separation with a different supported mode without replacing the original mixed source.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Markers, regions and chapters

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave supports stable MarkerID and RegionID entities for navigation, looping, chapters, editing targets and export metadata. Markers/regions may carry names, colours/categories, notes and references without changing underlying clip data.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Podcast, narration and spoken-word workflows

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Podcast/spoken-word workflows reuse normal Wave tracks, transcript, markers, effects and export rather than creating a separate engine. Useful capabilities include multi-speaker editing, chapter markers, silence cleanup, loudness targets, intro/outro, metadata and transcript export.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present narration and other 9to1 speech assets can open in Wave for detailed editing while retaining canonical timing/asset references.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Motion and Present interoperability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion and Wave MUST share compatible audio asset/clip/effect/timeline primitives. A Motion audio track can be opened/edited in Wave and return as the same canonical audio/project reference where supported, avoiding an unnecessary export-edit-import loop.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present recording/narration can use compatible Wave/shared-media assets and can deep-link to Wave for advanced cleanup/mix/editing without losing timing/reference identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files and storage identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files remains authoritative for source/export asset storage identity, create/move/rename/delete/recover/share and provider/cloud hydration. Wave project structures reference stable FileID/asset identities rather than absolute file paths.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recorded/generated/imported assets receive canonical storage/asset identity. Moving/renaming the underlying File does not detach the Wave reference.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Import and export

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave import MUST support common maintained codecs/formats through the shared media backend. Source sample rate, channels, timing and metadata are preserved where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Export can target full project, selected region, track(s), stems, selected clips or selected native generated components. Common outputs include WAV, FLAC, MP3, AAC/M4A and OGG/Opus where supported, plus other maintained codecs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Export options include sample rate, bit depth where applicable, bitrate/quality, channel layout, loudness/normalisation, metadata and relevant loop/chapter settings. Export never silently mutates the project.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI bar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST host the global persistent Dulche AI bar. Semantic context includes ProjectID, selected TrackIDs/ClipIDs/GeneratedComponentIDs, selected time/frequency range, playhead, markers/regions, sequencer patterns/notes/instruments, SFX graph selection, speech object/text, effects/automation state, transcript selection, sample rate/timebase and revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write-capable AI changes Wave only through typed Wave/shared-media/NodeGraph actions. It MUST NOT simulate timeline mouse gestures when semantic APIs exist.

heading: HEADING_3

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Wave.SplitClip(projectID, clipID, time);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Wave.TrimClip(projectID, clipID, sourceRange);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Wave.MoveClip(projectID, clipID, placement);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Wave.SetTrackProperty(projectID, trackID, property, value);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Wave.AddEffect(projectID, targetID, effect, config?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sound Effect Builder graph mutation uses 9to1.NodeGraph.* where the shared Node Graph Framework is the canonical graph-editing layer. Shared media operations SHOULD use their owning shared API namespace when that is canonical.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automation and integration events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations, Spaces, Dulche and other authorised clients can use the exhaustive Wave action catalogue. Long recording/render/export/transcription/separation jobs expose progress, cancellation, retry/idempotency where relevant and typed result/error state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave emits meaningful typed events such as project/revision changes, recording completed, export completed, render failed and generated component changed; it MUST NOT flood Automations with raw per-sample or pointer events.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Collaboration and revision conflicts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project/track/clip/pattern/note/patch/speech mutations are revision-aware. Independent object edits MAY merge when safe; incompatible concurrent edits to the same canonical object surface conflict rather than blind last-write-wins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A running render/export/recording is pinned to the required source/project revision and MUST NOT silently switch to a newly edited revision mid-job.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST be keyboard-operable for transport, clip selection/editing, sequencer editing, mixer controls, transcript editing and generated-component workflows. Waveforms/spectrograms provide semantic time/level/frequency information and non-pointer equivalents for required operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Meters, clipping, mute/solo, automation and error states MUST NOT rely on colour alone. Screen-reader users can inspect track/clip/note/patch/speech object identity and values.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and realtime safety

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The realtime audio path MUST remain isolated from blocking UI, disk, AI/model, network and export work. Playback/recording cannot glitch merely because waveform thumbnails, transcription, generation or export are running.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Waveforms/spectrograms are incrementally analysed/cached; large recordings are streamed/tiled rather than fully decoded into RAM. Realtime-safe effect/instrument processing obeys bounded allocation/latency constraints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated sequencer/SFX/TTS components render incrementally/cached for preview while preserving the structured source. Background renders are cancellable and caches are bounded/revision-invalidated.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave durably stores project structure, current recording chunks/takes, native generated-component state and edit history often enough to maximise crash recovery. Restart can recover incomplete recordings/project mutations without replaying committed destructive actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured failures include ProjectNotFound, TrackNotFound, ClipNotFound, GeneratedComponentNotFound, InvalidTimeRange, InvalidSequence, InvalidPattern, InstrumentUnavailable, InvalidSoundEffectGraph, VoiceUnavailable, RecordingDeviceUnavailable, RecordingFailed, CodecUnsupported, RenderFailed, ExportFailed, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable, plus shared backend/model errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A failed AI/native generation/render/export leaves the prior valid project and source assets intact.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave MUST provide useful Windows, 9to1-OS and web editing/creation experiences over the same canonical project model. Input devices, realtime audio APIs, codecs, plugin/instrument backends, MIDI/controller access and local/cloud model capabilities are explicit/queryable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web MUST remain a useful multitrack/sequencer/editor experience rather than a static player. Unsupported platform capabilities are disabled with a clear reason while preserving project state for another capable client.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wave is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A multitrack project can be recorded, edited, mixed, closed/reopened and exported while preserving stable TrackID/ClipID/revision identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recording supports device selection, metering, track arm and crash-safe recovery of an interrupted take.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Waveform clip editing is non-destructive and split/trim/move/fade/crossfade/undo survive restart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mixer/effects/automation are structured and editable, with realtime playback remaining stable during background work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Waveform/spectrogram editing and native/audio-model repair operate without destroying the original source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Music Sequencer persists editable note/pattern/instrument/arrangement/automation data and can render/export the result.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An AI music request generates a native sequencer arrangement with editable notes, patterns, instruments and effects instead of an opaque waveform.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sound Effects Builder persists an editable native patch graph and an AI request such as a laser sound generates/configures that graph rather than only returning rendered audio.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text-to-Speech persists editable text/voice/prosody state and regenerated speech remains linked to the same native SpeechSynthesis component.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated ambience/transitions use native Wave generators/patches/components whenever representable; an unavoidable external GeneratedSample is explicitly identified as a sampled fallback with provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transcript-based deletion maps to ordinary timeline edits and remains undoable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Separation produces derived stable tracks/assets while preserving the mixed source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Enhance Audio and Denoise are available as ordinary manual tools, support preview/bypass or equivalent before commitment, remain undoable/non-destructive and preserve the original source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom Censorship can detect at least an exact word/phrase rule and a semantic-theme rule, exposes detected ranges for review/correction, applies the selected treatment and remains reversible without altering the source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Split Stems is directly accessible from the Wave UI, creates stable derived track/asset identities for a supported separation mode and preserves the original mixed source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion/Present interoperability uses shared canonical audio primitives rather than export/import duplication.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent AI bar edits tracks/clips/sequences/patches/speech through typed APIs rather than raw UI simulation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large projects/recordings remain responsive through streaming, incremental analysis and bounded caches.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same project/generated-component model while capability-negotiating audio hardware/backend differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Wave follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract rather than launching an incompatible private runtime.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Motion

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and native project principle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Motion is the native CUI video editing, compositing, animation and motion-graphics application. It combines professional non-linear editing, layered visual composition, animation, titles/graphics, colour, audio production, AI-assisted editing and generative-video workflows while keeping the default editing experience approachable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical result of work in Motion is a structured MotionProject, not a rendered video. Normal edits such as trimming, crop, speed changes, transforms, masks, effects, colour changes, captions, keyframes, procedural animation and AI-assisted mutations MUST remain inspectable editable project state. Rendering, proxies, previews, caches and exports are derived outputs and MUST NOT silently replace canonical project state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shared engines and dependency boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST reuse shared 9to1 engines aggressively wherever the underlying capability belongs to more than one product. Shared capability MUST live in the appropriate shared engine/library rather than requiring another app UI process or duplicating private implementations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion reuses the Wave/shared-media engine for audio clips, tracks, waveform/spectrogram analysis, effects, mixing, generated speech/music/SFX and audio rendering; Picture/shared visual primitives for compatible raster/vector composition, masks, paths, still-image effects and object-level image manipulation; Present/shared animation primitives for compatible easing, interpolation and timing concepts; the Shared Productivity Engine for compatible text, vector shape, drawing/ink and transform primitives; Rnote-derived drawing/path primitives for annotation, matte/mask drawing and rotoscoping assistance; Files for canonical asset identity; Dulche/model infrastructure for analysis and generation; the shared Node Graph Framework for advanced graphs; and CUI for the shell/navigation/interaction system.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dependency direction MUST remain acyclic and engine-oriented. Motion MUST NOT require the Picture or Wave UI processes merely to crop an image or adjust audio. Picture, Wave and Motion consume compatible shared implementations. If Motion needs a capability that Picture, Wave, Present or another surface also materially needs, the implementation SHOULD be placed in the owning shared engine rather than copied.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical project model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MotionProject has stable ProjectID, Sequences[], AssetReferences[], GeneratedComponents[], GlobalSettings, ColourSettings, ProxyCacheSettings, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sequence has stable SequenceID, Width, Height, PixelAspectRatio, FrameRate/timebase, Duration, VideoTracks[], compatible AudioTracks[], Markers[], Guides/safe-area state where used, colour/HDR state and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VisualTrack has stable TrackID, name, ordered Elements[], visibility, lock state, compositing state where applicable and Revision. Audio tracks use compatible Wave/shared-media track primitives rather than a second incompatible audio model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MotionElement has stable ElementID, ElementType, SourceAssetID or GeneratedComponentID where applicable, TrackID, TimelineStart, Duration, SourceRange, Transform, Crop, Opacity, BlendMode, Masks[], Effects[], ParameterAnimation[], graph references where applicable and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Masks, EffectInstances, AnimationTracks, Keyframes, Titles/TextObjects, CaptionTracks, CaptionCues, analysis records and Motion node-graph objects MUST have stable identity and revision-aware state where they are addressable/editable. AI, Automations, collaboration and undo/redo address canonical object IDs and properties rather than screen coordinates.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Main workspace and contextual editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The default Motion workspace consists of Media/Assets, Viewer/Canvas, contextual Inspector and Timeline. Panels MAY be docked, resized, collapsed, moved or hidden, but the initial workspace MUST avoid exposing an unnecessarily large professional-panel wall to a new user.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Inspector is selection-sensitive: selecting video exposes video/transform/effect controls; text exposes typography/layout/animation; masks expose mask/path controls; audio exposes Wave-compatible controls; generated objects expose generation/provenance controls; and no selection exposes sequence/project controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Direct manipulation in the Viewer/Canvas MUST mutate the same canonical properties and typed actions used by the Inspector, keyboard operations, APIs and AI. The viewer MUST NOT maintain a separate UI-only transform or mask state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Timeline and non-linear editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST provide a professional multi-track NLE timeline with accurate frame/timecode semantics, in/out ranges, source/sequence viewing, snapping, multi-selection, markers, grouping, linked audio/video, track controls and nested sequences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Minimum typed editing operations include insert, overwrite, append, blade/split, trim, ripple trim, roll, slip, slide, ripple delete, lift, extract, move, duplicate, group/ungroup, link/unlink audio and video, track lock, video visibility, audio mute/solo where applicable, range selection and nested-sequence creation/use.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transport MUST support ordinary play/pause, frame stepping and efficient shuttle/scrub control, including keyboard-first operation such as J/K/L-style transport where appropriate. Editing operations MUST be deterministic at the sequence timebase and MUST NOT depend on pixel coordinates in the timeline UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Video tracks may contain video, images, Picture assets, titles/text, vector graphics, shapes/ink, generated media, adjustment/effect layers, nested sequences and other registered compatible visual elements. Timeline editing remains non-destructive by default.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Source media, proxies, preview and cache

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST separate canonical source media from proxy media, decode caches, analysis caches, preview renders and final render output. Editing against a proxy MUST preserve the same canonical source identity, timing, ElementID and project semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST support automatic proxy generation, user-requested proxies, configurable proxy resolution/codec where supported, per-asset proxy state, background generation, lower-resolution viewer playback and render/pre-render caching.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Final render/export MUST use canonical source media at requested output quality unless the user explicitly chooses a proxy-derived or otherwise lower-quality source path. Missing or stale proxies/caches are recoverable derived-state problems and MUST NOT make the canonical project invalid.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Viewer, transforms and visual composition

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Viewer doubles as an interactive composition canvas. Users can directly inspect and edit position, scale, rotation, anchor/pivot, crop, opacity, masks, alignment/guides, text bounds and compatible shape/path properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transform and visual-property edits MUST be represented by canonical property mutations. Source pixels/frames remain unchanged unless the user explicitly performs a destructive source-operation workflow outside normal Motion project editing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST support layered compositing with opacity, blend modes, alpha, masks, mattes, track mattes, chroma/luma keying, nesting/precomposition, adjustment layers and explicit compositing order where supported.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Animation and keyframes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Suitable numeric, vector, colour, mask, effect, text and generated-component properties MUST be animatable through a common parameter-animation system rather than each feature inventing incompatible keyframe storage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyframes have stable identity and support create, move, copy, duplicate, delete and value editing. Supported interpolation includes at least hold/step, linear and smooth/eased interpolation, with Bézier/value curves where meaningful. Motion MUST provide easing presets and a graph/curve editor for advanced editing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared Present animation/timing primitives SHOULD be reused when semantics are compatible, while Motion remains authoritative for timeline/frame-based video state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Advanced node editor

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST include a full visual node editor for advanced compositing, effects, transitions, motion graphics and procedural animation. It reuses the shared 9to1 Node Graph Framework for GraphID/NodeID/PortID identity, pan/zoom, selection, grouping, comments, typed ports, connection validation, copy/paste/duplicate, undo/redo, graph revisioning, AI graph mutation and execution-state visualisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion registers a rich Motion-specific node catalogue. Minimum families include media/sequence inputs, transform, crop, masks/mattes, compositing/blending, chroma/luma keying, colour processing, blur/sharpen, distortion/displacement, tracking data, procedural shapes, text/title generation, time offsets, retiming, parameter maths, curves, interpolation/easing, switching/conditions, generators and compatible particle/procedural systems where implemented.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Node graphs are structured project state. Branching graphs MUST NOT require destructive intermediate renders merely because an operation is non-linear. Render/cache intermediates MAY be produced for performance, but graph topology, parameters and inputs remain canonical.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The normal Motion UI MUST remain usable without nodes. Common effects and animation can be edited directly. Where an advanced representation is appropriate, Open in Node Editor/Advanced exposes or creates the structured graph without silently replacing unrelated project state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Motion graph types and reusable graph assets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion defines native reusable graph objects including MotionEffectGraph, MotionTransitionGraph, MotionAnimationGraph and MotionCompositionGraph. Each has stable identity, revision state, typed inputs/outputs, internal NodeGraph identity, exposed user parameters and provenance/origin metadata where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graphs may be embedded in one project or saved as reusable presets/components. Shared-definition instances MUST have explicit semantics for edit-this-instance, detach/copy or update-shared-definition; editing one instance MUST NOT unexpectedly rewrite every use.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Registered custom node types MAY be supplied through the broader 9to1 extension system subject to capability, trust and permission rules. First- or third-party node providers MUST participate in typed graph contracts rather than injecting arbitrary UI-only behaviour.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Custom transitions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transitions MUST support ordinary built-in transitions and reusable MotionTransitionGraph assets. A custom transition graph receives at least outgoing visual input, incoming visual input, normalised transition progress from 0 to 1, frame/time context, sequence dimensions and any declared exposed parameters.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transition graphs can therefore implement animated masks, zoom/whip transitions, blur, displacement, glitch/RGB treatments, procedural reveals and other advanced effects. The resulting transition remains editable and reusable rather than being permanently rendered into replacement clips.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transition duration, alignment and exposed parameters remain ordinary structured timeline state and can be animated where compatible.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Procedural animation and property drivers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MotionAnimationGraph can drive compatible properties without baking every frame into ordinary keyframes. Minimum useful node families include constants, vectors, arithmetic, clamp, map/remap range, curves, noise, oscillators, frame/time, velocity, distance, interpolation, easing, deterministic seeded random, tracking data, audio amplitude/frequency analysis and safe formula/expression nodes where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyframes, procedural graphs, tracking and linked values MUST interoperate through one canonical parameter-source model. A property can have a base/static value, keyframed value, procedural contribution and/or tracked/linked contribution only where the combination semantics are explicitly defined. The Inspector MUST make it clear what currently drives a property.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example: a title may follow tracked subject position, retain hand-authored keyframed movement and add a small procedural noise offset without baking thousands of frame values.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Masks, tracking and rotoscoping

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Masks are native editable objects supporting compatible path geometry, feather, opacity, expansion and animation. Manual drawing/path editing SHOULD reuse shared Picture/Rnote-derived primitives where semantics match.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion SHOULD support point, planar, subject or object tracking according to configured backends. Tracking data is structured and may drive transforms, masks, effects, text or procedural graphs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model-assisted subject/object segmentation and rotoscoping MAY initialise or update masks, but users MUST be able to inspect and correct results. Frame-by-frame/manual correction remains possible. Tracking or segmentation MUST NOT silently destroy source media.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Colour pipeline

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST include first-party colour correction/grading suitable for normal production. Minimum controls include exposure, contrast, highlights/shadows, temperature/tint, saturation and curves, plus channel/colour-wheel or equivalent advanced controls where implemented.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LUT import/use, histograms/scopes and per-clip or adjustment-layer grading SHOULD be supported where the backend permits. Sequence/project colour-space state MUST explicitly represent SDR/HDR and managed-colour configuration where supported rather than relying on hidden backend defaults.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Effects, titles and graphics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effects are structured EffectInstance objects with stable identity, provider/type identity, ordered placement, parameters, bypass state and animation references. Core families include colour, blur/sharpen, transform, keying, distortion, stylisation and utility effects. Effect stacks remain reorderable, bypassable, editable and removable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Titles and graphics MUST remain native structured objects rather than pre-rendered video. Text/title state includes text content, font/style, paragraph/layout, fills/strokes, backgrounds, transforms, shapes/images, effects and compatible animation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Lower thirds, callouts, captions and reusable title compositions can therefore remain editable. Complex title/graphic systems MAY use Motion node graphs while retaining the same canonical object identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Captions and transcript-based editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST support time-aligned transcription and first-class CaptionTrack/CaptionCue objects. Capabilities include transcript correction, generated captions, editable cue timing/text, split/merge, styling, multiple caption tracks/languages where supported and import/export of maintained subtitle formats such as SRT/WebVTT.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Export MUST support appropriate sidecar, embedded and burned-in caption output according to chosen container/backend capability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transcript-based edits such as deleting a spoken phrase or removing long pauses MUST translate into ordinary native timeline edits after preview/validation. Transcript state is a semantic editing view over the canonical timeline, not a parallel hidden authority.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Audio and Wave interoperability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion audio tracks/clips use compatible Wave/shared-media primitives. Motion directly exposes normal video-production audio controls such as gain/volume, pan, fades, waveform display, effects, normalisation, automation and applicable dialogue cleanup.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where supported, Motion can invoke the shared Enhance Audio, Denoise, Custom Censorship and Split Stems capabilities defined by Wave/shared media without creating incompatible private versions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Open/Edit in Wave MUST preserve canonical asset/clip/timing references so advanced audio work can return to Motion without a lossy export-edit-import cycle. Wave remains the full audio-production surface; Motion provides the subset appropriate to video workflows.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI-assisted editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche operates Motion through typed Motion/shared-engine actions and NodeGraph actions, never by pretending to drag timeline or canvas UI when semantic actions exist.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples: 'remove long pauses' performs transcript/time analysis and native ripple edits; 'make this vertical for a short' creates or adapts an appropriate sequence and uses structured reframing/crop/tracking; 'add animated subtitles' creates caption/title objects and animation; 'make this shot warmer' changes colour parameters; 'create a 30-second highlight reel' creates a new sequence referencing selected source ranges.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated edits MUST remain inspectable, undoable/revisioned project state. AI MUST NOT render an opaque replacement video and declare the structured editing task complete when Motion can represent the requested result natively.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Generative and model-backed video workflows

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subject to installed/configured provider capability, Motion MAY provide video generation, image-to-video, generated B-roll, object/background removal, semantic segmentation, smart reframing, scene/shot detection, motion/subject tracking, video restoration/denoise, enhancement/upscaling, frame interpolation, slow-motion generation, generative fill, temporal inpainting and frame/outpainting/extension.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When a generated result can be represented as editable native Motion structure, that representation remains canonical. When the model inherently returns raster/video frames that cannot reasonably be decomposed into lower-level Motion objects, Motion may create a GeneratedVideoAsset with stable identity, model/provider provenance, generation parameters, source references and revision metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native-generation rules MUST NOT be misinterpreted as requiring generated video pixels to be decomposed into fake editable vectors. The requirement is to preserve genuine structure where it exists and preserve provenance/editability around sampled/generated media where it does not.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Media analysis and indexing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MAY maintain source/revision-aware analysis metadata for cuts/scenes, transcript/speech, silence, audio peaks, motion, tracked subjects/objects, semantic tags and other useful signals supported by configured analysis backends.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Analysis results are cacheable derived metadata tied to source identity/revision. Unchanged media SHOULD NOT be repeatedly reanalysed merely because a project was reopened. Stale analysis is invalidated or refreshed explicitly when its source assumptions change.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files, asset identity and offline media

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files remains authoritative for source/export asset storage identity, move/rename/delete/recover/share and cloud/provider hydration. Motion projects reference stable FileID/AssetID identities rather than absolute paths.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Moving or renaming an underlying File MUST NOT detach a Motion reference. Unavailable source enters an explicit offline-media state and retains timeline/project identity. Relink resolves the existing reference rather than silently creating a new unrelated element.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated, proxy, cache and rendered assets MUST be distinguishable from canonical source identity and carry appropriate provenance/derivation metadata.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Import, export and render queue

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion import MUST support maintained video, image and audio formats exposed by the approved shared media backend. GStreamer/GStreamer Editing Services or an explicitly documented equivalent production-capable backend is approved for decode/encode/playback/timeline primitives. Backend-specific IDs MUST NOT leak into the canonical public Motion project contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Export MUST support sequence/project render, selected range, frame stills, audio-only output, caption/subtitle output and appropriate individual-clip/component exports. Options include maintained container/codec choices, resolution, frame rate, quality/bitrate, audio codec/rate/channels, hardware encoder selection or automatic acceleration and SDR/HDR/colour-space options where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST provide a render queue/background-job model with stable job identity, progress, cancellation, typed failure state and safe retry. Export/render MUST be pinned to the intended project/source revision and MUST NOT silently switch to newly edited state mid-job.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI bar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion hosts the global persistent Dulche AI bar. Semantic context includes ProjectID, SequenceID, selected TrackIDs/ElementIDs/GraphIDs, selected timeline range, playhead, viewer selection, masks/effects/keyframes, transcript/caption selection, source assets, colour state, analysis state and project revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write-capable AI changes Motion only through typed Motion/shared-engine/NodeGraph actions and respects normal permission, trust, revision and undo/audit contracts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
