Shared media, Files, Picture and other shared-domain operations SHOULD use the owning shared API namespace when that is canonical. First-party UI capabilities MUST NOT exist only as inaccessible private UI commands.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automation and integration events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations, Spaces, Dulche and other authorised clients can use the exhaustive Motion action catalogue. Long proxy, analysis, tracking, generation, render and export jobs expose stable progress, cancellation, retry/idempotency where relevant and typed result/error state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion emits meaningful typed events such as project/revision changed, source offline/relinked, analysis completed, proxy ready, tracking completed, render/export completed/failed and graph/generated-component changed. It MUST NOT flood Automations with raw frame, pointer or realtime preview events.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Collaboration and revision conflicts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project/sequence/track/element/mask/effect/keyframe/graph/caption mutations are revision-aware. Independent object edits MAY merge when safe; incompatible concurrent edits to the same canonical object or property MUST surface conflict rather than blind last-write-wins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Running proxy, tracking, generation, render and export jobs are pinned to their required source/project revisions. Their results MUST record which revision/input produced them.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST be keyboard-operable for transport, timeline selection/editing, track controls, inspector properties, captions, keyframes, render jobs and graph editing. Pointer-only gestures cannot be the sole route for required editing operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Screen-reader users can inspect project/sequence/track/element identity, source/offline state, time positions, duration, transform/effect values, keyframes, captions, graph nodes/ports and render/job state. Visual states such as lock, disable, offline, clipping, selection and errors MUST NOT rely on colour alone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Viewer/canvas operations that normally use direct manipulation MUST expose equivalent numeric/semantic controls.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and realtime preview safety

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion MUST decode/render frames on demand using bounded caches rather than loading entire long-form or high-resolution sources into memory. Thumbnail, waveform, proxy, analysis, tracking, generation and render work runs outside latency-sensitive interactive paths.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GPU acceleration and hardware decode/encode SHOULD be used where safe and available, with explicit capability fallback. 4K/8K and otherwise heavy media remain workable through proxies, reduced preview quality, caching and tiling according to available hardware rather than an architecture that assumes full-resolution residency.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Interactive editing MUST remain responsive while background jobs run. Preview quality MAY adapt under load, but canonical time/frame calculations and final requested render quality MUST remain deterministic and source-based.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project saves/autosaves MUST be crash-safe and preserve canonical project integrity. A crash or termination during proxy generation, analysis, tracking, generation, render or export MUST leave the project valid and the derived job recoverable/retryable where feasible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Partial derived output MUST NOT be reported as complete. Failures expose typed state such as ProjectNotFound, SequenceNotFound, ElementNotFound, AssetOffline, CodecUnsupported, ProxyFailed, AnalysisFailed, TrackingFailed, GraphInvalid, NodeUnavailable, GenerationFailed, RenderFailed, ExportFailed, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable plus shared backend/model errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Undo/redo and revision history MUST restore structured project changes without requiring source media to be rewritten.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Motion project/graph/generated-component model while capability-negotiating codecs, GPU/hardware acceleration, camera/device access, model availability and performance differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A platform may disable an unavailable codec, hardware encoder, node provider or model-backed feature with explicit CapabilityUnavailable state, but MUST NOT silently create an incompatible project schema.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Motion follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract rather than launching an incompatible private runtime.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A multi-track project containing video, image, title and audio elements can be edited, closed/reopened and exported while preserving stable project/sequence/track/element identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Insert/overwrite, split, trim, ripple trim, roll, slip, slide, ripple delete, lift/extract, linking and nested-sequence operations produce deterministic structured timeline state and remain undoable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal transforms, crop, masks, effects, colour and speed changes remain non-destructive and survive save/reopen.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Proxy editing retains canonical source identity and final export uses original source quality unless explicitly configured otherwise.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyframed animation persists stable property/keyframe state and the graph/curve editor reproduces the same rendered motion after reopen.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A MotionCompositionGraph can branch/composite multiple visual inputs without flattening the canonical graph; graph edits remain inspectable after restart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A custom MotionTransitionGraph receives outgoing/incoming inputs and normalised progress, renders between clips and remains reusable/editable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A MotionAnimationGraph can procedurally drive a property and can coexist with explicitly defined keyframe/tracking contributions without baking per-frame values.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Registered graph nodes enforce typed-port validation; an invalid connection is rejected without corrupting the graph.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Masking, chroma/luma keying, tracking and manual correction create inspectable editable state rather than rewriting source frames.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Titles/text remain editable native objects after animation/effects and do not require pre-rendering for ordinary editing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transcript/caption workflows create first-class timed caption state; transcript-based deletion maps to ordinary timeline edits; maintained subtitle import/export round-trips representative content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Motion and Wave share compatible audio identity so advanced Wave editing returns to the same Motion audio reference without an unnecessary export/import duplicate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared Enhance Audio, Denoise, Custom Censorship and Split Stems can be invoked from Motion where capability is available without creating an incompatible private audio model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI editing examples such as pause removal, vertical reframing, animated subtitles and highlight-sequence creation execute through typed Motion actions and leave inspectable native state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated video that cannot be represented structurally is stored as a provenance-bearing GeneratedVideoAsset rather than misrepresented as a fully editable native composition.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Offline source media preserves timeline/project identity and relink restores the existing reference.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Render queue jobs expose progress/cancellation/failure and remain pinned to the intended project revision; interrupted derived jobs do not corrupt the project.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large/high-resolution projects remain responsive through proxies, bounded caches, background analysis and adaptive preview rather than full-media RAM loading.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard and assistive-technology paths can perform required timeline, property, caption, graph and render-queue operations without pointer-only dependency.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical project model while capability-negotiating backend/hardware/model differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Motion follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Data Apps

heading: HEADING_2
text: Data

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and data paradigms

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Data is the native CUI spreadsheet, structured-data, relational-database, SQL-query and analytical workspace. It combines conventional spreadsheet work, rich structured cells, relational modelling, multidimensional analytical data, charts/pivots, data transformation, database exploration and AI-assisted analysis in one coherent product.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST support four native data paradigms without forcing one paradigm onto every project: spreadsheet/grid data, relational database data, hierarchical/rich structured data and multidimensional analytical data. These paradigms may interoperate through explicit projections, relationships and transformations, but their semantics MUST NOT be silently conflated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The ordinary spreadsheet remains the approachable default. Advanced relational, nested, multidimensional and query capabilities appear when the data or user workflow requires them. Native .9to1d projects MAY represent richer structures than XLSX/ODS; compatibility formats MUST NOT constrain the native model.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shared engines, donor source and implementation authority

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LibreOffice Calc is the spreadsheet-compatibility/donor engine for established spreadsheet behaviour, formula compatibility and XLSX/ODS interoperability. DuckDB is the local analytical SQL engine for local tables, files, queries and relational projections. Configured providers MAY add PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server and other supported external database systems through typed connection adapters.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The 9to1 source tree MUST contain or fetch the appropriate maintained LibreOffice Calc donor source required by the architecture, subject to the global donor-source and licensing contract. The implementation agent MUST NOT treat a missing LibreOffice installation or missing checked-out donor source as permission to build a miniature replacement spreadsheet engine. If the required donor source is absent during an autonomous development pass, the agent MUST obtain/fork the latest appropriate compatible source and record the exact upstream/version used before continuing dependent implementation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST integrate donor capability into the 9to1 product model, CUI and typed APIs. Merely shelling out to soffice as an opaque external black box while leaving the canonical Data experience or API surface incomplete does not satisfy the implementation requirement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared charting, Node Graph, Files, identity/permissions, credential storage, AI/model, action/audit and other cross-product infrastructure MUST be reused where canonical rather than privately reimplemented.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical Data project model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DataProject has stable ProjectID, Workbooks[], DataSources[], Connections[], SavedQueries[], DataModels[], TransformPipelines[], DataCubes[], Visualisations[], Charts[], PivotModels[], project settings, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A project MAY contain only a workbook, only database/query resources, only a multidimensional model, or any compatible combination. A user MUST NOT need to create unrelated projects merely because one analysis starts in a spreadsheet and later uses SQL or a transformation pipeline.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data resources reference stable identities rather than UI coordinates wherever the resource has independent semantic identity. Ordinary A1/R1C1-style references remain available for spreadsheet compatibility, but tables, records, queries, charts, pivots, connections, relationships, visualisations and pipelines have stable IDs.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Workbook and spreadsheet model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Workbook has stable WorkbookID, Sheets[], workbook names/named ranges, calculation settings, external/link metadata, compatibility metadata and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sheet has stable SheetID, ordered rows/columns/cells, tables, drawings/charts where applicable, filters, freeze state, view state and Revision. Reordering or renaming a sheet MUST NOT invalidate stable references that use SheetID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cells support ordinary scalar values, formulas, formatting, validation, comments/notes, hyperlinks/references and compatible Calc spreadsheet features. Grid coordinates identify a location in a sheet; they are not the sole identity mechanism for richer Data objects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal spreadsheet workflows include direct cell/formula-bar editing, fill/copy, pattern autofill, insert/delete rows and columns, row/column resize/hide/freeze, multi-range selection, find/replace, sort/filter, named ranges, tables, validation/dropdowns, conditional formatting, comments/notes, sheet management, protection where compatible and undo/redo.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Rich native cells and multiple values

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A native .9to1d cell MAY contain a typed value object rather than only one scalar. Supported native value families include scalar number/text/boolean/date/time/duration, formula, list/array, set/tags, record/key-value object, nested table, canonical 9to1 object reference, query-backed value, calculated structured value and other explicitly registered structured types.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiple values in one cell are first-class typed members, not comma-separated text. A list/set/record cell can expose member ordering, labels/keys, type validation, per-member editing, filtering/query semantics and explicit expansion into rows/columns when required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The grid MAY display a concise collapsed summary such as '3 values' or '5 related records'; selecting or expanding the cell exposes the complete structured value without altering the underlying schema.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Formula, filter, Visualise and SQL-projection semantics for structured cells MUST be defined explicitly. Unsupported operations produce typed errors or require an explicit projection/flattening step rather than silently stringifying complex values.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Nested cells, nested tables and hierarchical data

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A cell MAY own a nested table/record structure with stable nested identity and schema. Nested data is not represented as an untyped blob. Data supports drill-down, expand/collapse and focused child-table editing so hierarchical information can be represented without forcing every child structure onto a separate top-level sheet.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST distinguish nested owned data from references to separate related records. A nested child table is part of the parent value/object lifecycle; a relation/reference points to independently canonical records and MUST NOT duplicate them merely for display.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hierarchical structures MAY nest beyond one level when the schema requires it, subject to performance and usability limits. The UI MUST avoid expanding an entire deep hierarchy by default.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Multidimensional and 3D analytical data

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST support native multidimensional datasets beyond a two-dimensional row-by-column grid. A DataCube has stable CubeID, Dimensions[], Measures[], DimensionMembers/hierarchies, fact/cell storage or query definition, calculated measures, source/provenance and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A common three-dimensional example is Product × Region × Month, but the model MUST support additional dimensions such as Scenario, Currency or Channel. The UI presents manageable two-dimensional slices, pivots, comparisons and Visualise views rather than attempting to render arbitrary high-dimensional data literally.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can switch or compare dimension members, for example Month=January versus Month=February, without duplicating twelve nearly identical sheets. Multidimensional state remains canonical and may be queried through explicit relational projections/views.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DataCube projections to spreadsheet, SQL, pivot or Visualise views MUST preserve source identity and declare the projection rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Multiple views over one canonical dataset

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The same canonical dataset MAY be viewed as an ordinary spreadsheet grid, structured/nested table, relational table, pivot, hierarchy/tree, multidimensional slice, SQL relation, transformation graph or Visualise view. These are views/projections of the same data where possible, not independent copied datasets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Creating a new view MUST NOT silently duplicate source data unless the user explicitly requests a snapshot/materialised copy. Edits through a writable view update the same canonical object subject to that view's mapping and permissions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Formula engine and calculation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST preserve Calc-compatible formula semantics wherever spreadsheet compatibility is claimed. Supported families include arithmetic, logical, text, date/time, lookup/reference, statistical, financial, array/dynamic-array behaviour where supported and error-handling functions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Formula dependencies MUST be tracked so recalculation can be dependency-aware. Data MUST NOT blindly recalculate an entire large workbook after every unrelated edit when a narrower dependency recomputation is possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Formula errors remain typed and inspectable, including divide-by-zero, invalid/missing references, type mismatch, circular dependency and backend/function availability errors. Data MUST NOT collapse distinct formula failures into a generic error string.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured/native cell values may expose additional functions for contains/count/map/filter/member access and projection where explicitly supported; compatibility exports must detect when such formulas cannot be represented faithfully.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Tables, records and stable row identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured DataTable objects are first-class rather than merely formatted ranges. A DataTable has stable TableID, schema/header metadata, Records[], filters/sorts, source/query relationship, constraints and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Database-mode rows are Records with stable RecordID. Sorting, filtering or moving a visible row MUST NOT change the record's identity. Relationships and AI/Automation references target stable record/key identity rather than 'whatever is currently on row 37'.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A SQL result may materialise into or back a query-linked DataTable. Conversely, eligible DataTables can be exposed to DuckDB as relations without exporting them first.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Relational schema and field design

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any eligible DataTable may be promoted/configured as a relational table with explicit field/schema metadata. Fields support name, data type, nullability/required state, default, validation/check rules, uniqueness, generated/computed definition, key role, references and backend-specific metadata where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native field types include integer, decimal, currency, text, boolean, date/time, duration, enum/category, UUID/ID, reference, list/set, record/object, nested table and calculated/computed types. External database tables restrict available types and constraints to the connected backend's declared capability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST provide a Table Design/Schema view where field definitions, keys, required state, defaults, references and constraints can be inspected and edited directly without relying on scattered context menus.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Primary keys, candidate keys and indexes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Relational tables support single-column and composite primary keys, candidate/unique keys, generated IDs and UUID-style stable keys. Primary-key changes MUST validate duplicates, missing values and dependent references before commitment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Indexes are explicit schema metadata where the backend supports them, including primary/unique, ordinary and compound indexes. Data SHOULD explain index capability and likely purpose without automatically creating indexes everywhere.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project-local structured tables MAY use stable RecordID independently of a user-visible relational primary key; external relational projection semantics MUST define which key is authoritative for joins and persistence.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Foreign keys and sheet/table relationships

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data supports explicit relationships between tables/sheets through foreign-key/reference objects rather than requiring VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP-style formulas to express every data relationship.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Relationship types include one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many through a junction/association table. A relationship has stable RelationshipID, source table/fields, target table/key, cardinality, optionality, referential action rules and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example: Students.TutorID → Tutors.TutorID. The UI may display a friendly related value such as tutor name while storing the stable referenced key/record. Selecting such a reference can offer Open related record without duplicating the target record.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Relationship designer and ER diagrams

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST provide a visual Relationship Designer showing tables/entities, key fields and typed relationship edges with cardinality/optionality. Users can create, inspect, edit and delete relationships and can generate a junction table for a many-to-many relationship.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Relationship Designer SHOULD reuse the shared Node Graph Framework for pan/zoom/selection/grouping/connection mechanics while preserving Data-specific relationship semantics and constraints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data can generate an entity-relationship diagram showing entities/tables, fields, primary keys, foreign keys, cardinality, optionality and junction tables. The ER diagram is a Visualise/data-model representation, not a second independent schema.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Referential integrity and cascade behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Relationships may enforce referenced-key existence, restrict deletion/update, cascade delete/update or set-null according to backend/native capability. Consequential cascade operations MUST be previewable with affected-object/record impact where knowable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a relationship prevents deletion, Data MUST expose which dependency blocks the operation. It MUST NOT silently disable referential integrity or orphan dependent records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A large cascade such as deleting one parent that affects thousands of dependent records requires an explicit impact surface before execution in manual protected workflows and always in AI-originated mutation workflows.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Normalisation and denormalisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST include a Normalise tool that analyses selected relational/tabular structures for common design problems such as repeating groups, duplicated entities, non-atomic values where a relational design is desired, partial dependencies, transitive dependencies, duplicated lookup data and missing candidate keys.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normalisation assistance may propose transformations toward 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and, where appropriate for advanced users, BCNF. The proposal MUST show new tables, keys, relationships and record-migration effects before mutation. Data MUST explain assumptions rather than blindly applying a theoretical normal form to data that is intentionally hierarchical or multidimensional.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data also supports explicit Flatten/Denormalise transformations for analytics/export. Normalisation and denormalisation are controlled structured transformations, not destructive reinterpretations.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Lookups and related-record navigation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A foreign-key/reference field may display a user-friendly target field while retaining the stable referenced key/record internally. Lookup display configuration MUST NOT replace the actual stored relationship.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: One-to-many relationships can expose related-record counts or expandable related-record views. Such displays reference canonical records; they MUST NOT copy the children into a nested owned structure unless the user explicitly converts the relationship.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Data sources and connections

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data distinguishes static/imported data, linked files, project-local queryable data and external/live connections. Static/imported sources include declared CSV/TSV/JSON where supported and spreadsheet formats. Local query sources include DuckDB-accessible tables/files such as CSV/Parquet where supported. External/live connections use typed provider adapters.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DataSource and Connection objects have stable identity, provider/dialect, scope, capability metadata, source schema/version information where available and refresh state. Credentials/secrets MUST use the 9to1 credential/trust infrastructure and MUST NOT be embedded in .9to1d project content, query history or ordinary logs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connection capability negotiation defines supported transactions, snapshots/checkpoints, schema introspection, DDL/DML features, explain plans, cancellation and backup/recovery options.

heading: HEADING_3
text: SQL workspace

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST provide native SQL authoring/execution with syntax highlighting, dialect-aware parsing/validation, schema/object browser, table/column/function completion, relationship-aware join suggestions, query formatting, parameters where supported, saved queries, query history, execution timing/statistics, cancellation, paged/virtualised result sets, EXPLAIN/plan access where supported and result export/materialisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DuckDB SHOULD make local analytical querying nearly frictionless: eligible project tables and supported local files can be queried directly without requiring users to provision an external database.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SQL results can be inspected, opened in Visualise, saved as a query, materialised to a sheet/table, exported or used as downstream transformation input.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI / SQL bar switcher

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: In Data, the persistent floating input bar contains an explicit mode switcher between AI and SQL. AI mode routes natural-language requests through Dulche and typed Data actions. SQL mode treats the input as SQL and executes it natively against the explicitly selected SQL target; SQL text MUST NOT be sent to AI merely to emulate execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SQL mode MUST always display the active execution target, for example DuckDB · This Project or PostgreSQL · Production. The selected connection/database/schema scope MUST be visible enough that users cannot reasonably confuse a local analytical target with a live external target.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing the SQL execution target is explicit. Data MUST NOT silently retarget a query because another sheet, panel or connection became focused.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Native SQL execution records and results

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every execution creates a canonical SqlExecution record with stable ExecutionID, ConnectionID/target, dialect, statements, classification, ReadOnly state, initiator, start/completion state, result sets, affected objects/rows where known, recovery strategy/reference where applicable, transaction/savepoint metadata, outcome/error and audit reference.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SQL result sets preserve typed columns and support virtualised/paged browsing. Successful prior result state MUST remain available when a later execution fails unless the user explicitly replaces/discards it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Query history records target, dialect, classification, result metadata and outcome without storing secrets. SavedQuery objects are persistent editable query resources with stable identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Read-only and mutating SQL classification

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST parse/classify SQL before execution. Provably read-only statements such as ordinary SELECT/CTE SELECT, EXPLAIN and supported metadata introspection MAY execute directly subject to connection permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Potentially mutating or schema-changing SQL includes INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE and provider-specific mutation commands. Classification MUST be conservative when the dialect/parser cannot prove a statement is read-only.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multi-statement input is treated as one explicit execution plan with per-statement classification and declared atomicity/partial-execution risk.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Protected live-database SQL execution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consequential SQL against an external/live database enters the protected execution path. Before execution Data MUST identify the target, classify statements, inspect likely affected objects, use a transaction/savepoint where supported, determine preview/impact information where technically possible, establish an appropriate recoverable backup/checkpoint strategy when required, show the effect/recovery state and obtain the applicable confirmation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recovery strategy is backend-aware and may use transaction rollback, savepoint, affected-row before-image capture, table snapshot/copy, database-native snapshot, backup file/provider recovery point, schema export plus affected data or another verified recoverable mechanism. Data MUST record the strategy actually established.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If the safety contract for the requested live mutation requires rollback/backup protection and Data cannot establish it, execution MUST stop. Data MUST NOT state or imply that a backup, transaction or rollback exists when it does not.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: After execution Data verifies the actual outcome where feasible, records audit/recovery information and truthfully reports partial success/failure. It MUST NOT blindly retry consequential SQL without operation identity/idempotency or renewed confirmation where required.

heading: HEADING_3
text: DDL and dependency impact

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schema-changing SQL receives dependency-aware analysis where metadata is available. Before consequential DROP/ALTER/rename operations Data SHOULD identify dependent views, foreign keys, indexes, saved queries, linked Data views, Forms integrations, Visualisations and other known references.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DDL impact that cannot be determined reliably MUST be represented as unknown rather than assumed safe.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Manual SQL versus AI-proposed SQL

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Direct SQL typed and executed by the user remains native SQL interaction and is not treated as an AI mutation merely because it is entered in the shared bar. Read-only SQL should not acquire unnecessary AI-style approval friction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI may draft, explain, optimise, fix or generate SQL, but an AI-proposed consequential mutation MUST NOT bypass Data's per-action approval rules. For external database changes, the proposed SQL and target/impact/recovery information MUST be inspectable before approved execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If AI decides SQL is the best implementation of a Data task, the generated SQL remains visible/inspectable and execution occurs through the same SQL safety pipeline rather than an opaque hidden database mutation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Visual query builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data SHOULD provide a no-code/low-code visual query builder for select fields, filters, joins, groups, aggregations, ordering and limits. It produces an inspectable structured query/SQL representation rather than a second incompatible query engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Declared relationships SHOULD inform join suggestions. Users can switch to or edit equivalent SQL where the backend/query can be represented faithfully.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Transformation pipelines

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST support reusable structured TransformPipeline objects for data cleaning and reshaping. Core step families include type conversion, rename, split/merge, text cleaning, filter, replace, derive column, group/aggregate, sort, join, union/append, pivot/unpivot, deduplicate, fill missing values, date parsing and supported custom expressions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pipelines retain ordered step identity, source mappings, schema expectations, outputs, provenance and Revision. They are rerunnable against refreshed source data so recurring imports do not require repeating manual cleanup.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For complex branching/dependencies, Data provides an advanced transformation graph using the shared Node Graph Framework. Nodes may represent Source → Select → Filter → Join → Derive → Group → Output and other registered transforms. The step-list/table workflow and graph are representations of the same canonical pipeline where compatible.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Refresh and stale-data semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Linked/query-backed resources record source identity, last successful refresh, current source version/revision where knowable, stale state, refresh policy and downstream dependencies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Refresh failure MUST NOT erase the previous valid result. The previous result remains available with explicit stale/error state unless the user explicitly discards it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automatic refresh is permission- and resource-aware; external consequential side effects MUST NOT be hidden inside a data-refresh operation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Visualise mode from the persistent eye icon

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent floating toolbar's eye icon exposes alternative views of the current artifact. In Data, Eye → Visualise opens an interactive graphical analytical representation over selected ranges/tables, the active sheet or another explicit Data source without modifying the underlying workbook.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visualise is distinct from inserting a chart into a sheet. Inserted charts are persistent workbook objects. Visualise is an adaptive analytical lens over canonical data. A useful Visualise configuration MAY be saved as a DataVisualisation, embedded elsewhere or converted to a persistent chart/view where the representation supports it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening/changing Visualise MUST NOT require restructuring or duplicating the underlying spreadsheet.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Adaptive visualisation inference

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visualise inspects headers, types, ordering, table orientation and semantic structure to determine suitable graphical representations. It considers numeric versus categorical fields, dates/time, ordinal/ranked fields, probabilities, names/entities, groups, repeated measurements, paired numeric variables, distributions and declared dimensions/relationships.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data SHOULD rank sensible visualisations for the current structure instead of presenting every visual type as equally appropriate. Examples include category+value → bar/column; two numeric variables → scatter; numeric distribution → histogram/box/stem-and-leaf; time-indexed values → line/time-series; ranked outcomes → tier list; probability/distribution data → probability cloud; paired/ordered comparisons → alignment chart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automatic inference is always inspectable and overrideable. The user can explicitly map roles such as X/category, Y/value, series, group, label, size, rank/tier criterion, time, probability and comparison source.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Visualisation catalogue and specialised views

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visualise supports at least bar/column, stacked/grouped bar, line, area, scatter, histogram, box-and-whisker, stem-and-leaf, probability/distribution cloud, tier list, alignment chart, heatmap, pie/donut where mathematically appropriate, density/distribution views where supported and other registered visualisations whose input requirements match the selected data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A tier-list view can map entity, ranking field, tier boundaries/order, secondary labels and optional group. Tiers may derive from explicit categories or user-defined numeric/rule boundaries. The tier rules MUST be visible/editable rather than inferred invisibly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An alignment chart represents comparable ordered positions/values from two or more sources/groups with explicit mappings. Specialised views MUST define their required field roles and accessible non-visual representation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Multi-sheet and multi-source Visualise comparison

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Within Visualise, users can Add data → Sheet and add ranges/tables from additional sheets in the same workbook for comparison. Each source retains WorkbookID, SheetID and Range/TableID identity rather than copying values into an anonymous temporary dataset.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data can suggest field mappings across differently arranged sheets using headers, types and semantic similarity, but users can inspect/change mappings. Example: 2025 Results.Score ↔ 2026 Results.Score even when the physical column locations differ.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Saved visualisations refresh from their live canonical sources when those sources change, subject to refresh/version rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Visualise interaction, saved objects and cross-app reuse

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visualise views support appropriate selection, filtering, series isolation, sorting, zoom/pan where useful, exact-value inspection, mapping changes and type changes without losing source identity. Selecting a graphical mark SHOULD map back to the corresponding row/cell/record and offer Go to source where possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DataVisualisation has stable VisualisationID, Type, Sources[], FieldMappings, Filters, Grouping, Sorting, VisualSettings, ComparisonConfiguration, interaction/presentation state where appropriate and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write, Present, Home and other authorised surfaces can embed/reference saved Data visualisations as semantic/live objects rather than requiring screenshots, preserving accessibility labels, source relationships and refresh semantics.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Charts, pivots and analytical sheets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data includes persistent chart objects bound to ranges/tables/query results with editable series, axes, labels, legends, titles, source mappings and formatting. Common analytical chart families are available through the donor/shared chart engine and update as source data changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PivotModel/PivotTable objects support row, column, value and filter fields, aggregation choice, sorting, grouping where supported and refresh. Pivot configuration/source identity remains canonical rather than being pasted as static values.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MAY provide analytical/report sheets that compose tables, pivots, charts, metrics and controls. Persistent cross-9to1 dashboards remain owned by Home; Home can reference selected Data visualisations/metrics instead of Data becoming a duplicate dashboard product.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Cross-app conversion into Data

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST support AI-assisted conversion of structured content from other 9to1 surfaces into native Data structures. The preferred source is the source app's canonical semantic objects, not screenshots/OCR, whenever typed structure is available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Import/Convert to Data can accept compatible Write, Present, Canvas, Boards, Forms, Spaces and other registered 9to1 artifacts. Dulche analyses repeated structures, fields, lists, tables, objects, connections and metadata and proposes an explicit target schema/mapping before materialisation when the conversion is not deterministic.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conversion MUST preserve source provenance and provide Go to source where source identity is retained.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Write, Present, Boards and Canvas conversion semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write → Data can recognise native tables, headings, repeated document sections, lists, key/value blocks, dates, people and canonical references. Repeated sections may become records; list fields can become true multi-value cells rather than comma-separated text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Present → Data can map one slide to one record, repeated cards/objects to rows, native tables to Data tables, chart data to result/source tables where available, speaker notes to optional fields and slide metadata to columns. Repeated layout semantics SHOULD inform schema inference.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards → Data can map cards to records, columns/groups to categorical fields, labels to multi-value fields, assignees to person references, due dates to dates, checklists to nested tables/lists and linked objects to canonical references.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas → Data can map nodes/cards to records, groups/frames to categories and connections to a relationship/edge table. Connected diagrams SHOULD be represented as appropriate node and edge datasets rather than flattened nonsensically into one sheet.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Snapshot versus linked conversion

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app conversion supports Snapshot and Linked modes. Snapshot creates independent Data content from the current source state. Linked conversion retains canonical source/object references and a reusable mapping so refresh can import subsequent changes subject to conflict rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Linked mappings record source app/artifact/object IDs, conversion rules, last successful refresh, source revision where available, local-edit state and ambiguity/confidence metadata for AI-inferred mappings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Refreshing a linked conversion MUST NOT silently discard incompatible local edits; conflicts or schema drift are surfaced.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Data profiling and quality inspection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For selected ranges/tables Data SHOULD provide profiling including row/record count, null/blank count, unique count, inferred/declared type, min/max, mean/median where suitable, value distribution, duplicate detection and invalid/outlier indicators where statistically appropriate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Profiling distinguishes measured facts from heuristic anomaly suggestions. It MUST NOT label an observation erroneous merely because it is statistically unusual.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files and source identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files remains authoritative for source/export file identity, move/rename/delete/recover/share and provider/cloud hydration. Linked data sources reference stable FileID/AssetID identity rather than absolute paths.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Imported file workflows distinguish embedded/copy, linked-source and query-backed semantics. Users can inspect whether changes to the source will affect Data and whether Data can refresh/write back.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Moving or renaming an underlying source in Files MUST NOT break a stable link when the provider identity remains valid.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Import/export and compatibility boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data supports native .9to1d plus declared XLSX, ODS, CSV and TSV import/export and other explicitly supported data formats. LibreOffice Calc compatibility paths are used for representative spreadsheet interoperability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native .9to1d features such as nested tables, list-valued cells, records/objects, canonical cross-app references, multidimensional cubes, rich relationships and linked-source mappings may exceed XLSX/ODS capability. Export MUST detect unsupported semantics and present explicit transformations such as expand list to rows/columns, stringify, move nested table to another sheet, flatten hierarchy or export a cube slice/pivot.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST NOT silently flatten rich native content and claim a lossless round-trip. Compatibility warnings identify structures/formulas/objects that will be flattened, materialised or omitted before export.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Forms and other 9to1 integrations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data can create a Forms artifact from a relational/table schema rather than duplicating a full form builder. Field type, required state, enum/reference options and validation can seed the generated form. Submitted responses write through typed Data APIs subject to permissions and constraints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write/Present can embed live Data tables/charts/Visualisations; Forms responses can be analysed/queryable in Data; Automations can refresh/import/export/run permitted queries; Spaces can reference datasets/results; Home can surface selected metrics/visualisations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Database/table record editing MAY provide a focused single-record editor, but general form-design capability remains owned by Forms.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI context, provenance and analysis

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Data context includes ProjectID, WorkbookID/SheetID, selected range/table/RecordIDs, formula dependencies, QueryID/result set, relational schema/relationships, DataCube dimensions/measures, chart/pivot/Visualisation, TransformPipeline, ConnectionID/target capability and project/source revisions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI analysis can explain trends, propose transformations, create charts/visualisations, repair formulas, design relational schema and draft SQL using typed context. Where a request mutates canonical Data state, the explicit Data mutation approval contract applies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to inspect value provenance where available: literal/formula/query/transform origin, source cell/table/query/pipeline, refresh status, external connection/source and whether AI modified the value/object.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI mutation approval and live-database protection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data inherits the shared floating AI-bar Read-only / Write-mode contract but deliberately narrows Write mode: every AI-requested Data mutation requires explicit approval for that specific action. Switching the AI bar to Write mode, trusting the Agent/app or previously approving another Data action MUST NOT authorise subsequent Data mutations automatically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For workbook/local analytical changes, the approval surface MUST show the proposed operation/change set sufficiently for the user to understand what will change. For a connected live database, Data additionally shows meaningful SQL/action preview, target, affected objects/rows where knowable, schema/dependency/external-side-effect impact and the established recovery mechanism.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If required live-database rollback/backup protection cannot be established, the mutation MUST stop rather than falsely claim rollback protection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: After an approved live-database mutation, Data MUST verify the actual outcome where feasible, record the canonical Action Graph/audit result and preserve recovery references. Partial failure MUST be reported truthfully and MUST NOT trigger blind consequential retries.

heading: HEADING_3

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Data.SetFormula(sheetID, cellOrRange, formula);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Data.CreateTable(sheetID, rangeOrSchema, config?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1.Data.SetTableSchema(tableID, schemaPatch);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
