heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transformation and relationship graph mutation uses 9to1.NodeGraph.* when the shared Node Graph Framework is canonical. Files, credential and other shared-domain operations use their owning shared API namespaces when canonical.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automation and integration events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations, Spaces, Dulche and other authorised clients can use the exhaustive Data action catalogue subject to Data's mutation approval/security rules. Long imports, refreshes, profiling, transforms, SQL jobs and exports expose stable progress, cancellation and typed result/error state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data emits meaningful typed events such as project/revision changed, source stale/refreshed, schema changed, relationship changed, query completed/failed, SQL mutation completed/rolled back/partially failed, Visualisation changed and export completed. It MUST NOT flood Automations with raw per-cell hover/selection events.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Collaboration and revision conflicts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Workbook/sheet/table/record/formula/schema/relationship/query/pipeline/cube/Visualisation mutations are revision-aware. Independent edits MAY merge when safe; incompatible concurrent mutations to the same canonical object/property surface conflict rather than blind last-write-wins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Running query/refresh/transform/export jobs are pinned to the intended source/project revisions where applicable. Results record which inputs/revisions produced them.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST be keyboard-operable for spreadsheet navigation/editing, formula entry, tables, relational design, SQL authoring/execution, query results, Visualise controls, charts/pivots and transformation/relationship graphs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Screen-reader users can inspect cell coordinates and semantic type/value, structured-cell members, table/field/key identity, relationships, query target/result columns, chart/Visualise equivalents, refresh state and errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every graphical Visualise representation MUST expose a meaningful non-visual equivalent: for example scatter points as an accessible point table, box plots as quartile/statistical values, tier lists as ordered tier/entity lists, and stem-and-leaf as structured textual data. State MUST NOT rely on colour alone.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and large-data behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spreadsheet UI MUST virtualise cells/rows/columns so only required visible/nearby content is rendered. Large imports/query results use streaming/paging/chunking and background jobs rather than freezing the UI or loading every result row into presentation memory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Formula calculation is dependency-aware; chart/pivot/Visualise recomputation and profiling run incrementally/background where appropriate. Large source files/tables/cubes use bounded caches and query pushdown/column pruning where the backend supports it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI context MUST be scoped semantically to relevant ranges, tables, schema, query results or sampled/profiled context. Data MUST NOT dump an entire million-row workbook into a model prompt simply because the project is open.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project/workbook saves and schema changes MUST be crash-safe. Failed imports, refreshes, transforms, SQL executions, exports or Visualise calculations MUST leave previous valid canonical data intact unless the user explicitly accepted a destructive operation whose partial effects are truthfully reported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured failures include ProjectNotFound, WorkbookNotFound, SheetNotFound, TableNotFound, RecordNotFound, InvalidFormula, CircularReference, SchemaViolation, ConstraintViolation, RelationshipViolation, ConnectionUnavailable, AuthenticationRequired, SqlParseError, SqlExecutionFailed, MutationProtectionUnavailable, BackupFailed, RollbackFailed, PartialCommit, RefreshFailed, TransformFailed, VisualisationIncompatible, ExportCompatibilityLoss, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable plus provider/backend errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data MUST distinguish 'rollback attempted' from 'rollback succeeded'. Recovery/audit metadata remains inspectable after failure.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Data project/workbook/schema/query/pipeline/cube/Visualisation model while capability-negotiating local DuckDB execution, LibreOffice-derived compatibility components, external database drivers, file access and hardware/resource differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A platform that cannot execute a particular local/provider capability MUST expose CapabilityUnavailable or route to an explicitly configured supported service; it MUST NOT silently substitute incompatible semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Data follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract rather than launching an incompatible private runtime.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A representative workbook supports ordinary cell/formula editing, tables, formatting, sorting/filtering and save/reopen while preserving workbook/sheet/object identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative XLSX and ODS files round-trip through the declared LibreOffice-derived compatibility path within the documented compatibility contract, and the required donor source/version is present/recorded rather than replaced by a miniature spreadsheet clone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Formula dependency recalculation updates affected dependants without requiring whole-workbook recomputation for unrelated edits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: List-valued and record-valued cells preserve multiple typed members across save/reopen and can be explicitly expanded/projected without silent stringification.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A nested table retains stable nested identity/schema and remains distinct from a relationship to independently canonical records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A DataCube with at least three dimensions can be sliced/compared without duplicating separate sheets for every dimension member.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A relational table enforces a single or composite primary key and reports duplicate/missing-key violations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A declared foreign-key relationship enforces configured referential integrity; one-to-many and many-to-many/junction-table modelling persist correctly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Relationship Designer/ER view displays primary/foreign keys and cardinality from the canonical schema rather than maintaining duplicate diagram-only relationships.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normalise proposes a decomposition with keys/relationships and previews migration before mutation; Flatten/Denormalise remains an explicit separate transformation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DuckDB can query eligible project tables/local files and materialise a result into a native Data table without export/import duplication.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SQL mode in the persistent bar visibly shows the active target and executes native SQL against that target rather than routing commands through AI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A read-only SQL query produces a typed virtualised result set with execution metadata and preserves prior valid results after a later failed query.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A consequential external/live SQL mutation is classified, exposes target/impact, establishes the required verified recovery strategy, obtains the applicable confirmation, executes through transaction/checkpoint protection where supported and records the actual outcome.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data blocks a protected live mutation when required backup/rollback protection cannot be established and never falsely claims recovery succeeded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multi-statement SQL reports transactional atomicity or partial-execution risk and truthfully identifies any partial commit after failure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated consequential SQL is visible/inspectable and cannot bypass per-action Data mutation approval.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A transformation pipeline can clean/join/derive data, rerun after source refresh and preserve prior valid output if refresh fails.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Eye → Visualise opens an adaptive view without modifying the workbook, recommends compatible representations from source semantics and permits manual field-role overrides.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visualise supports representative specialised views including box plot, stem-and-leaf, probability/distribution cloud, tier list, scatter and alignment-style comparison with accessible non-visual equivalents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A saved DataVisualisation can combine ranges/tables from at least two workbook sheets with explicit field mapping and continues to reference live canonical sources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selecting a supported Visualise mark can identify/go to its source record/cell where mapping is one-to-one.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A linked conversion from at least one structured Write/Present/Boards/Canvas artifact preserves source provenance and refresh mapping; a snapshot conversion remains independent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards-style labels/checklists or equivalent source structures can become true multi-value/nested Data fields rather than comma-separated flattening.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Charts/pivots persist structured source configuration and refresh when source data changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native rich features that cannot fit XLSX/ODS trigger explicit export-compatibility choices rather than silent flattening/lossless claims.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large sheets/query results remain responsive through UI virtualisation, paging/streaming and bounded caches.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI context is scoped to relevant Data objects and does not serialise the entire large project by default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard/screen-reader users can operate spreadsheet, SQL, relational, Visualise and graph workflows without pointer-only dependencies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Data model while capability-negotiating local/provider execution differences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Data follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Forms

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and runtime principle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Forms is the native CUI structured form, assessment, data-entry and lightweight interactive-application builder. It covers surveys, questionnaires, applications, registrations, feedback, quizzes/tests, database-entry interfaces, conversational interviews, live multiplayer quizzes and custom event-driven experiences while keeping simple forms fast to create.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical result is a structured FormProject and runtime configuration, not a collection of rendered pages. Fields, pages, themes, logic, marking rules, timers, multiplayer state, Data bindings and custom mode behaviour remain typed editable state. The same semantic model is used by the builder, published runtime, AI, Automations and APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms MUST support simple no-code creation without exposing advanced complexity by default, but the product ceiling MUST NOT be limited to the capabilities of conventional survey builders. Advanced logic, layout, assessment and multiplayer features use the same underlying canonical objects rather than separate incompatible modes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical project model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: FormProject has stable FormID, ModeDefinition, FormVersions[], Pages[], Fields[], Components[], Theme, LogicGraphID where used, DataBindings[], MarkingScheme, QuestionBanks[], PublishingSettings, AccessPolicy, RuntimeSettings, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page/Section objects have stable PageID, ordered child components/fields, layout configuration, visibility rules and Revision. Field has stable FieldID, FieldType, label/help/content, response schema, required/validation state, appearance/layout state, marking configuration where applicable, Data binding where applicable and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Choice options, table columns, rubric criteria, marking rules, grading schemes, branching rules and reusable components have stable identity when independently addressable. Published runtime and stored responses reference IDs, not question text or screen coordinates.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Builder workspace and preview

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The default builder provides a structured page/canvas editor, field/component palette, contextual Inspector, logic/mode controls, theme/layout controls and Preview/Test. Common tasks MUST NOT require the node editor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preview supports desktop, tablet, mobile and narrow embedded layouts. Interactive preview can simulate answers, validate branching, exercise marking rules, test Data bindings with safe test context and identify unreachable pages/conditions before publication.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Builder and preview operate on the same canonical FormProject. Preview MUST NOT create a separate approximation that can diverge from published behaviour.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Core field and component types

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms supports at least short text, long text, number/decimal/currency, email, phone, date/time, duration, single choice, multiple choice, dropdown, checkbox/set, rating/scale, ranking, matrix/grid, file upload, signature where supported, person/reference picker, Data foreign-key lookup, rich text/content, image/media block, calculated/read-only field, hidden/system field, mathematical response, graph response, repeating group and table input.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Field types define canonical answer schemas rather than coercing everything to text. Validation, Data binding and marking consume the typed answer model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom/reusable Form Components may contain multiple child fields and layout/logic, for example Address, Person details, Emergency contact or Rating + comment. Reusing a component preserves structured child identity rather than pasting an opaque widget.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Table input and repeating structured responses

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms MUST provide a real TableInput field, not merely a multiple-choice grid. TableInput defines typed columns, optional fixed rows, respondent-added rows, minimum/maximum row count, required columns, per-cell/row validation, calculated columns, dropdown/reference columns, duplicate rules and Data bindings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A table input may write multiple related Data records rather than serialising an entire table into one string. For example an expense report may submit one parent Report record plus one related Expense record per entered row.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Repeating groups provide similar semantics for card/form layouts where each repeated item has multiple fields. TableInput and repeating groups preserve stable row/item identity within a response.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Native modes: Form, Test and Quiz

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms ships at least three first-party runtime presets built on the common Forms state/marking engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Form mode accepts any valid answer according to field validation. It is intended for surveys, applications, registration, feedback and general data collection. Correct/incorrect semantics are absent unless a field explicitly defines assessment behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Test mode supports correct/incorrect/partial answers, points, marking rules, grading schemes and result release. Respondents normally complete the assessment as a whole and receive score/grade/feedback according to configured release policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quiz mode uses the same assessment engine but supports question-by-question evaluation/progression. After each answer the runtime may show correct/incorrect/partial state, explanation/feedback and then advance according to mode settings. A final score/grade can still be produced.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mode semantics MUST be expressed through the common runtime/state system rather than three independent engines.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Custom modes and state-machine runtime

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Advanced authors can create Custom Modes using the shared node/state system. A custom mode can define start state, question/component selection, timers, score variables, lives/attempts, branching, dialogue turns, participant state, completion conditions and result calculation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples include 'answer three questions correctly as quickly as possible', adaptive difficulty, limited-lives games, interview/conversation flows, staged applications and game-show experiences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Built-in Form/Test/Quiz behaviour SHOULD be representable as first-party presets over the same runtime concepts so custom modes do not fork core response, Data, accessibility or publishing infrastructure.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Marking engine and multiple accepted answers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assessable fields support one or more typed MarkingRules. Rules can resolve Correct, Incorrect, Partial, NeedsReview or another configured outcome and award points according to explicit scoring policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text questions can define multiple accepted correct answers. Normalised matching can optionally ignore case, trim/collapse whitespace, normalise Unicode and ignore selected punctuation/diacritics according to author settings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example: a question asking for the name of the central processor may accept 'CPU' and 'Central Processing Unit' as equivalent accepted answers without requiring AI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rules can be combined with explicit boolean logic such as AcceptedAnswer(A) OR AcceptedAnswer(B) OR Regex(C), and more complex marking flows can use the node editor where appropriate.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Regex validation and marking

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Regex is supported for both response validation and marking. Authors can configure pattern, flags, explanatory label and accepted/rejected test cases.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The builder MUST include a regex tester with live example inputs, invalid-pattern diagnostics and clear indication of full-match versus partial-match semantics. Forms MUST NOT execute unbounded or unsafe regex behaviour in a way that can freeze the runtime; implementations use bounded/safe regex execution appropriate to the platform.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Regex rules remain inspectable structured MarkingRule/ValidationRule objects and can be combined with other deterministic rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI, human and hybrid marking

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Question-level AI marking can be enabled explicitly. AI marking uses a structured rubric with expected concepts/criteria, maximum points, optional sample correct/partial/incorrect answers, required/forbidden concepts and feedback policy. The result records awarded points, matched/missed criteria, feedback and uncertainty/review state rather than only an opaque prose verdict.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Marking mode may be deterministic automatic, mathematical/symbolic, AI, manual human or hybrid. Hybrid workflows can let deterministic rules resolve obvious answers, invoke AI for unresolved open responses and optionally require human moderation before release.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A useful default marking pipeline is deterministic accepted-answer/regex rules, then mathematical equivalence where applicable, then AI rubric evaluation only when configured and still unresolved. Authors can override this ordering.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: QuestionResult records marking provenance so consequential results can show whether a mark came from exact rule, regex, symbolic maths evaluator, AI, human marker or combination.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Partial credit, grading and feedback

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assessments support points, weighted questions, partial credit, criterion/rubric scoring, optional penalties where explicitly configured and section/category subtotals.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GradingScheme maps score/percentage or configured measures to grade/band/pass state. Boundaries are structured editable rules rather than hard-coded labels.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Feedback can be configured per answer/rule/rubric criterion and released immediately, after a question, after submission, after manual review or at a configured release state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: LaTeX and visual mathematics editor

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms MUST provide first-class mathematical authoring. MathExpression uses LaTeX-compatible canonical representation but can be edited through a visual equation editor so authors/respondents are not required to know LaTeX.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The editor supports fractions, powers/indices, roots, logarithms, trigonometry, calculus notation, sigma/product notation, vectors, matrices, inequalities, sets, piecewise expressions, probability/statistics notation, Greek/special symbols and aligned expressions where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual and LaTeX modes edit the same expression and remain bidirectionally synchronised. Invalid LaTeX produces an explicit recoverable editing error rather than losing the prior valid expression.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MathAnswer types include numeric, algebraic expression, equation, inequality, interval, coordinate, vector, matrix, set, multiple expressions and free-working response. Numeric rules can configure exact value, absolute/percentage tolerance, significant figures, decimal places and units where applicable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Graph plotter and graph-response questions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms MUST include a native mathematical graph plotter/editor for quiz/test content. Authors can define functions, equations, inequalities, points, coordinate tables, regions, axes, grid/domain/range configuration and other supported 2D graph primitives.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GraphResponse questions can ask respondents to place points, draw a line/curve, submit coordinates, enter a function/equation for plotting, identify a region or manipulate an existing graph according to declared tools.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph answers remain structured GraphDefinition/GraphResponse data, not screenshots. Marking compares the submitted mathematical/graph representation using configured tolerances/equivalence rules where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MathExpression, GraphDefinition and related primitives SHOULD be reusable shared mathematical objects across Forms, Write, Present and other 9to1 surfaces rather than privately reinvented.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Question banks, randomisation, attempts and timing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms supports reusable QuestionBank objects with tags, subject/topic, difficulty, points, marking rules and other metadata. A Test/Quiz can select deterministic or random subsets subject to constraints such as minimum questions from specified categories.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Question/choice order can be randomised per participant where configured. Attempts can be unlimited, fixed-count, one-only or custom-mode controlled. Retry policies may target only incorrect questions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Timing supports whole-assessment timers, per-question/per-section timers, countdowns, time bonus/penalty, late-submission policy and custom timer variables. Server-authoritative timing is required for multiplayer and integrity-sensitive modes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Forms and Data bidirectional integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms and Data are bidirectionally integrated through typed bindings. A form can store responses in a Data spreadsheet/table, relational table or permitted database-backed Data target while preserving field types, references, nested/repeating structures and provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A FormField may bind to a stable Data TableID/FieldID rather than a physical spreadsheet column letter. Relational lookups can write foreign-key references; repeating/table input can create child/junction records where the mapping defines that behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data may also define or evolve Form fields. Adding a compatible field to a bound Data schema can propose or automatically add an appropriate Forms field according to configured synchronisation policy. Forms changes may similarly propose/add Data fields where the binding policy permits.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Data schema synchronisation policies

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each Forms↔Data binding explicitly configures directionality: Forms→Data, Data→Forms or bidirectional. It also defines synchronisation mode such as Manual, Suggest changes, Automatic compatible changes or Strict schema binding.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Schema synchronisation MUST be migration-aware. Deleting or changing a Data field that has historical Form responses MUST NOT delete or reinterpret historical answers silently. Forms can archive/detach a field, migrate compatible data or surface a conflict according to policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Type changes, key/reference changes and destructive schema operations require preview of effect on field configuration, published versions, stored responses and dependent logic before commitment.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Full node editor and logic graph

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms MUST expose the full shared 9to1 Node Graph Framework for advanced behaviour. Simple conditional logic remains available through friendly controls, but advanced authors can open the underlying Form Logic graph without creating a second incompatible rules engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Logic graphs have stable GraphID/NodeID/PortID identity, typed connections, grouping/comments, copy/paste/duplicate, undo/redo, validation, Draft/Published revision semantics and Dulche graph mutation through 9to1.NodeGraph.*.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph validation MUST detect incompatible ports, unreachable states where knowable, missing targets, cycles that would create uncontrolled update loops and client/server trust-boundary violations.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Form events, conditions and actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Minimum Form events include FormOpened, PageEntered, FieldChanged/AnswerChanged, ValidationPassed/Failed, PageSubmitted, ResponseSaved, FormSubmitted, AnswerMarked, QuizGraded and runtime/session events defined below.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conditions include equality/inequality, contains, numeric comparison/range, answered/unanswered, selected option, validation result, calculated value, Data lookup result, participant/user/session state and other registered typed predicates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Actions include show/hide, enable/disable, required/optional, set/calculated value, jump to page/state, show message/content, add/remove repeating item, populate options, perform permitted Data lookup, trigger authorised Automation, mark/score, submit/block submission and custom-mode state transitions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Security-critical validation and consequential actions MUST execute or be verified server-side; client-side visibility logic alone cannot be treated as an access-control or integrity boundary.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Appearance, theme and layout system

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms MUST provide substantially deeper appearance control than conventional survey builders while preserving responsive accessibility. FormTheme includes typography, palette, backgrounds, surfaces/cards, borders, corner radius, shadows, spacing, content width, field/input appearance, buttons, progress/navigation, focus/error/success states and reusable design tokens.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pages use a responsive structured layout system supporting full-width and multi-column arrangements, grid, grouped cards/panels, inline/stacked labels, compact/dense modes, hero/header regions, dividers and rich content. Layout is responsive rather than relying on arbitrary absolute positioning for ordinary form design.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Authors can configure logos, organisation branding, custom header/footer, background artwork and hosted-form identity. Custom domains/advanced branding integrate with the wider 9to1 web platform where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Greater design freedom MUST NOT allow the form author to bypass minimum accessibility constraints such as semantic labels, focus order, contrast, tap targets or colour-independent state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Reusable components and templates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users/organisations can save reusable Form Components and FormTheme presets. Reusable components preserve structured child fields, validation, layout and optional logic while allowing controlled instance overrides.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Templates such as signup, application, event registration, feedback, quiz/test, database record editor and survey are starting configurations that produce ordinary editable FormProject state rather than locked special modes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Publishing, versions and response compatibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms has explicit Draft and Published runtime versions. Editing Draft MUST NOT mutate the currently published experience until the author publishes/activates the new version according to policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every response records FormID and the FormVersionID/schema revision answered. Historical responses remain interpretable even when fields are renamed, moved, hidden or removed in later versions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Publishing states include at least Draft, Published/Accepting responses and Closed, with optional scheduled open/close where the platform supports it. Authors configure whether in-progress respondents remain on the version they started or migrate only through explicitly safe rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Response model, save/resume and editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Response has stable ResponseID, FormID/FormVersionID, responder/participant identity where known, Answer records keyed by FieldID, started/submitted timestamps, attachments, state, score/marking result where applicable, Data-write status and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms supports configurable draft/save-and-resume, edit-after-submit policy, response limits, duplicate-prevention policy and confirmation/next-action behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Historical answer values MUST remain attached to the field/version schema that produced them rather than being reinterpreted based only on the latest field label.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Multiplayer live-session runtime

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms supports server-authoritative MultiplayerSession objects layered onto Form/Test/Quiz/custom modes. A LiveSession has stable SessionID, FormVersionID, hosts, Participants[], Teams[], current state/round/question, Scoreboard, timers, elimination/lives state, join policy, spectator policy, moderation state, event sequence and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typical first-party session states include Lobby, Starting, QuestionActive, Marking/Reveal, RoundTransition and Finished, but custom modes may define richer state machines using the same runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiplayer does not duplicate questions or marking rules. A Test/Quiz can be hosted live using its existing canonical content.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Joining, teams and host control

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live sessions support short join codes, QR/share links, CAKE ID authenticated joining, guest nickname joining where allowed, private/invite-only sessions, organisation/class restrictions, maximum participants, late-join rules and optional spectators.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sessions support individual and team play. Team scoring/answer semantics may use one nominated answer, shared answer, majority vote, fastest member, average/aggregate scoring or custom graph-defined policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Host controls include participant/connection state, start/pause/advance, skip, extend time, lock joining, reveal answer, invalidate question/round, adjust score with audit history, eliminate/reinstate, remove participant, moderate names/content and end session.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Multiplayer quiz, knockout and game-show modes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A standard Multiplayer Quiz can synchronise question reveal, answer window, marking, reveal/feedback and scoreboard progression across participants.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Knockout mode supports policies such as incorrect/timeout eliminates, configurable lives, eliminate bottom N or bottom percentage, fastest N advance, cumulative threshold, team elimination, re-entry/resurrection rounds and sudden-death rules. These are structured mode parameters or logic-graph behaviour rather than hard-coded one-off UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Buzzer rounds support server-authoritative first-buzz ordering, answering rights, lockout/pass behaviour and host/human judging where configured.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Question presentation can be on participant devices, host/projector only, both, participant-specific or team-specific according to mode.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Conversational and interview modes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom modes may create turn-based conversational experiences such as job interviews, oral quizzes, panel discussions or AI quizmaster sessions. The interviewer can be an authorised human or configured AI agent; next questions may depend on prior structured answers/context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conversational responses are stored as structured turn/question/answer records with speaker/participant identity and optional rubric results, not only one giant transcript.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI interviewers remain subject to configured scope, marking/review policy and disclosure requirements; human takeover/co-hosting can be supported where realtime collaboration infrastructure permits.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Multiplayer timing, reconnection and fairness

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiplayer timing and state transitions are server-authoritative. Clients MUST NOT decide whether an answer arrived before timeout, who buzzed first, the final score or whether a participant is eliminated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Session runtime records authoritative question-open/close and submission timestamps. Speed scoring MUST use a documented server-side policy and SHOULD avoid pretending millisecond differences are perfectly fair when network latency materially affects participants.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reconnect preserves participant identity, submitted answers and session state according to configured reconnect policy. A short connection loss MUST NOT silently erase prior responses or create a duplicate participant.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Anti-cheat and assessment integrity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms MUST provide configurable anti-cheat/integrity controls, with stronger options available for Tests and live assessments while making clear that browser-based controls reduce opportunities but cannot guarantee that cheating is impossible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core controls include authenticated participant requirements, one active attempt/session per identity where configured, server-authoritative timers and answer locks, randomised question/choice order, question-bank variants, delayed answer/reveal policies, duplicate-session/device anomaly detection where permitted, copy/paste/context-menu restrictions where appropriate, visibility/focus-change logging or warnings where platform policy permits, per-question navigation restrictions, locked previous answers, and host moderation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assessment authors can configure whether focus/tab changes are ignored, logged, warned or treated as an integrity event. Such signals MUST NOT automatically prove misconduct; they are contextual evidence and may be unreliable on some platforms.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: High-integrity deployments MAY integrate approved kiosk/lockdown or proctoring capabilities where separately configured, supported, legally permitted and appropriately disclosed/consented. Forms MUST NOT secretly access camera, microphone, screen or other sensitive capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Server-side validation, marking, attempt state and scoring MUST not trust client-supplied authority. Client code cannot award itself points, extend its own timer, resurrect an eliminated participant or reveal protected answers merely by modifying local state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Question/answer payload delivery SHOULD minimise unnecessary early exposure: the runtime need not send future protected questions/correct answers to clients before they are authorised to see them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Anti-cheat events and moderation actions are auditable, privacy-scoped and retained according to configured policy.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Live scoring and AI/human judging

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiplayer scoring can consider correctness, partial credit, time, streak/difficulty or custom variables only when explicitly configured. ScorePolicy is structured and inspectable; speed bonuses are optional.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-marked questions in live modes define how asynchronous model latency interacts with progression: wait for all marks, score later, exclude AI-marked items from speed bonuses, or require human review. The runtime MUST NOT silently disadvantage a participant because one model call completed more slowly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Human judges/hosts can accept/reject or adjust uncertain responses with an audit trail where the mode allows it.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Scoreboards and participant views

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scoreboards may show full live ranking, top N, team standings, personal position only, anonymous ranking, knockout/bracket/lives state or remain hidden until the end.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accessibility/fairness settings can disable speed-based ranking or reduce competitive disclosure. Participant views show only state permitted by the session policy.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Privacy, abuse prevention and public access

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public forms support explicit access policy, rate limiting, abuse/spam controls, duplicate-response controls and configured CAPTCHA/challenge integration where appropriate. File uploads enforce type/size/count and malware/scanning policy through the shared storage/security layer where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms supports anonymous, link-based, CAKE ID authenticated and organisation-restricted access according to configuration. Responder identity requirements and privacy/consent text must be explicit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sensitive answer data is permission-scoped. Submission events MUST NOT leak response content to Automations, hosts or integrations that lack the required permission.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI-assisted authoring, design and logic

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche can create forms from natural-language requirements or convert supported structured Write/Present/Data/Boards/Canvas content into Form fields/pages using canonical source objects rather than screenshots when possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI can propose or modify fields, layout, themes, pages, branching, marking rubrics, question banks and logic graphs through typed Forms/NodeGraph actions. AI edits preserve FieldIDs/Data bindings where the user's intent is to reorganise rather than replace them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples include 'turn this Write document into a survey', 'make this look like a university application portal', 'show a follow-up only when Other is selected' and 'reorganise this long form for mobile'.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI bar and context

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms hosts the global persistent Dulche AI bar. Semantic context includes FormID/FormVersionID, selected PageID/FieldID/ComponentID, field schema, layout/theme selection, Data bindings, logic graph selection, mode/state variables, marking rules, preview state and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write-capable AI changes Forms only through typed Forms/shared-engine/NodeGraph actions and remains subject to permissions, revision control and per-action Data mutation approval when a Form operation changes linked Data.

heading: HEADING_3
