heading: HEADING_3
text: Automation and typed events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations, Spaces, Dulche and authorised integrations can consume typed Forms events subject to permissions. Useful events include FormPublished, FormOpened/Closed, ResponseStarted/Saved/Submitted/Updated, ResponseMarked, QuizGraded, DataSyncConflict, LiveSessionStarted/Ended, ParticipantJoined/Left/Reconnected, QuestionOpened/Closed, LiveAnswerSubmitted, ParticipantEliminated/Reinstated and ScoreChanged.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Events expose stable IDs and minimal required metadata. Sensitive answers/identity are included only when the consuming principal has the corresponding permission.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Builder and published runtime MUST be keyboard-operable and screen-reader compatible for field entry, navigation, maths editor alternatives, graph-response controls, table input, validation, quiz feedback and multiplayer participation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every field has semantic label/help/error association. Dynamic show/hide/focus behaviour uses accessible announcements and predictable focus management. State MUST NOT rely on colour alone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph/math questions provide accessible textual/equation representations and non-pointer input paths for required operations where feasible. Multiplayer score/rank changes should not create unusable constant announcements; meaningful state updates are summarised appropriately.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Theme/layout freedom is constrained by minimum contrast, logical focus order, responsive reflow and touch-target requirements.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and realtime behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Published forms load only the assets/question state required for the current permitted experience. Large question banks, response sets, Data-backed option lists and multiplayer sessions use paging/streaming/cache strategies rather than unbounded client payloads.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Realtime multiplayer uses server-authoritative event sequencing and bounded fan-out/state updates. One slow participant or AI-marking task MUST NOT freeze the whole host interface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Autosave/draft persistence is incremental and resilient to transient network loss according to configured offline/retry policy.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: FormProject edits, Draft/Published versions and stored responses are crash-safe. A failed publish MUST leave the prior published version available unless explicitly withdrawn.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Response submission uses idempotency/operation identity where needed so retries do not create accidental duplicate records. Partial Forms→Data writes are detected and surfaced with recoverable state rather than falsely reporting a complete submission.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured failures include FormNotFound, VersionNotFound, FieldNotFound, ValidationFailed, MarkingUnavailable, MathParseError, GraphResponseInvalid, RegexInvalid, DataBindingUnavailable, DataSyncConflict, PublishFailed, ResponseClosed, DuplicateAttempt, SessionNotFound, SessionClosed, ParticipantNotFound, JoinRejected, IntegrityPolicyViolation, MultiplayerStateConflict, AIJudgeUnavailable, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable plus shared backend/provider errors.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical FormProject, response, mode, Data binding, graph and multiplayer-session model while capability-negotiating device features, realtime transport, identity providers, proctoring/kiosk integrations and mathematical/rendering backends.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A platform that lacks a configured capability exposes CapabilityUnavailable or a documented fallback; it MUST NOT silently change answer schema, marking or assessment-integrity semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Forms follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract rather than launching an incompatible private runtime.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A simple Form can be created, styled, published, completed and responses reviewed while preserving stable Form/Page/Field/Response identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Form, Test and Quiz presets use the common runtime but exhibit their intended answer/marking/progression semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A custom mode built with the node editor can implement a non-standard state machine such as 'three correct answers as quickly as possible' without forking the Forms runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: TableInput accepts multiple typed rows with per-column validation and can map rows to related Data records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A question accepts multiple deterministic correct answers such as CPU and Central Processing Unit under configured normalisation rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Regex validation/marking can be tested in the builder, rejects an invalid pattern safely and applies configured full/partial-match semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI marking uses a structured rubric, records marking provenance and can enter NeedsReview rather than fabricating certainty.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hybrid marking can resolve deterministic answers first and route only unresolved configured answers to AI/human review.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A visual maths expression round-trips to LaTeX and back without losing supported structure; malformed LaTeX does not destroy the previous valid expression.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A graph-response question stores structured graph data and can be marked against configured mathematical/coordinate criteria without relying on a screenshot.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Form can write responses into a Data spreadsheet/relational table while preserving types, references and nested/repeating structures.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data→Forms schema synchronisation can add a compatible field according to configured policy; destructive schema changes preserve historical responses and surface migration/conflict rather than silently deleting data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Simple conditional logic such as answer X → show question Y is configurable without nodes and is represented consistently in the advanced logic graph.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Node validation detects a cyclic/uncontrolled update loop or invalid target without locking the published runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Theme/layout controls can produce a branded responsive multi-column form while accessibility constraints remain satisfied.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Draft changes do not affect the currently published version until publication, and historical responses remain interpretable against the FormVersion they answered.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A standard live multiplayer quiz synchronises question state, answer windows, scoring and reveal using server-authoritative state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A knockout session can eliminate participants according to configured rules and finish when its declared completion condition is met.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Team and buzzer-style sessions preserve server-authoritative answer/buzz ordering and configured scoring semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A disconnected participant can reconnect according to policy without losing prior submitted answers or duplicating identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Anti-cheat settings can randomise questions/options, enforce server-side timers/locks and log configured focus-change/integrity events without treating such signals as automatic proof of misconduct.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Protected future questions/correct answers are not unnecessarily delivered to a participant client before authorised reveal.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Client-side manipulation cannot self-award points, extend authoritative timers, reveal protected answers or reinstate an eliminated participant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Optional high-integrity integrations require explicit configuration/capability and do not secretly activate camera/microphone/screen capture.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An AI-marked multiplayer question follows the configured latency/fairness policy and does not silently use model-response speed as participant performance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms↔Data write failures expose partial/retry state and do not falsely report submission success.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard and screen-reader users can complete representative simple, assessment, table, maths and multiplayer workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Forms model while capability-negotiating platform-specific realtime/integrity features.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Forms follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Developer Apps

heading: HEADING_2
text: Dev

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and engineering principle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Dev is the native CUI professional software-development environment. It MUST be fully useful without AI and provide mature project/workspace management, source editing, language tooling, build/run/test, debugging, terminal access, package/dependency management, source-control integration, visual CUI development, extension development, remote/container environments and structured agentic coding.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev is the authoritative code-development surface. Specialised products such as Stack, Sites and AI Studio retain their own domain authority, but Dev can open, inspect, edit and run their developer-facing project resources through stable shared identities and typed APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Repository-aware AI mutations MUST use typed code/file/project/task actions and MUST expose the resulting reviewable change set. Opaque desktop automation MUST NOT be used when a structured development action exists.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical workspace and project model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: DevWorkspace has stable WorkspaceID, Roots[], Projects[], OpenEditors[], Tasks[], RunConfigurations[], DebugConfigurations[], Toolchains[], Environments[], SourceControlBindings[], ExtensionState, WorkspaceSettings, CreatedAt, ModifiedAt and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A workspace may contain multiple folders, repositories and related projects. Monorepos, client/server solutions and multi-language workspaces MUST NOT require flattening into one artificial project type.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project has stable ProjectID, ProjectTypeID, language/framework metadata, source roots, build system, package/dependency metadata, target platforms, toolchain requirements, run/debug configurations, preview providers and Revision. Dev SHOULD consume existing ecosystem project files rather than replacing them with a proprietary project model where an established project format exists.

heading: HEADING_3
text: New Project workflow and project catalogue

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: File → New Project opens a searchable/filterable catalogue analogous to mature IDE project creation. Filters include language, framework, platform, project type, target runtime, installed toolchains, 9to1 product/surface and organisation templates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: First-party examples include console applications, CUI applications, class/static/shared libraries, web/API services, test projects, Python packages/CLI applications, Sites projects, Android/mobile projects, operating-system/kernel/bootloader projects, 9to1 extensions, CUI component libraries, AI provider/tool projects and other supported templates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project providers/extensions MAY register additional project templates, languages, frameworks and target types. The catalogue MUST NOT be hard-coded so tightly that adding a new ecosystem requires changing Dev core.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: After selecting a project type Dev exposes only applicable framework/toolchain/runtime options and validates requirements before creation. Missing required SDK/toolchain components are shown explicitly with install/configure actions where supported.

heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1 Extension project type

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Extension is a first-party New Project type. Its creation flow allows the developer to select one or more target 9to1 applications/surfaces and one or more contribution types.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Target applications may include Dev, Write, Present, Data, Boards, Canvas, Forms, Motion, Wave, Picture, Sites, AI Studio, Stack, Browse, Home, Files, Spaces and other extension-capable surfaces. Multi-target extensions are supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Contribution choices are filtered per target. Examples include Dev language/toolchain/debugger/project-template/editor/tool-window contributions; Forms fields/marking providers/modes; Data sources/transforms/visualisations/functions; AI Studio model/tool/evaluator/workflow providers; shared CUI components; Node Graph nodes; commands and integrations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The wizard generates the canonical extension manifest, SDK/API references, initial permission declarations, test scaffolding and appropriate extension-host Run configurations. Generated scaffolding MUST contain only selected contributions rather than a giant all-products starter.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Editor and navigation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The source editor includes tabs, preview/pinned tabs, split editors, editor groups, breadcrumbs, outline/symbol view, optional minimap, line numbers, indentation/whitespace guides, bracket matching, folding, multi-cursor, rectangular selection, snippets, configurable keybindings, encoding/line-ending awareness, large-file mode and undo/redo.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search/navigation includes file search, workspace text/regex search, go to line/file/symbol, references, implementations and structural/semantic search where the language provider supports it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editor state references canonical Files/project identity where possible rather than treating an absolute filesystem path as permanent identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Language intelligence and parsing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev uses established language tooling protocols/providers where practical. LSP or equivalent providers supply completion, hover, signature help, go-to-definition/declaration/type/implementation, references, rename, code actions, semantic diagnostics, document/workspace symbols, formatting and semantic tokens.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tree-sitter or an equivalent maintained parser MAY provide fast syntax structure, incremental parsing, selections and editor features where suitable, while language-specific semantic operations remain owned by the relevant language/tooling provider.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev MUST NOT implement language semantics using fragile regex parsing where a maintained compiler/LSP/parser exists.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Toolchain Manager and built-in/provisionable toolchains

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev provides a first-class Toolchain Manager. A Toolchain has stable ToolchainID, language, provider, compiler/runtime/interpreter, version, target architectures, debugger, language server, package manager, environment binding, capability state and provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Core supported ecosystems SHOULD be usable out of the box through bundled or one-click provisionable toolchains where licensing/platform constraints permit. Examples include .NET SDK/Roslyn for C#/F#, LLVM/Clang for C/C++, CPython plus Python language/debug/package tooling, rustc/Cargo, a JDK for Java/Kotlin and the relevant JavaScript/TypeScript runtimes/tooling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Python is treated correctly as a runtime/interpreter ecosystem rather than inaccurately labelling every execution as compilation. Native/package compilation tools may be added where project requirements need them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Platform-native toolchains such as MSVC may be discovered and used when installed. Remote/container environments expose their own toolchains through the same abstraction.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Missing compiler/runtime indication

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev MUST make toolchain readiness obvious before build/run. It must distinguish missing compiler/runtime, wrong version, missing debugger, missing language server, missing package manager, registry/authentication failure and general build failure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A project requirement such as '.NET SDK >= 10', 'clang >= 20' or 'Python 3.14' is compared against the selected environment. The UI shows Ready or explicit environment issues with required versus installed versions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Errors such as command-not-found or process spawn failure MUST NOT be the primary user experience when Dev can determine that a required toolchain component is missing. Supported components can be installed/configured directly through a typed toolchain operation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Build pipeline and tasks

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev supports structured Tasks and BuildPipelines. A pipeline may contain Restore, Generate, Compile, Link, Package, Test, Sign or other project-defined stages with dependencies, parallelism rules, environment, working directory, cancellation, timeout and diagnostics matching.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Build UI exposes stage-level state such as pending/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled and routes compiler/linter/build diagnostics into the common Problems model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tasks can be project-defined, extension-provided or inferred from recognised ecosystem files, but generated/inferred tasks remain inspectable and editable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Run configurations and target-aware Run

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run means execute the selected project's declared launch target rather than universally starting one host executable. RunConfiguration has stable ID, provider/type, target artifact/project, arguments, environment, working directory, target platform/device, pre-launch tasks, preview provider and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples include console → terminal, web → development server + preview, Android → emulator/device install + launch, CUI application → application runtime, 9to1 extension → extension development host, operating system → virtual machine, and library → test/sample host where configured.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Run selector shows the exact active target and environment. Dev MUST NOT silently run a different configuration because another panel gained focus.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Operating-system and kernel project support

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: OS/kernel/bootloader projects are first-class project types. Their Run pipeline may build the configured kernel/EFI/bootloader/ISO/disk image, verify the output artifact, start the configured virtual machine, attach the boot media and expose display/serial/debug channels in Dev.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An OS project can define architecture, firmware type, CPU/RAM, graphics, boot image/disk, networking, serial ports, snapshots, debugger transport and other virtual-machine settings through a VirtualMachineRunConfiguration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pressing Run on a valid OS project can therefore implement Build → Package boot artifact → Launch VM → Boot → attach configured console/debugger without the developer manually reconstructing a hypervisor command each time.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Virtual machine provider and OS preview

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Virtualisation uses a provider abstraction. QEMU is an appropriate first-party/default provider where supported, with hardware acceleration through the host's available mechanisms. Additional providers may register through extensions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project state stores semantic VM settings rather than treating opaque provider CLI flags as the only canonical configuration. Provider-specific advanced settings may still be exposed where necessary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The VM may render in an embedded Dev run/preview panel or a pop-out window and exposes power/reset/pause, display, serial console, boot logs, configured device state, basic performance information, snapshots and debugger status.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Workspace trust rules apply: opening an unknown repository MUST NOT automatically execute build scripts, boot images or VM configurations.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Low-level OS debugging

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the selected VM/debugger provider supports it, OS development integrates with the ordinary debugger plus low-level views for registers, memory, disassembly, symbols, raw addresses, threads/cores and source mapping.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Serial/debug output is a structured run channel. Kernel panic or boot output remains attached to the run session and can be correlated with debugger/build state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VM snapshots can be created/restored for repeatable kernel, driver, installer and boot-sequence debugging.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Debugger

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev provides a full debugger using DAP or another maintained abstraction where practical. Supported capabilities include launch/attach, source/conditional breakpoints, hit-count breakpoints where supported, logpoints, continue/pause, step into/over/out, call stack, scopes, variables, watches, expression evaluation, threads/processes and exception breakpoints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Capabilities are negotiated per debugger/provider; Dev MUST NOT expose controls that imply unsupported debugger semantics.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Testing and Test Explorer

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Testing is a first-class typed subsystem. Test Explorer shows project/suite/test identity, running/passed/failed/skipped state, duration, failure output, source location and rerun capability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users and AI can run one test, a selection, file/suite/project/workspace set or previously failed tests. Test results have stable identities and are available to AI/change review without scraping terminal output.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Problems and diagnostics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compiler, language-server, linter, build, package and test failures feed a common Problems model. Diagnostic records include provider/source, severity, message, code, file/resource identity, range and related information/quick fixes where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Diagnostics are semantic Dev objects consumable by UI, APIs and Dulche; they are not only coloured text in a terminal.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Terminal integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev uses the shared Terminal runtime rather than implementing an incompatible second terminal emulator. It supports multiple tabs/panes, shell profiles, project/environment working-directory binding, environment variables, command history, task integration and clickable file/line diagnostics where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Dev terminal remains a real shell terminal and does not require AI for ordinary command execution. Terminal actions use shared Terminal APIs when canonical.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Source control and Stack integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack remains the canonical 9to1 source-control/collaboration product. Dev presents working-tree/project source-control state and uses Stack/Git APIs for changed files, hunks, staged/unstaged state where applicable, branch/twig/leaf state, history, blame, conflicts, upstream state and other supported collaboration context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev MUST NOT implement a separate competing project/branch model that diverges from Stack. It can expose conventional Git concepts directly when the backing repository uses them and map Stack-specific structures through the Stack contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Source-control state is accessible without AI and is also available to Dulche/agents as typed context.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Diff and review editor

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev provides side-by-side, unified/inline and word-level diff views with file navigation, hunk/line selection where safe, staging/reverting, conflict resolution and navigation between changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Diff targets include working tree versus source-control base, branch/Stack comparisons, commits and AI change sets. Each comparison MUST identify its left/right revisions explicitly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated changes MUST NOT bypass normal diff/review visibility.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI ChangeSet model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every mutating AI coding pass has a stable AIChangeSetID recording initiating task/prompt, model/agent identity where available, starting workspace/repository revision, exact file operations/patches, created/deleted/moved resources, child-agent contributions, tests/tasks run, diagnostics before/after, completion status and timestamps.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev distinguishes the AI-pass diff from the overall working-tree diff. Existing user modifications are not relabelled as AI-authored merely because an AI later edited the same file.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Revert AI Change attempts to reverse only the recorded AI patch/change set while preserving unrelated user changes. If later overlapping edits prevent safe automatic reversal, Dev surfaces a conflict rather than discarding work.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI review workflow

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev supports Review first and Apply then review workflows. Review first presents proposed patches before application; Apply then review applies scoped edits and immediately exposes them in the AI review surface. Workspace/user policy selects the default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Review supports accept/reject by file and hunk, and finer region/line review where the patch model can apply it safely. AI may attach explanatory review annotations to hunks without inserting those explanations as source comments.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Review summaries include build/test/diagnostic outcomes where they were actually run, for example build passed, tests passed/failed, new warnings and resolved diagnostics. Dev MUST NOT claim tests/builds succeeded unless those executions occurred.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Structured AI coding and agentic development

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche/agent context includes workspace/project/repository identity, selected files/ranges/symbols, diagnostics, references/call relationships where available, tests, tasks/builds, source-control state, package state, terminal/run results and relevant preview state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI actions use typed operations such as read/search file, find symbol/references, create/move/delete file, apply patch/edit, semantic refactor, run task/test, inspect diagnostics, inspect diff, manage approved package operations and invoke owning shared APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Longer agentic development can inspect, plan, edit, build/test, diagnose, iterate and present the final change set within an explicit scope. Agent Activity exposes current goal, operation, files examined/changed, validation, blockers, retries, subtasks/child agents and pending human decisions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Parallel agents require scoped workspaces/branches/worktrees or another safe isolation/reconciliation mechanism. They MUST NOT blindly race edits against the same canonical files.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Symbol-aware editing and refactoring

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev exposes code symbols such as class/type, function/method, property/field, interface, namespace/module and references when supplied by the language provider. AI and manual operations SHOULD target semantic symbols where possible rather than fragile character offsets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Refactoring uses language/provider semantics where available: rename symbol, extract method/function, inline, move symbol, organise imports, change signature, safe delete and generate/implement members. Global text replacement MUST NOT substitute for a supported semantic refactor.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Package and dependency management

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Package management is first-class while preserving ecosystem-native package formats, registries, manifests and lockfiles. Dev provides a common Dependencies view over direct packages, transitive packages, framework/runtime references, project references and relevant native/system dependencies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Package installation/update/removal ultimately uses the configured ecosystem package manager and updates the real project/lock files. Dev MUST NOT create a proprietary dependency declaration that masks or conflicts with the project's native package manager.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dependency graph view MAY reuse the shared Node Graph Framework to show direct/transitive relationships and version conflicts while preserving the actual underlying manifests.

heading: HEADING_3
text: NuGet and .NET dependency support

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev MUST support NuGet for .NET projects where the configured .NET toolchain supports it. It understands PackageReference/project files, package sources, authenticated/private feeds, package restore and lock-file conventions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The package UI can expose Installed, Updates and Browse views plus package version, source, target-framework compatibility, dependency tree, licence metadata and known advisory/deprecation state where reliable metadata exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: NuGet actions use the actual .NET/NuGet tooling and resulting project/lockfile changes appear in the normal source diff. Private-feed credentials use shared secure credential infrastructure.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Other package ecosystems

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Supported providers include, where installed/configured: npm/pnpm/Yarn and package.json/workspaces/lockfiles; pip/uv/Poetry/pyproject/requirements/virtual environments; Cargo/Cargo.toml; Maven/Gradle; CMake/Meson project dependencies plus vcpkg/Conan; and additional extension-provided package systems.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev makes the selected Python environment, Node runtime, .NET SDK and analogous environment-critical context clearly visible. Dependency failures distinguish registry unavailable, authentication required, package/version missing, incompatible version and restore incomplete.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI/agent package changes MUST use the configured package manager and preserve the project's lockfile/dependency conventions unless the task explicitly requests migration.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dependency integrity and reproducibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev respects ecosystem lockfiles and project-local version constraints. Package operations SHOULD be reproducible and show manifest/lockfile diffs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When authoritative advisory metadata is available Dev may surface known vulnerabilities, deprecated/yanked versions, licence metadata and conflicts. It MUST distinguish an external advisory from an AI-generated suspicion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Offline/network/authentication states are represented accurately rather than collapsing every package restore problem into a generic build failure.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Native 9to1 extension platform

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev is the primary development/debugging environment for a shared native 9to1 Extension platform. Extensions MAY contribute language/toolchain/debugger/formatter/linter providers, project templates, package providers, editors, commands, tool windows, CUI/visual-builder components, AI context/tools, Node Graph node types and product-specific contributions exposed by host APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: One extension package may target multiple 9to1 products through explicit contribution contracts; products do not need separate unrelated plugin formats for the same extension.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extensions use a versioned manifest declaring ExtensionID, publisher/name/version, compatible host/API versions, entry points, target products, contributions, permissions/capabilities, dependencies, supported platforms, assets, update channel and signature/provenance.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Extension permissions, isolation and trust

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extensions declare required capabilities such as workspace read/write, process execution, network, terminal, credential access, Files, Stack or AI/model access. The host can present permissions during install/enable; low-risk themes/components MUST NOT silently inherit arbitrary process/filesystem/network rights.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension execution is isolated where practical with crash containment, startup timeout, resource monitoring, per-extension logs, disable/restart and safe-mode recovery. A broken extension SHOULD NOT crash-loop the whole Dev process.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension APIs are versioned/capability-negotiated. Deprecated APIs produce migration diagnostics and compatibility behaviour where reasonable rather than silent breakage.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Extension development host and inspector

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run on a 9to1 Extension project can launch the selected target product's clean Extension Host with the development extension loaded and debugger/logging attached. Multi-target extensions offer explicit target-host run choices.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension Inspector exposes registered contributions, activated services, requested permissions, host/API compatibility, logs/errors, extension-host state and performance/resource information where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension integration tests can target selected hosts and permissions without requiring installation into the developer's normal production profile.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Discover distribution and private extensions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension browsing/distribution integrates with the shared Discover/catalogue experience rather than creating an unrelated marketplace. Dev can filter Discover to compatible Dev/9to1 extensions and open listing/install/update flows through the shared extension service.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension listings expose publisher, version, compatible hosts/platforms, permissions, licence, source repository where supplied, dependencies, changelog and trust/signature information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Organisations/workspaces may distribute private extensions according to the shared identity/permission model.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Sites integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites and Dev share canonical project/resource identity. A Sites project can Open in Dev to expose underlying source/components/routes/styles/server functions/configuration/dependencies/tests/deployment configuration where that Sites project model makes those resources code-editable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites visual edits and Dev source edits SHOULD round-trip when the underlying representation is intentionally round-trippable. Unsupported visual-only structures MUST be represented as managed boundaries rather than silently destroyed by source editing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web/Sites-compatible Run/Preview may use Sites preview/runtime infrastructure for responsive preview, route inspection, development server integration, preview environments and deployment-oriented diagnostics without Dev duplicating the entire Sites authoring product.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI Studio integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Studio remains the specialised authoring/testing environment for models, agents, prompts, evaluations, tools and AI workflows. Dev is the engineering environment that consumes and extends those resources in application source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Studio resources referenced by a Dev project retain shared stable identities. Dev can Open in AI Studio, while AI Studio can Open source in Dev for custom tools, connectors, provider code, SDK integration and evaluation scripts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev may embed selected AI testing/inspection panels such as test conversation, structured output, tool calls, latency/token metadata where available, but MUST NOT reimplement the complete AI Studio product.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shared Sites + Dev + AI Studio workflows

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A project can combine Sites-managed frontend resources, Dev-managed application/backend source and AI Studio-managed agent/model resources without export/copy steps between products. Cross-product references use canonical IDs and declared version/revision bindings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing a shared AI resource or Sites component follows its owning product's version/revision rules; Dev detects relevant updates/conflicts instead of silently copying stale snapshots.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Visual CUI Builder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev MUST include a native visual CUI builder for CUI applications/components. The core layout is Component Tree + Visual Canvas + contextual Inspector, with source editing available alongside it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The builder exposes registered CUI controls/components such as text, buttons, inputs, switches, selectors, menus, tabs, lists/tables/trees, cards/panels, dialogs, navigation, images/media, canvas/chart surfaces and project-defined components.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual editing manipulates the same canonical CUI representation/source model used by the runtime. Dev MUST NOT maintain a hidden proprietary canvas model that drifts from or overwrites hand-written CUI source.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Visual CUI layout, properties and bindings

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The CUI builder supports hierarchy/nesting, reorder, grid/flex/dock-style layout according to CUI's real layout model, padding/margin/gap, alignment, min/max sizing, responsive behaviour, breakpoints, visibility/overflow and other supported CUI layout properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Inspector exposes real component properties grouped into content, layout, appearance, behaviour/events, data bindings and accessibility. Editing an Inspector property changes the canonical source/model and source changes update the canvas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Bindings such as model property → UI property and command/event bindings are first-class typed objects where CUI supports them. Simple event-handler creation can generate/navigate to real source handlers; graph-based behaviour may use the shared Node Graph Framework where the project architecture chooses it.

heading: HEADING_3
text: CUI states, component authoring and accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual preview supports representative states such as default, hover, pressed, focused, disabled, selected, loading, empty and validation error where components expose them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Developers can visually author reusable custom CUI components with typed properties/events/slots and reuse them throughout a project.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The builder continuously surfaces accessibility diagnostics such as missing labels, contrast problems, focus-order issues, unreachable controls, inadequate target size and colour-only state. These diagnostics integrate with the normal Problems model.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Two-way source and visual round-trip

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selecting a component in source/tree SHOULD highlight it in the visual preview where source mapping exists; selecting/inspecting a rendered element SHOULD reveal the owning component/source symbol/range where safe.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hand-written/custom constructs that cannot be represented by a visual editor remain code-defined and preserved. The builder MUST NOT delete or rewrite unsupported code merely to force visual round-tripping.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual AI edits such as 'make this sidebar collapse below 800px' mutate real CUI properties/layout/source through typed actions and therefore appear in normal code/AI diffs.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Live split view and preview providers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev supports flexible split layouts including Code | Preview, Code | Diff, Diff | Preview, Code | Terminal, Code | Tests, Code | AI and debugger-oriented layouts. Workspace/project layouts can be saved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PreviewProvider is a typed project/extension capability. Representative providers include CUI live render, Sites/web preview, Markdown render, extension host/sample host, AI Studio tool test harness, Android emulator/device and OS virtual-machine display/serial view.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: In Code | Preview mode, the developer can resize/swap panes and optionally Follow editor or Pin a particular component/page/application preview while editing related files.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Hot reload and last-valid preview

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the selected runtime supports it, source changes trigger incremental build/hot reload into the preview. Preview state clearly distinguishes Live, Building, Reloading, Build failed, Disconnected and Paused.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a new build fails, Dev preserves the last valid preview when technically possible and overlays/links the new diagnostics rather than replacing useful state with a blank pane.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PreviewConfiguration can retain viewport/device, route/component target, theme/state/sample data, environment and other provider-specific design-time inputs.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Interactive preview and source inspection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Applicable previews are interactive. CUI/web previews can accept pointer/keyboard/navigation input, resize, hover/focus state and other runtime interactions without becoming the general Browse product.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Inspect element can expose component/type, source file/range, runtime bounds, computed style/layout, bindings, accessibility state and event handlers where the preview provider supplies mappings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Responsive preview presets include phone, tablet, desktop and custom sizes where applicable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Visual diff and AI preview validation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: UI-oriented change review MAY offer Code diff | Visual diff and/or Diff | Preview. Source diff remains authoritative; visual comparison supplements engineering review rather than replacing it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a preview provider supports before/after rendering, AI review can show previous/current render or affected component state and link visual differences back to the associated source changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated UI work SHOULD perform build/runtime/visual validation when the required preview/inspection capability is available and within scope. Passing compilation alone is not sufficient evidence that a visual task is correct.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Remote, container and reproducible environments

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev supports environment adapters such as Local, WSL where available, SSH remote, devcontainer/container, cloud development environment and other extension-provided environments.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: File operations, LSP/toolchains, tasks, debugging and package operations execute in the selected environment where appropriate. Remote development SHOULD run language servers/build tools near the project filesystem rather than blindly copying whole repositories to the client.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev recognises project-native environment definitions such as devcontainer.json rather than replacing them with an incompatible format.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Workspace trust and execution security

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening a repository does not automatically trust or execute repository-controlled code. Workspace Trust controls execution of tasks/build scripts, package lifecycle scripts, debugger launch, extension recommendations, VM boot/run configurations and other code-execution surfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev clearly separates reading/editing files from launching code, installing packages, network access, credential access, privilege elevation and deployment/external side effects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Secrets/tokens use shared credential infrastructure where possible and MUST NOT be unnecessarily exposed to AI context, logs, source control, telemetry or generated diffs.

heading: HEADING_3
text: API and HTTP developer tooling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev SHOULD provide a native developer-oriented HTTP/API request tool for method, URL, headers, auth, body, environment variables, saved requests and response inspection, with WebSocket/event-stream capability where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: This tool remains developer-focused and does not replace Browse. Saved requests are project/workspace resources and secrets use secure variable/credential references.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Notebook and interactive execution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where relevant to supported ecosystems, Dev MAY provide notebook/cell-oriented interactive execution with code cells, rich outputs, plots and variable/kernel state. Notebook capability is developer-oriented and MUST NOT duplicate Data's full analytical spreadsheet/database experience.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Interactive execution uses the selected environment/toolchain and clearly identifies kernel/runtime state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Database developer handoff

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Basic database/schema/query context may be surfaced for development, but Data remains the full database/analysis product. Dev can Open in Data or embed/link query/schema results through typed integration rather than building a second competing database IDE.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI bar and context

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev hosts the global persistent Dulche AI bar. Semantic context includes WorkspaceID, ProjectID, selected files/ranges/symbols, diagnostics, build/test results, source-control/Stack state, packages/toolchains, Run/Debug/Preview configuration, active environment, CUI visual selection and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write-capable AI uses typed Dev/Files/Stack/Terminal/package/toolchain/NodeGraph actions under the owning API contracts and produces an AIChangeSet for repository/source mutations.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automation and events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev emits typed events such as WorkspaceOpened, ProjectCreated, FileChanged, DiagnosticsChanged, BuildStarted/Completed/Failed, TestRunCompleted, RunStarted/Stopped, DebugStarted/Stopped, ToolchainMissing/Changed, DependencyChanged, AIChangeSetCreated/Reviewed, PreviewUpdated/Failed and ExtensionHostStarted/Failed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations/agents use stable resource IDs and meaningful lifecycle events rather than raw keypress/editor-caret telemetry.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editor, project explorer, search, Problems, Test Explorer, debugger, source control/diffs, package/dependency views, terminal integrations, visual CUI builder, toolchain manager and AI review are keyboard operable and expose screen-reader semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Diagnostics, breakpoints, source-control state, diff additions/deletions and build/test state MUST NOT rely only on colour/gutter glyphs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual builder/preview functionality provides source/tree/Inspector alternatives so required project editing does not depend solely on pointer manipulation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and large-workspace behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev uses lazy/incremental workspace indexing, incremental parsing, bounded caches, cancellation, virtualised large lists and project ignore/exclusion rules. Vendor/generated/build directories are not fully indexed by default when the project/provider marks them as such.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening a large monorepo MUST NOT synchronously parse millions of files on the UI thread. Tooling status/progress is visible and expensive indexing can be cancelled or scoped.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large-file mode reduces expensive semantic/decorative features instead of freezing the editor.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unsaved editor changes, editor layout and recoverable workspace state survive crashes where feasible. File saves use safe/atomic behaviour appropriate to the backing filesystem/provider.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Failed AI or bulk refactors preserve a recoverable change set and MUST NOT report completion when only part of a requested patch applied. Conflicts are surfaced explicitly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured failures include WorkspaceNotFound, ProjectNotFound, FileNotFound, ToolchainMissing, ToolchainVersionMismatch, LanguageServiceUnavailable, BuildFailed, TestFailed, DebuggerUnavailable, RunConfigurationInvalid, PackageRestoreFailed, PackageAuthenticationRequired, ExtensionHostFailed, PreviewBuildFailed, VMProviderUnavailable, EnvironmentUnavailable, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable plus provider-specific diagnostics.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Dev project/workspace/action models while capability-negotiating local compiler availability, process execution, VM acceleration, terminal/debugger integration, filesystem access, extension hosting and remote environments.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a platform cannot provide a capability locally, Dev exposes CapabilityUnavailable or uses an explicitly configured remote/service provider. It MUST NOT silently pretend a build/debug/run occurred on an unsupported target.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Dev follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A representative multi-file workspace/project opens, edits and saves source while preserving project/file identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: New Project can filter/select a language/project type/framework and refuses or warns clearly when its required toolchain is unavailable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A 9to1 Extension project can select at least two target apps, generate corresponding manifest/contribution scaffolding and launch an appropriate Extension Host.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative C#/.NET, C/C++ and Python projects resolve the correct configured SDK/compiler/runtime and show a precise missing/wrong-version state when unavailable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A real build pipeline exposes stage-level restore/compile/link/package/test state and maps compiler diagnostics into Problems.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run launches the declared target rather than assuming every project is a host executable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An OS/kernel project can build a boot artifact and launch it through a configured VM provider with display/serial output; unsupported VM acceleration/provider state is reported clearly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Debugger breakpoints, stepping, call stack, variables and evaluation work for representative supported language/provider combinations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Test Explorer can run one test and a suite, preserves stable test/result identity and exposes failure source/output.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: LSP/provider completion, definition, references and semantic rename work for a representative supported language.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Semantic refactor uses the language provider rather than global text replacement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal integration uses the shared terminal runtime and respects the selected environment/project working directory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack/source-control state and file/hunk diffs match the actual repository state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An AI multi-file edit creates a distinct AIChangeSet whose diff excludes unrelated pre-existing user edits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI review can accept/reject at least file/hunk level and Revert AI Change preserves unrelated overlapping user work or surfaces a conflict instead of deleting it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI validation summaries only report build/tests actually executed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: NuGet package add/update/remove uses the real project/package manager and produces normal project/lockfile diffs; private feed credentials are not written into source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: At least one non-NuGet ecosystem package provider operates through the common Dependencies UI while retaining its native manifests/lockfiles.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension permissions are declared/inspectable, a crashing extension can be disabled/recovered without crash-looping Dev, and extension-host debugging works.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Sites-compatible project can Open in Dev with stable source identity and use the declared preview pathway without export/import copying.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An AI Studio resource referenced by a project retains shared identity and can Open in AI Studio rather than being copied into an unrelated file.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual CUI Builder edits real CUI layout/property state bidirectionally with source and preserves unsupported code-defined constructs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Code | Preview updates through hot reload where supported, preserves the last valid preview after a build failure and can map a representative rendered CUI element back to source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A UI-oriented AI change can expose source diff plus visual/preview validation where the provider supports it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Local and at least one remote/container environment use the same workspace/project model while executing toolchains/tasks in the selected environment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening an untrusted workspace does not automatically execute project-controlled build/package/VM/extension code.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Secrets are not unnecessarily inserted into AI context/logs/diffs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large workspaces remain responsive through incremental indexing/virtualisation/cancellation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard and screen-reader workflows cover editor navigation, Problems, tests, debugger, diff review and project creation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Dev model while capability-negotiating unsupported local execution features.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Dev follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Stacks

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack is 9to1's team-first source-control and software-collaboration product. It is not a conventional GitHub clone or a desktop Git client. It combines Git hosting/collaboration with a higher-level project model designed for parallel team development, cascading shared frameworks, strong source-domain rules, public collaboration and deep integration with the rest of 9to1.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Donors

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Primary donor: Gitea. Preserve mature donor features, quality-of-life behaviour and collaboration capabilities wherever they remain applicable, including repositories, users/teams, permissions, history/diffs, reviews, issues, releases, Git LFS, migration/mirroring and related backend features. Stack-specific behaviour replaces donor behaviour where the models conflict.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Secondary donor/reference: Gitnuro may be used for local desktop Git workflows and UX patterns where useful.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Donor parity must be explicitly audited. Every mature donor feature must be preserved, replaced by a 9to1-native equivalent, or explicitly recorded as not applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Project and storage model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each Stack project is an independent project boundary. A Stack project may use:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Files as the source backing store;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: its own dedicated public or private GitHub repository;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: both Files and GitHub together, according to the user's configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack must never combine unrelated Stack projects into one shared repository.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public Stack projects MUST expose a dedicated user-facing source-browsing, forking and contribution interface. Normal participation MUST NOT require direct access to Stack-managed backing folders, manifests or dependency branches.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack supports mixed public/private project components through an explicit visibility model attached to canonical resources/domains. Public projection is generated only from resources whose effective visibility permits publication; private files, objects, commits, credentials, metadata and historical objects MUST be excluded from the public Git/source projection, not merely hidden in the UI. Before publishing or mirroring a mixed-visibility project, Stack MUST validate the projected commit/object graph and block publication if private ancestry/content would be reachable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Startup and app shell

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack has two startup modes:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: New Session: open Home.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Last State: restore the previous tabs and navigation state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If Last State would reopen a tab/state that is known to have caused a repeatable crash, Stack must suppress or close the offending tab rather than crash-loop.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack always uses a tabbed interface:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ←  →  |  🏠  |  Project Tab 1  |  Project Tab 2  |  +

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home is permanently available as the leftmost tab. Opening a project opens a new tab. The + button opens a new tab.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home contains the main dashboard and its own sidebar pages, including My Projects, Discover Projects, Audit Log, My Team, Settings and similar administration/discovery surfaces. These pages stay inside Home rather than becoming separate top-level app tabs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clicking Home while Home is already selected returns Home to the main dashboard.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Back/Forward arrows sit to the left of Home and navigate history inside the currently selected tab. Unavailable navigation buttons are disabled/greyed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Source lineage

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: main is a special top-level source root and is above all normal Branches.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: main may contain normal project source and Roots. main may NEVER contain Twigs, Leaves or Subroots.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal development follows:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: main

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Branch

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Twig

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Leaf

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Branch is broadly analogous to a Git branch.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Twig is a nested development domain beneath a Branch.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Leaf is a nested development domain beneath a Twig.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack does not use worktrees as its user-facing or internal parallel-development model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: main

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ 9to1 2027 Q1 Update

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ├─ Write

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: │  ├─ New Font Switcher

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: │  ├─ Editor 2.0

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: │  └─ Persistent Word Counter

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ├─ Present

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Data 2.0

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Cascade semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Inheritance cascades downward by default:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: main → Branch → Twig → Leaf.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changes committed to main automatically cascade into every Branch and then through descendants.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changes made at a Branch cascade into its Twigs and Leaves.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: This allows shared frameworks/donor changes to be implemented once at a higher domain rather than duplicated in every child.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a cascade conflicts with descendant work, propagation for the affected path/node pauses until the conflict is resolved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The effective source state of a Twig/Leaf is its own changes combined with inherited state from its ancestors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deletion and rename semantics must be represented explicitly so inherited files do not incorrectly reappear after a child intentionally deletes or renames them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Active domain

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users do not switch branches in the traditional Git sense.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Right-clicking any Branch/Twig/Leaf exposes Set Active.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The active domain is only the default context used when opening an editor, running tests or building the project.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other Branches/Twigs/Leaves remain browseable and actionable at all times and can expose actions such as Open in Editor or Build without requiring the user to stash changes or change the active domain.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If no Branch/Twig/Leaf is active, main becomes active automatically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Project sidebar

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A project shows its whole lineage as one collapsible tree rather than hiding branches behind a branch selector:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Branches

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Branch (+A -D)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Twigs

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Twig (+A -D)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Leaves

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Leaf (+A -D)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project, Branches, Twigs and Leaves are collapsible headers.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Branch/Twig/Leaf label shows live diff totals, for example:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Notes Overhaul (+90 -20)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Displayed +A/-D totals MUST represent only the delta owned by that node relative to its effective parent. Inherited ancestor changes MUST NOT increase a child node’s own displayed totals.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selecting a node shows its effective source plus the node's diff against its parent. Changed filenames are visually status-coded, including green for additions/positive changes and red for removals/deletions, with clear states for renames and conflicts. Diff entries show the affected path and exact file/location.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Local and remote state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Uncommitted/unpushed changes appear at the top of a node's change view in bold with a yellow up-arrow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Committed changes appear underneath.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any Branch/Twig/Leaf containing uncommitted/unpushed changes also shows the yellow up-arrow beside its tree label.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A user setting can change this view to show only uncommitted/unpushed changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If changes exist on the remote but not the current machine, show a yellow cloud icon beside the node.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If remote and local changes conflict, the cloud turns red.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Conflict handling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When a conflict is detected, Stack opens a popup listing the conflicting filenames.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: View details opens the exact conflicting hunks/locations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Summarise with AI sends the relevant conflict context to Dulche/Home and returns a plain-language summary of the conflict.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Fix with AI asks Dulche to produce a resolution through typed source-control actions rather than opaque UI automation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: After an AI fix, Stack presents:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: a summary of what Dulche changed;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: the resulting diff;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reject;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept and Merge ▼.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The dropdown under Accept and Merge contains Accept without Merging.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reject restores the pre-fix state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept without Merging keeps the resolved changes but does not complete the merge.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accept and Merge accepts the resolution and completes the merge.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI conflict resolutions must never silently merge without this explicit review step.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Roots

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Root means: this file/folder/domain is structurally important and locked in Stack.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Root state is stored in roots.json in the owning domain. Domain means main, Branch, Twig or Leaf.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: All files/paths listed in that domain's roots.json are locked by Stack according to Root rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Root is authoritative for descendants: child domains cannot edit, replace or override the protected content directly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Roots represent authoritative shared frameworks, donor source or other protected components. Unless changed through the Root/Subroot workflow, Root content MUST cascade unchanged into descendant domains and descendants MUST NOT override it directly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Root may exist in main or another domain.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Root enforcement must derive from stored metadata, not only from transient UI state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Freeze

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Freeze is different from Root.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Root means “important/authoritative; direct editing below this domain is not allowed.”

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Freeze means “out of scope for now.”

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When creating a Freeze, the user chooses exactly which descendant subdomains inherit the Freeze. It does not automatically apply to every child unless selected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Freeze may have an expiry point/time/condition after which editing is restored automatically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack must clearly show:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: that a file/domain is frozen;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: which descendants the Freeze applies to;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: when it expires, if applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Freeze lifecycle is explicit. A Freeze records stable FreezeID, target Root/resource/domain, selected descendant scope, creator, reason, creation revision, optional expiry/condition and state. New descendants inherit an active Freeze only when they fall inside its configured scope policy. Early thaw requires the configured Freeze-management permission and is audited. Automatic expiry transitions the Freeze to Expired and restores editability only after Stack checks for in-progress operations and reconciles queued upstream changes. A user without Freeze-management permission cannot override or bypass an active Freeze.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Subroots

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Subroot is the controlled mechanism for testing changes to Root files.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subroots sit in the same domain that owns the Root, for example:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Twig

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ Twig Subroots

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Subroot explicitly selects which Roots are in scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each Root file/folder can be included in only one active Subroot at a time within that domain. Stack must prevent overlapping Subroots from claiming the same Root.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Root changes are developed/tested through the Subroot rather than by directly editing protected descendant copies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: main can contain Roots but can NEVER contain Subroots.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subroot completion is a first-class reviewed operation. Completing a Subroot requires a diff against the owning Root, configured validation/check results, conflict resolution and the required approvals. On completion the accepted change is applied to the owning Root as one auditable Root update, descendants receive it through normal cascade semantics, and the Subroot releases its Root claims. The user may instead abandon the Subroot, which discards its proposed Root changes while preserving audit/history. A Subroot cannot be silently deleted while it owns unresolved changes or Root claims.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Files-backed storage

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For Files-backed projects, Stack uses explicit Stack-managed dot folders:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project Name/

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ├─ .git/

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ├─ .branches/

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: │  └─ Branch/

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: │     └─ nested Stack structure

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ├─ .source/

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: │  └─ project source tree

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ .roots/

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: └─ roots.json

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Leading-dot paths are Stack-managed infrastructure. The UI MUST identify them as managed/internal state and MUST prevent ordinary project-editing flows from casually deleting or editing them. Explicit diagnostic/recovery tooling MAY expose controlled access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The exact nested on-disk schema for Branch/Twig/Leaf/Subroot domains and their per-domain metadata must be versioned and documented.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack MUST validate its managed folders/manifests when opening/synchronising a project. If required infrastructure is missing, moved, altered or partially deleted, Stack MUST enter a recoverable/diagnostic state, identify the damaged objects and attempt deterministic reconstruction from retained metadata/object IDs where reconstruction is possible; it MUST NOT silently treat damaged infrastructure as ordinary project source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: GitHub-backed storage

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each Stack project using GitHub maps to its own dedicated GitHub repository.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal Stack Branches remain normal native Git branches in that repository.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Twigs, Leaves and Subroot state are not represented as a proliferation of independent Git branches.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack stores Twig/Leaf/Subroot nested state in protected Stack-managed companion storage in the same repository. The canonical Git ref for that companion branch is `stack/twigs-and-leaves-dependency`; the UI presents it as managed infrastructure (for example “Twigs and Leaves (DEPENDENCY)”) and MUST NOT expose it as an ordinary user Branch.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: This dependency branch is never surfaced as a normal Branch inside Stack. Stack interprets it and renders the actual Branch → Twig → Leaf hierarchy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The dependency branch must contain a prominent README explaining that it is Stack-managed infrastructure and must not be deleted, merged into normal branches, rebased, renamed or manually edited.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: It must also contain a Stack manifest/schema sufficient to identify the project, version the storage format, map Branch/Twig/Leaf/Subroot IDs and recover safely.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If the dependency tree/manifest appears in a normal branch because somebody merged or moved it, Stack must recognise the signature, warn the user and recover/relink the dependency branch where possible rather than treating those files as normal project source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If the dependency branch is deleted, Stack MUST detect the missing managed ref and MUST attempt reconstruction from retained commit/object IDs, manifests and configured Files-backed recovery metadata. If complete reconstruction is impossible, Stack MUST preserve recoverable evidence, identify unrecoverable objects explicitly and block unsafe writes that could overwrite remaining recovery state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The GitHub adapter MUST preserve Stack semantics rather than mirror the Files backing layout literally. Branches map to native Git branches; Twig/Leaf/Subroot state maps to the protected Stack companion branch/manifest model defined above. Other entities MUST use a native GitHub/Git construct only when that construct preserves the canonical Stack identity, permissions and lifecycle semantics; otherwise Stack-managed metadata remains authoritative.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Sweeping and pruning

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sweep collects the changes from all descendant Twigs/Leaves into the owning Branch root, then removes those descendant development domains.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prune removes/discards a Stack Branch and its descendants from Stack.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prune requires 2FA.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: main can never be pruned.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pruning must not immediately destroy the backing source. The underlying Files/GitHub data must remain recoverable/auditable according to the project's retention policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Individual Twigs and Leaves can also be removed independently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pruned domains enter a recoverable Deleted state for the project's configured retention period. Restore reactivates the same stable DomainID and backing references when their retained source objects remain valid. Permanent purge is a separate privileged operation, requires explicit confirmation and 2FA for protected project policies, and is blocked while retained objects are referenced by active descendants, releases, change requests, audit requirements or recovery points. Purge records what was removed and what immutable audit evidence remains.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Public collaboration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public Stack projects expose a dedicated Stack interface for source browsing, forks and contributions rather than forcing users into internal Files storage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public projects provide project profiles, source browsing, history/releases, contributor identity, forks, Change Requests, notifications and Discover integration. Moderation supports project-level roles, report/block actions and removal of abusive public content without rewriting unrelated source history. Forks receive independent ProjectID/repository identity and record their source-project provenance. Contributions return through Change Requests against an explicitly selected destination domain; contributors never receive implicit access to private project components or Stack-managed dependency storage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where project components have different public/private visibility, Stack must preserve hard security boundaries and never rely on UI hiding.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Sites integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack is closely integrated with Sites.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: At minimum, Sites must be able to use Stack projects as source projects, open the relevant source domain, and maintain source ownership/history rather than publishing opaque generated output.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites binds deployments/previews to exact Stack ProjectID, DomainID and source revision. Branch/Twig/Leaf domains may create isolated preview deployments where policy permits; production deployments default to an approved Main revision unless the project explicitly authorises another release source. Build/deployment status is attached to the exact revision. Sites edits to source-backed projects are committed back into the currently bound Stack domain as ordinary reviewable source changes; Sites MUST NOT maintain an anonymous divergent copy of the project.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Gitea/Gitnuro donor parity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gitea is the primary donor and must be forked from the latest appropriate source at implementation time.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gitnuro may be used as a secondary donor/reference for local Git UX where its licence and architecture permit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Donor parity must cover, where applicable:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: repositories and repository settings;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: users, organisations/teams and permissions;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: commit history, branches, tags and diffs;
