NORMAL_TEXT
text: A feature may only be omitted when Stack deliberately replaces it or records it as not applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Domain identity and effective source

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every source domain has stable DomainID, ProjectID, type (Main, Branch, Twig or Leaf), parent DomainID where applicable, name, creation/base revision, local revision, effective revision, state, visibility, permission policy and Revision. Renaming or moving display labels MUST NOT change identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effective source is a deterministic projection of the domain's inherited ancestor state plus the domain's own deltas, tombstones, renames and Root/Freeze/Subroot rules. For a Leaf, the conceptual order is Main baseline → Branch delta → Twig delta → Leaf delta.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each effective file/resource can expose lineage: originating ancestor/domain, inherited revision, local override/delta, rename/delete state, Root authority and any paused/conflicted cascade. View lineage MUST use canonical history rather than infer origin from current path text.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Domain creation, hierarchy guards and reparenting

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hierarchy is enforced by the model/API: Main may create Branches; a Branch may create Twigs; a Twig may create Leaves; a Leaf cannot create children. Main cannot be a child and cannot contain Twigs, Leaves or Subroots.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Creating a child records its exact parent/base effective revision. Later parent changes arrive through cascade processing; the recorded base remains available for history, review and conflict calculation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reparenting is not a rename. Moving a Twig to another Branch or a Leaf to another Twig requires an explicit Reparent operation that calculates the new base/effective source, previews conflicts, preserves stable DomainID/history and requires the configured permission. Cross-project reparenting is prohibited; use fork/import/migration workflows instead.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deletion of a parent with active descendants is blocked unless the operation explicitly archives/prunes/migrates the descendants under the corresponding lifecycle rules.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Materialisation and concurrency model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack MUST support opening, browsing, building and acting on multiple domains concurrently without requiring user-facing Git worktree switching. Each active execution/editor receives a domain-scoped materialised view produced from canonical effective source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Implementations MAY use overlay filesystems, virtual projections, content-addressed materialisation, temporary isolated checkout directories or another robust mechanism, but the materialisation is derived state and MUST NOT become a competing source of truth.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Concurrent writes target stable DomainID/resource identity. Two clients or agents editing the same domain/resource use revision/merge conflict semantics; isolated domains may proceed independently. A failed materialisation or cache rebuild MUST be recoverable from canonical Stack/Git/Files state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Commit history for Branches, Twigs, Leaves and Subroots

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Branches use normal native Git commit history where Git-backed. Twig/Leaf/Subroot changes also have ordered canonical Change/Commit records with stable IDs, parent revision, author/initiator, timestamp, message, affected resources and resulting domain revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When GitHub-backed, Twig/Leaf/Subroot commit objects are represented through the protected Stack companion storage/manifest so their history is durable without exposing each nested domain as a normal Git branch. The manifest maps stable Stack change IDs to retained Git object/content identities sufficient for reconstruction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: History for a domain distinguishes inherited ancestor changes from locally authored changes. Rewriting or squashing history is explicit and permission-controlled; it MUST NOT silently invalidate descendants, releases or open Change Requests.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Promotion and Change Requests

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal contribution flow is Leaf → parent Twig → parent Branch → Main. Promotion is explicit upward movement of a reviewed change set; downward inheritance remains the separate cascade mechanism.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A ChangeRequest has stable ChangeRequestID, source DomainID/revision, destination DomainID/revision, included changes/commits, diff, author, reviewers, comments, required checks, approvals, conflict state, policy state, outcome and resulting revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Promote from a Leaf normally targets its parent Twig; from a Twig its parent Branch; from a Branch Main. Project policy MAY allow a deliberate bypass, but the UI/API must state which levels are being bypassed, calculate the complete destination diff and record the bypass in audit history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Promotion never silently includes unrelated descendant or working-tree changes. The source revision being reviewed is pinned. New source edits after review begins create a new revision and invalidate/re-run configured approvals/checks as policy requires.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Completing a Change Request applies the accepted change to the destination, records resulting lineage, then normal cascade semantics propagate the destination update downward. The source domain may remain open, be marked completed or be swept/pruned according to user/project policy.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Review, approvals and merge strategy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Change Requests support threaded review comments, requested changes, approvals, assigned reviewers, CODEOWNERS/ownership-style policies where configured, check requirements and protected-domain rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Available integration strategies may include merge commit, fast-forward, rebase or squash only where the target/domain policy and Stack lineage model can preserve stable identity and ancestry. The chosen strategy is explicit in the Change Request outcome.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Protected Main/Branch domains can require approvals, passing checks, signed commits or designated maintainers before promotion. An administrator override, where policy permits it, is explicit and audited.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Cascade implementation and update state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automatic Main/Branch cascade is represented as canonical ancestor revisions applied to descendant effective-source state, not as an uncontrolled series of user-visible Git merges. Each descendant tracks the highest ancestor revision successfully incorporated for each relevant lineage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When an ancestor changes, Stack computes the descendant update. Non-conflicting inherited changes become part of effective source automatically; locally owned +A/-D totals remain unchanged. If a resource conflicts, cascade for that affected resource/path pauses and the descendant records UpstreamConflict while unrelated safe updates MAY continue.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can inspect pending/inherited upstream changes and the ancestor revisions that caused them. Cascade processing is idempotent and crash-resumable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Deletion, rename and tombstone inheritance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A descendant deletion is represented as a tombstone bound to canonical resource lineage, not mere physical absence. The tombstone prevents the deleted ancestor resource from reappearing when a later cascade occurs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Renames/moves preserve stable resource lineage where deterministically known, storing old/new path plus resource identity. A later ancestor edit to the pre-rename resource is mapped to the renamed descendant resource when lineage proves equivalence; ambiguous cases surface a conflict.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replacing a resource with an unrelated new resource at the same path creates new lineage rather than pretending it is the old object. Tombstones and rename metadata are versioned and included in recovery/migration.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Conflict objects and resolver

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every unresolved conflict is a structured Conflict object with stable ConflictID, ProjectID/DomainID, resource identity/path, base revision/content, upstream side, local side, conflicting regions/properties, lineage, origin operation, state, assigned resolver where applicable and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text/code conflict resolution supports three-way views such as Upstream | Result | Local, hunk/region selection, take upstream, take local, combine/edit result, accept all non-conflicting changes and Open in Dev. Structured 9to1 resources SHOULD use semantic conflict resolution when a canonical domain API can represent it faithfully.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche may Summarise or propose Fix with AI through typed actions. AI proposals remain reviewable diffs; Reject restores the pre-proposal resolution state, Accept without Merging stores the resolution, and Accept and Merge completes the pending operation only after explicit user approval.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Root authority model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Root records have stable RootID, owning DomainID, protected resource identities/paths, creation revision, state, provenance/reason, policy and Revision. Root enforcement comes from canonical metadata; roots.json is a persisted projection/manifest, not the only source of truth.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Root locks descendant override of the protected resource. The owning domain may update its Root through authorised Root workflows, after which descendants inherit the new authoritative state through normal cascade rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Root scope may include a file, folder or registered structured resource. Overlapping Root definitions are validated so ownership is deterministic.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Subroot lifecycle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Subroot is a controlled experimental/update workspace for one or more Roots owned by the same eligible non-Main domain. It has stable SubrootID, owning DomainID, claimed RootIDs, base Root revisions, local proposed changes, checks/review state and lifecycle state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Within one owning domain, a Root can belong to only one active Subroot at a time. Main can contain Roots but cannot contain Subroots.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Completing a Subroot requires a diff against the owning Root, required tests/checks, conflict resolution and configured approvals. Accepted changes update the owning Root atomically as an auditable Root revision, release the claims and cascade to descendants. Abandoning a Subroot discards the proposal while retaining history/audit. Subroots with unresolved changes/claims cannot be silently deleted.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Freeze lifecycle and permissions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Freeze is a scoped edit restriction, distinct from Root authority. Freeze records have stable FreezeID, target resource/domain, selected descendant scope, creator, reason, creation revision, optional expiry/condition, policy and state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: New descendants inherit an active Freeze only according to its declared scope policy. Early thaw requires Freeze-management permission and is audited. Automatic expiry moves the Freeze to Expired and restores editability after checking in-progress operations and reconciling queued upstream updates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users without Freeze-management permission cannot bypass a Freeze through API, raw Git adapter or alternate client. Emergency administrator override, if enabled by organisation policy, is explicit, requires strong confirmation and is audited.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files and GitHub dual-authority/synchronisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When only Files backing is enabled, Files/Stack canonical metadata and source are authoritative. When only GitHub backing is enabled, native Git state plus protected Stack metadata are authoritative according to the adapter contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When both Files and GitHub are enabled, the project config explicitly selects authority mode: Stack/Files primary with GitHub mirror, GitHub primary with Files cache/backup, or managed bidirectional synchronisation. Bidirectional mode uses stable object/revision mapping and MUST surface concurrent divergent edits as sync conflicts; last-writer-wins is not an acceptable default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each successful sync records source revision, destination revision and mapping checkpoint. Partial sync leaves a resumable SyncConflict/Failed state and MUST NOT claim both backends are current.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Credentials and private remote metadata use shared credential/security infrastructure rather than being stored in project source.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Git compatibility and advanced Git operations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Git remains an interoperable underlying source-control substrate. Stack supports commit, stage/unstage where relevant, fetch, pull/synchronise, push, revert, cherry-pick, tags, signed commits, history, blame, diff, Git LFS, import/migration and mirrors where compatible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Raw Git operations that would invalidate Stack-managed lineage, dependency refs or Root/Subroot metadata are blocked or routed through an explicit Advanced/Unmanaged operation that explains consequences and repairs/reconciles Stack metadata before normal work resumes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Checking out an arbitrary Git branch inside a Stack-managed materialisation MUST NOT silently change the active Stack DomainID. Active domain is controlled by Stack's typed SetActive/OpenDomain operations.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Mixed public/private projection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visibility is attached to canonical domains/resources and inherited according to explicit policy. Public projection includes only content and history proven public for the selected release/domain projection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before public GitHub mirroring, forking or source browsing, Stack validates the projected tree and reachable object/history graph. If private content, credentials, private commit ancestry or private Stack metadata would be reachable, publication is blocked until the exposure is resolved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing a resource from public to private does not retroactively erase already-published Git history. Stack warns when historical exposure exists and offers supported remediation/rewrite workflows without pretending the previous public data was never published.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Team permissions and sensitive operations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permissions can be set at organisation/project and, where needed, domain level. Core roles/capabilities cover view source, contribute, create child domains, commit, promote/create Change Requests, review/approve, manage Roots/Subroots, manage Freezes, manage releases/packages, administer visibility/remotes and prune/purge.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Child-domain permissions inherit from parent policy unless an explicit narrower override is allowed. A child MUST NOT grant broader access to private ancestor material than the parent/project permits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sensitive operations such as permanent purge, private→public exposure, protected-domain override, remote replacement and destructive Root history rewrite require elevated permission and stronger confirmation; project policy MAY require 2FA.

heading: HEADING_3
text: CI, build and test checks

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Branches, Twigs and Leaves can run revision-pinned checks supplied by Dev, Automations or configured CI providers. CheckRun records provider, source DomainID/revision, workflow/config revision, status, logs/artifacts references and conclusion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Change Requests show required and optional checks. Protected destinations can require successful build/test/lint/security/package checks before promotion. A check result from an older source revision MUST NOT satisfy a requirement for a newer reviewed revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Checks run against the exact effective source of the target domain, including inherited ancestor state, not merely that domain's local delta.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Releases, tags and packages

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Release normally targets an approved Main revision. Project policy MAY permit another explicitly selected stable domain/revision, but the Release records its exact source identity and does not float with later domain changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Release has stable ReleaseID, source ProjectID/DomainID/revision, tag/version, notes, artifacts, checks, publisher, visibility and publication state. Tags map to immutable source revisions unless an explicit privileged retag operation is performed and audited.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Package/release distribution capabilities inherited from Gitea or shared 9to1 package infrastructure remain available where applicable. Packages record project, version, source/release revision, publisher, permissions and registry metadata so Dev can consume configured private/public feeds.

heading: HEADING_3
text: GitHub mirroring, backup and restore

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GitHub mirroring/backup records mirror configuration, last successful checkpoint and source/destination revisions. A mirror is never treated as current merely because the remote exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Restore can rebuild Stack state from the authoritative Git repository plus protected Stack manifests/object mappings and configured Files recovery metadata. Missing companion refs are reconstructed from retained object IDs when possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If complete reconstruction is impossible, Stack preserves available source/history, marks exact Domains/Roots/Subroots/changes that cannot be recovered and blocks writes that would destroy remaining recovery evidence. It MUST NOT fabricate successful restoration.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Sites and Dev integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites deployments/previews bind to exact Stack ProjectID, DomainID and revision. Branch/Twig/Leaf preview deployments are isolated where policy permits; production defaults to an approved Main release/revision unless explicitly configured otherwise.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites source edits are written back as normal changes in the bound Stack domain and become visible in diff/history/Change Requests. Sites MUST NOT maintain a hidden divergent source copy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Open in Dev opens the exact Stack domain/materialised effective source and provides ProjectID/DomainID/revision context. Dev edits become local Stack changes in that domain. Builds/tests/diffs shown in Stack and Dev reference the same canonical revision identities.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Issues and Boards integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack preserves source-oriented Issues, labels, milestones and repository issue workflows required by donor parity. Issues may link to commits, domains, Change Requests, releases and affected paths/resources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards owns richer planning/project-management workflows. Stack can create/link a Board card from an Issue and show linked Board state, while Boards can reference Stack issues/changes. The products MUST NOT silently duplicate and diverge two full project-management databases.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automations and webhooks

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack exposes typed triggers/actions for project/domain/change/review/release lifecycle through Automations. Webhooks/integrations can subscribe to events such as push/change committed, domain created/completed, Change Request opened/updated/merged, check completed, release published and issue changed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Webhook payloads expose stable IDs and permission-scoped data. Delivery has retry/idempotency identifiers and observable failure state; a failed webhook MUST NOT roll back an already-completed source operation unless an explicit transactional integration contract exists.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Public discovery, contributions and moderation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public projects expose profile, source/history/releases, contributors, forks, Change Requests and Discover integration without exposing Stack-managed internal storage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forking creates independent ProjectID/repository identity and records source-project provenance. Contributions return through a Change Request against an explicitly selected public destination domain and do not grant access to private components.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Moderation includes report/block capabilities, project-maintainer controls and platform policy enforcement for public-facing content. Moderation actions affecting source visibility/history are explicit and audited.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Sweep, prune, retention and purge

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sweep previews the descendant domains and changes to be consolidated into the owning Branch, verifies conflicts/checks as configured, applies accepted descendant changes to the Branch and only then marks/removes completed descendant development domains. It MUST NOT discard unmerged descendant work silently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prune removes a Branch/Twig/Leaf from active Stack navigation and requires the configured permission; protected project policy can require 2FA. Main can never be pruned.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pruned domains enter recoverable Deleted state for the configured retention period. Restore reactivates the same stable DomainID/backing references where retained objects remain valid.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permanent purge is a separate privileged operation and is blocked while retained objects are referenced by active descendants, releases, Change Requests, audit requirements or recovery points. Purge records what source/metadata was removed and what immutable audit evidence remains.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Audit log

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Audit coverage includes project creation/deletion/settings, domain create/reparent/archive/prune/restore/purge, commits and sync/push/fetch operations, Change Requests, approvals/overrides, conflicts and resolutions, Root/Subroot/Freeze lifecycle, permission/visibility changes, public projection, remote/mirror changes, releases/packages, CI/check state changes, moderation actions, autocommit actions and AI-authored actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Audit entries identify actor/initiator, stable target IDs, timestamp, operation type, relevant before/after revisions, outcome and linked recovery/change request where applicable. Sensitive values such as credentials are never logged.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Large repositories, binary data and LFS

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Repository browsing/history/diff uses virtualisation, paging and lazy content loading for large trees/histories. Stack MUST NOT materialise every domain or download every large object merely to open a project.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Binary files display metadata/history and binary-aware replacement state rather than bogus line diffs. Git LFS or an equivalent configured large-object backend is preserved where applicable; pointer/object availability is validated before claiming a domain/release is complete.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large-object quota/provider failures surface typed errors and do not silently replace missing binaries with empty files.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Metadata schema migration and disaster recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack-managed manifests and companion storage use explicit schema versions. Upgrades run idempotent migrations with pre-migration recovery checkpoints where feasible and never rewrite unknown/newer schema versions as if understood.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A migration failure leaves the previous recoverable state and marks the project NeedsMigration/Recovery rather than partially continuing normal writes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Disaster recovery documentation and APIs cover loss/corruption of local materialisations, Files backing, GitHub companion ref, metadata manifests and sync checkpoints. Recovery prioritises canonical source/history and stable IDs, reports unrecoverable state precisely and never fabricates missing commits/resources.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dulche and AI-assisted source control

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche context includes ProjectID, active/selected DomainID, ancestry/effective revisions, local/inherited changes, Roots/Subroots/Freezes, conflicts, Change Requests, checks, releases and permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples include explaining why a file differs from Main, summarising a Twig's owned changes, creating a Leaf for a task, proposing a conflict resolution and preparing a domain for promotion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI source mutations, conflict fixes, commits, domain creation and review actions use typed Stack/Dev/Files APIs. AI MUST NOT manipulate Stack-managed companion branches/folders through opaque shell/UI automation when a semantic action exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI claims about build/test/review readiness must reference actual executed check results for the pinned revision.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Autocommit

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Autocommit is disabled by default and must be enabled explicitly per repository/domain. It supports a configured elapsed interval or inactivity duration; settings may display friendly minutes while runtime stores precise duration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Autocommit detects eligible changes, excludes ignored/prohibited/known-secret material according to project security rules, refuses to run across unresolved conflicts, creates a normal canonical commit with an inspectable message/change selection and records the operation in audit history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Two policies are distinct: Autocommit locally only, and Autocommit + sync remote. Remote synchronisation occurs only when enabled and permitted. Failed push/sync leaves the commit local with explicit Ahead/SyncFailed state; Stack MUST NOT claim the domain is synced.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Autocommit can be disabled for individual repositories/domains even when enabled at a broader user/workspace level.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project/domain tree, change lists, diffs, conflict resolver, Change Requests, reviews, Root/Subroot/Freeze controls, releases and audit views are keyboard operable and expose screen-reader semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Addition/deletion/conflict/upstream/local/remote states MUST NOT rely only on colour or icons. +A/-D counts, status text and accessible descriptions identify state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Three-way conflict and diff views provide line/hunk navigation and textual descriptions usable without pointer-only interaction.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and resilience

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack virtualises large trees, history, diffs, reviews and audit streams; expensive lineage/effective-source calculations are cached by revision and invalidated deterministically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cascade, sync, Sweep, large Change Request checks, mirror operations and recovery run as cancellable/resumable jobs with stable JobID/progress/error state where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crash/restart MUST not lose canonical domain metadata, pending conflict state or accepted commits. Derived materialisations/caches may be discarded and reconstructed.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and typed failures

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured failures include ProjectNotFound, DomainNotFound, InvalidHierarchy, ReparentConflict, MaterialisationFailed, SourceCorrupt, ManagedMetadataMissing, SchemaVersionUnsupported, MigrationFailed, UpstreamConflict, ConflictUnresolved, RootLocked, RootClaimed, FreezeActive, ChangeRequestOutOfDate, RequiredCheckFailed, ApprovalRequired, SyncConflict, RemoteUnavailable, MirrorFailed, PrivateProjectionViolation, LFSObjectMissing, RestoreIncomplete, PurgeBlocked, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable plus provider-specific Git/Files errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Operations that partially affect external remotes or mirrors report exact completed/failed stages and preserve recovery checkpoints. Stack MUST NOT report rollback, restore, sync or merge success unless the resulting canonical and provider state was verified as required by that operation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Project/Domain/Root/Subroot/Freeze/ChangeRequest model. Local materialisation, Git executable availability, filesystem semantics, credential providers and build integrations are capability-negotiated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a platform cannot safely materialise or execute a local action, Stack uses an explicitly configured service/remote provider or reports CapabilityUnavailable; it MUST NOT silently change source-control semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Stack follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Main → Branch → Twig → Leaf hierarchy persists stable DomainIDs across rename/reopen and enforces legal parent/child types.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A child records its base revision and effective source correctly combines ancestor plus local deltas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening/building two domains concurrently does not require user-facing worktree switching and does not mix their writes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Local +A/-D counts exclude inherited ancestor changes, while upstream state remains inspectable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A non-conflicting Main change cascades through Branch/Twig/Leaf effective source; a conflicting resource pauses only the affected cascade and creates a structured Conflict.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A descendant tombstone prevents a deliberately deleted inherited resource from reappearing after a later cascade.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A tracked rename preserves lineage across a subsequent ancestor edit or surfaces an explicit ambiguity conflict.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Leaf → Twig → Branch → Main promotion uses revision-pinned Change Requests, required approvals/checks and produces an auditable resulting revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A reviewed source revision changing after approval invalidates/re-runs policy as configured rather than merging unreviewed edits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conflict resolver supports manual three-way resolution and reviewed AI proposals with Reject, Accept without Merging and Accept and Merge semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Root enforcement blocks descendant override while an authorised owning-domain Root update cascades normally.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Subroot claims non-overlapping Roots, runs required review/checks, completes into the owning Root and releases its claims; Main cannot create Subroots.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Freeze applies only to configured descendant scope, cannot be bypassed by ordinary clients, and early/automatic thaw follows permissions/audit rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files-backed managed folders/manifests validate on open and damaged derived state can be reconstructed without treating internal metadata as user source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GitHub-backed Branches remain native Git branches while Twig/Leaf/Subroot history survives through protected Stack companion metadata without appearing as normal Branches.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deleting the GitHub companion ref triggers deterministic recovery where retained objects permit it and otherwise reports exact unrecoverable state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dual Files+GitHub mode records authority/sync checkpoints and surfaces concurrent divergence as SyncConflict instead of last-writer-wins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A mixed public/private project cannot publish a projection whose reachable tree/history includes private source or credentials.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Raw Git operations that would corrupt Stack lineage/managed refs are blocked or require explicit advanced reconciliation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project/domain permissions prevent a child from granting access beyond private ancestor/project policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Revision-pinned CI/check results gate protected promotions and stale check results cannot satisfy a newer revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Release records immutable source revision/tag/artifacts/check state and package metadata remains linked to its source revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GitHub mirror/backup status exposes the last verified checkpoint and restore does not claim success when objects are unrecoverable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites preview/production deployment and Open in Dev retain exact Stack ProjectID/DomainID/revision identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stack Issues can link to Boards without duplicating Boards as a divergent project-management database.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations/webhooks receive typed stable-ID lifecycle events with observable delivery failure state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public forks use independent identity/provenance and cannot expose private Stack-managed storage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sweep previews/consolidates descendant work before removal; Prune is recoverable; Purge is separately privileged and blocked by active references.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Autocommit is opt-in, does not run over unresolved conflicts/ignored or prohibited content, and distinguishes local commit from remote sync success.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large repositories/history use virtualised/lazy behaviour and missing LFS objects are reported instead of replaced silently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Metadata migration is versioned/idempotent and migration failure preserves recoverable prior state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Audit history covers source, permission, visibility, Root/Freeze/Subroot, review, release, prune/purge, mirror, autocommit and AI actions without logging secrets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard/screen-reader workflows cover domain navigation, diffs, conflict resolution and review.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Stack model while capability-negotiating local materialisation/Git support.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Stack follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Sites

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and ownership principle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Sites is the native CUI visual website-building, CMS, preview and deployment surface. It MUST support professional source-backed websites and web applications while remaining approachable for users who prefer visual authoring.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites owns visual page/component authoring, responsive layout, site design systems, CMS/content authoring, routes/navigation, preview/deployment orchestration, domains, site diagnostics and site-specific runtime configuration. Dev owns general-purpose code engineering, Stack owns source-control/collaboration history, Files owns canonical file/asset identity, Data owns structured data/database semantics and Forms owns form/assessment runtime semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A SiteProject MUST remain user-owned and addressable as real structured project/source state. Sites MUST NOT make opaque generated output the only canonical representation or require an export-to-code step for ordinary Dev/Stack interoperability.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Primary donor: cakemods site plugin

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The latest appropriate cakemods website/site-plugin source is the primary donor and implementation reference for Sites. Its visual Page Editor, reusable-section/component model, design-system integration, preview behaviour, editor-shell/public-route separation, authoring quality-of-life and proven website-management behaviours MUST be preserved, expanded or replaced by demonstrably equivalent 9to1-native implementations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Implementation MUST inspect/fetch the current donor source at implementation time if it is not present in the canonical development environment, subject to licensing and the global donor rules. A simplified greenfield page builder is not an acceptable substitute merely because it is easier to implement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites may replace WordPress/PHP-specific storage, admin or runtime coupling with 9to1-native project, CUI, API and provider infrastructure, but donor functionality and useful interaction semantics must survive unless explicitly documented as not applicable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Donor parity audit

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A donor-parity inventory MUST classify every meaningful cakemods site/editor capability as Preserved, Expanded, Replaced by 9to1-native equivalent, or Not applicable with a recorded reason.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Parity review includes visual page editing, reusable sections/components, design-system/token handling, editor/public-shell ownership, page preview, route-specific asset/style loading, responsive behaviour, component state, site/content management, recovery and mature editing QoL visible in the donor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Missing donor source is not permission to invent a toy substitute; the autonomous implementation process must obtain the latest appropriate donor source where the global donor contract permits.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical SiteProject model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SiteProject has stable SiteID/ProjectID, source binding, framework/project type, Pages[], Routes[], Components[], ReusableComponents[], Layouts[], Theme/DesignSystem, Assets[], ContentCollections[], NavigationModels[], LogicGraphIDs[], DataBindings[], FormBindings[], Environments[], Deployments[], Domains[], Redirects[], SEO configuration, Analytics/Consent configuration, ExtensionState, Settings and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page, Route, Component, ContentCollection, ContentRecord, Asset reference, Deployment and Domain binding each use stable identifiers that do not depend on mutable display names, URL paths or visual order unless the entity is explicitly path-addressed by design.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persisted Sites-native formats are versioned. Unknown incompatible schema versions are rejected/preserved/migrated explicitly; they are not silently reinterpreted.

heading: HEADING_3
text: New Site and framework/project creation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: New Site provides searchable templates/project types such as Blank, marketing/business site, portfolio, blog, documentation, landing page, web application, community/project site, content-driven site and other installed provider templates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where applicable the user selects framework/runtime/provider rather than being forced into one proprietary framework. First-party/native Sites projects and supported source projects may include HTML/CSS/JavaScript and registered framework providers such as React/Next/Astro or later equivalents when those providers can preserve the required round-trip contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Existing source projects may be opened from Stack/Dev. Sites MUST detect whether the selected framework/provider supports full visual round-trip, partial visual representation or preview-only mode and state the capability clearly.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Visual Page Editor

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The normal Sites authoring surface is heavily based on the cakemods Page Editor model: site/page tree or layers, central visual canvas/preview and contextual Inspector/properties, with source available through Dev.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can create, select, move, nest, duplicate, hide, delete and configure supported components directly on the canvas/tree. Selection state is synchronised across canvas, component tree, Inspector, node graph and Dev/source mapping where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The editor manipulates canonical page/component state rather than a screenshot approximation. Published output, preview, Dulche actions and APIs consume the same semantic component/project model.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Component and section model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites uses a canonical structured component tree. Core component categories include section/container, header, footer, navigation, text/heading, image/media, button/link, card, list, table, form host, dialog, tabs/accordion, gallery, hero/splash, sidebar/rail, CMS collection renderer, embed, custom component and extension-contributed types.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Component has stable ComponentID, ComponentType, properties, child/slot structure, layout, design-token/style references, responsive overrides, bindings, interaction references, component state, accessibility properties, source mapping where applicable and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The donor's reusable-section/component concept is preserved and expanded. User/org component libraries may provide reusable headers, footers, heroes, pricing blocks, FAQs, CTAs and domain-specific components.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Reusable components and sections

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A reusable component/section definition has stable definition identity and may be instantiated across pages. Instances can expose declared properties/slots while inheriting the definition's structure/style/logic.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites distinguishes linked instances from detached copies. Editing a linked definition updates its instances according to override rules; Detach creates an independent component tree and must be an explicit operation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Overrides are structured and traceable. Sites MUST NOT duplicate an entire reusable definition into each instance merely to support one overridden property.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Editor-shell and public-route context ownership

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites MUST preserve the donor architecture's strict separation between editor/admin chrome and the public site being edited. Public headers, footers, theme chrome and public-only CSS MUST NOT leak into the Sites editor shell unless rendered inside the isolated public preview.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rendering contexts include at least editor shell, public/live route, page preview, component preview and CMS/dynamic preview. Each context resolves an explicit asset/style/component ownership manifest.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context boundaries are testable. A component or style registered only for a public route MUST NOT accidentally become part of the editor shell merely because the preview is open.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Layout and page composition

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The visual editor supports mature responsive web layout including normal document flow, stack/flex-style layout, grid, wrapping, alignment, gaps, padding/margins, min/max sizing, aspect ratio, container widths, sticky/fixed positioning where supported, overlays and deliberate absolute/freeform positioning.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured responsive layout is the default. Sites MUST NOT represent ordinary pages as arbitrary fixed coordinates that only happen to fit one viewport.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page/component hierarchy and layout rules remain editable through the Inspector and typed Sites actions; visual drag/reorder is a convenience over the same model.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Responsive design and breakpoints

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites provides desktop, tablet, phone and custom responsive previews plus drag-resizable viewport inspection. Breakpoints come from the active project/design system and may be provider-defined.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Responsive properties inherit through a predictable cascade. A breakpoint override records only the changed properties rather than cloning the entire page.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Inspector shows whether a value is inherited, defined at the current breakpoint or overridden elsewhere and allows resetting an override to inherited state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Design system and tokens

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Site-wide design state includes semantic colour tokens, typography, spacing scale, radius, shadows, breakpoints, container widths, component variants, interaction states and theme modes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Components SHOULD reference semantic design tokens rather than duplicating unrelated literal styling where the project/provider supports tokens. Changing a shared token updates consumers without rewriting page structure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites preserves the cakemods donor's design-system ownership concepts while migrating them into shared 9to1 theme/component APIs where appropriate.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Themes and component variants

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites supports site theme variants including light/dark/system modes where configured. Theme changes MUST NOT destroy page content or component structure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Components may define named variants and states such as primary/secondary button, compact/feature card, Default/Hover/Focused/Disabled/Loading/Error/Selected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual preview can force a component state for design inspection without mutating production runtime state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Visual source round-trip and code-defined constructs

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites and Dev operate on the same canonical project/source wherever the active framework/provider supports round-tripping. A visual property change updates the real source/project representation; a supported source edit is reflected back into Sites after parse/reconcile.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Source mapping relates runtime/visual components to component definitions, project resources and source ranges/symbols where available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a valid project construct cannot be represented visually, Sites MUST preserve it and mark it Code-defined, Partially visual or another explicit capability state. It MUST NOT delete, flatten or rewrite unsupported code simply to make the canvas editable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated code/assets derived from canonical node graphs or Sites metadata are marked as generated with provenance. Users are not encouraged to hand-edit generated output unless the provider declares supported reverse mapping.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Pages, routes and navigation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Page and Route are distinct canonical concepts. A Page may render at one or more routes according to provider/project rules; Routes support static, nested and parameterised/dynamic paths, redirects and error/not-found routes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing a route checks internal references and can offer redirects. Navigation items SHOULD reference PageID/RouteID for internal destinations rather than storing only fragile path strings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Navigation models support reusable menus, nested entries, active-state semantics, external links and conditional visibility where permitted.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Preview fidelity and asset manifest

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites preview MUST use the same applicable component styles, theme assets, route-specific assets, fonts and rendering rules as the corresponding public/live route wherever technically possible. The cakemods donor's route/context asset-manifest discipline is a mandatory architectural reference.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preview MUST NOT be a separately styled mock that can pass while the published page renders differently. Differences caused by deployment-only services are declared explicitly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Route-specific assets such as homepage-only CSS/scripts are loaded only in applicable preview/live contexts and MUST NOT leak into unrelated pages or editor chrome.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Live preview and last-valid render

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preview modes include in-editor canvas, interactive preview, full-screen preview and shareable preview deployment where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the framework/provider supports it, source/visual edits trigger incremental build/hot reload. Preview state visibly reports Live, Building, Reloading, Build failed, Disconnected or Paused.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a new change fails to build/render, Sites preserves the last valid preview and overlays/links the current diagnostics rather than replacing the canvas with an uninformative blank page.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Stack source-control integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A SiteProject may bind directly to Stack ProjectID/DomainID/revision. Editing context clearly identifies Main, Branch, Twig or Leaf and the exact source revision used for preview/deployment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites edits become ordinary reviewable source changes in the selected Stack domain. Sites MUST NOT create an anonymous divergent copy when a source-backed Stack project is active.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Branch/Twig/Leaf preview deployments bind to exact revisions. Production deployment defaults to an approved Main/release revision unless project policy explicitly authorises another source.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dev integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Open in Dev opens the same project/domain/source identity, optionally preserving selected page/component/source mapping. Open in Sites from Dev opens the visual authoring surface for the same compatible resource.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev Code | Preview may use Sites as the preview provider. Source edits, build diagnostics and visual preview remain revision-linked rather than being transferred through export/import.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Advanced code-defined components, server functions, framework configuration and tests remain fully available in Dev even when the visual Sites surface presents simplified controls.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Full shared Node Graph Framework

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites exposes the full shared 9to1 Node Graph Framework for advanced interaction and application behaviour. The node editor is a first-class companion to the cakemods-derived visual Page Editor rather than a separate incompatible automation product.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual Editor primarily answers structure/content/layout/style; Node Editor primarily owns events, runtime state, dynamic data, navigation/action flows, integrations and advanced animation/interaction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Graph objects use stable GraphID/NodeID/PortID identity, typed connections, validation, grouping/comments, copy/paste, undo/redo, Draft/Published revision semantics and Dulche mutation through 9to1.NodeGraph.*.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Simple interaction UI and graph parity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordinary interactions remain approachable without opening nodes. Examples include Button → Navigate to page, open dialog, submit Form, set link or trigger a simple animation through Inspector controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Simple interaction configuration MUST map to the same canonical behaviour/graph primitives used by the advanced Node Editor, or to a formally shared behaviour object represented consistently in both views.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Open in Node Editor reveals/extends the advanced representation without silently changing the simple configured behaviour.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Sites node events, conditions and actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative Sites events include PageLoaded/Unloaded, RouteChanged, ComponentClicked, Hovered, Focused, ValueChanged, Submitted, ScrollChanged, EnteredViewport, UserSignedIn/Out, CMSRecordChanged, timer/custom component events and provider/extension events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative actions include Navigate/Redirect, UpdateComponentProperty/State, Show/Hide, Enable/Disable, Open/CloseDialog, ScrollTo, SetVariable, PlayAnimation, query/mutate permitted CMS/Data state, invoke Forms/Automation actions, call permitted API/server functions and emit custom events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Conditions include typed comparisons, boolean combinations, role/auth state, viewport/capability state, collection/query results, component state and validation outcomes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Node execution contexts and trust boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every executable node declares execution context/capabilities such as client-safe, server/trusted backend, build-time, deployment-provider or external integration. Sites MUST NOT compile secrets or trusted permission checks into untrusted browser execution merely because a graph contains them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Security-sensitive permission, private Data mutation and credential operations are executed/verified in trusted environments through owning APIs. Client-side visibility logic is not an access-control boundary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The graph editor visually identifies execution-boundary transitions and validates impossible/unsafe client↔server data flows before publish where determinable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Node debugger and runtime inspection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Interactive preview includes node debugging: executed node/path highlighting, breakpoint/pause where supported, values, state variables, execution timing, errors and linked network/provider failures.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A user can exercise a page interaction and inspect the actual path taken through the graph rather than treating the node canvas as a static diagram.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Runtime inspection uses development/test context and respects secret redaction/permission boundaries.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Component state and node-driven animation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Components can expose named runtime states and node transitions, for example ProductCard Default → Loading → Selected/Error.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Simple animations remain configurable visually; advanced sequences may use graph/timeline primitives such as EnteredViewport → easing/spring → opacity/transform/property changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Responsive layout is normally expressed through design/layout breakpoints rather than width-check node spaghetti. Runtime viewport/capability nodes are reserved for behaviour that is genuinely conditional rather than ordinary responsive styling.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Native CMS and content collections

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites includes a native structured CMS. ContentCollection has stable CollectionID, schema fields/types, indexes/constraints where supported, relationships, permissions, publishing workflow and Revision. ContentRecord has stable RecordID independent of display title/slug.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typical collections include BlogPost, Product, Event, TeamMember, DocumentationPage or user-defined schemas. Supported fields include text/rich content, slug, number, boolean, date/time, media/File reference, enum, reference, list/set and structured/nested data where the provider supports it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CMS authoring provides list/table and record-editing interfaces appropriate to the schema rather than forcing content authors into page source.

heading: HEADING_3
text: CMS relationships and dynamic content

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Collections support references and one-to-one, one-to-many and many-to-many relations where the selected backend permits them. Relationship identity uses stable collection/record IDs rather than matching display strings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dynamic components can bind to record fields or collection queries. Collection renderers support filtering, sorting, pagination/loading and empty/loading/error states.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Complex structured data/database requirements may delegate to Data; Sites CMS remains optimised for web content authoring rather than duplicating Data's complete database product.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dynamic routes and page templates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dynamic routes such as /blog/:slug can bind to a collection/query and a reusable page template. Route resolution detects duplicate/conflicting slugs and unavailable records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dynamic page preview can select representative records and preserves the template/record distinction; editing template layout does not silently mutate record content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated sitemap/canonical metadata use resolved published routes/records rather than draft-only paths.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Rich content authoring

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CMS/page rich content supports headings, paragraphs, lists, links, images/media, tables, quotes, code blocks and registered rich components where supported. Long-form content MUST NOT require hand-authoring raw HTML for ordinary use.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rich content remains structured and sanitised according to project/runtime security policy; pasted content does not gain arbitrary executable privilege.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Data integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites can bind components, collections or server-side flows to Data projects/tables/queries through typed Data APIs. Examples include product grids, member dashboards, reporting widgets or structured content sources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Bindings reference stable Data IDs/fields and preserve typed values, permissions and Data's live-database protection semantics. Sites MUST NOT bypass Data safeguards by issuing hidden raw mutations directly to backing databases.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Data-backed collection/rendering state includes loading, empty, error and stale/unavailable handling.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Forms integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites embeds 9to1 Forms natively by referencing FormID/FormVersionID or another supported Forms embed/runtime reference. Contact forms, registrations, applications, quizzes and custom Forms modes remain owned by Forms.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Site styling may provide theme/context integration without discarding Forms validation, accessibility, response versioning, anti-abuse, assessment or Data-binding semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms events exposed to Sites node graphs are typed and permission-scoped.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files and asset management

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites uses Files as canonical asset/file identity where appropriate. Asset references include stable File/Asset IDs, origin/provenance, usage references, alt/caption metadata, transformations/derived variants and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The asset browser supports images, video, icons, documents, fonts where licensing permits and other registered media. Moving/renaming a Files-backed asset MUST NOT break references that use stable identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deleting an asset checks/reports site usages and follows Files recovery semantics rather than silently replacing broken content.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Image/media optimisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites supports crop/focal point, responsive image variants, appropriate format optimisation, lazy/loading policy and alt text. The canonical source/original remains preserved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated responsive thumbnails/encodings are derived build/cache assets with provenance; Sites MUST NOT create untracked duplicate originals merely to satisfy one page size.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Video/media embeds distinguish first-party/file media from external providers and expose privacy/performance implications.

heading: HEADING_3
text: SEO and discoverability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Per-page/route SEO supports title, meta description, canonical URL, robots/index policy, Open Graph/social metadata, structured data/schema and sitemap inclusion. Site-level configuration covers canonical hostname, sitemap, robots.txt and defaults.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites provides structured diagnostics for missing/duplicate titles, missing descriptions where policy expects them, broken canonical references, inaccessible/missing image alternatives and other deterministic SEO problems it can verify.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI may propose SEO content but must not invent factual business claims or silently publish changes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility diagnostics and guardrails

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites continuously checks representative accessibility requirements including contrast, missing image alternatives, semantic labels, heading order, focus/keyboard accessibility, colour-only state, touch target sizing, animation/reduced-motion behaviour and custom component accessibility where inspectable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accessibility issues appear as structured diagnostics tied to PageID/ComponentID/source location where possible and integrate with Dev Problems/Dulche context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual design freedom MUST NOT silently disable required semantic labels, focus order or other minimum accessibility behaviour.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and web-quality diagnostics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites surfaces web-performance problems it can determine such as oversized images/media, excessive bundles/scripts/fonts, known render-blocking resources, large page payloads and expensive third-party dependencies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preview/build may expose measurable runtime metrics where the provider/runtime supports reliable collection. Unknown metrics remain unknown rather than fabricated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Optimisation actions preserve behaviour/source ownership and remain inspectable changes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Domains, redirects and HTTPS

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites manages custom-domain bindings through a typed DomainBinding model with stable DomainBindingID, environment, hostname, canonical/apex/www policy, verification state, DNS requirements, TLS/HTTPS state and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can attach/remove domains, choose canonical host, configure redirects and inspect ownership/DNS/TLS status. Provider integrations may automate required DNS records only within the authorised scope and MUST NOT alter unrelated records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Route/domain changes identify broken links/redirect opportunities and do not claim a domain is live until provider verification succeeds.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Deployment environments

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites supports explicit Development/Preview and Production environments, plus Staging or provider-defined environments where configured.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deployment has stable DeploymentID, SiteID/ProjectID, Stack DomainID/revision where applicable, environment, build/config revision, provider, URL, build result, deployment result, timestamps, actor/initiator and status.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A deployment is pinned to source/config revisions. A preview URL MUST identify a concrete deployment/revision rather than silently floating to whatever source is latest.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Deployment providers and build pipeline

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deployment uses a provider abstraction. First-party/connected providers may offer static hosting, edge/server functions, object storage/CDN, DNS/domain integration and preview deployments according to capabilities. Extensions can register additional providers.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Build pipeline exposes dependency restore, build/generate, validation, packaging and deploy/verify stages where applicable. Failures produce typed diagnostics and stage status rather than a generic Deployment failed result.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites does not hard-code one provider's CLI/configuration as the canonical project model; provider-specific settings may be retained as explicit provider configuration.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Deployment history, rollback and publishing safeguards

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites preserves deployment history with source revision, configuration, build/check result, provider/environment, actor and URL/status.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rollback normally redeploys a previously successful known source/config revision; it MUST NOT erase newer source history merely to return production to an earlier deployment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Production publish is an external consequential action. The UI/API shows environment, domain, source DomainID/revision, build/check state and meaningful warnings before execution according to the global permission model. AI MUST NOT silently publish to production without an explicit authorised action/automation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Custom code, scripts and server functions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Advanced projects support controlled custom CSS, JavaScript/TypeScript/modules, head/body markup hooks, custom components and server/API functions according to framework/provider capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom code is source-backed, versioned and visible in Dev/Stack; Sites MUST NOT store consequential executable snippets only in an invisible proprietary database.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Server functions/endpoints are real project resources with Dev debugging/testing where supported. Sites may provide simplified configuration but does not invent an incompatible second backend language/runtime.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Environment variables and secrets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites distinguishes public build/runtime values from private server/provider secrets. Secret values use shared secure credential infrastructure where possible and are referenced by ID/name rather than committed into project source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Secrets MUST NOT be exposed into browser bundles, logs, previews, AI context or generated diffs unless the operation explicitly requires the value and the caller/environment is authorised.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Build/deploy diagnostics redact secret values while preserving enough context to identify which configured secret/reference failed.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Authentication and member areas

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites may integrate with 9to1 identity/auth providers to create login/account/member experiences and restricted routes/components. Identity objects and permissions remain owned by the shared identity/security layer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Restricted page visibility alone is not a security boundary; backend/private data access requires server-side authorisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Member/user-specific page state is represented explicitly so preview/test can simulate authorised roles without embedding real private credentials.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Localisation and site search

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites supports locale-aware content/routes, language selector, fallback language and alternate-language SEO metadata where enabled. Translations remain editable content with provenance even when AI-assisted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Site search can index selected published pages, CMS collections and permitted Data-backed content. Search provider/index state is typed and exposes stale/rebuild/error state for dynamic content.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Analytics, scripts and consent

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites supports registered analytics/providers and custom events without silently injecting tracking. Analytics configuration identifies provider, enabled environments, events/scopes and privacy/consent requirements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consent configuration can categorise integrations/scripts such as Essential, Preferences, Analytics and Advertising and delay applicable execution until consent where configured/required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Templates MUST NOT silently enable third-party tracking merely because the donor/template contained a tracking snippet.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Collaboration and revisions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Concurrent authoring uses stable page/component/content revisions and conflict detection. Sites MUST NOT silently overwrite another editor's changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Comments/review may attach to PageID/ComponentID/content where supported; source-level review remains available through Stack/Dev.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual and source edits participate in the same canonical revision/history model so conflicts can identify semantic component/property changes where possible.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dulche AI authoring and visual QA

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche semantic context includes SiteID/ProjectID, current Stack DomainID/revision, selected PageID/ComponentID, route, component hierarchy, layout/responsive breakpoint, design tokens, CMS schema/record, bindings, node graph selection, diagnostics, preview/build/deployment state and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI may create/refactor pages, components, responsive layouts, themes, CMS schemas/content, bindings, node graphs, SEO metadata and project structure only through typed Sites/shared-domain actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-created sites are ordinary editable SiteProjects, not screenshots or opaque generated bundles.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: UI-oriented AI changes SHOULD use available visual preview/QA in addition to build success. Overflow, clipped content, broken responsive layout, inaccessible contrast and visibly failed states must not be declared correct solely because compilation passed.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shared extension system

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites participates in the shared 9to1 extension platform. Extensions may contribute components, component inspectors, CMS field types, Data sources/bindings, deployment providers, analytics/SEO integrations, project templates, visual-builder panels, node types and preview/runtime providers.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension contributions declare target Sites API version, permissions/capabilities and compatible platforms. A crashing extension must be containable/disableable according to the shared extension-host contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites extension development can be created/debugged from Dev's 9to1 Extension project type and appropriate Sites Extension Host.

heading: HEADING_3
text: First-party Sites URL namespace

heading: HEADING_3
text: Every publishable SiteProject receives or may reserve a first-party Sites URL under https://sites.9to1.uk/<site-slug>. The first-party URL is path-based rather than per-site DNS subdomain. Site identity remains stable even if the slug changes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: The site slug and Sites-managed route segments use the restricted lowercase character set a-z and hyphen; slash is the path-segment separator. Digits, spaces, underscores, mixed case, Unicode lookalikes and other punctuation are not valid in the first-party Sites namespace. A segment MUST NOT begin or end with a hyphen, and empty/repeated path segments are rejected. Sites normalises valid input to one canonical URL representation rather than allowing visually ambiguous aliases.

heading: HEADING_3
text: For example, a project may publish at sites.9to1.uk/cake and expose routes such as sites.9to1.uk/cake/about or sites.9to1.uk/cake/contact-us. Reserved platform/system names cannot be claimed as ordinary site slugs.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Slug availability is checked atomically at reservation/publish time. Changing a published slug is explicit and can create a managed redirect from the previous first-party URL according to retention/conflict policy.

heading: HEADING_3
HEADING_3
text: AI name and domain verification

heading: HEADING_3
text: Every requested first-party site slug and every custom domain binding MUST pass automated name-safety verification before it can become an active public identity. Verification combines deterministic checks with an AI-assisted misleading-name assessment.

heading: HEADING_3
text: The assessment looks for likely impersonation, deceptive affiliation claims, confusingly similar names, misleading government/financial/security/support identities, obvious brand/person spoofing, homograph/punycode concerns for custom domains and other patterns that could materially mislead visitors about who operates the site. The AI assessment is a safety signal, not proof of wrongdoing.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Clear safe names may pass automatically. Ambiguous/high-risk names enter a PendingReview state rather than being silently published or permanently rejected by an opaque model decision. The user can see a meaningful reason category and use the supported review/appeal path where applicable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Owning or controlling a custom domain does not bypass misleading-name screening, and passing misleading-name screening does not prove domain ownership. Name-safety verification and technical ownership verification are separate mandatory gates.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Verification records use stable VerificationID, subject URL/domain, normalized representation, rules/model version, decision state, reason categories, timestamps and review/audit references. Sensitive model internals need not be exposed, but the user-visible result must be actionable and non-deceptive.

heading: HEADING_3
HEADING_3
text: Custom domains and provider connections

heading: HEADING_3
text: Sites supports custom apex domains and subdomains in addition to the default sites.9to1.uk/<site-slug> address. The user chooses which verified address is canonical and can configure redirects from other bound addresses.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Manual custom-domain ownership verification MUST use a secure provider-independent challenge, normally a purpose-specific DNS TXT record or equivalent proof whose random token is bound to the SiteID/account and expires/rotates according to policy. Merely entering a hostname, receiving traffic for it or controlling a Sites project is not sufficient proof of ownership.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Domain takeover protections include checking existing active claims, challenge freshness, account/site binding, DNS result validation, canonicalized IDN/punycode representation and safe reassignment/release semantics. A domain already actively bound elsewhere cannot be silently stolen by a second project.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Sites MAY connect to supported DNS/domain providers such as Cloudflare and later providers through typed provider integrations. With explicitly scoped authorization, a connected provider may enumerate eligible zones, create/verify only the required challenge/serving records, inspect DNS/TLS readiness and maintain authorised redirects/routing.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Provider authorization MUST be least-privilege where the provider permits it. Connecting a provider for one site/domain does not grant Sites permission to rewrite unrelated zones or records. All DNS mutations show affected zone/record scope through the global permission model and remain auditable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: If automated provider configuration is unavailable, Sites presents exact manual DNS instructions and continuously exposes Pending, Verified, Misconfigured, Conflict or provider-specific failure state without pretending propagation has completed.

heading: HEADING_3
HEADING_3
text: Canonical Sites directory in Files

heading: HEADING_3
text: Every SiteProject has an explicit user-addressable project directory under the user's Sites area in Files, conceptually Sites/<Project Name>/, or an equivalent stable Files location selected/managed by the user.

heading: HEADING_3
text: That directory contains the actual source-backed site resources appropriate to the project's framework: source, public/static assets, component/page resources, framework manifests/configuration and versioned Sites project metadata where applicable. Sites-internal derived caches or provider credentials MUST NOT be mixed into user source as if they were canonical project content.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files identity is canonical for Files-backed resources. Moving or renaming the project directory through supported Files/Sites operations preserves SiteID/project binding through stable IDs rather than creating a new site accidentally.

heading: HEADING_3
text: The site MUST remain reconstructable and editable from the canonical Sites/Files/Stack project resources. An external host MUST NOT be the only surviving copy of the source project.

heading: HEADING_3
HEADING_3
text: External hosting and deployment authority

heading: HEADING_3
text: The public website is stored/served through an external HostingProvider or configured first-party hosting service backed by an external provider. The deployed copy is derived runtime/deployment state, not an independently editable canonical authority.

heading: HEADING_3
text: The authority chain is: canonical editable Sites project and Files/Stack source → revision-pinned build artifact → external provider deployment → first-party/custom domain routing. Each Deployment records SiteID, source DomainID/revision where applicable, build/config revision, provider identity and deployment artifact/result identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Provider-hosted state may include generated static output, server bundles/functions, optimized media, CDN/cache objects and runtime configuration. These artifacts retain deployment provenance but do not replace canonical source.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Direct provider-side edits that cannot be mapped back to canonical source are treated as external drift. Sites MUST NOT silently adopt them as canonical. Where import/reconciliation is supported it is an explicit reviewed operation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: If a hosting provider is unavailable, loses deployment state or the user changes provider, Sites can rebuild from canonical Files/Stack source, deploy to another configured provider, remap first-party/custom-domain routing and verify the resulting deployment. Recovery MUST NOT depend on scraping the live public website to reconstruct the project.

heading: HEADING_3
HEADING_3

heading: HEADING_3

heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1.Sites.ChangeSlug(siteID, slug, options?);

heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1.Sites.VerifyPublicName(target, options?);

heading: HEADING_3
