heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1.Sites.BeginDomainVerification(siteID, domain, options?);

heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1.Sites.VerifyDomain(domainBindingID, options?);

heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1.Sites.ConnectDomainProvider(provider, scopes, options?);

heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1.Sites.ConfigureDomainRecords(domainBindingID, options?);

heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1.Sites.GetHostingState(siteID, environmentID?);

heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1.Sites.ChangeHostingProvider(siteID, providerID, options?);

heading: HEADING_3
text: Provider-specific DNS/hosting mutations still use the shared credential/permission model and MUST NOT bypass Sites deployment/domain safeguards.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automation and typed events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites emits typed events such as PageCreated/Changed, ComponentChanged, RouteChanged, ContentPublished/Changed, BuildStarted/Completed/Failed, PreviewCreated, DeploymentStarted/Completed/Failed, DomainVerified/Failed, DiagnosticChanged and provider/extension lifecycle events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations/agents consume stable IDs and permission-scoped data. External deployment/domain/content publication side effects remain subject to the global Home permission broker and product-specific protections.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Security and abuse boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites sanitises/validates untrusted rich content, embed/custom code boundaries and public form/data interactions according to the active runtime/provider security model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public site content MUST NOT gain access to Sites editor/admin privileges merely because it is rendered in preview. Preview documents/iframes/processes use isolation appropriate to the platform.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public/private source, CMS records, Data bindings and credentials preserve their owning permission boundaries through build and deployment.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and large-site behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites virtualises large page/component trees, CMS record lists, assets and deployment history. It loads/compiles only the content/assets needed for the active authoring/preview workflow where possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large CMS collections, asset libraries and Data-backed lists use paging/streaming rather than unbounded UI payloads. Preview/build work is cancellable where technically possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual editing MUST remain responsive while builds/deployments/background indexing occur; long work exposes JobID/progress/status rather than blocking the editor.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Draft visual/source edits are crash-recoverable where feasible and do not corrupt the last valid published/deployed source revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A failed build/deploy leaves the prior successful deployment intact unless the provider itself performed an irreversible partial side effect; Sites reports each completed/failed stage accurately.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured failures include SiteNotFound, PageNotFound, ComponentNotFound, UnsupportedVisualConstruct, SourceRoundTripConflict, RouteConflict, CMSValidationFailed, BindingUnavailable, NodeGraphInvalid, PreviewBuildFailed, BuildFailed, DeploymentFailed, ProviderUnavailable, DomainVerificationFailed, DNSConflict, SecretUnavailable, PrivateDataExposureBlocked, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable plus provider-specific errors.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical SiteProject/Page/Component/CMS/NodeGraph/Deployment models while capability-negotiating local framework tooling, embedded preview, browser isolation, filesystem/source access and provider integrations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A platform that cannot provide local build/runtime functionality uses an explicitly configured remote/provider capability or reports CapabilityUnavailable; it MUST NOT silently fake preview/build/deployment completion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Sites follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The latest appropriate cakemods site-plugin donor has been audited and each meaningful editor/site capability is preserved, expanded, replaced equivalently or explicitly marked not applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A source-backed site opens in the cakemods-derived visual editor with stable Page/Component identity and can be edited without an export-to-code step.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editor-shell/public-route isolation prevents public site header/footer/styles from leaking into Sites chrome while isolated preview still renders the selected public structures.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preview loads the same applicable route/theme/component asset manifest as the live route for representative homepage and ordinary-page cases.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A supported visual property edited in Sites updates the canonical source/project and a supported Dev source edit round-trips back into Sites.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An unsupported valid code construct is preserved and shown as Code-defined/partial rather than silently deleted or flattened.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Responsive desktop/tablet/mobile overrides inherit correctly without cloning the entire page and can be reset to inherited state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A linked reusable section updates its instances while Detach produces an independent instance without corrupting the original definition.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Simple Inspector interaction such as Button → Navigate behaves consistently with the advanced Node Editor representation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Sites node graph can implement a dynamic flow such as click → query/update state → show result, and the preview node debugger exposes the executed path/values.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A security-sensitive graph operation is kept in its trusted execution context and is not compiled into an untrusted client bundle with secrets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CMS collections create typed records/relationships and drive a dynamic route such as /blog/:slug without unstable title-string identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Forms embed retains Forms validation/runtime semantics and Data binding uses Data APIs/permissions rather than hidden direct database mutation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files-backed asset rename/move preserves site references and derived responsive image variants retain source provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SEO configuration generates correct representative title/canonical/sitemap behaviour and diagnostics identify representative missing/duplicate metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accessibility diagnostics identify representative contrast/alt/label/focus issues and the visual editor remains keyboard/screen-reader operable for core workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Stack Branch/Twig/Leaf opens in Sites with exact ProjectID/DomainID/revision; visual edits appear as ordinary changes in that same domain.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Open in Dev retains project/domain identity and Dev Code | Preview can use the Sites preview provider without export/import copying.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A preview deployment is pinned to an exact source revision and a production deployment records its exact source/config revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rollback redeploys a known prior successful revision without destructively deleting newer source history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Domain attach/verification reports exact DNS/TLS state and does not modify unrelated DNS records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A build/deployment failure preserves the prior successful production deployment and reports stage/provider failure accurately.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Private secrets are not emitted into browser bundles, logs, AI context or diffs during representative build/deploy workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated page/layout changes are normal editable source-backed objects and undergo available build plus visual QA rather than claiming success from compilation alone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Sites extension can register a representative component/node/provider contribution through the shared extension host with declared permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large page/component trees, CMS lists and asset libraries remain usable through virtualisation/paging and cancellable long-running jobs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Sites model while capability-negotiating local build/preview/provider features.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Sites follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A published site receives a default first-party address under sites.9to1.uk/<site-slug>; first-party slug/route segments enforce the specified lowercase a-z/hyphen character rules with slash only as a path separator, reserved-name checks and atomic slug reservation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A requested first-party slug and every custom domain binding pass deterministic plus AI-assisted misleading-name verification; ambiguous/high-risk cases become PendingReview with actionable reason/review state rather than opaque automatic publication.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom-domain ownership verification uses a site/account-bound secure DNS challenge and prevents duplicate/takeover claims; connected providers such as Cloudflare can configure only explicitly authorised records/zones under least-privilege scopes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every SiteProject has a user-addressable canonical project directory under the user's Sites area in Files containing the real source/project resources appropriate to its framework.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The external hosting provider stores/serves revision-pinned derived deployment artifacts and MUST NOT become the sole or independently editable canonical copy of the site.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A site can be rebuilt from canonical Files/Stack source, redeployed to a replacement hosting provider and remapped/verified without scraping the live website to reconstruct project state.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Terminal

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and core invariant

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Terminal is the shared first-party terminal runtime and terminal application for 9to1. It provides genuine interactive shell/PTY behaviour plus a distinct natural-language AI execution mode, while preserving the exact security, permission and side-effect boundaries of the underlying action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal is not an AI chatbot styled as a command prompt. Command Mode remains a normal terminal capable of running existing shell applications unchanged; AI Mode is an additional semantic command/action surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Natural-language phrasing MUST NOT lower safety. An operation that is destructive, privileged, externally consequential, credential-sensitive or otherwise high-risk remains equally protected when requested in natural language.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical session model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: TerminalSession has stable TerminalSessionID, EnvironmentID, ShellProfileID, mode, process/PTY binding, working directory, title, tab/pane location, command history references, running process/job state, Stack/Dev context where applicable, creation/reconnect metadata and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Environment identity is explicit. A session always knows whether it targets the local host, WSL, container, SSH host, VM, Dev environment, 9to1-OS host or another registered execution provider.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Display names, tab order and current path are not used as durable session identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent AI / Command mode switcher

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal provides an always-visible mode switcher comparable to Data's AI / SQL switcher. The two first-party states are AI and Command.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Command Mode sends ordinary terminal input to the selected shell/PTY with normal shell semantics, except for explicitly reserved Terminal meta-commands such as $Ask. It MUST NOT route ordinary recognised shell commands through an LLM merely because AI is available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Mode interprets user input as natural-language intent, resolves the appropriate typed 9to1/system action or shell operation, presents verification when required and then executes through the owning supported APIs/runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Switching modes does not create a new terminal session or lose working directory/environment context. The current mode is visibly obvious and included in accessibility state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Command Mode

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Command Mode behaves as a conventional professional terminal. Input supports the active shell's quoting, variables, pipes, redirection, chaining, job control, scripts, aliases/functions and interactive programs without Terminal rewriting command semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples such as git status, dotnet build, python, ssh, vim or a project's CLI run directly through the selected environment rather than requiring AI interpretation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal may enrich recognised output with clickable links or structured metadata, but the original output stream remains faithful and recoverable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: $Ask non-executing AI assistance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Command Mode reserves the Terminal meta-command $Ask for conversational AI assistance that has no authority to execute a shell command or mutate the environment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples include $Ask "why didn't this command work?", $Ask "what does this error mean?" and $Ask "what command lists processes on this shell?".

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: $Ask may receive permission-scoped context such as the immediately preceding command, exit status, selected/recent relevant output, shell/profile, environment type, working directory and registered project context. It MUST NOT indiscriminately send the whole terminal history or detected secrets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: $Ask returns explanation, troubleshooting steps and/or suggested command text. Suggested commands are not executed. The user may copy or insert a suggestion into Command Mode, after which it is treated as ordinary user-entered command input.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: $Ask itself MUST NOT invoke a hidden command, app mutation, package install, process kill or external side effect. An explicit transition to AI Mode or separate Run/Insert action is required for execution.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI Mode natural-language execution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Mode accepts natural-language requests such as "turn off my PC in 10 minutes", "find every PNG over 10 MB", "install the missing .NET SDK", "open the Data project for this CSV" or "show me what changed in this Stack Twig".

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The resolver prefers the owning typed 9to1/system API when one exists. Shell command synthesis is used when a shell command is genuinely the appropriate supported operation, not as a shortcut around a semantic API.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before execution Terminal produces an inspectable resolved action/plan containing target environment/app, operation, affected objects where knowable, risk level, whether it is reversible, scheduled/external effects and any shell commands that will actually run.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI execution verification and dangerous-command protection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Mode may execute low-risk, clearly resolved actions according to the user's existing trust/permission policy. Potentially dangerous or ambiguous operations require explicit verification before execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Verification is mandatory for destructive/bulk-destructive filesystem operations, shutdown/restart, privilege/security changes, process termination with material impact, package/system changes, credential access, permission changes, remote/external mutations and other actions classified as elevated by the owning app/system action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The verification view states what will run, where it will run, what is expected to change, affected object counts/scopes where determinable and what cannot be predicted. Unknown impact is displayed as unknown rather than omitted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ambiguous natural-language requests that could resolve to materially different consequential actions MUST pause for clarification/selection rather than choosing the more destructive interpretation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Mode cannot split one dangerous request into many nominally lower-risk commands to evade Home risk aggregation or approval.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Home permission-broker integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Protected AI Mode actions use the global Home permission broker. Terminal supplies stable caller/action identity, target app/environment, resolved scopes and risk metadata; it does not implement a weaker private approval system.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual Command Mode execution remains ordinary shell execution subject to OS/shell permissions and Terminal-specific guards. Where a shell command crosses a 9to1 protected semantic boundary such as Stack managed infrastructure, the owning product guard still applies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Always Trust or other Home trust grants never bypass OS elevation, provider authentication, 2FA, Stack protections or product-specific safeguards.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Real PTY and shell behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Supported local environments use a real pseudoterminal/conpty/PTY or platform-equivalent terminal backend. Terminal supports interactive stdin/stdout/stderr, ANSI/VT sequences, cursor control, terminal resize, signals, full-screen terminal applications and shell-native prompts/completion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Closing, resizing or switching UI panes MUST NOT convert an interactive shell into one-shot process execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the platform cannot expose a local PTY, Terminal uses a declared remote/service terminal provider or reports CapabilityUnavailable; it MUST NOT simulate successful local shell execution.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shell profiles and discovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal discovers installed shells and supports explicit ShellProfile objects. Representative profiles include PowerShell, Command Prompt where supported, Bash, Zsh, Fish, WSL distributions and extension/provider-contributed shells.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ShellProfile identifies executable/provider, arguments, environment setup, icon/name, default working-directory behaviour, shell-integration capability and environment compatibility.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Missing configured shells are shown as Missing/Unavailable with a clear reason and remediation path rather than failing with an unexplained spawn error.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Tabs, panes and window layouts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal supports multiple tabs and horizontal/vertical split panes. Each pane hosts a TerminalSession or attachable terminal job and can be renamed, pinned, moved, duplicated or closed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Workspace/session layout can be restored across restarts. Restoration recreates UI/session context according to policy but MUST NOT blindly rerun previously entered commands or consequential jobs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Closing a pane with an active process prompts or follows configured safe behaviour indicating whether the process will be terminated, detached or left remote.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Working directory and path semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each session maintains a real working directory appropriate to its environment. Working-directory changes initiated by the shell are tracked through shell integration where available rather than guessed solely from prompt text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Paths remain native to the environment so existing CLIs work correctly. Files integration adds stable identity/navigation where possible without replacing required filesystem paths.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drag/drop of a Files item into Command Mode inserts an appropriately escaped native path/reference for the active shell where supported.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shell integration protocol

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Optional first-party shell integration can report command start/end, command text, exit code, working directory, prompt boundaries and other safe semantic state. This allows reliable command/output grouping without fragile ANSI scraping.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Raw PTY operation remains functional when shell integration is unavailable. Terminal MUST NOT require modifying every third-party shell to provide basic terminal behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shell integration data is environment-scoped and cannot be trusted as an authorisation signal for privileged operations.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Command and output history

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal maintains configurable history for commands and Terminal-native actions, distinguishing user-entered shell commands, AI-executed actions, AI-generated shell commands, $Ask requests, denied/cancelled actions and scheduled actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can search, filter, copy, rerun eligible commands, pin entries and clear history according to policy. Sensitive commands or outputs can be excluded/redacted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: History records whether an AI suggestion was merely shown, inserted, or actually executed; the UI MUST NOT imply execution from proposal alone.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Streaming output and semantic links

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PTY output is rendered as real streaming ANSI/terminal content. Terminal may additionally recognise file:line references, directories, URLs, ports, process IDs, compiler diagnostics, Git/Stack identities and other registered entities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recognised entities become optional clickable actions such as Open in Dev, Show in Files or Open in Browse without altering the underlying captured output.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Third-party output remains displayable even when no semantic recogniser understands it.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Rich Terminal-native output

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-owned commands/actions and registered extensions MAY emit structured terminal blocks such as tables, progress, diagnostics, file results, images/previews or action cards where the terminal surface supports them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured output always has an accessible text representation and MUST NOT make standard stdout/stderr consumers depend on a proprietary renderer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Raw shell output and structured Terminal-native result objects remain distinguishable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Long-running processes and jobs

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal supports servers, watchers, builds, log tails, REPLs and other indefinite/interactive processes. Users can send input, interrupt, terminate, detach/reconnect where the environment permits and inspect current process/session state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured AI/system work may use TerminalJob with stable JobID, source request, resolved action, environment, process/provider identity, state, progress where real progress exists, timestamps, result/exit status and cancellation capability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal MUST NOT fabricate percentage progress for raw commands that do not expose meaningful progress.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Persistent scheduling

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Natural-language requests such as "turn off my PC in 10 minutes" or "run this script tomorrow morning" create a persistent scheduled action through the appropriate Automation/OS scheduling capability rather than an in-memory Terminal timer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The schedule records stable action/task identity, target EnvironmentID, requested action, execution time/rule, permission/trust context and cancellation/edit linkage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Closing Terminal MUST NOT silently cancel a persistent scheduled action unless that behaviour was explicitly selected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consequential scheduled actions require the same verification/permission classification at creation and, where policy requires, revalidation at execution.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Elevation and privileged sessions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Privilege elevation is explicit. When an operation requires Administrator/root/elevated privileges, Terminal identifies the target operation and uses the platform-supported elevation mechanism.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A normal session MUST NOT silently become permanently elevated because one command required elevation. Deliberately created elevated sessions are visually and accessibly distinguished.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Mode cannot bypass elevation prompts or OS security boundaries.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Environment providers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal supports environment providers for local host, WSL, containers, SSH/remotes, virtual machines, Dev environments, 9to1-OS systems and extension-contributed execution targets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Environment has stable EnvironmentID, type, host/provider identity, connection/runtime state, platform/architecture, capabilities and security context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every action/command preview in AI Mode states the target environment so users cannot accidentally shut down, delete files from or install packages on the wrong machine.

heading: HEADING_3
text: SSH and remote terminals

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SSH support includes host profiles, verified host-key workflow, secure key/credential references, reconnect and supported port-forwarding/tunnel capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Passwords/private keys are handled by shared secure credential infrastructure where possible and MUST NOT be copied into AI context/history/logs unnecessarily.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A host-key mismatch is a security error requiring explicit resolution; Terminal MUST NOT silently accept changed remote identity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Container, WSL and VM terminals

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal can open or attach to shells inside supported containers/devcontainers, WSL distributions and virtual machines. Environment identity remains visible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev's OS/VM run configurations may expose VM shell/serial/debug consoles through the shared Terminal engine. Reconnecting a VM console does not create a second conflicting VM unless the run provider explicitly requests one.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider lifecycle actions such as starting a stopped VM/container remain typed consequential operations rather than being hidden side effects of reading terminal history.

heading: HEADING_3
text: First-class Dev integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev uses the same Terminal engine rather than maintaining a private emulator. Dev can create sessions bound to WorkspaceID/ProjectID, RunConfiguration, toolchain environment and working directory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compiler/build/test diagnostics recognised in Terminal link to Dev source and Problems using stable source locations when available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev can host Terminal panes directly while Terminal can Open current directory/project in Dev without copying project state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: First-class Stack integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When a session is bound to a Stack ProjectID/DomainID, Terminal shows the active source-domain context and can expose Stack-native commands/actions such as status, owned/inherited changes, promotion/check state and Open in Stack.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Raw Git commands remain available in Command Mode, but Stack-managed lineage, protected companion refs, Roots/Subroots/Freezes and other guards cannot be bypassed by invoking Git from Terminal. Unsafe operations are blocked or require Stack's explicit advanced reconciliation path.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Mode uses 9to1.Stack.* actions for semantic Stack requests rather than shelling out to Git when Stack is the canonical owner.

heading: HEADING_3
text: First-class Data integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal can address Data projects, queries and exports through typed Data actions and can open returned tables/results in Data. AI Mode requests such as "run this query against my selected Data project" use Data's target/protection model rather than bypassing it with an arbitrary database CLI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Command Mode remains free to run installed database/SQL CLIs against user-configured connections, subject to their own credentials and permissions; Terminal clearly distinguishes those raw commands from 9to1 Data actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured Data results may render as accessible terminal tables and provide Open in Data.

heading: HEADING_3
text: First-class integration with all 9to1 apps

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every 9to1 app MAY register a Terminal integration provider exposing discoverable read/actions, context resolvers, entity links, completion/help metadata and structured renderers through the shared API model. Terminal treats this as a first-class platform capability, not bespoke one-off integrations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Mode can route requests to canonical app APIs such as Files, Boards, Write, Present, Forms, Sites, Browse, Wave, Motion, Pictures, Spaces, Automations, AI Studio and future apps when the requested operation belongs to them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Command Mode can expose explicit 9to1 command/meta-command tooling for users who want scriptable access, but those commands call the same app APIs and Home permissions rather than private UI automation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-app results support actions such as Open in <App>, reveal source object, continue in app or pipe/export structured data where the owning API permits.

heading: HEADING_3
text: 9to1 command-line bridge

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal SHOULD provide a scriptable 9to1 CLI/command bridge for canonical app APIs, with discoverable namespaces/actions, machine-readable output option, stable exit codes and authentication/permission behaviour consistent with Home.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The CLI is not a second business-logic implementation. It dispatches to the owning 9to1 APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automation/scripting can therefore use explicit commands for Stack, Files, Data and other apps while AI Mode uses the same semantic operations from natural language.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Package and tool installation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Mode may resolve requests such as "install numpy" or "install the missing C++ compiler" only after resolving the intended project/environment/package manager/toolchain.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project-native package managers and Dev Toolchain Manager remain authoritative. A Python project using a selected virtual environment MUST NOT silently install globally.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Package/system installation is a mutating/elevated action classified appropriately and shows target environment, package/tool and provider before execution when verification is required.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Error assistance and diagnostics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal recognises failed commands through shell integration/exit codes where available. $Ask can explain the failure without executing fixes; AI Mode can separately propose and, after required verification, perform remediation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal can classify common issues such as executable missing, PATH/toolchain mismatch, permission/elevation required, dependency/package failure, working-directory problem, network/SSH failure or Stack guard rejection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where another app owns remediation, Terminal links/routs to that app rather than duplicating its configuration system.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Search, scrollback and large output

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal supports plain/case/regex search over retained session output and optionally across retained buffers/history according to privacy settings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scrollback is configurable and bounded. Huge streams use virtualised rendering and, where configured, disk-backed spooling/truncation rather than unbounded UI memory growth.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When earlier output is discarded due to limits, Terminal visibly records the truncation boundary rather than pretending the full stream is retained.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Clipboard and multiline paste safety

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal supports normal copy/paste, copy command, copy output and platform clipboard conventions. Multiline paste is detected and may require review/warning according to security settings and content risk.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Paste protection MUST NOT silently rewrite commands. It either executes the exact accepted paste or cancels/returns it to editable input.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-generated multiline scripts are visually distinguished from user-authored pasted scripts until the user accepts execution.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Secrets, privacy and AI-context filtering

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal assumes arbitrary third-party processes may print secrets. AI context construction uses scoped recent/selected data and applies configured secret-pattern redaction plus known credential references, but Terminal MUST NOT claim perfect secret detection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal content is not automatically sent to Dulche merely because a session exists. $Ask/AI Mode specify the context slice they require and honour app/workspace privacy policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Credentials, private keys, tokens and secure environment values are excluded from routine history/telemetry/AI prompts unless the operation explicitly and safely requires them.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Command risk metadata and audit

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI-resolved actions record canonical action IDs, target app/environment, risk classification, verification/permission outcome, executed command/API operation, result and affected identities where known.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual raw shell commands are not reclassified as if Terminal semantically understood every side effect, but privileged/guarded platform integrations may emit audit events where required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Denied, cancelled, failed and partially completed AI actions remain auditable rather than disappearing from history.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Completion, aliases and snippets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal supports shell-native completion and may augment it with registered command/app/entity providers. AI is not required for ordinary tab completion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can manage reusable snippets/recipes and organisation-provided command templates. Snippets are inspectable text/structured actions, not opaque macros that bypass permission checks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI can draft a snippet from repeated work, but saving or running it remains an explicit user action.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dulche context and behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche context for Terminal may include current TerminalSessionID, mode, EnvironmentID, shell profile, working directory, selected/recent command groups, exit code, current process, Dev workspace/Stack domain and registered app context subject to permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: In AI Mode Dulche performs semantic planning/execution through typed actions; in Command Mode $Ask is constrained to advice/explanation and cannot execute.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI output MUST distinguish commands it suggests from operations it actually executed, and execution claims must be grounded in real process/API results.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Terminal API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal's first-party API catalogue is exhaustive under the global API-parity rule. Minimum canonical entry points include:

text: 9to1.Terminal.Execute(sessionID, command, options?);

text: 9to1.Terminal.SendInput(sessionID, input);

text: 9to1.Terminal.Interrupt(sessionID, options?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: App/business mutations resolved through Terminal use the owning 9to1 namespace; scheduling, Files, Stack, Dev, Data, credentials and other shared domains remain canonical in their own APIs.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automation and typed events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal emits typed events such as SessionCreated/Closed, ModeChanged, CommandStarted/Completed, ProcessStarted/Exited, WorkingDirectoryChanged, ConnectionLost/Restored, AIActionResolved/Verified/Executed/Denied, ScheduledActionCreated/Cancelled and guarded integration events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Events expose stable IDs and permission-scoped metadata. Raw terminal output is not automatically attached to every event; consumers request permitted output ranges explicitly.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Extension system

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal participates in the shared 9to1 extension system. Extensions may contribute shell profiles, environment providers, completion providers, semantic recognisers, structured renderers, Terminal-native commands, context providers and integrations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An extension gains only its declared capabilities. Rendering output or adding completion does not automatically grant process execution, filesystem write, network, credential or AI permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension failures are isolated/disableable according to the shared extension-host contract and cannot take down unrelated PTY sessions where avoidable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal provides keyboard-first operation for tabs/panes, mode switching, command input, history, output search, AI verification and structured result controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Screen-reader support exposes command/output group boundaries, prompt/mode state, exit status and meaningful structured result text where platform terminal accessibility APIs permit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Colour is not the sole signal for elevated session, AI/Command mode, failure, warning or protected action state. Text zoom, high contrast and visible focus are supported.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and resilience

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PTY rendering is virtualised/batched to remain responsive under sustained output. One noisy process MUST NOT freeze unrelated Terminal panes or the whole 9to1 shell.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI resolution, remote connection and structured jobs are cancellable where technically possible and do not block raw PTY input in other sessions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal crash/restart can restore layout/profile/environment references and retained history according to policy; it does not invent process survival. Live remote/process reconnection occurs only when the provider can prove the original process/session remains available.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and typed failures

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured failures include SessionNotFound, ShellUnavailable, EnvironmentUnavailable, EnvironmentDisconnected, PTYCreationFailed, ProcessLaunchFailed, ElevationRequired, CommandRejected, AmbiguousAIIntent, VerificationRequired, PermissionRequired, PermissionDenied, StackGuardViolation, ScheduledActionUnavailable, SSHHostKeyMismatch, CredentialUnavailable, OutputTruncated, ExtensionFailed, RevisionConflict and CapabilityUnavailable plus provider/shell-specific errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI multi-step operations report succeeded, failed, skipped and rolled-back stages where relevant. Terminal MUST NOT claim a command/action completed merely because it was proposed or started.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Failed remote reconnect, scheduled-action creation or app integration leaves explicit recoverable state rather than silently falling back to another environment.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same TerminalSession, mode, AI action and integration model while capability-negotiating local PTY implementation, shells, WSL, OS elevation, SSH/provider and process controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web Terminal requires an authorised remote/server environment provider for real shell execution unless the web platform exposes an approved execution environment. It MUST NOT present browser-side simulation as host terminal access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Terminal follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Command Mode runs representative real interactive PTY applications with ANSI, resize, stdin, signals and full-screen behaviour intact.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The persistent AI / Command switcher changes interpretation mode without losing the same TerminalSession/environment/working directory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An ordinary command such as git status in Command Mode executes directly without unnecessary LLM mediation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: $Ask "why didn't this command work?" receives scoped failure context and returns advice while performing no process, filesystem, package, app or external mutation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A suggested command from $Ask is not marked executed until the user separately runs it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Mode resolves a natural-language read-only request into an inspectable typed action/command and executes it according to permission policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A dangerous AI request such as shutdown, bulk deletion or privileged configuration displays target, impact/risk and requires the applicable verification/permission before execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An ambiguous dangerous natural-language request does not choose a destructive interpretation silently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Turn off this PC in 10 minutes creates a persistent scheduled action with cancel/edit identity that survives closing the Terminal UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shell/profile discovery shows a missing configured shell/tool with a clear unavailable reason instead of an unexplained spawn failure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiple tabs/splits maintain isolated shell/process/environment state and restoring layout does not rerun historical commands.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An elevated session/operation is visibly/accessibly distinct and AI cannot bypass the platform elevation boundary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SSH validates host keys, refuses a changed key without explicit resolution and keeps credentials out of routine AI/history output.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Container/WSL/VM/remote sessions expose explicit EnvironmentID so actions cannot silently target the wrong machine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev embeds the same Terminal engine and preserves WorkspaceID/project/toolchain/working-directory context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Stack-bound session shows DomainID context; raw Git cannot bypass protected Stack managed refs/Roots/Freezes/lineage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An AI Stack request routes through 9to1.Stack.* rather than using Git as a hidden substitute.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Data request uses Data target/write protection and can return an accessible structured result/Open in Data action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative integrations for Files, Boards, Forms, Sites and another registered 9to1 app route through canonical app APIs and Home permission scopes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The 9to1 CLI bridge and UI/AI action resolve to the same canonical app business operation rather than divergent implementations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Package installation resolves the active environment/project/package manager and does not silently install into the wrong global environment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large output remains responsive with bounded/virtualised scrollback and visibly reports truncation when history is discarded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiline paste protection does not rewrite the accepted command and can prevent accidental immediate execution according to policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI context excludes known secure credential values and uses only the permitted relevant terminal context slice.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: History distinguishes proposed, inserted, executed, denied, failed and scheduled AI/shell actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal hyperlinks open representative source paths in Dev, files in Files and URLs in Browse without altering raw output.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Long-running processes can be interrupted/terminated and pane closure does not silently kill them contrary to configured behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension-contributed renderer/completion does not implicitly receive process/filesystem/network privileges.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard/screen-reader workflows cover tabs/panes, switcher, command input, output, $Ask and dangerous-action verification.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and web/remote configurations preserve the same canonical Terminal model while capability-negotiating shell execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Terminal follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Mini Computer

heading: HEADING_3
text: Product role and shared virtualisation engine

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9-1 Mini Computer is the native CUI virtual-computer and virtual-machine management app and the shared virtualisation engine used by Dev, Terminal and other authorised 9to1 surfaces. It supports creation, installation, import, execution, inspection, configuration, snapshots, cloning, networking, device integration, templates, developer workflows and recovery of supported virtual machines.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer owns the canonical VirtualMachine/VirtualisationProvider model and VM lifecycle. Dev owns code/build/debug authoring, Terminal owns terminal sessions, Files owns user-addressable files/media identity and Home owns protected-action permission brokering.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A VM remains a real provider-backed virtual machine. Mini Computer MUST NOT replace mature hypervisor functionality with a simplified simulation merely to obtain a uniform UI.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Built-in default provider: 9to1 VirtualBox fork

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The built-in and default provider is a maintained 9to1 fork of the VirtualBox Platform Package source. Mini Computer MUST include this provider so a user can create and run supported VMs without first installing or connecting a third-party hypervisor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation MUST fork and maintain the latest appropriate VirtualBox source in accordance with the global donor/upstream contract and the applicable open-source licence/third-party licence obligations. The fork remains an auditable upstream-derived backend rather than an opaque binary dependency with no source provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VirtualBox's mature virtual-machine creation, configuration, storage, networking, snapshot, cloning, import/export, console and management behaviours are mandatory donor-parity inputs where supported by the target architecture/platform.

heading: HEADING_3
text: VirtualBox licensing and excluded separately licensed components

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The 9to1 fork covers only VirtualBox source/components that CAKE is legally permitted to modify and distribute under their applicable licences. Separately licensed proprietary components such as the Oracle Extension Pack MUST NOT be copied, bundled or represented as part of the fork unless CAKE has obtained the required rights.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a useful donor capability exists only in a separately licensed component, Mini Computer must either provide a legally independent 9to1-native replacement, support a separately user-installed/connected compatible component where lawful, or expose the capability as unavailable with a documented licensing/platform reason.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation architecture SHOULD keep the fork/provider boundary sufficiently clear for licence compliance, update/rebase management and optional alternative-provider support.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Provider abstraction and optional connected providers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer exposes a canonical VirtualisationProvider interface. The built-in 9to1 VirtualBox fork is selected by default, while users may connect/install additional compatible providers such as QEMU, KVM, Windows hypervisor integrations or extension-contributed providers when supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider has stable ProviderID, type/vendor, version, connection/install state, supported hosts/guest architectures, acceleration capabilities, firmware/security capabilities, device/network/storage features, import/export formats, debug/serial support and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connecting another provider does not change the canonical VM semantics automatically. Each VM records ProviderID, and provider migration/conversion is an explicit operation with a preview of unsupported/lossy features.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider-specific advanced controls remain accessible through typed provider configuration without leaking arbitrary implementation flags into the canonical cross-provider model.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Provider capability matrix

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every provider reports exact capability state rather than relying on feature hiding alone. Capabilities include supported guest architectures, hardware acceleration, nested virtualisation, snapshots, live snapshots, saved state, cloning, disk formats/controllers, BIOS/UEFI, Secure Boot, TPM, USB/device passthrough, shared folders, clipboard/drag-drop, virtual networking, graphics acceleration, multi-monitor, audio, serial/debug interfaces and live configuration changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A setting unsupported by the active provider/platform is marked Unsupported/Unavailable with a reason and remediation/alternative where applicable. Mini Computer MUST NOT accept a setting and silently ignore it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Capabilities may depend on host architecture and current host configuration, so provider/version support and effective host support are distinct states.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical VirtualMachine model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VirtualMachine has stable VMID, name, ProviderID, EnvironmentID, guest OS metadata, architecture, machine/chipset type, firmware/security configuration, CPU configuration, memory configuration, storage controllers/disks/media, network adapters, display/GPU, audio, USB/devices, integration policy, shared folders, clipboard/drag-drop policy, snapshot graph, template/source provenance, lifecycle state, Files/resource references and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Renaming, moving in UI or changing provider display labels MUST NOT alter VMID. Provider-internal identifiers are retained as mappings rather than becoming the only canonical identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VM configuration is versioned and migratable. Unsupported/unknown future configuration is preserved/rejected explicitly rather than silently dropped.

heading: HEADING_3
text: VM lifecycle states

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canonical lifecycle states include at least PoweredOff, Starting, Running, Pausing, Paused, SavingState, Saved, Resuming, ShuttingDown, Stopping, Crashed, Disconnected/ViewerUnavailable and ProviderUnavailable where distinct.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Viewer state and VM state are separate. Closing or losing a viewer MUST NOT cause the UI to report PoweredOff if the VM remains running.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Lifecycle transitions are driven by verified provider state. Mini Computer MUST NOT report Start/Shutdown/Save successful until the provider confirms the resulting state or the operation explicitly remains Pending.

heading: HEADING_3
text: New VM wizard

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Create VM provides a guided workflow for guest OS family/version, architecture, installation media, CPU, RAM, storage, firmware/security, networking and optional unattended installation, with Advanced settings available before creation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Defaults are recommendations based on detected/selected guest and current host/provider capabilities. Users can review/change them before the VM is created.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Creating a VM is atomic at the user-visible level where possible; partial provider/storage creation is either rolled back or returned with precise created resources and recovery actions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Guest/ISO detection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When installation media is selected, Mini Computer attempts to detect OS family, edition/version, architecture and boot compatibility using trustworthy metadata/content inspection available without executing the image.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Detected values are recommendations and are shown with confidence/source state where useful. Unknown media remains Unknown rather than being guessed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Detection may propose suitable CPU, memory, disk, firmware, TPM/Secure Boot and guest-integration settings while preserving user control.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Curated ISO Browser

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer includes a first-class ISO Browser/Discover OS experience for acquiring trusted operating-system installation media. It is a curated publisher catalogue, not an unrestricted Internet ISO search engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Catalogue entries may include operating-system family/distribution, publisher, edition/channel, version, architecture, desktop/server variant, approximate size, source/provider, acquisition policy, integrity metadata availability, licence/redistribution policy and branding/trademark usage metadata where relevant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative trusted publisher sources may include Microsoft, Canonical/Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch, openSUSE, FreeBSD, 9to1 OS and other audited providers. Addition of a catalogue source requires explicit provider/provenance configuration.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ISO acquisition policies

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every ISO catalogue entry declares one of the canonical acquisition policies or an equivalent explicit policy:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: OfficialDirect — the user's Mini Computer downloads from the publisher's authorised source and 9to1 does not rehost the file.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MirrorPermitted — CAKE may mirror/cache the exact permitted unmodified image only when redistribution rights/policy expressly allow it and all required licence/notices/provenance are preserved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: UserSupplied — Mini Computer can identify/configure the guest but the user must select media they already lawfully possess.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ProviderFlow — acquisition requires a publisher-specific authenticated/licensed/download flow that Mini Computer opens or integrates without bypassing its conditions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An OS being open source does not by itself authorise ISO redistribution or logo/trademark use. Acquisition/mirroring and branding rights are evaluated separately.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ISO download, integrity and provenance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Downloaded/registerable installation media uses stable ISOImageID/MediaID and records publisher/source, product/version/architecture, acquisition provider/URL reference, Files identity, cryptographic digest/signature state, download timestamp, redistribution/acquisition policy, licence/provenance metadata and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When the publisher provides authoritative checksum/signature information, Mini Computer verifies it before labelling the download Verified. A mismatch blocks automatic VM creation/use until the user deliberately handles the failed integrity state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If trustworthy verification data is unavailable, the UI states Integrity not independently verified rather than inventing trust.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: One immutable ISO can be referenced by multiple VMs without creating duplicate copies unnecessarily.

heading: HEADING_3
text: ISO Browser user flow

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A supported catalogue flow can perform Select OS → choose version/architecture → acquire from authorised source → verify integrity → register media → create/configure VM → mount media → boot installer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The user can inspect the source/publisher and acquisition policy before download. Any required login/product/licence flow remains the publisher's official flow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Open local ISO/import media remains available for images not represented in the curated catalogue.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Media library and cleanup

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer exposes reusable installation media through a media library backed by Files/provider storage. Media usage shows which VMs currently reference/mount the item.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Removing media does not delete installed VM disks. If the medium is still mounted or required for a configured boot workflow, deletion/removal shows the affected VMs and requires appropriate confirmation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Derived download caches can be cleaned independently from canonical retained media where provenance/re-download permits.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Unattended installation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the guest/provider supports it, users may opt into unattended OS installation. Configuration can include hostname, locale, time zone, user/account setup, product/licence information where required, disk install choices and guest integration installation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Passwords/product keys and equivalent sensitive values use secure credential/secret handling rather than being written into logs, screenshots, AI context or plain project metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual installation is always available and remains the fallback when unattended flow is unsupported or fails.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Interactive VM viewer

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Running VMs can open in an interactive Mini Computer viewer supporting keyboard, pointer capture/release, scaling, fullscreen, aspect handling, dynamic resolution when guest integration supports it and multi-monitor when the provider supports it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The viewer may be embedded or popped out to a dedicated window while retaining the same VMID/session state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Viewer disconnect/reconnect is separate from VM lifecycle and must not power off or duplicate the VM unless explicitly requested.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Power and state controls

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer distinguishes Start, Pause, Resume, Save State, ACPI/Guest Shutdown, Restart/Reset where supported and Power Off/Force Stop. The UI/API MUST NOT label destructive power-off as graceful shutdown.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Potential data-loss actions such as Power Off while a guest is running receive risk-appropriate confirmation unless a valid trust/policy explicitly covers them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Power actions are idempotent or return AlreadyInState/InvalidState semantics rather than creating contradictory provider operations.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Snapshots

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Snapshots are first-class canonical objects with stable SnapshotID, VMID, parent SnapshotID, name, description, creation time, provider reference, disk/memory-state coverage, guest state, size/retention metadata and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can create, inspect, restore, rename/descriptively edit where supported and delete/consolidate snapshots. Snapshot hierarchy is shown as a tree/graph rather than a flat list.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Restore explicitly states which disk/memory/config state is affected and what current unsaved state will be lost. External/shared resources not captured by the snapshot are clearly excluded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deleting/consolidating a snapshot MUST NOT silently delete a dependent branch/linked clone.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Cloning and linked clones

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer supports full clone and provider-supported linked clone from current state or a selected snapshot. Clone receives a new stable VMID and clear provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Linked-clone dependency on base disks/snapshots is visible. Deleting/moving a required base is blocked or performs a deliberate consolidation/migration first.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clone options include identity/network regeneration where needed to avoid duplicate machine identifiers.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Virtual disks and block storage

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer supports provider-compatible disk formats such as VDI plus supported VHD/VHDX, VMDK, QCOW2 and raw images through the active provider/conversion layer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Disk operations include create, attach/detach, resize where safe, compact where supported, clone, convert/import/export, inspect and delete.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VirtualDisk has stable DiskID, provider reference, format/type, logical/physical size, backing/base relationship, encryption state where supported, Files/storage-provider identity, attached VM/controller references and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Destructive resize/shrink/delete/raw-device operations require explicit validation and risk-appropriate verification.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Storage controllers and boot order

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer exposes provider-supported controllers such as NVMe, SATA, SCSI and legacy IDE/other controllers when required. Optical/floppy media appears only where supported/meaningful.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal VM creation configures conventional controller topology automatically; Advanced settings expose the real attachment slots/controllers.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boot order and one-time boot choices are explicit. Mounting a new ISO MUST NOT silently rewrite persistent boot policy unless requested.

heading: HEADING_3
text: CPU and memory configuration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VM settings include virtual CPU count/topology where supported, RAM and provider-specific advanced execution/CPU capabilities such as execution cap or nested virtualisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer warns when requested allocation is likely to leave insufficient host resources or exceeds provider/host capabilities. It must not silently overcommit resources while presenting them as guaranteed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Settings that require VM shutdown are marked Requires shutdown; supported live changes show real applied/pending state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Firmware, Secure Boot and TPM

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer supports BIOS/legacy firmware and UEFI according to provider capabilities, plus Secure Boot and virtual TPM where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Guest templates/detection can recommend required firmware/security configuration, especially for modern operating systems, while exposing the actual setting.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: TPM/Secure Boot backing state is included in snapshot/export/migration semantics only where the provider guarantees it; otherwise exclusions are explicit.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Networking

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VM networking supports provider-capable modes such as NAT, bridged, host-only, internal/private, NAT network/custom virtual network and disconnected state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each VirtualNetworkAdapter has stable AdapterID, mode/network binding, virtual NIC type, MAC configuration, cable/link state, port-forward rules and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: NAT port forwarding exposes host address/port, guest address/port and protocol and validates collisions before applying.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Virtual network manager

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer includes a network-management surface for provider-defined NAT networks, host-only networks, internal/private networks, DHCP ranges, forwarding and adapters.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deleting/modifying a network lists dependent VMs/adapters and blocks or migrates them explicitly rather than leaving hidden broken references.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Bridged network/device selection is capability- and permission-aware and does not silently expose a VM to external networks.

heading: HEADING_3
text: USB and device passthrough

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where provider/platform support exists, users may attach/detach USB devices and configure explicit passthrough/filter policies. Additional PCI/GPU/device passthrough is exposed only through providers with a supported implementation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Attaching a physical device that becomes unavailable to the host is communicated before execution. Auto-attach rules identify exactly which VM/device criteria they affect.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Device passthrough is treated as a high-trust boundary; Mini Computer does not grant broad host-device access to untrusted guests by default.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Display and graphics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Display configuration can expose virtual display controller, VRAM, monitor count, scaling, 2D/3D acceleration and provider-supported graphics features.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordinary virtual graphics acceleration is distinct from physical GPU passthrough. The latter uses its own provider/security/capability requirements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unsupported graphics settings remain visibly unavailable rather than being written into configuration and ignored.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Audio and microphone

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer exposes guest audio output/input routing where supported. Microphone input follows host privacy/device permission rules and MUST NOT silently activate because the VM starts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Per-VM audio policy can disable input/output entirely for untrusted/test guests.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Clipboard and drag/drop trust policy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shared clipboard and drag/drop support provider/guest-integration capabilities and explicit policies such as Disabled, HostToGuest, GuestToHost and Bidirectional.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: These capabilities are disabled or conservatively configured by default according to security policy for untrusted guests. Guest integration installation alone MUST NOT silently enable bidirectional host data access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clipboard/drag-drop state is visible while the VM is running.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shared folders

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can expose host/Files-backed folders to guests through stable SharedFolder configurations with host/File identity, guest name/mount path, read-only/read-write, auto-mount and persistence policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Writable host sharing is a security boundary because guest software can modify host/user data. The UI/AI verification must make writable scope clear.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deleting/moving a shared host resource resolves through Files identity where possible or leaves an explicit BrokenBinding state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Guest integrations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer detects and, where lawfully distributable/supported, can install appropriate guest integration tooling for dynamic resolution, clipboard, drag/drop, shared folders, guest status/shutdown and file transfer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Guest integration version/health is visible. The VM remains operable when integrations are unavailable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer MUST NOT bundle separately licensed donor guest components without the necessary rights.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Import and export

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer supports import/export of mature provider formats such as OVF/OVA and supported virtual-disk formats through the active provider/conversion layer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Import previews guest OS metadata, CPU/RAM, disks, networks, device requirements, unsupported features and resulting provider mapping before creation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Export records exact VM revision/snapshot/configuration scope and warns about excluded secrets, external disks/shared folders/device state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Templates and reusable machine profiles

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can save reusable VM templates/profiles for common environments such as Windows testing, Linux development, server labs or 9to1-OS development.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Template has stable TemplateID, guest/provider requirements, hardware defaults, media/acquisition references, optional bootstrap/unattended settings and Revision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Instantiating a template creates a new VM identity. The template itself is not accidentally run/mutated as an ordinary machine unless explicitly converted.

heading: HEADING_3
text: First-party guest templates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer may ship configuration templates for common operating systems without bundling proprietary installation images unless distribution rights permit it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A template may state ISO required and route the user into the ISO Browser/provider flow rather than implying the operating system is included.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Templates are updated independently from the hypervisor and preserve backward compatibility for already-created VMs.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files and storage architecture

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: User-addressable Mini Computer resources are organised in Files through stable identities, conceptually including Machines, Disks, ISOs/Media, Templates and Exports. Exact physical layout may vary by storage provider but remains user-inspectable where appropriate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Very large mutable virtual disks/snapshot chains may use a block/storage provider optimised for VM workloads rather than ordinary sync semantics. Provider-internal block state is not misrepresented as a normal small Files document.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canonical VM/resource metadata records the mapping between user-visible Files resources and provider-internal storage so recovery/migration can distinguish source/configuration from derived/provider state.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Resource references and deduplication

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Immutable installation media can be shared by reference across VMs. Linked/base virtual disks preserve explicit dependency identity rather than being duplicated or lost through path renames.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Moving/renaming a Files-backed ISO/export/template through supported Files/Mini Computer actions preserves references by stable ID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider caches, temporary differencing layers and ephemeral development disks are marked derived/ephemeral and can be cleaned without deleting canonical user resources unless explicitly selected.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Terminal integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every supported VM can expose Open in Terminal for guest shell/SSH where configured, serial console, debug console or provider-supported command channel. This uses the shared Terminal engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal creates/attaches an EnvironmentID tied to VMID/provider/guest channel and visibly identifies the VM so commands cannot be mistaken for host commands.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Closing Terminal does not power off the VM; VM lifecycle remains owned by Mini Computer.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dev integration and Run target

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev uses Mini Computer as the canonical VM runtime for projects whose RunConfiguration targets a VM. Dev MUST NOT maintain a parallel private hypervisor implementation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For OS/kernel projects, Run can execute Build → package boot artifact → obtain/start configured Mini Computer VM → attach disk/ISO/EFI/kernel artifact → boot → expose viewer/serial/debug state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run configuration references stable VM/template/provider identities and can declare reset/snapshot/discard policy for repeatable development.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Ephemeral development VMs

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev/CI can request ephemeral VMs derived from templates/snapshots for isolated testing. Policy can specify discard after success, preserve on failure, always preserve or snapshot-before-run.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ephemeral instances receive unique VMID/runtime identity even when created from the same template and do not mutate the reusable template/base unintentionally.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cleanup waits until logs/artifacts/checks referencing the ephemeral environment are retained or explicitly discarded.

heading: HEADING_3
text: OS/kernel debugging integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer exposes provider-supported serial ports/consoles, debug stubs, reset/power control, boot logs and low-level debug channels through typed capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev owns source-level debugger UI such as breakpoints, symbols, registers/memory/disassembly mapping where supported; Mini Computer supplies the VM/provider channel and exact machine state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Debug integration records the source VM/revision/artifact mapping so Dev cannot accidentally attach symbols from an unrelated build.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Headless operation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VMs may run without an open viewer. Closing Mini Computer follows explicit/configured behaviour such as Keep running, Save state or Ask; it does not inherently terminate a VM.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A background/service component owns provider sessions that must survive the UI process. Reopening Mini Computer discovers/reattaches to existing provider VMs instead of creating duplicates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: User logout/system shutdown semantics are platform-specific and exposed clearly when background VM continuation is unavailable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Provider and host virtualisation status

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer includes Virtualisation Status showing selected/default provider, provider install/driver/service state, hardware virtualisation availability, acceleration state, nested virtualisation, host architecture and key feature capability status.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Common blockers such as disabled hardware virtualisation, unavailable provider driver/service, architecture mismatch, acceleration conflict or unsupported host configuration are surfaced with actionable diagnostics rather than opaque provider codes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the built-in VirtualBox fork conflicts with another host hypervisor configuration, Mini Computer reports the specific capability degradation/conflict and supported resolution options.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Resource monitoring

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Running VM views expose provider-backed CPU, allocated/used memory where available, disk activity, network activity, uptime and relevant guest/provider health metrics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Host overview can aggregate VM resource consumption. Unknown/unavailable metrics remain explicitly unavailable rather than estimated and displayed as measurements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Monitoring is virtualised/streamed to avoid high overhead with many running VMs.

heading: HEADING_3
text: AI / Dulche integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche context can include VMID, ProviderID/version, lifecycle state, guest metadata, hardware configuration, attached media/disks, network state, snapshot tree, integration state, current diagnostics, Dev/Terminal bindings and Revision subject to permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI requests such as create a Windows test VM, take a snapshot before this kernel test, explain why boot failed or add disk capacity resolve to typed Mini Computer/provider actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI MUST NOT hide consequential operations behind generic wording. Disk deletion/shrink, snapshot restore, raw-device attachment, writable shared-folder exposure, device passthrough, bridged networking and provider installation/configuration receive the applicable verification/risk treatment.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Safety and high-risk operations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: High-risk classes include deleting/overwriting virtual disks, destructive snapshot restore/consolidation, raw host-disk access, physical device/GPU passthrough, writable host sharing, privileged provider installation/driver changes, security-device changes and network changes that materially expose the guest/host.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Impact previews identify VM, affected disks/snapshots/devices/files/networks and whether the operation is reversible where determinable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer cannot use opaque desktop automation to click provider UIs when a typed provider/API operation exists.
