heading: HEADING_3
text: Automation and typed events

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer emits typed events such as VMCreated/Updated/Deleted, VMStateChanged, SnapshotCreated/Restored/Deleted, ProviderConnected/Unavailable, MediaAcquisitionStarted/Completed/Failed, MediaVerificationChanged, DeviceAttached/Detached, NetworkChanged, MetricsUpdated and provider/guest integration events.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Events use stable IDs and avoid embedding secret credentials or unbounded VM console output. Consumers request additional permitted data explicitly.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Extension system

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer participates in the shared 9to1 extension platform. Extensions may contribute VirtualisationProvider implementations, ISO catalogue/acquisition providers, guest templates/integration providers, device/network/storage adapters, inspectors and diagnostics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider extensions declare host/platform compatibility, required privileges and permissions. Installing a provider UI extension does not automatically grant kernel driver, raw-disk, device or network privileges.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider failure is isolated where feasible and does not corrupt unrelated VM canonical metadata.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VM list, create wizard, settings, snapshots, networks, ISO Browser, provider status and power controls are keyboard-operable with screen-reader semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VM lifecycle/provider/security state MUST NOT rely solely on colour or icons. Dangerous Power Off/Delete/Restore/Raw device actions have explicit accessible labels and consequences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The embedded viewer provides accessible host controls around the guest even when guest OS accessibility itself is outside Mini Computer's control.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Performance and scalability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: VM lists, snapshots, ISO/media libraries and monitoring views are virtualised/paged where needed. UI rendering MUST NOT require loading every virtual disk/snapshot into memory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider operations such as import/export, clone, disk conversion, large download, snapshot consolidation and migration run as cancellable/resumable jobs where the provider supports it, with stable JobID/progress/error state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer remains responsive while one or more VMs generate heavy I/O or console output.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer distinguishes viewer disconnect, provider service failure, VM crash, host-resource exhaustion, disk/media missing, storage corruption and configuration incompatibility rather than collapsing them into VM failed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reopening after UI crash/restart re-discovers provider-managed running/saved VMs by stable mapping and reattaches without duplication where the provider can prove identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured failures include VMNotFound, ProviderUnavailable, ProviderCapabilityUnavailable, HardwareVirtualisationUnavailable, AccelerationUnavailable, InvalidVMState, DiskNotFound, DiskDependencyBlocked, MediaNotFound, MediaIntegrityFailed, MediaAcquisitionNotPermitted, SnapshotDependencyBlocked, SnapshotRestoreConflict, NetworkConflict, DeviceUnavailable, HostResourceRisk, CredentialUnavailable, ImportUnsupported, ExportFailed, ViewerDisconnected, GuestIntegrationUnavailable, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied and CapabilityUnavailable plus provider-specific diagnostic codes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Partial provider/storage operations return succeeded/failed/remaining resources and recovery steps; Mini Computer MUST NOT report rollback/cleanup success unless verified.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Platform capability behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and other supported desktop hosts preserve the same canonical VM/provider/media model while capability-negotiating the built-in VirtualBox fork, hardware acceleration, host networking, device passthrough and filesystem/storage behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web surfaces may manage/view remote Mini Computer providers/VMs when an authorised remote execution provider exists but MUST NOT pretend the browser itself can provide unrestricted local hardware virtualisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unsupported architecture/provider combinations are explicit release/platform exceptions rather than silent missing UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Mini Computer follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The maintained 9to1 VirtualBox fork is available as the built-in/default provider and a new supported VM can be created without connecting another hypervisor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The VirtualBox donor-parity audit records preserved/expanded/replaced/not-applicable mature VM capabilities and separately licensed proprietary components are not silently bundled.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A user can connect at least one alternative provider implementation through the VirtualisationProvider contract and provider capability differences are surfaced accurately.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A VM retains stable VMID across rename/reopen and provider-internal identity is mapped rather than becoming the only identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A supported guest can be created, install media attached, started, installed, shut down, reopened and run again without configuration loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Start, Pause, Resume, Save State, graceful Shutdown and Power Off have distinct verified lifecycle semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Closing/disconnecting the viewer leaves a headless-running VM running according to policy and reopening Mini Computer reconnects rather than creating a duplicate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Snapshot creation/restoration preserves the provider-declared disk/memory state and clearly excludes state the provider cannot capture.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deleting/consolidating snapshots cannot silently break a dependent linked clone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Full clone and provider-supported linked clone create distinct VM identities and preserve base dependencies correctly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Representative virtual-disk create/attach/resize/convert/delete operations preserve dependencies and require appropriate verification for destructive changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: BIOS/UEFI and supported Secure Boot/TPM configurations are represented accurately for a representative modern guest.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: NAT, bridged/host-only/private and representative port-forward configuration work on a capable provider and network dependencies block unsafe deletion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clipboard, drag/drop and shared folders enforce configured direction/read-write policy rather than enabling broad host access automatically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Physical device passthrough exposes the host-impact warning/permission and does not silently detach devices from the host.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider/host Virtualisation Status distinguishes disabled hardware acceleration, provider unavailable and feature unsupported states with actionable diagnostics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The ISO Browser lists only registered/curated publisher providers rather than arbitrary unverified Internet downloads.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An OfficialDirect ISO acquisition downloads from the publisher-authorised source without CAKE rehosting it and records acquisition provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A MirrorPermitted catalogue entry can be mirrored only when its configured redistribution policy explicitly permits the exact image; otherwise mirroring is blocked.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A downloaded ISO with authoritative checksum/signature metadata is verified before being labelled Verified and a mismatch blocks normal trusted acquisition flow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: UserSupplied and ProviderFlow catalogue policies work without falsely claiming CAKE supplies the operating system image.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The same immutable ISO can be referenced by multiple VMs without unnecessary duplicate canonical copies and removal identifies active mounts/dependencies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unattended installation keeps passwords/product keys out of ordinary logs, project source and AI context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: OVF/OVA or representative mature donor import/export previews hardware/network differences and preserves the declared source/revision scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mini Computer Files resources remain addressable while large mutable block data can use an appropriate provider without being misrepresented as ordinary sync documents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal opens a VM-specific EnvironmentID/serial or guest shell and clearly distinguishes VM from host command execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev OS Run uses Mini Computer's canonical engine to build/package → attach boot artifact → boot VM → expose viewer/serial/debug state rather than launching a separate hidden hypervisor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An ephemeral Dev VM can be discarded/preserved according to run policy without mutating the base template.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI VM actions route through typed Mini Computer/provider APIs and dangerous disk/snapshot/device/network operations receive the applicable impact verification.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Import/export/download/clone/snapshot consolidation jobs report real progress/cancellation/recovery state without fabricating completion.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Keyboard/screen-reader workflows cover VM creation, ISO Browser, VM state controls, settings, snapshots and provider status.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and supported remote/web management preserve the same canonical Mini Computer model while capability-negotiating local execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When Home is absent at process start, Mini Computer follows the global Install Home/bootstrap contract.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Utilities

heading: HEADING_2
text: Browse

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Browse is a full Firefox-derived browser product with native CUI chrome and native CUI internal surfaces. Firefox/Gecko is the primary donor, default web engine and behavioural baseline. Chromium/Blink is a first-class secondary browser/rendering backend available per tab. Browse MUST remain one coherent browser with one canonical 9to1-owned tab/session model; Chromium support MUST NOT be implemented as a second browser bolted onto Firefox or as a separate user profile universe.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Donor authority and parity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Firefox donor parity is the minimum supported capability set, not the finished feature ceiling. Unless a feature is explicitly replaced, excluded or made incompatible by an approved 9to1 architecture decision, Browse MUST retain mature Firefox functionality and quality-of-life behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tabs and windows, including restore/reopen behaviour, pinned tabs and normal navigation history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Profiles, bookmarks, history, downloads, browsing-data controls, site permissions, privacy/security controls and appropriate password/passkey integration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Firefox developer tooling, reader/media functionality, picture-in-picture where donor-supported, accessibility, keyboard navigation, crash/session recovery and mature settings/configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: WebExtension compatibility to the maximum extent supported by the retained Firefox APIs, with unsupported or engine-specific APIs surfaced explicitly rather than silently ignored.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All Firefox proprietary or embedded AI surfaces are non-authoritative and MUST be removed or replaced by Dulche-backed 9to1 surfaces. The agent MUST NOT preserve a Firefox AI sidebar, chatbot, assistant or proprietary AI integration merely for donor parity.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Web engine architecture

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each web BrowserTab selects a WebEngine value of Firefox/Gecko or Chromium/Blink. The normal user-facing choice SHOULD be labelled Firefox and Chromium; implementation and diagnostics MAY additionally expose the underlying Gecko and Blink engine names. Gecko is the default unless the user or a persisted site rule selects Chromium.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing a tab between Firefox and Chromium changes the renderer/backend used for the page, not the canonical identity of the tab, workspace or Browse session. Switching engines reloads/reconstructs the document through the selected backend. Engine-private runtime state such as DOM objects, JavaScript heaps and renderer-process memory is not required to transfer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browse MUST own canonical higher-level browser entities instead of allowing Gecko and Chromium to directly share raw profile databases. At minimum the architecture must model BrowserProfile, BrowserTab, NavigationEntry, Bookmark, HistoryEntry, Download, SitePermission, Workspace, TabGroup, SplitView, SearchProvider, SiteEnhancer and EnginePreference as typed 9to1-owned entities or equivalent strongly typed contracts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gecko and Chromium MUST be isolated internally. They MUST NOT be pointed at the same physical cookie/profile/session database. Engine adapters translate the relevant canonical Browse state into each backend and propagate supported changes back to Browse.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to use Firefox for this tab, Chromium for this tab, always Firefox for a site/domain, always Chromium for a site/domain, and reset a persisted site engine preference. A broken page SHOULD be switchable to the other engine with one obvious action without opening a separate browser product.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automatic upstream maintenance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Firefox/Gecko and Chromium/Blink frameworks MUST be maintained continuously against the latest appropriate upstream release and MUST automatically detect and ingest newer upstream versions when available. A long-lived stale engine is a maintenance defect.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automatic update does not mean blindly shipping an unvalidated upstream binary. The update pipeline MUST fetch/rebase or reapply maintained 9to1 changes, build the affected engine integration, run Browse compatibility and regression suites, verify CUI integration, engine switching, extension baselines, session/profile isolation, Site Enhancer behaviour, DevTools integration and Dulche browser capabilities, and promote the new engine only after the applicable acceptance gates pass. Security-sensitive upstream releases receive expedited priority. The previous known-good engine build MUST remain rollback-capable until promotion is proven stable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: CUI and URI namespace contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browse has four distinct first-class content namespaces. They MUST remain architecturally and security-distinct even when multiple namespaces ultimately render through CUI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: cui:// — generic CUI-rendered surfaces and extension-defined/custom CUI pages. This is the general CUI namespace and is not synonymous with Browse internals.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: browse:// — Browse-owned internal pages such as browse://newtab, browse://settings, browse://downloads, browse://history, browse://extensions and other Browse-owned management surfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1:// — native 9to1 application surfaces hosted inside a Browse tab, for example 9to1://Spaces, 9to1://Write or a typed deep link such as 9to1://Write/<resource>. These are the actual application surfaces, not web versions or reduced browser copies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: https:// and http:// — ordinary web content. User-facing normal web navigation uses these web schemes; Browse-owned, CUI and native-app content MUST NOT masquerade as an HTTP(S) origin.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Internal compatibility plumbing inherited from donors MAY exist only where technically unavoidable, but it MUST NOT be exposed as a competing public routing model. The 9to1 routing contract above is authoritative.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Native 9to1 app surfaces in tabs

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening 9to1://<App> MUST instantiate the real CUI application surface and the real application services inside the Browse tab. It MUST NOT load a separately implemented web edition, feature-reduced embedded edition or imitation of the app. Responsive layout adaptation is allowed and expected; capability divergence merely because the app is hosted in Browse is not.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1:// routes MUST be registered centrally by the application/router registry and support typed deep links to canonical resources where the owning app supports them. A tab title and icon should reflect the actual resource/app instead of exposing an opaque route string as its primary label.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The same canonical app data/state MUST be addressed regardless of whether the app is opened in its normal standalone surface or through 9to1:// in Browse. Opening the same Write document, Board, Space or Data workbook in multiple valid surfaces MUST NOT silently create disconnected copies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 native app tabs participate in normal Browse capabilities including tab groups, pinning, workspaces, restore/reopen and Split View. A user can therefore place 9to1://Write with a research document beside an https:// research page, or combine two different native 9to1 apps, without requiring a separate web version of either app.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Profiles and workspaces

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browser profiles are tab-scoped, not window-scoped. Every BrowserTab carries a ProfileID or equivalent profile context, allowing one window, one workspace and one Split View to contain tabs from different profiles simultaneously.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A BrowserProfile is an identity/storage/privacy boundary. Depending on supported configuration, it owns or scopes cookies, login sessions, site storage, site permissions, browsing-data attribution, extensions and extension state, search preferences, Site Enhancers, credentials/passkeys and other profile-specific browser configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Workspace is an organisational/session construct rather than an identity boundary. A workspace may contain tabs from multiple profiles and owns organisational state such as open tabs, groups, split arrangements, workspace pins and layout. Switching workspace MUST NOT inherently sign the user into or out of websites.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Profile identity MUST be visually discoverable on tabs and in relevant browser UI so the user can tell which account/session context will be used. Consequential actions and Dulche-controlled actions SHOULD make the active profile context clear where confusion could cause the action to occur under the wrong identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing a tab to another profile MUST reopen/recreate its web session under the destination profile rather than copying authentication material across profile boundaries. Safe navigation/organisation metadata such as URL, group, workspace and split position may be preserved where applicable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Tabs, groups and placement

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browse MUST provide modern tab management in addition to Firefox donor parity. Tab groups are first-class canonical entities with stable identity, naming, optional colour/icon metadata, collapse/expand state, persistence, restore, drag/drop and movement between windows/workspaces. Dulche and other typed APIs can address a group directly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tab-strip placement MUST be a first-class configurable preference with full feature parity in all four orientations:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Horizontal tabs at the top.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Horizontal tabs at the bottom.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vertical tabs on the left.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vertical tabs on the right.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The interface MUST adapt properly to each orientation rather than mechanically moving a top strip. Groups, pinned tabs, profile indicators, drag/reorder, tab search, previews, context menus, engine state where surfaced, close/reopen, Dulche mentions and split operations MUST remain functional in every orientation. Compact/collapsed and appropriate auto-expand behaviours may be provided as configurable presentation options.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Split View

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Split View displays two independent BrowserTab entities side-by-side in one browser content area with a resizable divider. The split container owns presentation only; each pane remains a real tab with its own URL/route, navigation history, profile, renderer/backend where applicable and canonical tab identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A split may mix any compatible tab surface classes, including web + web, 9to1 app + web, 9to1 app + 9to1 app, Browse internal + web and tabs from different BrowserProfiles. Either pane can be swapped, unsplit or moved without destroying the underlying tab.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The two-pane experience is the required baseline. The architecture SHOULD avoid assumptions that make future multi-pane layouts impossible, but more than two panes is not required unless separately specified.

heading: HEADING_3
text: New Tab canvas

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: browse://newtab is a fully customisable CUI-native canvas rather than a fixed shortcut grid. Users can add, remove, move, resize and configure components. Layout persists according to the active profile and may support workspace-specific overrides where configured.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canvas can host deterministic widgets, browser widgets, 9to1 app widgets, extension-provided CUI widgets, static content and Generative Areas. It SHOULD reuse shared 9to1 canvas/layout infrastructure where practical instead of creating an incompatible bespoke layout system.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Generative Area is a persistent container defined by a natural-language instruction, for example 'put some YouTube videos here for me to watch' or 'show my upcoming deadlines'. It stores the instruction/configuration, not merely one frozen model answer. It may refresh manually, on New Tab open or on an allowed schedule and may expose source restrictions, maximum item count, presentation style and network/Dulche permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generative Areas MUST resolve real canonical entities when the requested content refers to tabs, Files, events, 9to1 objects or other structured data. They MUST NOT fabricate canonical objects merely to fill a container. Generated/recommended content SHOULD remain distinguishable from deterministic widget output.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Search and AI entry

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The primary New Tab/address search entry MUST expose two explicit modes: Search and AI. Search is the default. The active mode is clearly visible and switchable quickly, including by keyboard.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search mode performs normal navigation/search behaviour and MUST NOT invoke an LLM merely to execute an ordinary URL or provider query. AI mode sends the request to Dulche and can use permissioned Browse capabilities and referenced browser/app context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browse MUST support a typed SearchProvider contract and allow the user to configure a default provider plus an optional secondary provider. Providers may supply query construction, suggestions and declared privacy/capability metadata. Extension-defined providers may participate through the same contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browse MUST support searching two providers at once. Dual-provider search creates one real tab per provider for the same query and places those tabs into the standard Split View, one provider per pane. This MUST reuse normal BrowserTab and SplitView infrastructure rather than a bespoke dual-search renderer. Single-provider search remains the normal default unless the user configures otherwise.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dulche browser experience

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche is the only authoritative AI system in Browse. Firefox-provided proprietary AI surfaces MUST be removed/replaced. Browse SHOULD provide both a persistent Dulche sidebar for larger tasks and a lightweight floating/command bar for contextual requests, using the shared Dulche runtime rather than launching a browser-specific model server.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Dulche UI MUST support @-mentioning canonical browser context. At minimum users can mention tabs and SHOULD be able to mention tab groups, workspaces, split panes and other supported Browse entities. Mention autocomplete resolves to stable canonical IDs rather than copying only titles/URLs into the prompt.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples include comparing @Durham with @York, summarising all tabs in @Coursework, or asking Dulche to use a referenced 9to1://Write document together with an https:// research tab. Where the referenced surface is a native 9to1 app, Dulche MUST use that app's semantic APIs rather than screen-scraping its CUI.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Permissioned autonomous browsing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: With explicit user permission, Dulche can autonomously operate Browse for a task. A request such as 'scroll through YouTube and pick out some good videos' may inspect visible/accessible results, scroll, open candidates, compare them and return recommendations without requiring confirmation for every benign intermediate interaction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permission scope MUST be explicit and composable. The implementation must support equivalents of read this page, control this tab, control these selected tabs and control Browse for this task. Granting one scope MUST NOT silently grant permanent global browser control.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browser automation SHOULD use structured semantic capabilities such as Navigate, OpenTab, CloseTab, ActivateTab, ReadPage, ReadElement, Find, Scroll, Click, FillField, SelectOption, GoBack, GoForward and Reload when structured control exists. Blind coordinate input is a fallback, not the primary architecture.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consequential external actions remain governed by the shared 9to1 permission/confirmation policy. Purchases, publishing/sending, destructive account changes, security changes, credential disclosure/entry and comparable external side effects MUST NOT become implicitly authorised merely because Dulche was permitted to browse.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Extensions and CUI extension surfaces

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Firefox/WebExtension compatibility MUST be retained to the maximum practical extent. Because a tab may use Firefox/Gecko or Chromium/Blink, extension capability MUST be explicit. An extension may be Gecko-compatible, Chromium-compatible through supported adapters, compatible with both, Browse/CUI-only, partially compatible or unsupported in the active engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Switching one tab to Chromium MUST NOT silently uninstall an extension, disable it globally or make it disappear. Engine-specific limitations MUST be surfaced predictably.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extensions can register supported CUI surfaces using cui:// routing and the extension CUI API, including settings pages, dashboards, sidebars, tool panels, New Tab components or other permitted custom pages. CUI rendering permission does not imply unrestricted Browse or 9to1 internal access; capabilities remain sandboxed and permission-scoped.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Site Enhancer

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browse MUST provide a first-class Site Enhancer feature inspired by mature site-customisation systems such as Arc Boosts while remaining a 9to1-native capability. A SiteEnhancer is a versioned, enable/disable-able canonical object associated with one or more domain/site match patterns.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Site Enhancers can define supported visual customisation such as colours, typography, spacing/layout adjustments, element visibility, backgrounds and custom CSS, plus controlled client-side behaviour/scripts where explicitly supported. They must declare permissions/capabilities and execute within a defined safety boundary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche can help create or modify a Site Enhancer from natural language, for example 'make YouTube less cluttered and hide Shorts'. Dulche MUST present the proposed effect/permissions at the appropriate confirmation boundary rather than silently installing arbitrary persistent scripts. Extensions may provide Site Enhancers through the same permissioned model.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Files, drag/drop and cross-app integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browse retains a mature Download entity/lifecycle while completed files integrate with the shared Files system so reveal/open/share/drag workflows use canonical 9to1 file semantics. Interrupted downloads, retries and completion state remain visible and recoverable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Split panes and tabs SHOULD support semantic drag/drop. Where both surfaces understand a canonical 9to1 entity, transfer the typed entity/link instead of degrading it to copied text. Examples include dragging a Maps place into Planner or a Board item into Write. Web upload targets may receive files through normal browser security/permission rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites can open project previews in Browse and Browse development context can offer Open project in Sites/Open source in Dev when the page is linked to a local project. Dev can launch localhost/development targets directly into Browse. Mature Firefox developer tools MUST be retained/adapted rather than replaced by a feature-poor custom inspector.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Security and origin isolation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: cui://, browse:// and 9to1:// are privileged/non-web namespaces with separate routing and origin/capability rules. Ordinary HTTP(S) pages MUST NOT be able to inspect native app state, call privileged CUI/Browse APIs, forge trusted 9to1:// content or inherit internal permissions simply by navigating to or linking an internal route.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A web page may request navigation to an allowed registered internal route only through the normal navigation/policy boundary. Navigating to 9to1:// does not grant the originating site the destination app's authority. Profile cookies/credentials and engine-private state MUST remain isolated according to their owning profile/backend.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Recovery and degraded states

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browse MUST handle Firefox renderer crashes, Chromium renderer crashes, whole-browser crashes, failed engine startup, unavailable selected engines, extension incompatibility, interrupted downloads, invalid/corrupt engine-private state and failed engine switches without corrupting the other engine or canonical Browse profile state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Session recovery SHOULD restore tabs, groups, workspaces, split arrangements, ProfileID and per-tab engine preference wherever safe. If a preferred engine is unavailable, Browse MUST surface the degraded state and offer a safe fallback rather than silently losing the tab or rewriting profile data.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Browse acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Firefox donor parity remains present except for explicit 9to1 replacements/exclusions; proprietary Firefox AI surfaces are replaced by Dulche.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gecko-default and Chromium alternative rendering work within one canonical Browse tab/session model, with engine/profile isolation and per-site engine rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Both upstream engine frameworks can update automatically through validated build/test/promotion and rollback pipelines.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: cui://, browse://, 9to1:// and HTTP(S) routes resolve to the correct security/content surface, including real native 9to1 app rendering inside tabs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Profiles can be mixed per tab, per workspace and inside Split View without cross-profile cookie/session leakage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tab groups, split tabs and top/bottom/left/right tab-strip placement retain equivalent core functionality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: browse://newtab provides the customisable widget/generative canvas, Search/AI switch and dual-provider split search.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche @ mentions resolve to canonical browser/app entities and permissioned autonomous browsing uses semantic browser capabilities with consequential-action safeguards.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extension compatibility states, extension CUI surfaces and Site Enhancer permissions behave explicitly and recoverably.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crash/session recovery preserves canonical Browse state and a failure in one renderer does not corrupt the other renderer/profile state.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Maps

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Maps is the canonical geospatial, place, landmark, routing and navigation service for the 9to1 ecosystem as well as a full user-facing CUI application. Other apps MUST consume Maps entities, APIs and embeddable CUI surfaces rather than independently inventing incompatible place, route or location models.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Primary donor and default provider stack

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The primary mature donor is the latest appropriate CoMaps source. The maintained 9to1 Maps fork/adaptation MUST preserve applicable CoMaps mapping, offline-map, POI, favourites, tracks, navigation and route-planning functionality and mature quality-of-life behaviour unless this specification explicitly replaces it. CUI replaces/adapts the donor user interface without reducing the mature capability baseline.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Maps MUST separate the donor application from provider services behind typed interfaces. The default open stack is:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: OpenStreetMap data as the principal open geographic dataset.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MapLibre Native as the default provider-facing/vector-map rendering framework where appropriate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The retained CoMaps-derived offline map/rendering/search/routing pipeline for mature downloadable/offline operation where it provides capability not equivalently supplied by the online stack.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pelias as the default self-hostable online geocoding, reverse-geocoding and place-search service.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Valhalla as the default self-hostable routing/navigation service for supported travel modes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: GTFS/GTFS-Realtime-compatible transit data through a typed transit provider; an OpenTripPlanner-compatible implementation may be used where appropriate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Traffic, satellite, terrain, street-level imagery and specialist datasets as optional provider capabilities rather than hard-coded assumptions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation MUST NOT make public OpenStreetMap community tile or public Nominatim endpoints an unlimited production dependency. Provider-specific usage, caching, attribution, redistribution and offline-storage rules MUST be enforced. 9to1-hosted/self-hosted services and user-connected providers can be substituted through the same typed provider contracts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: One provider does not need to supply every capability. Rendering, map data, geocoding, search, routing, transit, traffic, imagery and offline datasets MUST be independently replaceable where technically possible. Provider identity, provenance, freshness and required attribution MUST remain available to Maps.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical geospatial entities

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps MUST define stable canonical entities rather than allowing each app to store copied address strings. At minimum, the typed model must cover Place, Address, Coordinate, Route, RouteLeg, RouteStep, SavedPlace, PersonalLandmark, CommunityPOI, MapView, SearchResult, SearchProvider, MapProviderReference and SavedRoute/CustomJourney or equivalent strongly typed contracts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Place may reference one or more provider records, OpenStreetMap objects, community objects or user-authored data without making any single provider identifier the canonical 9to1 identity. Provider records are provenance references, not the primary identity of a saved 9to1 entity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner, Events, Spaces, Boards, Write, Present, Forms, Automations and other apps MUST reference canonical Place/Route/Landmark IDs through typed APIs where a persistent location relationship is required.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Search / AI interaction

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps MUST use the same explicit Search / AI interaction pattern established elsewhere in 9to1. Search is the default mode. The selected mode is always visible and can be switched immediately without losing the selected place, route or current map context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search mode performs deterministic geographic discovery and manual route construction. It must search, as applicable, addresses, postcodes, coordinates, named places, businesses/POIs, categories, saved places, PersonalLandmarks, CommunityPOIs and supported 9to1 entities with attached locations. Provider result confidence and ambiguity MUST remain visible; Maps MUST NOT fabricate an exact address or place identity from weak geocoding.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Selecting a result opens a canonical place/details surface with provenance and relevant actions such as View, Navigate, Add to route, Set as start, Set as destination, Add stop, Save, Share and other capability-appropriate actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI mode is a Dulche-backed natural-language Maps interface operating the same canonical Maps state and APIs. Requests such as 'take me to the nearest Starbucks', 'find somewhere quiet to study within a 15-minute walk', 'find a bench along this route' or 'add a coffee stop halfway home' MUST be resolved through real search/location/routing capabilities rather than invented model knowledge.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A request such as 'take me to the nearest Starbucks' should resolve the permitted current location, search real place providers, rank valid candidates according to the user's request and actual route/travel distance where available, resolve the chosen candidate to a canonical Place, calculate a route and start/present navigation according to the explicit user intent. If multiple interpretations materially affect the result, Maps must present candidates or request the minimum necessary disambiguation rather than guessing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search and AI are interoperable. A place found manually can become AI context, and an AI-generated route/place remains a normal canonical Maps object that the user can inspect, edit, reorder, save or share manually.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Saved places and personal landmarks

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can save ordinary provider/OpenStreetMap places and create PersonalLandmarks anywhere on the map. A PersonalLandmark does not require an existing mapped place, recognised address, road, POI or provider object; a coordinate and user-defined identity are sufficient.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to drop a pin at any coordinate, name it, optionally categorise it, add notes/metadata, save it privately, share it explicitly and navigate to it. Examples include a meeting point, favourite viewpoint, shortcut entrance, personal picnic spot or a specific bench.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Common saved places such as Home, College, Church or Work are canonical SavedPlace references. Other apps resolve these references through Maps rather than retaining independent copies of the underlying address.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Personal/private landmarks are private by default. Creating a private landmark MUST NOT implicitly publish its coordinates, name, notes or category to the community database or an external provider.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Community POIs and landmark presets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps MUST provide a first-class community POI system so users can contribute useful hyperlocal geographic data over time. Users can choose a structured preset when dropping a pin, including extensible categories such as Bench, Bin, Recycling point, Picnic table, Picnic area, Public toilet, Drinking-water point, Bicycle parking, Bicycle repair/pump, EV charger, Bus stop, Crossing, Defibrillator, Viewpoint, Playground, Entrance, Accessible entrance, Steps, Lift, Ramp and Shelter.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Presets represent typed POI categories, not merely icons. A category can expose optional structured attributes appropriate to that object. For example, a Bench may record backrest, armrests, cover, capacity, material, accessibility or condition; a Bin may record waste/recycling type and condition. The common contribution path MUST remain fast: a user can submit a useful POI with minimal required fields and enrich it later.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users choose explicitly between keeping a landmark private and submitting it publicly. Public submission creates or proposes a CommunityPOI in the 9to1 community geographic database; it is not the same action as contributing to OpenStreetMap.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CommunityPOI records must retain stable identity, coordinate, category, structured attributes, source/provenance, creation/update metadata, verification state, edit history, confidence/quality information and reports/flags as applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The community system MUST support a quality lifecycle such as Submitted/Unverified, Community-confirmed and Verified, together with corrections such as Removed, Wrong location, Wrong category, Duplicate and Details changed. A user can confirm that an existing object is still present without recreating it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before creating a public POI, Maps SHOULD perform deterministic nearby duplicate detection using distance, category compatibility and known identifiers. If a likely duplicate exists, the user can confirm/update the existing object or explicitly state that the new object is distinct.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Community POIs are first-class searchable/routable destinations. Users can search for categories such as benches, bins or picnic tables, enable category layers and ask Dulche structured queries such as 'find a walking route with benches along the way'.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a community contribution maps cleanly to OpenStreetMap semantics, Maps MAY separately offer an explicit 'Contribute to OpenStreetMap' flow subject to OSM account, licensing, validation and editing rules. Public submission to the 9to1 community database MUST NOT silently publish to OpenStreetMap or another third party.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Routing and route planning

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps MUST support route planning for driving, walking, cycling and public transport where the active providers/data support those modes, with typed extension points for additional modes. Routes contain structured legs/steps, provider provenance, travel-mode information, timing/freshness where applicable and sufficient geometry for rendering/navigation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A route can be referenced, embedded, shared and manipulated by other 9to1 apps. A route is not reduced to copied text directions. Alternative routes and provider uncertainty/freshness remain available where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal route building in Search mode MUST allow selecting an origin/destination, adding intermediate places, reordering/removing stops and editing route preferences without invoking AI.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Saved custom routes / Custom Journeys

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to build, name, save, edit, duplicate, share and later start reusable custom routes/journeys. A custom route can describe both where the user travels and what the user intends to do along the way; it is richer than a simple list of waypoints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A SavedRoute/CustomJourney must support ordered typed steps such as TravelStep, StopStep, WaitStep, ActivityStep and ManualInstructionStep or equivalent. Examples include walk to a coordinate, sit on a named bench, wait ten minutes, grab coffee from a selected place, use a shortcut, take a particular entrance, then continue to college.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each step may include a canonical Place/Landmark/Coordinate reference, transport mode, optional timing or stop duration, notes, routing preferences and required/preferred/optional semantics. These semantics allow dynamic rerouting to adapt ordinary travel segments without silently removing user-authored intent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users may create user-defined path segments that are not present in provider routing graphs, for example a campus cut-through, alley, informal footpath or other personally known shortcut. Such segments MUST be visibly marked as user-defined/unverified by provider routing data and MUST NOT be presented as provider-validated infrastructure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI mode can create and edit SavedRoutes from natural language, for example: 'Create my Walk to College route: walk to the bench by the river, sit there for ten minutes, grab coffee from Z, take the shortcut behind the library, then turn right to college.' Dulche resolves real referenced entities where possible and must present ambiguity rather than hallucinating a landmark.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: During active navigation, non-travel steps such as 'sit on Riverside Bench for 5 minutes' or 'grab coffee' are valid current journey steps. The route can continue after the user marks/completes/skips the step according to the journey model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Saved custom routes can be shared with other users where permissions allow, preserving route geometry, user-defined instructions, typed stops and shared/community landmark references. Private landmark details must not be leaked merely because a route is shared; sharing semantics must explicitly handle private dependencies.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Navigation to arbitrary/custom destinations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any canonical Place, PersonalLandmark, CommunityPOI or raw permitted coordinate can be a navigation destination even when no street address exists. Routing SHOULD bring the user to the closest supported route-graph point and then represent the actual final coordinate honestly rather than inventing a road/entrance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Custom/community destinations must participate in navigation, route sharing, Planner/Event references and Dulche requests just like provider-defined places, while retaining provenance and verification status.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Live information and dynamic routing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where providers support it, Maps can expose live traffic, incidents, road closures, transit departures/delays and dynamic journey times. Live-looking information MUST retain provider provenance and freshness timestamps/state. Stale data MUST NOT be represented as current.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Saved/custom journeys may be dynamically rerouted around disruptions while preserving required user-authored stops/instructions where feasible. If a required custom/user-defined segment cannot be validated or becomes impractical, Maps must surface the conflict rather than silently deleting that instruction.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Location permissions and privacy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Location data is sensitive. Maps/Home permissions MUST distinguish at least resolving a known PlaceID, searching places, approximate current location, precise current location and background location. Location history, if implemented, requires a separately explicit capability/retention model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An app does not automatically receive the user's live location merely because it can call Maps APIs. Dulche natural-language requests are subject to the same location permissions; 'near me' and routing requests cannot bypass precise-location controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search history, route history, precise locations, Home/Work-style places, saved routes and private landmarks require user-visible retention/clear controls. Sensitive location history MUST NOT automatically become globally indexed Go content or extension-readable data.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Offline operation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps MUST retain mature CoMaps-derived offline capability and support downloadable regions where data/provider licences permit. Offline mode should support map rendering and, where the retained/local datasets allow it, place search/geocoding and routing without requiring a live cloud service.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Downloaded region management must show storage usage, version/freshness and update state. Licence/provider rules govern whether particular imagery/tiles/datasets may be cached or redistributed; unsupported offline caching MUST fail explicitly rather than silently violating provider terms.

heading: HEADING_3
text: CUI embeds and cross-app composition

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps is both a full app and a CUI surface provider. It MUST expose reusable typed CUI components such as PlaceCard, MapView/MiniMap, LocationPicker, RouteCard and Journey/Navigation surfaces so other 9to1 apps can embed real Maps functionality without cloning it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Planner/Events can attach canonical Places/Routes; Boards and Spaces can embed interactive Place/Map cards; Write/Present can insert linked map/place/route objects; Forms can use the canonical LocationPicker; Automations can reference place/location conditions subject to permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps MUST be available as the real native surface through 9to1://Maps and support typed deep links to canonical place/route/journey objects. It therefore participates naturally in Browse tabs and Split View, for example Maps beside Planner or Write beside a route.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dulche integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche accesses Maps through typed semantic capabilities, not map-pixel scraping. Capabilities can include SearchPlaces, ResolvePlace, GetCurrentLocation, BuildRoute, ModifyRoute, SearchCommunityPOIs, CreateLandmark, CreateSavedRoute, AddRouteStep and StartNavigation subject to the appropriate permission/action policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Natural-language context such as 'near me', 'near college', 'between here and home', 'along this route', 'around that place' or 'the restaurant I just looked at' must resolve against real permitted Maps state: current location, SavedPlaces, selected Places, active route/journey and recent canonical Maps entities.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Automations and extensions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps may expose automation triggers such as arrive at place, leave place, enter/exit radius, material route-duration change or transit disruption where platform/background capabilities and permissions support them. Persistent/background location requires explicit OS/Home permission and MUST NOT be inferred from ordinary foreground Maps access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extensions may add providers, overlays, POI categories, route modes, map layers or specialist geospatial tools through typed capability contracts. Providing a layer/provider does not automatically grant precise location, private landmark access or route history.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Safety, provenance and disclaimer

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Maps MUST present map and calculated route data as guidance rather than guaranteed ground truth. A displayed road, path, crossing, entrance, restriction, building, POI or route MUST NOT be represented as guaranteed to exist, be accessible, be legal to use or be safe merely because it appears in provider/community data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The following compact user-facing disclaimer is required in Maps and MUST be available during route/navigation use: 'Map data is sourced by third party providers and community volunteers. Check important routes.'

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A fuller safety/data notice may additionally explain that provider/community data can be incomplete, inaccurate or outdated and that users should follow real-world signs, restrictions and conditions. The compact notice does not replace the product's separately reviewed legal terms.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Community/unverified objects must expose verification/provenance state where relevant and MUST NOT be styled in a way that falsely implies the same confidence as independently established/provider-verified data.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Maps acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The latest appropriate CoMaps donor baseline is retained/adapted with CUI without losing mature offline/navigation behaviour except where explicitly replaced.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Open provider interfaces support the agreed default OSM/MapLibre/Pelias/Valhalla stack and allow independent replacement of rendering, search/geocoding, routing, transit, traffic and imagery capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Place, Route, SavedPlace, PersonalLandmark, CommunityPOI and SavedRoute/CustomJourney have stable canonical identities usable across 9to1 apps.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search mode supports deterministic place discovery/manual route building; AI mode uses Dulche against the same canonical Maps state and typed capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can drop a pin anywhere, create a private custom landmark, navigate to it, choose structured POI presets and explicitly submit community POIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Community POI duplicate detection, provenance, verification/update lifecycle, reports and routable/searchable behaviour are implemented without silently publishing to OpenStreetMap.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Saved custom routes support typed travel/stop/wait/activity/manual steps, required/preferred/optional intent, user-defined shortcut/path segments, AI creation/editing and safe sharing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Location permissions distinguish approximate/precise/background access and prevent unrelated apps/extensions from inheriting sensitive location data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Offline maps remain usable where licences/data permit and do not rely on prohibited bulk use of public community endpoints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1://Maps and reusable Maps CUI surfaces integrate with Planner, Events, Boards, Spaces, Write/Present, Forms, Automations, Browse and Dulche.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The required route/data disclaimer and provenance/freshness states are present; Maps never represents provider/community route data as guaranteed real-world truth.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Launcher

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Launcher is the Android/9to1-OS home launcher. It is a maintained fork/adaptation of the latest appropriate Lawnchair source and is a distinct product from Shelf. Launcher MUST NOT be implemented as the cross-platform 9to1 package installer/updater or as the Shelf quick-access library.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Lawnchair donor authority

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Lawnchair is the primary donor and mature behavioural baseline for Launcher. Applicable donor functionality and quality-of-life behaviour MUST be retained unless this specification explicitly replaces it. The goal is not merely donor parity: 9to1 Launcher is intended to be substantially more customisable than conventional Android launchers, including mature highly-customisable launchers such as Nova Launcher, while remaining coherent, performant and accessible.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Core launcher surfaces

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launcher owns the Android-style home screen, home pages, app drawer, dock, folders, widgets, app shortcuts, gestures, app discovery and visual organisation of installed applications. It consumes the authoritative installed-application/package registry owned by Home/platform package infrastructure; it does not maintain a competing package database.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiple configurable home pages with drag/reorder and persistent layout.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: App drawer with configurable organisation, sorting, categories, visibility rules and search.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Configurable dock, including size, rows/columns where supported, presentation and behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Folders with configurable appearance, layout, ordering and appropriate actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pinned/favourite apps, hidden apps and application shortcuts/actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compatible Android widgets plus 9to1-native CUI widgets through a shared widget abstraction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Backup/restore of launcher layout and settings, with account/device sync where enabled and compatible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Full accessibility, keyboard/navigation support and appropriate touch/controller interaction.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Extreme customisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launcher MUST expose unusually deep customisation while preserving usable defaults. The architecture must avoid hard-coding one visual layout so additional options can be added without rewriting core launcher state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Grid dimensions, independent horizontal/vertical spacing, margins, page padding and icon placement behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Icon size, icon shape/masking, per-app icon overrides, icon packs, labels, label typography and label visibility.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dock geometry, drawer geometry, folder geometry and home-page-specific layout configuration where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Backgrounds, transparency, blur, theme/accent integration and supported animation/transition behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Gesture mapping including swipe, double-tap, pinch and other supported gestures, with actions resolved through typed commands rather than hard-coded donor-only behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Per-page, per-folder and per-component presentation options where doing so remains understandable and performant.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Import/export of launcher configuration and recoverable handling of unsupported/missing configuration after platform or donor updates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launcher should offer strong defaults and discoverable presets so extreme customisation does not require every user to configure dozens of controls before the launcher is usable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Applications and stable identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launcher placement MUST reference stable InstalledApplication/Application IDs from the authoritative platform registry rather than raw executable/package paths. Updating an app must not destroy its home-screen placement, folder membership or configured icon unless the application's canonical identity actually changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launcher can represent Android apps, 9to1-native apps and other platform-recognised application targets exposed through the OS compatibility/application registry. Package install, uninstall, update, repair, rollback and channel management remain Home/platform responsibilities. Launcher may surface status/actions such as 'update available' but delegates execution to the authoritative package service.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Widgets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-native apps and extensions can register typed CUI launcher widgets with declared supported sizes, configuration surfaces, update behaviour, data permissions and actions. Compatible Android App Widgets remain supported where the Android platform layer permits them. Launcher MUST present both through a coherent placement/resizing model without pretending they share identical runtime/security semantics.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Dulche integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche is a first-class Launcher capability rather than an add-on. With user permission it can inspect and modify semantic launcher layout/configuration through typed APIs instead of simulating touch gestures.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example requests include 'make a page for college', 'put all my games into folders', 'move Maps into the dock', 'make this page denser', 'add my upcoming events widget' or 'make a Development page with Dev, Stack and Terminal'. Dulche MUST operate on canonical launcher entities and honour the same profile, permission and package boundaries as manual actions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Search and Go integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launcher can expose search/application discovery, but universal retrieval/navigation/action logic belongs to Go, which is specified under OS. Launcher search SHOULD consume Go providers/results where appropriate and render them in Launcher context rather than implementing an incompatible second system-wide index.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Profiles and OS boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launcher MUST respect Android/OS user, work-profile and application-profile boundaries. Profile-specific apps/widgets/shortcuts must retain their owning profile identity and should be visually distinguishable where confusion could cause the user to act under the wrong account or authority.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Launcher acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The latest appropriate Lawnchair donor is forked/adapted and mature donor launcher behaviour is retained unless explicitly replaced.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launcher is the Android/9to1-OS home launcher only; Shelf remains a separate quick-access product and Home/platform services own package management.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home pages, app drawer, dock, folders, widgets, gestures, shortcuts, hidden apps, backup/restore and accessibility are production-capable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Customisation materially exceeds the donor/default Android baseline and supports deep grid, icon, folder, dock, page, theme, animation and gesture configuration without destabilising canonical launcher state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche can safely manipulate launcher layout through typed semantic APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Application placement survives normal app updates because layout references canonical application identity rather than copied package/executable metadata.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Shelf

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shelf is the cross-platform quick-access library for things the user wants to launch or open frequently. It is a separate product from the Android Launcher. Shelf can organise applications, games, 9to1 surfaces, projects, files, folders, websites and other supported shortcuts into reusable user-defined collections.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Core model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shelf MUST model launch targets as stable typed LaunchItem entities rather than a grid of copied shortcuts. A LaunchItem can represent, where supported and permitted:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Installed desktop/native applications.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 applications and 9to1:// routes/deep links.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Games detected from supported game/application sources or added manually.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Android applications where the hosting platform supports them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Executable/application targets with supported arguments and working-directory configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files and folders.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web URLs and registered URI schemes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dev/Stack projects or other 9to1 canonical resources with a launch/open action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Explicit user-created shortcuts and other extension-defined launch targets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each LaunchItem can retain a stable ID, name, icon/artwork, target type, canonical target/reference, optional launch parameters, tags, collection membership, launch behaviour and supported contextual actions. Shelf MUST preserve the underlying target identity instead of duplicating the actual app/game/file.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Collections and organisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Collections are first-class many-to-many organisational entities, not filesystem-style one-parent folders. The same LaunchItem may appear in multiple collections without duplication. Examples include Offline Games, FNAF Games, 9to1 Apps, Development, Blender & Unreal, Coursework or any user-created grouping.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shelf MUST support manual collections, favourites/pins, ordering, tags and smart/dynamic collections where reliable typed criteria exist. Dynamic collections may automatically surface targets such as detected Unreal projects or installed games matching declared offline-capability metadata without converting those results into duplicate LaunchItems.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Collections should support configurable presentation such as list/grid/card density, artwork/icon treatment and ordering while keeping the same canonical contents underneath.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Discovery and target import

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shelf can discover supported locally installed applications, platform-recognised games, 9to1 applications and registered projects through typed providers. Discovery MUST be permission-aware and reversible; detected items do not have to be added to the user's curated Shelf unless the user chooses or a configured smart collection references them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can always add a supported target manually when automatic discovery is unavailable. Missing/uninstalled targets SHOULD remain recoverable as unavailable entries when preserving them is useful, rather than silently deleting the user's organisation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Search / AI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shelf uses the shared Search / AI interaction pattern. Search mode performs deterministic lookup across LaunchItems, collections, tags and supported metadata. AI mode uses Dulche to interpret natural-language library requests and operate Shelf's typed APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples include 'add all my FNAF games to a FNAF collection', 'find all Unreal projects and put them in Development', 'show games I can play offline', 'where is that game I installed last month?', or 'open everything I use for Refuelled'. Dulche MUST resolve real discovered/canonical targets and MUST NOT invent installed applications or projects.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Launching and actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening an item delegates to the owning platform/application service using the target's canonical semantics. 9to1-native targets use their registered 9to1:// identity/deep-link contracts where applicable. Files/folders use Files/platform open semantics; web targets use Browse/default-browser semantics; applications/games use the appropriate registered launcher/provider.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shelf may expose typed contextual actions such as Open, Open with, Reveal in Files, Open project, Launch with arguments, Pin, Add/remove collection, Edit metadata or provider-specific actions where the underlying target supports them. Consequential or command-like launch actions remain subject to normal 9to1 permission/risk policy.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Cross-device and missing-target behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shelf organisation is user state and should be serialisable/synchronisable where enabled. A synced collection may contain a target unavailable on another device. That device MUST represent the item as unavailable/not installed or resolve an appropriate equivalent only through explicit canonical mapping; it must not silently substitute an unrelated app.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Extensions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extensions may register LaunchItem providers, target types, discovery providers, metadata enrichers, actions and smart-collection predicates subject to permissions. Providing Shelf integration does not grant unrestricted filesystem enumeration, package inventory or private project access.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Shelf acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Shelf remains a distinct cross-platform quick-access product and is never conflated with the Lawnchair-derived Android Launcher.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Apps, games, 9to1 routes, projects, files, folders, URLs and supported shortcuts can be represented as typed stable LaunchItems.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Collections support many-to-many membership so an item can belong to multiple groups without duplication.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manual and supported smart collections, search, favourites, tags, custom ordering and unavailable-target recovery work consistently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche can organise, discover and launch real Shelf targets through typed APIs without hallucinating installed content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launching delegates to the target's authoritative owner/platform service and respects normal permission/security boundaries.

heading: TITLE
text: Frameworks

heading: HEADING_1
text: Dulche

heading: HEADING_2
text: Framework role

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche is 9-1’s shared llama.cpp-derived local model framework/runtime. One Home-managed Dulche instance serves every 9-1 app through a broker API; apps must never launch their own competing local model servers. It owns model loading, inference lifecycle, resource limits, cancellation and local capability discovery while preserving upstream provenance.

heading: HEADING_2
HEADING_2
text: Voice

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Voice is a Dulche capability. Dulche owns the audio-session runtime, speech/model lifecycle, streaming, interruption and integration with requests, tools, permissions and logs. The user-facing controls live in Vision & Voice rather than Home.
