heading: HEADING_2
HEADING_2
text: Translate

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Translate is a first-class Dulche framework capability for multilingual translation, localisation and cross-language interpretation. It is not owned by a standalone Translate app. The primary user-facing product is the built-in Translate Space, while Write, Mail, Boards, Browse, Vision & Voice, AI Overlay, Sites and other authorised surfaces may invoke Dulche Translate directly for contextual translation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Translate owns language/locale resolution, translation execution, multi-target Translation Sets, variant identity, glossary/protected-term application, segment alignment, structured-artifact translation contracts, translation job lifecycle, provenance and translation-specific recovery. It MUST use the shared model/provider layer and normal Home/Dulche permission and audit contracts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Translation Sets and variants

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A translation request MAY target one or many languages/locales in a single operation. The canonical result is a TranslationSet with stable TranslationSetID, source reference/revision where applicable, source language/locale, request/instruction metadata, glossary references, model policy, created/modified timestamps and one or more TranslationVariants.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every TranslationVariant MUST have stable TranslationVariantID, TranslationSetID, target language/locale, status, translated content or canonical output reference, revision, provenance, errors/warnings and segment map where available. Retrying, regenerating, manually editing, applying or publishing one language MUST NOT discard successful sibling variants.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Language identity MUST use canonical language/locale identifiers. When a user supplies an ambiguous or unsupported language label, Dulche Translate MUST request/return a structured resolution requirement rather than silently guessing another language.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Conversational Translate Space rendering

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The built-in Translate Space renders translation work as normal conversation rather than a two-box translator. The selected target-language chips sit immediately above the standard Space chatbar; all source/context selection uses the normal Spaces context architecture.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: When one conversational request returns multiple TranslationVariants, each language variant MUST appear as its own assistant speech bubble. The language/locale name is displayed directly above that bubble. The bubbles are linked as siblings by the same TranslationSetID/request but remain independently addressable for retry, regenerate, edit, apply, export or agentic follow-up.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A prompt may temporarily target a subset/additional language without necessarily changing the Space's persistent language chips. Explicit requests to add/remove/change the default language set update the Translate Space configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Conversational refinement and agentic actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Translate MUST support natural follow-up refinement such as 'make the German version less formal', 'keep Action Graph untranslated everywhere', 'add Japanese', 'only redo French', or 'update these because the source changed'. Refinements target the canonical TranslationSet/variant rather than creating unrelated copies unless the user requests a separate result.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Translate Space MAY perform multi-step agentic localisation workflows using normal Space Plugins, Skills, persistent Dulche Agents, Automations and typed app actions. For example, 'translate this page into French, Spanish, German and Italian, then push them to the live site' may resolve the current page semantically, create/update four TranslationVariants, validate each owning artifact/site route and invoke the authorised Sites/WordPress/publishing APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Translate MUST NOT implement generic hidden publishing or file mutation that bypasses owning apps. Applying translations to Write/Present/Data/Boards/Sites/WordPress/GitHub or other systems uses those systems' canonical typed actions, revision checks, permissions, approvals, audit and idempotency contracts. Partial downstream failure MUST preserve already-successful translations/actions and expose targeted retry.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Structured artifacts and semantic preservation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Translate MUST translate human-language content while preserving supported non-linguistic structure and identity. For 9to1-native artifacts it should operate through the owning app/shared Productivity Engine using stable object identities rather than flattening the artifact into plain text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write translation preserves document structure/styles/tables/images/links/comments and other supported metadata while translating intended text. Present translation preserves slides/layout/theme/text boxes/speaker notes/animations/transitions and detects translated-text overflow instead of silently clipping. Data translation distinguishes human labels/descriptions/comments from formulas, numbers, cell references and identifiers. Boards translation preserves page/block identity and supported embedded artifact references.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Code, commands, URLs, formulas, JSON keys, identifiers, markup/code fences and other structured technical content MUST follow explicit structure-aware rules and MUST NOT be casually translated as prose. The user may explicitly request translation of translatable string literals/comments where the owning format supports safe editing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Whole-artifact translation SHOULD create a translated derivative/locale variant by default rather than destructively overwrite the source. Explicit in-place commands such as Replace selection with translation use the owning app's normal undo/revision semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Segments, provenance and incremental updates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where the source supports stable segmentation, Dulche Translate SHOULD preserve segment identity/alignment between source and each target variant. Segment maps enable side-by-side review, targeted retry, terminology correction and incremental updates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Translated derivatives MUST retain provenance sufficient to identify source artifact/file/entity, source revision, source/target language, TranslationSetID/VariantID, glossary IDs, model policy and translation time. When the source changes, Translate MUST be able to report that a translation is stale.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where safe segment identity exists, updating a stale translation SHOULD retranslate only changed/affected source segments while preserving unaffected translated content and user edits. Conflicts between manual target edits and changed source content MUST be surfaced rather than silently overwritten.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Glossaries and protected terminology

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Translate MUST support reusable and request-scoped glossaries. Glossary entries MAY define source term, required/preferred target translation by locale, Do Not Translate, notes/context and applicability scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Protected terminology MUST support names, trademarks, product names, case names, technical identifiers, commands and other content that should remain unchanged. Glossary/protected-term application MUST be recorded in translation provenance so unexpected terminology can be diagnosed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Text, image, document and media translation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Translate MUST support direct text and semantic selection translation. Image/screenshot translation MAY return extracted translated text and, where the selected model/tooling supports it, a translated visual derivative with mapped text regions. Semantic text from a 9to1 surface is preferred over OCR/pixels when available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: PDF handling MUST distinguish text, scanned and mixed PDFs where detectable. Structured text PDFs should preserve layout/structure as far as supported; scanned/mixed PDFs may require vision/OCR-style extraction. Any layout fidelity loss or uncertain extraction MUST be surfaced before export/apply.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Audio translation may produce translated text and, where supported, translated speech. Video translation MAY produce translated transcript/subtitles and advanced dubbed output where supported. Live realtime interpretation is exposed through Vision & Voice → Live Translate while reusing Dulche Translate language/context/glossary functionality.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Model routing and privacy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Translate uses the shared Universal Model Picker/model-routing system. Ordinary translation requests SHOULD resolve the highest-quality compatible configured route for the requested languages, modality, context size, latency, privacy/locality, entitlement/cost and tool requirements without forcing the user to manually choose a model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: An explicit local-only/private policy MUST NOT silently fall back to cloud translation. Unknown language-pair/provider capability is represented as unavailable/unknown rather than fabricated support.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Translation jobs and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Long or multi-artifact translation MUST use durable TranslationJob state with stable TranslationJobID and statuses such as Preparing, Translating, ReviewAvailable, Applying/Exporting, Completed, Paused, Failed and Cancelled as applicable. Progress MUST derive from real segments/pages/slides/files/variants rather than invented percentages.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Partial failure MUST preserve successful completed segments/variants. A failed page/language/action can be retried independently. Pause/resume/retry MUST not repeat already-completed consequential downstream actions without idempotency/operation identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3

NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.RefineVariant(translationVariantID, instruction);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.RegenerateVariant(translationVariantID, options?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.TranslateArtifact(sourceRef, targetLanguages, options?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.TranslateImage(source, targetLanguages, options?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.TranslateAudio(source, targetLanguages, options?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.CreateJob(config);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.GetJob(translationJobID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.PauseJob(translationJobID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.ResumeJob(translationJobID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.CancelJob(translationJobID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.Retry(translationJobID, target?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.Glossary.List();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.Glossary.Get(glossaryID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.Glossary.Create(definition);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.Glossary.Update(glossaryID, patch, expectedRevision?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.GetSegmentMap(translationVariantID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Translate.CheckSourceRevision(translationSetID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: These are minimum canonical entry points. Applying/publishing translated outputs remains the responsibility of the owning app/Plugin APIs; Dulche Translate returns typed TranslationSet/Variant/artifact references and orchestration metadata rather than bypassing those owners.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Translate MUST return structured failures including LanguageUnsupported, LanguageAmbiguous, LocaleUnsupported, TranslationModelUnavailable, TranslationCapabilityUnavailable, GlossaryUnavailable, SourceUnavailable, SourceRevisionConflict, SegmentAlignmentUnavailable, VariantNotFound, TranslationSetNotFound, TranslationJobNotFound, TranslationJobNotResumable, StructuredFormatUnsupported, LayoutPreservationUnavailable, PartialTranslationFailure, PrivacyPolicyDenied and ProviderUnavailable in addition to normal Dulche/tool/action failures.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Translate is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: One request can translate into multiple target languages and returns independently addressable TranslationVariants under one TranslationSetID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Translate Space places language chips immediately above the normal chatbar and uses normal Space context rather than a separate context row.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each conversational target-language translation renders in its own assistant speech bubble with the language/locale name above it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Retry/regenerate/edit of one language does not discard successful sibling language variants.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A conversational request can perform authorised downstream actions such as applying/publishing translated variants only through owning typed APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A partial downstream publish/apply failure preserves successful languages and supports targeted retry.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write/Present/Data/Boards translations preserve supported structure and do not flatten artifacts into plain text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Formula/code/identifier content is protected from inappropriate prose translation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Glossaries and Do Not Translate terms apply consistently and remain attributable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Source revision changes are detected and segment-aware incremental update preserves unaffected/manual target content where safe.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Image/PDF/media translation reports extraction/layout limitations truthfully.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Local-only/privacy policy cannot silently route translation to cloud.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Long/multi-artifact jobs preserve successful progress across pause/failure/retry.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice Live Translate reuses this framework rather than implementing a separate translation engine.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Agents

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agents are a first-class Dulche-wide persistent capability layer, not a standalone 9to1 app. Dulche owns the canonical Agent registry, scope/availability resolution, invocation, runs, queues, delegation, capability resolution, lifecycle and recovery. Agent definitions, durable Agent configuration, memory namespaces and relevant persistent run metadata are stored in Den. 9to1 surfaces discover and expose applicable Agents through Dulche.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: AI Studio → Agent Builder is the direct structured authoring/editor surface for this Dulche layer. It creates/edits the canonical Den-backed Agent entity. AI Studio is not the runtime host, and closing AI Studio MUST NOT stop, hide or delete an Agent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Dulche Agents are distinct from Dulche Subagents. Agents have stable identity, durable configuration/memory/scope and may exist across many runs. Subagents are transient child-execution units created inside a run for delegation/parallelisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Canonical Agent identity and Den persistence

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Agent MUST have stable AgentID independent of name plus versioned DefinitionRevision. The Den-backed Agent entity MUST retain at least name, icon/avatar, description, instructions, availability bindings, default model policy, Plugins/Connectors, Skills, Knowledge/Files references, Quick Actions, memory policy, capability/permission policy, delegation policy, graph reference where present, sharing metadata, revision history and lifecycle state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Renaming, moving scope or changing icon MUST NOT create another Agent. Agent display names MAY collide; AgentID remains canonical. An Agent definition revision used by an active/historical run MUST remain attributable even after later edits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Den MUST separate Agent definition/configuration from secrets and device-specific executable state. Connector credentials remain secure references; local executable paths/caches do not become portable Agent secrets merely because the Agent syncs through Den.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Availability scopes and cascading

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MUST support Agent availability scopes including Global, Surface, Space and Project/Entity or equivalent narrower canonical scope bindings. An Agent MAY have multiple compatible bindings when explicitly configured.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Global Agents cascade automatically into every compatible 9to1 surface. Surface-scoped Agents are available only on their declared surfaces. Space-scoped and Project/Entity-scoped Agents appear when the current invocation context matches those scopes. Availability is composed rather than overridden: a narrower scoped Agent supplements applicable broader Agents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: For a context such as Write inside a Study Space/project, the effective visible set is the compatible union of Global Agents, Write-scoped Agents, current-Space Agents and current Project/Entity Agents, subject to access restrictions. Dulche MUST return origin/scope metadata so CUI can group Agents by Global, current surface and contextual scopes rather than present an unexplained flat list.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Global cascading references the same canonical AgentID everywhere; it MUST NOT create per-app copies. Agent definition updates, memory and run history remain attached to the canonical Agent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Availability versus permission

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent availability and Agent effective permission are separate concepts. A visible Agent may still have actions disabled in the current invocation context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Effective permissions/capabilities MUST be no broader than the intersection of the Agent definition/instance policy, current surface capabilities, current Space policy, current project/entity scope, caller/user/organisation policy and Home permission/trust state. A surface/Space cannot grant a capability explicitly denied by the Agent/security policy, and a Global Agent does not gain universal data access merely because it is visible everywhere.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Agent updates — static and reactive animated icons

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agents MUST support both static image icons and animated avatars. Users MUST be able to choose the presentation for each Agent. The animated-avatar concept is a pet/companion-style icon, using the user's Codex pets/Dots comparison as a design reference, rather than being limited to an unrelated looping image.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Animated avatars MUST react to the Agent's actual activity and relevant conversational events. Required examples include the avatar sitting at a computer and coding while the Agent is coding, and laughing in response to a user joke. Task-state transitions and conversational reactions MUST be configurable and previewable. Reactions are presentation events, not permission grants or claims about hidden reasoning. Animation MUST respect the existing reduced-motion controls and provide a static fallback without losing the Agent's accessible identity or readable activity status.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Agent presentation API and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical Dulche Agent API MUST cover static/animated avatar selection, referenced asset and definition management, animation-state transitions and event/reaction mappings. Use Den-backed stable identities and versioned configuration shared with AI Studio’s visual builder; presentation changes MUST NOT fork the Agent, alter its permissions or leak private content. Verify saved/reopened configuration, static and animated icons, coding activity, joke/laugh reactions, reduced-motion fallback and readable accessible status, including permission-denied and missing-asset recovery. Connect’s Agent-contact contract supplies email, call and text entry points to these same Agents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Surface integration and Agent picker

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every compatible interactive 9to1 surface SHOULD expose applicable Dulche Agents through the shared AI/Agent picker or a surface-appropriate invocation UI. Apps query Dulche for context-resolved Agents rather than maintaining private Agent registries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The invocation context MUST be typed and may include SurfaceID, SpaceID, Project/Entity references, ArtifactID, selected ObjectIDs, current semantic context and available typed actions. Dulche filters this context through permissions before supplying it to the Agent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Surfaces MAY recommend specialist scoped Agents more prominently than generic Global Agents. Recommendation/order MUST NOT change Agent identity or silently select an Agent with broader permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Scoped surface Agents

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: First-party apps MAY ship/register useful surface-scoped Dulche Agent definitions/bindings. Once registered, they are canonical Dulche Agents rather than hidden app-local assistants and can be inspected/edited where policy permits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MAY expose specialist writing Agents such as Editor, Proofreader, Long-form Writer or user-created writing Agents. A Write-scoped Agent can receive authorised semantic document/selection/style/comment/reference context and Write typed actions without becoming available on unrelated surfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Vision & Voice MAY expose a Podcast Agent or similar specialist Voice Agents. A Podcast Agent can accept typed inputs such as Topic, optional Sources, target Duration and Style, then use the Voice Monologue mode to research/plan/generate/play a coherent long-form podcast. It remains a canonical Dulche Agent scoped to Vision & Voice, not a hardcoded private voice feature.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Agent invocation interfaces

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: An Agent definition MAY declare a typed InvocationSchema and optional CUI/Generative UI invocation interface. Surfaces SHOULD render the declared inputs rather than force every Agent through a blank chat box.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Invocation UI definitions MUST bind only to declared Agent inputs and approved typed actions; they MUST NOT grant new permissions. Examples include a Voice Podcast form with Topic/Sources/Duration/Style or a Write rewrite form with Tone, Preserve citations and Scope.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Quick Actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quick Actions are named manual entry points into a canonical Agent and cascade wherever that Agent is available, subject to each Quick Action's context requirements/visibility rules. They are not separate Agents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every QuickAction MUST have stable QuickActionID, AgentID, label, optional icon/description, predefined instruction or named graph entry point, optional typed InputSchema, context requirements, confirmation policy and ordering metadata.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quick Actions may be context-sensitive. For example, Rewrite selection should appear only where an editable selection exists; a Podcast Agent may expose Make podcast, Continue latest podcast or Create briefing. Invoking one creates a normal canonical AgentRun with standard permissions, Action Graph, side-effect/idempotency controls and run history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quick Actions are distinct from Automations. Quick Actions are manually invoked entry points; Automations own recurring, scheduled, event-triggered and condition-triggered execution. An Automation MAY invoke an Agent/Quick Action through the same Dulche APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Default model resolution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: An Agent may define Default Model = Inherit or an explicit Universal Model Picker policy. Inherit resolves from the invocation Space/surface/global policy. An explicit Agent default takes precedence over inherited defaults where allowed, while request-specific overrides may take precedence only if Agent/security policy permits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MUST capability-check the effective model against the Agent/run requirements such as tools, vision, audio, context or structured output. It MUST not silently cross local/private to cloud boundaries or substitute an explicitly forbidden fallback.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Plugins, Connectors, Skills and Knowledge

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent capability bindings reference canonical Dulche Plugins/Connectors/MCP capabilities and Skills by stable identity/version policy. They are not copied into the Agent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Knowledge/Files references point to Den memory and authorised canonical files/folders/artifacts/providers where possible. The Agent may retrieve current source revisions through owning APIs rather than rely on stale copies. Missing/revoked/incompatible sources or packages MUST be represented explicitly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Agent memory

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each persistent Agent MUST have an Agent-specific Den memory namespace governed by its memory policy. Durable memory is structured semantic/operational state, not simply an unbounded copy of every conversation/tool result.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Memory writes MUST carry scope/provenance and MUST respect personal/team/shared boundaries. A shared Agent MUST NOT silently copy a participant's private personal Den context, private connected-account data or secrets into shared Agent memory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent memory SHOULD support inspection, conflict handling, deduplication, recency/provenance metadata and removal/disable operations. Secrets encountered in tools/results MUST NOT automatically become durable Agent memory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Tasks, work queues and runs

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A persistent Agent MAY maintain a durable work queue in Dulche. Queue items MUST have stable QueueItemID, AgentID, objective, optional TaskID, priority, creator/trigger provenance, dependencies, status and timestamps. Work may arrive from a user, Space/Task, Automation, another authorised Agent or recovery flow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Task is user-level work; an Agent is the persistent worker; AgentRun is a specific execution. The relationship MUST remain explicit: a Task/objective may be assigned to an Agent, which creates one or more AgentRuns. Agents are not themselves a second Task or Automation system.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each AgentRun MUST have stable AgentRunID, AgentID, DefinitionRevision, objective, trigger/source, optional TaskID/QueueItemID, status, start/end timestamps, effective model/capabilities/permissions, ActionGraphID, outputs, blockers, approvals, usage/budget metadata and recovery/checkpoint state where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Run states and controls

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canonical user-facing Agent/run states MUST distinguish at least Idle, Queued, Running, Waiting, Blocked, Paused, Awaiting Approval, Completed, Failed/Error and Disabled as appropriate. Blocked and Awaiting Approval MUST NOT be conflated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run controls MUST support Pause/Resume, safe Stop and explicit Cancel where the runtime permits them. Resume continues the same AgentRunID and MUST NOT repeat already-completed consequential actions. Retry of a failed step/run uses idempotency/operation identity to avoid replaying unrelated successful side effects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Progress UI MUST show truthful objective/current step/known plan progress. It MUST NOT invent a percentage where the Agent cannot estimate completion meaningfully.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Blockers and approvals

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Agent runs MUST create first-class Blocker records for conditions preventing progress, including category, description, time, whether the Agent can self-resolve, required human action and related entities. Agents SHOULD attempt safe recovery of foreseeable recoverable blockers when their contract allows it instead of immediately escalating every failure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Human-required blockers and pending consequential actions MUST surface through relevant invoking surfaces and Home Events/Notifications/approval UX. Approval remains a Home permission/action decision; Dulche Agents cannot self-authorise through their own instructions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Agent-to-Agent delegation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Agent-to-Agent delegation is a Dulche Agent capability. Delegation MUST retain explicit parent/child AgentRun identities and a typed handoff containing objective, required context references, narrowed capability scope and expected output.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: DelegationPolicy MUST be able to constrain allowed persistent Agents/classes, whether Subagents are allowed, maximum concurrency, maximum depth and applicable token/time/cost/tool budgets. A receiving Agent does not automatically inherit all permissions or memory of its parent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Agent delegation remains distinct from Dulche Subagents. Subagents are lighter transient child execution primitives inside the runtime; persistent delegated Agents retain their own canonical AgentID, definition and Den memory policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Action Graph, outputs and operational visibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every AgentRun MUST use the canonical Dulche Action Graph/log/audit pipeline. 9to1 surfaces may render a concise human-readable Activity view and/or the full Action Graph, but they MUST NOT invent a second execution history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run outputs MUST be typed references to their canonical owning entities where possible, including Files, documents, Boards, code changes, Planner/Task items, messages, research outputs and other artifacts. Opening an output routes to its owning app/entity rather than copying it into an Agent-only store.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent runs, blockers, approvals and outputs may be surfaced contextually in Spaces, Agent Builder Preview, Automations that triggered them, Home Events/Notifications and the invoking app. No standalone Agents app is required or authoritative.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Lifecycle, recovery and budgets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Long-running/background-capable AgentRuns MUST checkpoint enough state to recover or truthfully fail across app closure, Home/Dulche restart, machine restart where supported, provider disconnect or temporary tool failure. Recovery states SHOULD distinguish Reconnecting, Recovering, Recovered and Cannot recover rather than silently restarting from scratch.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agents MUST support configured runtime/model/tool/delegation budgets such as maximum runtime, spend/tokens, tool calls, concurrent children or delegation depth where the platform can enforce them. Exceeding a budget produces an explicit blocked/failed/approval state rather than uncontrolled continuation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: These are minimum canonical entry points. All Agent Builder and 9to1 surface Agent operations MUST resolve through the same Dulche/Den contracts rather than creating app-private Agent stores or runtimes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Failure behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Agents MUST return structured failures including AgentNotFound, DefinitionRevisionUnavailable, AgentDisabled, AgentUnavailableInScope, AgentBusy, AgentRunNotFound, RunNotResumable, RunRecoveryFailed, QueueItemNotFound, CapabilityUnavailable, PermissionDenied, ApprovalRequired, BlockerUnresolved, DelegationDenied, DelegationDepthExceeded, ConcurrencyLimitExceeded, BudgetExceeded, ModelUnavailable, ToolUnavailable, MemoryScopeDenied, QuickActionUnavailable, InvalidInvocationContext and RevisionConflict in addition to the global Dulche error contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Agents is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An Agent created in AI Studio Agent Builder is stored as a canonical Den-backed Dulche Agent and remains usable after AI Studio closes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: There is no authoritative standalone Agents app or duplicate Agent database.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Global Agents appear on every compatible 9to1 surface through Dulche scope resolution without being copied.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Surface-, Space- and Project/Entity-scoped Agents appear only in matching contexts while applicable broader Agents remain available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent availability does not grant permissions; effective capability resolution narrows correctly across Agent, surface, Space, caller and Home policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write can expose/use specialist writing Agents with semantic document context, and Vision & Voice can expose/use a Podcast Agent that drives Monologue mode from typed inputs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quick Actions cascade with their Agent, obey context visibility/input schemas and create normal AgentRuns rather than duplicate Agents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Default Model inheritance/explicit override resolves through the Universal Model Picker without violating privacy/fallback restrictions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent memory persists in the correct Den namespace without silently ingesting private/shared-incompatible context or secrets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Task → Agent → AgentRun and Automation → AgentRun relationships remain explicit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent queues preserve provenance, priorities/dependencies and durable state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Blocked and Awaiting Approval states remain distinct and recoverable blockers can be handled autonomously where authorised.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pause/Stop/Resume/Retry do not replay completed consequential actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Agent delegation obeys depth/concurrency/budget limits and does not transfer unrestricted parent permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Agents and Dulche Subagents remain distinct in API, logs and UI.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AgentRun Action Graph is the canonical execution graph and outputs open canonical owning entities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home/Dulche restart can recover supported durable runs or reports Cannot recover truthfully without silently restarting work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent Builder Preview uses the same Dulche semantics while clearly remaining test-scoped.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agent Builder/other surfaces perform Agent operations through the canonical Dulche Agent API.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Action Graph

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Action Graph is a Dulche feature and the user-facing structured view of an AI/agent execution log. It turns the underlying request history into an inspectable graph rather than requiring users to read a raw continuous log.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The graph can show prompts, model calls, thinking/response phases where available, tool calls, AI actions, approvals, dependencies, retries, generated artifacts, failures, hard errors, blockers and timestamps. It is derived from Dulche’s audit/tool/full-log data so the graph and logs describe the same execution rather than separate histories.

heading: HEADING_3
HEADING_3
text: Action Graph API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.ActionGraph(requestID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Returns the structured Action Graph for a request, including the data needed for CUI/Markdown rendering.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.ActionGraph.GetNode(requestID, nodeID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.ActionGraph.ListEvents(requestID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.ActionGraph.RestartFrom(requestID, nodeID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: RestartFrom forks/restarts the prompt or agent run from the selected point while preserving the original history. Earlier completed actions remain auditable; actions after the restart point are re-executed as a new branch and remain subject to current permissions/approval requirements.

heading: HEADING_3
HEADING_3
text: Shared rendering

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche produces the Action Graph data and the CUI/Markdown representation needed to render it. The shared renderer source lives in Home and is reusable across the ecosystem, so apps do not need separate implementations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any app may surface the renderer where useful. For example, Spaces may expose a Show Action Graph button for a response, while Home can expose the same graph from logs or activity history.

heading: HEADING_2
HEADING_2
text: Runtime

heading: HEADING_3
text: Purpose

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Runtime provides a simple, consistent API for starting, configuring and controlling model endpoints without requiring each app or harness to manually manage model-server lifecycle.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Endpoint lifecycle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Start(port);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Starts a local Dulche endpoint on the specified port. Local Start requires an explicit port; Start(Remote(...)) instead requires an explicit remote target.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Test(port);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Checks whether Dulche is reachable on the specified port.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Prompt(port);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sends a prompt/instruction to the specified endpoint.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.SetModel(model, port);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sets the model used by the specified endpoint.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.SetTemperature(temperature, port);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sets the temperature used by the specified endpoint.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Pause(port);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Suspends model activity while keeping the model and its context loaded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Stop(port);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stops the model and clears the endpoint/port.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.SetReasoningLevel(level, port);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sets the endpoint's reasoning level. level may be a named effort such as low or medium, or a percentage. Percentages are mapped across the reasoning levels exposed by that model. For example, if a model exposes five reasoning levels, the 0-100 range is divided across those five levels and the matching level is selected.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Multi-endpoint scope

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For endpoint-wide commands other than Start, an omitted/null port targets the active endpoints authorised in the caller's scope. RequestID-based controls are never broadcasts. Return per-endpoint outcomes, retaining partial failures and isolated sessions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Test();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Returns the list of ports currently used by Dulche.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Prompt();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sends the prompt/instruction to all active endpoints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Stop();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stops all Dulche endpoints.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Endpoint configuration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Endpoints can be created and configured as one unit. Example:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Endpoint Laguna = new Endpoint(port) {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model = GetModelByID(laguna-xs);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context = 19000;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Timeout = 300;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ToolCallsAllowed = All;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: // Other supported model/endpoint properties may also be configured here.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Timeout is disabled by default. When set, an endpoint that remains inactive for the specified number of seconds is automatically paused rather than stopped, preserving the loaded model and context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Capabilities

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche natively provides the persistent Agent layer, Subagents/parallelisation, command usage, code execution, local and cloud models, tool calling, MCPs, Plugins, Skills and Generative UI. MCPs, Plugins and Skills are first-class extension types with stable identity, lifecycle, permissions, validation and dedicated APIs; they MUST NOT exist only as ad-hoc wrappers around generic tool calls. Persistent Agents are Den-backed durable Dulche entities, while Subagents are Runtime child-execution primitives. Capabilities can be disabled within scope when they are not permitted or required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.SetCapability(UI, false);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Tool registry, semantic capability discovery and feasibility resolution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MUST expose a canonical request-aware Tool Registry describing the tools, executable capabilities and usable resources that a model can employ to satisfy a request. The registry is broader than a literal list of function names: it includes first-party 9to1 app actions/APIs, Automations actions, Plugins, MCP tools, callable Agents, Skills that contribute executable workflows through authorised dependencies, Files/resource retrieval, image/audio/video generation capabilities, code/shell tools, web/network tools where permitted and other registered Dulche capabilities. Computer Use is represented only when it has been explicitly invoked under the Computer Use contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every registry entry MUST use stable identity and structured metadata. At minimum it exposes ToolID/CapabilityID, source type and owner, version/revision, human-readable name, action IDs, semantic capability/intent tags, supported input/output types, parameter schemas, prerequisites, permission scopes, side-effect/risk classification, platform/scope constraints, availability/health and whether user approval or additional configuration is currently required. Display name and wording of an action MUST NOT be the sole mechanism used to decide what a tool can do.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MUST derive an EffectiveCapabilitySet for each request from the canonical registry. The effective set is filtered by the active user/profile, current app/Space/project, installed/enabled package state, app/API availability, explicit @ invocations, platform capability, privacy policy, administrator policy, current permissions/trust and any request-specific restrictions. Installed-but-unavailable, available-but-unapproved and immediately executable capabilities MUST remain distinguishable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The active model/orchestrator MUST be given an inspectable, context-budget-aware representation of the EffectiveCapabilitySet. Dulche MAY provide a compact high-level catalogue initially and expose query/search APIs for deeper inspection so very large tool inventories do not consume the model's entire context. Capability discovery MUST nevertheless remain available throughout the request and MUST refresh when packages, permissions, target apps or connection state materially change.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tool selection MUST be intent-based rather than exact-name-based. Dulche MUST translate the user's requested outcome into one or more semantic intents and compare those intents against tool capability metadata, schemas and declared examples/aliases. A tool does not need an action whose literal name matches the user's wording when its underlying capability can satisfy the requested effect.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For example, a request such as 'remind me tomorrow at 4 PM' MUST be resolvable to a time-triggered Automations operation even if no action is literally named CreateReminder. The semantic requirement is a durable time-based trigger that produces the requested notification/action. Likewise, 'create an image of ...' MUST resolve to an eligible image-generation capability such as the first-party image app/tool or an installed authorised image-generation Plugin, even if the tool's action is named Generate, Render, Imagine or another equivalent verb.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Capability resolution MUST support composition. If no single tool can fulfil the complete request but a sequence of authorised capabilities can, Dulche MUST be able to construct a typed ResolutionPlan whose steps pass structured outputs/references between tools. For example, a request to 'create an image and put it on the title slide' may resolve to image generation followed by Present insertion; a request to 'find the file and email it' may resolve to Files search followed by a Mail/Plugin send action, subject to normal permissions and approvals.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ResolutionPlan steps MUST identify the selected ToolID/CapabilityID, action, required arguments, expected outputs, dependencies, permission/approval state and why the step satisfies part of the user's intent. Capability resolution is planning, not execution: selecting a feasible tool MUST NOT bypass its normal permission, approval, confirmation, privacy, cost or side-effect rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before a model states or implies that 9to1 cannot perform a requested digital action, it MUST first perform capability feasibility resolution against the current EffectiveCapabilitySet unless the impossibility is already established by a current authoritative hard constraint. The model MUST NOT answer 'I cannot directly create images', 'I cannot create reminders', 'I cannot access files' or equivalent merely because the base model itself lacks that native capability when Dulche exposes an authorised tool path that can perform it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A capability that exists but is missing a prerequisite MUST be described as blocked/configuration-required rather than impossible. Examples include ApprovalRequired, PermissionDenied, AccountConnectionRequired, MissingRequiredInput, AppUnavailable, ProviderUnavailable, CapabilityDisabledByPolicy and UnsupportedOnCurrentPlatform. When the missing prerequisite can be resolved within the current request and permission bounds, Dulche SHOULD resolve it or ask only for the specific user decision/input required and then continue.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If several feasible tools can perform the same intent, Dulche MUST select according to explicit user invocation/instruction first, then applicable app ownership/canonical-data rules, privacy/locality policy, capability fitness, permissions, reliability and configured user preferences. Cost/latency MAY participate where policy allows. Dulche MUST NOT choose an unrelated or lower-fidelity tool merely because its action name more closely resembles the user's wording.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Explicit @ invocation remains authoritative. An @Plugin, @App, @Agent, @Skill or other invocation narrows or prioritises the capability source according to that invocation's contract. However, ordinary natural-language requests do NOT require the user to know or name the underlying tool. 'Create a presentation', 'set a reminder', 'generate an image' and similar outcome requests MUST be sufficient for Dulche to discover and use the appropriate capability when one is available.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Skills, Agents and Files participate according to their real semantics rather than being falsely treated as identical callable functions. A Skill may contribute instructions/workflow/tool dependencies; an Agent may be invoked as a delegated execution capability; a File/resource may provide required input/context; an App/Plugin/MCP/native action may perform the mutation. The resolver MUST be able to combine these heterogeneous entries into one plan while preserving their distinct identities, permissions and audit records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MUST expose canonical discovery operations equivalent to Dulche.Tool.List(context?), Dulche.Tool.Search(intent, context?), Dulche.Tool.Get(toolID), Dulche.Tool.Resolve(intent, context?) and Dulche.Tool.ExplainResolution(resolutionID). Resolve MUST return either one or more ranked feasible ResolutionPlans or a structured no-feasible-path result containing the evaluated hard constraints and missing prerequisites. Search/Resolve MUST use semantic capability metadata in addition to lexical names.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Runtime MUST cache capability metadata efficiently but MUST version/invalidate the cache when relevant package versions, app capabilities, connection state, permissions, policy or provider health change. A model MUST NOT continue relying on a stale 'tool unavailable' conclusion after the capability registry has materially changed during the request.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A tool-result or retrieved document MUST NOT be able to self-register new authority merely by claiming that another tool exists or should be allowed. Registry membership and permissions come from trusted Dulche/Home registration, package manifests, app capability contracts and current policy. Semantic discovery MUST therefore improve capability use without creating a prompt-injection route to invented tools or escalated permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Failure to resolve a tool path MUST be truthful and inspectable. Dulche MUST distinguish NoMatchingCapability from MatchingCapabilityUnavailable, MissingPrerequisite, PermissionBlocked and PolicyBlocked. When no feasible path exists, the model MAY explain the limitation, but it MUST NOT fabricate a tool or claim to have performed the action. The Resolution attempt and selected/no-selected candidates MUST be visible in FullLog/Action Graph at an appropriate level of detail.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Acceptance coverage MUST verify at minimum that: a reminder request resolves to an Automations time-based workflow without requiring the phrase 'automation'; an image-generation request invokes an eligible image capability rather than returning a false inability statement; a presentation request can resolve to Present from another app; a multi-tool request produces a dependency-ordered ResolutionPlan; explicit @ invocation overrides automatic source choice; permission/configuration blockers are distinguished from true impossibility; Computer Use does not appear unless explicitly invoked; and removal/disablement of the only matching capability causes a structured no-feasible-path result rather than a fabricated success.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Subagents and parallelisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminology and boundary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subagent is the Dulche Runtime term for a child execution unit created by a request or another Subagent to delegate work and/or execute independent work in parallel. Subagents are execution primitives, not persistent Dulche Agents and not Den-backed Agent definitions. The public API MUST use the names Subagent and Dulche.Subagent for this capability so callers cannot confuse subagent parallelisation with persistent Agents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Subagent MAY execute one or more model/tool steps and MAY create nested Subagents within inherited limits. Every Subagent belongs to exactly one RootRequestID and, except for root execution, exactly one parent request or parent Subagent. Detached/orphan Subagents are outside the current contract; child work MUST remain causally attached to its parent tree.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subagent definition

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subagent Worker = new Subagent {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ParentRequestID = requestID;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prompt = "Perform the delegated work";

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model = Auto;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Endpoint = Auto;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context = SubagentContext.Inherit;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tools = Inherit;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permissions = Inherit;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: FailurePolicy = SubagentFailurePolicy.Collect;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Budget = new SubagentBudget {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MaxTokens = ...;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MaxTime = ...;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MaxSteps = ...;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MaxToolCalls = ...;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MaxCost = ...;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Limits = new SubagentLimits {

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MaxChildren = ...;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MaxParallelChildren = ...;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MaxDepth = ...;

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Constructing a Subagent object MUST NOT execute work. Construction only defines an inspectable configuration object. Execution begins only when submitted through Dulche.Subagent, preventing object construction from causing hidden model/tool/external side effects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canonical API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: SubagentHandle Handle = Dulche.Subagent.Start(Worker);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: SubagentHandle[] Handles = Dulche.Subagent.StartParallel([WorkerA, WorkerB, WorkerC]);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.Get(subagentID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.GetTree(rootRequestID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.ListChildren(parentID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.Wait(subagentID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.WaitAll(subagentIDs);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.WaitAny(subagentIDs);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.Pause(subagentID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.Resume(subagentID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.Stop(subagentID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.Restart(subagentID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.Checkpoint(rootRequestID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Subagent.Restore(checkpointID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Start creates one child and returns its handle after identity/state allocation. StartParallel submits the supplied definitions as sibling children under the same parent and returns one handle per child in input order. StartParallel grants permission for concurrent scheduling; it does not guarantee simultaneous execution when endpoint, provider or resource limits require queueing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wait returns that child’s terminal Result. WaitAll returns one terminal outcome per requested child and MUST preserve child identity even when one or more children fail. WaitAny returns when the first requested child reaches a terminal state and identifies that child. Join operations MUST NOT flatten or discard per-child errors, blockers, logs, token usage, model provenance or tool records.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Identity and state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Subagent MUST expose SubagentID, ParentSubagentID?, ParentRequestID, RootRequestID, SessionID, EndpointID, Depth, State, CreatedAt, StartedAt?, FinishedAt?, Model and its effective tool/permission/budget configuration. IDs MUST be stable for the lifetime/history of that execution and MUST NOT be derived from display names, array position or queue position.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subagent State MUST distinguish at least Created, Queued, Running, Waiting, Pausing, Paused, Completed, Failed, Blocked, Cancelled and TimedOut. Waiting means the Subagent is suspended awaiting dependencies/children and MUST NOT retain an execution slot that prevents those dependencies from running.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Scheduling and parallel execution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordinary requests on one endpoint remain serial by default as defined by the Runtime queue contract. Subagents do not silently change that rule. A parent waiting on a child that requires the same endpoint MUST yield its execution slot so the child can run; this is mandatory anti-deadlock behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sibling Subagents assigned to different eligible endpoints MAY execute concurrently subject to resource, provider and configured concurrency limits. Siblings assigned to the same endpoint execute serially unless that endpoint explicitly advertises concurrent execution and the request enables the supported parallel mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model = Auto and Endpoint = Auto permit the Runtime scheduler to select an eligible model/endpoint using declared capabilities, permission/privacy constraints and resource policy. An explicitly selected Model or Endpoint MUST NOT be silently replaced merely to increase parallelism; inability to satisfy the explicit selection returns a structured scheduling/capability failure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: MaxParallelChildren is a hard upper bound on concurrently Running children beneath the configured parent scope. Children above that limit remain Queued. Runtime-wide endpoint/resource limits MAY further reduce actual concurrency but MUST NOT increase it above the declared limit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context inheritance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context inheritance is explicit. Supported policies are None, Inherit and Selected(...). Inherit snapshots the authorised parent context at spawn time; it does not create unsynchronised mutable shared conversation state. Selected(...) copies only the declared messages/context objects/references. None starts without parent conversational context except identity/control metadata required by Runtime.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A child Result becomes visible to the parent through an explicit join/result path or another explicitly authorised shared data object. Child completion MUST NOT silently rewrite earlier parent messages or a sibling’s context. Multiple children MUST NOT concurrently mutate the same session history without an explicit revision/conflict mechanism.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permission and tool inheritance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Subagent MUST NOT acquire more authority than its parent/caller. Effective child authority is the intersection of the caller’s current authority, the parent’s effective authority and the scopes requested for the child. The same narrowing rule applies to tools, filesystem/data scopes, external integrations, network access, credentials and action approvals.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permissions = Inherit and Tools = Inherit copy only currently effective parent scopes. Expired/revoked grants are not inherited and no new approval is created by spawning a child. An action that requires approval in the parent context still requires approval when attempted by a child. Subagent creation MUST NOT provide privilege escalation or approval bypass.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hierarchical budgets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subagent budgets are hierarchical. Descendant consumption contributes to the ancestor/root aggregate for tokens, time, steps, tool calls and cost. A child MAY request stricter limits than its parent; it MUST NOT enlarge any hard parent/root limit. Parent and root budget exhaustion prevents further descendant work from starting and stops or blocks active descendants at safe boundaries according to the relevant resource type.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: SubagentBudget MUST support MaxTokens, MaxTime, MaxSteps, MaxToolCalls and MaxCost where those quantities are enforceable. Runtime resource policy MAY additionally constrain CPU, GPU, RAM, VRAM and endpoint occupancy. Provider-unavailable cost/token telemetry MUST use the Runtime’s existing null/Na rules and MUST NOT be treated as zero consumption.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Actual descendant consumption MUST be attributed to both the child and its ancestor aggregates without double-counting the same invocation. If the system reserves budget before dispatch, reservation and settlement MUST be visible separately from actual settled usage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Depth, child and concurrency limits

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: SubagentLimits MUST support MaxChildren, MaxParallelChildren and MaxDepth. MaxChildren counts direct children created by the configured execution scope. MaxDepth is measured from the root request, whose depth is 0; its direct Subagents are depth 1. Creating a child that would exceed a hard limit MUST fail before child execution begins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Runtime MUST also enforce implementation-wide safety ceilings even when the caller requests larger values. The effective limit is the minimum of caller/request limits, inherited parent limits and Runtime/provider limits. Limit failures return stable structured codes including MaxChildrenExceeded, MaxDepthExceeded and ConcurrencyLimitExceeded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Failure aggregation and join policy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Parallel sibling execution MUST retain independent terminal outcomes. One child failure MUST NOT erase successful sibling results. The parent/join operation receives a structured collection containing, for every child, SubagentID, terminal State, Result?, Errors?, Blockers?, FinishReason and relevant usage/telemetry.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: SubagentFailurePolicy MUST support at least Collect, FailFast, RequireAll and BestEffort. Collect waits for requested children and returns every outcome. FailFast requests cancellation of still-unfinished siblings after the first terminal failure/blocker while retaining already completed results. RequireAll treats any non-successful required child as a failed join. BestEffort permits the parent to continue with successful children while preserving explicit failed/blocked/cancelled outcomes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Failure policy changes orchestration/join behaviour only; it MUST NOT suppress logs, errors, blockers or completed side effects. External actions already completed by a failed/cancelled child are not automatically rolled back unless the action itself defines rollback semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cancellation, pause and restart propagation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stopping a root request MUST stop all unfinished dependent descendants. Stopping a Subagent MUST stop its unfinished descendants but MUST NOT automatically stop its parent or independent siblings; the parent receives the child’s Cancelled outcome and applies its configured failure policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pausing a parent MUST prevent it from dispatching new child work. Running dependent children follow the parent’s explicit pause policy: PauseChildren requests safe-boundary pause, LetChildrenFinish permits already-running children to complete, and StopChildren cancels them. If no policy is supplied, PauseChildren is the default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Restart creates a new attempt for the targeted Subagent using the specified/current authorised context and preserves the prior attempt in history. Restart MUST NOT replay already completed consequential tool/external actions automatically. Replacement/cancellation of an ancestor MUST invalidate stale descendant approvals and provisional output.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistence and recovery of subagent trees

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Den MUST persist the execution-tree metadata required to inspect and recover Subagent work: stable identities, parent/child relationships, request/attempt revisions, effective configuration, states, checkpoints, results, blockers/errors, tool/action records and durable side-effect evidence. Runtime remains the execution authority; Den is the durable record.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Checkpoint(rootRequestID) creates a durable tree checkpoint for all checkpointable active descendants. Restore(checkpointID) reconstructs the tree from the latest compatible durable state. Exact continuation is allowed only when the underlying model/backend/tool supports it; otherwise Restore MUST expose that it is a continuation/restart from checkpoint rather than claiming byte-for-byte execution resumption.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: On crash/restart, completed external/tool side effects MUST be reconciled from durable records before any step is retried. A restored tree MUST NOT repeat a non-idempotent completed action merely because the parent process lost volatile state. Uncertain side-effect state becomes a Blocker requiring reconciliation or approval.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Action Graph and telemetry

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Action Graph MUST render Subagent execution as an explicit causal tree/graph. Each Subagent is a distinct node/branch linked to its parent and MAY contain model calls, tool calls, approvals, outputs, child Subagents, blockers and errors. Parallel siblings MUST be visually distinguishable as concurrent branches rather than flattened into a fabricated sequential order.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subagent graph nodes MUST expose at least SubagentID, state, parent/root identity, model/endpoint, start/end/duration, token/usage data, tools/actions, errors/blockers and child count subject to permissions/redaction. Restart-from-here on a Subagent node creates a new attempt/branch under the existing historical tree and MUST NOT rewrite the original branch.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Runtime FullLog MUST retain causal parent IDs and per-execution sequence numbers. Parallel/nested timing MAY overlap; aggregate timing MUST NOT sum overlapping spans as if they were serial. Token/model/tool aggregation MUST use the existing no-double-counting rules for parent and child invocations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured failures

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subagent operations add stable structured failures including SubagentNotFound, MaxChildrenExceeded, MaxDepthExceeded, ConcurrencyLimitExceeded, BudgetExceeded, DependencyFailed, CheckpointUnavailable and RestoreConflict. These follow the Runtime error contract and MUST NOT rely on free-form string parsing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subagent support is implementation-complete only when automated/representative acceptance coverage verifies all of the following:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: One parent spawning and joining one child with preserved parent/child identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: StartParallel with multiple siblings on different endpoints demonstrating actual concurrent execution where resources permit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Same-endpoint child dependency without deadlock and without silently enabling unsupported backend parallelism.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context None/Inherit/Selected isolation, including no sibling context leakage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Permission/tool inheritance cannot exceed parent/caller authority and still triggers required approval.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Nested descendants obey MaxDepth, MaxChildren and MaxParallelChildren exactly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hierarchical token/time/step/tool/cost budgets stop or block descendants at the correct boundary without double-counting usage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Collect, FailFast, RequireAll and BestEffort preserve the documented per-child outcomes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Root/child stop and parent pause propagation follow the documented dependency semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Checkpoint + process restart + Restore reconstructs the tree without replaying a completed non-idempotent side effect.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Action Graph renders parent/child/nested/parallel branches with stable IDs and correct causal relationships.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Telemetry preserves overlapping parallel spans and model/token/tool attribution without parent/child double counting.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Subagent API failures return the documented structured error codes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Model resolution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche supports three model-resolution paths:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Den

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The user's Den may store models using both a stable ID and a user-facing name. Either can be used for lookup. User-facing names are not required to be unique.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Den.GetModelByID(id);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Returns the model matching the supplied ID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Den.ListModelsByName(name);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Returns all Den models matching the supplied user-facing name, including their IDs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Models.toml

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Models.toml contains the models available to the current Dulche configuration and the capabilities/properties associated with them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.GetModelByID(id);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Returns the configured model matching the supplied ID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.ListModelsByConfig(property);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Returns all configured models matching the supplied property. A property may describe a capability, such as reasoning support, or an identifying property such as an ID.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Local directory

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche can resolve a model directly from a local directory, with support for as many compatible model file types as practical.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.GetModelFromDir(directory);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where an operation fails because the requested model cannot be resolved, Dulche returns "model not found" rather than throwing an exception.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Model discovery and acquisition

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche can discover and obtain models from supported sources including llama.cpp, Ollama and Hugging Face.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.FindModel(source, id);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Checks whether the requested model exists at the specified source.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.ListModels(source, property);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Lists models from the specified source that match the supplied property.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Pull(source, model);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pulls a model temporarily. A pulled model survives endpoint suspension, but is discarded when the endpoint is stopped.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Install(source, model);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Installs a model persistently.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Model replacement

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Replace(oldModel, newModel);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replaces one model with another. When no replacement policy is specified, Dulche applies the safe replacement policy: preserve only metadata explicitly classified as model-independent (for example a user-facing alias), recalculate model-derived capabilities/limits from the replacement artifact, and reset configuration values that are invalid or unsupported by the replacement. Immutable artifact/model identity MUST NOT be copied from the old model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Replace(oldModel, newModel, preserveConfig);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preserves compatible properties from the old model where possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Replace(oldModel, newModel, wipe);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replaces the model without preserving its previous configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: safe MAY be specified explicitly as the preservation policy. Under safe, only fields classified by the replacement schema as model-independent/safe-to-carry MAY be preserved; all model-derived or compatibility-sensitive fields MUST be recalculated or reset.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: API authority and compatibility

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Documented API names, argument order, Result field names and explicit behaviours are binding and must be implemented verbatim. This is not an exhaustive API list: compatible overloads and missing APIs may be added. Resolve unspecified edge cases using the same simple, predictable, inspectable and permission-aware philosophy; do not silently rename or reverse an existing operation. The requirements below extend and clarify the earlier examples.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Requests, sessions and endpoints

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Retain port-based calls and add Dulche.Prompt(prompt, port) and Dulche.Prompt(request, endpoint). Request contains input/messages, SessionID, model selection, generation settings, permitted tools, output schema, streaming preference and limits. Input supports text, images, audio and authorised file/document references through capable adapters; other modalities are capability-gated. No private context/file is sent remotely without the required permission.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Prompt(port) and Dulche.Prompt() remain shorthand for an explicitly prepared request in the caller's scope. Add Dulche.PreparePrompt(prompt) to prepare caller-local input for those shorthand calls; consume a snapshot at submission and never reuse another caller's input. Without prepared input, return MissingPrompt. Explicit prompt/request overloads avoid hidden state and are preferred in concurrent code.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Assign RequestID immediately, before queueing. SessionID owns conversation/context; EndpointID identifies the logical execution target; port/URL identifies transport. Shared endpoints do not imply shared sessions. Add Dulche.CreateSession(endpoint) and session lookup/reset/close plus scoped context export/restore. Context is the token-window budget, not conversation identity. Overflow returns ContextExceeded unless the caller explicitly permits documented truncation/summarisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Endpoint Laguna = Dulche.Start(Remote("https://wherever.com"));

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The remote overload connects to an authorised remote target. It does not assume permission to manage the host's entire service. Targets declare provider, base URL, model identity, credential reference, transport/security settings and capabilities. Local Start requires a port; remote Start requires an explicit remote target. Return an endpoint handle with identity, state and structured failure information, never a false Ready state. Cloud targets do not require invented local ports.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Result contract and metric availability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Return Result using the exact field names below. The question mark denotes optional content, not part of the field name. Empty metrics return null. Provider-unavailable metrics return Na, serialised as the exact JSON string "Na" and exposed by typed bindings as an unavailable sentinel. A measured zero remains 0. This applies to all metrics, including those not originally marked optional and nested model metrics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Use value/null/Na-capable types and separate availability/provenance metadata for pending, disabled/redacted, measured, estimated and provider-unavailable values. Never substitute zero or an invented value for unavailable data. Required identity/status and the Runtime event-log container remain present. Collections with no applicable entries may be null; numeric counts may be a measured zero. A complete aggregate cannot silently ignore unavailable contributions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Response content and identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Text: the actual user-facing response, separate from tool arguments and undisclosed provider internals. No text may have been produced for a blocked, cancelled or non-text-only response.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Thinking: the thinking log actually exposed and permitted by the model/provider. Label traces and summaries distinctly; never present a summary as the complete internal thinking or reconstruct undisclosed reasoning. Empty content is null; provider-unavailable thinking is Na.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tools?: identities of the distinct tools actually used, with links to invocations. Tools offered but not called are not counted as used.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sources?: sources retrieved, supplied or cited, with provenance and relevant response-span references. Distinguish retrieved evidence from unverified model-generated citations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: GeneratedUI?: structured, versioned UI data, separate from Text and rendered only through an explicit CUI integration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Models: models actually used, including agent/subtask models, in first-use order and deduplicated by artifact/provider revision. Preserve roles, call counts, endpoints and invocation records. Models[i].Parameters exposes the individual parameter metric.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Also return RequestID, SessionID, Endpoint, Status, FinishReason, request revision and attempt identity. FinishReason distinguishes Completed, Cancelled, Replaced, Blocked, Error, OutputLimit and Refused. Paused is a non-terminal state, not successful completion. Preserve the original provider finish reason separately.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
