text: Earlier shorthand fields are compatibility views: Reasoning maps to Thinking; Model identifies the primary responding model; TokenUsage groups the token metrics; Error is the primary error from Errors. ToolCalls contains individual invocations, while Tools is their tool-identity summary. Endpoint identifies the primary request endpoint; additional endpoints remain in Models and logs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Timing and tokens

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: TimeElapsed: wall-clock seconds from acceptance to terminal result, including queueing/pauses; live snapshots measure through the snapshot time. Expose queue, pause and execution duration separately.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: TimeThinking?: attributable thinking duration. TimeAgentic?: duration of agent/tool work. TimeResponding: duration of generating the actual response. Use backend events or observed spans, not an assumption that all pre-first-token delay is thinking. Parallel and nested spans may overlap, so phase totals need not sum to TimeElapsed; report timing basis and estimate status.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: InputTokens: input processed by all included model invocations. OutputTokens: output generated by those invocations, including reported non-visible reasoning/tool output where applicable. TotalTokens equals InputTokens plus OutputTokens when both are known. Preserve provider tokenisation, cached-token details, modality usage and billing data per invocation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: ResponseTokens: output tokens attributable to the user-facing response. AgenticTokens?: output tokens attributed to agent orchestration/tool-call work. ThinkingTokens?: backend/provider-reported thinking tokens. These are labelled subsets of OutputTokens, not extra quantities to add to it. Subsets can overlap, such as thinking within an agent step; retain attribution rather than inventing a mutually exclusive split.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Aggregate actual invocations, including retries, within an explicit request/attempt/task scope. Do not double-count a child invocation through both parent and child totals. If a contributing provider withholds a required metric, the complete aggregate is Na; return a separate known subtotal and coverage when useful. Supported metrics with no value yet are null.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Model parameters, location and storage

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Parameters: architectural parameter totals across distinct model revisions actually used, counted once per model rather than once per prompt/instance. This is not a claim that several models behave like one larger model. Report per-model total and active MoE parameter counts separately when known, and label declared architectural active counts versus observed routing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Location: structured model-weight placement with a readable form such as "9.3% GPU | 90.7% RAM". This is residency, not utilisation. Include device IDs, measurement time/window, quantity basis, sampling method and any other/unknown location. Do not confuse parameter share with byte share, or include KV cache/activations as model weights. Shared/unified memory must not be double-counted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: MoEs expose separate Active and Total placement views. State the denominator: an active-set distribution normalises to the active set; active weights expressed as a share of all parameters must be labelled accordingly. Keep underlying quantities. A display such as "Active: 19.9% GPU | 20.1% RAM; Total: 6% GPU | 94% RAM" needs an explicit basis and remaining share; do not silently normalise or fabricate missing placement. Hidden provider placement is Na.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Storage: disk bytes occupied by response-associated model artifacts, not VRAM/RAM, token usage or cumulative download traffic. Deduplicate shared artifacts within each physical storage location and show local/device/remote breakdowns. Unknown remote storage makes the complete total Na, while a known local subtotal may be shown. Distinguish persistent versus temporary artifacts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Logs, blockers and errors

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: AuditLog?: timestamped reads, writes and other actions, with actor, request/attempt, target, permission/approval, start/end, outcome and side effects. ToolLog?: every tool invocation with ID, tool/version, timestamps, safe arguments/results, outcome and correlation IDs. Tools is the summary; ToolLog is the invocation history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: FullLog: the continuous ordered collection of Runtime-observed actions, model calls, available thinking/summary events, tools, queue events, pauses, replacements, retries, approvals, results, blockers and errors. Include UTC timestamps, per-request sequence numbers and causal parent IDs. Do not fabricate exact global ordering for concurrent work. Stream/paginate large logs without losing continuity. Undisclosed provider internals are not promised; sensitive payloads are redacted/permission-filtered with omissions recorded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Blockers?: structured reasons work cannot complete, with affected scope, evidence, attempted recovery, whether human input is needed, next action and retryability. Errors?: hard model/provider/Runtime/tool failures with stable code, message, component, timestamp, request identity and safe details. A blocker need not be a crash; cancellation need not be a hard error. Keep recoverable retries/warnings in logs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Use structured results for ModelNotFound, MissingPrompt, EndpointNotFound, PortInUse, InvalidArgument, OutOfMemory, ContextExceeded, ProviderUnavailable, AuthenticationFailed, PermissionDenied, UnsupportedCapability, ToolFailed, RequestNotFound, InvalidState, QueueFull, Conflict and ModelLoadFailed. Preserve "model not found" as the friendly message for resolution failure. Expected operational failures must not depend on string parsing or unhandled exceptions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Streaming and delivery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Streaming means delivering text pieces and events as they become available rather than waiting for the whole response. It changes delivery, not the intended answer. Add Dulche.PromptStream(prompt, endpoint) and Request.Stream while retaining a path that awaits one completed Result.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The submission handle exposes RequestID, Status, a final-result awaitable and optional event stream. Events include text deltas, permitted thinking/summary deltas, tool/approval events, validated UI changes, metrics and states. Include request/revision/attempt, sequence and timestamp. The final event contains the same Result contract as non-streaming, including final metrics or null/Na.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Never execute partial tool arguments or arbitrary partial markup. Mark provisional output and discard stale deltas after replacement. Reconnect using a cursor or current snapshot without starting another generation or replaying an external action. Use bounded buffering/backpressure with explicit gap/snapshot recovery; no silent audit-event loss. Closing a display stream does not automatically cancel its task.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Response controls and queues

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.StopResponse(requestID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stop that response, not the endpoint. Cancel queued work or halt running generation/future tool dispatch at a safe boundary; retain partial output/logs and return Cancelled. Repeated stops are idempotent. Dependent unfinished child work is cancelled, not unrelated requests. A completed external action is not automatically undone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.PauseResponse(requestID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pause the response, retain its output/context and prevent dispatch of its next steps. Report Pausing until a safe boundary is reached, then Paused. Paused work stays paused until resumed/stopped, not silently completed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.ResumeResponse(requestID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Resume paused work. Use exact continuation only when the backend supports it; otherwise return UnsupportedCapability or an explicitly disclosed, authorised continuation/restart mode. Buffering output while the provider keeps generating is not an exact pause. Never repeat completed tool side effects automatically.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.StackPrompt(requestID, string newPrompt);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Interrupt the current response with the new prompt at a safe boundary, ahead of ordinary queued work. Preserve interrupted state and return a linked RequestID for the priority prompt. The default stacked interruption resumes the interrupted request afterwards where supported and still applicable; superseded/cancelled work must not be revived. Multiple stacked interruptions use last-in-first-out order and a bounded nesting limit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.QueuePrompt(requestID, string newPrompt);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Queue a new prompt after the referenced request in its session without interrupting it; return a new RequestID. Commit session context in order. Failure/cancellation must not silently discard queued input: expose its dependency/state and revalidate its context before starting.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.ReplacePrompt(requestID, string newPrompt);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replace the targeted prompt, such as after a message edit. Retain logical RequestID, increment revision and create a new attempt. A queued replacement retains its position; a running replacement supersedes/cancels the old attempt at a safe boundary; a paused replacement stays paused; replacing a completed prompt creates a fresh response attempt from the relevant prior session state. Preserve earlier actions/output in history, invalidate stale deltas/approvals and never automatically undo external actions or replay subsequent turns.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: If response A is running on an endpoint, ordinary response B is queued by default, even if its backend permits parallel generation. Other endpoints may work independently within resource limits. Queue order, position, capacity and timeout are observable. Optional parallel mode cannot silently change this serial default. A task waiting for a child on the same endpoint yields its execution slot to the dependency rather than deadlocking its own queue.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Paused work may yield to independent sessions, but dependent work in the same session cannot overtake it. Recheck permissions/context before dispatch. Controls cannot target another user's work without authority. Remote tool cancellation is best-effort when a tool cannot stop; record actual completion/side effects rather than falsely claiming cancellation succeeded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Lifecycle, configuration and resources

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Add endpoint state inspection, explicit Resume, capability discovery and health events. Distinguish Starting, Loading, Ready, Busy, Pausing, Paused, Stopping, Stopped and Failed, plus model Downloading, Installed and verification states. Reachability is not model readiness.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Endpoint Pause retains local weights/context and suspends its work. Stop cancels its queued/running work, unloads owned resources and releases the port without deleting installed artifacts or Den history. Remote operations affect Dulche's own requests/sessions unless remote lifecycle control is supported and authorised. Manual pause requires resume; inactivity pause may auto-resume on new work with an event. Inactivity Timeout is distinct from request, queue, tool and network timeouts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Snapshot model identity and effective settings per attempt. SetModel, SetTemperature and SetReasoningLevel apply to future work unless safe mid-run reconfiguration is explicitly requested. Validate temperature, output limits, top-p/top-k, seed, stops, penalties and structured schemas against capabilities; silently ignoring an unsupported requested setting is not success.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reasoning percentages map to ordered supported levels: for n levels use min(n-1, floor(p*n/100)) for p in 0..100; reject out-of-range percentages. With five levels, 0-<20 selects the first, 20-<40 the second, and 80-100 the fifth. Named levels must resolve to advertised support; do not invent a mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Home owns the shared 9to1 Dulche broker/service. Multiple managed endpoints do not justify each app spawning competing unmanaged servers. Resource policy covers CPU/GPU selection, offload, RAM/VRAM budgets, active models, scheduling and explicit eviction. Pause does not promise memory release while weights remain loaded; pressure must not silently switch models or discard private context.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Providers, permissions and Generative UI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider adapters declare credentials by reference, capabilities, privacy/residency information, rate limits and bounded backoff/retry. Model/provider fallback must be configured and permission-compatible, never silently send local/private context to a cloud. Record actual fallback models and usage. Recover with Den checkpoints; reconcile uncertain non-idempotent actions before retry.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Add Dulche.GetCapabilities(model) and endpoint capability inspection. Separate model ability, adapter/backend support, host integration and granted permissions. A supported modality grants no automatic access to microphone, camera, files, shell or network. ToolCallsAllowed = All means all tools already permitted for that caller/request. Support None, ReadOnly, selected-tool policies, scope overrides, consequential-action approval, sandboxed code and revocation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: GeneratedUI is returned as data. A CUI developer explicitly implements <GenerativeContainer> and advertises supported schemas/components/actions. Without it, retain a usable text/data fallback rather than assume rendering support. Validate components, properties, limits, references and action bindings; model output never becomes trusted executable application code. UI actions use authorised typed tools tied to the request/revision. Invalid generated UI is isolated/logged without crashing the app or losing Text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Agents/tool loops require bounded step/time/token/cost budgets, visible progress, loop detection, approvals and cancellation. A proposed tool call is not proof of execution. Retrieved content and tool results cannot grant permissions or override the caller's restrictions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Acquisition, replacement and observability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preserve Den, Models.toml, local-directory, FindModel, ListModels, Pull, Install and Replace APIs. Adapters resolve supported artifacts/catalogues; a runtime backend is not assumed to be a universal registry. Pin/verify source revisions and expose download progress, cancellation, resumption and required storage. Unsupported formats return errors instead of false compatibility claims.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Temporary Pull ownership is tied to a consuming endpoint/request scope. Stopping releases that ownership; delete bytes only when no other live or persistent owner needs them. Install makes ownership persistent. Replacement stages/verifies the new model, applies preserveConfig/wipe/safe compatibility, records identities and supports rollback without deleting an in-use model. Logical IDs/aliases may survive; immutable artifact identity must reflect the replacement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Expose runtime/API/schema versions, states, queues, tokens/context, memory/storage, rate-limit status, time to first output, generation throughput and trace IDs through permission-filtered diagnostics. Use Na for unavailable telemetry, null for empty telemetry and labels for estimates. Publish SDK/adapter conformance tests and compatibility negotiation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Acceptance covers serial A/B queueing, streaming/non-streaming parity, every response control, queued/running/paused/completed replacement, null/Na/zero, withheld provider metrics/thinking, token aggregation, MoE denominators, scoped broadcasts, context isolation, unsupported exact resume, tool retry/cancellation, generated-UI fallback, provider failure, memory pressure and recovery.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Persistent request execution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PersistencePolicy MUST support at least Standard and Persistent. Standard retains the ordinary Runtime finish/timeout/checkpoint behaviour defined elsewhere. Persistent is a durable root-request policy intended for work that should continue until its user-visible completion predicate has been satisfied.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Persistent request MUST define or derive an inspectable CompletionContract from the user's request, active Skill requirements and target-app acceptance criteria. Completed is valid only when required outputs exist, required validation/verification has run where applicable, required target mutations are confirmed and no required work item remains Pending, Running, Retryable or Blocked. A checkpoint, partial deliverable, progress report or model statement such as 'done' is not itself completion evidence.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Soft request duration limits, provider execution leases and internal scheduling slices MUST NOT terminate a Persistent request merely because a continuation boundary was reached. When continued execution requires a new model invocation, endpoint lease or recovered process, Dulche MUST create a linked attempt under the same RootRequestID, restore the latest safe state/checkpoint and continue. Completed consequential actions MUST be reconciled before retry so persistence does not duplicate side effects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent requests MUST remain cancellable. Pressing the user-visible Stop control targets the root persistent request, requests safe-boundary cancellation of unfinished dependent work and produces the normal Cancelled result with retained partial output/logs. Persistence MUST NOT reinterpret an explicit user Stop as a transient interruption to auto-resume.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: While a Persistent root request is active, ordinary user messages sent through the same compose surface are SteeringMessages belonging to that root request. They are appended durably, ordered by receipt sequence and presented to the orchestrator at the next safe planning boundary without terminating the current turn. They MUST NOT be implemented as ReplacePrompt or StopResponse, and MUST NOT cause already completed actions to replay.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent orchestration MUST maintain a dependency-aware work graph. A structured Blocker marks only the work nodes that depend on it. When a blocker needs user action or permission that the agent cannot obtain itself, Dulche surfaces the blocker and continues every runnable node that does not depend on it. If all remaining nodes are blocked, the root state becomes AwaitingUser; AwaitingUser is non-terminal and keeps recovery/checkpoint state until the user resolves, changes or explicitly stops the task.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Budgets, administrator policy, permission boundaries and hard safety restrictions still apply. Persistence MUST NOT convert a denied action into an allowed action or silently purchase/consume resources beyond configured policy. A limit that can be changed by the user becomes a structured blocker; a hard non-overridable policy restriction remains recorded truthfully and the request continues any unaffected work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent state MUST survive supported Home/Dulche restarts. Den MUST retain RootRequestID, request revision, CompletionContract, task/dependency state, SteeringMessages, blockers, checkpoints, completed side-effect evidence, active Skill versions and attempt lineage required to resume without fabricating progress or repeating consequential work.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Context compaction and Context Summarisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context compaction is a first-class Dulche Runtime capability, not an app-specific prompt trick. Dulche MUST track the effective context budget for every model invocation and MAY initiate automatic compaction before hard exhaustion using model/provider-specific safety margins. Apps and Agents consume the same canonical compacted session state rather than implementing incompatible private compaction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compaction MUST preserve semantic obligations required to continue the task: current user instructions and constraints, active permissions/trust decisions, CompletionContract, outstanding tasks and blockers, accepted decisions, stable object/file/artifact IDs, current revisions, completed consequential actions, verification evidence, relevant source provenance and any exact values whose precision is required. Redundant conversational phrasing, duplicated status chatter and obsolete intermediate reasoning MAY be reduced.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compaction MUST be non-destructive to durable history. The original authorised conversation, tool records and artifacts remain in Den according to retention policy; the compacted context is a derived execution view with provenance back to source message/event ranges. A model MUST NOT be told that omitted content never existed merely because it is outside the active compacted view.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If ordinary compaction cannot create enough safe context without materially losing required information or required media fidelity, Dulche MUST transition to Context Summarisation rather than silently dropping required content or returning ContextExceeded immediately. Typical triggers include a conversation dominated by images/media that cannot be reduced further without unacceptable information loss, unusually dense tool history, or a model whose effective context limit is smaller than the preserved minimum working set.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context Summarisation is a distinct Dulche job. A summariser model reads the retained conversation/history section by section using bounded windows so the summariser's own context cannot overflow. Each section produces a structured intermediate summary containing obligations, facts, decisions, identifiers, artifacts/references, completed actions, unresolved work/blockers, provenance and continuity notes. Dulche then performs one or more bounded merge passes until a final execution summary fits the target context budget.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Section boundaries MUST be deterministic and provenance-preserving. A merge MUST NOT discard a requirement merely because it appears only once. Conflicting instructions or facts MUST remain represented as a conflict with source references instead of being flattened into an invented resolution. Exact code, identifiers, numeric values, legal/technical constraints or other precision-sensitive content that cannot be safely paraphrased MUST remain as pinned excerpts or stable references rather than approximate prose.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Images, audio, video and other large artifacts SHOULD remain out-of-band as stable artifact references wherever the target model can retrieve them on demand. Context Summarisation MAY summarise authorised derived observations/metadata, but MUST NOT claim that visual or media detail was preserved if the summariser could not inspect it. Required uninspectable media remains a blocker or retained reference, not fabricated text.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A local summariser model MAY be used automatically when an eligible local model is available under the configured routing/policy. Sending conversation content to a cloud summariser requires explicit user permission for cloud Context Summarisation or an existing user setting that clearly grants that permission for the relevant scope. A cloud-capable model in an ordinary fallback route does not by itself grant permission to upload context for summarisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If cloud summarisation is required to continue, permission is absent and no eligible local summariser can satisfy the job, Dulche MUST surface ContextSummarisationPermissionRequired/ContextCapacityBlocked as a non-destructive blocker. Persistent requests enter or remain AwaitingUser as necessary rather than losing history or pretending the task completed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MUST expose canonical operations equivalent to Dulche.Context.Compact(sessionID, options?), Dulche.Context.Summarise(sessionID, options?) and Dulche.Context.GetState(sessionID). Results MUST report source ranges/revisions, target model/context limit, method, summariser ModelID when used, retained pinned items, omitted/referenced artifacts, token estimates where available and whether the resulting context is sufficient for the next invocation.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Computer Use

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Computer Use is a first-class Dulche capability but MUST be opt-in per request. It is enabled only by an explicit @Computer Use invocation token or an equivalent explicit user control that resolves to the same ComputerUseInvocationID. An ordinary natural-language request, an @App mention or failure of a typed app API MUST NOT silently activate Computer Use.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Computer Use capability may control eligible graphical applications through supported pointer, keyboard, accessibility/automation and visual-interaction primitives. It SHOULD use the fastest reliable state channel available, including accessibility/automation metadata where appropriate, avoid unnecessary human-speed delays, batch safe independent interactions where supported and verify state transitions instead of relying on fixed sleeps. Speed MUST NOT weaken verification or permission gates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: By default, the first attempted interaction with each target application in a Computer Use run requires user approval for that AppID/process identity, and changes to application or operating-system settings require approval before mutation. Home settings MUST allow the user to change this policy to automatic approval for eligible apps and to an Approve All eligible-apps policy. Persisted approval policy remains scoped by user/profile, app identity and the normal Home trust/permission model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Auto-approve and Approve All MUST NOT bypass hard exclusions, administrator policy, OS security boundaries or other non-overridable safeguards. Computer Use receives no more filesystem, network, credential, settings or app authority than the invoking user/request already possesses.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generic Computer Use MUST NOT attach to, send input to, automate or manipulate game executables or anti-cheat-protected game surfaces, including games launched or managed through platforms such as Steam or Epic Games Launcher. When classification is uncertain and anti-cheat/game automation risk is plausible, the target is ineligible by default. This exclusion exists independently of user trust level because generic automation can create account/anti-cheat risk.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The game exclusion does not prohibit Dulche Agents from participating in games deliberately configured through the 9to1 Play framework. Play interaction MUST occur through Play's typed GameDefinition/Match/contestant actions and capability isolation, not by using generic Computer Use to drive an external game client.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Computer Use run MUST produce an inspectable action stream with target app/window identity, action type, timestamps, relevant pre/post state evidence, approvals, failures and side effects. Sensitive screen regions, credentials and typed secrets MUST follow the normal redaction and permission rules; logs MUST NOT become a second plaintext credential store.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Autoreview MUST inspect proposed and recent Computer Use actions continuously. It MUST flag patterns including repeated identical or near-identical actions without progress, repeated failing commands, oscillation between states, privilege escalation, bulk/destructive deletion, destructive shell commands such as rm -rf or platform equivalents, security-setting changes, suspicious executable/download flows and other high-risk sequences. High-confidence imminent destructive risk MUST be able to pause the next action for review rather than merely add a passive warning.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Autoreview findings are structured ProblemEvents and MUST feed the shared Problem handling contract. A Computer Use recovery intervention MUST preserve the current request, state and logs and SHOULD redirect to a safer or more direct interaction strategy. It MUST NOT hide that a risky action was proposed or attempted.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Thinking logs, work state and ETA

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Thinking-log presentation is a first-class Dulche feature backed by Runtime events. Home MUST expose one global user preference with the modes Precise, Concise, Detailed and Ramble; compatible apps inherit it unless an explicitly supported per-surface override exists. If no preference has been set, Precise is the default.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Precise shows only thinking/work events that materially advance the task, such as a resolved decision, discovered blocker, completed verification step or changed plan. It MUST suppress repetitive self-talk and events that do not change task state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Concise renders short activity summaries suitable for rapid scanning, for example 'Moving a square', 'Opening Browse', 'Checking the build' or 'Waiting for approval'. These summaries MAY be generated from richer telemetry but MUST remain faithful to the underlying action/state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Detailed exposes substantially more model/provider-permitted reasoning trace and task rationale, including intermediate decisions and why a strategy changed when that information is actually available and permitted. It MUST still distinguish observed facts, tool results, summaries and model reasoning.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ramble exposes the maximum provider/model-permitted thinking/work trace available to Dulche, including abandoned approaches, self-corrections and changes of mind when the provider actually supplies those events. Ramble MUST NOT reconstruct, infer or falsely label undisclosed private chain-of-thought as if it had been exposed by the model/provider.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Thinking mode changes presentation only. It MUST NOT change the model's configured reasoning effort, tool permissions, stored audit truth, Action Graph or provider privacy rules. Provider-unavailable thinking remains Na/Unavailable under the existing Result contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: While active, permitted thinking/work events render inline in chronological position with the conversation rather than in a separate hidden console. The visual treatment MUST be lower-emphasis/ghost-like relative to user/model message text while still meeting accessibility contrast requirements and MUST use non-colour cues so users can distinguish message content from thinking/work content.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When the active thinking/work phase ends, the inline region collapses under a disclosure labelled 'Thought for <duration>' when no tool/action execution occurred, or 'Worked for <duration>' when one or more tools/actions were executed. Duration uses the Runtime's active execution span for that phase rather than queue time. Expanding the disclosure restores the permitted events according to the selected display mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: After 60 seconds of continuous active execution in one foreground 9to1 turn, Dulche MUST request an ETA from the active orchestrating model through a canonical ETA request. The model returns an estimated completion timestamp plus optional confidence/reason. The UI displays the timestamp in the user's locale/time zone and clearly marks it as an estimate, not a guarantee. Paused/AwaitingUser time does not count as continuous active execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MUST expose an operation equivalent to Dulche.RequestETA(requestID). An ETA response includes RequestID, AttemptID, EstimatedCompletionAt, GeneratedAt and optional Confidence/Reason. If the active model cannot provide a meaningful estimate, the result is explicitly unavailable; Dulche MUST NOT invent a timestamp. Material replanning MAY request an updated ETA and MUST replace rather than stack stale estimates in the primary UI.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Problem detection, autoreview and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Problem handling is a first-class Dulche Runtime capability for detecting, surfacing and recovering from common model/agent failure modes without forcing every app to implement its own ad-hoc watchdog.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical ProblemType set MUST support at least Looping, NoProgress/Stuck, Repetition, HallucinationOrFabrication, OverAgreement/Sycophancy, InstructionDrift, ContradictionWithGroundedState, RepeatedToolFailure, UnsafeActionPattern and Other/UserReported. Additional typed categories MAY be added versionably without collapsing distinct existing meanings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Loop detection MUST consider semantic and action-level repetition, not only identical text. Examples include repeatedly issuing the same failing command, alternately undoing/reapplying the same mutation, reopening the same surface without new evidence, recreating completed work or repeatedly restating the same answer while the task remains unfinished.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hallucination/fabrication detection SHOULD use available grounded evidence such as tool results, canonical app state, source provenance, stable object IDs and completion evidence. Dulche MUST flag fabricated claims of completed actions, nonexistent files/entities/tool results or unsupported factual assertions when confidence is sufficient; it MUST NOT treat disagreement with an unverified model statement as proof that the user is wrong.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: OverAgreement/Sycophancy detection SHOULD flag responses that materially adopt or endorse a user's factual premise, conclusion or requested assessment without adequate evidence when the task calls for grounded evaluation. Recovery prompts the model to re-evaluate the evidence and user request; it MUST NOT mechanically disagree with the user merely to appear independent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When automatic detection reaches its configured intervention threshold, Dulche creates a ProblemEvent and injects a clearly identified Runtime recovery directive at the next safe boundary. The directive tells the model what failure pattern was detected, relevant evidence and the required correction, such as stop repeating the command, reassess grounded state, use a different strategy or verify the claimed result. Runtime recovery directives MUST NOT be forged as user-authored messages.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If the detected problem is associated with a proposed consequential or dangerous tool/Computer Use action, Dulche MAY pause dispatch before the action and require re-planning or applicable approval. Lower-risk reasoning-quality problems SHOULD normally correct the active request without cancelling the turn or discarding valid completed work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every conversational 9to1 AI surface MUST expose a small Problem pill above/adjacent to the compose bar. The user can invoke it even when automatic detection did not fire, select a ProblemType and optionally add a note. Manual reports enter the same ProblemEvent/recovery pipeline and are delivered to the active request at a safe boundary without implicitly stopping the request.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: ProblemEvents MUST record stable ProblemEventID, RequestID/AttemptID, category, detector source (automatic, autoreview or user), timestamp, safe evidence references, confidence when machine-detected, intervention taken, affected action/node and resolution outcome. They MUST appear in FullLog/Action Graph with sensitive content redacted as required.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Problem detection MUST itself be bounded and loop-safe. A false-positive recovery that does not improve state MUST NOT trigger an endless reviewer/model ping-pong. Repeated unresolved problems should escalate to a visible blocker, alternate model/strategy where permitted, or user decision while preserving completed work.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Dulche Den

heading: HEADING_3
text: Purpose

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Den is Dulche's persistent, cross-harness storage standard. It allows Dulche state to remain available across compatible apps and harnesses rather than being tied to one running endpoint or one application session.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Model catalogue

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A user's Den can maintain their model catalogue using stable model IDs alongside user-facing names. IDs provide unambiguous model references; names are intended for human-facing use and may be duplicated, which is why name lookup returns a list rather than assuming a single match.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Cross-app state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Den is also intended to provide persistent storage for cross-app context, agents and related Dulche state so compatible 9to1 surfaces can share the same underlying information instead of maintaining isolated copies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Storage structure and portability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Den is a directory-based persistent store with a versioned den.json manifest, structured records, a transaction journal and separately stored or referenced large objects. Portable records use UTF-8 JSON; local databases and indexes may accelerate access but must not be the only readable copy or create an incompatible private format. Exports contain authorised records and explicitly selected attachments. Reference model weights and external Files documents by identity/content hash rather than copying them by default. No special bundle extension is mandated.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: The manifest identifies DenID, FormatVersion, SchemaVersion, minimum reader/writer versions, namespaces, storage locations and required capabilities. Validate manifests, paths, sizes and hashes before import. Importing never executes code or automatically enables agents, tools, connections or permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Identity, namespaces and model records

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every model, agent, conversation, context object, workflow and request has a stable ID independent of name/path. Separate personal, team, organisation and app namespaces; device paths and hardware settings stay device-local. Shared namespaces are opt-in.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Model records contain logical ID, display name, aliases, provider/source, immutable revision/artifact hash, family, format, quantisation, modalities/capabilities, context/output limits, ordered reasoning levels, configuration overrides, installation references, timestamps, provenance and replacement history. Parameters, active MoE parameters, storage and hardware metrics use Runtime's availability rules. Local paths are not portable identities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: ID lookup is unambiguous in its namespace. Name/property lookup returns all matches, never silently chooses a duplicate. Aliases are explicit namespace-scoped references. Model replacement may retain logical ID/name but records changed artifact/provider identity, retained/reset settings and rollback history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Sessions, context and checkpoints

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Den persists messages/revisions, authorised context, agent definitions, requests/results, tool records, approvals and checkpoints as distinct record types. Runtime executes work; Den stores information needed to inspect or resume it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Portability covers supported messages, context, configuration, definitions and history, not arbitrary backend caches, GPU state or undisclosed internal model state. Checkpoints declare backend/model compatibility. Distinguish a continuation attempt from exact resumption and never automatically repeat completed external actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Context records identify source, owning app, timestamps, author/inference provenance, access scope and retention. Distinguish user-authored, imported and inferred context. Sharing a conversation does not automatically share its referenced sources, secrets, attachments or private inferences.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Persistent Memory

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Memory is a core Dulche Den subsystem for durable cross-session information about the user, recurring entities, preferences, decisions, projects and other scoped context that Dulche should be able to retrieve in future conversations or authorised surfaces. It is separate from Background Learning.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Memory is not one opaque prompt file. A persistent MemoryEntry should carry stable identity, content or structured value, subject/entity, memory type/category, scope, source/provenance, confidence where applicable, created/updated state, supersession/correction relationships, retention state and user-edited/locked state where supported.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Scopes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Memory can be scoped so unrelated Agents/apps do not receive unnecessary context. Supported scopes should include global/user memory plus narrower project, Agent, app/surface or other explicit contexts where appropriate. Retrieval MUST respect both scope and permission.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Creation and retrieval

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche may create or update memories from eligible conversations/context according to the user's Memory Frequency and memory policy. Retrieval is relevance-based: only memories useful to the active request/context should be injected, rather than the complete memory store.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Explicit user corrections supersede contradictory earlier memories. Den MUST retain enough provenance/revision information to distinguish an explicit user statement from an inference and to avoid repeatedly resurfacing a memory that has been corrected, superseded or deleted.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Memory Frequency

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Settings MUST expose a Memory Frequency preference with exactly four user-facing levels: Never, Sometimes, Often and Always. The selected level controls how readily Dulche autonomously creates, reinforces or updates Persistent Memory from eligible non-temporary interactions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Never: Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, reinforce or update Persistent Memory from ordinary interactions. Direct user-invoked memory-management actions are separate explicit operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sometimes: use a conservative threshold and retain only clearly durable, repeatedly useful or high-value information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Often: use a lower threshold and remember useful preferences, decisions, entities and ongoing context more readily when they are likely to help future responses.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Always: evaluate every eligible interaction for durable memory and normally retain information that satisfies the memory policy, while still deduplicating noise, respecting scope/retention rules and avoiding ineligible information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Changing Memory Frequency affects future autonomous memory behaviour; it MUST NOT silently delete existing memories. The setting is independent of Background Learning.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Temporary chats in Spaces

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spaces can provide Temporary Chats. Persistent Memory creation is disabled inside a Temporary Chat regardless of the user's Memory Frequency. While a chat is temporary, Dulche MUST NOT autonomously create, update, reinforce, merge or promote Persistent Memory from that conversation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any explicit action that would save new Persistent Memory from a Temporary Chat must be unavailable or clearly report that memory creation is disabled for temporary chats. Temporary-chat memory-write suppression MUST NOT be bypassed by an Agent, plugin, Skill, tool or Background Learning pipeline.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: This rule governs memory creation/writes. Whether existing authorised memories are retrieved into a temporary chat is a separate context/privacy policy and MUST NOT be inferred from the memory-write prohibition.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Management and lifecycle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users must be able to inspect, search, edit/correct, supersede and delete persistent memories through the appropriate settings/Den surfaces. Deletion and retention use Den's normal lifecycle, sync and purge contracts. Memory export/import must preserve scopes, provenance and deletion/supersession semantics rather than flattening entries into plain prose.

heading: HEADING_4
text: Persistent Memory acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Memory exists as a distinct Den record system and is not substituted by Background Learning, session context or Agent-only memory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Memory retrieval is relevance-, scope- and permission-aware.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Never/Sometimes/Often/Always control autonomous memory creation/reinforcement with the semantics above.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Temporary Chats in Spaces cannot create, update or reinforce Persistent Memory regardless of frequency or calling surface.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Corrections/supersession are durable and user-manageable, and explicit user statements remain distinguishable from inference.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Permissions and secrets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Authorise access per principal, namespace and object/action. Reading context, modifying an agent, executing tools and administering Den are separate permissions enforced below the UI. Revocation applies to future reads/searches/executions; it does not erase copies already disclosed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Store credential references, not plaintext API keys, passwords, private keys or tokens in records, exports or logs. Resolve references through secure credential storage on the relevant device/service. Protect sensitive storage and transport, document key ownership/recovery and redact sensitive log payloads without falsifying whether an action occurred.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Concurrent writes and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Use atomic transactions or crash-safe journalled updates. Mutable objects have revisions; updates supply expected revisions and return Conflict instead of overwriting newer data. Support concurrent readers and coordinated writes with bounded locking. Operation IDs make safely retryable writes idempotent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Validate before commit, preserve the previous valid record until commit and recover/quarantine incomplete writes after crashes. Export consistent snapshots. Caches and indexes are rebuildable, not the sole authority.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Synchronisation and conflicts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cross-device/team sync is optional and namespace-scoped. Track IDs, revisions, origin device and deletion tombstones. Offline changes wait for an authorised sync target. Merge compatible disjoint edits; preserve conflicting versions for review. Wall-clock timestamps alone never choose the winner.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Concurrent conversation edits create explicit revisions or alternate continuations. Sync does not execute stored requests or replay tools. Device-local paths, secrets and hardware settings are not portable values. Recheck permissions on reconnection and record deletion/restoration/revocation explicitly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Lifecycle and storage policy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Support create/open, inspect/search/update, export/import, backup/restore, soft-delete and explicit permanent purge. Retention is configurable and visible by namespace/category; do not assume indefinite retention or silently discard work under storage pressure. Soft-delete preserves recoverable revisions until expiry. Purge covers managed replicas/indexes/derived records under policy, with explicit limits for offline copies and external backups.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large files use content-addressed blobs or authorised external references. Reference counting prevents deletion while another owner needs an artifact. Distinguish quotas for metadata, logs, caches, attachments and model weights. Den metadata does not make a temporary Pull permanent: Install or an explicit pin creates persistent ownership.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Compatibility and migration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Publish versioned schemas, examples and conformance tests. Compatible writers preserve unknown optional fields; unknown security-critical fields or required capabilities block unsafe writes. Validate, back up and transactionally migrate schemas. Unsupported newer versions may open read-only when safe, never discard fields to force a downgrade.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Round-trip null for empty metrics and Na for provider-unavailable metrics, serialised as "Na"; measured zero stays 0. Permission-filter search/index results and include revision/provenance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Supporting APIs and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preserve Dulche.Den.GetModelByID(id) and Dulche.Den.ListModelsByName(name). Add compatible create/open, scoped search, revision-checked update, export/import, sync, restore and purge APIs with documented signatures and failures.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Acceptance covers cross-harness round-tripping, duplicate names, concurrent edits, offline conflicts, crash recovery, revocation, safe import, secret-free export, model replacement/rollback, retention/restore and migrations without data loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Generative UI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generative UI is a Dulche capability that allows a model or Agent to return arbitrary structured user interfaces when an interface is more useful than prose. Generated interfaces may be visual, interactive and stateful, but MUST be expressed through a validated declarative Generative UI schema and MUST NOT execute arbitrary model-generated application code.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Rendering and trust boundary

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CUI is the rendering layer for Generative UI. Generated surfaces render inside a CUI <GenerativeContainer> or equivalent trusted host component using approved CUI primitives, design tokens, theming, layout, accessibility and interaction behaviour. Any authorised 9to1 app may host a GenerativeContainer without implementing its own incompatible renderer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche may choose the structure and composition of the interface, including novel layouts, but the model output is data/schema rather than executable JavaScript, Python, shell commands, native binaries or arbitrary application code. The Generative UI runtime validates schema version, component types, properties, state bindings, declared actions and capability references before rendering.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Templates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generative UI provides reusable high-level templates for common interaction patterns. Templates are starting structures, not hard limits; Dulche can instantiate, extend, combine or restyle them through supported schema properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Flashcard set / study deck.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Table, sortable/filterable data table and comparison grid.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quiz, practice exercise and answer/reveal workflow.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Timeline and step-by-step guide.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Checklist and progress tracker.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Card grid / gallery / result browser.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Form, questionnaire and multi-step wizard.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Kanban/task-board style layout where appropriate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Glossary / FAQ / concept-reference layout.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Diagram, relationship map and structured visual explainer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other shared templates added by the Generative UI framework or authorised extensions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Primitive composition

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When no template fully fits the task, Dulche can compose a custom surface from approved lower-level primitives. The supported primitive set should include, where appropriate, text/heading blocks, icons or generated illustrations, cards, badges/tags, buttons, inputs, dropdowns, toggles, sliders, chips, lists, tables, grids, tabs, accordions, progress indicators, layout containers, drag containers, drop zones, connectors/relationships, semantic-object views and other safe CUI primitives.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The primitive library is extensible through versioned framework/extension contracts. Unsupported component types MUST be rejected or downgraded safely; a model cannot create a new privileged executable component merely by naming it in the schema.

heading: HEADING_3
text: State and interaction

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated surfaces may maintain bounded typed state. Supported interactions can include selecting options, sorting/filtering, expanding/collapsing content, progressing through steps, editing fields, revealing hints/answers, checking responses, reordering items, dragging supported objects between declared drop zones, switching views and updating selected data.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: State mutations are handled by the Generative UI runtime or by declared typed actions. Interaction support does not grant the model arbitrary code execution or unrestricted access to the host application's process.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Progressive conversational evolution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A generated surface is a first-class conversation artifact and may evolve across turns. Dulche should be able to patch or transform an existing surface instead of rebuilding unrelated output from scratch. Examples include turning a static explanation into an interactive exercise, adding another column to a table, converting notes into flashcards, adding filters, changing a card grid into a comparison view or preserving quiz progress while adding new questions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Updates must address stable SurfaceID/component/state identities or equivalent schema identities so user interaction state is retained wherever the requested transformation allows it. Partial regeneration is preferred when only part of a surface changes.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Typed actions and side effects

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated controls bind to declared typed actions rather than arbitrary executable handlers. An action definition includes stable identity, expected input schema, allowed state mutation or API binding, required capability/permission and result/error contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pure presentation and local interaction may execute inside the Generative UI runtime without external side effects. Actions that invoke 9to1 APIs, tools or external services remain subject to the same permission, confirmation, auditing and consequence rules as the underlying capability. Generative UI MUST NOT be a path around security prompts or tool permissions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Data binding and semantic objects

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generative UI can bind to authorised structured data and canonical 9to1 entities instead of flattening everything into prompt text. Examples include Data ranges, Planner tasks, Maps Places/Routes, Board items, Write selections/documents, search results, translation sets, code diffs or Dulche Action Graph state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Bindings retain source identity and permissions. A rendered card or table row that represents a canonical object should reference that object rather than silently creating a disconnected copy unless the user explicitly asks for a snapshot.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Ephemeral and saved artifacts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A generated surface may remain ephemeral to the current response/session or be promoted through an explicit supported conversion/save path. Examples include saving generated flashcards as a study resource, converting a generated task board into a Board, inserting a generated table into Write/Data or saving a generated route through Maps. Promotion uses the destination app's canonical API and permissions.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Third-party visual examples and assets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generative UI may reproduce the functional idea or spatial structure needed to explain a third-party product/game without copying proprietary artwork merely to imitate the source. Where licensed/authorised assets are not available, it should use generic, stylised, text-labelled or newly generated representations sufficient to communicate the concept.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Example: if the user asks how an item is crafted in Minecraft, Dulche may create a visual 3x3 crafting-grid representation using generic/stylised ingredient tokens and an output slot rather than copied official item textures or proprietary interface artwork. In later turns the same surface may be made interactive using approved drag/drop primitives so the user can move ingredient tokens, receive validation, request hints or turn the recipe into a quiz.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Accessibility and visual consistency

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated UI MUST inherit the host CUI theme/design system and remain accessible. The runtime should enforce semantic roles, labels, focusability/order, keyboard operation, screen-reader information, non-colour-only meaning and accessible alternatives for interactions such as drag/drop wherever the component library supports them.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Failure and fallback

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Invalid, unsupported or unsafe generated schemas MUST fail closed without executing arbitrary content. Dulche may repair/regenerate the affected surface or fall back to a non-interactive/native representation while preserving the user-visible answer where possible.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Result contract and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Result.GeneratedUI contains the generated UI payload when present and returns null when no generated interface is produced. The payload must identify schema version, surface identity, component tree, declared state/bindings and declared actions/capabilities required to reproduce the surface safely.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche can create arbitrary useful UI structures without arbitrary code execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Built-in templates and lower-level CUI primitives can be combined and extended within the declarative schema.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated surfaces support safe stateful interaction and can evolve across conversation turns without unnecessarily discarding user state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All external side effects route through typed permission-aware actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Structured 9to1 data can be bound by canonical identity, and generated artifacts can be promoted through destination-app APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Generated UI follows CUI theming/accessibility and safely handles invalid schemas or unavailable components.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Background Learning

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background Learning is an explicitly opt-in Dulche personalisation subsystem. It is separate from Persistent Memory. Enabling Background Learning allows Dulche to learn useful patterns, interests and reusable knowledge from eligible 9to1 activity over time; it does not itself enable or disable Persistent Memory and it does not imply continuous fine-tuning of the underlying base model.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Eligible learning classes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background Learning can maintain three broad classes of learned information:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 usage and project context: which authorised surfaces the user uses most, recurring workflows, recently or frequently active projects, apps commonly used together, important project terminology/entities and other usage patterns that improve contextual relevance.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Interests and topic Knowledge Banks: recurring subjects the user appears to care about, together with reusable factual/reference material that can improve later answers and remain available offline. For example, repeated questions about cars may lead to an Interest record for cars and a local Cars Knowledge Bank containing useful terminology, concepts and sourced reference material.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Other relevant personalisation information: additional permitted information that materially improves responses, such as preferred terminology, recurring goals, explanation preferences, established project conventions, frequently used tools, entity relationships and corrections that should influence future response behaviour.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Usage and project learning

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The usage-learning layer SHOULD retain useful semantic state rather than an indiscriminate permanent clickstream. For example, it may learn that Dev and Stack are frequently used for a particular project or that a project is currently active. Raw activity used to derive these signals should be retained only to the extent required by the configured retention/privacy model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Learned project context can help Dulche resolve ambiguous references, rank context candidates, suggest likely relevant surfaces and prepare authorised Agents with useful project context. It MUST remain scope-aware: project-specific learning does not automatically become unrelated global context.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Interest Knowledge Banks

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background Learning can create and maintain topic-specific KnowledgeBank entities. A KnowledgeBank can contain a stable ID, topic/title, entries, source/provenance metadata, confidence, freshness, creation/update state, storage/sync policy and enabled/disabled state. Knowledge Banks may be created automatically from recurring interests or explicitly managed by the user.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Knowledge Bank entries may include reusable summaries, terminology, relationships, reference facts and other material previously obtained from authorised local sources, user interactions or trusted retrieval. Factual entries MUST retain enough provenance/freshness information for Dulche to distinguish durable knowledge from information that may need refreshing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Knowledge Banks are not the same as Persistent Memory. For example, 'the user is interested in cars' is personalisation/user context; a structured offline bank explaining engines, EV charging and vehicle terminology is subject knowledge. Dulche may use both when relevant, but they remain separately inspectable and manageable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Structured learned state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background Learning MUST store structured learned records rather than relying on one opaque free-form profile. Records should carry stable identity, category/type, subject/entity, learned value, provenance, confidence, creation/update state, last reinforcement/use where useful, freshness/expiry semantics and user-edited/locked state where applicable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Explicit user corrections outrank contradictory inferred learning. If a user corrects an inferred preference, project status or interest, the system MUST revise/supersede the stale inference instead of allowing both to compete indefinitely as equally valid facts.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Selective retrieval

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The complete learning store MUST NOT be injected into every request. Dulche must retrieve only learning context relevant to the active request, Agent, app and permission scope. Retrieval should use current entities/topics/project context to select the smallest useful set of records and Knowledge Bank material.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Privacy and cloud boundaries

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background Learning data is private by default and exists to personalise the user's 9to1 AI experience. It MUST NOT be sold, used to build advertising profiles or indiscriminately uploaded to third parties. Enabling Background Learning does not itself grant permission to transmit learned information to a cloud model/provider.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a Dulche request uses a remote/cloud provider, disclosure of any learned context remains subject to the normal provider, privacy, permission and data-minimisation rules for that request. The implementation MUST distinguish permission to learn/store information from permission to disclose that information externally.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any optional cross-device synchronisation of Background Learning state must be user-controlled and protected by the applicable authenticated/encrypted 9to1 sync/storage architecture. The feature MUST remain useful locally and must not require insecure cloud upload merely to personalise responses.

heading: HEADING_3
text: User controls

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users must be able to enable/disable Background Learning, pause new learning, inspect learned information, inspect and manage topic Knowledge Banks, correct inaccurate learning, delete individual learned records or a complete topic bank, clear learned categories and configure which apps/projects/categories may contribute where supported. Disabling learning stops creation/reinforcement of new learned state but MUST NOT silently delete existing Persistent Memory or unrelated user data.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Relationship to Persistent Memory

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent Memory and Background Learning are independent. Persistent Memory stores durable cross-session memories under the Memory policy; Background Learning is the opt-in process that derives usage patterns, interests, Knowledge Banks and other personalisation state. Neither feature may silently enable, disable, clear or substitute for the other.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background Learning may identify information that would be useful as a durable memory, but any conversion into Persistent Memory must use the Memory subsystem and preserve that the source was an inference rather than an explicit user statement. Explicit Memory corrections remain authoritative over contradictory Background Learning inferences.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Background Learning acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Background Learning is off until the user opts in and remains independently configurable from Persistent Memory.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Eligible 9to1 usage/project patterns, interests/Knowledge Banks and other useful personalisation information can be learned as structured, inspectable state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Topic Knowledge Banks can provide relevant offline reference material and retain provenance/freshness sufficient to avoid presenting stale inferred facts as timeless truth.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Only relevant learning context is retrieved for a request; the full learning store is not injected indiscriminately.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Learned data is not sold, used for advertising profiles or uploaded to cloud providers merely because learning is enabled.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can inspect, correct, scope and delete learning independently of Persistent Memory.

heading: HEADING_2
text: MCP Support

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: MCP is a first-class Dulche extension/runtime capability. Dulche MUST support acting as an MCP client for authorised local/remote MCP servers and acting as an MCP server when 9-1 intentionally exposes approved capabilities to external MCP clients. MCP execution MUST use the same permission, audit, cancellation, timeout and structured-error contracts as native Dulche tools.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Identity and lifecycle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every configured MCP connection MUST have a stable ServerID independent of display name or transport address. Configuration MUST record role (client/server), transport/process/endpoint definition, credential references, trust state, capability snapshot/version and owner/scope. Credentials MUST be stored by secure reference and MUST NOT be embedded as plaintext in project manifests or logs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Client connections MUST expose at least Disconnected, Connecting, Ready, Degraded, Reconnecting, Failed and Stopped states. Reconnect MUST NOT replay a previously completed consequential tool call. A broken connection returns structured transport/provider failures and MUST NOT be reported as Ready.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Capability discovery and schemas

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche MUST discover and represent the capabilities actually exposed by an MCP server, including tools and, where supported by the negotiated MCP version/server, resources and prompts. Tool input/output schemas MUST be validated before dispatch/consumption. Capability changes MUST invalidate stale cached schemas before later calls use them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Capability identity is server-scoped: two MCP servers MAY expose the same human-readable tool name without collision because the canonical identity includes ServerID plus capability identity/name. User-facing aliases MAY exist but MUST NOT replace stable server-scoped identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Permissions and execution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connecting to an MCP server does not authorise all capabilities it exposes. Each tool/resource capability MUST resolve through Dulche/Home permission and risk evaluation according to its effective read/write/external-side-effect scope. Server-provided descriptions/content MUST NOT grant permissions, alter trust state or override caller restrictions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: MCP tool execution MUST support cancellation/timeouts when supported by the active transport/server and MUST record when cancellation is best-effort or too late because an external action already completed. Results, approvals, failures, blockers and side effects MUST appear in ToolLog, AuditLog, FullLog and Action Graph like equivalent native tools.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Canonical MCP API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.Connect(config);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.Disconnect(serverID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.ListServers();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.GetState(serverID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.GetCapabilities(serverID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.ListTools(serverID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.CallTool(serverID, toolName, arguments);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.ListResources(serverID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.ReadResource(serverID, resourceID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.ListPrompts(serverID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.GetPrompt(serverID, promptID, arguments?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.Server.Start(config);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.MCP.Server.Stop(serverID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Unsupported capabilities MUST return UnsupportedCapability rather than fabricated empty results. Protocol-version-specific functionality MAY extend this API while preserving compatibility with the stable core.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Tool Builder integration and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: MCP projects produced by AI Studio Tool Builder MUST validate against the same Dulche MCP connection/schema/permission contract used at runtime. MCP support is implementation-complete only when local and remote connections can be configured, discovered, permissioned, called, cancelled/failed, reconnected and audited without bespoke per-app wiring, and when approved 9-1 capabilities can be exposed through server mode without bypassing their original permission model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Plugins and web integrations — WebMCP and site-hosted MCP servers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Support MUST be added for WebMCP-enabled web pages and for remote MCP servers hosted by websites. These are distinct integration surfaces: browser-side WebMCP support alone does not satisfy remote MCP-server support, and connecting to a remote MCP endpoint alone does not satisfy WebMCP support.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The existing Plugin/MCP integration system MUST expose discovery/inspection, connection or permission setup, tool invocation, cancellation where supported, and disconnect/revocation for the appropriate surface. WebMCP integration MUST use the supported browser capability with explicit capability detection and origin boundaries. Site-hosted MCP connections MUST support the applicable remote HTTP transport and protocol-version/authentication contracts rather than assuming that a page URL is itself a valid MCP endpoint. The implementation MUST record supported browser/protocol versions and visibly report unsupported capabilities instead of claiming a successful integration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Both routes MUST retain Home-brokered permissions, declared scopes, caller/site identity, secret protection and consequential-action approval. Tool descriptions, page content and tool results MUST NOT be treated as authority to expand permissions. These requirements include interoperability with websites exposing MCP servers; they do not silently select or purchase a new hosting service for the Sites application.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Web integration API and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Extend the existing canonical MCP/Plugin APIs for capability inspection, discovery, connection/authentication setup, invocation, supported cancellation and revocation. Browser-side WebMCP bindings MUST preserve browser origin/document identity; remote MCP bindings MUST preserve ServerID, endpoint identity and negotiated protocol/transport metadata. Test an authorised WebMCP-enabled page and a website-hosted remote MCP endpoint separately, then test unsupported browser/protocol, denied scopes, disconnected transport, cancellation limits and revocation. Neither route may claim success from a placeholder, silently use a page URL as an MCP endpoint or expose secrets in logs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Skills + Plugins

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Skills and Plugins are separate first-class Dulche extension types. A Skill packages reusable instructions, workflows, context rules and resources for model/Agent/Harness execution. A Plugin packages executable or integrated capabilities and MAY expose typed tools/actions, CUI surfaces or external-service functionality. Neither type is interchangeable with MCP, although a Skill or Plugin MAY declare an MCP dependency.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Common package contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every Skill and Plugin MUST have a versioned manifest containing stable PackageID, package type, version, minimum/compatible Dulche versions, provenance/origin, declared capabilities, required/requested permissions, dependencies, entry points/resources, update metadata and integrity/signature information when the distribution channel supports signing. Display name MUST NOT be used as package identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Manifest parsing and dependency resolution MUST be deterministic. Unknown required manifest fields/capabilities block installation or enablement with a structured compatibility failure; unknown optional fields MAY be preserved for forward compatibility. Packages MUST NOT execute code merely because their manifest was inspected or imported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Lifecycle, trust and permissions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Installation, enablement, permissions and trust are separate states. Installing a package registers its files/manifest but MUST NOT automatically enable it for every caller, grant requested permissions, connect external accounts or grant Accept and Always Trust. Enablement only makes the package available within the selected scope; individual actions still use the normal Dulche/Home permission and risk model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Package lifecycle MUST expose at least Installed, Disabled, Enabled, Updating, Failed and Quarantined states. A package that fails integrity/signature/compatibility validation MUST NOT become Enabled. Quarantine preserves evidence/metadata needed for diagnosis while preventing execution.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Updates MUST be version-aware and transactional. Dulche MUST validate/stage the new version and dependency graph before switching the active version. Failure during update MUST leave the previous known-good version available when rollback is technically possible. Package updates MUST NOT silently expand effective permissions; newly requested scopes require a new permission decision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Uninstall MUST define what happens to package-owned persistent data. Shared/user-authored data MUST NOT be silently deleted merely because a package is removed. Orphaned package state MAY be retained for recovery/reinstall according to explicit retention policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Skill model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Skill is primarily declarative. It MAY contain instructions, workflow definitions, templates/prompts, context-selection rules, examples, resources/files and references to permitted tools/Plugins/MCP capabilities. A Skill MUST NOT gain arbitrary code execution solely by being a Skill; executable behaviour requires an explicitly declared/authorised executable extension capability such as a Plugin/tool dependency.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Skill activation MUST be explicit and observable in request/run metadata. Dulche MUST record which Skill IDs/versions contributed to a request so Result provenance, logs and Action Graph can identify the active Skill set. Conflicting or incompatible Skills MUST resolve through a deterministic precedence/compatibility rule or return Conflict; Dulche MUST NOT silently merge contradictory required policies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Built-in Persistent skill

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
