text: Dulche MUST ship a first-party built-in Skill with the canonical display name Persistent and a stable reserved SkillID. Activating Persistent on a request sets that root request's PersistencePolicy to Persistent. The Skill is declarative: it changes Runtime orchestration semantics and does not gain permissions, tools, external access, budget or trust merely by being active.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent activation MUST be explicit and visible in request metadata, the compose invocation state, FullLog and Action Graph. It MAY be invoked through the shared @ resource picker as @Persistent. The active version MUST be recorded like every other Skill so later inspection can prove which persistence contract governed the run.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Persistent Skill MUST use the canonical Dulche persistent-request contract. In particular, an ordinary checkpoint, context compaction boundary, provider lease expiry, model restart, recoverable tool timeout or similar continuation boundary MUST NOT be treated as successful completion of the turn. The Runtime preserves/reconstructs execution state and continues under the same RootRequestID until the task's completion criteria are actually satisfied, the user explicitly stops it, or all remaining work is non-terminally AwaitingUser because of an unresolved blocker.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: While a Persistent turn is running, an ordinary follow-up message sent by the user MUST join the same root turn as a SteeringMessage and MUST NOT implicitly cancel, replace or interrupt the active work. Dulche consumes the message at the next safe planning boundary, updates the plan and continues. Explicit Stop, explicit replace/edit semantics and any separately exposed interrupt/stack action retain their distinct meanings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A blocker that cannot be resolved within the request's effective permission and capability bounds MUST be surfaced to the user as a structured blocker immediately. The blocker MUST isolate only the dependent work. Dulche MUST continue any independent runnable work in the same persistent turn; if no independent work remains, the turn enters AwaitingUser without being misreported as complete or timed out. When the blocker is resolved, the same durable turn resumes from current state rather than silently restarting completed work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persistent MUST remain compatible with automatic context compaction, Context Summarisation, Subagents, checkpoints, crash recovery and provider/model fallback. None of those mechanisms may erase completed side-effect evidence, duplicate consequential actions or weaken permission/approval requirements.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Plugin model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Plugin MAY expose typed tools/actions, external-service connectors and optional CUI surfaces. Every exposed callable capability MUST declare input/output schemas, permission scopes, risk/side-effect classification and cancellation/timeout semantics where applicable. Plugin tool calls MUST enter the same ToolLog, AuditLog, FullLog and Action Graph pipeline as native tools and MCP calls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Plugin CUI surfaces MUST render through approved CUI contracts and MUST NOT inject arbitrary trusted application code/markup outside the declared host surface. A Plugin surface does not inherit permission to invoke its Plugin’s actions without the applicable caller/user permission grants.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: External-service Plugins MUST use secure credential references and explicit connection/account scopes. Provider tokens/secrets MUST NOT be stored in plaintext package files, logs or project definitions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Dependencies and persistence

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Package dependencies MUST be expressed by stable PackageID plus version/range and dependency type. Dulche MUST detect missing, cyclic and incompatible dependencies before enablement. Optional dependencies MUST be distinguishable from required dependencies so absence does not masquerade as a broken install.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche Den MUST persist the installed package registry, active versions, enablement scopes, package provenance, dependency graph and relevant package state. Device-specific executable paths/caches remain device-local; shared Den state MUST NOT imply that executable packages are installed on another device unless that device independently satisfies installation/integrity requirements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Canonical Skill API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Skill.Install(package);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Skill.List();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Skill.Get(skillID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Skill.Enable(skillID, scope?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Skill.Disable(skillID, scope?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Skill.Update(skillID, version?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Skill.Uninstall(skillID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Skill.ResolveFor(request);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Canonical Plugin API

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Plugin.Install(package);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Plugin.List();

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Plugin.Get(pluginID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Plugin.Enable(pluginID, scope?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Plugin.Disable(pluginID, scope?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Plugin.Update(pluginID, version?);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Plugin.Uninstall(pluginID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Plugin.GetCapabilities(pluginID);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche.Plugin.Invoke(pluginID, capability, arguments);

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: These are minimum canonical entry points. Tool Builder and other first-party clients MUST use the same package/runtime contracts rather than manipulating private package files or registries directly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_3
text: Tool Builder integration and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Skills and Plugins produced by AI Studio Tool Builder MUST validate against the exact manifest/schema/dependency/permission contracts used by Dulche after installation. First-class support is implementation-complete only when packages can be created, validated, installed, enabled/disabled, permissioned, updated/rolled back where supported, used in real Dulche requests, audited, persisted/recovered and uninstalled without bespoke per-app wiring or silent permission escalation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: External App Integrations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: External App Integrations is the shared 9to1 framework for connecting, authenticating and operating third-party accounts/services. Authentication, provider scopes, transport, sync, webhooks, rate limits, provider-specific errors and remote-entity identity MUST be encapsulated by this shared layer rather than reimplemented independently inside each consuming app.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Core connection model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The framework MUST define stable typed entities for IntegrationProvider, Connection, ExternalAccount, IntegrationCapability, CredentialReference, RemoteEntityReference, SyncCursor, WebhookSubscription and ConnectionHealth or equivalent contracts. A Connection represents one authenticated provider/account relationship and has stable identity independent of whichever 9to1 app first created it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiple accounts/connections for the same provider MUST be supported. For example, a user may connect separate personal and work Google accounts or multiple GitHub identities without those accounts being merged or ambiguously selected.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Connect once, reuse through authorised capabilities

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A provider account should be connected once through the integration framework and then reused by authorised 9to1 surfaces. Consuming apps MUST request capabilities from the existing Connection rather than maintaining private duplicate credentials or running their own hidden authentication flows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples include a Google connection supplying Drive capabilities to Files, Gmail capabilities to Mail, Calendar capabilities to Planner/Calendar and Contacts capabilities to relevant people pickers; a GitHub connection may supply repository/issue/pull-request capabilities to Stack, Dev or authorised Dulche Agents. The exact provider capabilities available remain determined by granted provider scopes and the integration adapter.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Provider scope versus 9to1 permission

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider authorisation and 9to1 authorisation are separate gates. A Connection may possess provider scopes that a particular app, Agent, Skill, Plugin or extension is not authorised to use. Both the remote provider scope and the applicable 9to1 permission/capability policy MUST allow an operation before it is executed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connecting an account MUST NOT implicitly grant every 9to1 surface unrestricted access to that account. Permission decisions should be made at an appropriate capability/resource scope and remain inspectable/revocable.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Typed capability contracts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consuming apps SHOULD depend on provider-neutral typed capabilities where equivalent semantics exist instead of embedding provider-specific endpoint logic. Examples include Files.List/Read/Upload, Mail.Search/Read/Send, Calendar.ListEvents/CreateEvent, Contacts.Search, Git.ListRepositories/CreateIssue and Chat.ListMessages or equivalent canonical contracts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider adapters map those typed capabilities onto the provider's API. Provider-specific features that cannot be represented faithfully through a common contract may be exposed through explicit provider-namespaced capabilities; the common abstraction MUST NOT silently discard important provider semantics merely to force false parity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Capability schemas MUST declare input/output shape, supported operations, required provider scopes, relevant 9to1 permissions, pagination/streaming behaviour, provider limitations and error states.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Authentication and credential storage

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The integration framework centrally owns supported authentication flows such as OAuth/OIDC, PKCE, device-code flows, API-key authentication or provider-specific enterprise methods where appropriate. Apps MUST NOT request or persist reusable provider credentials directly when the integration framework can broker them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Credential material such as access tokens, refresh tokens, API keys, passwords and private keys MUST live in approved secure credential storage. Integration records, Den records, logs, exports and app settings store credential references/connection identities rather than plaintext reusable secrets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Token refresh, expiry, revocation and provider reauthentication are lifecycle concerns of the integration framework. A consumer receives a capability result or typed authentication-required failure, not raw credentials it can reuse arbitrarily.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Scope escalation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If a Connection exists but lacks a provider scope required by a new capability, the consuming surface requests scope escalation through the shared integration framework. The user must be shown which additional provider access is being requested and why. The framework extends/replaces the existing authorisation where the provider supports it rather than creating a hidden duplicate connection.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Remote identity and canonical 9to1 entities

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: External objects MUST retain their remote identity and provenance. A RemoteEntityReference should identify the provider, Connection, remote object ID, remote revision/version where available, remote URL/reference and any mapped canonical 9to1 entity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening or referencing a remote object does not automatically create a separate canonical copy. The UI and APIs MUST distinguish operations such as Open remote, Import/copy into 9to1, Link/reference and Keep synchronised.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where an external object is mapped to a canonical 9to1 entity, the relationship must remain explicit so the system does not create multiple disconnected local copies of the same remote item or accidentally treat provider IDs as globally unique without Connection/provider context.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Live, cached, imported and synchronised state

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The integration layer MUST distinguish live remote data, cached metadata, cached content, imported local copies and synchronised mirrors. Consuming apps must be able to determine whether displayed information is current, cached, stale or locally diverged.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Caching policies must respect provider terms, account permissions, data sensitivity and user settings. A cached object must not be presented as live merely because a prior request succeeded.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Sync, webhooks and change feeds

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a provider supports webhooks, push notifications or incremental change feeds, the integration framework SHOULD use them rather than each app independently polling the same account. It owns webhook registration/renewal/validation, change cursors, deduplication, retry/backoff and background refresh.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Polling remains available where required by the provider or capability, but should be centralised enough to avoid redundant traffic and quota consumption. Sync state must include sufficient cursor/revision information to continue incrementally after restart or temporary offline periods.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Offline and queued-operation behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consumers may continue to display authorised cached state while a provider is unavailable, but the stale/offline state and last successful sync/freshness information MUST remain visible when material. The framework MUST NOT silently claim remote mutations succeeded when they have only been queued locally.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If queued remote writes are supported, each operation needs stable identity, retry/idempotency semantics, dependency ordering where applicable, visible pending/failed state and explicit conflict handling. Reconnection must not blindly replay an action that is no longer valid or that already completed remotely.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Conflicts and versioning

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For synchronised/mirrored objects, use provider revision identifiers, ETags/version tokens or equivalent change metadata where available. Wall-clock timestamps alone MUST NOT be the only conflict authority.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compatible disjoint edits may be merged where the owning capability can prove a safe merge. Otherwise preserve both versions or surface a conflict to the owning app/user. Provider-side deletion, permission loss and remote moves/renames require explicit typed states rather than being treated as generic missing-file errors.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Connection health and failure states

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connections expose typed health/lifecycle states such as Connected, AuthenticationRequired, ScopeRequired, RateLimited, ProviderUnavailable, Degraded, SyncError, Revoked and Disabled or equivalent. Apps consume these states and present appropriate user-facing recovery rather than leaking raw HTTP/provider exceptions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Health information should include the failing capability/provider account where relevant, last successful contact/sync, retryability and the action required from the user when one exists.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Rate limits and reliability

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The shared layer MUST centrally support pagination, retry-after handling, provider quotas, transient network retries, exponential backoff/jitter, idempotency, request cancellation, partial response handling and provider-specific service limits. Consuming apps MUST NOT each invent incompatible retry/quota behaviour.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Connection management UI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 MUST provide a central integrations management surface, hosted under the appropriate Home/Settings area, showing provider, connected account identity, connection status, provider-granted scopes/capabilities, authorised 9to1 consumers where exposed, recent/last successful activity, errors, reconnect/re-authorise, permission management and disconnect/revoke actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Individual apps may deep-link into this management flow or expose capability-specific connection prompts, but connection state remains owned by the shared framework.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Dulche and Agent access

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche, Agents and AI surfaces use External App Integrations through the same typed capabilities and permissions as first-party apps. Dulche does not own a parallel account-authentication layer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For example, a request to find an email uses an authorised Mail capability for an existing connection; a request to create a GitHub issue uses the relevant Git capability. Normal Dulche tool/action permissions and consequential-action confirmation requirements still apply. Merely connecting an account does not grant every Agent permission to mutate it.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Relationship to Plugins and MCP

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: External App Integrations, Plugins and MCP are distinct abstractions. External App Integrations represent durable authenticated third-party account/service relationships and their capabilities. Plugins are installable packages that may add executable/integrated functionality. MCP is a protocol by which Dulche can discover/use tools/resources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: They may interoperate: a Plugin may register a provider adapter; an integration capability may be surfaced to Dulche through an approved tool/MCP bridge. Such composition MUST preserve the underlying Connection identity, provider scopes and 9to1 permission checks rather than laundering authority through another abstraction.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Provider SDK and extension

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 SHOULD expose a versioned Integration Provider SDK/manifest contract so additional providers can be implemented without changing every consuming app. A provider definition can declare provider identity/branding metadata, authentication method, capability schemas, provider scopes, remote entity types, webhook/change-feed support, rate-limit semantics, health checks and provider-specific settings.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Third-party provider adapters remain sandboxed/permissioned according to their implementation model. Registering a provider does not grant unrestricted access to other Connections, credential stores or unrelated local data.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Disconnect and revocation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Disconnect semantics MUST be explicit and predictable. Disconnecting a Connection should stop sync/background activity, invalidate or remove local credential references as appropriate, disable provider capabilities and clear/expire caches according to policy. Where supported and requested, provider-side token revocation should also be attempted.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Disconnecting an account MUST NOT automatically delete unrelated local 9to1 artifacts previously imported from it. For linked/synchronised objects, the UI must explain what local data remains, what becomes unavailable and whether any pending remote operations are abandoned.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Security invariants

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Possessing a provider credential does not grant any app, Agent, Skill, Plugin or extension unrestricted access to the associated account.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every external operation must pass both provider scope/capability validation and the relevant 9to1 permission boundary.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consuming apps receive capability access/results, not raw reusable credentials.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Connection/account identity, remote-object identity, provenance and provider limitations must remain explicit across app boundaries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Logs, exports and Den records must not contain plaintext reusable provider secrets.

heading: HEADING_2
text: External App Integrations acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: One authenticated Connection can be reused safely by multiple authorised 9to1 apps without duplicated credentials or hidden per-app OAuth implementations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiple accounts per provider are unambiguous and stable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Typed provider-neutral capabilities work where semantics align, with provider-specific extensions exposed explicitly rather than silently discarded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider scopes and 9to1 consumer permissions are enforced as independent gates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Live/cached/imported/synchronised states, remote identity and conflict/version state remain explicit and recoverable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Webhooks/change feeds, polling, retries, rate limits, queued operations and connection health are handled centrally with deterministic failure semantics.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche/Agents use the same connection/capability layer and cannot bypass account permissions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Disconnect/revocation, secure credential storage and provider SDK integration are implemented without deleting unrelated local artifacts or exposing reusable secrets.

heading: TITLE
text: 9to1-OS

heading: HEADING_1
text: Platform foundation and donor authority

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-OS is derived from the latest appropriate maintained Ubuntu/GNOME stack. The project forks/adapts the complete relevant desktop/system stack rather than treating Ubuntu merely as a kernel image, then rebuilds the 9to1 user-facing desktop environment and first-party system interfaces in CUI.NET while preserving mature non-replaced functionality underneath.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The governing donor rule is preserve unless replaced: applicable Ubuntu/GNOME behaviour, hardware support, accessibility, session management, networking, Bluetooth, audio, displays, power, notifications, multi-monitor support, virtual desktops, filesystem/system integration and other mature platform behaviour MUST remain available unless this specification explicitly replaces or supersedes it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where 9to1 requires a CUI.NET replacement for functionality already supplied by Ubuntu/GNOME and that 9to1 product does not already have a different authoritative donor, the latest appropriate corresponding Ubuntu/GNOME application becomes its donor. The replacement preserves applicable donor functionality and rebuilds/extends its GUI in CUI.NET. Existing explicitly assigned donors take precedence; Files, for example, retains its existing donor rather than switching to the Ubuntu file manager.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Once an authoritative 9to1 app fully replaces a donor graphical application, the duplicate donor user-facing app SHOULD be removed from the default OS image. Required lower-level libraries/services remain installed where technically necessary. The objective is functional preservation without parallel competing GUIs.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Desktop shell and Windows-style interaction model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The default 9to1-OS shell uses a familiar Windows-like desktop interaction model while retaining Linux/Ubuntu capabilities. Conventional minimise, maximise/restore and close controls, taskbar representation, window switching, context menus, system tray/status, desktop workspaces and predictable mouse/keyboard behaviour are first-class rather than hidden or intentionally omitted.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Window management and quality-of-life

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drag windows to edges/corners to preview and snap them into supported layouts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Support built-in and user-defined snap layouts, including half, thirds, quarters and custom rectangular regions with configurable gaps/margins.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provide smooth configurable window movement, open/close, minimise/restore, maximise, snapping and desktop-transition animations, with reduced-motion/disabled options.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Support conventional app/window switching, previews, multiple windows per app, virtual-desktop awareness, task-view/overview and keyboard-first operation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Support user-configurable per-app/window rules such as initial monitor, desktop, size, snap region, maximised/fullscreen and always-on-top where compatible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Linux/GTK/Qt and other compatible desktop applications remain runnable even when they are not CUI-native. They participate in the taskbar, window switching, snapping, desktops and supported system integration to the extent the underlying platform permits.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Taskbar framework

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The taskbar is a first-class highly customisable shell framework, not a fixed strip of running applications. The default layout places Go at the left/start position and system/status controls toward the end, but supported regions/items can be rearranged.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can configure edge/position, floating versus edge-attached presentation, width, thickness, margins, corner radius, padding, item spacing, alignment, opacity, blur/material, borders, shadows, icon size, labels, grouping/combining, auto-hide/intelligent hide, animations, per-monitor behaviour, clock/tray content and compatible multi-row or multiple-taskbar arrangements.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Taskbar Layers

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A taskbar instance supports between one and five independently configurable Taskbar Layers. Scrolling or a configured vertical gesture while the pointer/focus is over the taskbar moves discretely between adjacent layers and snaps to a complete layer; layers are not an infinitely scrollable strip.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every layer has stable identity, name/order, item layout, presentation and visibility settings. Layers may differ in item size, alignment, grouping, height and visual presentation where supported. A visible accessible layer-position indicator shows the current position and number of available layers; its presentation can be configured but must not rely on colour alone.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A layer can contain typed items such as pinned/running apps, individual windows, Go, system controls, quick actions, settings, files/folders, Shelf items/collections, 9to1 routes, Dulche Agents, Agent runs, Automations actions, widgets, status indicators, media controls, spacers and authorised extension-provided modules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples are illustrative rather than hard-coded: one user may create Running Apps, Quick Actions, AI Agents, Development and Personal layers. No layer type is reserved to a specific category.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Desktop Spaces, Virtual Desktops and Desktop Pages

heading: HEADING_2
text: Naming and conceptual separation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The OS-level mode system is named Desktop Spaces. The existing conversational/AI product is named LLM Spaces. Documentation, APIs and UI MUST use these distinct names to avoid ambiguity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Virtual Desktops organise sets of windows within the current shell experience. Desktop Spaces redefine the surrounding shell/interaction experience. Desktop Pages are multiple pages of desktop icons/widgets within a desktop surface. These are separate orthogonal concepts.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Desktop Spaces

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Desktop Space is a versioned shell/behaviour profile that may change taskbars, taskbar layers, Go layout, quick settings, notification presentation, window rules, widgets/overlays, input model, theme, animations, performance/resource profile, default actions and Dulche behaviour without requiring applications to restart where avoidable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: First-party examples include a Gaming Desktop Space that can replace the standard taskbar with a lightweight floating gaming pill showing configurable telemetry such as FPS/frame time, CPU/GPU/RAM/VRAM, temperature, battery/power and latency, with an expandable quick menu; and a Touch Desktop Space that increases targets/spacing and adapts window controls, Go, quick settings, gestures, keyboard integration and snapping for tablet use.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can create, duplicate, rename, reorder, import/export, sync and delete custom Desktop Spaces. Optional triggers may suggest or activate a Desktop Space based on convertible posture, controller connection, application launch, display configuration, schedule or other supported state; automatic activation behaviour is user-controlled.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Virtual Desktops

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Virtual Desktops support create/delete, names, ordering, keyboard/touchpad switching, window movement between desktops, configurable transition, task-view overview, optional per-desktop wallpaper and configurable taskbar visibility across current/all desktops.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Desktop Pages and Widgets

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each desktop surface can contain multiple ordered Desktop Pages that users may add/remove, rename, reorder and navigate by configured gesture/scroll. Pages may contain icons, files/folders, Shelf collections, shortcuts and native CUI widgets and may be global or Desktop-Space-specific according to configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Desktop widgets are first-class CUI entities with resizing, grid/free placement where enabled, ordering, transparency/background material, interaction, update policy and per-page/per-Desktop-Space presence. First-party apps can expose widgets such as Planner, Maps, Files folders, Shelf collections, media, system resources, battery, clock/calendar, quick actions, Dulche Agents and Agent-run state.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Customisation Framework

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Customisation is an architectural property of 9to1-OS. The requirement is not satisfied by wallpaper, accent colour and taskbar-position options. Stable shell behaviour and presentation that can reasonably be represented as configuration SHOULD be configurable unless doing so would materially compromise security, accessibility, compatibility or system integrity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The OS MUST expose substantially deeper supported first-party customisation than stock Windows or stock GNOME without requiring registry hacks, shell patches, unsupported extensions or third-party Start/taskbar replacements. Configuration uses versioned typed schemas and transactions so Settings, Dulche, Automations and authorised extensions operate on the same underlying state.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Configuration scopes and precedence

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Applicable settings can be scoped globally, per device, display, Desktop Space, Virtual Desktop, application/window class or input mode. The implementation MUST define deterministic precedence so a Desktop-Space/display/app override cannot unpredictably conflict with global defaults. Device/display-specific state must not be blindly synced to incompatible hardware.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Visual and behavioural scope

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mouse pointer/cursor theme, colour, size, outline/high-visibility behaviour and supported custom pointer packs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Window button order/side, visible controls, button size/spacing/shape, title alignment, titlebar height, icon/title visibility and compatible extra window actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Window corner roundness, borders, shadows, glow, transparency, active/inactive treatment and user-selectable numerical/preset radius where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Theme profiles covering light/dark/automatic mode, colours, gradients, accents, glow, blur, transparency, shadows, borders, roundness, spacing/density, typography, icons, control shapes and animation character.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Built-in visual personalities such as clean/minimal, glow, playful, glass/classic or other first-party presets act as editable starting profiles rather than locked themes; users can create custom profiles.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Icon packs, per-app icon overrides, icon scale/shape/treatment and notification-badge presentation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Global and per-category animation enablement, speed, reduced-motion and presets/custom timing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rebindable keyboard shortcuts, supported mouse/touchpad/touch/controller gestures and conflict detection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: System tray/status ordering, visibility policy, overflow, icon size/spacing, clock/date/seconds/time-zone presentation, battery percentage/remaining-time presentation and network/audio/Bluetooth/VPN indicators.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Safe application and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large shell changes SHOULD support preview/keep/revert flows. Configuration mutations are transactional where practical and the shell maintains last-known-good recovery paths including reset current element, reset taskbar, reset Desktop Space, reset appearance, restore previous configuration and safe/default shell mode.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Configuration schemas are versioned and migrations MUST preserve supported user state across OS updates rather than silently discarding a highly customised desktop.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Quick Settings and system flyouts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Quick Settings combines Windows-style desktop system controls with Android-style customisation. Users can add/remove/reorder tiles, choose supported sizes, resize tiles, use multiple pages, configure layout/density/panel placement and install authorised custom tiles.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: First-party tiles should cover relevant controls such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, airplane mode, brightness, volume/audio output, microphone, battery saver/performance mode, night light, accessibility, hotspot, VPN, display/casting, input, focus/do-not-disturb, location, screenshot/recording and Dulche/AI state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tiles are typed CUI modules that may expose live state, icon, primary/secondary labels, toggle/action, slider and expanded view. Apps/Plugins may register tiles through a permissioned contract with declared supported sizes/actions; arbitrary shell code injection is not a tile API.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Related flyouts such as audio, network, Bluetooth, calendar, battery and notification centre must provide friendly direct controls and the expected Windows-class QoL, including optional battery percentage, output-device switching, tray overflow, date/calendar, power/session controls and useful status detail.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Dulche and AI-native OS integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche is an always-available OS assistant, not merely another application. 'Always available' does not require a large model to remain permanently resident: users control model residency/background behaviour while the lightweight service remains integrated with Go AI mode, shortcuts, voice where enabled, context menus, selections, taskbar layers/widgets, notifications, Settings and first-party apps.

heading: HEADING_2
text: AI settings

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Settings contains first-class AI areas for Models/Universal Model Picker, Dulche service/background behaviour, Always-active AI, Persistent Memory and Memory Frequency, Background Learning, Agents, MCP servers, Skills/Plugins, privacy and resource policy. Built-in MCP management includes add/remove, transport/endpoint configuration, authentication, capability inspection, enable/disable, Agent/app permission assignment, health and logs/errors.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Always-active AI is a configurable service mode and MUST NOT grant blanket access to microphone, files, external services or other sensitive capabilities. Those remain separately permissioned.

heading: HEADING_2
text: AI-aware RAM optimisation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The default OS must be aggressively memory-efficient without sacrificing specified functionality or quality so local models can use more of the machine. 9to1-OS should lazy-load non-critical services/surfaces, suspend or trim eligible inactive apps, reclaim caches, use appropriate compression/zram and memory mapping, avoid duplicated runtime state and unload inactive models/compatibility environments when policy permits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can configure a managed System Memory Budget/profile such as Minimum, Balanced, Performance, AI/Maximum model capacity or Custom. This is a target for reclaimable/non-critical OS consumption rather than an unsafe hard cap on kernel/critical services.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: An optional Prioritise AI memory policy may reclaim eligible caches/background apps/models more aggressively to make room for a requested local model. Dulche/runtime should report what can be reclaimed and coordinate with the OS resource manager rather than simply failing at the first memory-pressure condition.

heading: HEADING_1
text: GUI-first administration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Common useful system-administration operations that Ubuntu frequently exposes primarily through Terminal SHOULD have first-party CUI.NET workflows wherever they can be represented safely and coherently. Terminal remains fully available for advanced/unrestricted workflows, but ordinary maintenance must not require memorising shell commands.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Software/package install, removal, update and repository/source management.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: System updates, recovery, backups/snapshots and repair.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Drivers, devices, displays, audio, networking, DNS, VPN, firewall and hotspot.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Disk/partition/filesystem management, mounts, storage cleanup and health information.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users/groups, permissions/ownership, startup/background services, scheduled jobs and environment/PATH management where appropriate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Logs/journal/crash diagnostics, process/resource management and compatibility/runtime management.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Friendly GUIs should call stable typed system services/APIs rather than merely concatenate opaque shell strings. Where a shell tool is the only practical backend, arguments must be structured, privilege requirements declared and output/errors/progress handled safely.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Terminal safety and privileged destructive operations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Terminal Command Mode includes a Dangerous Command Guard that parses known commands/arguments/targets and classifies risk rather than relying only on substring matching. Potentially major irreversible operations such as destructive recursive deletion, filesystem formatting, partition-table mutation, mass permission changes or dangerous system/boot-path modification require OS-mediated protection.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: For a Dangerous operation the mandatory sequence is consequence-specific warning -> trusted user authentication -> second consequence-specific confirmation -> execution. Authentication is never treated as final consent. The warning should identify resolved targets and expected consequence where feasible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terminal AI Mode, Dulche, Agents, Plugins and Automations cannot type the password, approve their own warning or bypass the final confirmation. Script/program execution cannot be perfectly predicted; recognised dangerous privileged operations should still pass through the system safety broker where technically possible, without claiming semantic proof over arbitrary executable code.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Multiple users and administrator policy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-OS supports multiple isolated user accounts/profiles with standard and administrator roles, secure per-user data/settings/secrets, fast switching/sign-out and clearly scoped system-wide versus user-specific configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Administrators can create managed policy profiles for family, school, organisation or kiosk-style deployments. Policies can control application allow/deny lists, package/app installation, external providers, Plugins/MCP, Terminal/admin access, removable storage, networking/VPN, Desktop Space/customisation options, web/content controls where supported, update policy and other security-sensitive capabilities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A School profile can, for example, block launching unapproved applications and prevent the restricted user from disabling that policy without administrator authentication. Enforcement MUST occur below the normal app UI so renaming a binary, launching through Go/Terminal/Shelf or invoking an Agent does not trivially bypass policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Managed restrictions must be visible and attributable ('Managed by administrator/school policy') rather than presented as broken UI. Administrators require auditability of policy changes and clear recovery controls; administration must not silently expose another user's private content unless an explicit policy/capability legitimately grants that access.

heading: HEADING_1
text: First-party apps and deep OS integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All release-scope first-party 9to1 applications are installed by default as part of the complete 9to1-OS experience, while application updates are independently deliverable from full OS updates. A central update/package service handles discovery, automatic/manual updates, integrity checks, history, repair and supported rollback instead of every app shipping a private updater.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: First-party apps MUST behave as native OS components and register applicable typed integration with Go, Automations, Dulche, notifications, taskbar/layers, Desktop Spaces, widgets, system search/indexing, Files/open-with/default apps, share/clipboard/drag-drop, URI routes, permissions, External App Integrations, background tasks, crash/System Log, updates, backup/recovery, theming/accessibility and resource management.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Automations is a particularly strong integration requirement: apps should expose supported typed triggers/actions/events through the shared Automation framework rather than implementing incompatible private automation engines.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: First-party apps should expose lifecycle information allowing safe trim/suspend/resume under memory pressure without losing unsaved work. Desktop Spaces own shell layout/presentation; apps contribute declared widgets/actions/status rather than taking arbitrary control of the shell.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Setup and first-run experience

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-OS MUST provide a friendly graphical CUI.NET installer and first-run/OOBE experience. A normal installation MUST NOT require interacting with the traditional Linux text/terminal installer or memorising shell commands. Advanced/technical options may be exposed through expandable UI without making them mandatory for ordinary users.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The setup flow should cover applicable language/region, keyboard, accessibility from the first screen, networking, installation target/disk choices, encryption, timezone, user creation and administrator role, optional managed school/organisation setup, privacy/telemetry choices, update preferences, restore from an existing 9to1 backup/profile, initial appearance/Desktop-Space choices and optional Dulche/model/provider onboarding.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Installation progress is staged and truthful. Failures expose actionable explanation, retry/back navigation where safe, logs/technical details and recovery rather than dropping users into an unexplained terminal. Critical-stage failure MUST NOT be presented as successful installation.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Recovery environments

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-OS provides a custom CUI recovery environment designed for ordinary users. It should expose Continue/boot normally, automatic startup repair, restore a previous healthy snapshot, undo the latest system update, safe mode, package/system repair, filesystem/disk checks, disable problematic drivers or shell extensions, recover/reset shell configuration, inspect System Log, backup/restore, advanced Terminal and supported repair/reinstall-with-data-preservation flows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The custom 9to1 Recovery environment supplements rather than replaces the underlying Ubuntu/Linux recovery environment. The stock/default recovery path MUST remain available as an emergency fallback if the custom CUI recovery environment is damaged or cannot launch.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The custom and stock recovery paths must obey the existing boot-safety contract: ordinary snapshot restore, repair and rollback do not rewrite firmware or bootloader code. Any bootloader/firmware update is a separate tightly guarded operation.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Setup/recovery acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A normal user can install, create an account, configure basic hardware/privacy choices and reach the desktop without Terminal.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Accessibility and technical details are available during setup rather than only after installation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Recovery provides friendly repair/rollback tools, while the lower-level Ubuntu/Linux recovery environment remains independently reachable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Installer/recovery failures preserve diagnostic information and do not falsely report success or silently perform bootloader/firmware rewrites.

heading: HEADING_1
text: System updates, recovery and backups

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: System maintenance has a first-party CUI Settings workflow for checking, downloading, scheduling and installing OS updates, viewing changelogs/details, restart requirements, progress, failure/retry and update history. Terminal/package-manager commands remain optional advanced interfaces, never the required normal update path.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consequential system updates use verified recoverable system snapshots/rollback state where technically feasible. The system should confirm successful boot/health before retiring rollback state and provide a friendly recovery environment with restore previous snapshot, repair OS/package database, safe mode, diagnostic logs and extension/driver disablement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordinary backup/snapshot restoration and update rollback MUST NOT overwrite or restore firmware or bootloader code as part of the rollback transaction. Bootloader/firmware updates, if ever necessary, are separate tightly guarded operations with their own compatibility/recovery process so a normal failed OS update is not turned into a bricked device.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Software and package management

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-OS includes a friendly CUI graphical package manager with search, categories, source/publisher, version, architecture, size, installed/update state, screenshots/metadata where available, dependency/permission information and install/update/uninstall/repair workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The package manager uses typed PackageProvider adapters for applicable Linux package ecosystems such as Ubuntu/Debian packages, Flatpak, Snap if retained and coherent AppImage handling, plus Winget for supported Windows/Wine scenarios and 9to1 package sources. It may show multiple sources for the same product and explain meaningful differences instead of silently choosing an arbitrary provider.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: PackageProvider contracts define search, metadata, versions, install/update/uninstall, dependencies, progress, source trust, errors and capability limitations so additional providers can integrate without rewriting the package-manager UI.

heading: HEADING_1
text: System diagnostics and storage management

heading: HEADING_2
text: System Log and crash diagnostics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-OS includes a CUI System Log surface that translates underlying journal/service/app events into useful searchable/filterable diagnostics while retaining advanced technical detail. Events can expose timestamp, component/process, severity, subsystem, version/build, crash ID, stack/debug data where available and related logs/actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Crash records should group repeated failures, support export/diagnostic bundles and permit user-authorised Dulche analysis such as explaining why a component repeatedly crashed. Diagnostic information MUST NOT be silently uploaded.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Disk Management

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Settings includes CUI Disk Management covering physical disks, partitions, filesystems, mounts, labels, free/used space, removable storage, format/partition operations, encryption state, filesystem checks and SMART/health data where supported. Destructive operations require clear device identification and appropriate confirmation/authentication.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Task Manager and other donor-backed utilities

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Task Manager is rebuilt in CUI.NET using the appropriate Ubuntu/GNOME system-monitor tooling as donor baseline unless another donor is explicitly assigned. It preserves mature process/resource functionality and extends it with Windows-style usability plus 9to1-specific visibility for models, Agents, containers/compatibility environments and relevant GPU/RAM usage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The same donor fallback rule applies to Settings and other required CUI system utilities when an appropriate Ubuntu/GNOME app exists and no different donor has already been assigned.

heading: HEADING_1
text: 9to1-OS acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ubuntu/GNOME mature non-replaced functionality is preserved while the authoritative user-facing shell/system GUIs are CUI.NET and duplicate replaced donor apps are removed from the default image.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The taskbar is deeply customisable and supports one to five discrete snapping layers with a visible accessible layer indicator.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Desktop Spaces, Virtual Desktops, Desktop Pages and LLM Spaces remain explicitly separate concepts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The shell supports deep first-party customisation of taskbar, Go, Quick Settings, pointer, window chrome/roundness, themes, widgets, desktops, gestures, tray/status, animations and scoped per-device/display/Desktop-Space/app behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Dulche, MCP, models and AI-aware memory/resource controls are first-class OS settings and Dulche is always available without requiring a heavyweight model to remain loaded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Common administration has friendly CUI workflows and Dangerous Terminal operations use warning -> authentication -> final confirmation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Multiple users and enforceable administrator-managed profiles can restrict unapproved apps and other capabilities without trivial bypass through alternate launch surfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All first-party 9to1 apps ship installed by default, update independently and integrate deeply with shared OS services including Automations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: System updates have GUI installation, verified recovery/rollback mechanisms and ordinary rollback does not rewrite firmware/bootloader code.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A friendly multi-provider package manager, System Log/crash diagnostics, Disk Management and donor-backed Task Manager/Settings are present as first-class CUI system utilities.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Go

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Go is the universal Start/search/action surface for 9to1-OS. It combines the roles of a Windows-style Start menu, system-wide search, application launcher and contextual quick-action surface. Go is an OS primitive, not a separate heavyweight application, and the default taskbar places Go at the left/start position.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Default surface

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening Go without a query presents a customisable home surface that can contain Pinned items, Recent items, Suggested/contextual items, All Apps, recent files/projects, quick system actions, account/session controls and power controls. Users can reorder, hide, resize or regroup supported sections and choose compact search-first, Start-menu-like or larger dashboard-oriented layouts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All Apps is a first-class Go view containing installed applications/programs available to the current user/profile. It is separate from the Android-style Launcher app drawer. Go is the primary application-launcher replacement for the 9to1-OS desktop shell.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Search and AI modes

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Go provides a Search / AI switcher. Search is deterministic universal search/navigation; AI routes natural-language intent through Dulche while using the same canonical Go providers and typed OS/app actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Examples of AI-mode requests include opening the project the user was working on, finding the setting that controls display scaling, launching a group of development tools or locating notes by context. AI mode MUST NOT fabricate applications, files, settings or entities that do not exist and MUST surface ambiguity when multiple plausible targets remain.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Universal provider model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Applications, frameworks and authorised extensions register typed GoProviders rather than requiring Go to hard-code product-specific databases. Providers may expose search, suggestions, recent items, result categories, previews, aliases, quick actions, indexing/change notifications and query-time-only results.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Go may search applications, files/folders, settings, people/contacts, LLM Spaces/conversations where authorised, Boards, Planner tasks/events, Maps places, Shelf items/collections, Stack repositories/branches, Dev projects, browser history/bookmarks where enabled, installed tools, Plugins/extensions and registered system actions.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Canonical identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Go returns references to canonical entities owned by their source application/framework. Its local index may cache identifiers, search fields, aliases, presentation metadata, permissions and freshness state, but MUST NOT create a competing canonical copy of a file, document, project, place, person or other result merely because it is searchable.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Ranking and context

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ranking may combine exact/prefix/fuzzy match, aliases, keywords, recency, frequency, pins/favourites, current app, active project, current canonical object, Desktop Space, user-enabled Background Learning and provider relevance. Context can change ranking and available actions but never bypass access controls or change the canonical identity of a result.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Typed actions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Results can expose owner-provided typed actions such as Open, Reveal, Share, Navigate, New window, Pin, Create, Toggle, Open with or app-specific commands. Go may invoke these actions directly where appropriate but MUST NOT reproduce another app's private business logic.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Consequential actions remain subject to the underlying OS/app permission and confirmation requirements. Go and Dulche cannot use a quick-action surface to bypass security prompts.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Filters and previews

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Go supports optional user-selectable filters/categories such as Apps, Files, People, Settings, Places, Projects and Actions plus provider-defined categories where useful. Results may expose compact CUI previews supplied from canonical provider data.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Indexing, privacy and freshness

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Providers declare whether they are locally indexed, queried live or hybrid. They can push changed entities, invalidate deleted entities and request re-indexing. Search results MUST be permission-filtered before display, including for restricted folders/projects, managed user profiles and lock-screen contexts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can disable sensitive providers/categories such as browser history, message contents or private project indexing. Stale/offline remote results must be marked with their freshness state and invalid/deleted results removed rather than accumulating as zombie entries.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Scoped reuse

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The same Go framework may be embedded as a scoped picker/search surface in Launcher, Files, Shelf and other apps, and Dulche may query Go for authorised entity discovery. These are scoped views over the same provider contracts, not separate incompatible search engines.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Performance and failure isolation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening Go should be effectively immediate. Local providers should stream results incrementally; slow remote providers MUST NOT block applications, local files, settings or cached results. Failure of one provider is isolated and reported only for that provider.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Go acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Go acts as the primary 9to1-OS Start menu, universal search and quick-action surface, with Go at the default left/start taskbar position.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pinned, Recent, Suggested and All Apps views are first-class and deeply customisable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search and AI modes use the same canonical entity/provider/action contracts; AI mode cannot hallucinate unavailable entities.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Search results remain permission-filtered canonical references rather than duplicate Go-owned objects.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Provider failures and remote latency do not block local search/launch functionality.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Universal Model Picker

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: On 9to1-OS, the Universal Model Picker is the OS-hosted presentation of the same canonical Dulche/Home model/provider state used by regular 9to1. Model identities, provider connections, ordered Model Routes, active/background routing, category overrides, fallbacks, permissions and usage state MUST remain interoperable across Home and 9to1-OS rather than becoming separate OS-only configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The OS picker provides the same compact selection experience plus deeper integration with Settings → AI, system resource management, administrator policy and local-model lifecycle. It can expose local/cloud/remote identity, capabilities, reasoning/effort controls, aliases/nicknames, route order, fallback state, locality/privacy, loading/residency, RAM/VRAM fit and per-app/Agent/Desktop-Space overrides.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-OS may host the picker natively while Windows regular 9to1 hosts it through Home, but both clients MUST read/write the same versioned routing contracts and Dulche model catalogue. A route configured in Home remains meaningful on 9to1-OS subject to device-local model availability, provider authentication, administrator policy and device-specific resource constraints.

heading: HEADING_2
text: OS resource and policy integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: When a selected local model requires additional memory, the picker integrates with the 9to1-OS resource broker to show required/available/reclaimable RAM/VRAM and may request permitted reclamation before declaring the model unavailable. It MUST distinguish Installed, Unloaded, Loading, Loaded, Offloaded/Partially loaded where supported and Unavailable due to resources.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Administrator-managed user profiles can restrict allowed models/providers, cloud use, model acquisition and routing fallback. Model ordering MUST never bypass those restrictions; policy-ineligible candidates are filtered before route selection.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Shared-routing invariant

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordered model fallback is a shared 9to1 capability, not an OS-specific behaviour. Requests from regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use the same eligibility-first routing semantics: determine required capabilities and policy constraints, filter the configured route, then choose the highest-priority eligible available model and fall through only on classified model/provider-routing conditions.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Wine/WinBoat Framework

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Wine/WinBoat Framework is the unified 9to1-OS compatibility platform for non-native application packages. It provides one coherent installation, routing, execution, lifecycle, permissions, diagnostics and shell-integration model across Windows applications and Android APK applications rather than exposing Wine, VM/container tooling or an Android runtime as unrelated expert-only subsystems.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Compatibility backends

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A CompatibilityBackend is a typed implementation capable of installing/running one or more foreign application formats. Required backend classes include a Wine-compatible Windows runtime, a WinBoat-style Windows environment for applications needing a fuller Windows VM/container context, and an APK/Android compatibility layer for Android applications. Additional compatible backends MAY be registered later through the same framework.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The compatibility manager owns stable entities such as CompatibilityApp, CompatibilityPackage, CompatibilityBackend, CompatibilityEnvironment, CompatibilityRoute, AppRoutingRule, CompatibilityPermissionSet, CompatibilityHealth and CompatibilitySnapshot or equivalent contracts. Applications are identified by stable package/application identity rather than by the pathname of the installer that originally created them.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Automatic package routing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening or double-clicking a supported foreign application package MUST route through the compatibility framework automatically. Executable/package type should be determined from trusted file metadata/signature/MIME inspection where available rather than relying only on filename extension.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows .exe/.msi and equivalent supported installers are routed to an eligible Windows backend. Android .apk packages are routed to an eligible APK/Android compatibility backend. The normal user experience is Install/Open application, not manually invoking wine, configuring a prefix, running Docker/Podman/QEMU/RDP commands or issuing Android runtime commands in Terminal.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The router evaluates package type, known application identity, architecture, backend capability, existing environments, administrator policy, resource requirements, compatibility knowledge and user defaults. When there is one clear eligible default, routing should proceed without unnecessary questions. When multiple viable frameworks exist or the user requests control, the UI may ask which framework/backend to use.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Per-application framework defaults

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can set a preferred/default CompatibilityBackend for each installed application or recognised application identity. A chooser can provide an explicit 'Always use this framework for this app' action. This preference is stored against stable app/package identity and survives moves/renames of the original installer.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A per-app default does not override hard incompatibility, missing backend capability, administrator policy or unavailable hardware. If the selected backend cannot satisfy the app, the framework reports why and may offer other eligible backends rather than silently executing through an unrelated path.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users can change/reset the backend association later from the application's compatibility settings. Global defaults may exist for Windows packages and APK packages, but per-app rules take precedence where valid.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Windows: Wine path

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Wine backend manages Wine runtime/version, isolated prefixes/environments, application architecture, DLL/runtime dependencies, graphics/DirectX translation, environment variables, registry integration, drive mappings, fonts, file associations, launch arguments and per-app overrides through CUI.NET management surfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Ordinary users MUST NOT need to manually run winecfg, winetricks, edit registry state or construct WINEPREFIX environment variables. Advanced views may expose equivalent controls and raw technical details when useful.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Applications SHOULD normally use isolated managed Wine environments so dependency/runtime changes, repair, backup and uninstall do not corrupt unrelated apps. Applications may deliberately share an environment when required, but that relationship must be explicit.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Windows: WinBoat-style environment path

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The WinBoat-style backend provides a managed Windows VM/container environment for applications that need or work better with a fuller Windows installation. It may expose configurable CPU, RAM, storage, hardware acceleration, networking, shared folders, USB/device passthrough, graphics configuration and individual-app/RemoteApp-style window integration where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The management experience hides Docker/Podman, QEMU, VM orchestration and RDP implementation details during normal use while retaining advanced diagnostics. Individual Windows applications should appear as normal 9to1-OS windows where technically possible; a full Windows desktop remains available as a fallback/advanced mode.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Android/APK compatibility path

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1-OS MUST support Android APK applications through the same Compatibility Framework using an Android/APK compatibility layer. Installing an APK creates/registers a normal CompatibilityApp backed by the Android runtime rather than placing Android apps in a disconnected secondary launcher.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The APK backend is responsible for Android runtime/container lifecycle, package installation/update/removal, Android package identity, architecture/ABI compatibility, graphics acceleration, display/window integration, storage mappings, networking, clipboard, audio, microphone/camera, notifications, input, orientation, intents/file associations and other host bridges where supported.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Android applications should participate in Go, taskbar/taskbar layers, window switching, Desktop Spaces, notifications, Files/open-with/share flows, Shelf and other applicable 9to1-OS integrations. The Android compatibility layer MUST NOT require the user to launch a separate Android desktop merely to start an installed APK unless a full Android environment is explicitly requested.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If multiple APK-compatible runtimes/backends are available, the same automatic eligibility and per-app default framework rules apply. The user may choose a backend and persist it for that Android app; otherwise 9to1 selects the highest-priority eligible configured default.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Unified installation experience

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening a supported .exe, .msi, .apk or other registered foreign package invokes a single compatibility installation flow showing detected application/package identity, recommended backend, destination environment, required permissions, storage/resource estimate and relevant compatibility warnings. Advanced settings expose backend-specific controls without requiring them for a normal install.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The GUI package manager may also install Windows software through Winget or other approved Windows sources and Android packages through approved configured package sources where supported. Package-source discovery does not bypass administrator policy, signing/trust requirements or compatibility permissions.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Native-feeling OS integration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Foreign applications remain subject to the same shell/platform integration expectations as native applications wherever technically possible: Go search/launch, taskbar and layers, Desktop Spaces, snapping, app switching, tray/status integration, Files/open-with, default associations, clipboard, drag/drop, audio/microphone, printing, notifications, shortcuts, recent items, System Log/crash diagnostics and resource management.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compatibility apps may expose Automations/Dulche actions only through typed supported bridges. Running inside Wine, a Windows VM or an Android runtime does not give an application unrestricted access to the host Automation framework or other 9to1 capabilities.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Filesystem and host permissions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Host folder exposure is explicit and revocable. Compatibility environments receive only user/admin-authorised Files locations rather than unrestricted access to the entire Linux home directory by default. Shared-folder mappings identify the canonical host location and the guest-visible mapping.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Clipboard, microphone, camera, USB/devices, network modes, location and other sensitive bridges use the normal 9to1 permission/policy system where applicable. A locally running foreign application is not automatically trusted with unrestricted host resources.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Graphics, gaming and input

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The framework exposes backend-appropriate GPU acceleration, Vulkan/DirectX translation, discrete/integrated GPU preference, fullscreen, controller/input support and relevant compatibility/performance settings. Windows or Android games can integrate with Gaming Desktop Space telemetry/controls where the backend exposes the required data.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Resource and lifecycle management

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CompatibilityEnvironment lifecycle states include at least Starting, Running, Suspended, Stopped, Degraded/Error and backend-specific transitional states. The framework reports allocated and actual RAM/CPU/storage/GPU usage where available and participates in 9to1-OS memory/resource policy so idle VM/container environments can be suspended or stopped according to user policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compatibility environments must preserve application/user state safely across suspend/resume and OS memory pressure. The OS MUST NOT simply terminate a managed environment and discard unsaved guest/application state to satisfy a memory target.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Snapshots, repair and updates

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Backends supporting snapshots/checkpoints should expose them through the unified manager, particularly before major guest/runtime changes. Compatibility snapshots are separate from 9to1-OS system snapshots.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The framework manages or coordinates updates for Wine/runtime components, WinBoat-derived host integration, Android compatibility/runtime components and guest-integration tooling. Guest Windows/Android update behaviour remains explicit and must not be confused with host OS updates.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Repair/reset operations should be scoped to the selected app/environment and preserve unrelated environments. Destructive reset/uninstall flows explain whether app data, shared environment state or snapshots will be removed.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Diagnostics and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The CUI compatibility manager normalises common failures such as missing Wine dependency, application crash, graphics translation failure, Windows guest boot failure, RemoteApp disconnection, Android runtime failure, incompatible APK ABI, insufficient RAM, unavailable hardware acceleration, broken shared folder or package-install failure into actionable health states.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Advanced diagnostics expose underlying Wine/runtime/VM/RDP/Android logs and environment details through System Log integration. Dulche may analyse these diagnostics and invoke typed repair/configuration APIs but should not replace a supported manager operation with arbitrary host shell automation.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Managed-user policy

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Administrator policies can disable foreign-app compatibility entirely, restrict allowed backends, block arbitrary .exe/.msi/.apk installation, allowlist approved applications/package identities, restrict package sources such as Winget/Android sources, constrain host-folder/device/network bridges and lock per-app backend choices.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Launching through Go, Files, Shelf, Terminal, Dulche or another app MUST NOT bypass the same compatibility policy. Policy enforcement occurs in the routing/install/execution broker below the launch surface.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Compatibility Framework acceptance requirements

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Double-clicking/opening a supported Windows installer/executable or Android APK automatically enters the unified compatibility routing flow rather than requiring Terminal.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Wine, WinBoat-style Windows environments and APK/Android compatibility are represented as typed backends under one manager.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The user may choose among eligible frameworks and can persist a default framework per application; valid per-app defaults are remembered and editable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Installed Windows and Android applications integrate with Go, taskbar/window management, Desktop Spaces, Files, notifications, diagnostics and resource policy wherever technically possible.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Host files/devices and sensitive bridges remain explicit permission boundaries, not blanket compatibility-environment access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Administrator policy applies regardless of which launch surface or compatibility backend is used.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Backend-specific complexity remains available for advanced users but is not required for ordinary installation, launch, repair or troubleshooting.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
TITLE
text: Pass 2: Terra-form

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_1
text: Pass 2 operating contract

heading: HEADING_2
text: Pass identity and model

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Terra-form is the codename for this development pass only. It MUST NOT be interpreted as a model family, capability tier or instruction to use a model named Terra. All Terra-form implementation workers and the coordinator MUST use GPT-6.1 Sol wherever model selection is configurable. The intended execution shape is six parallel implementation workers plus the coordinator unless an external concurrency limit temporarily prevents it.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Hard deadline and outcome

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: By 21:00 Europe/London on 3 October 2026, the entire 9to1 application and OS MUST be feature-complete against the full active specification including the Terra-form tranche below, integrated, validated against the specification's required acceptance tests, and usable at release-level quality. The deadline does not permit fake implementations, hidden stubs, skipped required tests, weakened permission/security boundaries or silent regressions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Pre-pass baseline, merge and user test drop

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before Terra-form feature implementation begins, the final accepted Astra la Vista head MUST complete its exact-head acceptance, then be merged into main while preserving history. Do not squash, force-push, destructively reset or discard accepted evidence. The resulting main commit is the Terra-form baseline.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before the pass begins, build usable test artifacts for every currently shippable 9to1 product or platform target and deliver clearly named copies to the user's local PC. Include a manifest mapping each product to its artifact path, version, exact commit, cryptographic hash, platform/runtime requirements and launch instructions, plus a concise known-limitations record. An artifact that has not passed its required build/launch acceptance MUST be labelled honestly rather than represented as release-ready. User testing and feedback from this drop becomes a priority defect stream during Terra-form.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Scope expansion

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All mandatory requirements from the existing specification remain in scope and MUST NOT regress. The previously deferred Files organisation, Link, Prototype, Paths, Replay and Variants tranche below is now mandatory Terra-form scope. There is no generic Future or out-of-scope escape hatch for these named features. Only concepts explicitly left OPEN, such as the separate Playgrounds naming/product question, remain non-committal unless the user explicitly expands scope again.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
HEADING_2
text: Implementation and evidence contract

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: At pass start, regenerate a requirement-by-requirement index from the entire authoritative specification and this Terra-form tranche. Track every requirement as VERIFIED, IMPLEMENTED-UNVERIFIED, MISSING or BLOCKED. A source file, authored test, worker statement or isolated draft does not establish completion. Completed cohorts MUST be integrated continuously through bounded source capture, owning tests, regression/resource/native checks where applicable, accepted-root integration and exact-head CI rather than saved for a final mega-merge.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a named Terra-form feature needs a low-level format or interface that is not explicitly specified, choose the narrowest coherent shipping contract consistent with the product behaviour below, document that decision and validate it. An unspecified technical detail is not permission to invent an additional product, weaken canonical ownership/permissions, or defer the named feature to another pass.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Android and Go release rule

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Full Android/Go parity remains the target. If time is genuinely critical near the 21:00 deadline, complex newly added Terra-form surfaces MAY temporarily ship on Android/Go as responsive read-only or limited-editing experiences provided their canonical data formats, permissions and navigation remain compatible and all existing Android/Go functionality continues to work. Full authoring parity then continues overnight. This fallback does not apply to existing features that already had stronger mobile requirements.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Release exit gate

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
