text: Terra-form is complete only when every in-scope feature is implemented and reachable through normal user-facing navigation; no demo-only or stub path stands in for production behaviour; required specification acceptance suites are green; required native, device and provider paths have been exercised; accessibility, performance, reliability, recovery and failure behaviour meet the specification; production authentication/backend integration works; release packages build, install and run cleanly; and the final evidence ledger shows effectively 100% verified coverage. If a genuine external prerequisite prevents one item, isolate and report that blocker explicitly while completing everything else.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Terra-form product and interaction contract

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-01 — Scope, terminology and ownership

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All requirements in this section are active Pass 2 shipping requirements, in addition to the full existing specification and the operating contract above. This is one consolidated specification: product definitions, UI behaviour, data rules, APIs and acceptance criteria below describe the same required implementation. Earlier terminology is not an alternative implementation path.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files owns ten native organisation types: Folder, Project, Sheet, Tree, Smart, Timeline, Pipeline, Catalogue, Stash and Matrix. They are not ten separate applications. Link owns two authored document types: Flow and Binder. Sheet belongs to Files, not Link. Binder is the interconnected document previously called Flow; Flow now means the continuous reading document defined below. Prototype replaces the proposed name Models. Stash is the ordered collection. Variants is an integrated capability, not an app or Files organisation type. Project retains its Files meaning and MUST NOT silently become a separate Projects app.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files owns storage, canonical file identity, providers, contextual organisation metadata, sync and filesystem operations. Link, Prototype, Paths and Replay own their respective semantic document/session models. Existing owning apps retain authority over embedded originals and app-specific edits. The distinction MUST be visible in the interface: arranging a file, editing that file, editing an authored block and creating an independent copy are different operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The new surfaces MUST reuse CUI, Home services, the Shared Productivity Engine, the registered preview/editor system and the Node Graph Framework for their applicable capabilities. Domain-specific nodes and objects extend those shared contracts; they MUST NOT create competing permission brokers, generic content-merge engines or parallel implementations of the same shared object. Existing donor-backed apps retain their donor-parity requirements. This section does not select an additional donor, paid dependency, external hosting service or overlapping product.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-02 — Shared UI, navigation and authoring behaviour

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Link, Prototype, Paths and Replay MUST have functional launch screens: New, Open/import, Recent, Pinned, Shared with Me and search, backed by real artifacts and permissions. Link offers New Flow and New Binder; Prototype offers New Prototype; Paths offers New Path; Replay offers New capture and Open Replay. Templates use the existing template registry when compatible templates are available; an empty registry shows an honest empty state, not fictitious sample projects. Opening a specific artifact bypasses the launch screen. Returning Home MUST preserve saved work and session state.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each editor MUST have a clear title/location area, save/sync state, history access, share controls and an explicit distinction between authoring and viewing/running. Use a compact contextual command bar, a central work area, a collapsible navigation/outline or asset panel where required below, and an inspector for the current selection. Tools belong near the relevant work, not in a permanent wall of unrelated forms. Panels MUST be resizable or collapsible, preserve useful user preferences and leave a usable work area at smaller sizes. A Properties panel MUST not be the only way to perform ordinary creation, navigation or editing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Use the existing CUI typography, theme tokens, spacing, focus, menus, dialogs, tooltips, icons and persistent contextual AI bar. Labels MUST use the names in TF-01. Theme changes, reduced motion, contrast settings and scaling MUST apply to the actual editor, embedded content chrome and pop-ups. Product controls MUST not expose development jargon such as raw schema IDs, worker status or implementation notes as their ordinary labels. IDs and diagnostics belong in details/developer surfaces.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pointer selection, multiple selection, keyboard focus, context menus, clipboard operations, undo/redo, rename and delete MUST follow the owning app and shared engine conventions. Provide visible menu/button alternatives to drag-only, hover-only and shortcut-only actions. Text-entry focus MUST prevent a canvas shortcut from deleting an object or moving the viewport while the user is typing. Selection and contextual toolbars MUST identify the active object and the scope of the next action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spatial surfaces MUST provide pan, zoom, fit-to-content, fit-to-selection and an accessible outline/list alternative. They MUST distinguish moving an item from panning the surface and selecting an object from opening it. Authoring mode supports selection handles and explicit Open/Edit actions; reader mode allows direct activation of openable items. Touch input MUST distinguish tap, long-press and drag, and provide a visible alternative to context menus. Moving between an overview, a child container and a document MUST preserve the relevant selection, scroll/zoom position and navigation history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Inline and pop-up editors MUST visibly identify the source document and whether edits affect the original. Pop-ups require a title, Close, Open in owning app and permission/save state, plus Back or breadcrumbs when navigating within a nested container. Closing returns focus and the surrounding view to the originating item. Escape closes the innermost dismissible surface, not an unrelated outer editor; modal surfaces use the shared focus/inert contract. Dismissal MUST NOT discard uncommitted edits. Where a full-screen mobile view replaces a desktop pop-up, Back returns to the same contextual location.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All surfaces MUST distinguish Loading, Empty, No matching results, Read-only, Offline/unavailable, Permission denied, Unsupported capability, Missing source, Saving, Saved, Unsynced changes and Conflict where applicable. An empty state provides the relevant first action. A failed operation keeps the existing work intact, identifies the affected item and offers an appropriate retry, resolve or return action. A loading placeholder MUST NOT replace a recoverable draft or falsely represent an empty document.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-03 — Common data, source references and recovery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every organisation object, document, authored block, placement, relationship, section, step, event, checkpoint and variant MUST have stable identity at its owning scope. Names, row positions, coordinates and file paths MUST NOT be identity keys. Persist content/layout separately from per-user viewport, panel state and reading position. Format/schema versions, current/base revision, owner, storage location and permission references MUST survive save, reopen, sync and export/import through the supported native route.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A source reference MUST identify the canonical file/artifact, owning app, optional stable sub-object/section selector and revision policy. Ordinary references follow the current authorised source by default; an explicitly pinned revision and every Replay checkpoint identify a specific historical revision. Repeated appearances MAY have different local layout or labels while referring to the same original. Renaming or moving a source MUST NOT detach references. Deleting a selected source section produces a visible missing-section state; the app MUST NOT silently substitute the whole document or a different section.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Access to a container or composed document MUST NOT grant access to its sources. Recheck source permissions when resolving previews, opening, editing, exporting, sharing, searching and providing AI context. Inaccessible references appear as locked/redacted placeholders without leaking prohibited names, thumbnails, counts or content. Missing, offline and denied states MUST remain distinguishable only to the extent the caller is entitled to know them. A share dialog MUST explain that referenced originals may require separate access; changing their grants is a separate explicit action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Removing an appearance, connection or authored block removes that contextual object only. Deleting an original invokes the owning Files/app operation and its confirmation, Trash and recovery rules. Duplicating a placement or composed document preserves references by default; duplicating source content requires a separately labelled Make independent copy action, appropriate rights and an explicit destination. The UI MUST preview the difference before a consequential operation. Undo/redo MUST act on the same semantic operation and respect current revisions; it MUST NOT reverse unrelated collaborators' changes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Mutations MUST be validated and committed atomically at the smallest user-visible boundary using stable operation identity and expected/base revisions. Real-time updates and offline journals inherit the existing Files and owning-app contracts. Concurrent incompatible edits produce recoverable conflicts, not silent last-write-wins. Invalid edits preserve the last valid state and the recoverable draft. Save failure MUST remain visible until durability is established. Content and referenced assets MUST not be evicted while they are the only unsynced copy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Native export/import MUST preserve the organisation/document structure, supported authored objects, reference identities, revision policies and required dependency manifest. References are not silently flattened or copied. Portable exports that include source bytes require the source's export/copy permissions and MUST explain the resulting independent disclosure. Unsupported/missing dependencies remain explicit. Import validates schemas, quotas, references and permissions before commit and resolves identity collisions without overwriting existing artifacts. Static export is separately labelled and MUST disclose lost interaction; it is never a substitute for the native artifact.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Files — native organisation types

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F01 — Shared Files organisation shell and operations

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The existing donor-parity Files sidebar, tabs, Back/Forward, breadcrumbs/address bar, toolbar, selection, previews, location management and grid/list/details views remain the shell. The New menu MUST expose the ten organisation types at compatible locations, alongside existing native document creation. Creation asks for type, name and storage/backing location, then opens an immediately usable empty organisation. A provider lacking native metadata MAY use the existing Files-owned metadata capability; unsupported storage or write permissions MUST be explained before creation rather than falling back to an ordinary folder without consent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every non-Folder type is a first-class versioned Files organisation object with a stable Files item identity, type, storage location, settings and local membership/layout records. A membership records its stable membership/placement ID, target FileID/FolderID or organisation ID and any type-specific section/stage/cell/order data. Contextual membership is not a second filesystem parent. New files created from a virtual view use an explicit Files destination, initially the organisation's configured backing location; the location MUST be inspectable/changeable before creation. The owning app creates the file, and Files then adds its appearance. An external file is imported through the normal transfer flow before a new managed reference is committed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Organisation commands MUST include Add existing, New item, Rename, Open, Open in new tab/window, Show original location, Properties, Share, view/layout settings, Remove from this organisation and the separately labelled original-file delete action when permitted. Supported bulk actions show the selected scope and partial-success results. Dragging an existing item into a contextual collection adds a reference by default; the drop indicator MUST state Add reference, Move original, Copy original or Reorder as appropriate. The default MUST NOT unexpectedly move or duplicate source bytes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All organisation types MUST support nesting with every other type, including ordinary folders, subject only to explicit provider capabilities and coherent containment rules. Nested organisation objects are openable as units, not flattened into their parents. Owned containment MUST be acyclic; reference resolution MUST detect recursion and avoid infinite expansion. Smart query results MUST not recursively ingest their own collection. A relationship that cannot be represented safely is rejected with its reason and an alternative, not silently converted to a different type.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A normal folder-style contents view MUST be available for every specialised type without converting its data. Changing the view does not erase sections, coordinates, relationships, filters, stages, metadata or ordering. View choice and viewport are per-user preferences; authored layout and collection settings are shared document state. Tree retains its stricter editor-only visual mode. Breadcrumbs MUST distinguish a contextual section/group from an actual filesystem folder, and Show original location MUST resolve the canonical storage location.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F02 — Folder

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Folder remains an ordinary filesystem/location hierarchy with its existing donor behaviours, sorting, grouping, views, folder colours, navigation, permissions and file operations. The new organisation types MUST NOT reinterpret existing folders, add mandatory grouping metadata or replace normal move/copy semantics. Files can store a new organisation object within a folder, and a contextual collection can reference a folder without creating a second physical parent.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Folder acceptance MUST verify ordinary create, rename, move, copy, delete/restore, colour, sort and nested navigation before and after adding organisation objects. A normal folder opened from a Project, Tree or Matrix MUST still behave as a folder, and returning to the parent context MUST restore that view without moving the folder.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F03 — Project

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project is a folder-like view divided into visible named sections on the same page. For example, Homework shows Maths containing Mathshomework.pptx and Mathshomework2.pptx, and French containing Frenchlistening.docx. A Maths folder containing its own homework remains possible. Sections are not subfolders and assigning an item to a section MUST NOT change its underlying Files location.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The main view MUST show each section's title, authorised item count, collapse control, contextual menu and Add item entry point. A section contains the selected grid/list/details representation of its members. The toolbar provides Add section, Add existing, New item and view/sort controls. Sections support create, rename, reorder, collapse/expand, colour/label customisation through shared presentation controls and delete. A searchable section outline provides direct navigation for large Projects without forcing the user to open every section as a new page.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each section has a persistent SectionID and addressable deep link. Moving an appearance between sections updates that membership only; source rename/edit actions remain visibly separate. New unassigned members appear in an Unsectioned area. Removing a section MUST offer to keep its members in Unsectioned or remove those appearances; neither option deletes originals. Sorting items within one section MUST not reorder the other sections unless the user applies a Project-wide sort. Per-user collapse state MUST not rewrite shared ordering.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Project acceptance MUST create the Homework example, add a nested folder and another organisation type, reorder and rename sections, follow a SectionID link after rename, move an appearance and delete a section while retaining originals. Reopen and a second authorised client MUST preserve authored section order/membership; viewer mode MUST allow reading and navigation without showing usable mutation controls.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F04 — Sheet

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sheet is a Files-owned whiteboard-like workspace for arranging separate files and ideas. The canvas MUST support file/folder/organisation appearances, sticky notes, rich text, images, labelled connections, freehand drawing and shapes. These surrounding objects supply context; placing a file does not merge its contents into a new document. A Sheet can contain another Sheet, a Stash or a Link document as an openable item without spreading its contents over the parent canvas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The editor MUST provide Select, Pan, Add files, Text, Sticky note, Image, Shape, Pen, Eraser and Connector tools. A contextual inspector exposes supported appearance, fill/stroke, text style, dimensions, position, layering and link/target properties. Multi-selection supports move, resize where compatible, align/distribute, group/ungroup, duplicate appearance and remove. Snap/grid controls, zoom, fit and an object outline MUST be available. Connectors attach to stable object IDs rather than being abandoned when an item moves; deleting a connected object previews and removes its affected contextual connections, not its source file.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: File appearances MUST show a useful permission-safe name/type/preview and an identifiable open action. Each Sheet has a persisted File opening setting: Pop-up or Owning app, with Pop-up as the initial setting for a new Sheet. An item's explicit context command can choose the other route for that opening without silently changing the Sheet default. In authoring mode a click selects and the explicit Open action or normal activation gesture opens; in view mode activation opens directly. Pop-up editing uses only a safe registered owning editor and MUST identify that it changes the original; otherwise provide a read-only preview and Open in owning app.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persist ObjectID/PlacementID, source reference, geometry, z-order, grouping, notes, drawing strokes, shape properties, connector endpoints and opening policy. Viewport and selection remain per-user. Moving or deleting a file appearance MUST not alter an unrelated appearance in another Sheet, while editing the canonical file MUST update every authorised live reference. Undo for local geometry MUST not roll back source edits performed through a different editor.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sheet acceptance MUST combine a Write file, image, sticky note, labelled connection, freehand stroke, shape and nested Stash; arrange and group them; open and edit the same original from two contexts; close the preview and recover the prior canvas position; switch opening policy; and save/reopen with identical authored layout. Keyboard and touch users MUST be able to create, select, open and reposition items without precise pointer dragging.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F05 — Tree

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Tree is a structured Sheet connecting related files and groups. An editor can create a Maths group linked to Maths.pptx, Maths2.pptx and Algebra.pptx; activating Maths opens a pop-up containing its related contents and folders. The same actual file can appear in multiple Trees without unmanaged copies or separately created shortcut files. Tree relationship changes affect the Tree; source edits affect the shared original.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editors MUST see a Tree / View switch. Tree provides a connected layout with Add group, Add existing, Connect, Disconnect, arrange, expand/collapse and fit controls, plus a searchable outline and a selected-node inspector. Nodes display accessible names and authorised previews/counts. Connections, parent/group relationships and collapsed branches MUST be explicit. Reparenting MUST preview its structural effect; a cycle is rejected. Changing arrangement MUST not change logical relationships or file identity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: View presents the contents using ordinary folder-style browsing. View-only users MUST receive View, not a disabled visual Tree. They can open authorised groups/files and navigate Back, but MUST NOT obtain the protected visual layout through a hidden route, embed or layout API. An editor switching to View sees the same accessible logical contents. Editing permission on the Tree does not imply edit permission on its referenced files, and source permissions remain independently checked.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persist stable GroupID/NodeID/ConnectionID, memberships, hierarchy and authored layout. Removing a group or node MUST show whether children are being retained/reassigned or appearances removed and MUST never delete originals as an incidental graph operation. Tree acceptance MUST verify the Maths journey, one file in two Trees, rename/move stability, cycle rejection, editor/viewer mode differences, nested folders and no protected-layout leakage through APIs or Boards embeds.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F06 — Smart

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Smart is a rule-based collection of canonical originals from explicitly selected locations. The editor MUST show a readable rule builder, location/scope picker, All/Any condition grouping, supported operators and a live result preview. Required filter fields include tags, file type, work status and modification date where the source supplies them. Values that are unavailable MUST be treated as unknown, not silently replaced with false, zero or an empty string.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The command bar provides Edit rules, Add location, Refresh/reconcile, Pin item and view/sort controls. Each result exposes Why included, identifying the matching rule or manual pin. Pinned exceptions remain visible even when they stop matching; unpinning returns the item to rule-driven membership. Removing a dynamically matched appearance MUST explain that it will return while it matches and direct the user to adjust the rule or scope rather than pretending the source was removed from the collection. Original-file delete remains separate.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Optional AI setup converts a request into proposed visible rules and locations for review. It MUST not run an opaque classifier as the only explanation for membership or search private locations without permission. Membership updates use the Files change/index contracts, with visible freshness and partial/unavailable-provider state. A disconnected provider MUST NOT make its missing results look like confirmed non-matches. Nested organisations can be matched or pinned as whole objects under TF-F01.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persist the versioned rule expression, selected location IDs, recursion policy, pins and view settings; cached results are not authoritative copies. Smart acceptance MUST demonstrate entry/exit after tag and date changes, All/Any conditions, a pinned non-match, a newly inaccessible location, an offline result set and an inspectable AI-generated rule proposal. No match operation may move, duplicate or widen access to an original.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F07 — Timeline

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Timeline positions files and nested groups along a chronology. The main surface MUST provide a labelled time axis, zoom between broad periods and individual dates, pan, date navigation, fit, an Undated area and a visible Date source selector: Created, Modified, Deadline or Assigned. Labelled periods can contain material and open their contents in a pop-up. A date range is drawn as a span rather than forced into a single point.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The inspector MUST show the effective date/range, source of that value, relevant timezone/date-only interpretation and any locally assigned value. Users can add, rename, resize and reorder labelled periods, open an item/group and filter the displayed contents. Dragging a file to change its chronological position is available for Assigned dates and changes Timeline-local data. Under Created/Modified/Deadline, the UI MUST explain the source rather than secretly rewrite it; explicitly editing a writable source date invokes its owning operation with permission and impact checks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files with no value for the selected date source remain in Undated. Overlapping items MUST remain discoverable through stacking/grouping, previews and the folder-style alternative. Live source-date changes reposition the appearance without changing the file's identity. Changing the selected date source MUST preserve authored assigned dates and periods for later reuse instead of deleting them.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persist DateSource, assigned start/end values, period IDs/ranges, memberships and display settings. Timeline acceptance MUST cover all four date-source choices, an ongoing range, an undated file, overlapping files, a nested organisation, a period pop-up, timezone/date-only boundaries and a source modification that updates the view without rewriting unrelated dates.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F08 — Pipeline

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Pipeline represents progression through configurable stages, not a Project's static categories. The main view MUST show horizontally arranged stage columns, accessible stage titles/counts, item previews, Add stage and Add item. A compact list/grouped view remains available. Users can create, rename, reorder and remove stages, move appearances between stages and inspect an item's contextual process history without opening its source document.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The stage editor MUST support optional checklist requirements and reviewer approval. New personal Pipelines begin without mandatory gates. A transition preview identifies unmet requirements, approval status and any explicit shared-metadata mapping. An unmet mandatory gate blocks the transition with its reason; a request for reviewer approval becomes visibly pending and does not masquerade as a completed stage move. Reviewer identity and authority MUST be checked. Dragging, the Move to stage command and APIs enforce the same gates and revision checks.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each membership has a stable EntryID and local StageID, order, checklist state and approval/transition records. Pipeline stage state is local to that Pipeline by default. A Mapping control may explicitly connect a selected field/stage to global file metadata, showing the target field, conversion, affected items, required rights and conflict behaviour before activation. No implicit mapping occurs. If the global update cannot be authorised or committed, the transition remains blocked or reports an explicitly declared partial result; it MUST not silently claim both succeeded.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deleting a stage MUST require a destination for retained entries or explicit removal of appearances. Originals are unchanged. Pipeline acceptance MUST move an item by pointer, keyboard and API; reject an unmet checklist; obtain and revoke an authorised approval; handle a simultaneous transition; and prove that a stage change in one Pipeline does not change another Pipeline or source metadata without an explicit mapping.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F09 — Catalogue

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Catalogue is a file-centred collection with structured information attached to entries. It MUST provide Cards, Table and Grouped views, a field editor, sort/filter/group controls and an information panel that opens without launching the full source document. The file itself is the organised item; typing a filename into a disconnected table cell MUST NOT create a valid source reference.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Required configurable field kinds include text/description, person/owner reference, status/select, tags, date, number and rating. Each field declares its stable FieldID, type, source and validation. The UI MUST distinguish source metadata from Catalogue-local fields, and read-only source values from writable ones. Editing local notes or ratings MUST not alter another Catalogue. Editing an exposed global field invokes its actual owning operation and shows that broader scope. Changing a field type MUST preview incompatible values and preserve them until an explicit conversion is confirmed.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The entry panel MUST show the authorised source identity/location, available metadata, local values, Open, Show original location and Remove from Catalogue. Users can add/reorder/hide fields, resize columns, choose card preview fields, group results and edit compatible selections in bulk. Validation errors stay attached to the affected field/entry without dropping the rest of the user's edit. Removing a field previews affected local values and is recoverable through normal history; it does not delete source properties.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persist EntryID-to-source mappings, the field schema, local values and authored view configuration. Catalogue acceptance MUST use the same file in two Catalogues with different local notes, change a true global property visibly, reject an invalid field value, preserve values during type changes, open the information panel in all views and retain canonical identity after source rename.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F10 — Stash

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stash is a deliberately ordered collection for working through separate files one at a time. Its reader MUST show the current item, its position in the sequence, Previous/Next, an overview/filmstrip, Open in owning app and an optional Reviewed control. Keyboard and touch navigation MUST work. The sequence is persistent authored data, not an incidental filename sort, and files remain separate rather than forming Flow's continuous page.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editors can add, remove and reorder entries through the overview, using drag and explicit Move earlier/later commands. A Compare action opens two selected entries side by side with independent source identity and navigation; changing one comparison slot MUST not silently advance the main reading position. On narrow screens comparison may switch between clearly labelled A/B views while retaining both selected entries. A Stash opened from a Sheet remains one contextual surface rather than expanding every entry onto the canvas.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persist stable EntryIDs and sequence order. Reading position and optional reviewed state are per user, keyed to EntryID rather than numeric position, and survive restart. Reordering MUST retain the reader's current item when it still exists. Removing that entry moves to a clearly identified neighbouring position without deleting its original. The UI MUST distinguish Complete/reviewed status from actually changing a file's global work status.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stash acceptance MUST save a non-alphabetical sequence, reopen at the same item, mark reviewed items, reorder from another authorised client, compare two files, handle a denied/missing source and return from a Sheet pop-up without changing the canvas or cloning files.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-F11 — Matrix

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Matrix organises material by two authored dimensions. The main view MUST display user-defined row and column headings together, with sticky headings or an equivalent persistent orientation aid, cell counts/previews, Add row, Add column and view/zoom controls. Each intersection contains file/folder/organisation appearances. Users can open a cell group, a row's combined contents or a column's combined contents without traversing an invented outer-folder hierarchy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rows and columns support create, rename, reorder and remove. Each has a stable ID; a CellID is tied to those identities, not its visual coordinates or labels. Dragging an appearance between cells changes Matrix-local classification only. Keyboard navigation MUST identify the current row/column and provide explicit move/add/open commands. Large grids MUST remain navigable using filtering, scrolling and the normal contents view rather than shrinking every cell until its contents are unreadable.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Removing an axis previews the affected memberships and offers reassignment, retention in an Unassigned group or removal of appearances; it MUST not delete originals. A row/column combined view MUST not suggest that repeated appearances are independent copies: repeated canonical items are coalesced with visible placement context or clearly marked as repeated references. The authorised counts MUST correspond to the chosen displayed unit, not include hidden private entries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Matrix acceptance MUST build Topic A/B/C rows and Writing/Data/Presentations columns, populate a cell with a nested folder, open cell/row/column groups, rename/reorder both axes, move an appearance, remove an axis safely and reopen without losing identity, classification or readable orientation.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Link

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-L01 — Link shell, documents and shared content

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Link connects work together through Flow and Binder. The launch screen and New menu MUST distinguish them by both name and preview: Flow is a continuous page; Binder is an explorable interconnected document. Creating a document asks for its type, name and Files destination. A document can itself be placed in any compatible Files organisation, opened from Spaces or included in Boards without changing its identity. Link MUST NOT offer Sheet as a third document type or use Boards as the name of Binder.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The editor MUST expose the current document type, outline/search, Insert, source management, preview/view mode, undo/redo, save/sync/history and sharing. Link-authored text, tables, images, media, drawings and other supported objects use the Shared Productivity Engine. Embedded originals use registered owning-app renderers/editors. A Sources panel lists authorised references, live/pinned policy, selected source section, availability and permission status, with Reveal placement, Change source/section and Open original actions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Link owns its block/container structure, arrangement and directly authored information. Existing files stay independent originals. Authoring a note inside Binder does not require creating a new file; placing a Write document inside Binder does not silently import its text as Binder-owned content. The distinction MUST be visible in the inspector and destructive-action wording. Duplicate document copies its authored structure and preserves source references unless the user explicitly chooses independent source copies.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-L02 — Flow reading and authoring UI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Flow MUST render selected documents and other content inline in one chosen reading order, with one primary vertical scroll. It MUST not be a column of file icons, buttons to open pop-ups or permanently nested vertically scrolling document panels. The content width, typography integration and transitions MUST form a coherent page while preserving the owning source's meaningful content. Large tables may use local horizontal navigation; interactive media can retain their own controls, but normal document reading MUST remain continuous.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The author MUST have a reorderable block outline and an insertion affordance between blocks. Insert supports authorised whole documents or stable source sections, directly authored shared objects, images/media and a scoped report assistant. Each selected block shows Move, Duplicate placement, Remove, source/section selection and supported layout controls. Reordering by drag or outline commands changes only the Flow sequence. Duplicate placement can show the same original at a second point without cloning it. Source labels/chrome MUST be available on focus/selection or through the Sources panel without making the reading surface resemble a file-manager grid.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Annual report example is mandatory: Report.data, then Report.write, then an image, then another authorised section/appearance of Report.data, then an AI assistant for questions about the report. Readers scroll through all contributions as one page. The assistant's context is the report and its authorised sources; it cannot silently search unrelated work or reveal a source the reader cannot access. AI unavailability MUST not block reading the report.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A live source change MUST update the correct block while preserving the reader's stable location as far as the underlying content permits. Explicit revision pinning MUST be visible. Missing sections, unsupported renderers, offline sources and denied access get bounded, accurately labelled placeholders without erasing the block or substituting another source. Navigation back from an original editor MUST return to the corresponding Flow position. Large documents use incremental layout/virtualisation without changing source identity or making the scrollbar repeatedly jump during ordinary reading.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Inline viewing is required for supported sources. Inline editing is available only through a safe registered owning editor, with an explicit Edit original state and ordinary source permissions, revision checks and audit. A reader with edit rights to Flow but not its source can rearrange the reference where permitted but cannot edit that source. Where embedded editing is unavailable, provide faithful read-only inline content plus Open in owning app; do not flatten, fork or invent a private editor. Formatting a Flow-owned heading MUST not unexpectedly restyle a source document.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Flow acceptance MUST build the Annual report example; use the same Data source twice with stable section selectors; edit the original through a permitted route; revoke source access; delete a referenced section; reorder and undo; reopen and resume reading; and verify a continuous primary scroll on desktop and mobile. No source copy or widened permission may be introduced by composition.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-L03 — Binder overview, containers and navigation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Binder is one authored interconnected document with an overview and layers of detail: one file, connected ideas, and explorable contents. Its authoring surface MUST be a freeform overview containing clickable notes, cards, physical-style folders, binders, tabs, stacks and connected sections. These are real authored document containers with nested content, not ordinary filesystem folders with decorative styling and not merely shortcuts to other files.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The palette MUST provide note/card, folder, tabbed binder, stack, section/connection and supported shared content objects. Authors can place, resize, group, layer and label objects, create/reorder tabs and stack contents, connect stable items and edit a selected container's contents. The inspector exposes title, accessible label, appearance, target/open behaviour and relevant container settings. The hierarchy/outline is searchable and supports the same add, rename, move, reorder and open operations without relying on spatial precision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Opening a folder reveals its contained material. Opening a tabbed binder exposes named section tabs and the selected section. A stack exposes its ordered contents. A card or note can reveal writing, images, tables, audio and other supported material authored directly in Binder or referenced from an original. Containers can nest under the shared recursion safeguards. Visual physical metaphors MUST not conceal controls or require ornamental animations to finish before the content is usable; reduced motion preserves the same navigation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Reader mode hides layout handles and authoring chrome while retaining accessible openable items, connections, breadcrumbs/Back, Close and search/outline. Closing a detail view returns to the same surrounding overview and focus. A stable item deep link opens the corresponding detail and a route back to its context. Readers choose what to explore; Binder MUST NOT force a fixed sequence or masquerade as a Paths progression system. Connections are navigation links between related parts, not an obligation to turn the document into a flowchart.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Persist stable object/container/section/tab/connection IDs, nested authored content, geometry, source references and intended overview. Reader viewport, currently open containers and selected tabs are per-user session state unless the author explicitly sets a default starting view. Deleting a Binder container previews its authored descendants; separately referenced files remain intact. Extracting authored content into another app requires an explicit owning-app create/export operation, not an implicit file for every note.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Binder acceptance MUST author a folder with rich content, a tabbed binder, a stack, a referenced original and a connection; read them in a non-linear order; close back to the same overview; find an off-canvas item through the outline; follow a deep link after rename; and open the Binder from a Sheet and as a Boards page. Directly authored information, source references and all nested content MUST survive reopen without being flattened or split into unwanted files.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Prototype

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-P01 — Product boundary and editor layout

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prototype creates editable interactive systems: objects with typed properties, formulas, rules, relationships, adjustable inputs and visible outputs. Its scope includes simulations, calculations, interactive explanations and experimental tools, not only software-interface mock-ups or 3D geometry. It MUST be useful without AI and MUST NOT be renamed Models in menus, artifact types or launch screens.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The editor MUST provide a component/object library, an object hierarchy, a central Design surface, a Logic/relationships surface, a contextual property inspector and a Run/Preview surface. Users MUST be able to switch between Design, Logic and Run without losing work or creating separate copies of the model. A collapsible diagnostics area shows validation, formula errors and runtime problems with links to the responsible object/property. The contextual AI bar shares the selected model/object scope rather than creating an unrelated chat-only prototype.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The component library MUST include text/value outputs, numeric and text inputs, sliders, switches, buttons, selectors, tables/charts and reusable containers/components. The Design surface supports placement, size, grouping and shared layout controls. The inspector exposes accessible label, property type, default/current value, limits/options, units where declared, binding and event actions. Controls MUST be backed by typed properties and real behaviour; a visually plausible slider disconnected from the model is not implemented functionality.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-P02 — Typed model, logic and execution

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The canonical model MUST contain versioned stable object/property/component/relationship/event/action IDs, types, defaults, constraints, formulas, dependency references, layout, assets and saved authoring revision. Bindings target stable identities rather than display labels. The Logic surface uses the shared Node Graph Framework for applicable typed ports, connections, comments/groups, pan/zoom, keyboard editing, validation and execution overlays. A readable formula editor remains available for expressions that are clearer as formulas than as large graphs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Authors can create typed properties, bind controls to them, define formulas, connect object relationships, add events/actions and compose reusable components with explicit inputs/outputs. Numeric, Boolean, text and structured/list values MUST be distinguishable. Incompatible assignments/connections are rejected or require an explicit conversion. Renaming a property MUST not break its bindings. Removing one previews dependent formulas and controls and requires repair or an explicit unresolved state rather than quietly replacing references with zero.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Derived calculations MUST follow validated dependencies. Circular combinational dependencies, invalid types, division/domain errors and unavailable inputs MUST be surfaced at their actual source, not hidden as plausible values. Simulations that require feedback MUST use explicit state/time-step semantics rather than relying on an uncontrolled formula cycle. Evaluation MUST have bounded resource use, cancellation and inspectable diagnostics. Long-running calculation MUST not block navigation or Stop.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Run/Preview shows the interactive output with Play/Run, Pause/Stop where time-based execution applies, Reset and inspectable current input/output values. Runtime experimentation MUST be separate from saved authoring defaults: moving a slider during a viewer session changes that session, not every reader's shared model. An editor can explicitly apply chosen inputs as new defaults. Reset restores the declared initial state; reopening an authored model MUST not silently resume unintended external actions. Controlled calculations with the same revision and inputs MUST behave consistently; nondeterministic inputs and random seeds MUST be declared when used.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-P03 — Safety, reuse and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Expressions and scripts MUST execute in the declared sandbox, not arbitrary host code. No file, network, credential, process or device access is implicitly granted by opening or running a Prototype. External actions, when supported, go through existing typed app APIs and Home permissions, with visible effects and cancellation rules. Reader preview MUST not execute consequential actions solely because an author embedded them. The model MUST remain inspectable when execution is blocked.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Measured/imported values, assumptions, calculations and outputs MUST be identifiable in the inspector and relevant output presentation. Units and declared limitations MUST be preserved. AI-generated assumptions MUST not be presented as measurements or validated predictions. AI edits are reviewable typed model operations with normal undo, validation and source permissions. Reusable components retain stable definitions and explicit dependency versions; a component update MUST not silently break existing instances.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prototype integrates with Files, Spaces, Link, Boards and Paths through registered renderers, references and typed actions. A reader may adjust permitted local inputs without acquiring authoring rights. Native export/import preserves the model and declared dependencies; static output exports are labelled as non-interactive. Missing components keep their payload and show a repair state rather than disappearing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Prototype acceptance MUST build a working calculator with two inputs, a typed formula and output; build a bounded time-based example with Run/Pause/Reset; bind a slider and switch; display a chart; reuse a component; reject invalid types and a dependency cycle; change inputs without changing saved defaults; recover from a runtime error; and prove that an untrusted script cannot reach host files or network without an authorised capability. Save/reopen and API-driven edits MUST preserve the same model and behaviour.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Paths

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-H01 — Authoring, steps and route UI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Paths authors guided, repeatable interactive experiences with steps, choices, activities, checkpoints and branching routes. It is not a fixed presentation, an open-ended Binder overview or a sequence improvised afresh by AI. A Path may provide a guided process, exploration route or overview towards an outcome, with the available routes determined by its authored structure.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The authoring editor MUST provide a step library/outline, a route graph, a selected-step content editor, a condition/action inspector and Preview/Test. Add step offers information, choice, activity, checkpoint and outcome/end behaviour through typed step definitions. Steps can contain supported shared content and authorised embedded artifacts. Authors can reorder outline entries, connect or disconnect routes, label choices, designate the starting step, edit conditions, add checkpoints and define explicit completion outcomes. Graph position is not route identity or step order.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each choice MUST have a human-readable label and stable target. Conditional routing MUST expose its condition, required values and fallback/error behaviour. No eligible route MUST show a recoverable blocked state rather than select a random next step. Multiple eligible automatic routes require an explicit authored priority/selection rule and MUST not depend on incidental storage order. Deliberate loops/retries are allowed when explicitly authored and controllable; accidental automatic loops, missing targets and unreachable required outcomes MUST be detected in validation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preview/Test MUST run against an identified draft revision with disposable test progress, offer reset and route inspection, and show the choice/condition responsible for each transition. Authors MUST be able to test alternative inputs and inspect unreachable/missing routes without modifying real users' progress. Updating the shared authored Path uses a deliberate validated revision commit; a preview session is not automatically the published reader revision.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-H02 — Reader experience and durable progress

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The reader surface MUST show the current step, its content, available choices/actions, relevant checkpoint/completion status and a route/overview affordance when allowed by the authored Path. Continue appears only when its conditions are satisfied. Back/previous navigation, where permitted, MUST not repeat external side effects or silently clear completed work. Branch-dependent length MUST not be presented as a fictitious fixed percentage; show meaningful visited/checkpoint status instead.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Progress MUST be durable and separate from authored content, with stable PathID, authored RevisionID, UserID or clearly scoped guest-session identity, AttemptID, current StepID, visited route, responses, checkpoint states, completion outcome and timestamps. A signed-in reader can resume their authorised attempt after restart or on another compatible device. Guest/local-only progress MUST be labelled honestly and MUST NOT be represented as cross-device account sync.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Readers can restart/reset and complete the same Path more than once. Restart creates a new attempt with clean progress while preserving previous completed attempts under the declared retention policy. Clearing saved progress is a separate confirmed deletion operation. Checkpoints persist sufficient state for safe resume. An interrupted save or duplicate transition request MUST not create duplicate completions or repeat an externally consequential action. Sensitive responses and progress are not automatically exposed to every person who can read the authored Path.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Active attempts remain bound to their authored revision by default. When a newer revision is available, the reader MUST be told; switching/restarting requires an explicit action and a validated mapping or fresh attempt. Deleted/changed steps MUST not cause silent jumps into a different route. Opening an embedded file or Prototype obeys its own permissions, and completion MUST depend on an explicit typed result, not a fragile guess from visible pixels.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-H03 — Integration and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Paths owns step/route semantics and progress. Its graph reuses the shared graph editor, and embedded content reuses the shared object/owning-app systems. Activities that call another app or Automation remain subject to the user's actual permissions and the action's risk; a teacher/author cannot grant those rights merely by embedding the activity. AI can help author or explain a Path through typed operations but MUST not silently replace committed routing during a reader attempt.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Paths acceptance MUST create a branching experience with two outcomes, a required activity and checkpoint; preview both routes; detect a missing target and an automatic loop; resume a real attempt after restart; complete it twice with separate AttemptIDs; update the authored revision without corrupting an existing attempt; revoke a source permission; and prove that retrying a transition does not repeat an external action. Keyboard, screen-reader and narrow-screen users MUST be able to complete the same authored route.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Replay

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-R01 — Explicit capture and source selection

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replay creates explorable records of how selected work developed. Its core model is semantic revisions, events, work states and checkpoints, not a raw screen recording. Optional screenshots, video and narration may accompany that record. Capture MUST be explicitly started and limited to the selected authorised sources; opening Replay MUST NOT begin recording unrelated work or private activity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: New capture MUST present a source picker, selected files/sub-objects, available capture capabilities per owning app, destination, retention/export implications and optional media settings. Unsupported semantic sources are identified before starting; the UI MUST not silently claim semantic capture when it can only obtain an image. Optional microphone/camera/screen access requires its own explicit selection and platform permissions. A preview of the scope MUST be available before Start.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: During capture, show an unmistakable Recording/Paused state, selected-source summary, elapsed session information, Add checkpoint, annotation/narration controls and Pause/Stop. A source-scope change is explicit and timestamped. Stop MUST stop subscriptions and selected media capture, finalise durable state and show any pending/failed material. Losing permission to a source MUST stop future capture for that source and expose the limitation rather than continue through a cached unrestricted channel.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-R02 — Semantic timeline and playback UI

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The editor/player MUST provide a chronological event/checkpoint timeline, source tracks/filtering, a central historical artifact viewer, a checkpoint/annotation list and an inspector showing the selected source revision and capture completeness. Users can label/reorder presentation chapters where supported without falsifying the underlying event order, add explanations and choose a shareable presentation range. Changes to Replay presentation MUST NOT rewrite the original source's history.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Playback MUST support play/pause, seek, previous/next checkpoint and adjustable playback speed for timed material. At a checkpoint the recipient can inspect the document, calculation, diagram or other supported artifact as it existed then. The historical viewer MUST be visibly read-only and identify the captured revision. It MUST NOT resolve a checkpoint to the source's latest content merely because that is easier to load. Narrative media follows the selected timeline while retaining accessible captions/transcripts when provided.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Capture records MUST include SessionID, authorised source identities, ordered EventIDs, event/revision provenance, CheckpointIDs, timestamps/sequence, required base revisions or validated snapshot references, annotations and media references. Replay stores enough authorised retained state or pinned revision dependencies to reconstruct the included checkpoints under the declared retention policy. It MUST NOT depend on an ephemeral cache that disappears after the app closes. Missing bases, gaps and unavailable retained sources produce an explicit incomplete-checkpoint state, not invented reconstruction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Continue from here action is available only when the owning app supports an independent copy from that checkpoint and permissions permit it. The action shows destination, copy scope and unavailable dependencies, creates a new canonical artifact through the owner and opens that copy. It MUST NOT restore the original over its current version or imply that a Replay viewer has edit rights to the source.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-R03 — Review, sharing, failure and acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before sharing/export, Replay MUST provide an included-material review showing files, revisions, annotations, optional recordings and recipient access implications. Referenced live access and an exported independent snapshot are distinct. Copy/export rights are required for retained source bytes shared independently. Excluding or redacting captured content MUST also address derived thumbnails, search text, transcripts and dependent snapshots; metadata MUST not leak a supposedly removed secret. A presentation trim alone MUST not be labelled permanent redaction.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Session state MUST distinguish Not started, Recording, Paused, Finalising, Ready, Incomplete and Error. Interruption recovery resumes from a durable checkpoint/journal without claiming the missing interval was captured. Storage/quota exhaustion, unavailable owning apps and media-device failure MUST be visible, bounded and recoverable. Media failure MUST not silently destroy valid semantic checkpoints. Delete/retention cleanup applies to Replay-owned captures and assets, not the original source documents.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Replay acceptance MUST capture selected changes in two supported artifacts, exclude an unrelated open file, pause/resume, create an annotated checkpoint, restart after interruption, inspect historical state after the original advances, reveal a missing dependency, stop on revoked permission and create an authorised independent copy. Export/share review MUST detect excluded material in thumbnails/transcripts and MUST not claim that view-only rights permit exporting source bytes.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Variants

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-V01 — Integrated variant UI and branch identity

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Variants MUST ship within Write, Data, Present, Canvas, Picture, Prototype and Sites. It is not a separate app or Files organisation type. Version history answers which earlier state to return to; Variants lets users explore multiple directions in parallel without overwriting the starting version merely to experiment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each supported app MUST expose a consistent Variants entry near the document/version controls. The panel lists the main/current working line and named alternatives with base/current revision, modified state and useful compare/merge status. Required actions are Create variant, Switch, Rename, Duplicate variant, Compare, Bring changes back/Merge and Archive/remove variant through the owning recovery rules. The active variant MUST remain clearly identified in the editor title/status and save destination. A user MUST not unknowingly type into the main version after switching to an alternative.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Creating a variant records a stable VariantID, parent/base RevisionID and its own revision head. Switching resolves unsaved work through save or an explicit recoverable decision, not silent discard. A variant is a separately addressable branch of the owning artifact, not a manually duplicated filename or Files shortcut. Autosave, undo/redo, collaboration, search/deep links and restart MUST retain the active branch identity. A deep link to a variant MUST not silently open Main.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-V02 — Comparison, selective merge and conflicts

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Compare MUST allow selection of base/source/target variants and provide content-appropriate side-by-side or change-focused presentation. The interface MUST identify additions, removals, edits and conflicts, offer next/previous change and show what accepting a selected change will affect. Colour alone MUST not convey the difference. An edit to the source or target during comparison invalidates or refreshes the merge preview rather than permitting a stale overwrite.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Merge MUST be an owning-app semantic operation against explicit source, base and expected target revisions. It requires a preview, selected changes or a clearly labelled whole-version choice, validation and a final commit. Compatible independent changes can be combined; overlapping or incompatible changes remain visible for resolution. Resolution must state Keep target, Use source or the supported manual choice. The implementation MUST NOT guess away conflicts or claim a generic byte merge is safe for every artifact type.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: If safe selective merge is unavailable for a particular content operation, the app MUST provide a faithful compare-and-choose workflow and explain its scope. Choosing the source creates a new target revision while retaining recoverable history; it MUST NOT erase the target's earlier line. A failed/cancelled merge leaves both branches intact. Retry is idempotent, and a revision mismatch returns a conflict rather than overwriting newer work. Archive/remove MUST not delete the only retained content without the normal recovery/confirmation contract.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-V03 — Required owning-app comparison semantics

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Write MUST compare stable text/block structure, edits, formatting and referenced objects; text and formatting conflicts remain distinguishable. Data MUST compare sheets/tables, stable rows/columns/cells, values, formulas, schema and named dependencies; it MUST not splice unrelated rows merely because their current indices match. Present MUST compare slide identity/order, objects, content, layout and presentation-level dependencies.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Canvas MUST compare stable objects, geometry, strokes, grouping, connectors and source references. Picture MUST compare layers, masks, transformations, adjustments and image data using the actual supported document structure; incompatible raster edits require a visible choose/manual-resolution path rather than invented pixel-level semantic merging. Prototype MUST compare typed objects/properties, formulas, bindings, component definitions and relationships and validate the resulting model before commit.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites MUST compare pages, components, routes, content, assets and settings through Sites' own model. Comparing, switching or merging a site variant MUST NOT publish or change production deployment by itself. Deployment remains an explicit existing Sites operation with its separate permissions and confirmations. Secrets, credentials and live provider state MUST not be copied into a branch merely because project settings are versioned.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Variants acceptance MUST create, edit, switch, compare and bring changes back in all seven apps; retain the starting version; expose an overlapping conflict; exercise the safe whole-version fallback; reject a stale merge; recover after save interruption; and reopen at the selected branch. Test each app's specific content families above. A shared button bar without working per-app comparison/merge is not coverage.

heading: HEADING_1
text: Cross-app delivery and acceptance

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-X01 — Embeds, Boards pages and conversational editing

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Boards MUST be able to include a Flow or Binder as a page referencing the same canonical Link document. It MUST also support a Files Sheet as a live Files-owned organisation page, rather than mislabelling Sheet as a Link type. The same registered embedding contract applies to the other declared compatible organisation/artifact surfaces. The host page MUST identify the owning source, respect reader/editor capability, provide Open original and preserve navigation back to the Board.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A Binder or Flow placed on a Sheet MUST open through the Sheet's chosen policy while keeping the surrounding notes/files and viewport. A Stash on a Sheet remains an ordered group. A Prototype embedded in Link, Boards or a Path MUST retain its actual model and permitted session-local controls, not become a screenshot while being described as interactive. Replay checkpoint views remain historical. Every supported combination MUST reference canonical entities; unsupported combinations show their exact limitation instead of silently flattening or cloning.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Spaces and the persistent AI bar MUST use the same typed APIs as the UI for authorised creation, organisation and editing. The current artifact, selection, source scope, active variant and permissions MUST be supplied explicitly. AI suggestions that change organisation rules, dependencies, route logic or other significant behaviour must be inspectable and undoable. AI access remains a separate permission; opening a private file in an embed does not authorise cloud upload. Core manual workflows MUST remain usable when AI is disabled or unavailable.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-X02 — Canonical API action catalogue

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: New UI operations extend the existing canonical namespaces: 9to1.Files.Organisation, 9to1.Link, 9to1.Prototype, 9to1.Paths and 9to1.Replay. Variants actions live under the owning app's Variants capability, such as 9to1.Write.Variants; the shared implementation MUST not bypass that owner's semantics. Existing Files, shared-object and NodeGraph actions remain authoritative for their existing operations rather than being copied into incompatible new APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every mutation request MUST include the target stable IDs, typed payload, operation/idempotency key and expected revision, or an explicitly declared create precondition. Successful results identify affected objects, resulting revision and any job/change-event identity. Read/list operations accept explicit scope and filters and return bounded pages with continuation cursors. Long-running query, capture, evaluation, export and merge work exposes JobID, progress, cancellation and durable result/error. Events have stable IDs and resumable cursors. Home resolves caller identity, scopes and risk before dispatch; possession of an ID never grants access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Files.Organisation MUST expose Create/Get/List, UpdateSettings, AddReference, RemoveReference, Reorder and the type-specific operations: Project section CRUD and assignment; Sheet object/geometry/ink/shape/connector edits and opening policy; Tree group/node/connection edits plus separately authorised Tree-layout reads; Smart rule/scope/pin updates and membership explanation; Timeline date-source/assigned-range/period edits; Pipeline stage/gate/approval/transition/mapping actions; Catalogue field/schema/local-value/view edits; Stash order/position/review/compare selection; and Matrix axis/cell/membership operations. Generic command payloads MUST have registered typed schemas, not arbitrary unvalidated JSON.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Link MUST expose document creation and retrieval, block/container CRUD, ordering/geometry, source/section/revision-policy updates, outline/search, preview and export/import. Source edits dispatch to the source owner's registered actions. Prototype MUST expose object/property/component CRUD, formula/binding/relationship/event/action updates, validation, evaluation/run/stop/reset and session-input changes. Persisting runtime values as defaults is a separate authoring action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Paths MUST expose step/route/content CRUD, validation, preview/test sessions, authored revision commit, StartAttempt, GetProgress, SubmitResponse, Advance, checkpoint/resume, Restart and confirmed progress deletion. Reader-scoped progress actions MUST not allow changing another reader's attempt or the authored route. Replay MUST expose source capability inspection, capture creation/start/pause/resume/stop, scope changes, checkpoints/annotations, event/checkpoint retrieval, historical preview, independent-copy requests, review/redaction and export/delete. Variant APIs MUST expose branch create/list/get/rename/switch state, compare, merge preview, resolution, commit and archive/recover through each required owning app.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Action schemas MUST declare required target permissions, source permissions, reversible/destructive risk, external effects, limits and partial-success behaviour. Required structured errors include InvalidArgument, ItemNotFound, PermissionRequired, PermissionDenied, RevisionConflict, UnsupportedCapability, ProviderUnavailable, Offline, QuotaExceeded, MissingSource, MissingSourceSection, InvalidReferenceCycle, TypeMismatch, ValidationFailed, DependencyUnavailable, TransitionBlocked, CaptureIncomplete, MergeConflict and Cancelled, using existing canonical equivalents where already defined. Errors identify recoverability and the affected operation without leaking forbidden source details. Every action exposed by a context menu, keyboard command or editor control MUST be accounted for in the generated UI/API parity manifest.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-X03 — Platforms, responsive behaviour and resource limits

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Windows, 9to1-OS and browser/web MUST implement the useful core authoring and reader experiences for this tranche using the same canonical formats, account identity, domain APIs and permissions. Native interfaces use CUI/Home; web uses the existing authenticated web-service contract and MUST not require arbitrary local filesystem/process access. A narrow viewport by itself is not a reason to replace an otherwise supported app with an unrelated simplified data model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The operating contract's Android/Go timing exception remains limited to newly added complex Terra-form surfaces. Any temporary read-only/limited-editing mode MUST still provide source-aware navigation, faithful content, accessible controls, per-user reading/progress state where supported and a visible explanation of unavailable authoring. Tree viewers still receive only View. No disabled authoring control may pretend to save. Full Android/Go authoring parity remains required after the temporary fallback; existing stronger mobile functionality MUST not regress.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: At narrow sizes, navigation and inspectors become drawers or dedicated subviews, command overflow remains discoverable and pop-ups may use full-screen routes with preserved Back state. Flow retains continuous reading; Binder retains outline and open/close exploration; Files collections retain meaningful contents views; Paths retains choices and progress; Replay retains seeking/checkpoint inspection; Variants retains source/target identity in sequential comparison. Complex spatial authoring MUST provide fit and accessible structural alternatives, not an unreadable scaled-down desktop screenshot.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Large collections/graphs/documents MUST use bounded incremental loading, preview hydration, virtualisation and subscription cleanup. Closed/off-screen embeds MUST not continue uncontrolled computation, media playback or capture. Source resolution and exports MUST detect recursion and bound dependency traversal. Query, evaluation, capture, import/export and merge limits MUST be declared by the relevant capability and shown before an operation that exceeds them; limits MUST not silently truncate content. Existing platform-wide performance/resource thresholds remain mandatory. Actual supported workload sizes and measured results MUST be recorded rather than invented completion claims.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-X04 — Acceptance matrix and release evidence

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every numbered Terra-form requirement group MUST have a traceable implementation and test mapping. Evidence MUST distinguish source/unit coverage from real UI, runtime, cross-app, provider and package validation. The per-feature acceptance journeys above are mandatory minimums, not optional demonstrations. Test both ordinary authoring and reader roles, source permissions independent of host permissions, empty/loading/error states, source move/rename/delete, undo/redo, reopen, offline recovery and concurrent revisions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The Files matrix MUST cover all ten organisation types as parent and nested target, recording the exact reason for any genuinely incoherent or unsupported provider combination. Required cross-app journeys include Homework Project sections; the same file in Tree, Smart, Timeline and Pipeline without copies; a Sheet containing a Stash and Binder; the Annual report Flow; Flow/Binder/Sheet as Boards pages; an interactive Prototype in an authored Path; a Replay historical checkpoint after the source changes; and Variants in every one of the seven named apps. Tests MUST verify canonical IDs and actual content effects, not only screenshots of controls.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual/accessibility QA MUST inspect desktop and narrow/touch layouts, keyboard-only operation, screen-reader names/structure, visible focus, dialog return focus, 200% scaling, themes/contrast and reduced motion. Inspect normal, selected, loading, read-only, conflict and missing-source states. Verify that no pane overlaps the AI bar or prevents access to Save/Close/Back and that large canvases/graphs remain operable through their outlines. API tests MUST repeat consequential UI operations and prove equivalent permissions, validation, idempotency and results.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Recovery tests MUST interrupt source hydration, collection edits, native import/export, Prototype evaluation, Path progress writes, Replay finalisation and variant merge. Preserve originals and recoverable drafts, expose exact partial/failure state and prove safe retry. Resource tests MUST use populated realistic collections, long Flows, nested Binders, branching Paths and captured multi-source histories; record workload, platform and observed results. Empty fixtures alone do not establish production usability.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The release evidence ledger MUST identify each group as VERIFIED, IMPLEMENTED-UNVERIFIED, MISSING or BLOCKED, with tested revision/build, platform, evidence and exact remaining exception. A temporary Android/Go fallback is recorded as a scoped incomplete-authoring exception, not full parity. These tests add to, and do not replace or weaken, the operating contract, full active specification, donor parity, security, privacy, performance, native-device and package gates.

heading: HEADING_2
text: TF-X05 — Open naming decision and implementation defaults

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The separate Playgrounds naming/product relationship to Prototype remains OPEN. This section does not authorise another overlapping standalone app. All other named Terra-form behaviours above are active shipping scope. No legacy migration is required for genuinely new formats unless real existing data needs it; any such data MUST be inspected and preserved before a format change.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Where a low-level representation or provider adapter detail remains unspecified, workers MUST choose the narrowest coherent implementation consistent with these visible behaviours, version and document its contract, and validate it. This discretion MUST NOT be used to invent another product, drop a required control/workflow, weaken ownership or security, flatten a native format, conceal an unsupported platform or defer a named feature. Material product changes outside these requirements require an explicit canonical decision.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
TITLE
text: Pass 3: Sol Happy

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-01 — Purpose and required outcome

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sol Happy is the “systems online” development pass.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The pass brings the 9to1 ecosystem onto its real production infrastructure: public websites, browser applications, CAKE ID authentication, subscription billing, hosted files, hosted websites, cloud-backed application services and operational management.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The required outcome is a connected service that a user can access from a fresh device without a development environment. A user MUST be able to visit the website, create or access their account, open an eligible application in their browser, create and save real work, continue that work in a desktop application, purchase an available subscription and use the resources that subscription provides.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public production services MUST NOT depend on a developer’s PC remaining online, a temporary development tunnel or a manually started local server.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sol Happy includes completing the production integration of existing features. It MUST NOT become a separate, reduced product that merely resembles the desktop ecosystem.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: All existing mandatory product, donor-parity, accessibility, privacy, security, API and interoperability requirements remain active. Pass 3 does not retrospectively excuse missing requirements from earlier passes. The existing definition of implementation-complete continues to require validated behaviour rather than source presence, successful builds or rendered interfaces.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-02 — Baseline, authority and deployment permissions

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
