text: Before implementation begins, the coordinator MUST identify the authoritative repository, current accepted baseline, active workstreams, existing deployments and relevant infrastructure accounts. Existing work, credentials, production configuration and user data MUST be preserved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The pass MUST maintain a requirement ledger using VERIFIED, IMPLEMENTED-UNVERIFIED, MISSING and BLOCKED, with evidence tied to the exact tested revision, environment and platform. Existing acceptance evidence MUST be re-evaluated where changes affect its validity.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: This specification remains the product authority. Infrastructure notes, repository documentation and worker reports MUST NOT introduce competing requirements or silently narrow the pass.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Development, staging and production MUST be distinguishable. Test payments, test accounts, preview deployments and development storage MUST NOT be presented as live production services.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Approval to develop this pass is not blanket approval to spend money or change live production routing. Enabling billable services, increasing spending limits, making live test charges, changing production DNS, retiring WordPress or deleting production resources requires explicit authorisation covering the relevant action.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Independent implementation and testing MUST continue while a particular external approval is pending. A pending approval remains a visible deployment gate, not an excuse to stop unrelated work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sol Happy’s execution model and deadline MUST be specified separately. Terra-form’s deadline and temporary Android/Go fallback MUST NOT automatically become Pass 3 rules.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-03 — Production architecture and ownership

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cloudflare is the intended production hosting platform for the public websites, web applications, hosted files and hosted sites. Stripe provides subscription payment processing and associated billing services.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: These providers MUST NOT replace 9to1’s product ownership boundaries.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: CAKE ID and the shared account services own identity, sessions and entitlement evaluation. Files owns canonical file identity, storage operations, sharing, versions and synchronisation. Sites owns website authoring and deployment orchestration. Stripe supplies verified payment and subscription facts; it does not become the file-permission or application-authorisation system.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The proposed Cloudflare service mapping is:

NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cloudflare documents these services as different storage, coordination and task-processing building blocks. The exact combination MUST be validated against 9to1’s runtime, consistency, capacity and recovery requirements; it MUST NOT be selected merely because all services share one provider. Eventually consistent KV MUST NOT be the sole authority for operations requiring immediate, transactional enforcement. (developers.cloudflare.com)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public first-party websites MUST be independently deployable from customer projects and customer build workloads. A failed customer deployment or exhausted customer allocation MUST NOT take the main website offline.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every environment MUST have explicit resource bindings, secret references, deployment identities and rollback procedures. Private credentials MUST NOT enter browser bundles, public assets, repository history or ordinary diagnostic output.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-04 — WordPress-to-Cloudflare website migration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The pass MUST migrate the production website away from its WordPress runtime dependency.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The intended architecture for cakemods.com and 9to1.com is:

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Editable Sites project → canonical Files/Stack source → validated build → Cloudflare production deployment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites remains the authoring layer; the public websites are served from their separate production deployments. Published output MUST NOT become the only surviving copy of the website. This follows the existing Sites source and deployment authority contract.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Before migration, the implementer MUST inventory the actual website’s pages, routes, assets, redirects, navigation, forms, account links, downloads and backend dependencies. Every retained capability MUST have a working destination in the replacement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The migration MUST preserve required content and useful behaviour. It MUST NOT substitute screenshots, flattened pages or an unrelated redesign for the existing site and editor functionality. The cakemods site-plugin remains the donor reference for applicable authoring behaviour.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Moving DNS or placing Cloudflare in front of the existing WordPress server does not satisfy the migration requirement. The replacement MUST operate without WordPress supplying its ordinary public runtime, account backend or content-management operations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Domain registration MUST NOT be transferred again merely to complete hosting migration. Existing DNS configuration MUST be inspected, and unrelated records—including mail and verification records—MUST be preserved.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The replacement MUST first be validated in a non-production environment. Cutover requires a recoverable backup, a verified destination, a plan for any writes during migration and an authorised rollback path. WordPress MUST NOT be deleted or cancelled simply because the new homepage loads.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: There is no requirement to invent a legacy consumer-data migration programme for data that does not exist. Any real accounts, content, submissions or other records discovered during inspection MUST nevertheless be preserved or deliberately migrated.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-05 — CAKE ID and account services online

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Desktop and web MUST use the same CAKE ID, account identity, organisation context and entitlement services. Ordinary users MUST NOT require WordPress accounts.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Authentication MUST preserve the existing secure public-client contract, including the specified browser-based authorisation flow or an explicitly equivalent secure implementation. Clients MUST NOT contain provider credentials, billing secrets or entitlement-signing secrets.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The supported registration, sign-in, sign-out, recovery, profile, session-inspection and session-revocation journeys MUST work against the production backend. Any journey that sends verification or recovery email MUST use a configured delivery service and expose delivery failures honestly.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Any transition from WordPress-linked authentication MUST use verified account mappings and recovery rules. Matching a mutable username MUST NOT transfer account ownership, administrative authority or paid entitlements.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Jacob’s reserved @CroakyJake handle and account-bound free Business feature grant MUST survive the transition. That grant MUST NOT become an exemption from resource accounting, security permissions or third-party spending approval.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browser applications MUST use authenticated equivalents of Home’s shared services without requiring a local Home installation. Permission approval, trust, revocation and audit semantics MUST remain consistent with native applications.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Personal and organisation contexts MUST remain separate throughout navigation, storage, billing, search and AI access. Switching accounts or organisations MUST NOT expose cached private information from the previous context.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-06 — Full browser versions of the applications

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every non-exempt Workspace and AI application MUST have a functional browser version.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The target is the same application on the web, not a companion dashboard, viewer-only edition or simplified alternative. At equivalent viewport sizes, the browser version MUST preserve the desktop application’s information architecture, tools, editor structure, commands, menus, selection behaviour, settings and supported workflows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browser-specific adaptations are permitted for actual capability differences and responsive layouts. They MUST NOT justify avoidable feature loss.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Web implementations MUST preserve CUI’s public semantics, shared component contracts, canonical state identities and supported actions. A browser-specific runtime is permitted; an independently redesigned, incompatible UI framework is not the intended outcome.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each app MUST support its applicable create, open, edit, save, reopen, history, import/export, sharing and recovery operations. The shared contextual AI bar MUST operate on the real semantic artifact through authorised owning-app APIs.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The web inventory MUST include the active Terra-form additions: Link, Prototype, Paths, Replay, Files’ organisation types and Variants in their owning applications. These retain their existing ownership and terminology; they MUST NOT be reorganised into different products for the web implementation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Each application MUST have a capability matrix identifying supported browser operations, equivalent adaptations and exact remaining restrictions. A restriction MUST identify the missing capability, affected operation, user-visible behaviour and validation evidence.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A desktop-only feature is not sufficient reason to omit an otherwise useful web app. Mini Computer retains its existing web exemption unless the required hosted-compute capability is explicitly provided. Other missing native capabilities MUST NOT be represented as available merely because a browser interface exists.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Direct links, browser refresh, back/forward navigation and account restoration MUST preserve the intended application and artifact context. Unsupported browsers MUST receive a meaningful compatibility state rather than a broken interface.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-07 — Files and 9to1 Drive production hosting

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: 9to1 Drive MUST become a real hosted storage service used by the web and desktop applications.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A file uploaded in the browser and opened on desktop MUST retain the same FileID and durable revision history. Local materialisation is a managed replica, not an unrelated imported copy. Files remains responsible for storage and filesystem operations; the owning application remains responsible for semantic document editing and collaboration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Private file storage MUST remain private. Protected downloads and shares MUST use access-controlled routes that enforce current account, organisation and object permissions. Possession of an object key MUST NOT grant access.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: R2’s public development endpoint MUST NOT be used as the production delivery mechanism or as a substitute for protected sharing. Cloudflare explicitly identifies r2.dev as development-oriented rather than production hosting. (developers.cloudflare.com)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Transfers MUST have durable identities, resumable progress, cancellation, integrity validation and recoverable failure states. Upload completion MUST not be reported until both content and the authoritative metadata commit have succeeded. Interrupted operations MUST be reconciled without invisible orphan uploads or duplicated quota charges.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Storage enforcement MUST account for committed usage and in-flight reservations. Concurrent uploads MUST NOT overspend the same allocation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Normal connected synchronisation MUST be push-based and incremental, with durable cursors and replay-safe reconciliation. Polling and full rescans remain recovery mechanisms rather than the ordinary propagation path.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sharing, search, previews, AI retrieval, version restoration and Trash MUST operate on the same canonical objects and permissions. Restoring an earlier revision MUST preserve subsequent history. Ordinary deletion remains recoverable; permanent purge remains a distinct protected operation.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-08 — Sites publishing and customer hosting

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sites MUST publish real websites to Cloudflare through its existing deployment model.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A published deployment MUST identify its SiteID, source revision, build/configuration revision, environment, provider result and domain bindings. Preview and production MUST remain distinct.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Publishing MUST include actual asset delivery, route handling and any supported server-side functionality. Successful static deployment MUST NOT be used to claim that required forms, CMS, authentication or dynamic application behaviour also works.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Builds and customer-supplied code MUST execute within appropriately isolated, authorised environments. Customer code MUST NOT inherit the credentials or privileges of CAKE’s account, billing or administrative services.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A failed build or deployment MUST preserve the previous working deployment. Rollback MUST restore a known deployment without deleting newer source history. These behaviours extend the existing deployment and publishing safeguards.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: First-party addresses, slug validation, reserved names, misleading-name review, custom-domain ownership verification and DNS/TLS readiness MUST implement the existing Sites contract. The default sites.9to1.uk/<site-slug> namespace MUST NOT silently become a different address scheme.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Browser isolation requires an explicit design decision. Different paths on the same hostname are not separate browser origins. The implementation MUST NOT assume that /site-a and /site-b isolate customer JavaScript, browser storage or other origin-scoped capabilities. A validated isolation design—or an explicitly approved namespace amendment—is required before arbitrary customer active content ships. (developer.mozilla.org)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Hosting limits MUST be enforced server-side. The existing Free-site inactivity policy MUST take affected sites offline without deleting their stored project data.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-09 — Real Stripe subscriptions and billing

heading: HEADING_3
text: Canonical plans and resource configuration

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stripe integration MUST implement the canonical subscription model rather than replace it with whatever is easiest to express in a pricing widget.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Preset identity, customised resource quantities, price-threshold entitlements and account-bound grants MUST remain distinct. The server MUST calculate effective access; clients MUST NOT grant resources from a displayed plan name or locally supplied price.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Existing preset definitions MUST remain versioned. Changing a commercial preset MUST NOT silently rewrite existing subscriber allocations. Unspecified quantities MUST remain unresolved rather than being invented during Stripe setup.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Checkout and activation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Checkout MUST begin from an authenticated, server-generated configuration quote. The quote MUST identify the account or organisation, resource configuration, currency, billing cadence, applicable charges and effective change timing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The backend MUST bind Stripe customer, subscription, price and invoice identifiers to the correct canonical account or organisation. Usernames and client-supplied account claims MUST NOT determine that binding.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Returning to a success page MUST NOT itself activate paid resources. Activation requires verified payment/subscription state and a successful entitlement update.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: A payment that succeeds while provisioning is delayed MUST produce a recoverable pending state. Retrying that operation MUST NOT charge the customer again.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Webhooks and reconciliation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Webhook processing MUST verify Stripe signatures against the raw request body, durably record accepted events and process them through retry-safe handlers.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The implementation MUST handle duplicate deliveries and out-of-order events. It MUST prevent both repeated event processing and repeated business effects, such as granting the same invoice’s allocation twice. Stripe does not guarantee event order, and its documentation explicitly requires duplicate-event handling. (docs.stripe.com)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The backend MUST support reconciliation against current Stripe objects after delivery failures or inconsistent local state. A delayed older event MUST NOT overwrite a newer valid subscription configuration.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Payment state, entitlement state and provisioning state MUST remain separately diagnosable.

heading: HEADING_3
text: Customer management and lifecycle

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Users MUST be able to manage payment methods, inspect invoices, manage supported subscription configurations and cancel through authenticated billing flows.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Stripe’s customer portal MAY provide supported account-management functions. It MUST NOT be the only implementation of custom resource changes: Stripe documents limitations on updating subscriptions containing multiple products or usage-based billing. Those configurations require a compatible trusted CAKE billing flow. (docs.stripe.com)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Plan changes MUST preview the resulting price, resource allocation, effective date and any immediate charge or credit. Renewal failures, additional payment authentication, cancellation, refunds and disputes MUST map to explicit account states under the approved billing policy.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Billing failure or downgrade MUST NOT silently delete user files, site source or organisation content. Billing management, authorised export and recovery MUST remain available through the appropriate routes.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Business and Business + remain organisation add-ons with separately funded resources. Unlimited seat capacity MUST NOT be interpreted as unlimited storage or AI usage. Existing seat-remediation and account-bound grant rules remain applicable.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-10 — Cloud AI and connected application services

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Cloud-backed features MUST use real provider connections, with credentials held by trusted services.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The AI gateway MUST enforce identity, organisation policy, model entitlement, resource limits and Dust before execution. It MUST support streaming, cancellation, provider failures and recoverable interrupted sessions.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Usage MUST follow the existing reserve → run → settle contract. Parallel requests MUST NOT spend the same balance twice, and uncertain provider outcomes MUST remain subject to reconciliation rather than arbitrary charging or credit creation. Local models and core local tools MUST NOT be charged as cloud AI usage.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Desktop, web and Personal API access MUST draw from the same applicable entitlement and usage services. Personal API access retains its existing eligibility and shared-allocation rules.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Every existing feature that declares an online dependency MUST have that dependency implemented and validated. This includes applicable collaboration, organisation services, provider connections, notifications, Forms responses, published integrations, Agents and Automations.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Execution location MUST be explicit. A browser task, a cloud-hosted task and a task requiring an enrolled desktop device are different capabilities. Closing a tab MUST NOT silently terminate a task advertised as cloud-hosted; an offline device MUST NOT be shown as executing work.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Long-running operations MUST expose durable job identity, progress, cancellation, retries and results. Reconnection MUST NOT repeat consequential actions. Persistent work MUST retain its authorised identity, scope and funding source.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-11 — Operations, security and release delivery

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The production service MUST include health checks, actionable failure reporting, privacy-preserving diagnostics and alerts for material outages, failed billing processing, failed jobs and approaching resource limits.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Rate limits, account quotas and workload admission controls MUST prevent one customer from consuming another customer’s allocation or exhausting shared services without bounds. Spending alerts MUST NOT be treated as equivalent to an enforced spending ceiling.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Backups and recovery MUST cover canonical metadata, file revisions, account mappings, entitlement records, site source and deployment configuration—not merely a collection of uploaded bytes. Restoration MUST be tested, with documented recovery objectives.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The existing Privacy Ceiling applies to hosted services, provider integrations, telemetry, retention, exports and deletion propagation. Moving functionality online MUST NOT silently broaden AI access or weaken promised encryption.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Deployment pipelines MUST identify exact source revisions, validate changes before activation and support rollback. Database/schema and client updates MUST account for already-open browser sessions and older supported native clients.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public download and update paths MUST provide real, verified release artifacts. Home and Launcher MUST continue using their shared package authority, integrity checks and staged activation rather than separate manually maintained update lists.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-12 — End-to-end acceptance

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Acceptance MUST exercise the deployed services, not only mocks or isolated components.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Independent operation

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Public websites and cloud-hosted services remain operational without the developer’s PC and survive representative customer-workload failures.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
NORMAL_TEXT
text: Payment failure scenarios MUST first be exercised using appropriate test facilities. Live-mode validation requires an authorised merchant configuration and explicit approval for any actual charge. Test-mode success alone MUST NOT be reported as proof of live billing.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Visual and interaction testing MUST cover populated workloads, narrow layouts, keyboard operation, screen-reader semantics, 200% scaling, themes, reduced motion and failure/recovery states.

heading: HEADING_2
text: SH-13 — Decisions required before affected functionality goes live

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The following items remain explicit launch decisions rather than implementation guesses.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Commercial catalogue and lifecycle policy. Finalise all offered resource allocations, usage periods, rollover rules, configuration prices, downgrade behaviour, grace periods and retention consequences. The existing specification leaves material allocations and billing policies unresolved. Undefined configurations MUST NOT be offered for purchase.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Currency and entitlement-price calculation. Define how tax, discounts, promotional credits and non-monthly billing affect EntitlementPriceMonthly. Resolve the existing GBP resource pricing and USD Business add-ons through an approved billing policy. Stripe requires prices within a single multi-product subscription to use the same currency; silent relabelling or conversion is not acceptable. (docs.stripe.com)

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Production service configuration. Confirm the account-authentication implementation, transactional delivery provider, database/coordination boundaries, supported runtime capabilities and environment ownership. Existing compatible infrastructure MUST be inspected before replacement.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Customer-site browser isolation. Approve the isolation mechanism for active content under the specified path-based public addresses. Any change to the canonical URL model requires an explicit specification amendment.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Operational and launch parameters. Confirm supported browser versions, measurable performance/capacity targets, recovery objectives, infrastructure budgets, merchant readiness and production cutover authorisation.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: These decisions MUST block only their affected release paths. They MUST NOT be silently resolved by a worker, hidden behind defaults or used to stop independent implementation.

heading: HEADING_2
text: Release exit gate

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Sol Happy is complete only when the required online services are implemented, integrated, deployed to their authorised environments and validated against the applicable specification.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: Implemented, tested, deployed and commercially enabled MUST remain distinguishable states.

heading: NORMAL_TEXT
text: The final evidence ledger MUST identify the tested release, deployed service versions, functioning user journeys and every remaining blocker or approved scoped exception. No service may be described as online merely because its interface exists, a provider account has been connected or a test request succeeded.
